Gathering​ Use Downtime to Gather Herbs, max usage 3x a day (uses 8 hours in a session). Note: You can no longer sacrifice adventuring time to harvest extra herbs. Choose one environment [Cave, Forest, Desert, Grasslands, Swamp] + Rarity [Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare] Roll Nature/Medicine/Arcana + Herbalism/Poisoner/Brewer/Alchemist Tool Prof Bonus (If proficient) --> DC scales depending on rarity of ingredient. Once check is completed, post in transcript using template found in pins of transcript . Craftmaster will roll for the herb gathered randomly depending on location chosen and DC rarity met. DCs for Enchantment Ingredients:​ Rarity DC Common DC 10 Uncommon DC 13 Rare DC 17 Very Rare DC 20 Targeted Gathering​ You can target herbs based on which potion you wish to make! If you are targeting a herb for a specific potion, use the Targeted gathering Template pinned in transcript If the herb you are searching for isn't in the environment you chose, you get nothing. If it is, a Craftmaster will roll the herb normally, and you only get the herb if the dice comply. The DCs for targeted gathering are as followed:​ Rarity DC Common DC 13 Uncommon DC 17 Rare DC 20 Very Rare DC 23 Bonuses:​ You can only target one herb per day until you have gathered 3 of that herb, at which point you may target for two herbs per day due to your familiarity. You cannot use help actions in herb gathering. Self-Buffs are allowed for now. Nat20 Rule: If you roll nat20 on the check (RAW Nat20 without modifiers and bonuses) you get 1 Extra Herb. Over10 Rule: If your total roll is 10 over the applicable DC you get 1 Extra Herb. Example, if your total roll for a rare is 31, you get 2 Herbs instead of 1. Nat20 and Over10 rules can both apply, to a max of 3 Herbs per roll.

Potions are brewed using herbs, each herb is used for a specific potion, the potion is hinted at in the description. Time, base Cost, Herb Requirement to brew: Rarity Time (Days) Cost Herb Requirement Common 2.5 25 gp 1 Herb Uncommon 5 100 gp 1 Herb Rare 12.5 1,000 gp 2 Herbs Very Rare 25 10,000 gp 3 Herbs Monster Part Substitution​ You can substitute 1 Herb for a monster part, however uncommon and higher potions need at least 1 Herb. Potion Rarity Monster CR Loot DC Common CR 1-3 DC 13 Uncommon CR 4-8 DC 17 Rare CR 9-13 DC 21 Very Rare CR 14-18 DC 24 Legendary CR 19+ DC 26 Bulk Brewing​ Bulk Brewing has a discount on overall cost now. For every 10 potions you make at a time, you get a 5% discount on cost, cap for the discount is 20%. Bulk Brewing also requires less herbs. For every 10 potions you brew, you only need 7x the amount of herbs for one potion of the same rarity. Example: 10 common potions of healing - 7 enchantment herbs needed. Time Reduction​ You get a 50% time reduction if you use double the amount of enchantment herbs for the potion. Sacrificing Potions: You can sacrifice one potion per brew. Lowers base time by half the time it takes to brew a potion of that rarity.

A PC may attempt to tame animals over an extended period of time. Taming Check​ Check: Wisdom (Animal Handling) Tame DC: 15 + (2 * CR) (minimum 11) Time: 1 full day of calm interaction (one day of downtime) Initial Tame​ Before training begins, the creature must first be made non-hostile through patience, calmness, or courage. Roll Result Natural 20 Start at 25% Bond Progress Success Creature becomes non-hostile and open to training Fail by 5 or less You fail to train the creature, you may retry after 1 day Fail by 5 or more You fail to train the creature, you may retry after 3 days Natural 1 The creature flees or attacks, you may retry after 1 week Long-Term Bond Training​ Each day requires 8 hours of focused interaction. You can train only one creature at a time. Each success adds your roll to a cumulative total. Roll Result Natural 20 Add roll plus 10% of total progress threshold Success You Progress your bond with the creature Fail by 5 or less Your bond with the creature does not progress Fail by 5 or more The creature refuses training, you may retry after 3 days Natural 1 The creature flees or attacks, you may retry after 1 week Progress cannot fall below your current bond stage unless broken by neglect or narrative reason. Bond Progression​ Bond Stage Progress Threshold Non-Hostile Success on Initial Tame Sociable 10 + (10 * CR) Basic Commands Stay. Come. Stop. 15 + (15 * CR) Complex Commands Dodge. Attack X creature. Hide. 20 + (20 * CR) Mounted / Complex Tasks Scout X area. Return to X location. Find X person. 25 + (25 * CR) Example: A CR 3 beast needs 80 total progress to reach Complex Commands. Once a stage is reached, it remains permanent unless broken through RP.

It must be reasonable for the creature to be tamed, per DM discretion. It must make sense within the context of TWR lore, per DM discretion. The creatures you can potentially tame are limited by the CR. In order to have the skill necessary to safely handle a creature, you must be capable of hitting the initial tame DC through just a straight animal handling roll without additional modifiers from items, spells, abilities, etc. Maximum Tamable CR = (5 + Your Base Animal Handling Modifier) / 2 Creatures with legendary or mythic abilities can not be tamed. Creatures with an INT of 1 can not be tamed. Creatures with an INT of 4+ can not be tamed. The initial tame, and subsequent checks, must be RPed for and submitted in transcript. For CR 1+ The initial tame must occur in a mini-quest or RPed targeted hunt run by DM. A DM can not run their own quest if they are attempting to tame a creature. For any creatures intended as a mount, the initial tame must occur in a mini-quest or RPed targeted hunt run by DM. A DM can not run their own quest if they are attempting to tame a creature. Purchasable domesticated mounts are an exception, and can be purchased as normal. No more than 1 creature can be tamed per day. Exceptions may exist for things such as domesticated animals, per discretion of the DM. Only creatures at least one size larger than a PC are mountable. Owl-Bear Taming Example Steps​ Go on a mini quest hosted by a DM. RP to find and convince the Owl-Bear that you are both not food and non hostile. CR3 creature, so DC 30 animal handling check for an adult Owl-Bear. Upon success, it will be non hostile but still aggressive. Cumulative DC of 300. The daily RPed animal handling checks would be added together. With an average roll of 10, with the +10 modifier required to initially tame the creature, it would take 15 days in real life of daily checks and RP to tame the creature. At 75 points, it would become sociable At 150 points, it would accept simple commands At 225 points, it would accept complex commands and barding At 300 points, it would accept complex tasks and be mountable To be updated
The creature acts on its own initiative. You control it as you would a summon RAW from spells such as Conjure Animals.

documents.t: Because of the inherent danger of things such as meteor swarms, when you are mounted the creature shares your HP. If you fall to zero HP, your mount falls to 1 HP, you are dismounted if on land, and if it is a flying creature it begins to crashland at 60ft/round. For the purposes of movement, the mount replaces your move speed(s). HP when dismounting: When you dismount, if your HP is lower than the mount's HP, the mount will adopt the same current HP as you. If you choose to have the mount attack, take any action, or otherwise treat it as a separate creature, ignore points 1~4 and it will be treated as a normal mount RAW. Mounted Combatant Feat interaction​ Under this system you can use either RAW and risk damage to the mount or the alternative rules in the Animal Taming doc. If you're using the alternative rules only point 1 of the feat pertaining to advantaged against creatures is applicable, the other two are nullified.

The recipient must be capable of hitting the initial tame DC to be capable of controlling the creature in any way. By default, the bond level resets to zero. If you are proficient in Animal Handling, it resets to 25%. If you have expertise in Animal Handling, it resets to 50%
If your tamed creature dies and is revived it will regress one cumulative level. If your tame is regressed past 0 the taming process with restart requiring a new initial tame roll.

The rules for Character Creation are below. For how to manage characters as they level up, see the Character Progression page.

The Wandering Realms is primarily a Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (2014) server and maintains a baseline of 5e gameplay rules. Approved 5.5e (Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (2024)) Sourcebooks will only permit use of the below types of features. Please note that 5.5e Backgrounds are never approved. The types of content which will be approved are: Species Classes Subclasses Feats Spells Items Some of this content has been banned or errata'd for use in our server. Please read 5.5e Integration page for more details on 5.5e content.

Unless otherwise stated, rules regarding characters are RAW (rule as written). Approved/Disapproved Modules can be found here: Approved and Disapproved Modules Characters can start at level 1-3 (player choice) Items, Experience, Abilities, etc do not carry over from other games/servers/campaigns. Backgrounds which grant feats are disallowed. You may choose Fixed or Rolled HP for your character, but must continue with that method for the lifetime of your PC. If rolling, ping a @Dungeonmaster to record your rolls. Character level advancement is via XP, not Milestone. All character stats are Point Buy or Standard Array. Character sheets must be kept up to date. If there is ever a question as to what level you are supposed to be, what items you have, how much gold you have, then we need to be able to refer to your sheet and check it against what we have on record in #records, #story-log or #transaction-log. You may have no more than 8 player characters to begin with. Once a character reaches T3, you may submit a request for additional PC slots.

New PCs begin with standard starting equipment per the PHB. Starting gold is not allowed. PCs may select a single Uncommon magic item to start with, if they submit a written backstory that includes receiving it. This item must be available from the Favor Tables. This can be access in discord with <!loot uncommon wondrous s>, <!loot uncommon armaments s> or any +1 weapon or shield. The base value of the item may not exceed a gold value of 400gp (i.e. no Mithral Plate, firearms, except a pistol or arquebus, etc.) Approved PCs may ping @sky or @Todo for Adventurer's Fund money (400 gp) Character Sheet Generators​ Dndbeyond is recommended for easy character creation, but you may use another system if you wish. (Avrae supports Dndbeyond, Dicecloud, and Gsheet) For DNDBeyond users, you may join one of the donated campaigns for access to sourcebooks. Disclosures​ DMs have the right to refuse characters a spot in their quests, including those using UA/Homebrew supplements otherwise permitted by the server

Submit a link to your character sheet using the Character Submission template pinned in #transcript for Staff review and approval. Once approved, it will be posted by a Staff Member to #active-pc-sheet-links at which time your character can officially be played on the server. While not required, it is highly recommended you set up a "tupperbot" for your character. This allows you to speak "in character" easier when participating in role-play. Refer to Discord Commands for more information on the tools we use. While not required, if you desire you may introduce your character in #pc-introductions and include an image and short description of them.

documents.t: Sometimes your original concept for a build doesn't exactly work out. We get it. While you are in T1, you can make any changes you wish to your character to bring it in line with what will be most fun for you to play. Once you have made changes, post a summary to #transcript for review and records keeping. Once your PC is in T2, your choices are locked in without following Retraining Rules where they apply. Regardless of any other changes your PC's name must not change.

Gaining Experience​ Once your character has been approved, any successful gameplay logged in #story-log or #records will provide you with XP to add to your sheet. Characters level up following the normal XP Tables defined in the Dungeonmaster’s Guide. PC Tiers and Levels​ Gameplay is generally restricted to “Tiers” as defined in the Dungeonmaster’s Guide. Tier Level Range Tier 1 1-4 Tier 2 5-10 Tier 3 11-16 Tier 4 17-20 Post-20 “21-26” Paragon Special Item Rarity and PC Level Restrictions​ The item restrictions below determine whether your PC is able to use/attune to a magic item: Tier Level Range Rarity Tier 1 1-4 Uncommon Tier 2 5-10 Rare Tier 3 11-16 Very Rare Tier 4 17-20 Legendary Soft Level Cap​ You have the option to apply a level cap to any of your PCs. If you choose to do this, any experience you would have gained while capped cannot be applied at a later time/date. You must state your intention to cap a character in #transcript. If you wish to uncap the character, you must announce your intention to do so the same way. Either instance will be posted to #records for record keeping. Character Retirement​ Sometimes the arc of a character results in their retirement from the life of an adventurer. Other times you may simply wish to no longer play that character. It is possible to turn that character into an NPC via ‘retirement’. See Character Retirement for a full understanding of how to retire a PC.

Character Retirement​ Sometimes the arc of a character results in their retirement from the life of an adventurer. Other times you may simply wish to no longer play that character. It is possible to turn that character into an NPC via ‘retirement’. Simply make a post in the #transcript channel stating your intention to retire the character as an NPC. To unretire a PC NPC, they start at level 1-3 and need to start as if they are new PC. Defining What A Retired PC Can Do in Regards for Their Downtime Activities​ Retired PCs Can: Craft Perform Services (Including spellcasting.) Run Businesses, Organizations, and other passive income/influence. Retired PCs Cannot Train Obtain Vehicle or Tool Profs Obtain Languages Other Item Production (Such as using class features for item production) Converting an NPC to a PC​ To unretire a PC NPC, they start at level 1-3 and need to start as if they are a new PC. Unretirement​ Unretiring requires a PC slot available. Unretiring characters are limited to level 20 (post20’s revert back to level 20). Retired PC sheet link must be in ⁠npc-listings to keep any form of wealth or level. If the sheet isn’t there, then the PC must be created as any new PC would be Unretiring an ex PC​ Unretire at previous level with old items and gold, provided the following: 2d4 * PC level days of retraining (via downtime) PC can still be used to roleplay/adventure while retraining Cooldown of 1 month to unretire another PC Make a report and post in ⁠transcript (staff approving will roll the 2d4) Report should consist of player name, character name, and character level Otherwise, the PC will Methods to Speed Up Unretirement​ RP related to returning to adventuring, retraining, or something of the sort. Submit a rp xp request, but state you want it to speed up retraining instead. Staff approving the request decides how many days to remove, to a max of 10. Money Pit​ Tier Daily Cost Maximum # of Days T1 - - T2 1,000 gp 3 Days T3 10,000 gp 5 Days T4 20,000 gp 5 Days

Companion Leveling System Converting your Companions to Player Characters Boon of Ascension

Presenting the Companion Leveling System, allowing creatures special to your characters to gain a spotlight of their own, matching the power-scaling of the character themselves. Below details the system and how your companions can gain levels, and which are eligible for use in this system.

All subclass companions are eligible for this system. This includes, but is not limited to: Beast Master’s Animal Companion The Extraplanar’s Planar Tether Purple Dragon Knight’s Amethyst Dragon Battle Smith’s Steel Defender Other creatures can be eligible, but must be either permanently available to you, or otherwise not tied to a duration. Examples of this include: Creatures Tamed by your character Artificer’s Homunculus Servant Spirits Summoned by Find Familiar, Find Steed, or similar magic Hirelings are not eligible for this system.

To start the leveling process for a character’s companion, the character must first take the [Boon of Ascension] detailed later in this document. This boon may be taken multiple times, but only once for each 20 class levels a character has. When the character takes the boon, they may select a single companion that they control and is eligible for this system, and grant that creature a single level in a class of their choosing. The creature then may gain experience through RP as if they were a paragon PC, with the ability to level up all the way to P26. A companion under this system has the following restrictions: The companion must fill an empty PC slot. You cannot add a creature to this system if you do not have an available slot. The companion does not gain a Boon, Blessing, or Feat at P26, but must still meet the requisite xp to enter a new paragon cycle in order to do so. The companion counts as a controlled entity for the purposes of Hunts, Trials, Raids, etc. A DM can rule otherwise for the purpose of quests. The companion may not reach a level higher than the original character. In return, the companion gains the following benefits: If the companions actions are normally determined by the original character’s actions, bonus actions, or other similar requirements, they no longer need to do so in order to act. The companion rolls its own initiative in combat. The companion retains any benefits that it had as part of the original character’s class features
This section contains guidelines for converting your companions into player characters.
documents.s: Converting Your Companions to Playable Characters

documents.t: When your companion becomes a player character through this system, it retains its previous hit point maximum. It then gains hit points equal to the [Hit Points at 1st Level] hit points of the class it gains, and [Hit Points at Higher Levels] as it gains levels.

Your companion also retains any skill or saving throw proficiencies it had, as well as any bonuses to them that your class features provided. In addition, your companion gains the skill, saving throw, tool, weapon, and armor proficiencies that would normally be given with their selected class. Armor and Other Equipment: More bestial creatures can still make use of barding, of which they are always considered proficient. In order to use weapons, a creature must have a reasonable capacity to use it. If a creature is a size other than medium, any weapons and armor it uses must be properly sized for its use, following the same price conversions as barding.

You may create a character sheet for your companion on any of the available platforms that allow you to do so. Some may be better suited than others for this. When your sheet is completed, you may submit it as normal to #transcript for approval. Please provide the original character’s name, and specify that the sheet is for a companion when you do so. Example: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/therestoftheurl Companion Sheet of Syn. Original Character: Bim
Below are the details of the Boon of Ascension

Prerequisites: Having at least one companion eligible for ascension One eligible companion of your choice gains a level in a single class of your choosing. The companion then may level as normal as through the Paragon System.

If you are being revived by a member of your own party during the course of any content, revival is successful with no penalty aside from the typical cost of casting and any damage to your body or belongings. If you died but your party succeeded, you may skip the below retrieval steps provided that the party members state your corpse was recovered.

Characters wishing to return to the scene of a failed hunt to recover their fallen allies or missing friends may do so by engaging the creature that killed them, by targeting them in a hunt. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

To retrieve lost bodies in Trials of Tempus, a new party must first spawn into the trial per all the usual rules at the same level of the bodies. The players must then fight through the temple to secure the room containing the corpses before recovery is possible. Once the room is secured, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

Characters wishing to return to the scene of a failed hunt to recover their fallen allies or missing friends may do so by engaging in a random deadly hunt using the applicable alias of the same tier as the dead party. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

The Party is banished to a special retrieval zone that acts like a hunting ground Any Tier party, excluding Paragon, can attempt to retrieve them, but there needs to be In character motivation or reason to look for the party. #leaveanote The Party will do a random hunt at deadly difficulty for the Party, upon conclusion of the hunt. A single Investigation check per dead body can be made to retrieve the dead party members. If the party fails the check, they must do another random hunt to repeat the attempt

If you die as a part of a quest or roleplay session run by a @Dungeonmaster, who will provide you details about the location and condition of your body, as well as any necessary information regarding retrieval. Body Retrieval Checks​ Only PCs within the same tier as the dead character may participate in body retrieval. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check: Tier Investigation DC T1 10 T2 15 T3 20 T4 25 Post-20 30

If your PC is going on a dangerous mission, read below! Leave a Note Before You Go: • Tag: @YourName | PC Name • What part of the map are you’re exploring (coords or pin) • How long do you expect to be gone • When others should start searching • How you want to be revived if you die • If you don’t list revival plans, retrieval parties decide your fate • Unknown/isolated PCs may not be retrieved at all •Leaving a note does not guarantee that the party will perform the task as wished as this extends outside of the player's control Pre Retrievals MUST be roleplayed and require staff approval. It is not necessary to roleplay dungeons/hunts/raids Further Options: Fate’s Offer – Return from the Dead Quest Hosted by: @ todo (Entity: Fate) If your PC dies and can’t be retrieved, this quest gives a final chance to return. High risk. If you fail, your PC is likely lost forever. Open and always available.

The first time a PC dies within a trial or hunt in tier 1, their body is automatically collected and brought to a nearby clinic, where they are revived via raise dead or resurrection (in cases of disintegration). Note that this only occurs once per pc, and thus will not be available after prestige, or retirement. For tracking reasons, when this is done, add Collection Agency in a separate line within the hunt or trial transcript, with the collected character's name printed again after it in the case of multiple characters.

Summoned and PC controlled entities, can attune to magic items, but they share the attunement slot of the PC. Examples of Entities: Simulacrum, Familiars, Beast companions, steel defender, undead, planar bound summons, etc. When a controlled entity uses a PC's attunement slot to attune to an item. Only one item of the same name can be attuned by either PC or Controlled entity. ex: A Wizard and their Simulacrum can't both be attuned to Illusionist Bracers.

Sometimes, you feel the need to take a break from the server or leave. That's okay! However, if you DO plan on leaving, you should retire your PCs so that the sheets are not lost. When a player leaves, their sheets will be moved to the Inactive PC Links thread. If you wish to bring back an Inactive PC, just post in #transcript with a link to their inactive sheet and a staff member will move it for you.

A player may run an NPC with the following caveats. Breaking any requires the permission of a @Dungeonmaster or @Loremaster. 1: The NPC must act according to its character, or alignment. 2: The NPC cannot be a high-standing or of great importance individual. 3: The NPC must be given adequate reason to physically exist in this plane. 4: The NPC cannot grant PC's mechanical benefits of any sort. Items, Crafting, Gifts, all of the like. Only acceptable as shopkeep or storefronts selling items. ---- Rule 1 dictates that monsters must act relevant to lore. To break such action, or to play an outlier, requires permission. Rule 2 dictates that NPC roleplayed must be of low bearing. Shopkeep, Bartenders, Apprentices and the generic like. A player cannot run any characters which could influence a greater plot that they are not actively running. Rule 3 dictates that no creature may exist without bearing. A mind flayer would not exist in a town as a vampire lord would not be sleeping in a forest. Rule 4 dictates that NPC may not grant mechanical benefits. Pure and simple, save shopkeeps selling mundane items at reasonable (per market discretion) prices.

A Player Character is considered to be Post20 if they have reached 385,000xp, and receive rewards at the following thresholds: XP Threshold Reward 385,000 ASI +1 415,000 AS1 +1 445,000 Boon/Feat/Blessing 475,000 AS1 +1 505,000 AS1 +1 535,000 Boon/Feat/Blessing

Boon/Blessing/Feat choices are permanent. Your PC's first Boon/Blessing may be chosen from the list of Boons or Blessings once the slot has been unlocked (use the !boon or !blessing command in discord) For PCs who earned Boons via a quest before this change, you may choose the next Boon slot that you unlock through the Post-20 or Paragon systems Feats can be selected once unlocked. Feats can be retrained into quested Boons/Blessings if desired Boon and Blessing choices are permanent Blessings/Charms can be removed by the granting Deity at DM discretion. Blessings are not limited to a fixed list, and can be shaped and created to better fit a circumstance, at the DM’s discretion. This would require a majority vote to proceed. Post 20 Boons and Blessings can be obtained using the Wish spell, but the Wish must be worded appropriately. This only applies to the second Boon slot of a PC's first 20 levels. PCs cannot use Wish to gain boons or blessings for any paragon cycle boon slots. A comprehensive list of blessing and boons can be viewed on discord using !boon or !blessing Please post your Post 20 rewards in #transcript as you receive them A PC that gets Post20 rewards is still considered a level 20 character for all intents and purposes

If a player leaves during a quest, trial, or other event without the permission of the DM or person running it, they will be cursed, and put into the @Cursed role for two weeks. During this time, all characters belonging to the player receive only half XP and gold rewards, and cannot be resurrected if killed (except via Revivify spell). The @cursed role may also be given for other offenses at the discretion of the DM, Moderator, and Admin teams.

TWR is a server based on mutual respect. Rude, disruptive, and generally toxic behavior will be subject to moderator review. Below are some explanations of behavior which is not acceptable, but this is by no means an exhaustive list: Abuse/harassment/bullying/threats of mental or physical harm against one or more people. Insults directed against any player or staff on the server. Repeated insensitive or inappropriate jokes. Be respectful of subjects such as race, religion, politics, etc. Use of any type of slur. Threats of self harm Self harm is a serious matter and should not be joked about or taken lightly. Follow Discord TOS found here https://discord.com/terms No spamming, raiding, or anything that disturbs the peace. While mods and admins are here to help you, abuse of moderator or staff pings may result in a warning. Voice chats: Don’t play any alarmingly loud sounds or scream into the mic. Please keep channel content appropriate to the channel being used Keep memes and shitposting to #the-c-o-r-n-e-r where possible. #general can be a fun place, but please don’t flood the channel with memes. Swearing is banned in #the-peoples-court Roleplay in RP channels, Out of Character talk in OOC etc Art Advertising or solicitation of any kind is not allowed. If you are ever made to feel uncomfortable by content on the server, or by someone’s behavior, please report it to anyone with the @Moderator or @Admin role. We want everyone to feel comfortable and safe here.
Companion Leveling System Converting your Companions to Player Characters Boon of Ascension

Presenting the Companion Leveling System, allowing creatures special to your characters to gain a spotlight of their own, matching the power-scaling of the character themselves. Below details the system and how your companions can gain levels, and which are eligible for use in this system.

All subclass companions are eligible for this system. This includes, but is not limited to: Beast Master’s Animal Companion The Extraplanar’s Planar Tether Purple Dragon Knight’s Amethyst Dragon Battle Smith’s Steel Defender Other creatures can be eligible, but must be either permanently available to you, or otherwise not tied to a duration. Examples of this include: Creatures Tamed by your character Artificer’s Homunculus Servant Spirits Summoned by Find Familiar, Find Steed, or similar magic Hirelings are not eligible for this system.

To start the leveling process for a character’s companion, the character must first take the [Boon of Ascension] detailed later in this document. This boon may be taken multiple times, but only once for each 20 class levels a character has. When the character takes the boon, they may select a single companion that they control and is eligible for this system, and grant that creature a single level in a class of their choosing. The creature then may gain experience through RP as if they were a paragon PC, with the ability to level up all the way to P26. A companion under this system has the following restrictions: The companion must fill an empty PC slot. You cannot add a creature to this system if you do not have an available slot. The companion does not gain a Boon, Blessing, or Feat at P26, but must still meet the requisite xp to enter a new paragon cycle in order to do so. The companion counts as a controlled entity for the purposes of Hunts, Trials, Raids, etc. A DM can rule otherwise for the purpose of quests. The companion may not reach a level higher than the original character. In return, the companion gains the following benefits: If the companions actions are normally determined by the original character’s actions, bonus actions, or other similar requirements, they no longer need to do so in order to act. The companion rolls its own initiative in combat. The companion retains any benefits that it had as part of the original character’s class features
This section contains guidelines for converting your companions into player characters.
documents.s: Converting Your Companions to Playable Characters

documents.t: When your companion becomes a player character through this system, it retains its previous hit point maximum. It then gains hit points equal to the [Hit Points at 1st Level] hit points of the class it gains, and [Hit Points at Higher Levels] as it gains levels.

Your companion also retains any skill or saving throw proficiencies it had, as well as any bonuses to them that your class features provided. In addition, your companion gains the skill, saving throw, tool, weapon, and armor proficiencies that would normally be given with their selected class. Armor and Other Equipment: More bestial creatures can still make use of barding, of which they are always considered proficient. In order to use weapons, a creature must have a reasonable capacity to use it. If a creature is a size other than medium, any weapons and armor it uses must be properly sized for its use, following the same price conversions as barding.

You may create a character sheet for your companion on any of the available platforms that allow you to do so. Some may be better suited than others for this. When your sheet is completed, you may submit it as normal to #transcript for approval. Please provide the original character’s name, and specify that the sheet is for a companion when you do so. Example: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/therestoftheurl Companion Sheet of Syn. Original Character: Bim
Below are the details of the Boon of Ascension

Prerequisites: Having at least one companion eligible for ascension One eligible companion of your choice gains a level in a single class of your choosing. The companion then may level as normal as through the Paragon System.

Time passes at the same rate within the world of TWR that it passes in our world. For easy reference, there is a channel in the server that lists the time on Elysium. This is an optional time you can use for coordination and envinronmental change, but you may act out your character’s life within each day as it meets your schedule. Daily Reset​ For the purposes of downtime and daily activities, your PC’s day begins when you wake up in the morning and ends when you go to bed. For fringe cases, daily resets should occur roughly every 24 hours.

Each day, characters have the following resources: Hunting Tags - 5​ Trial Tags - 2​ Downtime Hours - 8​ Long Rest - 1 *​ Short Rest - 8 *​ Long and Short Rests​ Aside from rests which occur in Trials or Quests, players are limited to 1 Long Rest and 8 Short Rests per day. These can be taken at the player’s discretion by using the !sr or !lr command in discord.

During the course of a quest, characters may be restricted by the DM from pursuing hunts, trials, downtime options and rests as usual. While your PC is attending a quest, work with your DM to determine what parts of their daily routine can be continued.

Some spells or projects require daily activity to fully realize. In cases like this, players should post in #transcript describing the action, how long they will repeat it, and outlining all the materials required (which must be procured ahead of time). Staff will then review the post, notify you of any issues or extra requirements, and when the time has passed your actions will become official.

Each PC may utilize 8 hours per day of downtime to further their character’s goals and story. Downtime options can be pursued as outlined by RAW in books such as the PHB, DMG, and XGtE. Some examples include crafting magical items, performing research, gambling, or working a mundane job. Additional downtime options may be defined in other TWR supplements. This server uses the “Optional Rule” for sleep deprivation located in Xanathar’s Guide to Everything if you wish to work through the night.

If you are being revived by a member of your own party during the course of any content, revival is successful with no penalty aside from the typical cost of casting and any damage to your body or belongings. If you died but your party succeeded, you may skip the below retrieval steps provided that the party members state your corpse was recovered.

Characters wishing to return to the scene of a failed hunt to recover their fallen allies or missing friends may do so by engaging the creature that killed them, by targeting them in a hunt. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

To retrieve lost bodies in Trials of Tempus, a new party must first spawn into the trial per all the usual rules at the same level of the bodies. The players must then fight through the temple to secure the room containing the corpses before recovery is possible. Once the room is secured, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

Characters wishing to return to the scene of a failed hunt to recover their fallen allies or missing friends may do so by engaging in a random deadly hunt using the applicable alias of the same tier as the dead party. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check.

The Party is banished to a special retrieval zone that acts like a hunting ground Any Tier party, excluding Paragon, can attempt to retrieve them, but there needs to be In character motivation or reason to look for the party. #leaveanote The Party will do a random hunt at deadly difficulty for the Party, upon conclusion of the hunt. A single Investigation check per dead body can be made to retrieve the dead party members. If the party fails the check, they must do another random hunt to repeat the attempt

If you die as a part of a quest or roleplay session run by a @Dungeonmaster, who will provide you details about the location and condition of your body, as well as any necessary information regarding retrieval. Body Retrieval Checks​ Only PCs within the same tier as the dead character may participate in body retrieval. Once the enemy has been defeated, make a body retrieval (Investigation) check: Tier Investigation DC T1 10 T2 15 T3 20 T4 25 Post-20 30

Violation of any of the rules will generally result in a verbal warning. A second violation of the same rule will result in a strike. A strike typically lasts for 2 months from the date of issue. Players with three active strikes will be banned from TWR for a 3 month period Any other disciplinary action up to and including a permanent ban may be dispensed by the mods following a majority vote. Some examples of what might bypass the process include, but are not limited to: Art Advertising (specifically public posting or DMing other server members) Trolling and Raids (coming to the server with the sole intent of causing trouble) Extreme cases of rule #1 violations (slurs, excessively vulgar/targeted language, harassment, etc.) Illegal Activities Repeated disregard of staff instructions regarding rules or server norms. (Especially if such disregard comes in the form of blatantly disrespectful or hostile behavior in violation of of our Code of Conduct) If you are ever made to feel uncomfortable by content on the server, or by someone’s behavior, please report it to anyone with the @Moderator or @Admin role. We want everyone to feel comfortable and safe here. Bans issued for any reason are, of course, subject to an optional appeal by the offending player, if they should choose to do so. Contact a @Moderator or @Admin if you wish to appeal a ban issued to you or to another member of the server.

When performing any downtime activities, any bonuses to skill checks made must last for the full eight hours of downtime to be applicable to the final skill check. (Cases that specifically state otherwise overrules this, i.e. herb gathering)

To ensure a fair and predictable economy on TWR, trades and purchases are limited by a minimum value, which can only be exceeded through Roleplay with @dungeonmaster or @craftmaster approval. Minimum Selling Price Limits for Trading Magical Items to Other PCs: Base Price + Rarity Mods as below. If an item does not have a base price, then just use the rarity mods below. this applies if the base price is above 400gp. Rarity Minimum Trade Value Common 100 gp Uncommon 400 gp Rare 4,000 gp Very Rare 40,000 gp Legendary 200,000 gp * Consumable items can be traded for (rarity)/2 gp For example plate being 1500 gp the magic item variants will be 1500 gp + x amount of gold

Players can now sell magic items to NPCs for gold, or offer it to a deity of their choice for favor. Selling to NPCs gives the character gold equal to half the minimum price of that item. Offering it up to a deity of their choice gives the character favor equal to a quarter of what it costs to roll a random item of that category.

There are three item types: Scrap, Old, and New. Scrap sells at 10% of sale value. Unusable Old sells at 50%. Used & Starter Gear New sells at 100%. Recently Forged Repairing takes 1/8 of the item cost in material, and value/100 days. For example, 15 days for plate, around 200 gp to repair. If Mending is used, scrap items are repaired into functional old items. Halving time on repair, unless additional replacement material is required.
Crafting materials are only interchangeable for money. Monster Parts may not be traded for magic items

Characters may not gift each other money or items at will. Characters within the same party may loan each other items during the course of a quest, trial, or other content, but must retrieve their belongings at the end. If your character would like to gift an item, you must first roleplay a justification for the gift, then submit the below report to #transcript for review. Gift Request Transcript Template​ Gifting Request Characters Involved: (Please @ any players involved) Item being gifted: Start: (Please link the start of your rp here) End: (Please link the end of your rp here) Summary: (Summarize your rp here as well as brief reasoning/justification for gifting) Siege weapon prices​ Ballista, 8,000gp Cannon (arcane), 20,000gp Cannon (powder), 18,000gp Suspended-Cauldron 4,000gp Mangonel 10,000gp Ram 4,000gp Siege-Tower 5,000gp Trebuchet 15,000gp Boilerdrak 25,000gp Gnomeflinger 22,000gp

For the sale of objects Any object valued under 200gp will not be taxed. Any object valued between 200gp and under 20,000gp will be taxed at 5%. Any object valued at 20,000 GP and above will be taxed at 20% tax. This applies per item, meaning bulk purchases are taxed based on the value of each individual object. Taxes only apply when transactions occur in civilized areas Tax Evasion Guidelines​ To evade taxes of any amount, you need to roleplay the transaction at a location that would prevent the enforcement of tax. Requirements below: Administratively, the roleplay must be linked into the ⁠transaction-log. Title the transaction as “Tax Evasion” for ease of search. Failure to do so may summon an angry pink god(dess) and void the transaction or enforce the tax and other demerits.

Base costs: Magic items will cost more if the base item is worth 100 gp or more will cost more accordingly Example: Double bladed scimitar (100 gp): +1 DBS is 500 gp Plate armor (1500 gp): +1 Plate armor is 5500 gp (these are the minimum prices)

CR 1-3 (Common): 20 Cr 4-8 (Uncommon): 80 Cr 9-13 (Rare): 400 Cr 14-18 (Very Rare): 2,000 Cr 19 (Legendary): 5,000 Quested Legendary Mats: can be sold for whatever price --------------------------------

Common: 60 Uncommon: 150 Rare: 300 Very Rare: 600 -------------------------------- No item can be sold at more than 250% of their base cost, unless there is approval from a Craftmaster independent of the transactional party. Finally, when any item is sold, it can only be bought back at the highest price of which it was sold. This requirement ends a month after the item is sold (to ease tracking).

How to Start Your Farm​ Choose what crops and land you will be using: Select a crop from the list available in the document below. Each crop has a maximum amount that can be planted per acre, a cost per pound, and a base yield stat which determines the multiplier of how much crops you gain at the end of a growing period. The minimum amount of land you must have to use the agriculture system is one acre, and each crop takes 90 days to plant and/or harvest. To use the agriculture system, you must select an amount of acres of land that you own to become farmland. Determine the Statistics of your Land: Ping Craftmaster in ⁠#crafting-ooc stating where geographically you are planting. You will be told the statistics of the land, including Disease Resistance, Pest Resistance, Ground quality, and weather. Multiply these together with the yield- this is your overall amount of crops gained. These statistics can be increased for the next growing period using roleplay and money investments submitted to the Craftmaster team. Find Workers: A hireling of any CR is required to work your land. Each hireling can work on 3 acres for the entire 90 days of a growing period. You must pay the deployed rate for the hireling for each day of the growing period. The amount of time and gold it takes to originally till an acre of land to be ready for crops is negligible. Any supplies and resources used in the growing process are included in the hireling’s pay. Submit a filled in Template to ⁠#crafting-submissions. Agriculture Report Template​ @you (PC Name) would like to grow <crop> in <Location> Total Yield: (Amount planted) x (Base Yield) x (Disease Resistance) x (Pest Resistance) x (Ground Quality) x (Weather) Total Acres: Hirelings Used: Start Date: End Date: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10NkTBM6IeO6RNk_rxIioqGoj6HV2f7u7Q0t-3evMGnM/edit?usp=sharing

Gathering​ Use Downtime to Gather Herbs, max usage 3x a day (uses 8 hours in a session). Note: You can no longer sacrifice adventuring time to harvest extra herbs. Choose one environment [Cave, Forest, Desert, Grasslands, Swamp] + Rarity [Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare] Roll Nature/Medicine/Arcana + Herbalism/Poisoner/Brewer/Alchemist Tool Prof Bonus (If proficient) --> DC scales depending on rarity of ingredient. Once check is completed, post in transcript using template found in pins of transcript . Craftmaster will roll for the herb gathered randomly depending on location chosen and DC rarity met. DCs for Enchantment Ingredients:​ Rarity DC Common DC 10 Uncommon DC 13 Rare DC 17 Very Rare DC 20 Targeted Gathering​ You can target herbs based on which potion you wish to make! If you are targeting a herb for a specific potion, use the Targeted gathering Template pinned in transcript If the herb you are searching for isn't in the environment you chose, you get nothing. If it is, a Craftmaster will roll the herb normally, and you only get the herb if the dice comply. The DCs for targeted gathering are as followed:​ Rarity DC Common DC 13 Uncommon DC 17 Rare DC 20 Very Rare DC 23 Bonuses:​ You can only target one herb per day until you have gathered 3 of that herb, at which point you may target for two herbs per day due to your familiarity. You cannot use help actions in herb gathering. Self-Buffs are allowed for now. Nat20 Rule: If you roll nat20 on the check (RAW Nat20 without modifiers and bonuses) you get 1 Extra Herb. Over10 Rule: If your total roll is 10 over the applicable DC you get 1 Extra Herb. Example, if your total roll for a rare is 31, you get 2 Herbs instead of 1. Nat20 and Over10 rules can both apply, to a max of 3 Herbs per roll.

Potions are brewed using herbs, each herb is used for a specific potion, the potion is hinted at in the description. Time, base Cost, Herb Requirement to brew: Rarity Time (Days) Cost Herb Requirement Common 2.5 25 gp 1 Herb Uncommon 5 100 gp 1 Herb Rare 12.5 1,000 gp 2 Herbs Very Rare 25 10,000 gp 3 Herbs Monster Part Substitution​ You can substitute 1 Herb for a monster part, however uncommon and higher potions need at least 1 Herb. Potion Rarity Monster CR Loot DC Common CR 1-3 DC 13 Uncommon CR 4-8 DC 17 Rare CR 9-13 DC 21 Very Rare CR 14-18 DC 24 Legendary CR 19+ DC 26 Bulk Brewing​ Bulk Brewing has a discount on overall cost now. For every 10 potions you make at a time, you get a 5% discount on cost, cap for the discount is 20%. Bulk Brewing also requires less herbs. For every 10 potions you brew, you only need 7x the amount of herbs for one potion of the same rarity. Example: 10 common potions of healing - 7 enchantment herbs needed. Time Reduction​ You get a 50% time reduction if you use double the amount of enchantment herbs for the potion. Sacrificing Potions: You can sacrifice one potion per brew. Lowers base time by half the time it takes to brew a potion of that rarity.

Barding is equipment made for creatures not Medium size. Barding can be either mundane or magical. The base cost of creating the item will be increased by the following modifier for each size above and below Medium: Size Cost Modifier Diminutive x 64 Tiny x 16 Small x 4 Large x 4 Huge x 16 Gargantuan x 64

Walls and floors are all considered to be 1 feet thick, a 1 foot by 1 foot by 1 foot cube of material is considered to be 1 unit. How to Build a Structure​ Determine the floor plan of your building. For example, you wish to build a 20 by 20 shack made of stone brick, the walls are say 8 feet high and for ease of calculation the roof is flat, there are no extra internal walls and is just open. If the floor is 2 feet thick, it will be 20 long x 20 wide x 2 thick = 800 units The ceiling is normal (1 feet thick) and is 400 units Walls are 8 feet high and 20 long x 8 high x 1 wide, and you have 4 of them, therefore they equate to 640 units The building is a total of 1840 units, and can now be priced and the time can be found accordingly. Base Construction Time​ Base Time: Units/100/number of workers = # workweeks it takes to construct. Workers​ Decide the wages you want to advertise to determine how many NPCs will work. A Craftmaster will roll only 1 time and that number is final. Cost (Per NPC/Day) Roll for Workers 5 gp 1d20 NPC Workers 10 gp 1d15 + 5 NPC Workers 15 GP 1d10 + 10 NPC Workers 20 GP 1d5 + 15 NPC Workers Note: You can do Craftmaster-approved roleplay to increase worker count, but what you roll is limited to what you can achieve without roleplay. Notes:​ On Elysium, the limit is 20 workers Limit is based off population, depending on where you want to build. Contact craftmasters for a different limit. You must decide on the wage before rolling for results If you have some kind of other material you plan on using, ping a @craftmaster Construction Material Costs​ Material Selected Cost (per Unit) Stone Brick 5 gp Low-End Wood 4 gp Mid-Range Wood 8 gp High-End Wood 12 gp Glass 10 gp Note: Materials not listed above can be taken on a case-by-case basis. Please ping Craftmaster for approval and costs of those materials. Elysium Map Relevant Information and Lot Purchasing Form​ Parcels are sold in 2,500 sq. ft. increments only. Please submit construction proposals to ⁠transcript in the following format: ***__Charter Request__*** @Loremaster @Craftmaster **Buyer:** @yourself (PC_Name) **Plot Size:** [dimensions of plot, in feet] **Construction Plans:** [description of what is being built, where on the island, physical appearance, etc.]

Unnamed NPCs can only work on mundane items, and building projects. These types of crafters require a Named NPC or PC to lead the project. Unnamed NPCs working on mundane equipment are required to be paid at least 25 gp a day. Named NPCs originate one of two ways; either through roleplay ran by a Dungeonmaster and approved by a Craftmaster, or when a PC retires. These types of crafters can lead their own projects, and can increase their magical crafting capabilities through means separate of both PCs and Unnamed NPCs. PCs are characters that are actively being controlled by a player. These types of crafters can lead their own projects, make their own decisions (unless given up by the player to a guild), and are limited in what they can craft based on rarity which is determined based on the level of the character. Magic Item Proficiency Requirements: A character needs to be proficient with the tools needed to craft an item and have access to the appropriate equipment. Everyone who collaborates needs to have the appropriate tool proficiency. You need to make any judgment calls regarding whether a character has the correct equipment. The following provides some examples. Herbalism Kit: Antitoxin, Potion of Healing Leatherworker's Tool: leather Armor, Boots Smith's Tools: Armor, Weapons Weaver's Tools: Cloaks, Robes Tinker's Tools; Wondrous Items Note: The above are just examples. If you can justify the use of a tool in a craft/project, it would be acceptable for that craft/project. Magical Crafting Subsection​ Any player characters (active or retired) involved with the crafting needs to meet a level requirement to craft items of certain rarities: Level 1-4: Uncommon and Below Level 5-10: Rare Level 11-16: Very Rare level 17 and up: Legendary Named NPC: To allow for Named NPC crafters to upgrade the rarities they can craft. A specific amount of crafts of a certain rarity must be made (listed below) as well as a Wisdom check (made by PC) following the final craft (DCs also listed below). Common -> Uncommon: 20 Common crafts with DC 15 Wisdom Check Uncommon -> Rare : 40 Uncommon crafts with DC 18 Wisdom Check Rare -> Very Rare: 60 Rare crafts with DC 20 Wisdom Check Very Rare -> Legendary: 80 Very Rare crafts with DC 22 Wisdom Check

When calculating time reduction, the order in which a player should calculate is as follows: Magic Item Sacrifice Magic Item Adept (MIA) Master Scrivener (MS) Workers Craft Roleplay Reduction Magic Item Sacrificing​ You can sacrifice one item per craft. Lowers base time by half the time it takes to craft an item of the rarity of the item sacrificed. Sacrificing an item that would make the craft instant instead results in the craft taking 1 day. Magic Item Adept​ An artificer only class feature that reduces both time and cost of crafting common and uncommon items. Master Scrivener​ A wizard only class feature that reduces both time and cost of scribing scrolls. Workers​ To a max of five; the more people working on a project, the quicker it gets done. To calculate this reduction method, you divide the base time by the amount of workers you have on the project. Players who have not received the @player role cannot assist with a craft as a worker Craft Roleplay Reduction​ Add the initial roleplay in the crafting submission. Additional roleplay regarding the craft, brew, or construction can be submitted in the crafting submissions channel. No XP or favor can be given out in the same request as time reduction. The Craftmaster approving the log, and any subsequent RP submissions that may follow, will determine how long it reduces by, to a max of three days per submission. No reduction can take the completion time below 1 day. Reductions are capped at a 25% total reduction to the original crafting time. Each roleplay request can reduce the log by more than three days, but this requires two or more Craftmaster approval.

You can add a + enchantment onto an existing magic item. This upgrade will boost the crafted item's rarity a tier up, starting at the higher rarity item. The item's rarity can't exceed legendary, and the + enchantment can't exceed +3. Example 1: Adding +1 to a Dragon Slayer Sword will make it Very Rare and +2 Example 2: Adding +1 to a Serpent Scale Armor will make it a Very Rare and +1 This upgrading process is limited to weapons and armors only.

You can re-forge the type of item you have according to the class and enchantment of the item. The class of item refers to the grouping allowed by the enchantment, found in parenthesis after the item type in its description. Whether that be simple/martial, melee/ranged, any, any kind of sword, etc. The enchantment of the item refers to the magical ability of the item. You can only re-forge an item to another item of the same class and enchantment. For example, a Dragon Slayer Longsword couldn't be re-forged into a Flame Tongue Greatsword, but it could be re-forged into a Dragon Slayer Rapier. Re-forge Cost: Half of the cost it takes to craft an item of that rarity. Re-forge Time: Half of the time it takes to craft an item of that rarity. Re-forging is only applicable with weapons and armor. Magic Item Adept feature works with re-forging.

Base costs: Magic items will cost more if the base item is worth 100 gp or more will cost more accordingly Example: Double bladed scimitar (100 gp): +1 DBS is 500 gp Plate armor (1500 gp): +1 Plate armor is 5500 gp (these are the minimum prices) **Leg Quested Mat Use and Acquisition Expansion** Acheron artifacts will be considered quested leg mats and leg mats to contribute to the formation of gravity drives. Transforming an Acheron artifact to a quested leg mat will alert enemies and players within Acheron. Gravity drives require one quested leg mat can you shove this in the crafting wiki

You can now find gainful employment within the city of Waterdeep (and abroad). This can be done in two ways, a weekly job or daily job. Daily Jobs​ Daily Jobs uses an alias in discord and can only be done once a day per PC, this also takes your downtime. To do the job, use the alias: !job skill Then link the result in #transaction-log with a short deception of what you did in character and the amount earned Weekly Jobs​ Part time jobs, such as casual work at a smithy or a bard playing for a tavern, will take up all of your downtime (meaning no crafting or learning skills) but still let you quest, hunt, and trial. Full time jobs pay more but in addition to no downtime you will no longer have time to trail, quest, or freely adventure. Q: How do you find employment/work? A: Provide a brief description of the job you’re looking to do, such as a part time job at an apothecary, then roll 2d20 and add your proficiency bonus if applicable (In this case it would be alchemy or herbalism). (2d20 + applicable mod) * 14 * Tier = gp/wk using all downtime. x2 for full time, but no hunts/trials as a result Part Time tier averages T1 = 294 T2 = 588 T3 = 882 T4 = 1,176 Weekly Job Report​ @ Player PC & Tier: Lanscan Tallfast, T2 Job: Bard at a the The Silken Slyph Tavern & Inn Roll: 22 Link to the roll: https://discord.com/channels/817263494818693170/817269893514395658/928341274916962386 Wages: Start Date: MM/DD/YYYY End Date: MM/DD/YYYY

Team involved: @Loremaster Hello lurkers! This update is an addendum to the previously released Hireling spreadsheet for NPC pricing. Utilizing this, you will have guidelines with which you may hire NPCs over time, up to a predetermined maximum amount, for whatever individual, group, or organizational needs you have. If there is confusion on how this works, please use the attached spreadsheet, or ask a @Loremaster. Contracting NPC Requirements: Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20 Total CR across all hired units is capped at CR = 30 Hiring occurs weekly, using a point deduction system (Hire Points) Points accrue at a rate of 1/week from the time interest is expressed, and equate to the Total CR that can be used to hire units Point deductions are based against the CR being hired. Example: Player currently has total of 5 Hire Points. The player can Hire any combination of humanoid creatures less than or equal to the total CR of 5. Spreadsheet for CR to Hire Points breakdown can be seen here: https://docs.google.com/file/d/1Qv2-Cna8BUpkpW0geMdIO68BIL-coSrd/edit?usp=docslist\_api&filetype=msexcel Please submit these hire requests to transcript and ping a @Loremaster for approval. Attunement and Magic Items for Hirelings Hirelings can equip and attune to magic items provided to them by their employer based upon their CR, as shown below: CR 1/8 - CR 1/2: Common (no attunement) CR 1 - CR 4: Uncommon (attunement up to 1 item) CR 5 - 10: Rare (attunement up to 2 items) CR 11 - 16: Very Rare (attunement up to 3 items) CR 17+: Legendary (attunement up to 3 items) If the hirelings statblock has an armor or weapon listed, they are treated as proficient with all weapons or armor of that same type (e.g. leather - light armor, Shortsword - martial weapons). If you have questions or concerns, please me know, and I will be working with existing groups/organizations to get you switched over to this new framework From #Patch-Notes​ Much discussion and collaboration has gone into the merger of Hireling system with the previously used Organizations system. They will now be brought under one framework, with some added rules for how groups and organizations will work under this system, how hirelings can be equipped with items from their employers, and some promising prospects for future updates. Individual & Group Hirelings The ability for individuals and established groups to hire NPCs to augment their personal or collaborative efforts will be broken into one of two categories, with slightly different considerations for each. Hirelings can be reskinned to represent any humanoid race or alignment, and can speak common by default. Contracting Requirements (Individual) Hiring updates occur once per week, using a point deduction system (Hire Points) Points accrue at a rate of 1/week, requiring an approved post from a Loremaster These points are logged via ⁠transcript and the total equates to the Total CR that can be used to hire units for that update. Point deductions are based on the CR being hired. CR 0 units count as CR 1/8 for this, there is a graph that breaks down these numbers in more detail. Individuals contracting NPCs will use the 'Deployed Monthly' rate, as opposed the normal Daily/Monthly rate. These expenses are logged via ⁠transaction-log after the update is approved by a Loremaster. These expenses occur at the 1st of every month. Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20 Total CR that can be hired is capped at CR 20 The screenshot below shows a week-by-week breakdown of how hire points can be spent on the corresponding CR. Contracting Requirements (Group/Organizational) Hiring updates occur once per week, using a point deduction system (Hire Points) Points accrue based upon the modifiers calculated for your group, from 1-10, requiring an approved post from a Loremaster. These points are logged via ⁠transcript and the total equates to the Total CR that can be used to hire units for that update. Publicity (popularity, reputation, goodwill) Accessibility (access, reach) Logistics (training, supplies, budget) Opportunity (job security, importance, need) Temp buffs (quests/significant events) Groups/Organizations consisting of multiple PCs behave as a single ‘entity’ for the sake of point accumulation and spending. Updates will be logged with a single PC representing the group. Point deductions are based on the CR being hired. CR 0 units count as CR 1/8 for this, there is a graph that breaks down these numbers in more detail. Groups/Organizations contracting NPCs will use the normal 'Monthly' rate. These expenses are logged via ⁠transaction-log after the update is approved by a Loremaster. These expenses occur at the 1st of every month. Maximum CR that can be hired as a single unit is capped at CR 20

Players are limited to three retired PC crafters at any one point. All retired PCs may do other allowed forms of downtime, but only three can craft at any one time. Reason: To prevent people from overpopulating their personal supply of crafters by making and retiring PCs over and over again.

If a player leaves the server, their characters can not be used to craft. If a character is retired and their sheet is not posted in ⁠retired-listings, they can not be used to craft. This change also removes the 3 month mandatory check-in between Guild Owner and Employee, because the assumption is the employee can leave the guild whenever they see fit. Note: If a craft has already been initiated, and the player or players involved in the craft leave the server, the craft will be completed on schedule.
When you are using a PC to craft (everyone aside from the 'starter'), you MUST pay them each a minimum of 25 GP per day of crafting. This includes your own PCs, if applicable.

Guild/organization stock and coin cannot be taken out of the guild or used in non-guild pursuits by the leaders and officers unless rules in its constitution grants them the power to do so. The rules being amendable are dependent on the guild/organization. Server default is yes, rules are amendable. Guild Legislation​ For sole leaders, if you have Player Characters working under you. It is required that changes to the guild constitution first be presented to all the players in employment for a vote, passing on at a majority. This will give them the chance to respond to changes, or at least fair notice. We know that a sole owner has significant authority of their enterprise, but this rule is in place in interest of providing a fun environment for all players.
Donations to Guilds or Player Organizations require Craftmaster Approval. Ping Craftmaster in all Guild or Player Organization donations. This does not include selling materials or items to guilds.

Class Retraining​ By spending 10 workweeks of downtime, a character can choose to replace one of their levels in one class with a level in another class. This time is reduced by a number of workweeks equal to the character’s ability modifier in the key ability of the new class. If their new class has more than one key ability, the characters lowest ability modifier should be used for this calculation. The character must have a minimum of 13 in the key abilities of both their current class and their new class They must have an instructor of at least 1 level higher (or be level 20) than your new level in the new class and must spend 50gp per week for the instructor and relevant supplies. Fighting Style Retraining​ (For Fighters, Rangers, Paladins, Blood Hunters, and College of Swords Bards only) By spending a week of downtime, you can choose one of the (insert class name here) fighting style you know and replace it with another fighting style from the (insert class name here) class. Feat / ASI Retraining​ By spending a week of downtime, you can choose to replace one Feat or ASI you qualify for with another Feat or ASI you qualify for. Post20 ASIs can be retrained only to ASIs, and Post20 Feats can be retrained only to Boons or Feats. Spell Retraining​ (For sorcerers, warlocks, bards and rangers only) By spending a week of downtime,you can choose one of the (insert class name here) spells you know and replace it with another spell from the (insert class name here) spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
Warlocks can spend 1 week of downtime to retrain one of their mystic arcanum spells for another spell that is applicable for that version of the mystic arcanum classfeat.

When you undergo retraining, you can submit an RP-XP request for roleplay related to the retraining and receive a reduction in the overall time spent retraining. Each RP-XP request is worth a 5% reduction, up to a maximum of 25%.

We get it, you can’t always plan your character’s lives in real time. That’s why we’ve designed Retroactive Downtime, which lets you apply unused downtime at a reduced wait to cover gaps in gameplay and incetivize coming back to TWR! Starting from the last date your PC used their downtime, you can now file a report to use 1/3 of the total days (rounded down) on a single goal or downtime activity with staff approval.

Players wishing to file for retroactive downtime must complete the report on the right and submit it to #transcript. Staff will determine the appropriate daily value for your character and resources and return the report with any important notes. Custom Retroactive Downtime​ We are also introducing a few new forms of “retroactive” downtime you can add to the report: General Adventuring: XP Bonus​ Characters who spend their time hunting, traveling, or otherwise generally adventuring receive bonus XP: Tier Bonus XP Cap (Per Day) 1 5 xp 2 20 xp 3 100 xp 4 200 xp Post-20 300 xp Service to a Deity: Favor Bonus​ Characters who spend time in service of a deity will be rewarded for their faith with favor: Tier Bonus Favor Cap (Per Day) 1 1 Favor 2 3 Favor 3 5 Favor 4 8 Favor Post-20 10 Favor The Career Path: Gold Bonus​ Through smart investments, performance bonuses, side hustles and promotions, business ownership, etc., you receive bonus Gold: Tier Bonus Gold Cap (Per Day) 1 5 gp 2 25 gp 3 50 gp 4 200 gp Post-20 250 gp Roleplay Bonuses​ Players who perform roleplay with themselves or others to justify their downtime may include a summary and link to the roleplay for additional rewards. Transcript Report: Retroactive Downtime​ 🕐 Retroactive Downtime Request 🕐 @(Player) Last Downtime Date: DD/MM/YYYY Retroactive Downtime: (Days since last downtime) / 3 = X Summary of Downtime: Type of a brief summary of your character’s actions during their time away. You may only select a single downtime option or project. Specifics: If you are selecting a specific downtime option as outlined in the source books, this document, or other TWR systems, include the report here using the “Retroactive Downtime” value above as the number of days spent. Then perform any rolls, checks, transactions, etc. as necessary here. You may also choose to perform more complicated projects such as starting a business, building a home, making friends in the form of NPCs, etc. through expanded roleplay. Staff Review: Craftmasters and Dungeonmasters will review the report and consider any complications, necessary materials, or other concerns and work with you to apply your downtime in a reasonable way. Approved By: @(DM or CM) Requirements to Complete: Any costs, roleplay requirements, or contingencies for the downtime to become official Plain Report​ 🕐 Retroactive Downtime Request 🕐 @(Player) Last Downtime Date: DD/MM/YYYY Retroactive Downtime: (Days since last downtime) / 3 = X Summary of Downtime: Specifics: Staff Review: Approved By: @(DM or CM) Requirements to Complete:

Settlement Endeavors allow characters to attract residents, workers, specialists, and families through roleplay and investment in a growing settlement.

A Sponsor is an individual who begins a Settlement Endeavor. There may be multiple Sponsors for the same Settlement. The sponsor need not personally appear. Narrating recruiters or employees, creating housing or employment, negotiating with communities, or hosting an event may qualify.

Each resident requires at least 25 sq. ft. of residential interior space. Empty land does not count, occupied space cannot be reused, and multiple floors count separately. Examples: 100 sq. ft. houses 4 residents; 400 houses 16; 900 houses 36; and 2,500 houses 100. Workshops, farms, shops, and public facilities provide employment or opportunity but only count as housing if residential space is included. The Endeavor must link its approved Charter Request or identify unused space in an existing approved structure.

An individual may recruit up to 5 residents per month. An established agency, organization, or player settlement may recruit 5 residents per participating player, to a maximum of 50 residents per month. Only distinct players who meaningfully contribute to that month’s Endeavor count toward its limit. The agency submits one combined monthly Endeavor through a single representative. Each character may participate in only one Settlement Endeavor per month. Unused recruitment does not carry over. A major quest or event may receive a one-time Craftmaster and Loremaster-approved exception. The requested population cannot exceed the settlement’s unused housing capacity.

Craftmasters confirm construction, housing, and available support. Loremasters approve the residents’ origins, culture, faction connections, and effect on the setting. Recruiting an established community, faction, or large migration requires approval before roleplay begins. Staff records the final residents and approved specialists gained. A successful Endeavor may gain any number from 1 up to its recruitment limit. An unsuccessful Endeavor gains 0.
Note where the residents will live, what work or opportunities are available, and how they will fit into the settlement. Requested specialists or communities should be listed here.

A settlement must pay 50 gp per resident each month for food and basic necessities. This includes food, clean water, medicine, clothing, fuel, sanitation, and common household supplies. Examples: 5 residents cost 250 gp; 15 cost 750; 30 cost 1,500; 50 cost 2,500; and 100 cost 5,000. Upkeep may be paid with coin or an equal value of appropriate food and supplies. Any number of players, Ventures, or organizations may contribute. Residents maintained through another system, such as paid hirelings, are not counted again. Paying upkeep grants no ownership or control over residents and creates no exclusive supplier rights. If upkeep is missed, the settlement cannot begin another Endeavor. After two consecutive missed months, 1 resident leaves for every 10 unsupported residents, minimum 1.

Settlement residents are independent NPCs and cannot be commanded by a sponsor. Anyone recruited for personal service, military use, or direct control must use the appropriate hireling or follower rules. Residents do not automatically become soldiers, controlled NPCs, or sources of passive income.

documents.t: Training Downtime​ Characters can perform activities to train and practice in their free time, those who do not wish to hunt can spend time training themselves as well, this could be tinkering and experimenting for Artificers, praying and studying for Clerics, scribing and practicing spells for Wizards, sparring for fighters, and stealthing around for rogues, all forms of training are applicable and make no mechanical difference Characters can choose to spend 5 Hunting Tags or expend 8 hours of downtime in training which awards experience points to reflect the development of skills. Players who choose to roleplay the lessons will be awarded with additional RPXP as per usual Tier | XP Per Day (not RPXP) 1 | 100 xp 2 | 250 xp 3 | 500 xp 4 | 1,000 xp Post-20 | 2,000 xp

Business empires and peddler wagons. Player characters can now obtain money, experience, and more by roleplaying their business ventures. The owner of a venture, need not be personally involved. Narration of employees and the setting or providing venues for an event qualifies for gain. Investment: The value of things committed to make coin. Capital is the stuff that are not consumed in the venture. General examples: land, property, and facilities. Gain: Scaling from 0 to 200% of the investment. Graded by pinks and bookworms. Because we do not capture depreciation here, more weight will be given to expended coin than capital, which can be reused. Do not be surprised if your million gold cargo ship does not get you 1.5 million in returns. Distribution: Player notes the percentage of gain given to people involved. If you wish for particular items, materials, or other gains that are not coin, do it here and mark to whom it should go to. Pinks/bookworms will revise this section which tells the player(s) what was earned. Including RPXP.

documents.t: At 11th level, you can now store a spell in an object. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch one simple or martial weapon or one item that you can use as a spellcasting focus, and you store a spell in it, choosing a 1st- or 2nd-level spell from the artificer spell list that requires 1 action to cast (you needn't have it prepared). You may upcast a 1st level spell to use a 2nd level slot, if previous conditions are applicable. (edited)

Experimental Elixir Drinking an Elixir: As a Bonus Action, a creature can drink the elixir or administer it to another creature within 5 feet of itself. You can create additional experimental elixirs by expending a spell slot of 1st level or higher (to a maximum of 5th level) for each one. When you do so, you use your action to create the elixir in an empty flask you touch, and you choose the elixir's effect from the Experimental Elixir table. Experimental Elixir d6 Effect 1 Healing. The drinker regains a number of hit points equal to 2d4 + your Intelligence Modifier (+2d4 hit points restored for every spell slot level above 1st) 2 Swiftness. The drinker's walking speed increases by 10 feet for 1 hour. (+10 feet walking speed for every two spell slot levels above 1st) 3 Resilience. The drinker gains a +1 bonus to AC for 10 minutes. (+1 bonus to AC for every two spell slot levels above 1st) 4 Boldness. The drinker can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to every attack roll and saving throw they make for the next minute. 5 Flight. The drinker gains a flying speed of 10 feet for 10 minutes. (+10 feet flying speed for every two spell slot levels above 1st) 6 Transformation. The drinker's body is transformed as if by the Alter Self spell. The drinker determines the transformation caused by the spell, the effects of which last for 10 minutes. Restorative Reagents Whenever a creature drinks an experimental elixir you created, the creature gains temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier plus your Artificer level

For the duration your reach increases by 5 ft, and if you are smaller then large you become large, along with anything your wearing. This spell channels vitality into plants within a specific area. There are two possible uses for the spell, granting either immediate or long-term benefits. If you cast this spell using 1 action, choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100-foot radius centered on that point become thick and overgrown with a year's worth of growth. A creature moving through the area must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves. Any harvestable plant in this area produces a poor quality harvest for the next [month]. Additional casts in this manner will regrow damaged areas to maintain the rough terrain, but grants no additional agricultural benefits beyond what was granted in the first cast until the cooldown period has elapsed. You can exclude one or more areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected. If you cast this spell over 8 hours, you enrich the land. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 1 year. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested then return to their normal production levels. When the land is enriched this way, casting Plant Growth in a attempt to enrich the soil again within one year and six months after the initial casting will grant no additional agricultural benefits.
