This is similarly done with gestalt, in which the format is G#L#, where G represents your Paragon stage, and L represents your current level, up to 26. This can be similarly done with tiers. After Ascension:​ When a pre-existing character begins their first ascension cycle (starting to level a new class system) or converts from gestalt, they can choose to adjust their base ability scores through point buy and may choose to swap current feats, asi, and p20 asi at no penalty. This must be submitted through transcript Gestalt and Ascension Interaction:​ Gestalt or Ascension can be chosen when a character finishes p20 or completes a paragon cycle (finishes p20 on another class system). In doing so, a character may choose to Gestalt as a way to prestige and change through their class choices, though would still level according to their paragon cycle number. For example, a P3L0 (has finished this cycle but has not started a new one) may choose to Gestalt, and become a G4L1, where they may again choose to move back into ascension after leveling to p20. Changes to Gestalt System:​ Gestalt would remain with the ability to adjust stats upon reset, as stated previously. In addition, they would no longer be required to level their base class as they would normally, and may choose to level a different class instead. Retroactive Adjustments:​ For those who choose to stay in gestalt, characters may receive retroactive rewards. Firstly, a character may adjust base stats and character levels, submitting a new sheet to transcript along with the old (make a copy and do changes from there) to be used as a reference. Additionally, players may reclaim downtime for changing class levels for characters or training characters, since the gestalt system was first introduced. Players must submit the time they would receive to transcript, with relevant links, where they would then be able to use that time in the future. Players may complete this same process for the gold cost. Note:​ All character changes must be done through the transcript. It is recommended that you make a copy of your old gsheet when adjusting things. PART 6 | GESTALT PRESTIGE Gestalt Prestige System This is a variant to the typical prestige system, and while it may grant great boons it also has great restrictions as well. When you Gestalt Prestige, you must post in #transcript including both the new and original sheets for reference. Once approved, the new sheet will be posted in #3-gestalt-pc-links Please note this system is still in playtesting and is subject to change at any time Gestalt Overview All Gestalt PCs begin at level 1 Upon gestalt prestige you can select a class to level alongside your current one. The starting proficiencies, skills, and other benefits are granted to the character. See Here for a detailed explanation of how class features stack. When you level up, both classes level simultaneously, and you gain the benefits from both. Put simply, you have build A which was prestiged and locked in, getting added to build B. This is similar to if you had two separate characters who were merged into one. ASIs granted through level ups can be reassigned. Original class and subclass levels are locked in. This process can be repeated, allowing for a singular character to slowly grow in power over the years as they grow more involved in the world at large. Cumulative Level Cumulative Level is the total number of levels from all your classes combined. Cumulative Level is used to calculate what trials, hunts, and quests you can be involved in. Current Level Current Level is the current base level of the character and calculated as it would be normally, as though you were leveling a normal character. The Current Level is what is used to calculate proficiency bonus, character progression, and RP experience gains. Things that scale based on level use your Current Level. Gestalt Reversion At any time a character can revert a gestalt prestige. This will reset the character to a level 1 class of their choice akin to a normal prestige, provide zero cosmetic and stat benefits, and allow the character to once again gain experience from trials, hunts, etc. The character will then be locked out of the gestalt prestige system for 6 months. This can be done at any time and at any level. Restrictions Class levels do not mix between Gestalt Prestiges. Each prestige is treated as a unique PC build. To qualify a PC must be fully leveled, meaning level 20 with all post 20 levels completed. Gestalt PCs cannot gain experience from hunts, trials, DM-XP, Transcript-XP, etc. They can only gain experience from RP-XP or Quests. In quests that involve combat, while you will receive XP for the RP, you will receive no XP for the creatures killed. Gestalt PCs may not change their race, background, Racial ASIs, class or subclass choice, or anything else regarding the basis of the character which was set during their initial creation. On level up, the initial class chosen will follow the same build path (for example Fighter Champion) and multi class level split (if applicable) that the character had PRIOR to that prestige. Gestalt hit dice are restricted to the two highest hit dice per level (as opposed to gestalts getting all hit dice per level). Rather than gaining the save proficiencies of all classes, Gestalts choose one strong save and one weak save from the options given to them by their classes: Strong Saves Weak Saves DEX STR CON INT WIS CHA Any changes to the locked classes or subclasses are allowed and follow the normal retraining rules based on the level of the class being retrained. Due to the documentation required for this system, character sheets must be handled in G-Sheets. ASIs stack, but do not stack past the normal cap of 20 unless otherwise specified. Stats may not exceed 30 for any reason. You can not take the same feat multiple times unless otherwise specified. Feats that scale based on level are calculated based on your Current Level not your Total Level. Gestalt PCs may attune to any item they own, however, Gestalt PCs may not use items which exceed their “Current Level” during hunts or trials with non-Gestalt PCs. Gestalt PCs may choose to join hunts above their Current Level, but not if non-Gestalt PCs are present. This does not affect Body Retrieval Hunts. If a gestalt hunting party is a mix of tiers, they can not recover a body. Spell save DCs and spellcasting follow multi classing rules. Spell Save DCs and Spell Attack Bonuses calculate based on the class providing the spell. Combining Gestalt Classes Class Features, Spell Slots, Proficiencies and Stat Changes generally stack unless otherwise specified. Exceptions The following features do NOT stack when creating a Gestalt PC: Proficiency Bonus Multi Attack Unarmored Defense Duplicated Paladin Auras Movement speed increases from duplicate sources. Bladesong, and other features with limited uses such as rage, do not get doubled buffs but do get a increased number of uses. Gestalt FighterWatermark Gestalt/Wish Patch: tl;dr - Introducing a very arduous method to regain wish through a whole gestalt prestige and questline using a Post20 Blessing/Boon Slot. Requirements Gestalt prestige into a spellcasting class that also learns wish Complete self RP and DM-led quests (at least 4) throughout your prestige that meet the following guidelines Integrate with an existing group of worshipers for a particular deity Receive character references from leadership within the church/group Reach a level that would otherwise grant you wish from your prestige class Travel to the chosen deity’s home plane and petition their aid directly with offerings and references prepared Donate at least 2 items to the god directly, sacrificing them to prove your devotion. One item must be of legendary power and the second must be of great personal importance to your PC. Perform a quest for that god directly, run by a Dungeonmaster and approved by at least 2 more DMs or LMs Regaining Wish Once all of the requirements have been met and your PC is eligible for a Post20 Boon/Blessing Slot, the God will decide whether or not to grant you the Blessing of Forgiveness: Blessing of Forgiveness - This blessing removes one existing instance of permanent loss of wish. Once a creature has received this blessing, they can no longer receive it from the same deity. Note: It may not be possible to convince any other gods to grant this blessing or you may attract significant attention from your previous god if so. It would require unfathomable time and effort to regain wish a second time.
Sims Simulacrums are considered NPCs. Paragons will not be able to earn rpxp and quest xp by way of proxy

Class Retraining​ By spending 10 workweeks of downtime, a character can choose to replace one of their levels in one class with a level in another class. This time is reduced by a number of workweeks equal to the character’s ability modifier in the key ability of the new class. If their new class has more than one key ability, the characters lowest ability modifier should be used for this calculation. The character must have a minimum of 13 in the key abilities of both their current class and their new class They must have an instructor of at least 1 level higher (or be level 20) than your new level in the new class and must spend 50gp per week for the instructor and relevant supplies. Fighting Style Retraining​ (For Fighters, Rangers, Paladins, Blood Hunters, and College of Swords Bards only) By spending a week of downtime, you can choose one of the (insert class name here) fighting style you know and replace it with another fighting style from the (insert class name here) class. Feat / ASI Retraining​ By spending a week of downtime, you can choose to replace one Feat or ASI you qualify for with another Feat or ASI you qualify for. Post20 ASIs can be retrained only to ASIs, and Post20 Feats can be retrained only to Boons or Feats. Spell Retraining​ (For sorcerers, warlocks, bards and rangers only) By spending a week of downtime,you can choose one of the (insert class name here) spells you know and replace it with another spell from the (insert class name here) spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
Warlocks can spend 1 week of downtime to retrain one of their mystic arcanum spells for another spell that is applicable for that version of the mystic arcanum classfeat.

When you undergo retraining, you can submit an RP-XP request for roleplay related to the retraining and receive a reduction in the overall time spent retraining. Each RP-XP request is worth a 5% reduction, up to a maximum of 25%.

We get it, you can’t always plan your character’s lives in real time. That’s why we’ve designed Retroactive Downtime, which lets you apply unused downtime at a reduced wait to cover gaps in gameplay and incetivize coming back to TWR! Starting from the last date your PC used their downtime, you can now file a report to use 1/3 of the total days (rounded down) on a single goal or downtime activity with staff approval.

Players wishing to file for retroactive downtime must complete the report on the right and submit it to #transcript. Staff will determine the appropriate daily value for your character and resources and return the report with any important notes. Custom Retroactive Downtime​ We are also introducing a few new forms of “retroactive” downtime you can add to the report: General Adventuring: XP Bonus​ Characters who spend their time hunting, traveling, or otherwise generally adventuring receive bonus XP: Tier Bonus XP Cap (Per Day) 1 5 xp 2 20 xp 3 100 xp 4 200 xp Post-20 300 xp Service to a Deity: Favor Bonus​ Characters who spend time in service of a deity will be rewarded for their faith with favor: Tier Bonus Favor Cap (Per Day) 1 1 Favor 2 3 Favor 3 5 Favor 4 8 Favor Post-20 10 Favor The Career Path: Gold Bonus​ Through smart investments, performance bonuses, side hustles and promotions, business ownership, etc., you receive bonus Gold: Tier Bonus Gold Cap (Per Day) 1 5 gp 2 25 gp 3 50 gp 4 200 gp Post-20 250 gp Roleplay Bonuses​ Players who perform roleplay with themselves or others to justify their downtime may include a summary and link to the roleplay for additional rewards. Transcript Report: Retroactive Downtime​ 🕐 Retroactive Downtime Request 🕐 @(Player) Last Downtime Date: DD/MM/YYYY Retroactive Downtime: (Days since last downtime) / 3 = X Summary of Downtime: Type of a brief summary of your character’s actions during their time away. You may only select a single downtime option or project. Specifics: If you are selecting a specific downtime option as outlined in the source books, this document, or other TWR systems, include the report here using the “Retroactive Downtime” value above as the number of days spent. Then perform any rolls, checks, transactions, etc. as necessary here. You may also choose to perform more complicated projects such as starting a business, building a home, making friends in the form of NPCs, etc. through expanded roleplay. Staff Review: Craftmasters and Dungeonmasters will review the report and consider any complications, necessary materials, or other concerns and work with you to apply your downtime in a reasonable way. Approved By: @(DM or CM) Requirements to Complete: Any costs, roleplay requirements, or contingencies for the downtime to become official Plain Report​ 🕐 Retroactive Downtime Request 🕐 @(Player) Last Downtime Date: DD/MM/YYYY Retroactive Downtime: (Days since last downtime) / 3 = X Summary of Downtime: Specifics: Staff Review: Approved By: @(DM or CM) Requirements to Complete:

In the ancient epochs, when the world was young and the weave of magic was still being shaped, the gods and primordial forces sought to leave their mark upon the mortal realm. They imbued certain objects with Runes of their essence, creating artifacts that resonated with the very souls of those who wielded them. These are the Soulbound Items. A Soulbound Item is more than just a tool; it is a companion, a reflection of the bond between the bearer and the object. To attune to such an item is to forge a pact, intertwining one's fate with the artifact's power. As the wielder grows in strength and experience, so too does the Soulbound Item, awakening latent abilities and evolving in response to the challenges faced together. However, this bond is not without its trials. The path to unlocking a Soulbound Item's full potential is fraught with challenges, requiring the bearer to prove their worth and commitment. Only through perseverance, valor, and a deep connection can the true power of the Soulbound Item be realized.
A Player Character can only ever be attuned to one Soulbound Item The Item is a relic

Each Soulbound Item has its progression on the relevant Item Progression table At certain levels the weapon gains one of 4 types of features, Base, Ability, Unique and Runes. Each feature will have options to choose from. For Ability and Unique features, The player can decide whether to take a Novice Rank option or to promote an previously chosen option to the next rank Runes provide minor benefits, where some Runes you need more than 1 before unlocking its benefits When you choose an option as part of a feature you cannot choose that option again, other to promote it, unless it's stated otherwise. Ability and Unique feature ranks are constrained limited by the strength of its owner. To unlock an Expert feature the owner must be level 11 or higher, to unlock a Master feature they must be level 17 or higher The Weapon can at no point be at a higher level than it's owner Item Leveling​ While the item is attuned to a character, any experience that the player gains while attuned to the item is split 50/50 between the player and their soulbound item The XP will be scaled to the item's level via an alias. This includes XP from random hunts, dungeons, raids and quests. It is the players choice if up to 50% of RPXP goes to the weapon Example: If a level 8 Player gets 5000XP for Killing a Monster in a hunt and the item is also level 8, the Player and the Item each gets 2500XP If the weapon was at level 5, Player would get 2500XP which is 18% of XP Required to level to level 9. Thus the Item will get 18% of the exp required to go from level 5 to level 6, which is 1350 XP. When a player caps their level, the Item will still get 50% of the Exp that the player would have received This seems like complicated math, but there will be an alias to take care of all that Paragons: 50% of the experience gained from non-hunt combat participation can still go towards the weapon, this will be scaled for the Weapons level Paragon's Soulbound Items receive 50% of the Experience they would have gotten from combat. This includes Non-targetted hunts, Delves, Trials and Raids

The secret of creating a soulbound item has been unlocked, but as the magic is tied to the wielder and not the crafting they can only be crafted at its common stage. In lieu of choosing an uncommon item tied to the backstory of a submitted character, a player can choose a Soulbound* item, with the item starting at the same level of the Character, however this should be covered in the backstory Soulbound Items can be traded, but they will start at level 1 for a new PC and progress will be reset. For all intents and purposes when being traded, they use common item selling values.

By spending 1 workweek of downtime a Level feature can be retrained to a different option for that level. Only a single level can be retrained at a a time If you are Master of item Feature A, and want to retrain the weapon into a Journeyman of Path B and Path A, you will spend 1 workweek to go to Expert Path A and Novice Path B and then another workweek to reach Journeyman Path A and Journeyman Path B
A soulbound weapon can be reset at anytime. This does mean that that it restarts at level 1, and any progress or experience it gained will be lost.
Players are Encouraged to Homebrew their own Unique Features and Runes via Homebrew System & Index, this will expand the options for other players as well
As this is a new system, it may receive some balancing updates, either with nerf, buffs or sideways adjustments. Participation in this system acknowledges that your Item may change.

To carry a soulbound ward is to carry more than protection — it is a covenant between bearer and bulwark. These wards are not merely hammered plates or shaped wood; they are vessels of resolve, tempered by sacrifice and sealed with spirit. At first they guard as any armor or shield might, but as the bond deepens, the ward awakens — answering the bearer’s instincts, hardening in defiance, softening in stealth, or shining in defense of others. In time, the warrior is no longer clad in armor, but in a living testament of their soul’s endurance. To wield a conduit is to place your soul in the current of the unseen. A staff, gem, or relic can be bound not by chains, but by resonance—its lattice aligned with the bearer’s essence. At first, it channels spells as any focus would, but soon the conduit hums with hidden voices, amplifying thought, bending the weave, answering only to the one who claimed it. By journey’s end, mage and conduit are indistinguishable: the caster’s will flows as lightning, and the relic itself becomes the echo of their soul. A Soulbound focus can be any focus as determined by the Spellcasting feature of class. However the Owner can only attune to it if the item is an acceptable focus. This does include instruments and tools as well. If the player character can use a weapon as a spellcasting focus, they can choose whether to use it as a soulbound focus or weapon. However once the choice is made the item will be locked into either a soulbound focus or soulbound weapon. For example if a player decided to make their weapon a soulbound focus, the progression is locked into conduit and focus abilities. Spell Save DC granted by class items do not stack with this focus. The Spell Save DC and spell attack bonus only applies if using the focus to cast. As the Soulbound Item grows in power, etchings, runes or engraving may appear on it, this will either directly confer benefits, or in combination with other runes provide additional benefits.

These Runes can be used on weapon, armor, shields and foci: Reclamation Rune - You can return the item to your hand (or your body in the case of armor) as an action. Quick Reclamation Rune - You can return the item to your hand (or your body in the case of armor) as a bonus action, requires Reclamation Rune Glamour Rune - You can freely change the appearance of the item as an action. Compass Rune - While holding or wearing the item, you can determine the direction of true north, or the direction to a creature of which you speak its name. Echo Rune - You can cast the message cantrip while the item is on your person. Skill Runes - Once the item has accumulated two skill Runes, you gain proficiency in one skill of your choice while attuned to the item. An item can take skill Runes more than two times, and grant a new skill for every two of them it has accumulated. Shifting Rune - Once the item has two shifting Runes, over the course of a long rest, you can move the properties of the item to another of the same category, in your possession, making the new item your soulbound item. For example, you can move the properties of a soulbound dagger onto a mundane spear, receiving a soulbound spear. Shining Rune - The item sheds bright light out 10 feet, and dim light another 10 feet. This Rune can be taken a second time, doubling the radius of the light. Specialization Rune - Once an item has accumulated four specialization Runes, the item gains one level of any path, ward, or conduit. Intricate Rune - Once an item has accumulated four intricate Runes, the item gains one point to spend on any base feature. Mnemonic Rune (2x) – The item can “store” one memory you designate. At 2 Mnemonic Runes, you can replay it vividly. Expertise Runes - Once the item has accumulated two skill Runes, and two expertise Runes, you can add double your proficiency to the skill Rune skill, instead of normal proficiency. Awakening Rune - When you have two Awaking Runes, your weapon gains sentience. See link for detail information Awakening Rune

These Runes can only be taken on weapons: Twin Rune - When you have 2 Twin Runes, as a bonus action, you may split your weapon into two identical light versions for two-weapon fighting. They recombine as a bonus action, only works with weapons with the light property. Each of these weapons function as your Soulbound weapon, but still only requires one attunement slot. Master Reclamation Rune - Immediately after hitting or missing, the weapon flies back to your hand, this requires a Quick Reclamation Rune, Thrown Property and a Level 12+ Soulbound weapon Identical Rune -When you have 2 Identical runes and 2 Twin Runes, as a bonus action, you may split your weapon into two identical versions for two-weapon fighting. They recombine as a bonus action. It only works if your soulbound weapon is light, versatile or lacks the heavy property. Hunter’s Rune - While attuned, you can spend 1 minute studying a creature’s tracks or remnants to learn the direction it traveled within the past 24 hours. Sanguine Rune - Once per short rest, when you reduce a creature to 0 HP, you get THP equal to your Path Die. Dueling Spirit Runes - With 2 Deuling Spirit Runes, while fighting with the weapon in one hand and no other weapon or shield in the other, you gain +1 AC. With 4 invested, increase it to +2 AC. Thrown Rune - After taking this rune a second time, your Weapon gains the following thrown properties based on its properties: Finesse: 30/60 Heavy: 10/20 Else: 20/40 Additionally, if the weapon already has the thrown property, you instead add these distances to the weapon's base distances. Each additional time you take this rune after the second, you add the following distances: Finesse: 10/20 Else: 5/10

These Runes can only be taken on Armor or Shields: Defiant Rune – When you have 2 Defiant Runes, Once per long rest, when reduced to 0 HP while wearing the ward, you drop to 1 HP instead. Aegis Rune – When you have 2 Aegis Runes and you succeed on a saving throw against a spell, you can use your reaction to grant advantage to one ally within 10 feet against the same effect. Mirrorplate Rune – As a reaction once per short rest, impose disadvantage on an attack against you. Beacon Runes – When you have 2 Beacon Runes, allies within 5 feet gain +1 on saving throws against being frightened. At 4 Runes, the aura extends to 10 feet and grants advantage instead. Masterwork Rune - If you have 3 Masterwork Runes, you can upgrade your armor to highest tier armor of its type, any light armor, becomes studded leather, medium armor becomes half-plate and heavy armor becomes plate.

These Runes can only be taken on a focus: Sigil Rune – While holding the conduit, you can inscribe temporary glowing runes that last 1 hour. You may leave one “mark” at a time that sheds dim light in 5 feet. Spellkeeper Rune – You may store a cantrip in the conduit each long rest. You can cast it once as if you knew it, you can take this Rune again. If you have more than 1 you can store a spell you know during a long rest. The maximum level of spell you can store is equal to the number of Spellkeeper Runes minus 1. Regardless of how many Runes you have, you can only store 1 spell, and you can cast the spell without expending a spell slot. Scryer’s Rune – Once per long rest, you can use the conduit as a divining rod, giving you advantage on a single Wisdom (Perception) or (Survival) check. Resonance Runes – (Requires 2+) When you cast a spell, faint motes of energy linger. Allies within 5 feet gain +1 to their next attack roll. At 4 resonance Runes, the bonus is +1d4 instead.

documents.t: This is the general process through which our staff process any complaints or necessary review of a player's actions.

In the event that a Warning or strike is needed, the person first calling for a vote will create the poll in the Moderator Votes thread with a Moderator role ping, a brief description and a link to the comment. A 24 hour period will be given for moderators to discuss or vote. At the end of the 24 hours, or a majority is reached whichever comes first, the Moderator creating the poll will issue the action to the player and post in #The-Strike-Zone.

In the event a player incurs a 3rd strike, the moderator issuing the strike will instead issue the ban message from the template, ban the player, and make the record in the strike zone. If it is for a major event, or other concern, any moderator may open a discussion and call for a vote. Once the vote is open with the ping, the issue is decided as soon as there is a majority vote or super majority vote either direction. The three strike process may be bypassed if especially toxic or repeated inappropriate behavior is present, to the discretion of a supermajority of the Mods. A supermajority is 70% of available persons voting in favor of a particular position. A majority vote is required for Moderators to escalate such a case to Admins for final vote approval to ban or not. IF a Supermajority for Ban is reached by Moderators then the moderator starting the vote will ban the player, record the reason in Strike Zone, and ping admins with a summary so they’re aware.

A PC may attempt to tame animals over an extended period of time. Taming Check​ Check: Wisdom (Animal Handling) Tame DC: 15 + (2 * CR) (minimum 11) Time: 1 full day of calm interaction (one day of downtime) Initial Tame​ Before training begins, the creature must first be made non-hostile through patience, calmness, or courage. Roll Result Natural 20 Start at 25% Bond Progress Success Creature becomes non-hostile and open to training Fail by 5 or less You fail to train the creature, you may retry after 1 day Fail by 5 or more You fail to train the creature, you may retry after 3 days Natural 1 The creature flees or attacks, you may retry after 1 week Long-Term Bond Training​ Each day requires 8 hours of focused interaction. You can train only one creature at a time. Each success adds your roll to a cumulative total. Roll Result Natural 20 Add roll plus 10% of total progress threshold Success You Progress your bond with the creature Fail by 5 or less Your bond with the creature does not progress Fail by 5 or more The creature refuses training, you may retry after 3 days Natural 1 The creature flees or attacks, you may retry after 1 week Progress cannot fall below your current bond stage unless broken by neglect or narrative reason. Bond Progression​ Bond Stage Progress Threshold Non-Hostile Success on Initial Tame Sociable 10 + (10 * CR) Basic Commands Stay. Come. Stop. 15 + (15 * CR) Complex Commands Dodge. Attack X creature. Hide. 20 + (20 * CR) Mounted / Complex Tasks Scout X area. Return to X location. Find X person. 25 + (25 * CR) Example: A CR 3 beast needs 80 total progress to reach Complex Commands. Once a stage is reached, it remains permanent unless broken through RP.

Proper care sustains trust. Food Creature Size Daily Cost Tiny 10gp Small 30gp Medium 50gp Large 100gp Huge 150gp Gargantuan 200gp Unique Diets: Costs may be altered at DM Discretion Shelter: Will be determined by DM Luxury Care: Double Daily Cost Care Factors​ One day without care: Lose 10% Progress Two days without care: Creature may flee and reset to 0% Luxury Care: After 3 days of Luxury Care you gain advantage on the next training roll

Class/Sub-class Benefit Ranger (Any) Advantage on Initial Tame for beasts with CR level beasts with CR ≤ half proficiency bonus Ranger (Beast Master) Advantage on Initial Tame for equal to or less than half your ranger Ranger (Drakewarden) Advantage on Initial Tame for draconic creatures or wyrmlings with CR equal to or less than half your level Druid (Any) +2 to one Animal Handling check per long rest; reduce daily food cost by 25% Druid (Circle of the Shepherd) Add 1d4 once per day to a training check. Barbarian (Totem Warrior) Advantage when taming beasts matching your Totem Spirit * Only one class bonus applies at a time.​

Beasts & Monstrosities comprised of Beasts (ex: Griffon, Hippogriff) Subject to DM discretion. A number of monsters that may technically fit the criteria may not be tamable for lore reasons, or may otherwise be inaccessible due to where they may be located. Young Griffin (CR 0, ¼, 1) Griffon (CR 2) Owlbear (CR 3) Amphisbaena (CR ½) Peryton (CR 2) Kamadan (CR 4) Death Dog (CR 1) Shadow Mastiff (CR 2) Giant Strider (CR 1) Skyjek Roc (CR 2) Two-Headed Owlbear (CR 3) Hippogriff (CR 1) Giant Ice Toad (CR 3) Two-Headed Cerberus (CR 2) Snowy Owlbear (CR 3)

It must be reasonable for the creature to be tamed, per DM discretion. It must make sense within the context of TWR lore, per DM discretion. The creatures you can potentially tame are limited by the CR. In order to have the skill necessary to safely handle a creature, you must be capable of hitting the initial tame DC through just a straight animal handling roll without additional modifiers from items, spells, abilities, etc. Maximum Tamable CR = (5 + Your Base Animal Handling Modifier) / 2 Creatures with legendary or mythic abilities can not be tamed. Creatures with an INT of 1 can not be tamed. Creatures with an INT of 4+ can not be tamed. The initial tame, and subsequent checks, must be RPed for and submitted in transcript. For CR 1+ The initial tame must occur in a mini-quest or RPed targeted hunt run by DM. A DM can not run their own quest if they are attempting to tame a creature. For any creatures intended as a mount, the initial tame must occur in a mini-quest or RPed targeted hunt run by DM. A DM can not run their own quest if they are attempting to tame a creature. Purchasable domesticated mounts are an exception, and can be purchased as normal. No more than 1 creature can be tamed per day. Exceptions may exist for things such as domesticated animals, per discretion of the DM. Only creatures at least one size larger than a PC are mountable. Owl-Bear Taming Example Steps​ Go on a mini quest hosted by a DM. RP to find and convince the Owl-Bear that you are both not food and non hostile. CR3 creature, so DC 30 animal handling check for an adult Owl-Bear. Upon success, it will be non hostile but still aggressive. Cumulative DC of 300. The daily RPed animal handling checks would be added together. With an average roll of 10, with the +10 modifier required to initially tame the creature, it would take 15 days in real life of daily checks and RP to tame the creature. At 75 points, it would become sociable At 150 points, it would accept simple commands At 225 points, it would accept complex commands and barding At 300 points, it would accept complex tasks and be mountable To be updated
The creature acts on its own initiative. You control it as you would a summon RAW from spells such as Conjure Animals.

documents.t: Because of the inherent danger of things such as meteor swarms, when you are mounted the creature shares your HP. If you fall to zero HP, your mount falls to 1 HP, you are dismounted if on land, and if it is a flying creature it begins to crashland at 60ft/round. For the purposes of movement, the mount replaces your move speed(s). HP when dismounting: When you dismount, if your HP is lower than the mount's HP, the mount will adopt the same current HP as you. If you choose to have the mount attack, take any action, or otherwise treat it as a separate creature, ignore points 1~4 and it will be treated as a normal mount RAW. Mounted Combatant Feat interaction​ Under this system you can use either RAW and risk damage to the mount or the alternative rules in the Animal Taming doc. If you're using the alternative rules only point 1 of the feat pertaining to advantaged against creatures is applicable, the other two are nullified.

The recipient must be capable of hitting the initial tame DC to be capable of controlling the creature in any way. By default, the bond level resets to zero. If you are proficient in Animal Handling, it resets to 25%. If you have expertise in Animal Handling, it resets to 50%
If your tamed creature dies and is revived it will regress one cumulative level. If your tame is regressed past 0 the taming process with restart requiring a new initial tame roll.

A character who has reached level 20 and achieved the 6 post-20 milestones may choose to undergo a divine transformation in which the gods revert their mind and body to the state of a neophyte adventurer. Starting again at level 1-3, a ‘prestiged’ adventurer may begin again - choosing any new class, feats, or even remodeling their own personal attributes. They retain all knowledge, wealth, and any items they had prior to this. Upon choosing to undergo the transformation, the adventurer may choose a cosmetic effect to be bestowed upon them. This effect must be proposed by the player, and approved by a DM in the request to prestige the character (in #transcript). Examples of such an effect could include: Flittering sparkles that follow the character, an ethereal halo above their head, or a glowing/changing tattoo.

Gestalts are now considered a Paragon system, with the addition of Ascendants, which operate in a similar way - granting class levels past 20 - without having to reset. A character’s Paragon stage represents the number of times they have completed a full class level system (finished p20), starting at a value of 1. This number is used to determine experience gain, and for communicating your character’s progress, as seen in “How are Levels Counted”. Such systems and changes can and will be subject to change and active monitoring. How Levels are Counted​ Levels are counted through the following format A#L#, where A represents your paragon stage, and L represents your remaining levels. For example, a P26 wizard with 10 additional levels from this system would be an A1L10. This can be similarly done with tiers. This is similarly done with gestalt, in which the format is G#L#, where G represents your Paragon stage, and L represents your current level, up to 26. This can be similarly done with tiers.

Characters can now progress past level 20, continuing to gain character levels, being known as Ascendants rather than Gestalts. The character’s XP counter would reset to zero, though they would keep their character levels, proficiency bonus, and P20 rewards. Such Ascendants would proceed to level another class, starting from T1, and gaining an appropriate amount of XP, with the ability to do so again upon completing P20.

To qualify a PC must be fully leveled, meaning level 20 with all post 20 levels completed. Ascendant PCs cannot gain experience from hunts, trials, DM-XP, Transcript-XP, etc. They can only gain experience from RP-XP or Quests. In quests that involve combat, while you will receive XP for the RP, you will receive no XP for the creatures killed. Ascendant hit dice are restricted to the two highest hit dice per level (as opposed to getting all hit dice per level). Rather than gaining the save proficiencies of all classes, Ascendants choose one strong save and one weak save from the options given to them by their classes: Strong Saves: Dex, Con, Wis Weak Saves: Str, Int, Cha Any changes to the locked classes or subclasses are allowed and follow the normal retraining rules. Due to the documentation required for this system, character sheets must be handled in G-Sheets. ASIs stack, but do not stack past the normal cap of 20 unless otherwise specified. Stats may not exceed 30 for any reason. You can not take the same feat multiple times unless otherwise specified. Feats that scale based on level are calculated based on your class levels. Ascendant PC's, May only hunt, trial or delve with PC's who are also Ascendant Spell save DCs and spellcasting follow multi classing rules. Spell Save DCs and Spell Attack Bonuses calculate based on the class providing the spell. Class features that references class levels are self contained for the applicable class and paragon cycle

Class Features, Spell Slots, Proficiencies and Stat Changes generally stack unless otherwise specified. Exceptions​ The following features do NOT stack when creating a Ascendant PC: Proficiency Bonus Extra Attack Unarmored Defense Duplicated Paladin Auras Movement speed increases from duplicate sources. Bladesong, and other features with limited uses such as rage, do not get doubled buffs but do get a increased number of uses.

The Ascendant Paragon system also includes Prestige Classes, classes that have specific requirements for their use and play, but are generally stronger than the normal classes. Further information can be found at the Prestige Classes page.

This is a variant to the typical prestige system, and while it may grant great boons it also has great restrictions as well. When you Gestalt Paragon, you must post in #transcript including both the new and original sheets for reference.

Upon gestalt prestige you can select a class to level alongside your current one. The starting proficiencies, skills, and other benefits are granted to the character. When you level up, both classes level simultaneously, and you gain the benefits from both. Put simply, you have build A which was gestalted, getting added to build B. This is similar to if you had two separate characters who were merged into one. ASIs granted through level ups can be reassigned. This process can be repeated, allowing for a singular character to slowly grow in power over the years as they grow more involved in the world at large. Cumulative Level Cumulative Level is the total number of levels from all your classes combined. Cumulative Level is used to calculate what trials, hunts, and quests you can be involved in. Current Level​ Current Level is the current base level of the character and calculated as it would be normally, as though you were leveling a normal character. The Current Level is what is used to calculate proficiency bonus, character progression, and RP experience gains. Things that scale based on level use your Current Level.

At any time a character can revert a gestalt prestige. This will reset the character to a level 1 class of their choice akin to a normal prestige, provide zero cosmetic and stat benefits, and allow the character to once again gain experience from trials, hunts, etc. The character will then be locked out of the gestalt prestige system for 6 months. This can be done at any time and at any level.

All Gestalt PCs begin at level 1 Class levels do not mix between Gestalt Prestiges. Each prestige is treated as a unique PC build. To qualify a PC must be fully leveled, meaning level 20 with all post 20 levels completed. Gestalt PCs cannot gain experience from hunts, trials, DM-XP, Transcript-XP, etc. They can only gain experience from RP-XP or Quests. In quests that involve combat, while you will receive XP for the RP, you will receive no XP for the creatures killed. Gestalt PCs may not change their race, background, Racial ASIs, class or subclass choice, or anything else regarding the basis of the character which was set during their initial creation. On level up, the initial class chosen will follow the same build path (for example Fighter Champion) and multi class level split (if applicable) that the character had PRIOR to that prestige. Gestalt hit dice are restricted to the two highest hit dice per level (as opposed to gestalts getting all hit dice per level). Rather than gaining the save proficiencies of all classes, Gestalts choose one strong save and one weak save from the options given to them by their classes: Strong Saves: Dex, Con, Wis Weak Saves: Str, Int, Cha Gestalt PC's may choose to redistribute their ASI's and redo their first class in any way that is within the rules. Due to the documentation required for this system, character sheets must be handled in G-Sheets. ASIs stack, but do not stack past the normal cap of 20 unless otherwise specified. Stats may not exceed 30 for any reason. You can not take the same feat multiple times unless otherwise specified. Feats that scale based on level are calculated based on your Current Level not your Total Level. Gestalt PCs may attune to any item they own, however, Gestalt PCs may not use items which exceed their “Current Level” during hunts or trials with non-Gestalt PCs. Gestalt PCs may choose to join hunts above their Current Level, but not if non-Gestalt PCs are present. This does not affect Body Retrieval Hunts. If a gestalt hunting party is a mix of tiers, they can not recover a body. Spell save DCs and spellcasting follow multi classing rules. Spell Save DCs and Spell Attack Bonuses calculate based on the class providing the spell.

Class Features, Spell Slots, Proficiencies and Stat Changes generally stack unless otherwise specified. Exceptions​ The following features do NOT stack when creating a Gestalt PC: Proficiency Bonus Extra Attack Unarmored Defense Duplicated Paladin Auras Movement speed increases from duplicate sources. Bladesong, and other features with limited uses such as rage, do not get doubled buffs but do get a increased number of uses.
tl;dr - Introducing a very arduous method to regain wish through a whole gestalt prestige and questline using a Post20 Blessing/Boon Slot.

Paragon into a spellcasting class that also learns wish Complete self RP and DM-led quests (at least 4) throughout your prestige that meet the following guidelines Integrate with an existing group of worshipers for a particular deity Receive character references from leadership within the church/group Reach a level that would otherwise grant you wish from your prestige class Travel to the chosen deity’s home plane and petition their aid directly with offerings and references prepared Donate at least 2 items to the god directly, sacrificing them to prove your devotion. One item must be of legendary power and the second must be of great personal importance to your PC. Perform a quest for that god directly, run by a Dungeon master and approved by at least 2 more DMs or LMs

Once all of the requirements have been met and your PC is eligible for a Post20 Boon/Blessing Slot, the God will decide whether or not to grant you the Blessing of Forgiveness: Blessing of Forgiveness - This blessing removes one existing instance of permanent loss of wish. Once a creature has received this blessing, they can no longer receive it from the same deity. Note: It may not be possible to convince any other gods to grant this blessing or you may attract significant attention from your previous god if so. It would require unfathomable time and effort to regain wish a second time.

Gestalt or Ascension can be chosen when a character finishes p20 or completes a paragon cycle (finishes p20 on another class system). In doing so, a character may choose to Gestalt as a way to prestige and change through their class choices, though would still level according to their paragon cycle number. For example, a P3L0 (has finished this cycle but has not started a new one) may choose to Gestalt, and become a G4L1, where they may again choose to move back into ascension after leveling to p20.

Such Ascendants would proceed to level another class, starting from T1, and gaining an appropriate amount of XP, with the ability to do so again upon completing P20. How can you Swap​ For Gestalts currently in place, they may choose to revert to P20 and take 20 levels in each class system they have already finished leveling. They would take levels equal to their level before the shift in the class levels they had taken. For example, an A2 Level 13 whose base classes are 20 Fighter and 20 Wizard, and is currently leveling Artificer, would revert to 20 Fighter, 20 Wizard, and 13 Artificer, along with P20 rewards. For example, a P26 wizard with 10 additional levels from this system would be an A1L10. This can be similarly done with tiers. This is similarly done with gestalt, in which the format is G#L#, where G represents your Paragon stage, and L represents your current level, up to 26. This can be similarly done with tiers. After Ascension:​ When a pre-existing character begins their first ascension cycle (starting to level a new class system) or converts from gestalt, they can choose to adjust their base ability scores through point buy and may choose to swap current feats, asi, and p20 asi at no penalty. This must be submitted through transcript Gestalt and Ascension Interaction:​ Gestalt or Ascension can be chosen when a character finishes p20 or completes a paragon cycle (finishes p20 on another class system). In doing so, a character may choose to Gestalt as a way to prestige and change through their class choices, though would still level according to their paragon cycle number. For example, a P3L0 (has finished this cycle but has not started a new one) may choose to Gestalt, and become a G4L1, where they may again choose to move back into ascension after leveling to p20. Changes to Gestalt System:​ Gestalt would remain with the ability to adjust stats upon reset, as stated previously. In addition, they would no longer be required to level their base class as they would normally, and may choose to level a different class instead. Retroactive Adjustments:​ For those who choose to stay in gestalt, characters may receive retroactive rewards. Firstly, a character may adjust base stats and character levels, submitting a new sheet to transcript along with the old (make a copy and do changes from there) to be used as a reference. Additionally, players may reclaim downtime for changing class levels for characters or training characters, since the gestalt system was first introduced. Players must submit the time they would receive to transcript, with relevant links, where they would then be able to use that time in the future. Players may complete this same process for the gold cost. Note:​ All character changes must be done through the transcript. It is recommended that you make a copy of your old gsheet when adjusting things.
