If a player leaves during a quest, trial, or other event without the permission of the DM or person running it, they will be cursed, and put into the @Cursed role for two weeks. During this time, all characters belonging to the player receive only half XP and gold rewards, and cannot be resurrected if killed (except via Revivify spell). The @cursed role may also be given for other offenses at the discretion of the DM, Moderator, and Admin teams.

Training Downtime​ Characters can perform activities to train and practice in their free time, those who do not wish to hunt can spend time training themselves as well, this could be tinkering and experimenting for Artificers, praying and studying for Clerics, scribing and practicing spells for Wizards, sparring for fighters, and stealthing around for rogues, all forms of training are applicable and make no mechanical difference Characters can choose to spend 5 Hunting Tags or expend 8 hours of downtime in training which awards experience points to reflect the development of skills. Players who choose to roleplay the lessons will be awarded with additional RPXP as per usual Tier | XP Per Day (not RPXP) 1 | 100 xp 2 | 250 xp 3 | 500 xp 4 | 1,000 xp Post-20 | 2,000 xp

This page is a guide to getting started running Quests on TWR, a discord-based Westmarches campaign. Quests can be run by any player, with certain exceptions where the player may need to seek approval from staff for lore/balance reasons. As noted in our Code of Conduct, while running a quest or other content, the player acts as the DM and is considered such during play.

Being a DM on TWR is easy and fun. Most of the adventures can be prepared in a short period of time, and you don’t have to create an entire setting and form a campaign or spend a ton of time plotting out a large overarching plot. Most Quests on TWR are run as “one-shots,” though more advanced DMs may choose to run quests in a series to tell a more intricate story.

In order to run a game as a DM on TWR, you’ll need the following: Players​ The #quest-board channel is the perfect place to seek out players, if you do not have a full group in mind already. For traditional adventures a group of 4-6 players is recommended, but there is no specific number of players required to participate in a quest. Just be sure to balance any potential combat or roleplay encounters around the number of participants to ensure everyone gets to play. A Plot​ Balance the three pillars of gameplay (Roleplay, Adventuring, Combat) to your liking and create a plot for your quest. It is best to keep plots simple at first until you’ve got some practice running Quests. Consider what type of story you want to tell, what type of rewards might fit with the quest, Prepare any puzzles, difficult choices, or monster statblocks for combat ahead of time so that you can spend gameplay time interacting with the players and building the story. Remember, CR values translate to what an average difficulty is for a group of 4 well balanced adventurers. Though combat should be challenging, it should still be possible to win (unless your story dictates that the party loses!). A Format​ Some DMs prefer to run quests in a dedicated session for a more traditional experience, planning a start and end time. Others prefer a play-by-post (PBP) format, which can span multiple days or weeks and provide a more relaxed pace. Each option has benefits and detriments, so it's important to specify which one in your #quest-board post to attract the right players. Other Tools​ Avrae​ For combat, spellcasting, and other mechanical functions it is highly recommended that you use Avrae which will automate the majority of tracking and run combat. You can also upload maps to use for tactical placement during combat. Tupperbot​ You will want to set up at least a "Narrator Tupper" to describe scenes, effects and other miscellaneous actions during play. You may also consider creating specific Tuppers for your NPCs to improve immersion and create a more aesthetically pleasing experience.
documents.s: What you Need to Run a Game

documents.t: There’s no general rule that requires members of a group be of the same level. In quests that revolve around combat, we recommend restricting them by Tier as defined in the Player’s Handbook and Rules Compendium. For quests that are more roleplay-centric, this is less necessary, but bear in mind that some high level PCs may have spells and abilities that far outshine the rest of the group.

You have the most important role. You guide the narrative and provide the players with an immersive and enjoyable quest. While guiding the players, it is also your responsibility to make everyone feel welcomed, creating a fun and fair environment. Here are some things to keep in mind:

Make decisions about how the group interacts with the quest; adjust or improvise your plan as needed. You have the ability to create NPCs, locations, challenges and scenarios with broad authority within your quest. Interacting with official D&D NPCs, Factions, Deities and other key lore entities may require approval from Staff; we encourage DMs who are concerned that their content may not accurately reflect the setting reach out to an official Dungeonmaster or Loremaster for guidance. See the "When to Seek Staff Approval" section below for a better understanding of when to reach out. Be aware that, in the instance of particularly challenging deviations from the setting Staff may have to retcon the contents of your quests to maintain fairness and server continuity. Challenge your Players​ Gauge the experience level of your players, as well as what they enjoy in a game and attempt to deliver what they’re after; everyone should be able to shine. You can adjust an encounter’s difficulty by adding or removing thematically appropriate monsters but can’t create new monsters or modify them in such a way that modifies their challenge rating (aside from changing their hit points within the range afforded by their hit dice). Be careful of going too far, however. The intent is to have a collaborative and challenging story-telling experience; it’s not to do everything you can to kill your players’ characters. Similarly, destroying equipment generally shouldn’t happen unless an encounter specifically directs you to. In fact, unless they have conditions detailing their destruction (such as an ioun stone), permanent magic items can’t be destroyed. Dealing with Disruptive Players​ If a player is acting in a disruptive manner during a play session, attempt to address the issue as soon as it becomes clear that someone (including you) might be uncomfortable. Take the player aside and explain why the behavior might be causing others to feel uncomfortable. If the problem persists, contact a Moderator or Admin for help with resolution. Disruptive Magic Items, Spells or Class Features​ There are several magic items, spells, class features and homebrew submissions within the rules of TWR that might become disruptive to the overall enjoyment of others at the table. If use of any personal equipment, features etc. through play leads to an uncomfortable play experience, take the player aside and explain the issue. You may wish to discuss temporarily removing the item or ability from the character and providing them an alternative replacement instead. You may choose to review a character’s sheet prior to play to help identify any potential issues, You should not mandate removal of magic items or gear solely on your preferences, but rather on their impact to the story and enjoyment of the players/DM as a group. Safety Tools​ Safety tools help ensure players aren’t pushed beyond their comfort levels. These tools let your players know you want them to have a positive experience. Some common safety tools are provided below, each with a summary of how they work. An article about one such safety kit is provided to help with further information. Ensure that you discuss these tools with your players before the game: Code of Conduct: TWR has a code of conduct that outlines rules for play across the server. It defines desired and prohibited behaviors and possible consequences. Familiarize yourself with the Code of Conduct before running a quest to help understand what is acceptable and what is not. Pregame, Postgame, and Out of Character Discussions: Use time before the game to explain content warnings and set boundaries. This helps you understand the players' various goals and comfort levels. Be sure to discuss the possibility of lethal combat, if applicable, as many players prefer to avoid risking the safety of their long-running PCs. During play, most DMs prefer to have an Out of Character (OOC) thread for combat and ongoing discussion of the story. After the quest, decompress and discuss what worked and what didn't with the players. Be Welcoming: Welcome and encourage respectful and open conversations about issues as they arise. Show that you’re listening by avoiding defensive responses. Direct Communication: Allow direct messaging between the players and yourself as the DM. Generally, do not share information sent to you in private with the rest of the group without permission. Keep the Game Moving​ If the game gets bogged down, provide hints and clues to your players facing puzzles or engaging in combat and roleplay interactions that get frustrating. This gives players “little victories” for making good choices based on clues. Don't be afraid to skip someone's turn or allow them the ability to act retroactively in the future if one player is unavailable and disrupting the flow of play. Running the Game​ As the DM, you are charged with not only guiding the story, but also fairly adjudicating the game’s rules and rewarding your players’ characters for their accomplishments. The Rules of the Game​ TWR generally uses Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (2014) with some added Homebrew Rules. You can issue rulings to your table when the rules of the game are ambiguous or vague, but you must otherwise adhere to the rules as they are provided in the core rulebooks and can’t change them or make up your own. You must always use the most current incarnation of a rule. Oftentimes, if a rule is in dispute, you can go to the #questions channel or ping a Dungeonmaster for assistance; generally, we follow Sage Advice for clarification from the game developers and, in some cases, Homebrew or #town-hall posts will include rules clarifications. Don't be afraid to ask for help, or issue a temporary ruling while you wait to maintain the flow of play. Otherwise, the rules as written in the rulebooks always take precedence. Quest Locks​ Depending on the content of your quest, you have the ability to "Quest Lock" PCs who are participating. Locked PCs cannot gain experience from or participate in Hunts, Trials, or any form of activity outside of your quest. They are also unable to benefit from downtime while engaged in your quest. Whether or not to lock a PC is up to you, as is whether or not their possible progression applies within your quest. Keep in mind travel, in-character duration, and mechanical balance when deciding whether or not to lock the PCs, and be sure to communicate a quest lock during your original post or pregrame discussion. Death, Disease and Curses​ Adventuring is a risky job, and bad things often happen to adventurers. Diseases, poisons, and other similar effects persist until they’re removed, and death within a quest applies to a PC outside of the quest as well. However, thanks to the proliferation of healing and revival services from players in our setting, they are often simple to overcome. If you wish to enact permanent effects, be sure to communicate that possibility to the players during your original post or pregame discussion.

You award the players rewards for their accomplishments in the form of experience, gold, and magic items for their characters, which must be detailed in your #story-log post recording the quest. Experience​ Players should receive experience for participating in combat and for engaging in good roleplay. DMs should follow the usual guidelines for granting Experience, and are encouraged to request approval for more than the general amount in quests which are long-running or highly impactful. Magic Items​ Player generally expect to receive a Magic Item as a reward for their participation in your quest. It is often most exciting to include these items as possible rewards within the quest which they can then use or keep, but sometimes it is most appropriate to provide the items as a form of payment at the end. Regardless of the source, the below table outlines what rarity of items can be rewarded per PC without Staff Approval, provided that the items are available on the loot list: Tier Rarity Tier 1 Uncommon Tier 2 Rare Tier 3 Very Rare T4 and Above Legendary Misc. Treasure​ You may wish to award the players with gold or valuable treasures which they may keep or sell as an additional reward from the questgiver or discovery during play. The below table outlines what the maximum amount of additional treasure which can be rewarded per PC without Staff Approval. If no Magic Items are awarded, you may increase this amount by the item's trade value: Tier Amount Item Trade Value Tier 1 200 gp 400 gp Tier 2 2,000 gp 4,000 gp Tier 3 20,000gp 40,000gp Tier 4+ 100,000 gp 200,000 gp

DMs may provide cosmetic rewards such as eye color changes, floating halos, or other thematically appropriate character options as they see fit, provided that they do not allow for any mechanical benefits.

As mentioned throughout the above document, there are a number of times when it is appropriate to seek approval from Staff to assist with running your quest or to ensure that your quest is in-line with the general lore and balance expectations of our server. The following list outlines the most common reasons you may need to request Staff oversight: Running named NPCs, Deities or important factions from the Forgotten Realms setting Providing players with information relevant to ongoing Questlines or content provided by members of staff Running content inside of an area of the Forgotten Realms which a staff member is currently focused on Attempting to exceed the XP, Item or Gold reward limits for long-running quests or exemplary gameplay Rewarding magic items which do not appear on the existing loot lists Rewarding high-level awards such as Super Legendary items, Artifacts or Boons Rewarding items which provide a permanent stat boost Providing other custom rewards such as automatons, legendary crafting materials, custom items, or anything that may impact future gameplay on TWR Including homebrewed monsters or equipment within your quest (if included, such additions cannot leave your quest without majority Dungeonmaster approval)
Running a quest takes time and effort that we feel should be rewarded. Rewards for running a quest come in two main ways:
Omni-XP is awarded to the DM based on the average amount of XP delivered to their players. Omni-XP is restricted by tier and only applies to non-Paragon PCs.

Paragon Tokens can be taken in lieu of Omni-XP and can be applied to future roleplay to increase the amount of RP-XP rewarded to one of your Paragon PCs. Please note that you MAY choose instead to have one of your PCs participate in the request and receive the same rewards as the players, instead of choosing one of the above rewards. If you do so, Staff must approve the rewards whether they fall within the otherwise stated limits or not.

Once every 7 days you can summon 1d4 +2 Spectral Warriors to fight by your side for 1 hour. These warriors use the same statblock as the Bandit captain, but can be flavored as any relevant type of ally.
Your constitution score increases to 19. If it is already 19 or above, it instead increases the score by 2, to a maximum of 30.
The time it takes you to gain tool and language proficiencies is reduced by 15%.
Your crafting tools are enchanted by the gods. 15% reduction to your crafting time.

Prerequisite: Blessing of the Masked Lord (Soultheft) The practice of Soultheft has become second nature to you, allowing you to better subjugate the souls you capture and extract even greater potential. When you use Soultheft, and you can exploit a soul up to 12 times before the soul is released instead of 6. In addition you gain two new ways in which you may exploit souls: Ethereal Stride (2 uses). As a Bonus Action you can teleport to the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane for up to 1 minute or until you end the effect (no action required). You can expend another use of this exploit to extend the duration by up to 1 minute per use expended. At the end of the duration, you reappear in the same location on the Material Plane, or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied., Soul Mask (3 uses). You can use an action to call the Soul to you and disguise your appearance. When you do so, your appearance magically transforms into the souls as it was in life, healthy and alive. Another creature can see through this disguise by succeeding on a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check. You gain a +5 bonus to your check. This disguise lasts for 1 hour or until you end it as a bonus action. You can expend another use of this exploit to extend the duration by up to 1 hour per use expended.

Guided by the Masked Lord himself, the caster can snare a departing soul to fuel their spells, a practice called Soultheft. Once per day as an action, the caster can touch their holy symbol to a creature that’s been dead no longer than 1 minute, and capture their departing soul into the holy symbol, placing them under the effects of the ‘Soul Cage’ spell until the soul is released, or this blessing is used again. In addition to the spell's normal effects, the caster can also dispel the effects to cast a spell they know or have prepared without expending a spell slot, of a level equal to proficiency bonus of the captured creature. When casting a spell in this way, the creatures soul is damaged, and cannot be revived by any means short of a wish or divine intervention. Souls obtained via the Soultheft blessing MUST be canon. Hunts, Trials, Delves or Raids do not count, the usage must explicitly be approved by staff

This blessing is bestowed by a powerful metallic dragon upon a creature it recognizes as a dragon friend—one who has proven loyalty, courage, or respect worthy of draconic favor. Draconic Recognition Other metallic dragons instinctively recognize the bearer of this blessing as friendly, unless the bearer acts with obvious hostility. This recognition does not compel obedience or trust, but it greatly improves initial attitudes. Draconic Transformation You learn the Draconic Transformation spell. Once per long rest, you can cast a special version of the Draconic Transformation spell without expending a spell slot or material components. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell. While concentrating on the Special Draconic Transformation spell cast in this way, you gain the following additional benefits: Scaled Majesty. You gain 60 Temporary Hit Point as scales harden around your skin. Draconic Potency. Whenever you roll damage dice of the same type as the dragon that granted this blessing (such as fire for a gold dragon or lightning for a bronze dragon), any roll of 1 or 2 on a damage die is treated as a 3. Altered Breath: You can change the damage type of the Draconic Transformation spell's breath to the type associate to the dragon that granted the blessing. Draconic Gift This blessing can only be granted directly by a dragon. It cannot be replicated, transferred, or bestowed through training, magic items, divine intervention, or the wish spell. OOC clarification, you cannot learn this blessing via wish or the free boon or blessing, it must be quested for.

The blessings of a deity aligned to the moon protect and empower you. You gain resistance to radiant damage, and are empowered in the following ways at night: Lunar Magic Your learn the Moonbeam (DC19) and the Healing Spirit spells, and they are always prepared for you. You can cast each of these once per Short Rest without expending a spell slot, empowering it. While empowered, these spells are centered on and follow you, and their radius is increased to 15ft instead of 5 ft. You are immune to the damage caused by your own Moonbeam cast in this way. Moon Fever As a reaction immediately after you take damage or fail a saving throw against a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself, you can force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC19). On a failed save, the creature feels an intense urge to move towards or away from you (your choice). It must move as close or as far (depending on your choice) as its movement allows on its turn, taking the safest and most direct path available. You can use this feature a number of times equal half to your proficiency bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

The Cat Lord, god of tabaxi, sometimes confers the blessings of his people to those who prove to be great allies of his people. You are granted Feline Agility. Your reflexes and agility allow you to move with a burst of speed. When you move on your tum in combat, you can double your speed until the end of the turn. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you move 0 feet on one of your turns. If you are a tabaxi and receive this boon, your walking speed increases by 15ft.
Your intelligence or wisdom score increases by 2, to a max of 30. In addition, skill checks of the chosen ability score are rolled with advantage.

Granted by the god of sailors, storms, and naval prowess, Valkur, this blessing imbues the recipient with the courage, resilience, and maritime skill befitting a legendary seafarer. Storm's Resilience: You have resistance to lightning and thunder damage Navigator’s Instinct: You always know which direction is north, and you have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to navigate or predict weather conditions at sea. Mariner's Might Your swim speed is equal to your walking speed, and you can hold your breath for double beyond your normal capacity. Blessing of the Sea: You gain proficiency with navigator's tools and vehicles (water). If you already have these proficiencies, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

When wielding a ranged or melee weapon, you receive a +1 to attack and damage rolls with the affected weapon. In addition, you can add a +5 bonus to attack rolls affected by the blessing a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, resetting at dawn. You can use this after you see the roll, but before you know the result.
Whenever you have advantage on an attack roll, you can reroll one of the dice once. Condition: Cannot be taken with Elven Accuracy

You gain the ability to attune to one additional magical item, through a special attunement slot. Additionally, as an action, you may end your attunement to the item in the slot granted by this boon, unless the item is cursed, to immediately attune to another. Once you do this, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
You can bypass the charmed condition immunity of creatures

Whenever you move, you may instead expend movement and teleport an amount of feet equal to the expended movement to an area you can see. You may do this an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses on a short or long rest.

Prerequisites: Elemental Adept Feat The chosen element for this boon is the element chosen in the elemental adept feat. If you have taken the feat multiple times, you may choose which of these elements applies to this boon. This element cannot be later changed. You can treat immunity to the given element as resistance. this resistance cannot be overcome by the elemental adept feat. When you cast a spell of 5th level or lower that deals damage of your chosen element, you can choose to treat all damage dice rolled as their maximum amount. once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

When another creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an ability check, an attack roll, or a saving throw, you can roll a d10 and apply the result as a bonus or penalty to the roll. You may do this an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses at the next dawn.

Prerequisite: Crossbow Expert or Gunner Your mastery over the weights of these weapons has allowed you to use them at higher efficiencies. You can use any two-handed crossbow or firearm with one hand, and you do not require a free hand to load ammunition into one. Using a two-handed crossbow or firearm with one hand gives a -2 penalty to attack rolls. Additionally, two-weapon fighting now applies to any crossbow or firearm you wield.
Your hit point maximum increases by 40. If, instead, you have gestalted or ascended, your hit point maximum increases by 80.
You have immunity to cold damage. You can cast Frost Fingers (save DC 15) at will, without expending a spell slot or using components.

As an action, you unleash a freezing aura that radiates from your body in a persistent chill. This aura remains active until you dismiss it as a free action or until you become incapacitated, at which point you must reactivate it to regain its effects. While this boon is active, any creature that touches you or hits you with a melee attack takes 10 (3d6) cold damage. Additionally, any creature or object that is grappling, restraining, carrying, or otherwise holding you takes the same cold damage at the start of each of your turns.
You have immunity to cold damage. You can cast Frost Fingers (save DC 15) at will, without expending a spell slot or using components.

As an action, you unleash a freezing aura that radiates from your body in a persistent chill. This aura remains active until you dismiss it as a free action or until you become incapacitated, at which point you must reactivate it to regain its effects. While this boon is active, any creature that touches you or hits you with a melee attack takes 10 (3d6) cold damage. Additionally, any creature or object that is grappling, restraining, carrying, or otherwise holding you takes the same cold damage at the start of each of your turns.
You can bypass the frightened condition immunity of creatures

Once per turn, if a legendary monster would use a legendary resistance to succeed on a saving throw, you can use your reaction to have them use a second legendary resistance to succeed on that save. If they cannot, they fail the save.

You have a certain level of mastery over positive energies. You have resistance to necrotic damage, and your maximum hp cannot be reduced. Additionally, when you cast a spell or use an ability that restores hit points to other creatures, you may apply one of the following additional effects to targets other than yourself: One of the targets gains double the hit points. All of the targets benefit from a Lesser Restoration The targets regain lost maximum hp equal to twice the healing done. Adding on an effect can be done an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, resetting upon finishing a long rest.

You have a certain level of mastery over positive energies. You have resistance to necrotic damage, and your maximum hp cannot be reduced. Additionally, when you cast a spell or use an ability that restores hit points to other creatures, you may apply one of the following additional effects to targets other than yourself: One of the targets gains double the hit points. All of the targets benefit from a Lesser Restoration The targets regain lost maximum hp equal to twice the healing done. Adding on an effect can be done an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, resetting upon finishing a long rest.

Prerequisite: Boon of Magic Resistance You may not be affected or detected by spells of 3rd level and lower unless you choose to be. (Disclaimer that upcasting spells past third level bypasses this immunity)

Prerequisite: Boon of the Shapechanger Your mastery over transformation deepens. The CR increase granted by your Boon of the Shapechanger is now equal to your full post-20 level, rather than half your post-20 level. For example, an effect normally limited to CR 20 can access CR 22 at level 20p2, CR 24 at level 20p4, and CR 26 at level 20p6. This increase only modifies the original CR limit of wild shape, shapechange, or polymorph. It cannot be applied repeatedly through chained transformations. Transforming into a CR 26 creature does not allow that creature's level or CR to establish a new transformation limit. This does not function for things such as chain polymorphing.

Prerequisites: Poisoner Feat You can treat immunity to poison damage as resistance. This resistance cannot be overcome by the poisoner feat. When you cast a spell of 5th level or lower that deals poison damage, you can choose to treat all damage dice rolled as their maximum amount. When you hit with a weapon attack that deals poison damage, you can choose to treat all damage dice rolled as their maximum amount. Once you use one of these features, you cannot use either again until you finish a long rest.

You gain one additional reaction per round. This additional reaction is subject to the following restrictions: Diminishing Returns: You cannot use this reaction to take a Reaction Option that you have already taken this round (such as Cast a Spell, Opportunity Attack, or a specific class feature), nor can you take it in response to a trigger you have already reacted to. Defense Limit: You cannot apply a bonus to your Armor Class if you have already done so since the start of your last turn.
You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from weapon attacks.

Prerequisite: Boon of the Storm Born Calamity of the Storm: First there was lightning…then there was thunder! Once per turn, you may add 10 extra lightning damage to an attack . After you've dealt this damage three times you become supercharged allowing the recipient as a bonus action to emit a wave of thunder dealing 2d8 thunder damage in a 15 ft cube originating from the recipient. When you would take lightning damage you may instead add half of that damage to your next thunder wave. Cloud Jumper: The recipient of this boon gains a flight speed equal to half their movement speed Where the wind takes you: As an action the recipient of this boon to assume the form of a cloud. While in this cloud form, a creature has a flying speed of 150 feet and has resistance to damage from nonmagical weapons. The only actions a creature can take in this form are the Dash action or to revert to its normal form. Reverting back take a full round during which time the recipient is incapacitated as they reconstitute themselves. If hit by lightning while in cloud form the recipient becomes 'Charged' for 1 minute, while Charged they may cast call lightning at will in the area directly below them (dc 15)

Awareness. You automatically know the strongest emotion being experienced by any creature within 30 feet of you. You have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks. Connection. As a bonus action, you can establish a telepathic bond with one creature you can see within 60 feet for 1 minute. You do not need to share a language with the target, but the target must know at least one language. While bonded, you can communicate telepathically and know whenever the creature is frightened, charmed, stunned, or reduced below half its hit points. Protection. When a creature bonded to you fails a saving throw made to frighten, charm, or stun them, you can use your reaction to allow them to reroll the save, adding your Wisdom modifier as a bonus. If the creature succeeds, the creature that invoked the saving throw takes the same amount of psychic damage as the new save rolled (including modifiers). You can use this effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, resetting on a Long Rest.
You gain a +5 bonus on Arcana, Nature, or Survival checks made to discern plants. In addition, you may cast the spell Find Familiar and summon a Chwinga (Missing it's magical gift) using it

Prerequisite: Boon of the Fire Soul Whenever you are subjected to fire damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the fire damage dealt. Fire Form. The recipient of this boon can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing. Any creature that touches the phoenix or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. In addition, the recipient of this boon can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. The first time it enters a creature’s space on a turn, that creature takes 5 (1d10) fire damage. With a touch, the recipient of this boon can also ignite flammable objects that aren’t worn or carried (no action required). Fiery Death and Rebirth. When the recipient of this boon dies, it explodes. Each creature within 60-feet of it must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The fire ignites flammable objects in the area that aren’t worn or carried. The explosion destroys the recipient's body and carried items and leaves behind an egg-shaped cinder that weighs 5 pounds. The cinder is blazing hot, dealing 21 (6d6) fire damage to any creature that touches it, though no more than once per round. The cinder is immune to all damage, and after 1d6 days, it hatches a new Phoenix. Due to the strain put on the Phoenix’s soul, this forces a new prestige, requiring a small tattood Roman numeral on their body to increase by one. The tattoo can be placed wherever this boon recipient wishes. If the recipient of this boon has paragon levels, they are reset to the beginning of a gestalt prestige in their current Paragon.

The CR range for wildshape, shapechange, and polymorph is increased by half of your post 20 lvl rounded down. This does not function for things such as chain polymorphing, shapechanging, etc; For example you can not poly into a CR23 creature, then a CR26, then CR29. You are limited to CR23 at lvl 20 with 6 post 20 lvls. For clarity, avilable CR is 21 at lvl 20p2, 22 at 20p4, and 23 at 20p6.

Your illusions have become so perfectly crafted that even those with true sight have become impaired by their effects. Your illusion spells appear real to any creature. Truesight no longer automatically succeeds through your illusions and will now provide only advantage on saving throws and checks made to discern your illusions.
You regain 5 hitpoints at the start of your turn. If you are damaged by fire, acid, or radiant damage, this trait ceases to function until your next short or long rest.

Your melee weapon attacks deal an additional 1d8 necrotic damage. Additionally, you regain hit points equal to half the amount of necrotic damage dealt by this boon, unless the target is an undead or construct.

You sprout a pair of wings. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed. You can furl the wings against your back as a bonus action and unfurl them the same way — while furled, they don't interfere with armor, but you can't fly. Grounded: If you're incapacitated, restrained, or wearing armor you're not proficient with, your wings fail and you fall.

Roll or choose. Each grants a minor trait beyond flight. d8 Wings Trait 1 Bat Blindsight 15 ft. while flying. 2 Eagle Advantage on Perception checks relying on sight in daylight. 3 Angelic Once per long rest, shed daylight out to 5 feet from your feathers for 1 minute. 4 Dragon Resistance to one damage type matching your scale color. 5 Spectral Your flight is silent; you can hover, and you leave no tracks in air or on soft ground. 6 Insectile Your flying speed increases by 10 ft., but you can't fly in strong wind. 7 Moth Advantage on Stealth checks in dim light or darkness while airborne. 8 Storm-torn When you take the Dash action while flying, lightning crackles: one creature you fly past takes 1d6 lightning damage.

Optional Additions They are now granted proficiency with firearms if they do not already have it. Eldritch Cannons, when tiny, can now be integrated into a firearm. They now move with you if integrated, but otherwise function RAW. The Arcane Firearm feature can now be used on firearms as well, instead of just a wand, staff, or rod.

Optional (Replaces Current Spell-Storing Item feature) At 11th level, you learn how to store a spell in an object. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch one simple or martial weapon or one item that you can use as a spellcasting focus, and you store a spell in it, choosing a 1st- or 2nd-level spell from the artificer spell list that requires 1 action to cast (you needn't have it prepared).You may upcast a 1st level spell to use a 2nd level slot, if previous conditions are applicable. While holding the object, a creature can take an action to produce the spell's effect from it, using your spellcasting ability modifier. If the spell requires concentration, the creature must concentrate. The spell stays in the object until it's been used a number of times equal to twice your Intelligence modifier (minimum of twice) or until you use this feature again to store a spell in an object.

They now move with you if integrated, but otherwise function RAW. The Arcane Firearm feature can now be used on firearms as well, instead of just a wand, staff, or rod.

Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch one simple or martial weapon or one item that you can use as a spellcasting focus, and you store a spell in it, choosing a 1st- or 2nd-level spell from the artificer spell list that requires 1 action to cast (you needn't have it prepared).You may upcast a 1st level spell to use a 2nd level slot, if previous conditions are applicable. While holding the object, a creature can take an action to produce the spell's effect from it, using your spellcasting ability modifier. If the spell requires concentration, the creature must concentrate. The spell stays in the object until it's been used a number of times equal to twice your Intelligence modifier (minimum of twice) or until you use this feature again to store a spell in an object.

Optional Class Feature (Replaces Counter Charm) At 6th level, you gain the ability to use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. As a reaction when you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw to prevent or remove the charm or frightened condition, you can have the creature reroll the saving throw with advantage. A creature must be able to hear you to gain this benefit.

Optional Class Feature (Replaces Superior Inspiration) At 20th level your inspiration becomes more than a just a short lived burst. When a creature uses your bardic inspiration, the effect is not expended, allowing for the creature to use it multiple times. Your bardic inspiration now only ends once used a number of times equal to your charisma modifier, or once ten minutes pass.

A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you and are not included as part of the Spells Known column of the Bard table. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, ,Underdark, Hills, Underwater, or Urban. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in. While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits: Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel. Your group can't become lost except by magical means. While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area. You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.

Your patron bestows upon you special clothing in the form of ceremonial garbs or eldritch garments that can protect you and bolster your abilities. While not holding a shield, the garb is light armor with an AC of 10 + your charisma modifier + your dexterity modifier You can don and doff the garb as an action, and it cannot be removed unless you wish it to be. If the garb is lost or destroyed, you can perform a 1 hour ceremony to receive another from your patron. This ceremony can be performed on a short or long rest, whereupon the previous garbs disappear. The garbs fade away when you die. You cannot benefit from the garbs or it's invocations while wearing other armor.

This overhaul is mostly a buff to the base class as written by Matt Mercer. There were a number of features that went largely unused, were very situational, or generally underwhelming in practice. The main draw the class presents in this overhaul is that it leans more into the sacrificing of your hit points, using your health more as a typical mana pool for your abilities, and gives you more ways to spend your hit points to do so. Every other class resource the Blood Hunter had previously is gone. This overhaul also features a true distinction between using intelligence and wisdom as your hemocraft modifier. Intelligence leads to a more monstrous take on your blood magic, granting you greater offensive ability as your hemocraft takes shape. Where wisdom takes a more defensive route, and later grants more control over your hemocraft.
