As a Blood Hunter you gain the following class features. Hit Points Hit Dice: 1d12 per Blood Hunter Level Hit Points at 1st Level: 12 + your constitution modifier Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d12 (or 7) + your constitution modifier per Blood Hunter level after 1st Proficiencies Weapons: Simple, Martial Armor: Light, Medium, Shields Tools: Alchemist’s Supplies Saving Throws: Dexterity, Intelligence Skills: Choose three from Acrobatics, Arcana, Athletics, History, Insight, Investigation, Religion, and Survival

At 1st level, you have survived the Hunter’s Bane - a dangerous, long guarded ritual that alters your life’s blood. You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track fey, fiends, and undead, as well as Intelligence checks to recall information about such creatures. The Hunter’s Bane also empowers your body to control and shape hemocraft magic, using your own blood and life-essence to fuel your abilities. Choose either your intelligence or your wisdom score. Your hemocraft modifier is equal to the modifier of the chosen ability. The ability you choose also determines the effects of features you gain at later levels. When you reach a feature that has [Monstrous] or [Stable] options, you gain the [Monstrous] option if your hemocraft modifier uses your intelligence, or the [Stable] options if your hemocraft modifier uses your wisdom. Some of your Blood Hunter features require you to sacrifice hit points in order to activate or sustain. When a feature asks you to sacrifice hit points, your hit points are lowered by that amount. This sacrifice cannot be reduced in any way. If the sacrifice would leave you with 0 hit points, you fall unconscious as normal, and the ability fails. When any of your Blood Hunter features require a target to make a saving throw, the save DC is calculated with the following: Hemocraft save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your hemocraft modifier

Also at 1st level, you gain the ability to sacrifice your vital essence to curse and manipulate creatures through hemocraft magic. Blood Curses Known: You know two Blood Curses of your choice, and learn additional blood curses at later levels as shown by the “Blood Curses Known” column of the Blood Hunter Table. Invoking a Blood Curse: To use a Blood Curse, you must roll your hemocraft die, sacrificing hit points equal to the number rolled. Amplifying a Blood Curse requires you to roll three hemocraft dice instead of one. You can Invoke or Amplify your known Blood Curses as many times as you like, so long as you pay the hit point cost each time.

At 2nd Level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can’t take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again. Archery: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons. Blind Fighting: You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn’t behind total cover, even if you’re blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you. Defense: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC. Dueling: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon. Great Weapon Fighting: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

Also at 2nd level, you learn to invoke a rite of hemocraft that infuses your weapon strikes with energy. As a bonus action, you can activate any rite you know, enhancing one weapon that you are holding. The rite remains in effect until you finish a short or long rest. When you activate a rite, you sacrifice hit points equal to one roll of your hemocraft die. While a rite is in effect, attacks made with that weapon are considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage, and deal extra damage equal to one roll of your hemocraft die of a damage type determined by the chosen rite. When you attack a creature with a weapon affected by any of your Crimson Rites, and deal damage to them, you can choose to amplify the effect. Doing so causes you to sacrifice hit points equal to one roll of your hemocraft die. A single weapon can only hold one rite at any given time, and other creatures cannot benefit from your rite. Choose one of the following rites when you gain this feature. You learn one additional rite at 7th and 14th level: Rite of the Flame - The extra damage dealt by your rite is fire damage. When amplified, the target is burned, taking fire damage equal to your hemocraft modifier at the start of each of it’s turns. You may stack this effect on a single creature up to a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus. The burning creature, or a creature within 5 feet of it can use an action to douse the flames. Rite of the Frozen - The extra damage dealt by your rite is cold damage. When amplified, the target’s move speed is reduced by 5 times your hemocraft modifier, to a minimum of 0 feet. Rite of the Storm - The extra damage dealt by your rite is lightning damage. When amplified, electricity arcs to other targets within 20 feet of your choice. You can target a number of creatures equal to your hemocraft modifier. Each extra target takes lightning damage equal to one roll of your hemocraft die. Rite of the Dead - The extra damage dealt by your rite is necrotic damage. When amplified, the target has its strength sapped until the end of its next turn. While sapped, it has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks and saving throws. Rite of the Oracle - The extra damage dealt by your rite is psychic damage. When amplified, visions of dread flood your target’s mind. The target is frightened of you until the end of their next turn. Rite of the Roar - The extra damage dealt by your rite is thunder damage. When amplified, a thunderous crash slams into your target. The target is either pushed up to 10 feet away from you or knocked prone (your choice). Rite of the Dawn (Order of the Ghostslayer) - The extra damage dealt by your rite is radiant damage. Additionally, while the rite is active, you gain the following benefits. Your weapon sheds bright light out a range of 20 feet, and dim light out 20 past that. You have resistance to necrotic damage. When you hit an undead creature with a weapon effected by this rite, roll one additional hemocraft die when determining the extra damage. When amplified, if the target is an undead, they are placed under the effect of turn undead. Rite of the Blighted (Order of the Symbiote) - The extra damage dealt by your rite is poison damage. Additionally, hitting a creature with a weapon affected by this rite that is neither undead or a construct deals extra poison damage equal to your hemocraft modifier. When amplified, the target suffers the poisoned condition until the start of your next turn, bypassing immunity to the condition.
At 3rd level, you commit to an order of blood hunters whose philosophy will guide you throughout your life. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level, and again at 7th, 11th, 15th, and 18th level.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.
Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

At 6th level, when you damage a creature with your crimson rite, you can channel hemocraft magic to sear an arcane brand into that creature (no action required). Doing so requires you to sacrifice hit points equal to two rolls of your hemocraft die. You always know the direction to the branded creature, so long as it is on the same plane as you. Additionally, each time the branded creature damages you or creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you, it takes psychic damage equal to your hemocraft modifier (minimum of 1). Your brand lasts until you dismiss it or until you use this feature to brand another creature. Your brand can be removed with a [Remove Curse] spell or similar effects.

When you reach 9th level, you gain a supernatural talent for discerning secrets surrounding relics or places touched by evil. You can cast the [Contact Other Plane] spell without needing to make an intelligence save. When you do so, you may ask only about your immediate surroundings, but you will only receive clear answers if what you are asking about is linked to evil. Once you cast the spell in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest. You also learn the Identify spell, and can cast it as a ritual. The spell fails if the item you attempt to identify is not linked to evil in some way.

When you reach 10th level, the magic of hemocraft suffuses your body. You either control it, or let it control you. You gain a bonus to strength, dexterity, and constitution saving throws equal to your hemocraft modifier. Additionally, your hemocraft begins to warp your body and mind, the way you channel your blood magic determines how. You gain one of the following benefits: Monstrous: You gain a bonus to weapon damage rolls equal to your hemocraft modifier. Stable: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

Starting at 13th level, your brand works to bind your foes. The damage dealt by your Brand of Castigation doubles to twice your hemocraft modifier (minimum of 2). Additionally, creatures branded by it cannot take the dash or disengage actions. If a branded creature attempts to teleport, or leave its current plane by any means, it takes 4d6 psychic damage and must succeed on a wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the teleportation or attempt to leave the plane fails.

Your mind hardens to external influence when you reach 14th level. How you channel your blood magic determines its effect. Gain one of the following benefits: Monstrous: You are immune to the frightened condition, and you have advantage on saving throws to end or resist the charmed condition. Stable: You are immune to the charmed condition, and you have advantage on saving throws to end or resist the frightened condition. You also gain resistance to psychic damage, regardless of how your hemocraft takes shape.

When you reach 17th level, you gain the ability to fuel your magic more efficiently, so long as your wounds remain open. While you have half your maximum hit points or less, you roll one less hemocraft die when determining the hit point cost of your hemocraft abilities (to a minimum of 0).

Upon reaching 20th level, your blood magic reaches its height, and either grants you mastery over it, or consumes you. How you channel your blood magic determines the effect. Gain one of the following benefits: Monstrous: You roll one additional hemocraft die when determining the damage dealt by your crimson rites, including their amplified effects. The cost of amplifying blood curses increases by one roll of your hemocraft die. Stable: When you use a blood curse and roll a hemocraft die, you can choose to reroll the die and use either result. You can only reroll each die once. The cost of amplifying crimson rites increases by one roll of your hemocraft die.

As a blood hunter, you have access to a range of blood curses that can tax the resilience of any foe. Blood Curse of the Anxious​ As a bonus action, you harry the body or mind of a creature within 30 feet of you, making them susceptible to forceful influence. Until the end of your next turn, Charisma (Intimidation) checks made against the cursed creature have advantage. Amplify. The next Wisdom saving throw the cursed creature makes before this curse ends has disadvantage. Blood Curse of Binding​ As a bonus action, you attempt to bind a Large or smaller creature you can see within 30 feet of you, which must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the cursed creature’s speed is reduced to 0 and it can’t use reactions until the end of your next turn. Amplify. This curse lasts for 1 minute and can affect any creature regardless of size. The cursed creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on itself on a success. Blood Curse of Bloated Agony​ As a bonus action, you curse a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you, causing its body to swell until the end of your next turn. For the duration, the creature has disadvantage on Strength checks and Dexterity checks, and takes 1d8 necrotic damage if it makes more than one attack during its turn. Amplify. This curse lasts for 1 minute. The cursed creature can make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on itself on a success. Blood Curse of Corrosion​ Prerequisite: 15th level, Order of the Mutant As a bonus action, you cause a creature within 30 feet of you to become poisoned. The cursed creature can make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on itself on a success. Amplify. The cursed creature takes 4d6 necrotic damage when you inflict this curse, and it takes this damage again each time it fails a Constitution saving throw to end the curse. Blood Curse of the Exorcist​ Prerequisite: 15th level, Order of the Ghostslayer As a bonus action, you choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you that is charmed or frightened, or which is under a possession effect. The target creature is no longer charmed, frightened, or possessed. Amplify. A creature that charmed, frightened, or possessed the target of your curse takes 3d6 psychic damage and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn. Blood Curse of Exposure​ When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage from an attack or spell, you can use your reaction to temporarily weaken its resilience. Until the end of the target’s next turn, it loses resistance to all the damage types dealt by the triggering attack or spell (including for that triggering effect). Amplify. The target instead loses invulnerability to the damage types of the triggering attack or spell, but has resistance to those damage types until the end of its next turn. Blood Curse of the Eyeless​ When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack, you can use your reaction to roll one hemocraft die and subtract the number rolled from the creature’s attack roll. You can choose to use this feature after the creature’s roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack hits or misses. The creature is immune to this curse if it is immune to the blinded condition. Amplify. You apply this curse to all the creature’s attack rolls until the end of the creature’s turn. You roll separately for each affected attack. Blood Curse of the Fallen Puppet​ When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to instill that creature with a final act of aggression. The creature immediately makes one weapon attack against a target of your choice within its range. Amplify. You can first cause the cursed creature to move up to half its speed, and you grant a bonus to its attack roll equal to your Hemocraft modifier (minimum of +1). Blood Curse of the Howl​ Prerequisite: 18th level, Order of the Lycan As an action, you unleash a bloodcurdling howl. Each creature within 30 feet of you that can hear you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn. If a creature fails its saving throw by 5 or more, it is stunned while frightened in this way. A creature that succeeds on its saving throw is immune to this blood curse for the next 24 hours. You can choose any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by the howl. Amplify. The range of this curse increases to 60 feet. Blood Curse of the Marked​ As a bonus action, you mark a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. Until the end of your turn, whenever you hit the cursed creature with a weapon for which you have an active crimson rite, you roll an additional hemocraft die when determining the extra damage from the rite. Amplify. The next attack roll you make against the target before the end of your turn has advantage. Blood Curse of the Muddled Mind​ As a bonus action, you curse a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you that is concentrating on a spell or using a feature that requires concentration. That creature has disadvantage on the next Constitution saving throw it makes to maintain concentration before the end of your next turn. Amplify. The cursed creature has disadvantage on all Constitution saving throws made to maintain concentration until the end of your next turn. Blood Curse of the Soul Eater​ Prerequisite: 18th level, Order of the Profane Soul When a creature that isn’t a construct or undead is reduced to 0 hit points within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to offer their life energy to your patron in exchange for power. Until the end of your next turn, you make attacks with advantage and you have resistance to all damage. Amplify. Additionally, you regain an expended warlock spell slot. Once you’ve amplified this blood curse, you must finish a long rest before you can amplify it again.

Where the Alchemist brings life, the Bombardier brings ruin. Bombardiers are masters of volatile reagents, crafting incendiary flasks, caustic vials, and toxic brews designed to engulf their foes in lingering devastation. On the battlefield, they are walking arsenals, hurling explosive concoctions that set the world ablaze. Features: 3rd Level - Tool Proficiency 3rd Level - Bombardier Spells 3rd Level - Experimental Bomb 5th Level - Volatile Savant 9th Level - Corrosive Concoctions 9th Level - Rapid Alchemy 15th Level - Master of Ruin

When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with alchemist’s supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with another type of artisan’s tools of your choice.

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Bombardier Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you and don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare. Artificer Level | Spells 3rd | grease, inflict wounds 5th | web, Melf's acid arrow 9th | gaseous form, stinking cloud 13th | greater invisibility, vitriolic sphere 17th | wall of force, immolation

Starting at 3rd level, whenever you finish a long rest, you can magically produce an experimental bomb in an empty flask or vial you touch. Roll on the Experimental Bomb table to determine its effect, which is triggered when you throw it. As an action, you or another creature can throw the bomb up to 30 feet, where it shatters and releases its effect. A creature in the bomb’s area must make a saving throw against your artificer spell save DC to avoid or reduce its effects. You can create additional experimental bombs by expending a spell slot of 1st level or higher for each one. When you do so, you use your action to create the bomb and roll for its effect on the Experimental Bomb table. Creating a bomb requires alchemist’s supplies on your person, and any bomb you create with this feature lasts until it is thrown or until the end of your next long rest.

Corrosive Acid. Deals 2d6 acid damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, the acid clings to creatures, dealing 1d6 acid damage at the start of each of their turns until a creature uses its action to scrape or wash it off. Incendiary Fire. Deals 2d6 fire damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, creatures are set ablaze, taking 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns until they or an ally uses an action to douse the flames. Toxic Gas. Creates a 10-foot radius cloud of poisonous gas that lasts for 1 minute. (Con save or be poisoned until the start of your next turn; repeat the save at the end of each turn). A creature must make the save whenever it enters the gas or starts its turn in the gas. Cryo Flask. Deals 2d6 cold damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, a creature is hindered by ice formations for 1 minute, or until it or another creature within reach uses an action to break the ice. Shrapnel Bomb. Deals 2d6 piercing damage in a 10-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, the creature takes 1d6 slashing damage the first time on each turn it moves 1 foot or more without teleporting. An affected creature or ally can use its action to remove the shrapnel. Sonic Blast. Deals 2d8 thunder damage in a 10-foot radius (Str save for half). Creatures that fail the save are pushed 10 feet from the center of the blast and are deafened until the start of your next turn. Scaling: The initial and persistent damage increase at higher levels: 6th level: +1d6 (or +1d4/+1d8 for relevant bombs) 11th level: +2d6 16th level: +3d6

At 5th level, you have mastered the art of combining spellwork and alchemical destruction into seamless attacks. Whenever you cast an artificer spell or cantrip on your turn, you can throw one of your Experimental Bombs as a bonus action. You can treat any alchemical item (such as alchemist’s fire, acid vial, or an experimental bomb) as a simple ranged weapon with a range of 30/90 feet, using your Dexterity or Strength modifier for attack rolls. Damage dealt by the throw is 1d4 slashing damage plus your Dexterity or Strength modifier, in addition to the damage or effect normally dealt by the item.

At 9th level, your concoctions weaken enemy defenses and allow you to control the battlefield: Creatures that fail their saving throw against one of your bombs have disadvantage on saving throws against the next alchemical effect you deal to them (from your bombs or alchemical items such as acid vial or alchemist’s fire) before the end of your next turn.
Also at 9th level, you are able to craft bombs with remarkable speed: You can use a bonus action instead of an action to craft your Experimental Bombs.

At 15th level, your expertise in destruction allows you to maximize the potency of your creations and have better control over what you use: You gain resistance to fire, and acid damage. When a creature takes persistent damage from one of your Experimental Bombs (acid or fire) or an alchemical item (alchemist’s fire, acid vial), you can use your reaction to make the creature take maximum damage instead of rolling. You can use this ability a number of times equal to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). All expended uses are restored when you finish a long rest.

Outside the king’s chambers, still as an armor display, the royal guard stands post as they await the coming rebelion force. Ready to meet it head on, no matter the result. A scrappy militiaman clad in chainmail stands on the battlefield, now alone and bloodied, having outlasted all others through wit and defensive positioning. Beneath a greathelm, the dwarf’s face pools with sweat as he crosses the great desert, sent on a mission to deliver an important message that cannot afford to fall into the wrong hands Bulwarks spend large portions of their lives covered in heavy armor to the point that they are seldom ever seen without it. Their mastery over using it fully to their advantage naturally comes as second nature, allowing them to outperform nearly any other. What truly distinguishes a bulwark from other users of heavy armor is their distinct focus on making the absolute most of the defense it offers, knowing how best to move themselves to avoid or block incoming assaults. Bulwarks are often kept as personal guards to high ranking officials, as front-liners in the field of battle, or even as couriers who’s senders need certainty their message will arrive. Adventuring parties who are graced with the inclusion of one of these masters of defense can rest assured that at least one of them will be making it back alive.

A Bulwark will tend to focus fully on a defensive standpoint in battle, as an overtly pressing offense might lead to gaps in your attention. In fact, some Bulwarks even refrain from having an actual offense entirely, relying on those around them to defeat their enemies while they spend their attention and energy on lasting as long as possible.

When creating a Bulwark, consider why your character might have needed to train such a rigorous defense. What training have they undergone to truly set themselves ahead of their peers? Perhaps you were a member of a royal guard, someone trained to protect at any cost. Or rather just a soldier who has taken to protecting themselves a bit further than most. A Bulwark could be anyone of the great strength needed to use heavy armors, and utilizes it to the fullest, and you get to decide just how your character does that.

Level Proficiency Bonus Features 1st +2 Defensive Stance, Weapon Mastery 2nd +2 Fortitude 3rd +2 Defensive Specialization 4th +2 Ability Score Improvement 5th +3 Extra Attack, Emissary 6th +3 Conditioning 7th +3 Specialization Feature 8th +3 Ability Score Improvement 9th +4 Dueling Stance 10th +4 Mental Fortitude 11th +4 Shattering Stance 12th +4 Ability Score Improvement 13th +5 Specialization Feature 14th +5 Reinforcing Fortitude 15th +5 Steel Endurance 16th +5 Ability Score Improvement 17th +6 Mountain Stance 18th +6 Specialization Feature 19th +6 Ability Score Improvement 20th +6 Adamantine Endurance
As a Bulwark, you gain the following class features.
Hit Dice: 1d10 per bulwark level Hit Points at 1st Level: 10 + your constitution modifier Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d10 (or 6) + your constitution modifier per Bulwark level after first.

Armor: Light, Medium, and Heavy Armor, Shields Weapons: Simple Weapons, Warhammers, Heavy Crossbows Tools: none Saving Throws: Constitution and Charisma Skills: Choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion

You start with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment granted by your background: (a) a warhammer or (b) a simple weapon of your choice and a shield A suit of chainmail armor (a) an explorer’s pack or (b) a diplomat’s pack (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) a shortbow and 20 arrows

While you are wearing heavy armor, you can choose to take up a defensive stance to bolster yourself for incoming force. As an action, you can give yourself a +2 bonus to your armor class and resistance to force damage for 1 minute, or until you are no longer wearing heavy armor. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your constitution modifier before completing a long rest.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice that you have proficiency with, such as maces and light crossbows. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of warhammers and handaxes.

At 2nd level, you can lessen the impact of weapons against you. While you are wearing heavy armor, and are hit by a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your bulwark level.

Additionally at 2nd level, you radiate an aura that compels your foes to battle against you, and you alone. While your defensive stance is active, enemies that start their turn within 10 feet of you must make a charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be forced to use their action to attack, or otherwise harm you.

When you reach 3rd level, you choose a defensive specialization that dictates the types of strategies you employ to protect yourself and others. Juggernaut Phalanx Rook Spellbreaker Unfettered Templar Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 13th, and 18th level.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase two ability scores of your choice by one. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

Additionally at 5th level, your voice carries with you a supernatural sense of purpose and authority. You gain a bonus to all charisma (intimidation and persuasion) checks equal to your strength modifier (minimum bonus of +1).
At 6th level, you gain an uncanny knack for endurance. You no longer suffer the adverse effects of a forced march, and are treated as having two less levels of exhaustion than you normally would.

At 9th level, you become harder to ignore by those you are engaged with. Creatures have disadvantage on the saving throw against your Dueling Stance feature if you have dealt damage to them since the start of your last turn.

At 10th level, you gain the ability to harden your mind to attacks with a similar effectiveness as your armor can block physical blows. You gain proficiency in intelligence or wisdom saving throws (your choice). You can replace your selection with the other whenever you finish a long rest.

When you reach 11th level, you learn to redirect the energy meant for you back to your attacker. While your defensive stance is active, you deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus when you attack with a weapon. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

Starting at 14th level, your ability to shrug off attacks extends to even the mightiest of blows. When you use your Fortitude feature, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the amount of damage you prevented. Once you gain these temporary hit points, you cannot do so again until you finish a short rest, or enter a new defensive stance.
At 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no remaining uses of your defensive stance, you regain one use.

When you reach 17th level, your stance becomes as unbreakable as the very earth itself. While your defensive stance is active, you cannot be moved against your will, and you are immune to the frightened condition and critical hits.
At 20th level, the duration of your defensive stance increases to 10 minutes, and the bonus it confers to your armor class increases to +4.
When multiclassing with the Bulwark class, use the following: Prerequisite: Strength 13 and Constitution 13 Proficiencies Gained: Light armor, Medium armor, Shields, and Heavy armor

Clad in rusted armor with a fizzling blade in their right hand, a warrior strikes down their goblin foe with the crackling might of a bolt of lightning. Electricity arcs up and down their blade, converging on the tip and electrocuting its unassuming victim. Laughter echoes across the dank walls of a dungeon as an elf sits, cross-legged, amongst the bodies of her victims, eyes clouded by maddening power. Though her victims show little signs of external damage, their eyes roll up into their sockets, leaving behind only a white gleam. Snowflakes whiz across the air in a beautiful miniature blizzard, centered on a Dragonborn with scales as white as the snow surrounding him. Raising his twin daggers, he weaves together a pattern of rime and frost that leaves his enemies disoriented in a dazzling display of elemental prowess. These individuals, regardless of origin, share one point in common; pure energy flows through their veins, seemingly bursting from their bodies with little control or conviction. Whether they’ve received this energy through a higher power’s blessing, an experiment gone terribly wrong, or were born as natural capacitors for magic, each of these individuals must quickly learn to channel their internal energy, else it burns them up from the inside.

A channeler is forced to learn to control their energy, as it can be dangerous to both themselves and others to leave it unmanaged and unchecked. How they choose to do so differs from channeler to channeler: some embrace the chaos caused by their energy, some try to hide it and seal it away as much as they can. Some notice the value of the power they hold and try to shape it to their whims, while others still allow their energy to shape themselves and their actions. Regardless of how they decide to use their power, there still comes the issue of channeling it in the first place.Channelers generally train their whole lives to control their energy, from the moment they receive it onwards. Particularly talented channelers might be able to channel their power into objects at will, though regardless of talent, mastery over their power requires hard work. What constitutes ‘mastery’, however, is different from channeler to channeler; some may tell you complete control represents mastery, while another may tell you that you’re not a master lest your mind and body are completely broken under the weight of your own might.
documents.s: A Channel for the Arcane Arts

documents.t: Most commonly, channelers use weapons to control their abilities. Channelers use the same martial training these swordsmen and soldiers use to visualize and concentrate their own energy. As martial warriors consider their weapons as extensions of their own body, it’s the easiest for channelers to use weapons as a focus. A trained channeler is as deft with a weapon as any other combatant, and can use their energy to amplify their combat abilities to their liking.

As you’re making a channeler, you must take a few things into consideration; where did the source of their internal energy come from? Was it the result of a deal with a higher being? A curse put on them by a practiced mage? An artificer’s experiment on humanoid test subjects? These may have all been reasons for the extensive energy you find yourself containing. In addition, think about the method that you used to channel your energy. How you managed to circumvent your energy destroying you internally is just as important as how you managed to receive that energy in the first place.

Level Proficiency Bonus Features Imbuement Dice Antes Known 1st +2 Arcane Channel, Elemental Imbuement 1d4 — 2nd +2 Arcane Attraction, Fighting Style 1d4 — 3rd +2 Ante 1d4 3 4th +2 Ability Score Improvement 1d4 3 5th +3 Overchanneled Imbuement 1d4 3 6th +3 Arcane Channel Feature 1d4 3 7th +3 Elemental Boon 1d4 4 8th +3 Ability Score Improvement 1d4 4 9th +4 Overchanneled Imbuement Improvement 1d4 4 10th +4 Elemental Imbuement Improvement, Raze 1d6 4 11th +4 Arcane Channel Feature 1d6 4 12th +4 Ability Score Improvement 1d6 5 13th +5 Up The Ante 1d6 5 14th +5 Flash Charge 1d6 5 15th +5 Greater Boon 1d6 5 16th +5 Ability Score Improvement 1d6 5 17th +6 Arcane Channel Feature 1d8 6 18th +6 Elemental Imbuement Improvement, Ruin 1d8 6 19th +6 Ability Score Improvement 1d8 6 20th +6 Pinnacle Channel 1d8 6
As a channeler, you gain the following class features.
Hit Dice: 1d10 per channeler level Hit Points at 1st Level: 10 + your Constitution Modifier Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d10 (or 6) + your Constitution modifier per (your class) level after 1st.

Armor: Light armor, medium armor Weapons: Simple weapons, longswords, rapiers Tools: None Saving Throws: Constitution, Intelligence Skills: Choose two from Acrobatics, Arcana, Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Perception, and Survival.

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background: (a) chain mail and a shield (if proficient) or (b) scale mail or (c) leather armor and 2 daggers (a) a longsword or (b) a rapier or (c) a martial weapon (if proficient) (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) two handaxes (a) a scholar’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your channeler spells. The way you channel your innate abilities relies greatly on your experience. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a channeler spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one Spell save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier Spell Attack modifier = your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Choose one outlet in which to channel your energy. Your choice grants you certain features and proficiencies when you choose it at 1st level. It also grants you additional features at 6th, 11th, and 17th level. The choices are detailed at the bottom of this document. Channel of Artistry Channel of Madness Channel of Volatility Channel of Containment Channel of Devastation

Your arcane energy is beginning to leak uncontrollably, forcing you to find a focus to channel it through. Starting at 1st level, whenever you finish a long rest, you can imbue your energy in one weapon you are proficient with. Choose a damage type from acid, fire, cold, lightning, or thunder. The weapon deals an additional 1d4 damage of the chosen type. This damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d6 at 10th level, and to 1d8 at 17th level. When an effect would deal damage using your Elemental Imbuement die, the damage type is the same as your Elemental Imbuement unless stated otherwise.

At 2nd level, your internal magical power tends to seek out various sources through which to channel itself to, allowing you to get a sense for what is magical and what’s not. As an action, you can sense the presence of magic in the area. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of each source of magic within 30 feet of you— whether it’s a magic item, a spell, or a creature created by a spell. You know which kind of magic source it is, but you do not know the details of the source; you can’t tell the type of magic item, the specifics of the spell, or the kind of creature. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

At 2nd level, you adopt a style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can’t take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if something in the game lets you choose again. Archery​ You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons. Dueling​ When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon. Great Weapon Fighting​ When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit. Two-Weapon Fighting​ When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack. Unarmed Fighting​ Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren’t wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8. At the start of each of your turns, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to one creature grappled by you.

At 3rd level, your elemental energy burns and crackles within you, proving to be a fickle source of power. You can use the energy to empower yourself, but you run the risk of your power backfiring on you. You gain three Ante options of your choice, detailed at the bottom of this document. You gain another at 7th level, 12th level, and 17th level. You have an amount of Ante charges equal to your Intelligence modifier. Each use of an Ante consumes a charge. You may not use more than one Ante at the same time. You replenish Ante charges on a short or long rest. Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you may replace one Ante option with another that you meet the prerequisites for. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Starting at 5th level, you gain more control over the energy channeled through your weapon of choice. Whenever you finish a long rest, choose two cantrips that share a damage type with your chosen Elemental Imbuement and have a casting time of one action or bonus action. Immediately after you hit with an attack from your imbued weapon, you may cast one of the chosen cantrips as a bonus action. If a spell allows you to choose the damage type you deal, the chosen type must match your Elemental Imbuement. At 9th level, you may choose two 1st level spells that share a damage type with your chosen Elemental Imbuement. You may cast either of those spells rather than a cantrip without expending a spell slot.

Starting at 7th level, your experience with channeling your energy through weapons is beginning to allow you to channel your energy through living beings as well. As a reaction whenever another ally within 30 feet hits with an attack roll, you can channel your energy through their attack. The attack deals bonus damage equal to your Elemental Imbuement die, and shares the damage type you’d chosen for your Elemental Imbuement. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a short or long rest.

Starting at 10th level, your imbued weapons are growing in destructive force, letting you use them to tear objects to shreds. Attacks made using your imbued weapons deal twice as much damage to objects and structures.

Starting at 13th level, the power of your Antes grows, but so do their destructive effects. When you use an Ante, you may choose to Up The Ante, making you roll your Elemental Imbuement die an extra time, adding it to the effect. If the Ante cares about whether the total is even or odd, rather than adding the die an extra time, you instead may use either roll. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

At 14th level, you’ve learned to quickly and deftly control the elemental energies inside of you. Once per day, as an action, you may change the damage type of your Elemental Imbuement, as well as the spells you’d chosen for your Overchanneled Imbuement. You may optionally also choose to imbue your energy in a different weapon.

At 15th level, the boons you bestow upon others strengthen to their peak. The elemental boon now deals extra damage equal to twice your Elemental Imbuement die, and the attack ignores damage resistances.

At 18th level, your magic energies can bring down the very foundations of structures around you. By spending one minute concentrating as if concentrating on a spell, you can plunge your imbued weapon into the ground and begin breaking the foundations of nearby buildings. Once one minute has passed, choose a non-magical object or structure within 60 feet. If that structure can fit within a 30 foot cube, it is immediately destroyed, crumbling to dust. If it is any larger, you can instead destroy a 30 foot cube portion of it within range.

At 20th level, you’ve reached the height of elemental control, and can display your mastery on a consistent basis. At the end of a long rest, choose two 2nd or 3rd level spells that share a damage type with your Elemental Imbuement; you may cast those spells at will or any time you can cast one of your Overchanneled Imbuements. If you use your Flash Charge feature, you may also exchange these spells for any others that fit the prerequisites. Additionally, you may upcast your 1st and 2nd level channelers spells to 3rd level.

Antes are a core part of a channeler’s toolkit, and are the representation of their capricious magic. Each ante provides some sort of benefit to you that can help you accomplish certain tasks or utilize certain abilities, but every single one runs the risk of backfiring, leading to inconvencience, injury, or even certain death. A good channeler knows when to use an ante and when not to take needless risks, but each and every channeler would do well to understand that no matter how many steps one might take to mitigate risk, chances of failure are never zero. Pinpoint Ante​ When you make an attack roll, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to it. If the attack misses, your AC decreases by an amount equal to the Elemental Imbuement die’s result until the end of your next turn. Reflex Ante​ When you make a dexterity saving throw, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the save. If the save fails, you take damage equal to twice the Elemental Imbuement die’s result. Prodigious Ante​ When you make a skill check in a skill you’re not proficient in, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the check. If the check fails, you subtract the Elemental Imbuement die’s result from all ability checks for the next hour. Quickstep Ante​ When someone makes an opportunity attack against you, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to your AC. If the attack hits, your speed is reduced by five times the result until the end of your turn. Blasting Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Devastation)​ When you make an attack roll, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If the attack hits, each creature of your choice other than the target within 15 feet takes damage equal to the result. If the attack misses, each creature other than the target within 15 feet of you takes damage equal to the result. Mindmeld Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Madness)​ When a creature makes a saving throw against a channeler spell you cast, you may subtract your Elemental Imbuement die from the save. If the save succeeds, you become the spell’s target, and your saving throw against the spell’s effect is reduced by your Elemental Imbuement die’s result. If the spell would require you to concentrate, it doesn’t require concentration when cast against you. Curtain-raiser Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Artistry)​ When you roll initiative, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the result. If you’re in the top half of initiative, you have advantage on attack rolls against each creature below you in the initiative order until the end of your next turn. If you’re in the bottom half of initiative, each creature above you in initiative has advantage on attack rolls against you until the end of your next turn. Unstable Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Volatility)​ Before you make an attack roll, call if the result will be even or odd. If the result matches your guess, add another Elemental Imbuement die to your Volatile Charge feature. If the results don’t match your guess, you take damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die. Fray Ante (Prerequisite: Channel of Containment)​ If you’re within 5 feet of an enemy, roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If the result is even, you regain hit points equal to three times the roll’s result. If the result is odd, your AC decreases by the roll’s result. Arcane Ante (Prerequisite: 5th Level)​ Whenever you cast a channeler spell, you may use this Ante. If the spell hits or if the target fails the save against it, you may add two rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die to that spell’s damage. If the spell misses or the target passes the save, you take damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die. Reactive Ante (Prerequisite: 5th Level)​ Whenever an attack roll is made against you, you may use this Ante as a reaction. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die; if the result is even, you gain immunity to the triggering attack’s damage until the end of the turn. If the result is odd, you gain vulnerability to the triggering attack’s damage until the end of the turn. Goading Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Devastation)​ When a creature rolls a saving throw against your Devastating Presence feature, you may force them to subtract your Elemental Imbuement die from the result. If they succeed, they add the Elemental Imbuement die’s result to their attack and damage rolls that target you until the end of their turn. Headspin Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Madness)​ If a creature within 30 feet of you rolls an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw with advantage, you may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the result. If they fail the save, you subtract the Elemental Imbuement die’s result from your saving throws for the next minute. Blitzkrieg Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Artistry)​ If you make an attack roll against a creature, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If you hit, your speed increases by an amount equal to five times the result until the end of your turn. If you miss, you fall prone and your speed is reduced by an amount equal to five times the result until the end of your turn. Surge Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Volatility)​ After you roll on the Volatile Surge table, you may use this ante. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die and call if the result will be odd or even. If you guess correctly, you may use the effects of both the new and the old roll. If you guess incorrectly, you may use neither effect. Grasp Ante (Prerequisite: 7th Level, Channel of Containment)​ When you make a Strength (athletics) check to grapple a creature, you can add your Elemental Imbuement die to the check’s result. If the creature succeeds against the grapple, you are restrained until the start of your next turn. Mental Ante (Prerequisite: 11th Level)​ When you make an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you may reduce the result by your Elemental Imbuement die. If you pass the save, you may add the Elemental Imbuement die’s result to the failed saving throw of a creature of your choice within 60 feet of you. Proactive Ante (Prerequisite: 11th Level)​ Whenever an attack roll is made against a creature other than you within 60 feet, you may use this Ante as a reaction. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die; if the result is even, they gain resistance to the triggering attack’s damage until the end of the turn. If the result is odd, you take damage equal to the triggering attack’s damage. Sticky Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Devastation)​ You may use this Ante at the start of a creature’s turn. If the creature ends their turn within 5 feet of you, they take damage equal to three rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die. If the creature ends their turn more than 5 feet away from you, you take force damage equal to three rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die. Hivemind Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Madness)​ When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you makes a saving throw or ability check that they’re not proficient in, if you’re proficient in that saving throw or ability check, you can roll your Elemental Imbuement die and add the result to their roll. If they fail, you take force damage equal to three times the result. Haphephobic Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Artistry)​ When you hit with an attack roll, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If the target damages you before the start of your next turn, you take force damage equal to five times the result. If the target does not damage you before the start of your next turn, they take damage equal to five times the result. Anti-Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Volatility)​ You may use this ante immediately after using another ante. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die; if the result is even, neither this Ante nor that Ante consumes an Ante charge. If the result is odd, you lose one Ante charge. Stance Ante (Prerequisite: 13th Level, Channel of Containment)​ When a creature hits you with an attack, roll a concentration check and add your Elemental Imbuement die. If the check succeeds, you gain resistance to the attack’s damage. If the check fails, you gain vulnerability to the attack’s damage. Gambler’s Ante (Prerequisite: 18th Level)​ When you use your last Ante charge, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die; If the result is even, you regain an amount of Ante charges equal to the roll. This amount cannot exceed your maximum. If the result is odd, your hit point total is set to 1. You may only use this Ante once per long rest. God Ante (Prerequisite: 18th Level)​ You may use this Ante as an action. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die; if the result is even, you may immediately cast a ninth level spell with a casting time of one action from any spell list without expending a spell slot. If the result is odd, you die and cannot be revived except by the effects of a wish spell. You may only use this Ante once per long rest. Warmind Ante (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Devastation)​ When you make a melee weapon attack, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. Up to that many other willing creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you may make one melee weapon attack as a reaction. If any of them miss, each creature takes damage equal to five times the result. InsanAnte (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Madness)​ When you cast an enchantment spell on one or more creatures, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If they fail the save, they take psychic damage equal to four times the result, and if any of them pass the save, you take force damage equal to four times the result. Masterpiece Ante (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Artistry)​ When you use your Flash Charge feature, roll your Elemental Imbuement die. The next time you cast a channeler spell, if it hits or if the spell’s target fails its save against it, you gain hit points and temporary hit points equal to three times the result. If it doesn’t hit or the target’s save is successful, you take damage equal to three times the result. Soulshredder Ante (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Volatility)​ When you use your Culmination of Volatility feature, you may roll your Elemental Imbuement die. If the result is even, rather than dying immediately, you regain half of your maximum hit points and your gear and equipment aren’t destroyed. If the result is odd, your soul is shredded into nonexistence and you cannot be revived by any means, even through divine intervention or a wish spell. Havoc Ante (Prerequisite: 20th Level, Channel of Containment)​ When you make an unarmed strike against a creature, they must make a strength saving throw against your spell save DC. Roll your Elemental Imbuement die and subtract it from the save. If they fail, they are knocked back a distance equal to ten times the die’s result. If they succeed, you are knocked back a distance equal to ten times the die’s result. The one knocked back by this effect takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet they traveled.
Ability Score Minimum: STR 13 or DEX 13, and INT 13 Armor: light armor, medium armor Weapons: simple weapons, longswords, rapiers

Those that follow this path believe that rather than hard training, true mastery comes with application. Like a branch drifting across a river, such practitioners make do with what’s thrown at them, adapting to the issues they are faced with and prospering in the worst of conditions.

At 2nd level, you find it easy to manipulate your techniques to fit their situations. As a bonus action, you can enter the flowing river stance for 1 minute, gaining the following benefits: If you focus a technique, you can choose whether it’s a mental or physical type for you. When you make a weapon attack with a technique, you can use your mental ability for attack and damage rolls rather than Strength or Dexterity. If a creature fails its save against your technique, you can use a reaction to regain mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up). After you use this feature, you must take a short or long rest before you can use it again. You can exit the flowing river stance as a bonus action. It ends early if you are incapacitated or if your turn ends and you haven’t used a technique since your last turn. You can enter the flowing river stance a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.

At 6th level, you improve upon your ability to adapt to change. When you enter the flowing river stance, choose a damage type aside from bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. You become resistant to that damage type until the flowing river stance ends.

At 14th level, you become adept at stringing techniques from different forms together. After spending mastery points to focus a technique while in the flowing river stance, you can use a bonus action to use another technique from a different martial form.

At 18th level, if you use three physical techniques or three mental techniques in a row, you gain a benefit: Physical. The next time a creature hits you with an attack until the end of your next turn, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against them. Mental. The next time you use a technique that forces a creature to make a save until the end of your next turn, they have disadvantage on that save.

Type: Varies Prerequisites: Novice, Drifter Make a weapon attack against a creature or object. The attack deals an amount of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus in additional psychic damage if this technique is mental or bludgeoning damage if this technique is physical. Focused (1 point, or 0 points if in flowing river stance). If the target is a creature, they must make a Constitution saving throw or have their speed halved until the end of their next turn. Your movement speed increases by the same amount until the end of your turn.

Type: Varies Prerequisites: Intermediate, Drifter, Flowing river stance If you take damage that matches the damage type you chose for your flowing river stance, you can use your reaction to become immune to that damage instead. Focused (1 point). In the same reaction, you can use another technique that includes a weapon attack.

Type: Varies Prerequisites: Advanced, Drifter The next technique you use from a different form until the end of your next turn can be focused with 1 less mastery point (min. 1) Focused (1 point). The next technique you focus does not require mastery points, and once performed, you can immediately make a weapon attack against a creature or object.

Type: Varies Prerequisites: Master, Drifter, Flowing river stance Duration: Concentration, 1 min. If you use a physical or mental technique, you gain a benefit. Physical. If you hit a creature with a weapon attack during this technique, they must succeed on a wisdom saving throw or be forced to use their action to make one melee weapon attack against you on their next turn. Mental. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack during this technique, they must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. Focused (1 point). Whenever you use a physical or mental technique, it counts as if you had used three physical or three mental techniques respectively.
Exorcists use their spiritual abilities to purge the lands of evil spirits and those that would do harm to society. With pure souls and unmatched bravery, they face the most vile of creation head-on.

At 3rd level, you become adept in tracking down and hunting all manners of evil. You gain proficiency in Investigation and Survival, and undead and fiends have disadvantage on saving throws against your exorcist arts. If the target of your spirit tether is a creature and is reduced to 0 hit points, you can regain a number of spirit points equal to half your spiritualist level (rounded down). If the target was an undead or a fiend, you regain additional spirit points equal to your wisdom modifier. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your power over evil forces.

If your tethered target is a creature, you can use your action to spend 1 spirit point to root your target in place. The target must make a strength saving throw or be restrained for one minute and take 2d6 radiant damage at the start of each of its turns. A target can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending this effect on a success.

You can use an action and spend 1 spirit point to lash out at your target with your righteous spirit. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the target takes 4d6 radiant damage, taking half of the damage on a success.

You can use an action and spend 1 spirit point to cover your target in radiant light. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or be covered in an aura of light that emits bright sunlight for 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet. When the target fails its saving throw against your radiant lash while this sunlight persists, you can blind them until the end of its next turn.

At 6th level, you can use an action to exorcise creatures of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. For each creature, you can spend 1 spirit point to end one effect that’s causing the creature to be charmed, frightened, or possessed.

At 13th level, you can cleanse an area and temporarily ward it from evil. As an action, you can spend 3 spirit points to create a field in a 20-foot-radius sphere at a point you can see within 120 feet of yourself. The area becomes pure, and creatures of your choice within the area cannot be frightened, charmed, or possessed, and have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws. The field lasts for one minute, whereupon its cleansing abilities fade and its effects end.
At 18th level, you master your abilities to drive evil from this world. You learn the following spirit art:

You can use 10 minutes of chanting and 20 spirit points to attempt to banish a creature from existence. At the end of the ten minutes, the target must make a Charisma saving throw or be banished. Regardless of the target’s native plane, they are banished to an empty and infinite demiplane that is accessible by nothing less than a god. It is impossible for the creature to leave the demiplane from the inside by any means. While banished, the target does not need to breathe, eat, or sleep, and it doesn’t age. Divination spells can’t locate or perceive the target. You can spend 10 minutes to bring a banished creature back from its banishment. If you’re within 30 feet of the location the target was originally banished from, you can bring them back to a point you can see within 30 feet of you.

Since the dawn of humanity, there has always been a frontier to conquer. Between the wastes of the east, the fires of the hells, and the vastness of the astral plane, there has always been those that dared to tread the road less traveled. Traversing each regional obstacle brings with it a unique solution— the hellfire engines of Avernus, the spelljammers of the astral sea, and the machinations inspired by the great inventor Kwalish, all formed to blaze a trail through every path they come across. Through the use of arcane influence and artificing prowess, a new school of thought has arisen among artificers; why spend your days walking through the most hazardous conditions when you can drive, sail, or fly through them instead? Thus, under the influence of vehicles from all different planes, the most ingenious of traveling artificers got to work. Features: 3rd Level - Bonus Proficiency 3rd Level - Greaser Spells 3rd Level - Arcane Vehicle 5th Level - Extra Attack 9th Level - Enhanced Modifications 15th Level - Overdrive

When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with smith’s tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan’s tools of your choice. In addition, you gain proficiency in land and water vehicles

Starting at 3rd level, you always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Greaser Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare. Artificer Level Spells 3rd Level - Burning Hands, Fog Cloud 5th Level - Locate Object, Dust Devil 9th Level - Slow, Stinking Cloud 13th Level - Hallucinatory Terrain, Sickening Radiance 17th Level - Passwall, Rary's Telepathic Bond

By 3rd level, you’ve successfully managed to create your first vehicle for traversal. At the end of a long rest, you may create a vehicle by choosing one of each of the following vehicle mod options below. The vehicle is a large magical object that can be mounted as if it were a creature, after which it acts as a controlled mount. It shares its turn with you, and can only take the dash and disengage actions. It is immune to psychic damage and uses your saving throw bonuses when applicable. If the mending spell is cast on it, it regains 2d6 hit points. If it has been destroyed within the last hour, you can use your smith’s tools as an action to repair it, provided you are within 5 feet of it and you expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher. The vehicle returns to working order after 1 minute with half of its hit points restored. At the end of a long rest, you can create a new arcane vehicle if you have your smith’s tools with you. If you already have an arcane vehicle from this feature, the first one is immediately destroyed. The vehicle is also destroyed if you die.

Each vehicle can only have one vehicle mod of each option listed below active at one time. At the end of a short rest, you can use your smith’s tools to replace one vehicle mod of your choosing with another eligible of the same category. If a vehicle mod has prerequisites, you must meet them to learn it. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class. Weapons mounted on your vehicle are simple weapons you are proficient in that can only be used by yourself while you are mounted. If the weapon requires an attack roll, you can add your Intelligence modifier, instead of your Strength or Dexterity, to the attack and damage rolls. Use your spell save DC for any saving throw related to your weapon. These weapons can be infused.
