You have a pool of spell levels equal to half your wizard level (rounded up), which you can use to recover your expended spell slots. When you finish a short rest, you can spend any number of spell levels from the pool to regain expended spell slots of a combined spell level equal to the amount of levels you expended. For example, if you’re a 4th-level wizard, you have a pool of two spell levels. You can spend these to regain a 2nd-level spell slot, or two 1st-level spell slots. You regain all expended spell levels from this pool when you finish a long rest. Ritual Master You can cast any spell in your spellbook with the ritual tag as a ritual, even if you don’t have it prepared.

When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of the eight schools: Abjuration, Conjuration, Divination, Enchantment, Evocation, Illusion, Necromancy, or Transmutation. Alternate traditions are also available, and grant their own features. Your choice grants you features at 2nd level, and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

At 3rd level, your mastery over certain spells grows onto you, and you can cast them with little effort. Choose one 1st-level spell from your spellbook. You always have the chosen spell prepared, and it does not count towards your total number of spells prepared. You can cast a signature spell at its lowest level without expending a spell slot. Once you cast a signature spell in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest. When you reach higher levels, you gain additional signature spells of higher levels. You gain one 2nd-level signature spell at 7th level, and one 3rd-level signature spell at 13th level.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

At 5th level, your ability to adapt your spells throughout the day increases. Whenever you finish a short rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the spells you have prepared for another spell from the book.

When you reach 7th level, your understanding of magic has come to the point where you can modify some of the properties of the spells you know. You can spend 10 minutes in study, requiring your full concentration and attention (as if concentrating on a spell) to modify one of the spells you have prepared. At the end of the 10 minutes, the chosen spell gains one cosmetic effect of your choice, and one of the following changes of your choice: Components: Remove one of the spell’s components; Verbal, Somatic, or Material. You cannot remove the Material component of a spell that consumes the component. Concentration: If the spell requires Concentration, damage can’t break your concentration on the spell. Damage Type: If the spell has a damage type, replace it with one of the following types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, or Thunder. If the spell has multiple damage types, you change only one of them. Range: If the spell has a range of at least 5 feet and doesn’t have a range of self, increase its range by five times your wizard level. Ritual: If the spell lacks the ritual tag and has a casting time of at least one minute, give it the ritual tag, unless the spell is of 9th level. Targets: If the spell affects one or more creatures and doesn’t have a range of self, it now affects only your allies or enemies (your choice when you cast the spell). This modification lasts until you modify a spell again or until you finish a long rest. The altered spell cannot be added to your spellbook.

Your capacity to experiment with spells has reached new heights at 13th level, granting you the ability to save your work for future use. While a spell is modified with your Spellforge feature, you can copy it into your spellbook as if it were a normal spell. Doing so requires 30 minutes of work and costs 1,000 gp per spell level, representative of your work grounding the spell in your own notation. Upon completion, give the spell a name, and the spell is added to your spellbook. It is considered a wizard spell, and you are thereafter able to prepare the spell as normal. A spell created by this feature can only ever hold two modifications from your Spellforge feature. Any attempts to add more than two modifications to the same spell will fail.

At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Your 1st and 2nd level signature spells, as well as any created spell based on them, are able to be cast at will.

When you reach 20th level, your capacity to work with and create branching spells based upon your signature spells reaches untold heights. When you use your spellforge and spellset features on a signature spell, or a spell based on your signature spells, the new limit of modifications is 4, instead of 2. Additionally, you can prepare a number of extra spells equal to your intelligence modifier. These extra spells must be spells created by spellset based on your signature spells.

Prerequisite: Skeleton Your wisdom score increases by one. You can designate one inanimate skeleton by touch as an action. After 30 days, an invisible spiritual connection is made between you and the skeleton. If you are destroyed while such a connection is active, you rise again from the skeleton you had designated. You can only have one skeleton designated in this way at a time.

Prerequisite 4th Level, Spellcasting Feature Description You have learned to channel your magic through a deck of cards. You can use a card deck as your spellcasting focus, and you gain the following benefits: Card Tricks. You learn the Prestidigitation cantrip and can use it to create illusions that duplicate the effects of stage magic. When you use Prestidigitation in this way, you can conceal the verbal and somatic components of the spell as ordinary conversation and card handling. Hidden Ace. When you finish a long rest, you can choose one first level spell from your class's spell list and imbue that spell into a card. The chosen spell must have a casting time of 1 action. The card remains imbued with this spell for 8 hours. While the card is imbued with the spell, you can use a bonus action to flourish the card and cast the spell within. The card then immediately loses its magic.

Prerequisite Aasimar Description You learn how to better control your celestial power, and are able to draw more energy from it. You gain one of the following benefits, which will replace your Celestial Revelation feature. You may activate your Celestial Legacy as a bonus action or an action (your choice). Your transformation lasts for 1 minute or until you end it as a bonus action. Once you transform using your Celestial Legacy, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest. Celestial Reaper. This feature replaces your Necrotic Shroud. Your eyes briefly become pools of darkness, and ghostly, flightless wings sprout from your back temporarily. Creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you that can see you must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn. Furthermore, while they are frightened in this way, you have advantage on any attack rolls against them. Until the transformation ends, once on each of your turns, you can deal extra necrotic damage to one target when you deal damage to it with an attack or a spell. The extra damage equals your level.

Prerequisite: Changeling Your ability to shapechange is more than skin deep, and you are able to assume more forms than the average Changeling. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Consititution score by 1, to a maximum of 20 When you use your Shapechanging trait, you can choose one of these benefits which lasts until you change your shape again: - Darkvision You adapt your eyes and gain Darkvision out to 60ft. - Aquatic Adaption You sprout gills and are able to breath underwater, and you gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. - Natural Weapons You grow claws, fangs, spines, horns or a different natural weapon of your choice. Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage as appropriate, and you are considered proficient with unarmed strikes. - Wings You grow wings, which can take on whatever appearance/shape you desire. You gain 30 ft. of flying speed. - Extra Appendage You grow a prehensile tail, tentacles, crab claws, or another limb of your choice, which can only be used to grapple someone as an action (even if your main hands are currently full), and cannot be used to hold equipment, weapons, or any other objects. You can use these features an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus (shared among all), resetting on a Long Rest.

Prerequisite: Defensive Duelist, 12th level+ You turn a parry into the opening for a deadly counter. Counterstance. While you benefit from the AC bonus of your Defensive Duelist Parry, you gain the following special reaction: Counterattack. When a creature misses you with a melee attack, due to the AC Bonus from the Defensive Duelist feat, you can make one melee weapon attack against it. You can use this reaction once on each creature’s turn, except your own. You can only use this counterattack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest* Ranged Parry. When you aren’t wielding a shield, you can also use your Defensive Duelist Parry against a ranged weapon attack that targets only you.

The Daredevil fighter thrives on style, versatility and unpredictably. Their use of different weapon types makes them dangerous to any foe and they gain more confidence the more stylish their fighting is.

Starting at 3rd level, every time you make an attack of a type different from the previous attack in the current combat, you gain one Style point. You have a maximum amount of style points equal to your proficiency bonus. When you roll Initiative your Style points reset to 0. Attack types are classified as: Melee weapon attack, Ranged weapon attack and thrown attacks. Style Points can be used to power your Flairs. Flairs:​ Wide attack: If you hit with a melee attack, you may spend 2 Style points to deal melee damage equal to half your Fighter level to all foes within 5 feet of your target. Laser Focus: Spend 2 Style Points to gain advantage on your next attack roll. Range Extender: You can add 10 feet to any ranged or thrown weapon's normal range for every point spent Rush: Gain 10 feet of movement speed for each Style Point spent until the end of your turn. Burst (4th level and up): As a bonus action, Spend 3 Style points to make a weapon attack.
At 3rd level, whenever you make an attack roll with a weapon, you can sheathe it and draw another in the same action. You can only do this once per action.

From 7th level you have a choice between staying in action and fighting defensively or moving around or to continue as is. As a bonus action you can choose to either fight or flee from combat. Fight: As a Bonus action you can give yourself a Bonus to your AC equal to the amount of Style Points you spend. This bonus lasts until the end of your next turn or until you are incapacitated. While Fight is active you cannot gain more Style points. Flight: You can spend 2 Style points to disengage, you can't be targeted by opportunity attacks. You gain an additional 10 feet of movement until the end of your turn for every additional Style Point spent.

You can choose an additional Fighting Style. Additionally, using the Disengage, Dodge or Dash actions also builds your Style chain. For example: If you use a dodge action and make an attack on your next turn or vice versa you also gain a Style Point

Starting at 15th level, when an enemy within 30 feet of you gets incapacitated or restrained you can use 2 Style Points as an reaction to dash straight toward the enemy. You move 10 feet for every point spent (minimum 2 points) and can spend additional Style for added Rush movement. You can sheath your current weapon and draw another as part of the dash and make a single attack against that target.

From 18th level, once per short rest you can expend 6 Style points as an action to trigger your Inferno action. Inferno action: Can attack 6 times, ignore the loading and ammunition properties if the weapon has it. Any Critical hit deals an additional 10 damage of the weapons damage type. These attacks don't provide any Style points

The embodiment of grit, luck, and a well-placed shot, fighters who choose this martial archetype strive to emulate paradigms of accuracy. Deadeyes generally prefer fighting from comfortable ranges, employing the use of crossbows, firearms, and even throwing knives if a situation calls for them. 3rd Level - Perfect Sixth 7th Level - Line ‘em Up 10th Level - Gambit 15th Level - Duelist’s Aim 18th Level - High Noon

Once per attack action beginning at 3rd level, when you make a ranged weapon attack roll against a creature, you can add a d6 to the result. You can add the d6 before or after seeing the results of the attack roll, but before the effects are applied. If the result of the d6 is a 6, you severely injure your target. Roll on the severe injury table to see the effect of the injury. Severe Injury Table​ 2d6 | Severe Injury 2 | Shock. The target is stunned until the end of its next turn. 3 | Fracture. The target can only take either an action, bonus action, or move on its next turn. 4 | Punctured Lung. The target gains one level of exhaustion for the next minute. 5 | Crushed Throat. The target cannot speak, use verbal components, or use any features that involve its voice until the end of its next turn. 6 | Crushed Grip. The target drops anything it is currently holding, including grappled creatures. 7 | Whiplash. The attack deals one additional die of weapon damage. 8 | Broken Leg. The target’s movement speed is halved until the end of its next turn. 9 | Embedded Ammunition. Until the end of its next turn, for every 5 feet the target moves, it takes 1d6 slashing damage. 10| Tear. The target has disadvantage on melee attacks until the end of its next turn. 11| Blind. The target is blinded until the end of its next turn. 12| Dead Shot. The triggering hit becomes a critical hit. Before you make a ranged weapon attack, you can take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If you hit, you apply a severe injury immediately. You can only apply one severe injury with each attack action. A creature cannot be affected by the same severe injury more than once at a time, and a creature can expend one use of legendary resistance to ignore a severe injury’s effect.

At 7th level, you become a master at hitting successive targets. When you take the attack action on your turn, each time you target a different creature than any other you’ve targeted this turn, you gain a cumulative +1 bonus to the attack roll.

At 10th level, when you roll initiative, you can gambit a d4, d6, d8, or d10. Roll the chosen die and subtract it from your initiative. Until the end of your next turn, every creature below you in initiative takes extra damage when hit with your ranged attack rolls equal to the chosen die.
At 15th level, when you use the attack action to make a ranged weapon attack and you hit at least three consecutive attacks, your third attack inflicts a severe injury.

At 18th level, you are adept at ending multiple targets at once. As an action, choose any number of targets that you can see within a cone the size of your weapon’s short range, up to 60 feet. You may make one ranged weapon attack against each target you chose inflicting the Dead Shot severe injury with each of them. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.

Dragonborn and Draconic Bloodline Sorcerers, Drakewarden Rangers and Ascendant Dragon Monks are updated to include the new types of dragons. New racial types follows gem dragonborn guidelines, This updated only changes the given Damage and Resistance types. -NEW- Time Force Moonstone Radiant Solar Radiant Lunar Cold Deep Psychic -Traditional- Black Acid Blue Lightning Brass Fire Bronze Lightning Copper Acid Gold Fire Green Poison Red Fire Silver Cold White Cold -Gem- Amethyst Force Crystal Radiant Emerald Psychic Sapphire Thunder Topaz Necrotic

Prerequisite Dual Wielder feat Description Excessive training and mastery of fighting with two weapons has allowed you to make use of your attacking momentum as well as to strike swiftly against those that would grant you an opportunity If you have hit with at least three attacks on your turn, including your two-weapon fighting bonus attack. You can make another attack as part of that bonus action When a creature provokes an opportunity attack from you while you are engaged in two-weapon fighting, you can make one attack with each weapon you are wielding as part of that reaction, instead of a single attack.

Exposure to distant forces - those that observe from beyond time or space - has left a mark on your soul. You now wield magic that shields and strikes in equal measure. Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20., You learn the sanctuary spell and one 1st-level spell of your choice. The 1st-level spell must be from the abjuration or evocation school of magic. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

Wondrous Item, varies Attunement Requires Attunement Description These magical gloves allow you to throw objects at astounding speeds. When you make a ranged weapon attack using a non-magical thrown weapon, the weapon gains a bonus to attack and damage rolls and is considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage. The bonus depends on this item’s rarity. Additionally, if you attack with a thrown weapon with advantage, you deal one additional weapon damage die in addition to the weapon’s normal damage. +1 : Uncommon +2 : Rare +3 : Very Rare

Weapon (glaive), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement by a creature with a Strength score of 15 or higher Description This magic glaive has tattered remains of a banner from the base of its blade and coiled around its shaft. The color and symbol have long faded and forgotten but whose task still persists. This weapon feels heavier than it looks to the wielder. Some say the banner appears at moments when the glaive is swung, showing the vibrant colors it once had. You have a +2 bonus to attack rolls made with this weapon. You also gain the following abilities. Strength in Numbers. You gain an additional +1 bonus to attack rolls for each friendly creature within 20 feet of you up to a maximum of +3(total bonus of +5). You also give a +1 bonus to attack rolls to friendly creatures within range. Assisted Assault. While you have at least one friendly creature within 30 feet of you, you deal an extra 3d4 of the weapon's damage on hit. Alternatively, you can forgo the extra damage at the start of your turn to give one friendly creature an extra 3d4 weapon damage on one attack they make on their next turn.

Prerequisite: Ritual Caster feat (2014 or 2024); Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score of 18 or higher Your mastery of ritual magic reaches new heights. You gain the following benefits: • Ability Score Increase. Increase the same ability score you chose for the Ritual Caster feat (Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma) by 1, to a maximum of 20. • Quick Ritual. Once more per long rest, you can cast a ritual spell at its normal casting time instead of adding 10 minutes. • Expanded Ritual Repertoire. You can learn one additional ritual spell of each level equal to or lower than your spellcasting ability modifier(maximum 5). • Growth of Knowledge. For each level you gain, you may replace one ritual spell of that level with another once on a level up, or when you PERMANENTLY increase your casting modifier.

Prerequisite: Proficiency with at least one type of hammer You have become adept at using hammers and can make use of their crushing weight against your opponents. When you wield a hammer and attack a creature with it, the target's AC is reduced by 2 for that attack, and you ignore the detrimental effects of the heavy property of hammers. Additionally, once per turn, when you hit a creature with a hammer, you can immediately take the shove action targeting the same creature. Hammers: Light Hammer, Warhammer, Lucerne Hammer, Maul

Description You are a master hurler of thrown weapons and can make shots that others find impossible, impaling your foes with the greatest of ease. You gain the following benefits: Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your thrown weapon attack rolls. Pinning Impalement: When you hit a creature with a thrown weapon attack from a spear, javelin or trident, you may attempt to impale them onto an adjacent surface. The creature must make a DC 8+PB+STR strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is pinned to the surface for 1 minute, or until it or another creature within reach of it uses an action to remove the weapon. A creature impaled by the weapon has its speed reduced to 0. If a flying creature with no adjacent surface is impaled this way, instead reduce their movement speed by 10ft until the weapon is removed as an action. Pinning Impalement can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all uses on a long rest.

Prerequisite Proficiency in a Martial weapon Description Iaijutsu is the martial art of drawing a weapon and attacking with it in the same fluid motion. It is the foundation of some forms of dueling in Kara-Tur, and its masters are feared and respected throughout Rokugan and other lands where iaijutsu is practiced. When you draw a weapon in combat, you have advantage on the first attack you make with that weapon until the end of the turn. If that attack hits, you may reroll the weapon's damage dice, taking the higher rolls.

Prerequisite: Vedalken “Perfection is a myth. Progress is measurable.” Your relentless pursuit of improvement turns every flaw into a chance for refinement. You gain the following benefits: +1 ASI to any ability score up to a maximum of 20 Analytical Adjustment. When you miss a melee/ranged/spell attack, should the next attack be made with the same weapon, or the same spell, against the same creature/object, that attack can be made with advantage and adding half of your ability modifier to that attack roll.

Prerequisite Leonin Description Your ancestry manifests in your fierceness; the pride of Oreskos echoes through you. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the frightened condition on yourself. Your natural weapons count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. The range of your Daunting Roar trait increases to 30 feet and you can add your Charisma modifier to its Save DC. Additionally, you regain a use of this trait when you bring a Huge or larger creature to 0 hit points.

Prerequisite: Proficiency with at least one type of light-blade Description You have become adept at using light-blades, allowing you to quickly put out attacks with them. When you hit with a light-blade, the target and up to one other creature within 5 feet of you takes slashing damage equal to half your dexterity modifier as you cut across them. Additionally, when you score a critical hit with a light-blade, the weapon's damage die becomes 1d12 instead of it's usual amount. Light-Blades: Dagger, Sickle

Prerequisite: Proficiency with at least one type of mace Description You have become adept at using maces, and can lever their use more effectively. When you attack with a mace, you deal bludgeoning damage equal to your strength modifier if you miss on the attack roll. Additionally, when you hit a creature with a mace, you can reduce that targets AC by 1 for one minute so long as they are wearing armor. You can do so no more than once per turn, and you cannot reduce a targets AC to a score lower than they would be without armor. Maces: Flail, Mace, Morningstar

Prerequisite: Mage Slayer Description Guarded Mind: If you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you can cause yourself to succeed instead. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest, but you can only regain uses of this ability up to twice per day through short rests. Spellbreaker: When you hit a creature with an attack as part of your reaction granted by the *Mage Slayer* feat, and that creature is casting a spell, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw as if the creature were concentrating on a spell. On a failed save, the spell is interrupted, and the spell slot and action used to cast it are wasted. If the target is concentrating on a spell, they make their concentration save immediately after their Constitution save for this ability. You may use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all uses upon completing a short or long rest.

Description Your training has taught you to strike faster and in key points rather than rely on brute force. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes. You can roll a d4 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strikes.

Description You master performance so that you can command any stage. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency in the Performance skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it. While performing, you can try to distract one humanoid you can see who can see and hear you. Make a Charisma(Performance) check contested by the humanoid’s Wisdom (Insight) check. If your check succeeds, you grab the humanoid’s attention enough that it makes Wisdom (Perception) and Intelligence (Investigation) checks with disadvantage until you stop performing.

A Phalanx draws their strength from their allies and coordination. Phalanx make excellent commanders as their leadership and guidance helps to assure not only their own success, but their entire unit’s as well. Features: 3rd Level - Tactical Commander 3rd Level - Unbreakable Formation 7th Level - Tactical Authority 13th Level - Perfect Block 18th Level - Battle Tide

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain access to your cohesion die, which is a d4. Other features will refer to your cohesion die, and will allow you to roll it. Your cohesion die is not expended when rolled. Your cohesion die increases to a d6 at 7th level, to a d8 at 13th, and to a d10 at 18th.

Additionally at 3rd level, you learn to weave your own defenses into those around you, resulting in a stronger whole for both you and your allies. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you gains a bonus to saving throws equal to one roll of your cohesion die. Additionally, creatures of your choice that start their turn within that range gain a +1 bonus to their armor class for each creature within 10 feet of you, with a maximum bonus equal to half your proficiency bonus.

At 7th level, you gain the ability to have greater control over how a fight will play out. When you enter your defensive stance, choose either the dodge, disengage, or dash action. Creatures of your choice within 5 feet of you while your stance is active will be unable to take the chosen action. You may select a new action from the specified list at the start of each of your turns until your stance ends (no action required). Additionally, creatures of your choice within the same range (other than you) gain a bonus to damage rolls equal to a roll of your cohesion die. They can use this bonus no more than once per turn.

Your ability to use shields extends to protecting your allies as well as you beginning at 13th level. When an ally within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to give them a bonus to their armor class equal to one roll of your cohesion die. If this bonus causes the attack to miss, you may use this reaction again, even if you have already used your reaction this round.

When you reach 18th level, your ability to shift the tide of battle with your presence alone has been realized. As an action, you can grant each creature of your choice within 20 feet of you temporary hit points equal to twice your Bulwark level, and remove all conditions of your choice from them. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

Description You can keep your enemies at bay with reach weapons. You gain the following benefits: When you take the Attack action and attack with only a glaive, lance, pike, quarterstaff, spear, or trident, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon. This attack uses the same ability modifier as the primary attack. The weapon's damage die for this attack is a d4, and it deals bludgeoning damage. While you are wielding a glaive, halberd, lance, pike, quarterstaff, spear, or trident, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter the reach you have with that weapon.

Prerequisite: Skeleton Your Constitution Score increases by 1. The necromancy that stitched you together is shockingly good at keeping you intact. When you become stabilized as a result of succeeding three death saving throws, you regain hit points equal to your level.

Prerequisite Elf Description You are descended from a master of the double-bladed scimitar, and some of that mastery has passed on to you. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Dexterity or Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20. While you are holding a double-bladed scimitar with two hands, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. A double-bladed scimitar has the finesse property when you wield it.

Prerequisite Shifter Description Your heritage has opened you to exceptional abilities as you tap into the unchecked powers that dwell in your blood. Increase your Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20. You can use your Shifting trait as a reaction to taking damage (you apply the temporary hit points before taking the damage). Each of your transformations also gain one more effect: Beasthide. You gain resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (Your choice when you shift). Longstooth. You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift. If you use your Shifting trait as a reaction, you can use your fangs to make an unarmed strike against a target within range as part of the reaction. Swiftstride. You gain climbing speed equal to your movement speed. Wildhunt. You don't suffer from disadvantage when making an attack roll against a target within 30 feet of you.
General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+) Any firearm that could normally be loaded as an action, can now also be reloaded as a bonus action.

Prerequisite Dexterity 15 or higher Description Your reflexes show moments of great ability as a result of your training. You have the following benefits: When you attack for the first time on your turn, you can have advantage on the attack roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. When your speed reaches to zero due to using it all or from an effect, you can use your reaction to gain an extra 10 feet to your speed. You can't use this reaction if the effect inflicted you with the grappled or restrained condition.

Prerequisite Proficiency with at least one type of sword Description You have become adept at using swords and can maneuver them effectively as a result. When you wield a sword, it gains the finesse property if it does not already have it and lacks the heavy property. Additionally, when a creature misses you with a melee attack while you are wielding a sword, you can use your reaction to make one attack with the sword against that creature. Swords: Short Sword, Scimitar, Rapier, Longsword, Greatsword

Prerequisite Tortle Description You have a higher grasp in making full use of your shell to better protect yourself and others. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20. Your Natural Armor trait now provides a base AC of 18 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). As a reaction when you are forced to make a Dexterity saving throw, you can choose which of the two will take effect: You gain a +4 bonus to Dexterity saving throws until the end of your next turn. All creatures within 5 feet of you are considered to have half cover against any harmful attacks or effects while within range until the end of your next turn. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you've finished a short or long rest.

Starting at 3rd level, after you make a weapon attack using the attack action you can use a free action to swap to another weapon. When you attack with a weapon, you receive a bonus to the attack based on the list below, however you may only benefit from a single bonus once per turn, even if your attack misses; You can however receive an additional bonus if you attack with a different weapon that causes a different type of damage. Ranged weapons do not benefit from Deft Grip, nor do generic “Elemental Weapons” (which collectively count as a single weapon), consumable items that grant additional damage, or spells. Deft Grip DC: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier Damage Type Effect Bonus Damage Bludgeoning The heavy blow causes both stone and steel to crumple. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≥ 15 1d6 or 2d6 bludgeoning damage Piercing A swift thrust gives you extra reach. +5ft attack range 1d6 piercing damage Slashing A swift slice carves through lightly armored opponents with ease. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≤ 15 1d6 or 2d6 slashing damage Acid The acid begins to eat away at flesh and damage armor. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, the creature’s AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn. At level 10 the AC reduction is increased to 2, and at level 20 it is increased to 3. 1d6 acid damage Cold Frost begins to coalesce around the creature’s body, restricting movement. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature’s speed is reduced by half until the end of your next turn. 1d6 cold damage Fire Flames engulf the target. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is set ablaze and takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of their turn. The fame can be put out by a suitable liquid or by using an action to extinguish it. 1d6 fire damage Force The weapon impacts with incredible force. Strength saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is knocked prone. 1d6 force damage Lightning Lightning arcs to the flesh of another creature on impact. A random hostile creature within 10ft is chosen. That creature makes a dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, they take the full damage of the attack. 1d6 lightning damage Necrotic The necrotic energy tears apart facsimiles of life. Doubled damage against temporary hp and creatures not in their original form (wildshape, poly, true-poly, shapechange, etc). Any damage that goes over the temp HP or the HP of the transformed creature is not doubled when applied to their HP/base form. 1d6 necrotic damage Poison Poison seeps into the wound. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature suffers from the poisoned condition. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of their turns. 1d6 poison damage Psychic Psychic damage racks the mind of the target. The creature has disadvantage on any concentration saving throws for the damage caused by this attack. 1d6 psychic damage Radiant Radiant light bursts from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is blinded. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 radiant damage Thunder A thundercrack roars forth from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is deafened. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 thunder damage

At 3rd level, when you successfully hit another creature with a weapon that benefits from the Deft Grip bonus you receive a +1 to hit and to damage for your next attack if your next attack will also benefit from the Deft Grip bonus. These bonuses stack then reset to zero at the end of your turn.

Starting at 7th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you take the Attack action on your turn and have advantage on an attack roll against against one of the targets, you can forgo the advantage for that roll to make an additional weapon attack against that target, as part of the same action. You can do so no more than once per turn.

Starting at 10th level you can expend a use of your Action Surge to cause your melee attacks to strike any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target. This benefit lasts for a single turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn.

Starting at level 15 you can expend a use of your Action Surge to focus all of your ability into a singular strike. Instead of making multiple attacks, you make a single attack against a target, and if it hits that attack is essentially multiplied by however many attacks you have remaining, including bonuses for each attack from Deft Grip and Flowing Stance; Additionally, after you use this ability, you can make no more attacks on the same turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn. This ability must be declared prior to knowing if the Focused Strike hits.

At level 18, attunement slots for weapons that require attunement can shared in a single slot however, you can not dual wield weapons that require attunement without using a second slot, you receive no benefit from the weapon when it is not in use (such as auras or other passive buffs), and you can use one of the weapons at a time.

Armor (shield), very rare Attunement: Requires Attunement Description A ring of runes runs along this shield's circumference. While holding this shield, you gain a +2 bonus to AC. This shield has 6 charges, and it regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you take damage that isn't bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing damage, you can use your reaction to expend one charge to produce the effects of a 1st-level Absorb Elements spell, but it can also absorb force, necrotic, poison, or radiant damage. This feature does not function if the triggering damage is paired with bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing damage.

Very Rare, Weapon (Firearm) Attunement Requires Attunement Description An unstable device that outputs a staggering amount of energy the longer it remains active. The weapon has a normal range of 60 feet and a long range of 180 feet, and it has the two-handed property. It deals 1 fire damage on a hit. Unstable - The weapon's damage cannot be modified by your ability modifier, or any other bonus provided by items, spells, or class features. However, for each consecutive hit against the same target, the weapon's damage doubles. This effect resets if an attack from this weapon misses, you attack a different target, or you do not attack the target on your turn. Continuous - No more than two attacks can be made with this weapon per round.

Wondrous Item, common Description A beautiful blue and white feather that when worn ones hair will billow majestically, even if there is no wind present as a bonus action; works with the cloak of billowing.

Wondrous Item (Consumable), uncommon Description When measuring and balancing the herbal specimens [Devil's Bloodleaf leaves and Phorus Blossom nectar] needed to make this tea, 2d4 + 2 bags of magical tea can be created with each 'batch'. You can steep a bag of tea for 1 minute in a cup of boiling water to transform the water into a rich, flavorful tea that calms the nerves and revitalizes the spirit. When you drink a cup of the hot tea, you gain 2d6 + 2 temporary hit points. In addition, you may roll with advantage on saving throws caused by any effect causing you to be charmed or frightened for 10 minutes. You can drink the tea using an action, although it's most commonly finished over the course of at least 1 minute. If the tea has been left to cool [10 minutes+] before you drink it, you regain only half the amount of temporary hit points, and no other benefits are present.

Wondrous Item (Consumable), uncommon Description When measuring and balancing the herbal specimens [Devil's Bloodleaf leaves and Phorus Blossom nectar] needed to make this tea, 2d4 + 2 bags of magical tea can be created with each 'batch'. You can steep a bag of tea for 1 minute in a cup of boiling water to transform the water into a rich, flavorful tea that calms the nerves and revitalizes the spirit. When you drink a cup of the hot tea, you gain 2d6 + 2 temporary hit points. In addition, you may roll with advantage on saving throws caused by any effect causing you to be charmed or frightened for 10 minutes. You can drink the tea using an action, although it's most commonly finished over the course of at least 1 minute. If the tea has been left to cool [10 minutes+] before you drink it, you regain only half the amount of temporary hit points, and no other benefits are present.

Alchemy Blade Weapon (All Blades), rare Description This sword has a glass channel running down its length. In place of a traditional pommel, it instead has a open hole designed to fit atop a typical flask or vial. While holding the sword, you can use an action to attach a flask or vial to the sword and draw its contents into its blade; doing so changes the sword's properties based on the attached flask or vial. Acid Vial. The sword deals an extra 1d6 acid damage on a hit. When the target is an object or structure that isn't being worn or carried, the acid damage is maximized. Alchemist's Fire. The sword deals an extra 1d6 fire damage on a hit. When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points using the sword, a creature of your choice within 5 feet of it also takes 2d6 fire damage. Basic Poison. The sword deals an extra 1d6 poison damage on a hit. The first time that the target hits with an attack that uses Strength before the start of your next turn, the damage is reduced by the poison damage dealt. Holy Water. The sword deals an extra 1d6 radiant damage on a hit. The radiant damage is doubled against fiends and undead. Each attached vial can produce the above effects for 3 attacks before the contents of the vial are exhausted. You can remove the flask or vial using an action, destroying its contents and leaving the container empty.

Ring, uncommon Description While wearing the Amentum, you can throw a weapon with the Thrown property a further distance equal to the object's initial minimum distance. Additionally, the Amentum corrects an object's trajectory while in flight. If the player rolls a 1 on a ranged attack roll from a weapon with the thrown property, while wearing the Amentum, they may choose to reroll, but must take the results of the second roll. This feature can be used three times, resetting at dawn.

Wondrous item, rare This wondrous, arcane-fueled stone bearing the power rune, can be fitted to any tiny object, this process takes an hour to complete. Once the item is complete the item becomes a weapon that can only be thrown. The weapon has the following properties: Thrown: (20/40), Damage: 1d6[magical bludgeoning] The item appears normal but can be detected using spells like detect magic. It uses your Dexterity or Strength modifier for attack and damage rolls. Invoking the Rune. When you make an attack with the item and hit, it deals an additional 2d6 force damage to the target. Any creature or object within 5 feet of the impact must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take 3d6 force damage and are pushed back 10 feet from the point of impact. On a successful save, they take half damage and are not pushed back. Once the rune has been invoked, it can't be invoked again until the next dawn. If the attack misses, it will travel to max thrown range and can be picked up and used.

Wondrous item, uncommon Description This quante, sphere shaped metal device is just big enough to be held in one hand when inactivate. When activated, either by a command word or by a button activation on the side of the object, it unfurls and begins to hover soundlessly 5 feet off the ground near where it was activated. It can be pushed or moved out of the way, and will magically slow down to avoid collision if pushed into a wall or person. It has a 12 in AC, and 12 hit points with resistance to all damage types, but immune to psychic damage. While active, it spends 10 minutes turning all available air in it's facility into comfortable, clean and breathable air and will constantly renew this process and keep the area as comfortable as possible until destroyed or deactivated. Once it has been active for 24 hours, it cannot be used again until the next dawn. This item cannot be used in the middle of combat to filter poisonous air, such as by a Green Dragon's Breath weapon, but can clean extra dimensional spaces such as a bag of holding.

A sorcerer of selfless nature and protective pursuit, your magic manifests itself through your desire to support others, bringing you safety and security in the process. Imbuing allies with the same magic that suffuses themselves, these sorcerers augment their strengths, covering their weaknesses, and upon reaching mastery, become catalyst for the inevitable success of everyone under their influence. Often called Arcane Guardians these sorcerers take a backseat to the events of life, letting others shine while they lift them higher, watching and protecting them. Many a hero was made by the hands of an Arcane Guardian. Features: 1st Level - Guardian Magic 1st Level - Loving Protection 6th Level - Gifting Inner Strength 14th Level - Altruistic Splinter 18th Level - Arcane Enlightenment

You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Guardian table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know. Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be an abjuration or a transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list.
1st: bless, protection from evil and good 3rd: aid, pass without trace 5th: aura of vitality, protection from energy 7th: aura of life, aura of purity 9th: mass cure wounds, skill empowerment

Starting at 1st level, your selfless nature begins to show in your spellcasting. Whenever an ally within 30 feet of you fits the casting requirements for a spell with a casting time of 1 Reaction, you can spend an amount of sorcery points equal to the spell level to cast the spell and give the effects to them. You can do this an amount of times equal to your Charisma modifier, resetting when you finish a long rest.

Starting at 6th level, you harness the ability to spread your talents to your allies. Once per turn, as a bonus action, you can strengthen an ally's next spell or attack with a Metamagic option you have access to, spending sorcery points as you would to use the options normally. These options last for a minute. The viable Metamagic options are as listed:

When your target casts a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, they can choose to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting. Alternatively, they can make one melee or ranged weapon attack as a bonus action.
When the target casts a spell, they can choose to cast it without any somatic or verbal components. Alternatively, they can give themself advantage on one melee or ranged weapon attack roll.
When the target rolls damage for a spell or weapon attack, they can reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). They must use the new rolls.

When the target casts a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, they can give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell. Alternatively, if they make a melee or ranged weapon attack and hit, they can add your Charisma modifier to one of the damage rolls (minimum of one).

Starting at 14th level, you learn to manipulate the bounds of your sorcery. Whenever you cast a spell that has a range of Self, you can spend an amount of sorcery points equal to twice the spell's level to change the range to Touch as long as the target is a willing creature. The spell level limit of this feature is half your Charisma modifier. You can do this an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, resetting when you finish a long rest.

Starting at 18th level, you gain the ability to funnel your strength into your allies. As an action on your turn, you can boost your allies' power until the end of your next turn. Every creature of your choice that is currently under the effects of a concentration spell cast by you receives the following additional effects: Their speed is increased by 30 feet. Every melee and ranged weapon attack roll they make is made with advantage. This advantage ignores any disadvantage also being applied to the target. Any attacks the target makes that hit receive a damage bonus equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). The target gains a bonus to AC equal to half your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). This feature can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, resetting on a long rest. Simulacrums are unable to use this feature.

Wondrous Item, rare Description This wondrous item takes the form of a normal-sized two-person tent. Setting up the tent takes ten minutes of effort. What appears to be an ordinary tent, yurt, or otherwise culturally appropriate transient dwelling from the outside is revealed to be significantly larger on the inside. Upon stepping through the entrance flap the individual finds themselves in a larger than expected space - containing 240 sqft of floor room and a 15ft high ceiling, with a small kitchen, separated outhouse, and a central hearth and sitting area. There are enough beds and accommodations for 4-6 people to sleep comfortably, even if more may fit physically. Rain will not enter through the roof, but the tent is not waterproof and will flood if submerged. Air also enters the tent from outside, leaving those within vulnerable to suffocation or otherwise if something should happen to that air. If the tent is punctured or damaged to a significant degree (AC 11, HP 15, resistant to all damage except fire and acid), the magic will cease to function until repaired with the mending spell. All creatures and objects inside will be dumped into the space of the two-person tent, possibly breaking it further, and until repaired it will function like the tent it appears to be. Additionally, the tent has a number of furnishings and furniture which are bound to it; these will remain inside at all times, and cannot be removed. If destroyed, the furniture will reappear the next time the tent is set up. Any objects left inside will be dumped out after the tent is dismantled.

Arcanist's Magnificent Magnifier Wondrous Item, rare Description This magical magnifying glass helps deduce the arcane nature of items. While looking through the glass at an object within 1 foot of you, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any Intelligence (Arcana) or Intelligence (Investigation) check you make regarding that object’s magical properties if your proficiency bonus is not doubled already. In addition, you can speak the glass’s command word as an action to cast the "identify" spell from it, targeting an object with the spell that you can see through the glass within 1 foot of you. Each time you do, there is a cumulative 5 percent chance that the glass shatters and is destroyed after casting the spell.

Arcanist's Magnificent Magnifier Wondrous Item, rare Description This magical magnifying glass helps deduce the arcane nature of items. While looking through the glass at an object within 1 foot of you, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any Intelligence (Arcana) or Intelligence (Investigation) check you make regarding that object’s magical properties if your proficiency bonus is not doubled already. In addition, you can speak the glass’s command word as an action to cast the "identify" spell from it, targeting an object with the spell that you can see through the glass within 1 foot of you. Each time you do, there is a cumulative 5 percent chance that the glass shatters and is destroyed after casting the spell.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description The pages in this tome are crafted so they never run out. When the user fills up the pages within the tome, the book automatically creates new, blank pages. The older pages are automatically erased from the pages and stored, and the contents will reappear on command.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description The pages in this tome are crafted so they never run out. When the user fills up the pages within the tome, the book automatically creates new, blank pages. The older pages are automatically erased from the pages and stored, and the contents will reappear on command.

Wondrous Item (tattoo), varies Attunement Requires Attunement Description Produced by a special needle, this magic tattoo depicts an intricately designed weapon. Tattoo Attunement. To attune to this item, you hold the needle to your skin where you want the tattoo to appear, pressing the needle there throughout the attunement process. When the attunement is complete, the needle turns into the ink that becomes the tattoo, which appears on the skin. If your attunement to the tattoo ends, the tattoo vanishes, and the needle reappears in your space. Proficiency. While attuned to this tattoo, you have proficiency in the weapon type associated with the tattoo. Transformation. As a Bonus Action, you can transform this tattoo into the depicted weapon or change the weapon back into a tattoo. You must be holding the weapon to transform it back into a tattoo. The weapon form of this tattoo gains a bonus to attack and damage rolls depending on the tattoo's rarity, as shown below. RARITY | BONUS Uncommon | +1 Rare | +2 Very Rare | +3

Wondrous item, uncommon Attunement Requires Attunement Description While attuned to this talisman, your ranged weapon attacks no longer suffer disadvantage at long range. This is not limited to bows, but also affects crossbows, spears, javelins, daggers, etc.

Wondrous item, uncommon Attunement Requires Attunement Description While attuned to this talisman, your ranged weapon attacks no longer suffer disadvantage at long range. This is not limited to bows, but also affects crossbows, spears, javelins, daggers, etc.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This item appears as a rolled-up scroll of blue parchment paper with white gridlines at regular intervals. When unfurled, a creature holding it may use an action and envision a creature, landscape, or anything they can think of the blueprint projects a three-dimensional illusion of the thing envisioned as a rough sketch of lines, tracing the contours and edges of the item. The illusion can be freely tampered with through intuitive hand gestures, such as enlarging or reducing, rotating and turning. Changing the illusion itself requires a bonus action. The illusion lasts for 10 minutes starting from the time it was left inactive or deactivated with a bonus action. A creature has advantage on the check (if needed) when creating or constructing something according to the blueprint (DM's discretion). The extent of the detail the illusion has is limited, it appears as white lines, and grants the observer no knowledge they otherwise wouldn't have, such as the inner workings of a specific lock they have not disassembled.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This item appears as a rolled-up scroll of blue parchment paper with white gridlines at regular intervals. When unfurled, a creature holding it may use an action and envision a creature, landscape, or anything they can think of the blueprint projects a three-dimensional illusion of the thing envisioned as a rough sketch of lines, tracing the contours and edges of the item. The illusion can be freely tampered with through intuitive hand gestures, such as enlarging or reducing, rotating and turning. Changing the illusion itself requires a bonus action. The illusion lasts for 10 minutes starting from the time it was left inactive or deactivated with a bonus action. A creature has advantage on the check (if needed) when creating or constructing something according to the blueprint (DM's discretion). The extent of the detail the illusion has is limited, it appears as white lines, and grants the observer no knowledge they otherwise wouldn't have, such as the inner workings of a specific lock they have not disassembled.

Wondrous Common Description The Audioshard is the audio version of the Spellshard. As an action, the user can activate the shard which allows it to store sound up to a max of 10 ft away, determined whenever the user activates the shard. The shard can store up to 40 hours of audio. The user can also take an action to play any recorded audio which can be played at a volume ranging from a whisper to a scream. *Artisans Guild invention

The Augmenter is a unique blend of artificer and psychic, merging technology with mental prowess. These specialists understand the psyche and wield their own bodies as tools for both combat and manipulation. Whether augmenting their limbs or delving into the minds of others, Augmenters are masters of self-enhancement Features: 3rd Level - Augmenter Spells 3rd Level - Self Augmentation 5th Level - Extra Attack 9th Level - Mind Over Matter 15th Level - Master Augmenter Augmenter Infusions

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Augmenter Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare. Augmenter Spells reflect your understanding of the psyche and allows you to influence the mind of others. Augmenter Spells 3rd Level - Command, Dissonant Whispers 5th Level - Tasha’s Mind Whip, Crown of Madness 9th Level - Antagonize, Fast Friends 13th Level - Raulothim’s Psychic Lance, Compulsion 17th Level - Synaptic Static, Modify Memory

Starting at 3rd level, you master the technique of augmenting your own body. Each of the following parts of your body can be infused using your artificer Infusions; Torso, Head, Legs. You also gain access to Augmenter Infusions, these infusions are known and does not count toward your total of known infusions. For the purposes of normal Infusions, the Torso is seen as Armor, head as a Helmet or any peripheral that is worn on the head, and legs are seen as boots. You also learn how to augment your arms with special arm weapons. These can also be infused, and you can only have one arm enhancement active at a time. Whenever you finish a long rest you can swap arm enhancements.

These Enhancements count as weapons and infusions can be applied to them. Each enhancement grants the artificer an applicable fighting Style based on the installed enhancement. Mantis Blade​ You gain retractable blade attachments on either of your arms Properties: Finesse Fighting Style: Dueling Damage: 1d6 piercing Special: The blade can be retracted or unsheathed as a bonus action, leaving the hand free to wield other items. When you score a critical hit with the mantis blade the target needs to make a constitution save against your Spell DC or start to bleed. When bleeding the target loses hp equal to your proficiency bonus at the start of each of its turn. It can make the save again at the end of each turn. Monowire Attachment​ These fine wires get pulled from your wrists and are wielded like a whip. Properties: Finesse, Reach Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting Damage: 1d4 slashing Special: The wires count as two separate weapons for the purpose of two weapon fighting, but only require a single infusion. The wires use Intelligence for its attack and damage modifiers. Gorilla Arms​ Your Hands and forearms are augmented with heavier metals and mechanical support. Properties: Heavy Fighting Style: Unarmed Fighting Damage: Unarmed Strike, Bludgeoning Special: You make your attacks with the Gorilla Arms as unarmed strikes. You also have advantage on Strength( Athletics) checks to escape, attempt, maintain grapples. Arm Launcher​ You can load bolts or sling bullets into your arm and fire them as projectiles. Properties: Ranged (40/80), Reload (6) Fighting Style: Archery Damage: 1d8 piercing (bolts), bludgeoning (sling bullets) Special: The Launcher leaves your hands open while firing. On a hit, the launcher does 1d4 force damage to the target, all creatures within 5ft of the target must make Dexterity save against your spell save DC or take 1d4 force damage.
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

At 9th level, your deep understanding of the mind allows you to manipulate the physical world with your thoughts. You gain the following abilities: Mental Shield: You gain resistance to psychic damage. Additionally, when you take psychic damage, you can use your reaction to reflect half of that damage back to the attacker. Psychic Insight: You can use your action to read the surface thoughts of a creature you can see within 30 feet. This effect lasts for 1 minute, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you can also implant a simple suggestion (as per the Suggestion spell) into their mind. This ability can be used once per short rest.

At 15th Level your ability to enhance your augmentations has reached unparalleled heights: You can now add 2 infusions to any of your augmentations. You are able to use master properties for your arm augmentations. Each arm augmentation has two possible properties. When you switch out your arm augmentation you can choose which master property to use. Mantis Blades: Graze, Sap Monowire: Nick, Slow Gorilla Arms: Sap, Push Arm Launcher: Push, Vex

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter, Unarmored Item: Torso Augmentation (requires Attunement) Effect: Your skin is reinforced with a layer of protective material, making you more resilient to physical attacks. Subdermal Armor makes the wearer’s AC equal 10 + Constitution Modifier + Intelligence Modifier

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Torso Augmentation (requires Attunement) Effect: You can use an action to blend into your surroundings, gaining advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks for 1 hour. This ability can be used once per short or long rest.

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Torso Augmentation (requires Attunement) Effect: A sophisticated system of micro-projectors and sensors enables you to alter your appearance at will. As a bonus action you can cast the Disguise self spell on yourself, without spending a spell slot. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.
Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Head Augmentation Effect: You gain proficiency in the perception skill, and can use Intelligence instead of Wisdom for Passive perception and perception checks
Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Head Augmentation Effect: You gain dark vision out to 60 feet, if you already have dark vision from another source, its range is extended by 60 feet.

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Head Augmentation Effect: The infusion highlights your positive features and filters your words, making you sound and look more alluring than you are. You can add your Intelligence modifier to any charisma(persuasion) check you make against a single target.
Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Leg Augmentation Effect: You gain a +10 feet to your walking speed, and your high and long jump distances are doubled.

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Leg Augmentation Effect: Your footfalls are dampened allowing for silent movement. You gain advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. Damage taken from falling is halved.

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Leg Augmentation. Effect: You can take the dodge action as a bonus action. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 6th Level Augmenter Item: Special Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: After finishing a short rest you can load any magical potion into the pump. You can then as a reaction to taking damage, prior to taking damage or making an attack inject the potion to activate its effect. Once activated the potion is consumed.

Prerequisite: 6th Level Augmenter Item: Special Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to cast Shield without expending a spell slot. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 6th Level Augmenter Item: Special Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: As a bonus action, you can release nanobots that heal a creature you touch for 2d8 + your Intelligence modifier hit points. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter Item: Mantis Blade Effect: When you hit a creature with the Mantis Blades, you can choose to deal an additional 2d6 psychic damage. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter Item: Monowire Attachment Effect: When you hit a creature with the Monowire Attachment, you can choose to restrain the target. The target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be restrained until the end of your next turn. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter Item: Gorilla Arms Effect: When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can choose to knock the target prone. The target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked prone. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter Item: Arm Launcher Effect: You gain a +4 bonus to attack rolls with the Arm Launcher. Additionally, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on a ranged attack made against you.

Prerequisite: 14th Level Augmenter Item: Torso Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: Advanced optical technology allows you to blend into your surroundings, becoming nearly invisible. As a bonus action you become invisible until the end of your next turn, or until you take damage from any source. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 14th Level Augmenter Item: Head Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal 1d6 lightning damage to the attacker. This damage increases to 2d6 if the attacker is wearing metal armor.

Prerequisite: 14th Level Augmenter Item: Leg Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: You can use a bonus action to jump up to 30 feet in any direction. If you land within 5 feet of an enemy, you can make a melee attack as part of the same bonus action.

2nd-level abjuration. Artificer, Cleric, Paladin Meta Casting Time: 1 Bonus Action Range: Self (10ft) Components: V, S, M (a small magnet) Duration: 10 minutes Description: You grant yourself and allies within range the ability to transfer the kinetic energy of attacks. Until the spell ends you can use an action to gravitate all attacks against allies within range until the end of your next turn. All allies within range can use their reaction to redirect any attack made against them, or an ally within 5ft of them, to you. Melee attacks will still be able to be made regardless of the effective range of the attack. Attacks made at long range because of this effect aren’t at disadvantage. At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the range increases by 5ft for every 2 slot levels above 2nd.
Avengers seek to right a wrong, stopping at nothing to correct a past sleight. They dole out their revenge with their own hands, using steel just as much as spirit to forward their goals.

At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons, and you can use weapons as your spiritual focus. When you activate your spirit tether, you gain an amount of temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + half your spiritualist level (rounded down).
Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your soul’s hunger for vengeance.

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to initiate a spirit duel with your target. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or be blinded. While the target is blinded this way, you are also blinded, except you and your target can still see each other normally. As long as this blindness persists, your weapon attacks deal an additional 1d6 damage.

When you are attacked by your tethered target while you are holding a shield, you can use your reaction to spend 1 spirit point and force the target to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the attack misses, and the next attack you make against the tethered target has advantage.
As an action, you can spend 2 spirit points to share your suffering with the tethered target. For the next minute, whenever you take damage, the target takes half as much necrotic damage.

Beginning at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can use a spirit art that uses an action in place of one of these attacks.

At 13th level, your soul lashes out at any creature that would harm you or your allies. Whenever a creature you can see within range of your spirit tether damages you or an ally within 30 feet, you can use your reaction to immediately create a spirit tether. The creature must be one of the targets.
At 18th level, you master the art of vengeance. You learn the following spirit art:

You can use 5 spirit points as an action to empower your weapon. For the next minute, whenever you hit a tethered target with a weapon attack, the attack deals an additional 3d6 force damage. The first time you hit a tethered target after using this art, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the target is rended by your spirit, and cannot restore hit points or gain temporary hit points as long as your spirit tether lasts.

2nd-level Necromancy (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock) Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30ft Components: V, S, M (A dagger) Duration: 1 hour The weapon you indicate during the spell's casting briefly shimmers with a black aura that disappears in an eyeblink. When you cast this spell, choose one melee weapon within range. The next time a creature uses this weapon to make a melee attack, they have advantage on their attack roll and then the weapon turns on its wielder, provided the spell hasn't ended. The next attack afterward that hits a creature deals damage to the weapon's wielder instead of their target, in addition to the weapon's typical effects. This damage cannot be made non-lethal. As an action, a creature can attempt an investigation check against your spell save DC when closely analyzing the weapon to find that it was tampered with. As an action, a creature can make an arcana check against your spell save DC to disarm the weapon and end this spell. Once the weapon attacks its wielder, regardless of whether the attack hits or misses, the spell ends. At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd or 4th level, this spell lasts up to 8 hours. When you use a spell slot of 5th or 6th level, this spell lasts up to 24 hours. When you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, this spell lasts until dispelled.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This item resembles a bag of holding, but is cool to the touch and emits visibly cold air while opened. It can only hold 100 pounds of items, but any perishable items do not degrade while within the bag. It is otherwise identical to a bag of holding.

Balance Weapon (greatsword), legendary Attunement: Requires Attunement Description Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Antithesis. Attacks with this weapon deal extra damage of a predetermined type depending on the user's alignment. If the user is of evil alignment, Balance deals an extra 2d6 radiant damage. If the user is of good alignment, Balance deals an extra 2d6 necrotic damage. If the target is of neither good nor evil alignment, Balance deals an extra 1d6 radiant and 1d6 necrotic damage. Unwavering Neutrality. You may use an action to cast the Protection from Evil and Good spell on yourself at will, requiring no material components or concentration. Unity. While this weapon is visible, you have advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) and Charisma (Intimidation) checks made to interact with creatures that can see it.

Wondrous Item, rare Description This bandolier comes equipped with a single scroll case, inside of which up to 100 levels worth of scrolls can be stored. The wearer of this bandolier can produce a scroll from this case as part of the action used to cast the spell.

Bard-in-a-Box Wondrous Item, common Description This small music box can play songs at the request of the holder. As a bonus action, you can command the box to play a song that it knows, causing the contraption to emit a slightly tinny rendition of the musical number at a moderate volume. The box can know up to five songs at a time, and can not recreate lyrics or other creature sounds. It has a small knob on the side that adjusts the box's volume, being as quiet as a whisper to as loud as a scream. Sheet music can be fed into the box through a narrow slot along the bottom of the device. Sheet music must be labeled with a song title, page number, and instrument in order to be replayed. Pages failing to meet the requirements causes the box to make a sad, trumpeting noise, and are spat back out. Once a sheet is successfully fed into the box, it is consumed and cannot be retrieved. If the new piece of music will cause the box to forget an older one, it quickly plays several bars of the now-forgotten number before slowing to a stop.

Wondrous Item, Uncommon Requires use by a creature with any musical instrument proficiency Description This bugle is magical, lined on it's edges with a faint swirling pattern which flares at the horn end. The unique grooves of the instrument allow it to reverberate sound more effectively. Condensing it and emerging as volumes louder than originally played from one end. This item comes with an inter-changeable mouthpiece, which is much wider and allows speech through the piping. Sounds made through this instrument are audible out to a distance of 300 feet. As an action once per day, you may choose to blare this instrument. Doing so requires creatures in a 30-foot cone originating from you to make a DC 13 constitution saving throw unless they are covering their ears. On a failure, they take 1d10 thunder damage are deafened for one minute. Objects in this area take 3d10 thunder damage. They may repeat this saving throw again at the end of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

Wondrous Item, rare Description A finely crafted dark leather belt with two loops, each decorated with a shard of sapphire. The magic of the belt leaves an invisible mark on the surface of the weapons stowed in each loop and invisibly inscribes the name of the item on the sapphire shard. Two one-handed weapons with the thrown property can be stowed in the belt. When you make ranged attack with a weapon marked by the belt, immediately after the attack, hit or miss, the weapon returns to the belt.

Black Cleaver Weapon (battleaxe), very rare Attunement: Requires Attunement Description You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. After you have made a successful weapon attack with this weapon, you gain an additional 10 feet movement speed which lasts until the end of that turn. Additionally, you can also lower the defensive prowess of the one you are attacking. The battleaxe has 5 charges, and it regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you attack with this weapon, you can use your reaction to expend a charge to lower the target's AC by 2, includes against the triggering attack, until the start of its next turn. You can only use feature once per turn.

Weapon: Simple, Melee 1gp, 2 lbs. --- 1d4 slashing - light, two-handed Description Proficiency with a cestus allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special: As a bonus action, you can make one attack with this weapon.

Staff, rare Blightstaff Attunement Requires Attunement by a Druid Description This magic staff was created from a long, straight branch from a petrified tree. It has a small animal skull on the top with thorns to mimic antlers, and two dark gems in the eye sockets. While holding this staff, you gain a +2 bonus to the saving throw DCs of your Druid spells. When you create an area of difficult terrain, any creature moving through it takes 1d4 necrotic damage for every 5 feet it moves in that area.

Considered taboo by many societies and magic practitioners, the use of blood magic—also known as hemocraft—is a rare art that harnesses the latent powers of a creature’s vitality to fuel and amplify the caster’s own capabilities, while manipulating and weakening the bodies of enemies from the inside. Some of the more macabre mages seeking to empower their arcane pursuits turn to hemocraft as a means of bolstering their spells, giving their own life’s blood to reach new heights of frightening magical prowess. The secrets of hemocraft and other forms of blood magic were once the sole purview of the mysterious Claret Orders. In recent years, however, these secrets have begun to spread beyond the order’s members and into the hands of less scrupulous mages. Blood magic has a bad reputation in Tal’Dorei, even though its powers can be used for much more than evil. Features: 2nd Level - Blood Channeling 2nd Level - Sanguine Burst 6th Level - Bond of Mutual Suffering 10th Level - Glyph of Hemorrhaging 14th Level - Thicker than Water
