When you choose this arcane tradition at 2nd level, you are able to use your own depleted life essence to channel your magical abilities. Whenever your current hit points are below your hit point maximum, you can use your own body as an arcane focus. In addition, when casting a wizard spell that requires a costly material component, you can forego the component by taking 1d10 necrotic damage per 50 gp of the cost of the component (minimum 1d10). This damage can’t be reduced in any way. If this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, the spell fails but the spell slot is not expended.

Also at 2nd level, you learn how to weave your life force into a spell you cast, boosting its intensity at the cost of your vitality. Whenever you roll damage for a spell you’ve cast of 1st level or higher, you can choose to take necrotic damage equal to the spell’s level to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one). This damage can’t be reduced in any way, and you must use the new rolls.

At 6th level, when a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to bind your vitality to the attacker and force them to share your pain. The attacker takes damage equal to the damage you took. This feature cannot be used against constructs or undead. You can use this feature once. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. At 14th level, you can use this feature twice between rests.

Starting at 10th level, when you damage a creature with a spell, you can choose to curse that creature for 1 minute. While cursed in this way, whenever the creature is hit by an attack, it takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. At the end of each of the creature’s turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the curse on a success. This feature cannot be used against creatures that are undead or constructs. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Upon reaching 14th level, the blood that flows through your veins is empowered with arcane vigor that mends wounds and helps preserve your life. Whenever a spell or magical effect causes you to regain hit points, you regain an additional number of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. In addition, while you are concentrating on a spell, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

Wondrous Item, uncommon(+1), rare(+2), very rare(+3) Attunement: Requires Attunement by a Blood Hunter Description This symbol resembles that of the clan, coven, or circle that brought you into the blood hunting tradition to which you belong. It may be placed anywhere on your body. Typically, these are applied via the use of a needle and removed upon losing attunement to this item. While wearing this brand, your hemomancy DC is improved by an amount corresponding to this item's rarity. In addition, you may use a bonus action to regain a use of your blood maledict feature. This ability recharges at dawn.

Weapon (dagger), legendary Attunement: Requires Attunement Bloodneedle Description Bloodneedle sits in a sheath covered in glimmering dark rubies that always seem to be crusted in blood. It's blade appears to be hollow glass. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit with an attack, the target takes an extra 1d10 necrotic damage (ignores resistance and immunity).When you throw it and it hits or misses, it teleports instantly to your hand. Whenever you roll a 1 on an attack roll using this weapon, you takes 3d8 necrotic damage(ignoring resistance and immunity). This damage decreases your maximum hit points until you have rolled a 20 with this weapon(ending attunement with the weapon does not removed the decreased hit points). You can also remove this using a greater restoration spell. While you are holding Bloodneedle, you can use an action to cast the harm spell (save DC 15) from the weapon, and this action can't be used again until the next dawn.

Prerequisite: Skeleton Your wisdom score increases by one. You can designate one inanimate skeleton by touch as an action. After 30 days, an invisible spiritual connection is made between you and the skeleton. If you are destroyed while such a connection is active, you rise again from the skeleton you had designated. You can only have one skeleton designated in this way at a time.

Book of Instant Copying Wondrous Item, common Description This book has a glass cover and is typically found with 2d10 + 30 blank pages. As an action, you can place a piece of paper or similar object (such as a leaf or patterned fabric) between the book's glass and the page below it and speak the book's command word. When you do, the book magically inscribes an image of the placed object in black ink as it appears pressed against the glass on the first blank page of the book. Copied magic scrolls or spellbooks appear as nonsensical glyphs when copied in this way. When the last page of the book has been used, you can rebind it with 50 blank new pages using 50 gp of fine materials and 8 hours of work.

Wondrous Item, rare Description This magical tome appears to contain several spell scrolls. Each scroll can be used once per day, and regenerates daily at dawn. If the scrolls are ever removed from the tome, they disappear. The spells are inscribed wrong, and their effects vary wildly from the intended. The spells are cast as normal, except have the following effects rather than their original effects: Message / Massage. You point your finger toward a creature within range. The target receives a pleasant back rub. Mage Armor / Mage Armoire. A fancy wardrobe is conjured in the nearest empty space to the caster, containing three sets of clothes. Roll a 1d20 three times. On a result of 1, the clothes are common quality. On a result of 2-10, the clothes are traveler's quality. On a result of 11-15, the clothes are costume quality, on a result of 16-20, the clothes are fine quality. Hold Person / Fold Person. Choose a humanoid that you can see within range. The target must succeed a Wisdom saving throw or be bent over backwards. On a failed save, the target takes 4d6 bludgeoning damage and is paralyzed for one round. Speak with Dead / Speak with Dad. For one minute you can communicate telepathically with your biological father, as long as they are living and on the same plane as you. Ice Storm / Ick Storm. Gross sludge rains down for one minute creating difficult terrain in a 20-foot radius centered on a point within range. Teleport / Telepoot. Creates a loud fart at a destination you select. The destination you choose must be known to you, and it must be on the same plane of existence as you.

Weapon (maul, warhammer, light hammer), very rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon. Attacks against constructs and objects are made with advantage. The hammer has 10 charges. When you hit with a melee attack with this weapon, you can expend up to 3 of its charges. For each charge you expend, the target takes an extra 1d6 thunder damage. Alternatively, you can spend 5 of its charges for the target to take 3d6 thunder damage and force them to make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be stunned for 1 minute, creatures immune to thunder damage are unaffected by the stun and the stun cannot be applied if there is no sound. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turn. Recharge 1d6+4 charges at dawn.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This magical ivory bottle can store up to 40 gallons of liquid at once (As much as 1 barrel), after adding any amount of liquid to the bottle, no other liquid can enter the bottle (meaning can't mix liquids, only liquids of the same type, eg Potion of Superior healing to Potion of Superior healing, salt water can't mix with water etc). The liquid can be poured or drank like any other container Time passes for the liquid inside as usual

weapon (Longbow), very rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description This white longbow is set with four gemstones: a ruby, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond. Attacks with this longbow deal 2d8 damage instead of 1d8. When you make an attack with this longbow, you can conjure an elemental arrow as part of the attack. Using an elemental arrow changes the damage type of the attack. Arrow of Air. On a hit, the arrow of air deals lightning damage. Arrow of Earth. On a hit, the arrow of earth deals magical bludgeoning damage. Arrow of Fire. On a hit, the arrow of fire deals fire damage. Arrow of Water. On a hit, the arrow of water deals cold damage.

Weapon (any bow), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description This magical bow has the power to silence its victims. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. On a successful hit the victim must make a dc15 charisma saving throw or be mute for 1d4 rounds. If they fail by 5 or more they won't be able to say the name of their assailant for 1d4 days. If the victim passes a save, they are immune to this effect for the next 24 hours.

Outside the king’s chambers, still as an armor display, the royal guard stands post as they await the coming rebelion force. Ready to meet it head on, no matter the result. A scrappy militiaman clad in chainmail stands on the battlefield, now alone and bloodied, having outlasted all others through wit and defensive positioning. Beneath a greathelm, the dwarf’s face pools with sweat as he crosses the great desert, sent on a mission to deliver an important message that cannot afford to fall into the wrong hands Bulwarks spend large portions of their lives covered in heavy armor to the point that they are seldom ever seen without it. Their mastery over using it fully to their advantage naturally comes as second nature, allowing them to outperform nearly any other. What truly distinguishes a bulwark from other users of heavy armor is their distinct focus on making the absolute most of the defense it offers, knowing how best to move themselves to avoid or block incoming assaults. Bulwarks are often kept as personal guards to high ranking officials, as front-liners in the field of battle, or even as couriers who’s senders need certainty their message will arrive. Adventuring parties who are graced with the inclusion of one of these masters of defense can rest assured that at least one of them will be making it back alive.

A Bulwark will tend to focus fully on a defensive standpoint in battle, as an overtly pressing offense might lead to gaps in your attention. In fact, some Bulwarks even refrain from having an actual offense entirely, relying on those around them to defeat their enemies while they spend their attention and energy on lasting as long as possible.

When creating a Bulwark, consider why your character might have needed to train such a rigorous defense. What training have they undergone to truly set themselves ahead of their peers? Perhaps you were a member of a royal guard, someone trained to protect at any cost. Or rather just a soldier who has taken to protecting themselves a bit further than most. A Bulwark could be anyone of the great strength needed to use heavy armors, and utilizes it to the fullest, and you get to decide just how your character does that.
When multiclassing with the Bulwark class, use the following: Prerequisite: Strength 13 and Constitution 13 Proficiencies Gained: Light armor, Medium armor, Shields, and Heavy armor

As a Bulwark, you gain the following class features.

Hit Points​ Hit Dice: 1d10 per bulwark level Hit Points at 1st Level: 10 + your constitution modifier Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d10 (or 6) + your constitution modifier per Bulwark level after first. Proficiencies​ Armor: Light, Medium, and Heavy Armor, Shields Weapons: Simple Weapons, Warhammers, Heavy Crossbows Tools: none Saving Throws: Constitution and Charisma Skills: Choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion Equipment​ You start with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment granted by your background: (a) a warhammer or (b) a simple weapon of your choice and a shield A suit of chainmail armor (a) an explorer’s pack or (b) a diplomat’s pack (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) a shortbow and 20 arrows

While you are wearing heavy armor, you can choose to take up a defensive stance to bolster yourself for incoming force. As an action, you can give yourself a +2 bonus to your armor class and resistance to force damage for 1 minute, or until you are no longer wearing heavy armor. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your constitution modifier before completing a long rest.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice that you have proficiency with, such as maces and light crossbows. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of warhammers and handaxes.

At 2nd level, you can lessen the impact of weapons against you. While you are wearing heavy armor, and are hit by a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your bulwark level.

When you reach 3rd level, you choose a defensive specialization that dictates the types of strategies you employ to protect yourself and others. Juggernaut Phalanx Rook Spellbreaker Unfettered Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 13th, and 18th level.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase two ability scores of your choice by one. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

Additionally at 5th level, your voice carries with you a supernatural sense of purpose and authority. You gain a bonus to all charisma (intimidation and persuasion) checks equal to your strength modifier (minimum bonus of +1).
At 6th level, you gain an uncanny knack for endurance. You no longer suffer the adverse effects of a forced march, and exhaustion does not affect you until you have at least three levels.

Starting at 9th level, you radiate an aura that compels your foes to battle against you, and you alone. While your defensive stance is active, enemies that start their turn within 10 feet of you must make a charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be forced to use their action to attack, or otherwise harm you.

At 10th level, you gain the ability to harden your mind to attacks with a similar effectiveness as your armor can block physical blows. You gain proficiency in intelligence or wisdom saving throws (your choice). You can replace your selection with the other whenever you finish a long rest.

When you reach 11th level, you learn to redirect the energy meant for you back to your attacker. While your defensive stance is active, you deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus when you attack with a weapon. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

Starting at 14th level, your ability to shrug off attacks extends to even the mightiest of blows. When you use your Fortitude feature, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the amount of damage you prevented. Once you gain these temporary hit points, you cannot do so again until you finish a short rest, or enter a new defensive stance.
At 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no remaining uses of your defensive stance, you regain one use.

When you reach 17th level, your stance becomes as unbreakable as the very earth itself. While your defensive stance is active, you cannot be moved against your will, and you are immune to the frightened condition and critical hits.
At 20th level, the duration of your defensive stance increases to 10 minutes, and the bonus it confers to your armor class increases to +4.

Weapon (greatclub), legendary Attunement Buster Bat Requires Attunement Description This bat is created from unknown origin and exudes devastating capabilities. It is made from a type of wood called Ironwood, an extremely hard but light wood when compared to oak wood and while remaining natural wood in almost every way. It is as strong, heavy, and resistant to fire as steel. You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, in addition to the following abilities. Battery. You are able to deflect anything coming your way. All ranged attacks against you are made with disadvantage and you take no damage from magic missile. Knock. The impact caused by this weapon will undeniably cause damage. The weapon ignores resistance to bludgeoning damage. When you hit and roll a 15 or higher on the attack roll with this weapon, the target takes extra 2d12 bludgeoning damage. Home Run. At extreme cases, this weapon will perform impossible feats. Once in each combat, the third time you roll a 20 on an attack roll with this weapon, the target by the last roll dies instantly and their soul is destroyed if its a creature. A creature can negate this effect by using one use of their Legendary Resistance if they have the trait. If the target is a nonmagical object or structure, the object is pulverized to dust and a portion of the structure is destroyed making a hole 10 feet in diameter and can go as far as to 20 feet deep into the structure. Bulk Up. The longer the battle persists, the more battle-hardened you become. When you are in combat for 5 rounds or longer, you gain a +3 bonus to AC, advantage on saving throws, and you have resistance to all damage except force, radiant, and psychic damage. And when combat reaches 10 rounds or longer, you also gain immunity to being inflicted with conditions.

Casting Time: 1 Action Range: Self; 10 ft cubes Components: S, M (a citrus fruit) Duration: concentration up to 1 minute A viscous and caustic substance spills out across eight 10 foot cubes, which you can arrange as you wish. Each cube must have at least one face adjacent to the face of another cube. Each creature in the area when the spill appears must make a dexterity saving throw or take 6d4 acid damage. After which the spill settles, making the spell's area difficult terrain. For the remainder of the spell's duration, the first time a creature enters the spill on their turn, or starts their turn in the spill, they take 6d4 acid damage. A creature also takes 2d4 acid damage for every 5 feet they move through the spill.

Weapon: Simple, Melee 1gp, 1.5 lbs. --- 1d4 bludgeoning - light, two-handed Description Proficiency with a cestus allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special: As a bonus action, you can make one attack with this weapon.

Weapon: ( Martial, Melee) 30gp, 3lbs. --- d4 slashing - finesse, light, thrown (10/30), Description Proficiency with a chakram allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. On a missed throw, a chakram returns to the thrower's hand. Finesse: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. Light: A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons. Thrown: If a weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack. If the weapon is a melee weapon, you use the same ability modifier for that attack roll and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon. For example, if you throw a handaxe, you use your Strength, but if you throw a dagger, you can use either your Strength or your Dexterity, since the dagger has the finesse property.

Weapon (Any simple or martial weapon), legendary quest-able; uncraftable Attunement Requires Attunement Description This weapon carries the last breath and fighting spirit of old champions, buried with them in their tombs as they carry their greatest arms into the afterlife. You have a +3 to attack and damage rolls made when using this weapon. While wielding this sword, the threshold required for you to score a critical hit with weapon attacks is reduced by 1.
Artistry Channeler

The Channel of Artistry represents channelers who want to master controlling the flow of their arcane energy, manipulating their power with finesse and elegance. They weave through combat like dancers and cast spells with the delicacy of an accomplished maestro. Features 1st Level - Armaments of Artistry 1st Level - Elemental Savant 6th Level - Weaving Strike 11th Level - Beautiful Virtuosity 11th Level - Harmonized Strikes 17th Level - Culmination of Artistry
When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in shortswords, scimitars, and whips. You also gain proficiency in one type of artisan’s tools of your choice.

Your use and control of elemental energy is beautiful to many, and distracting to your opponents. Starting at 1st level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you have resistance to the first attack they make against you until the beginning of your next turn. Additionally, you may imbue two weapons instead of one. The imbued damage types must be the same for both weapons.

At 6th level, you can sculpt your elemental energy with your weapon, enhancing both your own movements and your energy’s potency. When you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement, the next attack roll you make during this turn has advantage, and your movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks until the beginning of your next turn.

At 11th level, the beauty of your movement and the flow of your energy is entrancing and inspiring to allies. When you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement, you may choose a creature within 30 feet that can see you. That creature may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check they make until the beginning of your next turn.

At 11th level, if you hit with a weapon attack from your attack action and hit with a spell attack roll made with your Overchanneled Imbuement in one turn, you may take a second bonus action that turn.

At 17th level, you’ve perfected your casting as a form of art. You may use your Flash Charge feature an unlimited amount of times per day. When you hit with an attack, you may use your Flash Charge feature as a reaction. When you do, the attack deals additional damage equal to two rolls of your new Elemental Imbuement die.
Features: 1st Level - Armaments of Containment 6th Level - Brawl Binding 11th Level - Elemental Fortitude 11th Level - Extra Attack 17th Level - Culmination of Containment

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in improvised weapons. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor. Elemental Core You learn to confine your arcane energy within your body, empowering your unarmed attacks. You may choose to Imbue your body with elemental energy as opposed to a weapon. While imbued, you gain the following benefits: Your unarmed strikes use your Elemental Imbuement dice for its damage type. When you attack with an unarmed strike, you may use your Intelligence modifier, rather than your strength modifier, for attack and damage rolls. You gain resistance to the damage type you chose for your Imbuement You can use your body as a focus for your Channeler spells

Beginning at 6th level, when you use the attack action to grapple a creature, the target takes damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die if the grapple succeeds. Whenever you take the attack action against the creature on subsequent turns, if you are still grappling the creature, you may choose to deal this damage again. Additionally, if you succeed on grappling a creature, you can use your Overchanneled Imbuement as a bonus action. Creatures you grapple have disadvantage on saving throws against spells you cast.

At 11th level, your contained energy provides a defensive ward that sits just under your skin, protecting you from harm. When you are subjected to an effect that has you roll a saving throw to take half damage, if the damage type is acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

Beginning at 17th level, your arcane energy binds perfectly to your flesh. You gain the following benefits while Imbued: You gain immunity to the damage type you chose for your Imbuement Your walking speed increases by 20 feet You no longer need to hit with an Imbued weapon attack to cast Channeler spells as a bonus action. When you cast a Channeler spell, add your Intelligence modifier to your unarmed strike damage and any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution checks you make until the end of your next turn.
Devastation Channeler

The Channel of Devastation represents channelers who prefer focusing their energy in short, powerful bursts, often leading to disastrous results. Those who choose this channel work tirelessly to keep their energy concealed and suppressed, until they can let it all out in a violent burst. Features 1st Level - Armaments of Devastation 1st level - Accelerant 6th Level - Devastating Presence 11th Level - Devastating Strikes 11th Level - Extra Attack 17th Level - Culmination of Devastation
When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in glaives, greataxes, greatswords, halberds, and pikes. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor and shields.

At 1st level, you’ve learned how to create an accelerant with your devastating energy, overcharging your attacks. When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can force the target to roll a strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the target is knocked prone and suffers an additional effect depending on your imbuement. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier. When you take a short or long rest, you regain all expended uses. Accelerant Effect​ Damage Type Effect Acid The target’s AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn. Fire The target takes additional fire damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die. Cold The target’s speed is reduced by half of their maximum until the end of your next turn. Lightning You may force one other creature of your choice within 10 feet of the target to take lightning damage equal to two rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die. Thunder The target is pushed back 15 feet.

At 6th level, your mere presence is recognized as a threat, inciting opponents to focus their aggression on you. Each creature of your choice that starts its turn within 30 feet of you and can see you must roll a Wisdom saving throw against to your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature has disadvantage on attacks that don’t target you until the end of that creature’s turn. If a creature succeeds on this saving throw, they are immune to this effect for the next 24 hours.

Starting at 11th level, whenever you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement or a channeler spell that shares a damage type with your chosen Elemental Imbuement, you ignore resistance to that damage type, and you may treat immunity to that damage type as resistance.
Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

At 17th level, you’ve wrought elemental devastation everywhere you’d gone, and have found the perfect way to channel it. When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can reroll that attack against any number of other targets within 30ft, hitting each target simultaneously. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.
Madness Channeler

The channel of Madness represents a rare and often fanatical sect of channelers that believe in submitting control over their mind and actions to the powers within themselves, even to their own detriment Features 1st Level - Armaments of Madness 1st Level - Medium For Madness 6th Level - Braincharge 11th Level - Mental Overchannel 11th Level - Psychic Armaments 17th Level - Culmination of Madness
When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in hand crossbows, heavy crossbows, and longbows.

At 1st level, you may select two 1st level enchantment spells. You learn these spells and may cast each of them once per day without expending a spell slot. At 6th level, you may choose two 2nd level enchantment spells, two 3rd level enchantment spells at 11th level, and two 4th level enchantment spells at 17th level. Additionally, you may pick psychic damage as the damage type for your Elemental Imbuement.

At 6th level, you’re able to overload the minds of others, driving them further towards insanity. When a creature fails the first save from an enchantment spell you cast, they take extra psychic damage equal to your Elemental Imbuement die. Then, you may have one creature you can see within 30 feet of you gain advantage on the next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw they make until the beginning of your next turn.

At 11th level, when you deal psychic damage to a creature, you may choose to deal maximum psychic damage rather than rolling. If you do, the target is stunned until the beginning of your next turn. You cannot use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

At 11th level, when you imbue a weapon with psychic damage, you can change that weapon’s base damage type to psychic for as long as it’s imbued. Add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage of your weapon attacks imbued with psychic damage.

At 17th level, it’s hard to tell if you’re still sane or not; your internal energy has corroded your mind past the point of no return. You gain advantage on saving throws against enchantment spells. In addition, you gain immunity to psychic damage and immunity to effects that would charm or frighten you. Once per day, when you cast an enchantment spell, if it would target only one creature and no other creatures, you can instead make it target as many creatures as you can see within 60 feet of you.

The Channel of Volatility is a controversial path to undertake, as though it is the easiest channel to ‘master’, it may prove most perilous to the channeler using it. Those who practice the channel of Volatility must exercise extreme caution, else they risk losing control of their magic to horrific consequence. Features: 1st Level - Armaments of Volatility 1st Level - Volatile Charge 6th Level - Volatile Surge 11th Level - Risk and Reward 11th Level - Extra Attack 17th Level - Culmination of Volatility
When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in flails, mauls, and warhammers. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor and shields.

Your internal energy is difficult to predict and control, yet it assists you when you need it most. Starting at 1st level, whenever you hit with a weapon attack using your imbued weapon, note the result of the attack roll and your Imbuement die roll. Odd. If the result of the attack roll is odd, you gain temporary hit points equal to the result of your Imbuement die, which disappears whenever you take a short or long rest. Even. If the result of the attack roll is even, the attack deals extra damage equal to the result of your Imbuement die.

The unpredictable effects of your magic have branched into even more peculiar effects. Starting at 6th level, when you cast a channeler spell, roll your Elemental Imbuement die and note the result. Consult the Volatile Surge table for additional effects. Surge Effect​ Result Effect 1 You take damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die. 2 You add another roll of your Elemental Imbuement die to the spell’s damage. 3 Your AC increases by 1 until the start of your next turn. 4 You gain advantage on your next attack roll until the end of your next turn. 5 You gain additional temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die. 6 You can make an additional weapon attack as part of the same bonus action. 7 You gain resistance to the next attack that hits you until the start of your next turn. 8 Reroll on this table twice, and the effects of both rolls occur. If you roll the same effect twice, the effect only applies once.
At 11th level; your frequent interactions with fickle energies have allowed you to lean further into their volatility. You learn one additional Ante option, and gain an additional Ante charge.
Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

At 17th level, your destructive magic is longing for escape from your mortal shell. Once per day, when you’re reduced to zero hit points, you may choose to release all of your internal energy in one burst. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must roll a dexterity saving throw equal to your spell save DC. On a failed save, a target takes 15d10 damage and is stunned until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and isn’t stunned. The damage type is the same as your elemental Imbuement. In either case, the explosion kills you immediately, disintegrating all non-magical gear and equipment you’re carrying and wearing.

Wondrous Item, uncommon(+1), rare(+2), very rare(+3) Attunement Requires Attunement by a Channeler Description This is a glob of discolored clay that you apply to a weapon you're proficient with. While wielding the applied weapon, you gain a bonus to spell attack rolls and to saving throw DCs of your channeler spells. This bonus is determined by the clay's rarity. In addition, you can regain 1 ante as an action while wielding the applied weapon. You can't use this property again until you finish a long rest.

Wondrous Item, uncommon(+1), rare(+2), very rare(+3) Attunement Requires Attunement by a Channeler Description This is a glob of discolored clay that you apply to a weapon you're proficient with. While wielding the applied weapon, you gain a bonus to spell attack rolls and to saving throw DCs of your channeler spells. This bonus is determined by the clay's rarity. In addition, you can regain 1 ante as an action while wielding the applied weapon. You can't use this property again until you finish a long rest.

Weapon: Martial, Melee 5gp, 1 lbs. --- 1d4 Slashing - Finesse, Light, Nick Finesse: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. Light: A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons. Special: Claw Caps can be fitted over a creature's natural weapons as an action changing it's base statistics and properties to match that of the natural weapon it is fitted over, it then gains a new weapon mastery depending on the natural weapon's damage type: Bludgeoning: Topple Piercing: Sap Slashing: Vex Natural Weapons with Claw Caps cannot be used to make unarmed strikes.

Wondrous Item, very rare Description This magical item is made up of two distinct parts, the first being a claw-like structure, and the second being a handle. The two pieces fit together in such a way that the open claw points away from your hand when held. While you are holding the handle, and the claw is attached, you can use a bonus action to speak the items command word, causing the claw to be magically propelled up to 30 feet. When you do so, you may target either an object or creature. At the end of the claws journey, the claw embeds itself harmlessly into the target and two pieces are magically pulled back together. If the target object or creature is either your size or larger, you are pulled up to 30 feet towards it. Inversely, if the target object or creature is at least one size smaller than you, it is pulled up to 30 feet towards you. If the target is a creature, make an attack roll with a +10 bonus against its armor class. If the attack misses, the claw returns to the handle without moving either you or the target. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. The clawshot is a magical device first invented by the artificer Flare. The clawshot is used for quick movement and repositioning, and for getting past otherwise impassable obstacles. It is also quite effective in low gravity environments, like those it's inventor commonly reside. "It's perfectly safe to use, I swear. Just look at me, I use it all the time!" - Flare

Wondrous Item, legendary Attunement Requires Attunement by a Sorcerer, Wizard, or Warlock of a Non-Evil Alignment Description The Cloak of Levitation is one of many items imbued with power to sustain magics that practitioners of the mystic arts cannot. While you wear this cloak, you have a fly speed equal to your walking speed. If you fall while in the air when wearing this cloak, you descend at a rate of 30 feet per round until you land, taking no fall damage. If you are not wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 13 + your Dexterity modifier while wearing this cloak. When a melee attack made against you would reduce you to 20 points or lower, you can use your reaction to have the cloak fly off of your shoulders and immediately attempt a grapple against the attacker. The cloak counts as a medium sized creature for the purposes of grappling and has a +8 modifier to Strength (Athletics) checks made to grapple. If the the grapple is successful the attacker also gains the Blinded condition for the duration of the grapple. As a bonus action you may call the cloak back to you if it is within 60 feet. When targeted by an attack or by a feature that forces a Dexterity saving throw, you may use your reaction to have the cloak take the brunt of the attack, transferring half of the damage you take to the cloak. Once the cloak is used this way, it cannot be used to fly until the next dawn. Additionally, this property cannot be used again until the next dawn. Sentience. The Cloak of Levitation is a sentient chaotic good wondrous item, with an Intelligence score of 16, a Wisdom score of 14, and a Charisma score of 17. It has hearing and blindsight out to a range of 120 feet. The cloak can communicate by transmitting basic emotion to its wielder and can communicate basic concepts through gestures. It can read and understand Common. While you are attuned to it, the Cloak of Levitation also understands every language you know. Personality. The Cloak of Levitation has a flamboyant and playful personality, but is also a stout defender of its wearer. The cloak generally dislikes anyone of evil alignment, and tends to display said dislike to its wearer. The cloak's purpose is to protect its wearer, and assist in their pursuits in whatever way it can. The cloak is drawn towards assisting in academia and adventuring, being quick thinking in combat and unafraid to communicate its ideas in the study.
Five legendary mantles, forged in answer to the Masks of the Dragon Queen

When word first reached the temples of Bahamut that the Cult of the Dragon had gathered five masks of chromatic power — one for each of the Dragon Queen’s brood — the Platinum Dragon’s clergy did not counsel the forging of five masks in reply. A mask hides the face. A mask makes the wearer into the dragon it depicts, and swallows the name beneath it. The cult’s champions had been happy to disappear into their masks. Bahamut’s would not. So the Talons of Justice, that old and stubborn order of dragon knights, asked instead for cloaks. A cloak is worn openly. A cloak is a thing given, thrown over the shoulders of someone who has been recognized, and it leaves the wearer’s face bare to be seen and answered for. The petition was carried to the Monastery of the Yellow Rose and from there, by means no chronicle records plainly, into the presence of the Platinum Father himself. Bahamut consented, but not alone. Five of his metallic children came to the anvil — gold, silver, bronze, copper, and brass — and each gave something of itself: a shed scale, a breath held in a stoppered horn, a drop of blood, a memory, a laugh. Bahamut set his own power over the working like a hand over a candle flame, and what came off the anvil were five mantles of woven metal, each light as a summer cloth and each carrying a fragment of the draconic soul that had answered the call. He laid one condition on the gift, and the condition is the whole of its purpose. The cloaks cannot be combined. Where the cult’s masks could be gathered into a single crown for a single tyrant, the Platinum Ward was made to resist exactly that: the mantles cannot be merged, reforged, nested, or fused by any magic yet found, and no creature may be attuned to more than one of them at a time. Tiamat’s power concentrates. Bahamut’s distributes. Five champions, five names, five reasons to stand — and if one falls, four remain, and the cloak of the fallen will find another shoulder. The Talons hold that this is why the Ward has never been broken. A cabal can be beheaded. A conspiracy of five friends who each hold one fifth of a weapon and none of the whole is a harder thing to unmake. Each cloak also carries the last clause of its making, spoken by Bahamut over the finished work and known to every wearer the moment the clasp closes: stand always against the Dragon Queen. No wearer has ever needed the words explained.

The following applies to all five Cloaks of the Platinum Ward. Sized to the Wearer. The cloak reshapes itself to fit any creature Small, Medium, or Large that attunes to it, and cannot be damaged by ordinary means. One Mantle, One Champion. You can’t be attuned to more than one Cloak of the Platinum Ward at a time. If you attempt it, the second attunement fails and you take no benefit from either cloak until you finish a long rest. Singular. There is only ever one of each of the five cloaks, and their magic cannot be replicated, copied, or reproduced by any craft or spell. Unjoinable. The cloaks cannot be combined, merged, reforged, or made into any other item, by any means. Attempts to do so fail, and the cloak is unharmed by the attempt. Anathema to the Masks. A Cloak of the Platinum Ward and a Mask of the Dragon Queen cannot be borne by the same creature. If you are attuned to one, you can’t attune to the other, and while you carry both, the two items physically repel each other — clasps refuse to close, straps slip free, and the mask will not seat against the face of a cloaked wearer. Held forcibly together, they shed sparks of gold and black smoke and can’t be made to touch. No power short of a god has yet compelled them to share a wearer. The Cloak’s Urging. The cloak is not sentient. It cannot speak, plan, or be reasoned with. But something of the dragon that gave its scale remains in the weave, and it leans. A wearer finds the merciful choice arriving in their mind a moment before the ruthless one, feels a reluctance they can’t quite source when they consider abandoning the helpless, and sleeps easier on the nights they did right. This is influence, not compulsion: the wearer keeps every scrap of free will, and a determined villain can wear a cloak and remain a villain. They will simply find it a slightly wearying garment.

Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A mantle of burnished gold scales, each no larger than a thumbnail and each perfectly overlapping the last, so that the whole hangs like heavy silk and rings faintly when it moves. Fine metallic whiskers trail from the collar, and the clasp is worked in the shape of a dragon’s brow crowned with a fan of spines. It is warm to the touch at all hours, in all weather. While you are wearing the cloak and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against fire damage. If you already have resistance to fire damage from another source, you instead have immunity to fire damage. If you already have immunity to fire damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to fire damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the fire damage dealt. Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class. Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6. Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with gold dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Weakening Flame. If you deal fire damage to a creature, then until the end of that creature’s next turn it has disadvantage on Strength-based attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.
documents.s: Gold Cloak of the Platinum Ward

documents.t: Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A mantle of mirror-bright silver plates, smooth and seamless, edged in a swept crest of frost-white metal that rises behind the wearer’s head like a breaking wave. It shows reflections a half-heartbeat late. The clasp is a single unbroken ring, cold as a mountain spring and never dulled by tarnish. While you are wearing the cloak and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against cold damage. If you already have resistance to cold damage from another source, you instead have immunity to cold damage. If you already have immunity to cold damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to cold damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the cold damage dealt. Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class. Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6. Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with silver dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Cloudwalk. You can walk, run, and stand upon clouds, fog, mist, and similar vapors as though they were solid ground. While within 10 feet of such a vapor, you can also treat open air as solid footing, and you take no damage from a fall that begins while this benefit is active.
documents.s: Silver Cloak of the Platinum Ward

documents.t: Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A mantle of weathered bronze, verdigris settled green in every groove, its plates broad and ridged like the scutes of something built for deep water. The collar rises in a hooked jaw plate, and the whole garment smells faintly of salt and lightning-struck air. Rainwater beads and runs from it without leaving a mark. While you are wearing the cloak and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against lightning damage. If you already have resistance to lightning damage from another source, you instead have immunity to lightning damage. If you already have immunity to lightning damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to lightning damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the lightning damage dealt. Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class. Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6. Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with bronze dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Water Breathing. You can breathe underwater. Repulsing Shock. If you deal lightning damage to a creature, you can push it up to 10 feet directly away from you.
documents.s: Bronze Cloak of the Platinum Ward

documents.t: Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A mantle of hammered copper, every plate marked with the dents of the hammer that made it, its collar flaring into a pair of backswept horns. The clasp is worked into a wry, upturned mouth, and more than one wearer has sworn the expression changes when no one is looking directly at it. It never quite hangs straight. While you are wearing the cloak and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against acid damage. If you already have resistance to acid damage from another source, you instead have immunity to acid damage. If you already have immunity to acid damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to acid damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the acid damage dealt. Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class. Dragon Breath. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with copper dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Stonestride. You have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. Trickster’s Tongue. You have advantage on Charisma (Deception) and Charisma (Performance) checks.

documents.t: Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A mantle of dull brass, pitted and scoured by windblown sand, its plates overlapping in a single blunt crest that runs from collar to hem. It is the plainest of the five and the lightest, and it stirs faintly even in still air, as though remembering a wind. The clasp is a simple sand-worn disc. While you are wearing the cloak and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against fire damage. If you already have resistance to fire damage from another source, you instead have immunity to fire damage. If you already have immunity to fire damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to fire damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the fire damage dealt. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with brass dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Brass Lullaby (1/Day). As a Magic action, you exhale a cloud of sleep gas in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 18 Constitution saving throw or fall unconscious for 1 minute. The effect ends on a creature if it takes damage or if another creature uses an action to shake it awake. Constructs and undead are unaffected, as are creatures immune to the Unconscious condition.
documents.s: Brass Cloak of the Platinum Ward

documents.t: Uncommon, Wondrous Description A swirling cloud sealed within a small glass bottle. While a Cloud in a Bottle is on your person, you gain the ability to jump while mid-air. Additionally, you can treat your long and high jumps as if you had moved 10 feet before doing so, even if you didn't. Once you jump in this way, you cannot do so again until you land on the ground.

Wondrous Item, common Description This 3-inch cube is the direct counterpart of the thermal cube, it emanates cold to keep the temperature within 15 ft of it at 41 degrees Fahrenheit (5 degrees Celsius)

Wondrous Item, Legendary Description This 3-inch cube is a direct counterpart of the Thermal Hypercube. The cube resonates slightly when touched, and emanates cold to keep the temperature within 30 ft of it at -20 degrees Fahrenheit (~-29 degrees Celcius). This area is also subject to extreme cold.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This mask like accessories produces a voice based on the wearers thoughts, it fits over the mouth and allows someone or something who doesn't have capabilities of speech to speak a language they know, in addition, you are able to speak and understand spoken Common while wearing this mask

Wondrous Item, very rare Description This scabbard is decorated with depictions of the deity it was dedicated to, and it automatically adjusts to what kind of melee weapon it will hold, such as changing size to fit any blade or becoming a series of metal rings to holster weapons like axes, hammers, or spears. When you draw a melee weapon that is held by this scabbard, you can bless the weapon. For the next minute, whenever you make an attack roll with this weapon, you can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to the attack roll. Additionally, attacks made with this melee weapon are considered magical and deal an additional 1d4 radiant damage. This effect ends early if you stow the weapon or if a different creature other than you wields it. The effect can be applied three times, after which you regain all expended uses at the next dawn. If you are under the effects of the bless spell while wielding a melee weapon with the scabbard's effect, the d4s granted by the bless spell and this item turn into d6s.

Wondrous Item, rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description This magic longcoat is adorned with raven feathers and carved jet buttons. While wearing this coat, you have advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks. Inaddition, the coat has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the coat, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 of its charges to disappear, releasing up to three ravens from your location under your control that scatters into the air. Each raven has AC 12, 1 hit point, and can fly up to 40 feet as part of this bonus action without provoking opportunity attacks. At the start of your next turn, the ravens vanish, and you reappear in the space of one of the ravens (your choice). If all the ravens are reduced to 0 hit points, you reappear early in the same space as the last one that died. When you do, any excess damage dealt to the raven carries over to your normal form.

Wondrous Item, rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description This magic longcoat is adorned with raven feathers and carved jet buttons. While wearing this coat, you have advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks. Inaddition, the coat has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk. Each raven has AC 12, 1 hit point, and can fly up to 40 feet as part of this bonus action without provoking opportunity attacks. At the start of your next turn, the ravens vanish, and you reappear in the space of one of the ravens (your choice). If all the ravens are reduced to 0 hit points, you reappear early in the same space as the last one that died. When you do, any excess damage dealt to the raven carries over to your normal form.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Container of Heat and Frost Description This dense metal container is adorned with three arcane designs along the edge of its removable lid. When filled with up to one gallon of watery liquid (Liquid with the same viscosity as water), the vessel can either heat, chill, or maintain the liquid's temperature. As an action, you can press one of the arcane symbols to heat the liquid to a boil (212 degrees Fahrenheit or 100 degrees Celsius), chill it (33 degrees Fahrenheit or 1 degree Celsius), or keep it at temperature for up to 24 hours. It takes one minute for the vessel to heat or cool a liquid down, and, once at temperature, maintains it. Liquids placed inside without activating the arcane designs will maintain its temperature for up to one hour before becoming tepid.

Wondrous Item , Uncommon Description This 3' cube glows slightly with yellow light while active, which can be identified as a standard "hazard" symbol while in darkness. The cube has 3 charges. As an action, you can touch the cube to a non-magical metallic object. If the object is smaller than the cube, it is destroyed as the object melts over the course of one minute. Otherwise, the cube melts away a section of the object equal to the cube in volume over the course of one minute. Either result spends one charge of the cube. The cube regains all of it's charges daily at dawn. The cube makes a fairly loud cracking sound as it melts metal, which can be heard easily from up to 30ft away.

Wondrous Item, very rare Description A Couriers Cradle needs two pieces to have any sort of effect. A Sending Stone, and a Couriers Cradle. Without both components it has no function. A Courier's Cradle consists of three parts. A chassis, typically squared and made of polished stone, granite, or marble for particularly wealthy folk. A basin sat in the cubed bottom, around half a foot wide and typically filled with water. And lastly a bowl mounted over the basin, made of rare material such as gemstone, brass, or pure quartz. While a creature is within 5 feet of a cradle, it may place a sending stone into it's bowl. It then takes a minute to fasten and adjust the cradle for speaking. After this process is complete the cradle is assembled. Connection A creature may connect to another Courier's Cradle within a distance of up to the plane they exist according to the following difficulties, using an Intelligence (Arcana) check. If another Cradle is connected to this one, they establish a line of communication. This allows each to hear from the other side as if they were in the same room. Distance (Miles) DC 5 10 50 15 200 20 Planar 25 Disconnection A Courier's Cradle is automatically disconnected if both sides are not connected to one another or if the cradle is moved from where it was first activated.

A Courier's Cradle consists of three parts. A chassis, typically squared and made of polished stone, granite, or marble for particularly wealthy folk. Distance (Miles) DC 5 10 50 15 200 20 Planar 25 Disconnection A Courier's Cradle is automatically disconnected if both sides are not connected to one another or if the cradle is moved from where it was first activated.

Weapon (spear), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description The spear once used by the Storm Maiden of Norland, Hergatha, was said to be lost following her ultimate defeat during her efforts to conquer the Sea of Swords. It was written to have been bestowed by Tempus, but rumors whisper that it was actually bestowed to her by Valkur. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, the weapon ignores resistance to piercing damage. Blood Ocean. When you draw this weapon within one mile of a large body of water such as an ocean or lake, the seas within a five-mile radius become red like blood. When you attack a creature with this weapon while they are within a mile of the blood water, you have advantage on the attack roll. If it hits, the blood waters darken, and you deal an extra 2d6 piercing damage, or 2d8 piercing damage if wielded with two hands. The water returns to its normal color when you sheathe this weapon again. Umberlee's Blessing. While holding this spear, you can breath underwater and have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. You also gain the following character trait: "I have the compulsion to drown other living creatures". Norland's Champion. Each time you attack with this weapon, creatures of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you are inspired. Each creature gains temporary hit points equal to your constitution modifier. While a creature has these temporary hit points, they are immune to being frightened.

Wondrous Item, Uncommon Description Control your emotions, sweetheart, or the witches will come and steal your feelings away. Originally used as a toy to train young eladrin, this fey-infused flower crown changes appearance based on the wearer's mood. These moods also reflect the four seasons: winter, spring, summer, and autumn. The flowers will shift between four seasonal types dependent on the wearer's mood and the corresponding season. In addition, a harmless illusory effect will hover over the blossoms to reflect the same thing (Snowflakes fluttering around for winter/sadness, Fiery sparks for summer/passion etc). When the wearer undergoes a burst of any type of emotion (Flash of anger, sudden surprise etc), the flowers will wilt to a dull gray and the illusory effects will vanish to signify a loss of control. The next morning, the flowers will blossom to their full color after the lesson has been learned

Specializing on ice magic, wizards that have learned from the Cryomancy arcane tradition manipulate the crystalline structure of ice and bend it to their will. Many foolishly only see this magic as beautiful, and it is, but within the beauty of all that shimmering ice, is a slow and shivering death.

Your manipulation of ice allow you to acclimate to it and change the properties of spells. When you cast a spell that deals damage, you are able to change the damage type to cold damage unless its bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. You gain resistance to cold damage. When you reach 13th level on this class, you also gain resistance to fire damage, and at 17th level, you gain immunity to cold damage and the area 5 feet of you has the effects of extreme cold.

As an action, you can freeze a 5-foot cube of nonmagical water. The cube will remain frozen for one minute or until your concentration ends (as if you were concentrating on a spell). You can manipulate the ice as a bonus action to mold its shape to form objects or structures. The objects or structures you make have hit points equal to your wizard level. At 8th and 15th level, you freeze an area of 15-foot and 25-foot cube respectively. You can also create the ice out of moisture in the air, though the cubic footage you are able to manipulate is halved (i.e. you can produce a 7-foot cube from a 15-foot cube of air). Additionally, when you reach 15th level you can also freeze magical water, manipulate magical ice, and the cube can now be frozen for up to 1 hour.

Your body fills with ice magic and acts at times in preservation from external factors. When you become unconscious or asleep or are rendered unconscious or asleep, you are immediately encased in a layer of dense ice. This ice has hit points equal to twice your wizard level and an AC equal to your spell save DC. When the ice encases you as a result of being reduced to 0 hit points, the ice will stabilize you and freezes the area around you. All creatures within 10 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be restrained until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, they are not restrained but their speed is halved. When the restrained condition from this feature ends, the creature's speed is also halved. They can make another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of their turns. On a success, their speed returns to normal. The ice lasts for 1 minute, until it is destroyed, or when you choose to break the ice upon regaining consciousness. Once this feature is used it cannot be used again until a long rest.

Your control over ice have reached to an abnormal extreme, even by magical standards. Choose one wizard spell that deals damage in your spellbook. That spell's damage type permanently becomes cold damage when you cast it without using your Frigid Magic feature or other similar effect. You can change the spell for a different spell by spending 8 hours in study. The first time you deal damage to a creature that does not have resistance or immunity to cold damage on your turn, they take extra cold damage equal to your wizard level.

After extensive use of bending ice to your every whim, you understand all of its inner workings. You're able to apply this knowledge by performing grand feats on a monumental scale. As an action, you are able to freeze everything within a 60 foot radius sphere centered around you. This creates sleets of ice and snow on the ground and super chilling the air, rendering the area as difficult terrain. All creatures of your choice takes 3d6 cold damage upon activation and must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be frozen. While frozen, a creature is considered incapacitated and their speed is reduced to 0 until the end of their next turn. Furthermore, you create a 30 foot radius sphere of a perpetual blizzard that is centered around and moves with you. When a creature of your choice enters the area for the first time or starts their turn in it, the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take cold damage equal to half your wizard level and have its speed halved until the start of its next turn. The area inside the blizzard acts as a heavily obscured area for all creatures except you. Both the difficult terrain and blizzard lasts for 1 minute or when you end both effects using an action, afterwards you no longer gain the effects of the Frigid Magic feature until you take a short rest. Once this feature is used it cannot be used again until a long rest.

Wondrous Item, very rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description While you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can Hide as a bonus action if you are not being directly observed. The cloak has 3 charges for the following other properties. The cloak regains all expended charges daily at dawn. Blacklight. You can spend 1 charge as an action to cast the Shadow of Moil spell. Umbral Augment. You can spend 1 charge as a reaction when you fail a saving throw or ability check and add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to the roll.

Wondrous Item, legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description Used to summon daylight, this 6-inch-diameter, gold-white orb is warm to the touch. You can spend 10 minutes to activate it, causing the area within 10 miles of it at the moment of activation to become daylight even if it is nighttime. This daylight lasts for 24 hours, until you cancel it as an action, or until your attunement to the pearl ends. Once used, the pearl can't be used again for 24 hours.

Weapon (Musket) Rarity Varies (Rare/Very Rare/Legendary) Attunement Requires Attunement by a spellcaster Description This magical firearm is designed for use in magical combat. Due to this fact, a spellcaster can use the weapon as their spellcasting focus. You gain a +1/2/3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magical weapons, and the same bonus to spell attack rolls you make while holding this weapon. When you cast a spell using this weapon as your spellcasting focus, your next attack made with the weapon uses your spellcasting ability instead of dexterity. Additionally, if the spell deals damage, the weapon's damage type changes to that of the spell.

Weapon (Musket) Rarity Varies (Rare/Very Rare/Legendary) Attunement Requires Attunement by a spellcaster Description This magical firearm is designed for use in magical combat. Due to this fact, a spellcaster can use the weapon as their spellcasting focus. You gain a +1/2/3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magical weapons, and the same bonus to spell attack rolls you make while holding this weapon. When you cast a spell using this weapon as your spellcasting focus, your next attack made with the weapon uses your spellcasting ability instead of dexterity. Additionally, if the spell deals damage, the weapon's damage type changes to that of the spell.

1st-level evocation. (Cleric, Druid, Paladin) Meta Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V, M (a shield worth at least 1 sp) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description As a bonus action, you can infuse a shield you're currently wielding with divine energy. If the shield is not magical, your AC increases by 1 until you stop wielding the shield or the spell ends. The first time a creature targets you with a melee attack and misses during this spell's duration, your shield bursts with divine radiance as you deflect the blow. The stored energy within releases and deals 1d6 radiant damage to any hostile creatures within 5 feet. When this blast hits an undead or a fiend, it deals an additional 1d6 radiant damage to it. After the blast, the spell ends. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the radiant damage dealt by the blast increases by 1d6 for each slot level after the 1st.

Weapon: Martial, Melee 120gp, 8 lbs. --- 2d4 slashing - Reach, Two-handed, Special Description Proficiency with a double-bladed scythe allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special. If you attack with a double-bladed scythe as part of the Attack action on your turn, you can use a bonus action immediately after to make a melee attack with it. This attack deals 1d4 slashing damage on a hit.

Weapon (any firearm), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description The barrel of this magic firearm is shaped like a dragon's maw, and the weapon is infused with the essence of a chromatic, gem, or metallic dragon's breath. When you hit with an attack roll using this magic firearm, the target takes an extra 1d6 damage of the same type as the breath infused in the firearm--acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, radiant, or thunder. If you load no ammunition in the weapon, it produces its own, automatically creating one piece of magic ammunition when you pull the trigger. The ammunition created by the firearm vanishes the instant after it hits or misses a target.

Wondrous Item, rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description While wearing these knuckles you get a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with unarmed strikes. While these knuckles are equipped you can’t use other weapons and the knuckles take an action to equip or unequip. The knuckles deal an additional 1d6 damage of which the type is determined by the dragon scales used to create it. Scale Color Damage Type Red Fire Green Poison Blue Lightning Black Acid White Cold Gold Fire Brass Fire Copper Acid Silver Cold Bronze Lightning Sapphire Thunder Emerald Psychic Amethyst Force Crystal Radiant Topaz Necrotic

Weapon (dagger), uncommon Description You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. You also add 1d4 to all stealth checks made while you are holding this weapon. This dagger appears to be of Elven make, and has a long, cruel, slender black blade. The dagger always appears wreathed in shadows, making it hard to focus upon clearly, even on a bright summer's day. It also bestows some of this uncanny ability to its wielder. Proficiency with a Dagger allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it

Weapon (double bladed Scimitar), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description One Blade of Light contains the essence of goodness and holiness, the other Blade of Darkness contains the essence of evil and deceit. When attacking with this weapon you choose with which blade you attack. Light Blade: Deals an additional 1d6 radiant damage, and another 1d4 against undead or fiends Dark Blade: Deals an additional 1d6 necrotic damage, and restores 1d4+4 hp to the wielder if a humanoid or celestial is killed using this blade. The additional damage applies to the bonus attack damage.

Wondrous Item, rare Description A Dugger's Tome is a large leather bound book. Each tome can only be used once by placing it on any book, as soon as it touches the other book, the Tome will become an exact replica of the copied book, and the copied book now has a magical aura of conjuration magic, whatever happens to one book will likewise happen to the other if both are on the same plane (Words written, water spilled, pages torn etc) It was originally created to sync libraries and records across long distances but was later adapted by spies and criminal for espionage.
