Each tome can only be used once by placing it on any book, as soon as it touches the other book, the Tome will become an exact replica of the copied book, and the copied book now has a magical aura of conjuration magic, whatever happens to one book will likewise happen to the other if both are on the same plane (Words written, water spilled, pages torn etc) It was originally created to sync libraries and records across long distances but was later adapted by spies and criminal for espionage.

Weapon(any), rare Description You have a +1 bonus to attack rolls made with this magic weapon and on a hit, the weapon deals an extra 1d6 damage of a type determined by the runes engraved upon the weapon, which the DM chooses or determines randomly. D5 Extra Damage Type 1 Fire 2 Cold 3 Lightning 4 Thunder 5 Acid

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description A simple, platinum-plated square flask carved with simple, almost childish sylvan runes. You cannot fill this flask with anything, as it is perpetually filled with fresh hot cocoa, peppered with little marshmallows, and partially melted chocolate chips. Sprinkling a pinch of flavorings, such as caramel sugars or peppermint crumbs, will permanently flavor the hot cocoa similarly. This can be reversed by dropping in a pinch of unflavored chocolate chips. If you pour hot chocolate from the bottle, rather than drinking from it, the liquid vanishes the moment it leaves the bottle.

Wondrous , Common Description While a sword is within the scabbard, the blade can't be damaged by fire or rusted by water. In addition, the scabbard preserves the current sharpness of the blade ensuring it never dulls while sheathed.

Wondrous Item, common Description A stick of Eternal Chalk never breaks or wears down during use. When writing or drawing with this chalk, you choose the color of its marks and whether they emit a faint glow. Any marks you make with this chalk cannot be wiped away, washed out, or erased for 7 days by anyone except you. If the chalk ever becomes the sole target of "Dispel Magic" or another magical effect intended to leave it permanently inert, it instead crumbles to dust, marks it has produced cease glowing, fade to a dull grey, and are no longer protected from erasure.

Wondrous item, uncommon Description This small, glass sphere is enchanted with weak divination magics to help you find specific words or phrases in writing. It has a stylized iris etched into the glass. You can use a bonus action to speak the Eye's command word aloud, followed by the word or phrase you're searching for. The word or phrase magically appears and floats within the sphere. By holding the Eye in a free hand, your vision becomes magically enhanced to subconsciously highlight the word or phrase you searched for in a green light whenever you see it. Once you've used the Eye's ability for the first time, you can change the word or phrase as many times as you like for the next hour, after which the item can not be used again until the following dawn.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description There are several known versions of this hooded cloak; some look plain and common, while others appear intricate and expensive. When the hood is raised, a minor illusion appears which hides the wearer's face in total magical darkness. The wearer can see out with no penalties, but only truesight or other magical means of seeing through illusions can penetrate the hood's darkness from outside.

Ammunition (Arrow), Legendary Description This arrow has a black lusterous shaft and adorned by an arrowhead made from a crystal like material that shines a gentle blue hue. In its original form, this magic arrow is ammuntion for bows but can alter its form(no action required) into a bolt that can be loaded to crossbows. The Failnaught never misses on a ranged attack and is an automatic hit, it will curve and move on its own in mid-air until it hits its target. If no open pathway is available, it pierces through any physical obstruction that is less than 1 foot thick or any magical barrier that may block its path (i.e. a metal door or a wall of force spell). The Failnaught uses a damage die of 1d8 instead of the weapon's damage die and ignores any damage resistances and immunities that it deals or inflicts. It retains its magical properties after an attack and can be reused again. Alternatively, the Failnaught can be used without a bow or crossbow, it can be used as a dart with a damage die of 1d6. [When obtained in any way, quest, loot, craft(if CMs make it craftable), etc., you only get 1 arrow and not a bundle.]

Fallen King's Halberd Weapon (halberd), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description This halberd was owned by a great king whose name is long forgotten who reigned from a kingdom that has long been destroyed. Its old but strangely robust body has scattered dents and damage from all around. In contrast, both the point and blade remain seamless and sharp against all the roughness of use and wear it has experienced. Unflinching. While you wield this weapon, you gain immunity to the charmed and frightened condition. Ever Strong. When you hit with this weapon, you deal an extra 5 weapon damage. If you have less than half your maximum hit points, this damage instead becomes 10. Till my Last Breath. When you drop to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack with this weapon on that turn at a target within range with advantage before going down. If you have the Extra Attack feature, you can make those attacks from this reaction as if its an Attack action(No other feature or effect can treat this reaction this way). You regain the ability to use this reaction again at dawn.

Fallen King's Halberd Weapon (halberd), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description This halberd was owned by a great king whose name is long forgotten who reigned from a kingdom that has long been destroyed. Its old but strangely robust body has scattered dents and damage from all around. In contrast, both the point and blade remain seamless and sharp against all the roughness of use and wear it has experienced. Unflinching. While you wield this weapon, you gain immunity to the charmed and frightened condition. Ever Strong. When you hit with this weapon, you deal an extra 5 weapon damage. If you have less than half your maximum hit points, this damage instead becomes 10. Till my Last Breath. When you drop to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack with this weapon on that turn at a target within range with advantage before going down. If you have the Extra Attack feature, you can make those attacks from this reaction as if its an Attack action(No other feature or effect can treat this reaction this way). You regain the ability to use this reaction again at dawn.

Weapon (greataxe), artifact (requires attunement) Forged from the remains of the nightmare known as False Razor, this alien weapon still hungers for life. False Razor has three forms, retaining all previous properties as it advances. This weapon must be obtained in Chult from beating a Trial of Orolunga. Form I — Base Form +3 Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with False Razor. Damage. On a hit, False Razor deals: 1d12 slashing + 2d6 piercing + 1d8 necrotic + Strength modifier + 3 Siphoning Edge. Whenever you hit a creature with False Razor, you regain 1d4 hit points. If you are already at your hit point maximum, you instead gain 1d4 temporary hit points. Form II — Mind Splitter As a bonus action, choose one creature within 30 feet. It must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw. Failure: The creature is stunned until the end of its next turn. Success: The creature takes 2d6 psychic damage, and its speed is halved until the end of its next turn. You can use Mind Splitter a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1) per long rest. Unlock: Complete a solo quest and kill a CR 25+ creature. Form III — Existence Rend Once per turn when you damage a creature with False Razor, you can force it to make a DC 23 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, its hit point maximum is reduced by 3d4. This reduction can reduce a creature’s maximum HP to 0. Unlock: Complete another solo quest, kill another CR 25+ creature, and personally kill a level 20+ good-aligned humanoid. Sentience Alignment: Neutral Evil INT 16 | WIS 14 | CHA 18 False Razor has hearing and darkvision out to 120 feet and communicates telepathically with its wielder. It speaks, reads, and understands Common, Abyssal, and Tabaxi. False Razor is patient, predatory, and fascinated by killing. It has a particular hatred for Blackrazor, desiring the death of any creature wielding it and ultimately the destruction of Blackrazor itself. Curse — The Razor’s Hunger Once attuned, the wielder cannot willingly part with False Razor or end their attunement. Whenever the wielder attempts a long rest, roll 1d3. On a 1, False Razor compels them to abandon the rest and seek out something to kill. Breaking the Curse. The curse can only be broken by the attuned wielder using Wish specifically to sever their bond with False Razor. Doing so permanently destroys False Razor. No other spell or effect can end the attunement or remove the curse.

The Fey Duelist archetype merges the cunning and agility of a rogue with the enchanting power of the Feywild. These rogues are gifted (or cursed) with the boons of Archfey patrons, weaving magic and mischief into their every movement. They are agile combatants and masters of manipulation, channeling Fey magic to outmaneuver foes, charm allies, and spread chaos on the battlefield. Whether as emissaries of a Fey court, champions of their Archfey patron, or independent agents who stumbled into the gifts of the Feywild, Fey Duelists tread a fine line between mortal pragmatism and the capricious beauty of the Fey. Their motivations are as varied as the Feywild itself, often driven by a blend of personal ambition, devotion to their patron, or a desire to unweave the chains of mundane reality and reshape the world with Fey-inspired artistry. Playstyle and Motivations​ The Fey Duelist excels in roles that combine agility, cunning, and creativity. They bring versatility to combat and social interactions, offering a mix of mobility, control, and spellcasting that allows them to adapt to nearly any situation. Players who enjoy weaving spells and martial combat together will find the Fey Duelist a rewarding choice. Motivations for a Fey Duelist might include: Devotion to an Archfey: Serving a powerful Fey entity as a trusted agent or champion, spreading their influence or carrying out their will. Personal Freedom: Using Fey gifts to escape or defy systems of control, embracing the chaotic and whimsical nature of the Feywild. Vengeance or Redemption: Seeking to right a past wrong or balance a perceived injustice using the unique powers of the Fey. Curiosity and Mischief: Exploring the boundaries of mortal and Fey realms, motivated by wonder and the joy of discovery. Who Would Thrive as a Fey Duelist?​ The Fey Duelist appeals to characters who want to: Command the Social Arena: Features like Binding Words provide robust tools for persuasion, manipulation, and intrigue. Outmaneuver and Disrupt Enemies: Abilities like Elusive Action and Distant Dodge emphasize mobility and tactical positioning. Ideal Players and Characters​ The Charismatic Manipulator: Players who enjoy talking their way out of trouble, influencing NPCs, and using charm to solve problems. The Tactical Trickster: Players who like to use cunning, positioning, and the environment to control the flow of combat. The Fey Enthusiast: Players who love the whimsical, mysterious, and chaotic themes of the Feywild and want to embody its spirit. When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells. Cantrips You learn three cantrips: Vicious Mockery and two other cantrips of your choice from the warlock or bard spell list. You learn another warlock or bard cantrip of your choice at 10th level. Spell Slots The Fey Duelist Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your warlock or bard spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest. For example, if you know the 1st-level spell Charm Person and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast Charm Person using either slot. Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher You know three 1st-level warlock or bard spells of your choice, two of which you must choose from the enchantment and illusion spells on the warlock or bard spell list. The Spells Known column of the Fey Duelist Spellcasting table shows when you learn more warlock or bard spells of 1st level or higher. Each of these spells must be an enchantment or illusion spell of your choice, and must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 7th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level. The spells you learn at 8th, 14th, and 20th level can come from any school of magic. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the warlock or bard spells you know with another spell of your choice from the warlock or bard spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, and it must be an enchantment or illusion spell, unless you're replacing the spell you gained at 3rd, 8th, 14th, or 20th level from any school of magic. Spellcasting Ability Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your warlock or bard spells, since you learn your spells through dedicated study and memorization. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a warlock or bard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one. Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

Start at 3rd level, when you cast Vicious Mockery, you can now cast it as a Bonus Action. Additionally, the first attack roll, ability check or saving throw you make against an affected creature before the end of your next turn is made with advantage.

Starting at 9th level, you can weave Fey Magic into your movements and attacks, enhancing them. Once per turn, you can modify a rogue feature to add an additional effect, as listed below: Fey Attack: Sneak Attack deals an additional 1d6 psychic damage. This additional damage is increased at 13th (2d6) level & 17th (3d6) level. Elusive Action: Immediately before or after using Cunning Action, a 5ft cube surrounding you becomes Heavily Obscured to everyone except you until the start of your next turn. Distant Dodge: Whenever you use Uncanny Dodge after being hit with an attack, you may teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can also regain uses by expending a spell slot for each use you want to restore (no action required).

At 13th level, you can weave a magical enchantment into your words, undermining and binding those that hear it. As an action you can speak a word infused with fey magic to a creature within 30 feet that can hear you, forcing them to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). On a failed saving throw, fey magic binds it, and the only actions that it can take before the end of its next turn are the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, or Hide action. If the target succeeds on its saving throw, it has no hint that you tried to bind it. Any creature under the effect of Vicious Mockery cast via your Vexing feature automatically fails the saving throw for this feature. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest. You can also regain uses by expending a spell slot (3rd level) for each use you want to restore (no action required).

Starting at 17th level, as an action you can make a Charisma (Persuasion or Deception) check against a creature that you can see that isn’t incapacitated, contested by a Wisdom (Insight) check. If you succeed, for the next minute, any deception or suggestions you make towards that creature are suffused with fey magic, and that creature remembers the conversation in a way that favors your intent, even creating temporary artificial memories that support your statements. Any contradictory evidence to oppose your deception is disregarded and they will rationalize any memories or statements from friends as illogical or even possible attempts to deceive them. When presented with facts contradicting your deception, the target can repeat the Wisdom (Insight) check, ending the beguiling effects on a success. This benefit lasts for 10 minutes or until you successfully use this feature against a different creature. The effects of your magic linger on the target for up to 1 hour after you’ve successfully used this feature, or until they have a Dispel Magic or Remove Curse cast upon them. If the target remained beguiled for the full duration, the affected memories and altered perceptions become permanent.

Wondrous Item, uncommon(+1), rare(+2), very rare(+3) Attunement Requires Attunement by a fighter Description This finely detailed band can be a ring, bracelet, necklace or anklet. While wearing it, you gain a bonus to the saving throw DCs of your fighter features. The bonus is determined by the band's rarity. In addition, when you use your Second Wind feature, you can regain additional hit points equal to 1d10 + half your fighter level. You can't use this feature again until the next dawn.

Wondrous Item, uncommon(+1), rare(+2), very rare(+3) Attunement Requires Attunement by a fighter Description This finely detailed band can be a ring, bracelet, necklace or anklet. While wearing it, you gain a bonus to the saving throw DCs of your fighter features. The bonus is determined by the band's rarity. In addition, when you use your Second Wind feature, you can regain additional hit points equal to 1d10 + half your fighter level. You can't use this feature again until the next dawn.

Wondrous item, uncommon (requires use by a warforged) A final messenger is a tiny homunculus—a delicate winged creature designed to facilitate communication between warforged soldiers during the Last War.If you are a warforged, you can use an action to hold a final messenger and integrate it into your body. While it is part of your body, the messenger cannot be targeted by any attack. You can only have one messenger attached to your body at a time. A final messenger holds four pieces of data, accessible only to the warforged it is attached to: A destination for the messenger. This can be very specific (a particular apartment in Sharn) or more general (an open marketplace). A target individual. This could be a specific person or a category (“Any Karrnathi warforged”). A single image recorded through the eyes of a warforged attached to the messenger. A message of up to 25 words. While the messenger is attached to you, you can use an action to review the data currently stored within the final messenger, and if you choose, to change any or all of these data points. You can release the final messenger as a bonus action, at which point it flies to its destination by the most direct route possible. Once it reaches the destination it seeks the target individual; if no target has been set, it approaches the nearest warforged. If you are reduced to 0 hit points while a final messenger is attached to you, it immediately detaches and seek out its target. It retains its stored message, but replaces its stored image with the last thing you saw before dropping to zero hit points. A final messenger is a Tiny construct with an AC of 20, 6 hit points, and a flying speed of 60 feet. It is immune to poison damage, psychic damage, and all conditions other than unconsciousness. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, treat all its ability scores as 10 (+0). It has darkvision with a range of 60 feet. It has no limbs and the only action it can take on its turn is the Dash action. A messenger can only remain active for 8 hours after it detaches from a warforged body, after which time its energy dissipates and it falls unconscious. An unconscious messenger must complete a short or long rest attached to a warforged, after which it regains its energy, as well as regaining all lost hit points.

Ammunition (Firearms), uncommon Description A selection of various flammable substances combined with a hint of evocation magic allows this specialty ammunition to turn any firearm into a different style of weapon. Weapons loaded with a flame cartridge deal fire damage instead of the damage type it would normally deal. Additionally, when you attack with this weapon, instead of making an attack roll, the target must succeed a dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + the weapon's attack bonus) or take the weapon's damage, or half as much on a successful save. Effects that require you to hit a target instead require them to fail their saving throw.

Weapon (scrapshot), very rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description This heavy incendiary weapon functions by superheating the metal scraps typically used as ammunition by a scrapshot, resulting in a spread of molten slag being launched at its targets. This magical weapon has a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls, and deals fire damage instead of slashing. Targets hit by the weapon are coated in molten metal until they, or a creature within 5 ft of them, use an action to scrape it off of them. A creature or object coated in this molten metal takes 1d10 fire damage at the start of each of its turns. The molten metal effect can stack up to three times. Additionally, creatures reduced to 0 hitpoints by damage from this weapon are reduced to ash.

Wondrous Item, varies Attunement Requires Attunement Description These magical gloves allow you to throw objects at astounding speeds. When you make a ranged weapon attack using a non-magical thrown weapon, the weapon gains a bonus to attack and damage rolls and is considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage. The bonus depends on this item’s rarity. Additionally, if you attack with a thrown weapon with advantage, you deal one additional weapon damage die in addition to the weapon’s normal damage. +1 : Uncommon +2 : Rare +3 : Very Rare

Very Rare, Wondrous Item Description A crystal for focusing magical energies for use in weapons. Such crystals can be inserted into weapons with the [Battery X] property, and will continue to supply them power until destroyed. It takes an action to insert or remove a Focusing Crystal from a weapon.

In the clandestine world of rogues, a select few find themselves touched by the enigmatic forces of fate. These shadowy figures, known as Fortune’s Shadows, navigate the perilous dance of danger with a unique connection to the threads that weave destiny. Embracing Fortune’s Shadow means walking a razor’s edge, where every calculated risk and precise strike is a step further into the weave of destiny. Those who witness a Fortune’s Shadow in action may question whether their abilities are a result of skill, luck, or a mysterious force guiding their every move. One thing is certain – in the world of shadows and secrets, the Fortune’s Shadow is a rogue unlike any other, their fate entwined with the very essence of chance.

At 3rd level, upon dealing sneak attack damage with an even number, you gain a Fate Point. As a bonus action, you can expend a Fate Point to make a daring gambit. Roll a d6 to determine the effect of the Gambit. d6 : Gambit : Effect: Fleeting Shadows: You become invisible until the start of your next turn, you lose invisibility whenever you attack, or force a saving throw. Lucky Strike: Your next attack gains advantage. Evasive Maneuver: The next attack against you must be made with disadvantage. Weave of Fate: You gain temporary hit points equal to your rogue level. Deft Diversion: You can move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Fortune's Grace: Add your proficiency bonus to your AC until the start of your next turn. When rolling initiative your Fate Points reset to 0. You can a flip a coin, on a head to you gain a Fate point.

At level 9 when you are reduced to 0 hit points and not killed outright, you can expend a Fate Point to cheat death. Instead of falling unconscious, you remain conscious with 1 hit point, and can immediately use a reaction to move up to your speed, without provoking opportunity attacks. Additionally, you gain advantage on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws for 1 minute, representing the temporary escape from fate’s grasp. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

At 13th level your Gambit's are improved. when you roll for a Gambit, you instead use the Greater gambit table: d6 : Gambit : Effect: Persistent Shadows: You become invisible until the end of your next turn. Foretold Strikes: You gain advantage on attacks until the end of your next turn. Evasive Expert: You impose disadvantage on all attacks against you until the start of your next turn.. Architect of Fate: You gain temporary hit points and regain hit point equal to your rogue level Perfect Diversion: You can move up to your speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Fortune's Gift: Add your proficiency bonus to your AC until the start of your next turn. Reduce damage taken from attacks by the same amount. When rolling initiative you can now flip 2 coins, gaining a Fate point for each coin that lands on a head.

At level 17, when you use your uncanny dodge feature to halve damage received, you can spend a Fate Point to roll a d6. On an even result, the attacker takes force damage equal to the damage you received. On an odd result, you don't take any damage from the attack.

Weapon (glaive), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement by a creature with a Strength score of 15 or higher Description This magic glaive has tattered remains of a banner from the base of its blade and coiled around its shaft. The color and symbol have long faded and forgotten but whose task still persists. This weapon feels heavier than it looks to the wielder. Some say the banner appears at moments when the glaive is swung, showing the vibrant colors it once had. You have a +2 bonus to attack rolls made with this weapon. You also gain the following abilities. Strength in Numbers. You gain an additional +1 bonus to attack rolls for each friendly creature within 20 feet of you up to a maximum of +3(total bonus of +5). You also give a +1 bonus to attack rolls to friendly creatures within range. Assisted Assault. While you have at least one friendly creature within 30 feet of you, you deal an extra 3d4 of the weapon's damage on hit. Alternatively, you can forgo the extra damage at the start of your turn to give one friendly creature an extra 3d4 weapon damage on one attack they make on their next turn.

Wondrous item (torch), very rare Attunement Requires Attunement by a creature with resistance or immunity to cold damage Description The torch, whose wood carry no magical properties, brings an icy blue flame that defied the very essence of warmth but still possess its comfort and reliability. This torch provides bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet much like normal torches except this is unimpeded by effects caused by cold environments and instead overcomes them (i.e., instead of being subjected to a heavily obscuring blizzard, you and those around you are able to see with ease within this torch's light). Creatures within its light's range are free from the effects of extreme heat. If you make a melee attack with this lit torch and hit, it deals 1 cold damage. If the flames are in contact to a body of water, it will slowly freeze the water within its light's range. You can freely decrease the size of the flame and the light it makes to an inch in diameter and revert it back, but it cannot be completely snuffed out. You can transfer it to another torch and leave the previous holder as a mundane torch. If this torch is held by a creature that does not have resistance or immunity to cold damage, they will take 1 cold damage every minute until they drop this torch. The blue flame has 6 charges. While holding the torch, you can use an action to expend 1 charge to blow on the fires to cast the cone of cold spell (save DC 17; you can choose whether each creature makes a Constitution or Dexterity saving throw) from it. Each expended charge makes the flames smaller and smaller. If you expend the last charge, the flames and light it produces will only be 1 inch in diameter and will stay in that size. The blue flame regains 1 charge daily at dawn, as well as increase in size bit by bit.

Weapon (any weapon), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description Choose a magical bonus of +1 to +3. This weapon gains that bonus to its attack and damage rolls. For each point of bonus you choose for the weapon, you take a corresponding penalty (−1 to −3) to your death saving throws. You can change this magical bonus each day at dawn. Curse. This weapon is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. Until the curse is broken with a remove curse spell or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the weapon.

Weapon (any weapon), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description Choose a magical bonus of +1 to +3. This weapon gains that bonus to its attack and damage rolls. For each point of bonus you choose for the weapon, you take a corresponding penalty (−1 to −3) to your death saving throws. You can change this magical bonus each day at dawn. Curse. This weapon is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. Until the curse is broken with a remove curse spell or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the weapon.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Attunement Requires Attunement Description While wearing these gauntlets, you have proficiency with the musket and pistol, and you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls on ranged attacks made with such weapons.

Prerequisite Aasimar Description You manifested some of the powers from the Upper Planes, granting you the following benefits: Your Healing Hands and transformation traits can now use either an action or bonus action to activate and can be used again after finishing a short or long rest. Each of your transformations also gain additional effects: Necrotic Shroud. The range of the effect increases to 30 feet, and you gain advantage on attack rolls against creatures frightened by this trait. Radiant Consumption. The radius of both bright and dim light increases to 30 feet. Hostile creatures can't benefit from being hidden while within the light. If you are within magical darkness, the light would only remain on your body and won't be shed but you are able to see through that darkness instead. Creatures within or outside the magical darkness would be able to see you. Radiant Soul. You can hover. When the transformation ends while you are not on the ground, your rate of decent slows to 60 feet per round until you land. Upon landing, you take no falling damage and can land on your feet.

1st-level transmutation. (Cryomancy Magic) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60 feet Components: V, S, M (a piece of pure ice) Duration: Instantaneous Description You form a large ice shard from the moisture of your surroundings to launch at a target that you can see within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. If the attack hits, the target takes 2d6 cold damage and the shard shatters into pieces that embed into the target until the start of your next turn. If the target takes an action or bonus action before then, the target takes 1d4 cold damage. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 to the target, and the damage the target takes for doing an action or bonus action increase by 1d4 for each slot level above 1st.

Weapon (quarterstaff), rare Description As a reaction or an object interaction, this quarterstaff can be converted into a glider, or from a glider back into the quarterstaff. It can't be used as a weapon while in glider mode. As a bonus action you can will the glider to activate. For 1 hour you have a flying speed of 45 feet, but you can't use this speed to gain altitude, and while using this speed you lose 5 feet of altitude plus any unused lateral movement at the end of each turns. (For example if you fly 30 feet on a turn, you will fall 20 feet at the end of the turn. You can land safely this way.)

5th-level divination. (rtificer, Bard, Cleric, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 minute Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a focus worth at least 1,000 gp, such as a crystal ball, a silver mirror, or a font filled with holy water) Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Description You can choose a small or smaller object that is familiar to you that isn’t being worn or carried and is on the same plane of existence as you. The spell creates an invisible sensor within 10 feet of the object’s location for the duration. You mentally receive visual information from the sensor, which has normal vision and darkvision out to 30 feet. The sensor allows you to look in every direction. The sensor moves with the object, remaining within 10 feet of it for the duration. A creature that can see invisible objects sees the sensor as a luminous orb about the size of your fist. At any time while concentrating on the spell, you can use an action to ping the object’s location. If the object is on the same plane as you, you learn the object’s general direction (but not its distance or any other information).

Wondrous Item, rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description These gloves have 3 charges. While wearing them, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast the spell Spirit Shroud from it. For 1 charge, you cast the 3rd-level version of the spell. You can increase the spell slot level by one for each additional charge you expend. The gloves regain all expended charges daily at dawn.

Wondrous Item (consumable), rare 3 lbs. Description This kit is made from a combination of rare herbs and magical compounds, providing potent healing properties. Special bandages infused with healing magic, designed to accelerate the natural healing process. Healing Salve: This kit contains five salve charges and as an action, one charge of the salve can be applied to the wounds of a creature, The creature restores 2d6 + 4 hit points. Healing Bandages: This kit contains 3 bandage charges and as an action, one charge of the bandages can be applied to the wounds of a creature, The creature restores 1d8 + 2 hit points and stabilizes them.

Prerequisite: Ritual Caster feat (2014 or 2024); Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score of 18 or higher Your mastery of ritual magic reaches new heights. You gain the following benefits: • Ability Score Increase. Increase the same ability score you chose for the Ritual Caster feat (Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma) by 1, to a maximum of 20. • Quick Ritual. Once more per long rest, you can cast a ritual spell at its normal casting time instead of adding 10 minutes. • Expanded Ritual Repertoire. You can learn one additional ritual spell of each level equal to or lower than your spellcasting ability modifier(maximum 5). • Growth of Knowledge. For each level you gain, you may replace one ritual spell of that level with another once on a level up, or when you PERMANENTLY increase your casting modifier.

Armor (shield), very rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description This shield is adorned with angelic wings and a crystal at the center which glows with a calming blue hue. While holding this shield, you have a +1 bonus to AC and resistance to necrotic damage. When you die as a result of failing all your death saving throws or when you are subjected to an effect which causes you to instantly die, you instead fall into a stasis until the start of your next turn. During this stasis, you are incapacitated while remain conscious of your surroundings, you are immune to all damage and cannot be affected by any other effect or condition. If you are under other effects or conditions when you fall into stasis, all of these instantly end. At the start of your next turn, your current hit point total resets to 20 hit points and you gain advantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw you make. Once you have used this feature, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Weapon (lance), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Attacking a target within 5 feet of you with this weapon doesn't impose disadvantage on the attack roll. If you are attuned to Guild Palace Shield, you gain access to the following additional properties: The bonus to attack and damage rolls instead becomes +3. You can wield this weapon with one hand, instead of two, while also holding the shield. When you attack with this weapon, you deal an additional 1d12 force damage. If you roll a 20 on the attack roll, it rolls damage dice three times, instead of twice. You can cast the Raulothim's Psychic Lance spell (save DC 17). Once you cast the spell this way, you regain the ability to use it again at dawn.

Armor (shield), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description While holding this shield, you have a +2 bonus to AC. This bonus is in addition to the shield's normal bonus to AC. If you are attuned to Guild Palace Lance, you gain access to the following additional properties: Your attack rolls using the Guild Palace Lance have advantage against targets that is 10 feet away from you. The bonus to AC instead becomes +3. The first time an attacker misses you with a melee attack in a turn, they take 1d8 force damage. You can cast the Globe of Invulnerability spell. Once you cast the spell this way, you regain the ability to use it again at dawn.

Hammer of the Ram Weapon (Maul), Rare Attunement Requires attunement. Description This all-silver hammer carries a mighty force behind it with every swing. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. If the hammer hits an object that isn’t being worn or carried, the hit is a critical hit. The hammer has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target with the hammer, you can expend 1 to 3 of its charges to force the target to make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. For each charge expended, the target takes an extra 1d10 force damage and is pushed 5 feet away from you on a failed save. On a successful save, the target takes half as much force damage and isn’t pushed. 𝙍𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙤𝙛 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙍𝙖𝙢. If you’re also attuned to the “ring of the ram,” your bonus to attack and damage rolls with the hammer increases to +2, and the hammer’s every swing creates a projection of the spectral ram from the ring. The ram lurches forward from the head of the hammer, effectively increasing your reach with the weapon by an additional 5 feet. In addition, the hammer and ring share a pool of charges: any charge you have with the ring can be used for the hammer’s properties, and vice versa.

Weapon (Longbow or Shortbow), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description This bow has 6 charges and regains 1d4+2 charges at dawn. When you use your action to fire this bow, you can expend a number of charges to shoot one of the arrows at an ally within normal range. This arrow deals no damage, but restores 1d6 HP to the target for each charge expended. Alternatively, once per turn, you may instead use one of your attacks to fire a single arrow at an ally within the normal range of the bow. When you do so, you Cast a Spell you have prepared that restores HP to a single target other than the caster, does not deal damage, and has a casting time of 1 action. The arrow deals no damage, but the effects of the spell are applied to the target. Casting a spell in this way does not require a free hand. If the spell requires a spell slot, the slot is expended as usual.

Weapon (longbow), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement by a Non-Evil Alignment Description A Heartseeker bow is a beautifully crafted elven longbow +3 made of polished wood. The elven craftsmen made the bow so strong even stone cannot scratch the marvelous wood, and the deep finish of its polish can be returned by a single brush of the hand. You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, in addition to the following abilities. Lightning Arrow. A Heartseeker Imbues the arrows it shoots with lightning. Add an additional 1d8 of lighting damage Heartseeking. A Heartseeker aids the archer in finding the most vulnerable parts of their targets. A critical hit is achieved on a roll of 19 or 20. Elven Craftsmanship. Due to the strength of the fine wood used in the crafting of a Heartseeker, it can be used as a quarterstaff dealing 1d6 damage.

In The Wandering Realms, we allow homebrew. Homebrew get approved in the server on a dual voting system. Any Player can submit homebrew in the #homebrew-ua-submissions Channel. Each homebrew submission follows the same method: A Player Creates a Post in the #homebrew-ua-submissions channel. They Ping @homebrewer in the post. And react on the post with a 1, 2 and 3. Players then vote on the submission by reacting. Yes No Abstain Once the Submission reaches 10 Yes votes, the submission is moved to homebrew-ua-approver-votes where a team of staff members will either approve or deny the homebrew Some Rules: A Player is allowed one submission per week. Unless their submission get's approved by staff, in which case they can submit another. #homebrew-ua-submissions is reserved for submissions only. Players can discuss or query active homebrew in #homebrew-ua-discussion. In-Character Homebrew Creations: When submitting Homebrew, a player can declare an item to be invented, or otherwise created by one or multiple characters. The creation or access to that Homebrew is then restricted to those with the same in-character access to it. In The Wandering Realms, we allow homebrew. Homebrew get approved in the server on a dual voting system. Any Player can submit homebrew in the #homebrew-ua-submissions Channel. Each homebrew submission follows the same method: A Player Creates a Post in the #homebrew-ua-submissions channel. They Ping @homebrewer in the post. And react on the post with a 1 and 2. Players then vote on the submission by reacting. Yes No Once the Submission reaches 10 Yes votes, the submission is moved to homebrew-ua-approver-votes where a team of staff members will either approve or deny the homebrew, if after a month a submission doesn't reach 10 votes, it gets denied. Some Rules: A Player is allowed one submission per week. Unless their submission get's approved by staff, in which case they can submit another. #homebrew-ua-submissions is reserved for submissions only. Players can discuss or query active homebrew in #homebrew-ua-discussion. Evocation cantrip. (Artificer, Ranger, Sorcerer, Warlock) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 20 feet Components: S, M (a ranged weapon worth at least 1 sp) Duration: Instantaneous Description You brandish the weapon used in the spell’s casting and make a ranged attack with it against one creature within 20 feet of you. On a hit, your walking speed increases by 5 ft until the end of your turn. This spell’s damage and speed bonus increases when you reach certain levels. At 5th level, the ranged attack deals an extra 1d6 fire damage and your speed increases by 10 feet instead of 5 feet. The damage roll and speed bonus increases by 1d6 and 5 feet at 11th level (2d6 and 15 feet) and 17th level (3d6 and 20 feet).

Weapon (Blunderbuss), rare Description This modified blunderbuss instead condenses all of its ammunition into a single clump, which detonates on impact. This weapon deals bludgeoning damage instead of piercing damage. When you hit a target with this weapon, it and every other creature within 5 ft of the target must succeed a DC15 dexterity saving throw, taking 2d6 slashing damage on a failed save.

Wondrous Item, Very Rare Description Made as a replacement for a faulty heart, this metallic organ was created to help terminally ill patients become well again. To use this item, you need to undergo an hour-long ritual in which the heart merges into your chest, permanently replacing your original heart. As well as being able to function as a normal heart, this magic item grants you advantage on any saving throws or checks made to resist or end blood-borne diseases and injury poisons.

Weapon (martial), 1d6 slashing or 1d4 bludgeoning, 50gp, 4 lbs. Finesse, Reach, Two-Handed, Special Description Special: You can choose to attack with either the kama (sickle) or the weighted chain on your turn. You may then make an attack with the other weapon as a bonus action. In addition, this weapon may be a monk weapon despite its properties. Kama (Sickle): The sickle deals 1d6 slashing damage. The range of this is 5ft. Weighted Chain (Kusari): The chain deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage. The range of the chain is 10ft.

Weapon (Pistol), Very Rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description This pistol feeds off of its users vitality, but can provide great assistance in their hour of need. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this magic weapon. Every time you attack with this weapon, you take 2 necrotic damage that cannot be reduced in any way. Additionally while you are below 25 hit points, all targets are vulnerable to the piercing damage dealt by this weapon. If you are reduced to 0 hit points or die from causes other than this weapon's self damage, you are revived with 1 hit point at the start of your next turn. During this turn, the weapon does not require your hit points to attack, but you die at the end of your turn. Once the weapon has revived you, it cannot do so again until the next dawn.

Weapon (longsword), uncommon Description This item appears to be a longsword hilt. While grasping the hilt, you can use a bonus action to cause a blade of pure radiance to spring into existence, or make the blade disappear. While the blade exists, this magic longsword has the finesse property. If you are proficient with short-swords or longswords, you are proficient with the lesser sun blade. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon, which deals radiant damage instead of slashing damage. When you hit an undead with it, that target takes an extra 1d4 radiant damage. The sword's luminous blade emits bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet. The light is sunlight. While the blade persists, you can use an action to expand or reduce its radius of bright and dim light by 5 feet each, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 5 feet each.

Wondrous Item, Uncommon Description While holding the lesser thought gem, you can use an action to store a single thought strand created by the encode thoughts cantrip. The thought strand remains present for seven days before it decays, vanishing from the gem. You can use an action to touch the gem's surface and retrieve a thought strand within it, though it maintains its original duration as well as the decay time from being stored. Only one thought strand can be stored in a lesser thought gem at a time.

Your powers are drawn from the spark of light kindled within you. In places of great darkness, there are those born with an affinity for light, and every shadow has a source. The magic within you represents cosmic balance, flickering from radiance to darkness moment to moment. Features: 1st Level - Trick of the Light 1st Level - Flickering Aura 6th Level - Refraction Shield 14th Level - Aura Magnification 18th Level - Light Weaver

Starting at 1st level, you have darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, it increases its range by 60 feet. You learn the Light and Sacred Flame cantrips. At 3rd-level you learn the Darkness and Faerie Fire spells, which are sorcerer spells and do not count against your spells known. They can cast normally, or by expending 2 sorcery points.

Starting at 1st level, you can magnify the properties of light around you. At the end of a short or long rest, you can choose whether your magic is light-shifted or dark-shifted. While light-shifted you can use an action to emit an aura in a 15-foot radius around you. This area is bright light. While the aura persist, you can use a bonus action to expand or reduce its radius by 5 feet, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet. While dark-shifted you gain the same ability, but you project an aura of nonmagical darkness. This effect lasts for 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated. Once used, you cannot use this ability again until you finish a short or long rest

At 6th level, you can manipulate the light around you for protection. As a bonus action, you can spend 2 sorcery points to magically create a shield of light or dark. The shield lasts for 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated. While this shield is in place, whenever a creature within 10 feet of you hits you with an attack, this shield flashes with searing energy, and the attacker takes 2d6 radiant damage if you are light-shifted or 2d6 necrotic damage if you are dark-shifted.

While your Flickering Aura is active, you can now expand it up to 10 feet as a bonus action, up to a maximum of 60 feet. While within the aura, a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier also gain the benefit of your Refraction Shield, but no more than once per turn. Additionally, you and those creatures have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) skill checks made while light-shifted, or Dexterity (Stealth) checks made while dark-shifted. You can add your proficiency bonus when making these skill checks by expending a sorcery point.

Embodying both aspects of Light and Dark, you gain resistance to both radiant and necrotic damage. Additionally, as part of the action to activate your Flickering Aura, you can transform yourself and gain the following benefits for up to 1 minute: Upon activation or as part of the bonus action to expand or reduce it's radius, you can switch to either light-shifted or dark-shifted. Each creature of your choice within your aura must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 radiant and 2d8 necrotic damage and becoming blinded till the end of their next turn on a failure, or half as much damage and not being blinded in a success. While your Radiant Shield is active, the radius of its effect increases to 30 feet, and you deal both the radiant and the necrotic damage when hit with an attack. Once you use this action, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 5 sorcery points to use it again.

Weapon: Martial, Melee 10gp, 4 lbs. --- 1d8 Bludgeoning - Reach, Two-handed, Special Description Proficiency with a Long Bo-Staff allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special: Counts as a Monk weapon (For martial arts), as well as monks would be proficiency This weapon has the following weapon mastery: Push: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or Smaller

Martial Melee Weapon - 20 gp, 6 lbs - 1d10 bludgeoning - Two-handed, Heavy, Reach, **Topple** A pole hammer designed for armored combat, or cracking the thick hides of monsters. Counts as both a hammer and a polearm.

Armor (Heavy), Non-Lootable Description Armor infused with the essence of stars. A suit of luminite armor holds with it the power to boost it's wearers abilities across a spectrum of focuses. When luminite armor is made, it can come in one of the following forms, which determines it's properties: Solar - While wearing this magical armor, you have a +3 bonus to your armor class, and resistance to fire damage. Your melee weapon attacks deal an additional 1d8 fire damage, and have a +1 bonus to hit. The armor has three charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you can expend one charge as a reaction to halve the damage, and cause the attacking creature to take fire damage equal to the reduction. Vortex - While wearing this magical armor, you have a +2 bonus to your armor class, and resistance to lightning damage. Your ranged weapon attacks deal an additional 1d6 lightning damage, and have a +2 bonus to hit. The armor has three charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. As a bonus action, you can expend one charge to become invisible until you move. Attacking does not break your invisibility. Nebula - While wearing this magical armor, you are considered to be proficienct with it even if you lack proficiency with heavy armor, and you are resistant to psychic damage. Your spell attacks have a +3 bonus to hit. The armor has three charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. As an action, you can expend one charge to gain one of the following effects for one minute: Regeneration - you regain 5 hit points at the start of each of your turns. Power - each of your spells gains a 2d8 bonus to one damage roll. Mana - When you cast a spell of 3rd level or lower, roll a d6. If the result is greater than the level of the spell, you do not expend a spell slot. Stardust - While wearing this magical armor, you are considered to be proficient with it even if you lack proficiency with heavy armor, and you are resistant to cold damage. Creatures you summon through class features or spells gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls. The armor has three charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. When you summon a creature throigh a class feature or spell, you can expend one charge to summon one additional creature. This creature lasts only half as long, or for one hour in the case of indefinite durations.

Prerequisite: Mage Slayer Description Guarded Mind: If you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you can cause yourself to succeed instead. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest, but you can only regain uses of this ability up to twice per day through short rests. Spellbreaker: When you hit a creature with an attack as part of your reaction granted by the *Mage Slayer* feat, and that creature is casting a spell, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw as if the creature were concentrating on a spell. On a failed save, the spell is interrupted, and the spell slot and action used to cast it are wasted. If the target is concentrating on a spell, they make their concentration save immediately after their Constitution save for this ability. You may use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all uses upon completing a short or long rest.

Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual) Range: 30 feet Components: V, S, M (a pinch of iron and cobalt powder worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Until Dispelled You implant a small repeatable magical mechanical force within a tiny object within range. When you do so, choose two rotational states relative to it's current rotation for the item to switch between. When the spell causes the item to switch between the two rotational states, it does so with the least required movement and can be designated to take anywhere from 1 second to 10 minutes. Finally, determine the circumstance that will trigger the spell to rotate the object. When the circumstance occurs, the object rotates to the next or previous state (the second state when triggered for the first time). If an outside force or object would prevent the object from rotating, it stops harmlessly and that particular trigger is ignored. When you cast this spell, you can have the spell end after it returns to its original position, or it can remain and repeat its rotation whenever the trigger occurs. The triggering circumstance can be as general or as detailed as you like, though it must be based on visual or audible conditions that occur within 30 feet of the object. For example, you could instruct a lock to automatically reset its rotation when the door is closed.

4th-level evocation. (Bard, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard, Battle Smith) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self Components: S Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description You charge a free hand with crackling magical energy. When you cast this spell, and as a bonus action on subsequent turns, you can point at a creature you can see within 60 feet of you and release a bolt, provided the spell hasn't ended. The target must make a constitution saving throw or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn. When you successfully incapacitate a target with this spell, you can instantly teleport to an empty space of your choice within 5 feet of it, and your melee weapon attacks against the incapacitated creature deal an additional 1d6 lightning damage. The spell ends early if a target succeeds on its saving throw, or if you use your bonus action to do anything else. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the additional lightning damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 4th.

Marshwarden Bow Weapon (any bow), Rare Attunement Requires attunement. Description This bow is made of twisted cypress roots and covered in long, stringy moss. The bowstring is always slick with water. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon and nonmagical arrows fired from this bow deal an extra 1d6 acid or poison damage on a hit (your choice each time). When you’re in a forest or swamp and are hidden from a creature, missing with an attack against it doesn’t reveal your position. Wretched Burst. When you hit a target with an arrow fired from this bow, you can cause it to erupt in a putrid cloud centered on the target, duplicating the effect of the “Stinking Cloud” spell (save DC 15). This version of the spell doesn’t require concentration. Once this property of the bow has been used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn or until it’s spent at least 1 hour submerged in naturally occurring swamp water.

Wondrous item, uncommon Description This quill-like tool has a narrow brush that extends from its end, which produces its own ink. You can use this marker in place of ink and a quill as calligrapher's supplies. While holding it, you can use a bonus action to mentally change the color of the ink that flows from the brush. Decorating the marker's metal casing is a dazzling spectrum of colors, which move and shimmer while the marker is being used. The brush can be retracted into the metal casing to keep it from leaving errant marks by clicking a button at the top of the marker. While holding the marker, you can use a bonus action to triple-click its button. For the next minute, the marker magically erases any of its own-generated ink it's brushed across without a trace, instead of leaving ink behind. This effect ends early if you use a bonus action to triple-click the button again. For the duration, you can erase up to 1 square foot of the marker's ink, containing no more than 150 characters or 25 words. Once this property of the pen has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Legendary, Wondrous Attunement Requires Attunement Description These masks are made of dark tempered steel usually found within the infernal courts, used to mark those who bear them with a respect and leadership, and the capabilities for subterfuge that would befit a king. While attuned to this mask, you gain the following benefits: Your Charisma Score becomes 20, unless it is already 20 or higher. When you see a creature, and analyze them for 1 minute or more, as an action, you may turn yourself into a perfect illusionary representation of it, mimicking both its appearance and its voice for as long as you maintain concentration. (For clarification, this illusion can be dispelled by dispel magic, amf, and can be seen through with truesight) You have advantage on charisma checks

Wondrous Item, varies Attunement Requires Attunement Description These dark ceramic and gold masks are fashioned after animals that are sacred in certain cultures. Each mask's appearance and properties are based on the sacred beast it represents. While attuned to a mask, you can end your attunement to it and attune to a different one over the course of 1 minute, instead of over the course of one or more short rests. Crocodile (Common). While wearing a crocodile mask, you gain a swimming speed of 30 feet and can hold your breath for up to 10 minutes at a time. Lion (Uncommon). While wearing a lion mask, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell. In addition, your nails extend into claws, turning your unarmed strikes with your hands into magic weapons that deal slashing damage with a damage die of 1d6. Hawk (Rare). While wearing a hawk mask, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, and attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls. In addition, you can cast the feather fall spell at will, targeting only yourself. Mule (Very Rare). While wearing a mule mask, your Strength score increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, you count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift, and you have advantage on Strength and Dexterity ability checks and saving throws against being knocked prone. In addition, when you hit a Large or smaller creature with a melee weapon attack, you can use a bonus action to force that creature to make a DC 16 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice). On a failed save, the creature is knocked prone. Jackal (Legendary). While wearing a jackal mask, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and immunity to necrotic damage. In addition, you can use an action to fire a beam of deathly green magic from your forehead at a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The creature must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 7d8 + 30 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once this property of the mask has been used, it can't be used again until the next dusk. A humanoid killed by this necrotic damage rises at the start of your next turn as a mummy under your control. The mummy acts on its own initiative count. On your turn, you can mentally command the mummy if it is within 120 feet of you and you aren't incapacitated (no action required). You decide what action the mummy takes and where it moves during its next turn, or you can issue it a general command, such as to attack your enemies or guard a location. The mummy remains until you dismiss it as a bonus action, until it's reduced to 0 hit points, or until you are no longer attuned to any mask of the sacred beast, causing it to turn to dust. You can only create and control one mummy at a time in this way.

Wondrous Item, Common A blank, porcelain masquerade mask, it covers the full face and sports a pair of holes for eyes and a slit for the mouth. While it is being worn on the face, the wearer may choose to have the appearance of the mask change (no action required). It can change to any design, but must be of a style typical for a masquerade.

Weapon (maul), legendary Attunement requires attunement by a Barbarian Description You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Seething with unbridled rage and untamable anger this weapon was made to force enemies to their breaking point. This magic weapon reacts to the rage pouring out of barbarians and uses their anger to their advantage. While raging this weapon deals an additional 3d6 force damage when you hit an enemy. Bloodlust: Once per attack action, if you score a critical hit, you may make one additional attack as part of that same action.

Megaton Hammer Weapon (Maul), legendary Attunement requires attunement by a creature with Strength 17 or higher Description The Megaton Hammer is a maul of extraordinary size, shape and weight. This maul is so heavy, in fact, few can lift it off the ground and fewer still can wield it in battle. The haft of this weapon is made of a sturdy wood, reinforced by adamantium, and attached to the end of this haft is a hammer head of unusual build. One side of the head is a spiked head whilst the other side is a one-foot diameter cylinder of pure metal with rivets and inscribed runes circling the side of the head. Between these two heads lies a single, fat, rounded spike that caps the end of the haft. The Megaton Hammer has a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls and knocks back Large or smaller creatures 1d4 spaces (5-20 feet) on hit. The wielder can call upon the power held within the Megaton Hammer and strike the ground in front of them causing a fiery tremor within a 40-ft cone in front of them. Creatures caught in this cone must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw to take half of the 3d6 bludgeoning damage and 3d6 fire damage, and to avoid being knocked prone if they are a Large or smaller creature. This ability, rightfully called Earth-Shattering Strike, can not be used again until after you finish a long rest.

1st-level illusion. (Bard, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 10 minutes (ritual) Range: Touch Components: S, M (enchanted ink worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Special Description You imbue a piece of parchment, paper, or some other suitable writing material with illusory writing that lasts for the duration. This writing is not suitable for scribing a spell scroll or filling a spellbook. When you cast this spell, the page is instantly filled with text of your choosing. Choose a duration between 1 minute and 1 year. After this amount of time has elapsed, the magic fades and the writing vanishes. Any time before the spell ends, you, and any creatures you designate when you cast the spell, can cast it again to extend the duration, up to a maximum of 1 year. Extending the duration in this way does not require the material component.

Weapon: Martial, Ranged 3000gp, 20 lbs. --- 3d10 piercing - ammunition, special, range (120/480), two-handed Requires a Strength score of 21 or higher and have a carrying capacity of a Huge or larger creature to be able to wield this weapon Description When making an attack with this weapon, you use your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. The arrows used by this weapon costs 1000 gp (Items that create ammunition still require 1000 gp, gold is magically disappeared from your characters pouch, magic knows all).

Weapon: Martial, Ranged 300gp, 6 lbs. --- 2d6 piercing - ammunition, special, range (150/600), two-handed Requires a Strength score of 18 or higher and be Medium or larger to be able to wield this weapon Description When making an attack with this weapon, you use your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

Wondrous Item, rare Description This single lens has three filters that you can peer through. You can change the monocle's filter by rotating the lens' outer ring. A small arrow along the edge of the frame indicates the monocle's selected filter. The monocle has 4 charges and regains 1d3+1 each day at dawn. As an action, you can expend a charge to look through and activate one of the filters to gain one of several benefits: Filter of Comprehend Languages. When you peer through this filter, you can read and comprehend any written language as per the written language portion of the comprehend languages spell. Filter of Darkvision. While looking through this filter, you have darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. Filter of See Invisibility. When gazing through this filter, you see invisible creatures and objects as if they were visible. You gain the benefits of the activated filter while you wear the monocle for 1 hour or until you change the filter.

Armor (any armor), very rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description Armor of this variety is crafted from the very creatures it was designed to hunt, Dragons, Monstrosities, Undead etc. You have a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor. While wearing this armor, you have advantage on attacks against all creatures this armor was made to hunt, skill checks to track this creature. Can be made of any creature type except humanoid.

5th-level evocation. (Cleric, Paladin, Sorcerer, Ranger, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a melee weapon worth at least 1 sp) Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Description You imbue a melee weapon you touch with moonlight and enchant your own shadow to hinder your foes. Until the spell ends, the weapon emits bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15. If the weapon isn't already a magic weapon, it becomes one for the duration. When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn, that attack can originate from any space within the lights radius as if you were in that space. You make this choice for each attack, as the moonlight solidifies to attack them. Once during this spell's duration, you may use an action to fill a 30-foot radius circle, centered on the ground underneath you, with a magical shadow that remains there for the spell's duration. If a creature ends it's turn within this area, you may force them to make a strength saving throw. On a failure they are knocked prone and must use all of their speed to stand back up, rather than half.
Level 20 Cycle: You must have completed 20 levels of Warlock (PHB-2024) with no multiclassing.

When you take this prestige class, choose two additional skills from the Warlock skill list. You gain proficiency in both.
Your amount of available pact slots increases per the Morelock Table.
You can now Expend an action, bonus action and all your movement to use Magical cunning.

Your eldritch mastery has grown so strong you can now have 2 different patrons without conflict, You may choose the same warlock patron, or you may choose a new one. At PL 23, PL 26, PL 31 and PL37, you gain more features from your warlock patron.

At PL 24, 28, 32, 36, and 39, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or two ability scores by 1. As normal, you cannot increase a score above 20 (unless another feature allows it). You may select a Feat instead of an ASI.

Your Pact Slots increase in power. All of your available Warlock Pact Slots are now 6th level. You do not learn any new 6th-level spells to cast with these slots; they can only be used to upcast the Warlock spells you know of 5th level or lower, or to cast the specific 6th-level Warlock spells you have already learned through your Mystic Arcanum feature.

Your connection to your patron transcends the boundaries of the planes. When you use your Warlock Contact Patron feature to cast Contact Other Plane, the casting time is reduced to 1 Action, and you do not need to speak aloud to ask your questions. Additionally, once per Long Rest, you can cast the Gate spell without expending a Pact Slot or requiring material components. When cast in this way, the portal can only open to the home domain of your Patron, allowing you to step into their realm.

Choose another level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum. You can cast your 6th level arcanum spell twice without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again. As shown in the Morelock Features table, you gain another Warlock spell of your choice that can be cast in this way when you reach Warlock levels 33 (level 7 spell), 35 (level 8 spell), and 37 (level 9 spell), these can be cast as arcanums twice per long rest. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a Long Rest. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your arcanum spells with another Warlock spell of the same level.

Your soul acts as a massive conduit for your patron's magic. All of your Warlock Pact Slots are now 7th level. As before, you do not learn new 7th-level spells for these slots; they may only be used to upcast your known Warlock spells of 6th level or lower, or to cast the 7th-level Warlock spells you have learned through your Mystic Arcanum feature.

Your mind has expanded to withstand the cosmic weight of your patron's true power, allowing you to fracture your focus without breaking it. You can now concentrate on two Warlock spells simultaneously, provided both spells were cast using your Pact Slots. Wielding this dual magic is a volatile and taxing endeavor. If you take damage while concentrating on two spells and are forced to make a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you must make the roll with Disadvantage. If you fail the saving throw, the magic violently unravels, and you lose Concentration on both spells simultaneously.
