Wondrous Item, rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description: A fine silver chain holds a small crimson gem cut to resemble a heart. The stone feels faintly warm, pulsing with a soft rhythm that never quite matches your own. Properties Heart’s Reserve. When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, the necklace flares with a pulse of red light. You instead drop to 1 hit point, and the gem dims until the next dawn. Empathic Sense. Once per short or long rest, you can focus on the necklace to read the emotions of a creature within 30 feet that you can see. You immediately sense its strongest emotion (such as fear, anger, or calm)

You learn the art of siphoning life from dying enemies and combining it with negetive energy to imbue necromancy into your fighting style. Reavers often kill those who are closest to death, whose spiritual binds are thin enough to cut free and use. Features: 3rd Level - Criticality 9th Level - Rend 13th Level - Ward of Mortality 17th Level - Echo of Reaping

Starting at 3rd level, creatures with less than half of their total hit points gain a Death Mark, granting you the following benefits: You gain an additional way to use your sneak attack; you don’t need advantage on the attack roll to use your Sneak Attack against a marked creature, so long as you don’t have disadvantage on the attack roll. Attack rolls against marked creatures crit on 19-20. You have a bonus on attack rolls against marked creatures. This bonus equals half your proficiency bonus.

Starting at 9th level, you gain the ability to rend those close to death. When you hit a marked creature with your Sneak Attack, you can deal additional damage equal to your rogue level. Once you use this ability, you may not do so against until you complete a short or long rest. If you reduce a creature to zero hit points with this ability, you regain a use.

Starting at 13th level, you learn to collect and conserve the life force you steal from dying opponents, which materializes as a ward. When you hit a marked creature with rend, roll your total sneak attack die. You gain temporary hit points equal to the total, unless you already have more.

Starting at 17th level, you learn to travel to and harness remnants of death. When you hit a creature with rend, you may teleport to a corpse within 90 ft of you as a bonus action, and the next attack you make before the end of your next treats the target as being blood marked. In addition, through a one-minute ritual, you may travel to an area of mass death or a sight where you slew a creature within 2 miles, bringing a number of willing creatures equal to the number of creatures you have killed today (maximum of 10). Once you use this ability, you may not do so again until you complete a long rest.

This philosophical path is dedicated to the total mastery of the body. Shinobi of the Iron Fist view complex Ninjutsu as secondary, focusing instead on internal chakra circulation to achieve unmatched physical speed, durability, and raw striking power. They seek to surpass biological limitations through sheer willpower and rigorous training, defining their power by control over their chosen Master Weapon.

Nindo Jutsu. At certain levels you learn jutsu from your Shinobi Nindo, you always know these Jutsu and they do not count against your total known jutsu. Rank Jutsu Learn Level D Lion Combo 3rd C Shadow of the Dancing Leaf 5th B Leaf Great Whirlwind 8th Fighting Style Options: You must choose a Fighting Style suitable for a close-quarters brawler. Choose one from: Unarmed Fighting Dueling Defense Master Weapon Discipline: You designate one Master Weapon from the following options: Unarmed Strike, Club (Nunchaku), Dagger, Sickle, Shortsword, Scimitar, Kusarigama or Dart. Master Property: You can use the master Property of your Master Weapon. If you choose unarmed strikes as your master weapon, it gains the Push master property. Gate of Opening: You gain access to the first stage of the legendary Eight Gates. As a Bonus Action, you can open the Gate of Opening for 1 minute (opening your gates costs no Chakra). While active, your movement speed increases by 10 feet, and your attacks with your Master Weapon deal an additional 1d4 Force damage. You can open your gates a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest Higher Gates: As you unlock higher Jutsu Ranks, you can open deeper gates whenever you open your gates, gaining each gate’s benefit cumulatively. Second Gate — Healing (C-Rank, 5th level): you have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Third Gate — Life (B-Rank, 8th level): your gate Force damage increases to 1d6. Fourth and Fifth Gates — Pain and Limit (A-Rank, 13th level): your gate speed bonus increases to 20 feet and your gate Force damage increases to 1d8 (4th Gate) or 1d10 (5th Gate). Sixth Gate — Joy (S-Rank, 17th level): your Master Weapon attacks gain an additional 5 feet of reach. When your gates close, you take 1d10 damage for each gate you opened beyond the first; this damage cannot be reduced or prevented.

You master physical movement, making you a highly mobile and resilient skirmisher. Iron Conditioning: You can take the Dash or Disengage action as a Bonus Action on your turn. Weight Drop: Your jumping distances are tripled. Additionally, when you fall, you can use your Reaction to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your Shinobi level.

You have attained such mastery over rapid Taijutsu that your attacks move with explosive speed, allowing you to bypass typical action limits. The Third Punch: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make three attacks instead of two. Explosive Blows: When you hit a creature three times with your Master Weapon in a single turn, the target takes an extra 3d6 Fire damage from the explosive friction created by your speed.

You puncture the cardiac pressure point, unleashing the red vapor of your burning blood to gain power that rivals the gods, at the cost of your own life force. Activation: As a Bonus Action, you can open the Eighth Gate. You enter the Gate of Death Mode for 1 minute, or until you are reduced to 0 Hit Points. While this mode is active, you gain the following benefits: God-Like Speed: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make five attacks instead of two. Pressure Strikes: Your melee weapon attacks gain an additional 10 feet of reach, striking enemies with air pressure alone. Overwhelming Power: On a hit, your melee weapon attacks deal an additional 2d10 Force damage. Unrestrained Chakra: The Chakra cost for all Taijutsu and Bukijutsu you cast is halved (rounded down, minimum of 1). The Cost: Burning Life: You cannot regain Hit Points by any means while this mode is active. Inevitable Decay: At the end of each of your turns, you take 35 Bludgeoning damage. This damage cannot be reduced or prevented in any way, and it bypasses all resistances and immunities (including Temporary Hit Points). Ending the Technique: The mode ends automatically if you drop to 0 Hit Points. You can also choose to close the gate early as an Action. When the mode ends (either by dropping to 0 HP or closing it early), you immediately suffer 2 levels of Exhaustion.
documents.s: Level 20 - Eight Gates Release: Gate of Death (Capstone)

documents.t: Wondrous Item, uncommon(+1), rare(+2), very rare(+3) Attunement Requires Attunement by a spiritualist Description This small, square talisman is inscribed with occult runes. While this seal is adhered to your spiritual focus, you gain a bonus to the saving throw DCs of your spirit arts. The bonus is determined by the seal's rarity. When a creature targets you with an attack or forces you to make a saving throw, you can activate this seal as a reaction, allowing you to instantly tether (one tether only) to the creature. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until the next dawn.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This glassy orb is 3 inches in diameter, weighs 1/2 pound, and is wrapped in a golden wire cage. Strange, wispy smoke drifts around inside the orb, creating cloud-like shapes that are almost recognizable as real-life objects. While holding the orb, you can use an action to speak its command word, priming the orb and causing the smoke inside to restlessly billow and swirl. While holding the primed orb, you can gently squeeze it (no action required) to cause it to record that moment in time around you. When you do, the glassy sphere becomes perfectly clear over the course of 1 minute and reveals an exact duplicate of the area around you in up to a 30-foot radius as a miniature, illusory diorama inside it. While holding the orb, the scene inside soundlessly replays the next 6 seconds following the diorama's capture. An orb remains primed for 1 minute or until used to capture a diorama. Touching a primed orb of remembrance to one that already has a diorama creates a duplicate of the diorama in the primed orb. Speaking the command word again while shaking the orb causes the diorama inside to disappear into smoke, allowing it to be primed once more.
4th-level illusion. (Wizard (Legacy), Wizard, The Undead (VRGtR))
Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual) Range: 30 feet Components: V, S Duration: 1 hour

A Huge, quasi-real, horse-drawn coach appears on the ground in an unoccupied space of your choice within range. You decide the creature's and coach's appearance, and it is equipped with the necessary gear to pull the carriage. Any of the equipment created by the spell vanishes in a puff of smoke if it is carried more than 10 feet away from the steed or coach. For the duration, you and up to 4 other creatures you choose can ride in the coach. The steeds uses the Riding Horse stat block, except it has a Speed of 100 feet and can travel 11 miles in an hour. When the spell ends, the steeds and coach gradually fades, giving the riders 1 minute to dismount. The spell ends early if the steed takes any damage.

Potion, Uncommon Description For a period of 2d4 hours after you drink this potion, any mundane inanimate object you name will materialize in your hand for 1-minute as a sentient, uncooperative version of itself. This materialized sentient object will be capable of speaking any languages you are proficient in. This potion takes the form of an indigo-colored, effervescent liquid that pours like water.

Wondrous Item (Legendary), Attuenement Requires Attunement by a Spellcaster Description You can cast plane shift and demiplane once per day each, without material components. When you cast demiplane using this item, you may expand a demiplane you previously created with it instead of creating a new one. Each expansion permanently increases its size by one additional 30-foot cube. While inside a demiplane created by this item, you can use an action to reshape nonliving aspects of it (terrain, structures, lighting, temperature, and harmless sensory effects). You can’t create creatures or duplicate spell effects without casting spells normally. Carved Keys. When you create or expand your demiplane, you can form a number of fragile planar keys equal to your proficiency bonus (minimum 1). Each creature can carry only one of these keys at a time. If a creature already holds one, it cannot receive another until the first is used or destroyed. A creature can use a key as an action to open a doorway to your demiplane and enter it. The key crumbles to dust after use. While inside, that creature can exit as an action, appearing in the nearest unoccupied space to where the key was used. This return does not require a key. Only the attuned wielder can create new keys.

Rare Weapon (Firearm) Requires Attunement A heavy weapon that utilizes high concentrations of lightning magic to accelerate heavy metal rods at super sonic speeds. The weapon has a range of 400 feet, and it has the following properties: two-handed, ammunition (firearms), ultra-heavy, reload (1). It deals 8d8 piercing damage on a hit. Attacks with this weapon cannot be made as part of the attack action. Instead, as an action on your turn you can target a 1 foot wide, 400 foot long line, which then becomes the weapon's target area. At the start of your next turn, the weapon fires, automatically hitting the first target within the weapon's target area. Once the weapon has been aimed, you cannot move or be moved, and the trajectory cannot be adjusted until the weapon fires. Siege Engine: This weapon deals double damage to objects and structures.

Volatile and dangerous, Powderkegs typically make use of exceedingly dangerous chemicals or magic to act as the ultimate deterrent. Despite this, Bulwarks under this specialization tend to show great care for the power they wield. Features: 3rd Level - Powderkeg Training 3rd Level - Volatile Ward 7th Level - Combustion 13th level - Explosive Ward 18th Level - Fission
When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with firearms and alchemist supplies.

Additionally at 3rd level, you have the ability to work volatile compounds into your armor and defensive strategies. Whenever you use your fortitude feature, the triggering creature takes fire damage equal to your bulwark level.

Starting at 7th level, your knack for mixing potent reactions extends to aid you in combat. While you are holding alchemist supplies and take the attack action, you can replace one attack on each of your turns with a burst of chemical energy. Target a creature within 15 feet of yourself. The target must succeed a Dexterity Saving Throw (DC 8 + your Strength Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d8 damage. This damage is acid, fire or poison (your choice).

When you reach 13th level, you learn to improve your Volatile Ward with even more explosive potential. When you use your Volatile Ward feature, you can choose to have each creature within 20 feet of you take the damage, instead of just the triggering creature. If you do so, the feature deals only half damage.

Starting at 18th level, the explosive potential within you reaches its pinnacle. As an action, you can trigger a chain reaction within your armor to detonate out in a violent burst. You immediately take 20d6 fire damage and 20d6 bludgeoning damage, and each creature within 40 feet of you must succeed a dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Strength Modifier + you Proficiency Bonus) or take the same damage, taking half as much on a successful save. Objects that are not being worn or carried in the area also take this damage. After using this feature, you have immunity to all damage until the end of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

8th-level necromancy. (Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 Action Range: 60 ft. Components: V Duration: Instantaneous Description You utter a word of defilement on a creature you see within range. If the creature you choose has 150 hit points of fewer, the target gains vulnerability to all damage that they are not resistant or immune to. Otherwise, the spell has no effect on it. A defiled creature must make a Constitution Save at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, the creature is no longer defiled.

Wondrous Item, varies Attunement Requires Attunement by a Rogue Description These finely crafted gloves improves the precision of a rogue's skills. While wearing it, you gain a bonus to the saving throw DCs of your rogue features. The bonus is determined by the glove's rarity. In addition the gloves have 3 charges that recharge at dawn. Whenever you use a cunning or devious strike you can use one of the charges instead of using sneak die. Uncommon: +1 DC Bonus Rare: +2 DC Bonus Very Rare: +3 DC Bonus

2nd-level illusion. (Artificer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual) Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (crushed glass worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Until Dispelled Description You implant a magical light into an object that you touch which activates when a trigger condition is met. Next, determine the circumstances that will trigger the spell to turn on the light. When that circumstance occurs, the object begins to glow, emitting dim light in a radius of 5 feet around the object. If the trigger condition you specified is a spoken phrase, the object itself becomes colored if the final word of the phrase is a color. Otherwise, the object turns white. When you cast this spell, you can have the spell end after it activates for the first time, or it can remain and continue to change colors if the trigger condition occurs again. If the trigger condition occurs while the light is already on, the object changes color to the new color at the end of a spoken message, or returns to normal and stops glowing if no color is spoken. The triggering circumstance can be as general or as detailed as you like, though it must be based on visual or audible conditions that occur within 30 feet of the object. For example, you could instruct the object to light up when any creature moves within 30 feet of the object or when a silver bell rings within 30 feet of it.

At 1st level, whenever you start casting a spell that deals fire damage, fiery magic erupts from you. This eruption causes creatures of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you to take fire damage equal to half your sorcerer level (minimum of 1).
At 6th level, you gain resistance to fire damage. In addition, spells you cast and effects you create ignore resistance to fire damage.

Starting at 14th level, when you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal fire damage to the attacker. The damage equals your sorcerer level, and ignores resistance to fire damage.

At 18th level, you gain immunity to fire damage. In addition, you ignore resistance to fire damage and treat immunity to fire damage as resistance to fire damage. When treating immunity as resistance, features or feats that allow you to ignore resistance do not do so.

Wondrous Item, common Description This small orb of silver, watery liquid is strangely dry to the touch. While holding the 1-inch-diameter metallic sphere in the palm of your hand, you can mentally control the form that it takes using an action. The form stretches and turns into the imagined shape and remains centered in your hand. Regardless of the form, it can be no larger than the palm of your hand and is always a liquid. The form returns to its natural orb state when you end your focus on the quicksilver clay (no action required) or it leaves your hand. Eating or drinking the liquid is harmless, but takes 1d4 days to exit the body.

Weapon (crossbow, heavy), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. With a bonus action you can deploy or retract the stand system. When the stand is deployed you gain advantage on your attack rolls made by this weapon. But as a result you can't make any movement, or you lose the bonus.

A Raven Knight is fearsome in battle, fusing martial prowess with strange abilities gifted by the Raven Queen. Many Raven Knights work alone, though some may find a small band of companions to aid them in battle, and some may even command and lead entire armies into battle. Masters of death, Raven Knights seek to protect those who cannot protect themselves from undeath and the afterlife. Powerful Raven Knights may even become champions of the Raven Queen, and thus champions of the battlefield.

When you choose this Archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Investigation and Medicine skills. Additionally, you can make Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Medicine) checks with advantage when attempting to determine the cause of death of a creature.

At 3rd level, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points you sever the connection of the creatures soul to its body. That creature cannot be turned into an undead. Additionally, as a reaction, when a creature is reduced to 0 hit points within 15ft of you you can empower your next attack with that creatures soul energy. Your next weapon attack deals additional necrotic damage equal to half your fighter level.

At 7th level, you move with the grace of the raven. Your walking speed increases by 10ft. Additionally, as a bonus action you gain a flight speed equal to your walking speed until the end of your turn, if you end your turn in midair you drop to the ground.
At 10th level, the Raven Queen grants you a blessing. You gain advantage on death saving throws, immunity to the frightened condition, and resistance to necrotic damage.
At 15th level, when you or an ally critically hit a creature, you can use your reaction to add 3d10 necrotic damage to the attacks damage roll.

At 18th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack against the creature that killed you. On a hit you critically hit that creature and regain hit points equal to the damage dealt. You can do this once per long rest.

Weapon (crossbow, heavy), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. With a bonus action you can deploy or retract the stand system. When the stand is deployed you gain advantage on your attack rolls made by this weapon. But as a result you can't make any movement, or you lose the bonus.

Weapon (Kusarigama), very rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description Based on the Scythe of Reaping, this Kusarigama is adorned by grotesque engravings of tragedy, and has an obsidian lining running the length of the kusari blade, along with depictions of mass graves on the kama. Within crafting, death of any living creature must take place, each being slain with one section of the weapon before the magic may be imbued within it. Once per turn when you hit a creature with this Kusarigama, it gains a stack of reap, which lasts until its next short or long rest. Once per turn, this weapon deals an additional 1d6 necrotic damage for every stack of reap the target has. A target may have a maximum of 5 stacks of reap. A target looses all stacks of reap if it is targeted by greater restoration, heal, or a similar restorative magic. When a target with at least 1 stack of reap is reduced to zero hit points with this weapon, you gain 5 temporary hit points for each stack of reap the target had.

Weapon (Kusarigama), very rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description Based on the Scythe of Reaping, this Kusarigama is adorned by grotesque engravings of tragedy, and has an obsidian lining running the length of the kusari blade, along with depictions of mass graves on the kama. Within crafting, death of any living creature must take place, each being slain with one section of the weapon before the magic may be imbued within it. Once per turn when you hit a creature with this Kusarigama, it gains a stack of reap, which lasts until its next short or long rest. Once per turn, this weapon deals an additional 1d6 necrotic damage for every stack of reap the target has. A target may have a maximum of 5 stacks of reap. A target looses all stacks of reap if it is targeted by greater restoration, heal, or a similar restorative magic. When a target with at least 1 stack of reap is reduced to zero hit points with this weapon, you gain 5 temporary hit points for each stack of reap the target had.

Prerequisite: Skeleton Your Constitution Score increases by 1. The necromancy that stitched you together is shockingly good at keeping you intact. When you become stabilized as a result of succeeding three death saving throws, you regain hit points equal to your level.

Flask - Adventuring Gear - 250 gp, 2 lbs. Also referred to as thermite in other settings, red powder is a volatile mixture of iron and aluminum powders. It burns rapidly and at extremely high temperatures, though it is not an explosive. A single flask can be emptied and contains enough powder to cover one square foot. It can then be ignited, where it burns for 1 round, shedding bright light in a 30 foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. The powder can burn or melt away a single tiny non-magical item that it remains in contact with while burning. As an action, you can recollect or brush away red powder that is yet to be ignited. Once ignited, the powder sticks to the surface and can no longer be removed until it burns away. A creature that touches red powder, or starts its turn touching red powder, while it is burning takes 4d8 fire damage, that ignores a target's resistance to fire damage.

6th-level abjuration. (Bard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a small sprinkling of powdered silver) Duration: 10 minutes Description You create a reflective magical barrier that turns harmful attacks back upon their attackers. For the duration, when a creature hits you with an attack, it takes 2d8 radiant damage. Additionally, if you fail a saving throw against a spell cast by a creature you can see, they take 1d8 radiant damage + an extra 1d8 for each spell slot level of the spell cast.
Five legendary ornaments, made by Sardior for no cause but his own

Sardior did not enter the war between his creators, and he was never asked to. That was the injury. Tiamat forged masks and the world spoke of them for a hundred years. Bahamut answered with cloaks and the world spoke of those for a hundred more. In all that talk there was no line, not one, about the Ruby Dragon — who is older than the quarrel, who rules a palace of gemstone that drifts through the night sky, and who has never in his existence been anyone’s second choice. So he made five things of his own, and he made them for the opposite reason. A mask conceals its wearer. A cloak covers them. Sardior made jewelry, which exists for one purpose only: to be looked at. He gave the pieces no oath, no enemy, no cause. He did not ask them to stand against anything. He asked them to be noticed, and to make certain that whoever wore them was noticed too. The five gem dragons contributed as the metallics and chromatics had, though the accounts differ on how willingly. An amethyst gave a shard from a torc it had worn as an arbiter of disputes; a crystal gave a night’s worth of swallowed starlight; an emerald gave a secret it had held for eight hundred years and would not miss; a sapphire gave a piece of its hoard-wall, cut from the stone of a fortress it had held alone; a topaz gave nothing and had something taken. Sardior set them in gold in his own workshop in the Ruby Palace, and when they were finished he looked at them for a long while and did not give them away. That is the part the chroniclers find funny and the wearers do not. The Regalia was never sent to champions. It escaped. The pieces left the Ruby Palace one at a time over the centuries — by theft, by wager, by gift to a favorite who was later forgotten — and each has since passed through more hands than anyone can count, because each is worth a kingdom and none of them wants to stay anywhere it has already been admired. There was a sixth setting on the workbench. It is empty in every description that survives, and it was cut for a stone the size of a fist. Sardior intended, when the Regalia had made a sufficient noise in the world, to wear the last piece himself. He was scattered before he got to it. The Regalia has been looking for its sixth ever since, and it is not particular about whose brow it ends up on.
documents.s: Lore: What the Ruby Dragon Wanted

documents.t: The following applies to all five pieces of the Regalia of the Ruby Court. Sized to the Wearer. The piece adjusts itself to fit any creature Small, Medium, or Large that attunes to it, and cannot be damaged by ordinary means. Singular. There is only ever one of each of the five pieces, and their magic cannot be replicated, copied, or reproduced by any craft or spell. Unjoinable. The pieces cannot be combined, merged, reset, or made into any other item, by any means. Not one of them will surrender its own shape to become part of a greater whole, and attempts to force the matter fail without harming the piece. Worn to Be Seen. A piece grants none of its benefits while it is concealed. It must be worn openly, over clothing and outside armor, in plain view of anyone facing you. Covering it with a cloak, a glove, a helm, or an illusion suspends every benefit until it is uncovered. Rival Ornaments. Unlike the masks and the cloaks, the Regalia will share a wearer — Sardior saw no reason to deny himself. But each piece expects to be the one anyone notices first. While you are attuned to more than one piece of the Regalia, you have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and on Wisdom (Insight) checks, and you can’t take the Hide action while any Regalia piece is uncovered. Indifferent to the Quarrel. The Regalia has no opinion about Tiamat or Bahamut and imposes no conditions on your conduct. A piece can be worn alongside a Mask of the Dragon Queen or a Cloak of the Platinum Ward without either repelling it. A cloak’s wearer who also wears Regalia will notice, over time, that they are being pulled in two directions by two things that want different accounts of them: one wants them good, and one wants them looked at. The Flattery. A piece of the Regalia is not sentient, but it is vain, and vanity does not require a mind. It leans. A wearer finds their own reflection arriving more often than it used to, hears their better qualities enumerated in their own voice at odd hours, and grows quietly certain that a room went duller when they left it. This is influence, not compulsion. The wearer keeps every scrap of free will. Most of them simply stop wanting to take it off. Jealous Regard. The Regalia has no opinion about Tiamat or Bahamut, and no piece will repel a Mask of the Dragon Queen or a Cloak of the Platinum Ward — it does something worse. While you wear a piece of the Regalia, any mask or cloak of that kind worn by you is suppressed: it grants none of its benefits, its attunement remains but lies dormant, and its colors go flat and lightless for as long as the Regalia is uncovered. The suppression lifts the moment the Regalia piece is removed or concealed, which is precisely the choice Sardior wanted his wearers to have to make. Whatever else you have made yourself a champion of, you may be that or you may be looked at, and you may not be both.

Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A heavy open collar of violet crystal, faceted along its whole length and terminating in two blunt dragon heads that almost touch at the throat. It weighs nothing at all until someone tries to take it from you, at which point it becomes as immovable as a millstone. Held to the light it throws violet bands across every surface in the room, and it makes a low humming note when the wearer speaks a hard truth. While you are wearing the amethyst torc and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against force damage. If you already have resistance to force damage from another source, you instead have immunity to force damage. If you already have immunity to force damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to force damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the force damage dealt. Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class. Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6. Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with amethyst dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Psychokinetic Rive. If you deal force damage to a creature, it can’t take reactions until the end of its next turn.

Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A slender band of clear crystal that sits on the brow without any clasp or pin, rising to a single upswept point above the forehead. It holds starlight the way a cistern holds water: on a clear night it drinks the sky, and for hours afterward it gives that light back in a soft, cold shine. In darkness the wearer’s face is always faintly visible, which the diadem considers a courtesy and its wearers do not always agree. While you are wearing the crystal diadem and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against radiant damage. If you already have resistance to radiant damage from another source, you instead have immunity to radiant damage. If you already have immunity to radiant damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to radiant damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the radiant damage dealt. Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class. Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6. Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with crystal dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Revealing Glare. If you deal radiant damage to a creature, it sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius until the end of its next turn and can’t benefit from being invisible during that time.

Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A broad ring of green gold set with a cabochon emerald cut into a coiled dragon in profile, made for pressing into wax. Documents sealed with it cannot be opened by anyone but their intended reader without the wax visibly cracking. The stone is warm and slightly damp to the touch, like the inside of a cave, and it has an unnerving habit of catching the light whenever someone nearby is about to lie. While you are wearing the emerald signet and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against psychic damage. If you already have resistance to psychic damage from another source, you instead have immunity to psychic damage. If you already have immunity to psychic damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to psychic damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the psychic damage dealt. Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class. Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6. Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with emerald dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Keeper of Secrets. You can’t be compelled to reveal a secret you have knowingly sworn to keep by any magic that would read your thoughts or force your speech, though such magic still detects that a secret is being kept.

Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A palm-sized brooch of blue-black sapphire in the shape of a dragon at rest, wings folded, pin worked into the tail. It is heavier than it looks and colder than the room. When battle is joined anywhere within a mile it grows perceptibly warmer, and it will not consent to be pinned anywhere but the left breast, over the heart, where a soldier would wear a commendation. While you are wearing the sapphire brooch and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against thunder damage. If you already have resistance to thunder damage from another source, you instead have immunity to thunder damage. If you already have immunity to thunder damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to thunder damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the thunder damage dealt. Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class. Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6. Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with sapphire dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Precognitive Guard. You have advantage on initiative rolls, and you can’t be surprised while you are conscious.

Wondrous item, legendary (requires attunement) A wide, unornamented cuff of pale golden topaz, seamless, with no visible way to put it on or take it off. It is always faintly gritty, as though it has just come out of dry sand, and no amount of polishing changes this. Wearers report that it sits more comfortably when they are alone, and that it tightens by a hair’s breadth in crowds. While you are wearing the topaz bangle and attuned to it, you gain the following benefits. Damage Absorption. You have resistance against necrotic damage. If you already have resistance to necrotic damage from another source, you instead have immunity to necrotic damage. If you already have immunity to necrotic damage from another source, whenever you are subjected to necrotic damage, you take none of that damage and regain a number of hit points equal to half the necrotic damage dealt. Draconic Majesty. While you are wearing no armor, you can add your Charisma bonus to your Armor Class. Dragon Breath. If you have a breath weapon that requires rest to recharge, it gains a recharge of 6. Dragon Sight. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or to an additional 60 feet if you already have that sense. Once per day, you can gain blindsight out to 30 feet for 5 minutes. Dragon Tongue. You can speak and understand Draconic. You also have advantage on any Charisma check you make when interacting with topaz dragons. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Desiccating Grip. If you deal necrotic damage to a creature, it can’t regain hit points until the end of its next turn.

Ring, uncommon Description This seemingly mundane ring can store a single cantrip. Only one of these rings can be worn at a time, if another Ring of Cantrip Storing is equipped both cease to function. The ring takes one turn to equip, and one turn to unequip. The cantrip, if used for a spell that requires a save, has a DC of 10, and if used for a attack roll receive no modifiers and is treated as a straight roll. If the spell is affected by the caster's level, such as eldritch blast, it is casted at its lowest level. A cantrip of any class can be stored within the ring. To store a cantrip, one must be able to cast the cantrip themselves, or find someone else who knows the cantrip that can store it in the ring on their behalf through a 10 minute ritual.

Ring, uncommon Description This ring a golden band, with an amethyst gem and scribings in either Celestial, Draconic, or Sylvan. Activated by a spoken or mental command, the ring allows the wearer to either suppress a specific emotion, or emotion in general on themselves. The chosen effect lasts until cancelled. This does not confer the below effect. This effects takes a free action. Additionally, the ring can also be used to fight off fear and/or infatuation. When you make a saving throw to avoid or end the charmed and/or frightened conditions on yourself, you can give yourself advantage on the roll if you are wearing the ring. You must decide to do so before rolling the d20. If the save succeeds, you can't use the ring in this way until you finish a long rest. Only the wearer can receive the effects of this ring, and effects cannot stack with duplicate Rings of Emotional Suppression or Cuddly Strixhaven Mascots.

Ring, common Description As an action, you can cause a single rose to grow and appear in your hand. The stem is a foot long and has small, dull thorns. The rose blossoms in a color of your choice as it finishes growing, but withers and disintegrates after 24 hours. You can cause a single rose to grow 5 times per day, which refreshes at dawn.

Ring, Common Description While wearing this ring, you can use a bonus action to mentally command the ring to transform into a fork, spoon, or other harmless element of a set of cook's utensils (such as a ladle or spatula). The transformed ring returns to its normal form on your finger if you mentally end the effect (no action required) or are no longer holding it.

Wondrous Item, rare Description This ring stores spells cast into it, holding them until the wearer uses them. The ring can store a single level 1 spell (Casted with a first level slot), but the casting time for this spell is automatically a reaction rather than an action or bonus action. Only one of these rings can be worn at a time, if another Ring of Triggered Spells is equipped both cease to function, and you cannot cast spells from it. This trigger must be specified when the spell is stored into the ring. For example: A Cure Wounds spell is triggered as a reaction if the wearer becomes bloodied. While wearing this ring, you can cast any spell stored in it. The spell uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster, but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell. The spell cast from the ring is no longer stored in it, freeing up space.

Wondrous Item Attunement Requires Attunement Description A pair of magically fueled and regulated rockets rigged together to form a wearable backpack. While wearing the rocket pack, you have a flying speed of 30 and can hover. Additionally, you may use a bonus action to move up to 30 feet in a straight line without provoking opportunity attacks.

Martial Melee Weapon - 1d10 piercing - two-handed, thrown (range 20/20), heavy, special, topple - 500 gp, 12 lbs Rocket spear. It's a spear with a rocket. Pressurized combustion reimagined to strap a simple oil-powered rocket to the head of a spear to deliver a rather excessive amount of melee force. Special - As an action, you can fuel the rocket spear with one flask of oil. While fueled, the rocket becomes active, and the weapon's thrown range increases to 60/60. While the rocket is active and you throw the spear, you can choose to hold onto it during its flight, landing in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target. Once fueled, the rocket burns out of fuel at the end of your next turn or when you make an attack with it.

Wondrous Item (consumable), uncommon Description This 12-ounce bottle of red grape wine is created by infusing the magicked flesh of sentient fungi into the yeast during the fermentation process. When ingested in its entirety, this potent alcohol inflicts the poisoned condition. A creature poisoned in this manner is considered drunk for a number of hours equal to 1d6 - their constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hour). A creature who is normally immune to poison still suffers this effect but can choose to resist the poison as an action, ending the condition.

Wondrous Item, very rare Attunement Requires Attunement by a monk Description This sash of elk hair from the frigid north is as white as the endless snowy dales. The eldr (focus) rune is sewn into it with bright red threads. The sash has the following properties while you wear it: Heightened Focus. As an action, you can channel the sash's magic to increase the potency of your ki. For the next minute or until you lose concentration as if concentrating on a spell, you can increase the DC of your ki abilities by 2. This property can’t be used again until the next dawn. Lightened Focus. By spending 3 ki points, you can double your movement speed for 1 minute. Imbuement of Focus. You can transfer the sash's magic to a nonmagical item -- either one of your monk weapons or a pair of gloves -- by tracing the stein rune there with your finger. The transfer takes 8 hours of work that requires the two items to be within 5 feet of each other. At the end of the 8 hours, the sash is destroyed, and the rune appears in silver on the chosen item. You can only be attuned to one of the items at a time, which gains a benefit based on its form in addition to its normal effects: Weapon. The weapon becomes a very rare magic weapon that requires attunement by a monk. While you wield it, you can use your Wisdom modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls using the weapon and has a +2 bonus to the attack and damage rolls of those attacks. Whenever you use a ki point as part the attack made with the weapon, your attack deals additional damage equal to your Wisdom modifier. Gloves. The pair of gloves is now a rare magic item that requires attunement by a monk. While you wear the gloves you can use your Wisdom modifier instead of Strength when making Strength (Athletics) checks and your unarmed strikes gains a +2 to damage rolls.

Weapon (dagger), uncommon Description This dagger is adorned with a magical leaf at it's base, and is otherwise seemingly normal. This dagger may be thrown at an object or creature, at which point it will seamlessly embed itself. While embedded, the throwing creature may use it as 5 feet of stable ground no matter the height it is embedded. As a bonus action on a subsequent turn, the throwing creature may recall it through the use of a string tied to it's hilt.

Weapon: Simple, Melee 5gp, 2 lbs. --- 1d6 slashing - finesse, versatile (1d8) Description Proficiency with a scythe allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Finesse: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. Versatile: This weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property--the damage when the weapon is used with two hands to make a melee attack. Mastery Property - Cleave: If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

Weapon (Scythe), very rare Description This scythe is adorned by grotesque engravings of tragedy, and has an obsidian lining running the length of the blade. Each time you hit a creature with this scythe, it gains a stack of reap, which lasts until it’s next short or long rest. This weapon deals an additional 1 slashing damage for every stack of reap the target has. A target may have a maximum of 7 stacks of reap. A target looses all stacks of reap if it is targeted by greater restoration, heal, or a similar restorative magic. When a target with at least 1 stack of reap is reduced to zero hit points with this weapon, you gain 5 temporary hit points for each stack of reap the target had.

Wondrous Item, common Description While standing on a solid surface, you begin to sit down in an open space as if there were a chair beneath you. When you would normally crouch or fall to the ground when doing this, you can mentally command the belt to summon an invisible, incorporeal chair as a bonus action instead. The chair can be of any style you choose, such as a stool, recliner, throne, or rocking chair, and can support up to 500 pounds. While it is comfortable, it is nevertheless invisible and cannot be interacted with beyond simply sitting on. The chair disappears if it is no longer on a solid surface, you stand up, or if you're pushed or moved while sitting on it.

The Sentinel Blade embodies the essence of unwavering defense, blending masterful swordplay with unbreakable resolve. Trained to stand as the ultimate shield for their allies, these warriors adopt a specialized stance that turns every strike against them into an opportunity. Their blades move with precision, deflecting blows with ease and delivering calculated ripostes.

Starting at 2nd level, you learn to develop flow during the midst of combat, building on each success as you begin to flow like a dance. While using a melee weapon without a shield, whenever you land a successful hit your first time in a turn, an attack misses you, or you succeed on a saving throw from a hostile creature, you gain flow equal to 1d6 + half your total mastery. Whenever you take damage from an attack, you lose flow instead. If this damage reduces your flow to 0, you take any remaining damage. If you reduce an attack's damage to zero, you suffer no additional effects from the weapon. You can have a max amount of flow equal to twice your practitioner level, which depletes at the end of combat. You can only build flow whilst in combat.

Starting at 6th level, when an attack misses you, or you block one with flow completely, you may make a melee attack as a reaction against the target. Additionally, you may instead spend 1 mastery point to use a technique.
Starting at 14th level, when an ally within melee range is hit by an attack, you can use your flow to block the attack as if it were targeting you.

Starting at 18th level, you learn to harness your flow into focus. When you have at least 75% of your maximum flow and focus on a technique or use a technique through riposte, you may sacrifice 7 flow to spend 1 less mastery point. The following goes with the subclass as part of the practitioner class

Type: Physical Prerequisites: Novice, Sentinel Blade Make a weapon attack against a creature or object. The attack deals a number of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus in additional damage. Focused (1 point) Hit or miss, roll a number or d4s equal to half your total mastery. You gain flow equal to the total.

Type: Physical Prerequisites: Intermediate, Sentinel Blade You move in a mirage, teleporting to an area within 60ft of you. Focused (1 point, 0 if you have your maximum flow). You can use another technique that includes a weapon attack. This may be before or after you teleport.

Type: Mental Prerequisites: Advanced, Sentinel Blade You may temporarily steel yourself against other manners of attacks. Until the end of your next turn, you may block damage from any source using Aegis Flow. Focused (2 points, 1 if you your maximum flow). The duration of this technique becomes 1 minute. Until the end of your next turn, if you would succeed on a saving throw and normally take half damage, you would instead take no damage.

Type: Physical Prerequisites: Master, Sentinel Blade Duration: 1 minute For the next minute, your maximum flow and the flow you gain is doubled. During this time, you have vulnerability to attacks while your flow is 0. You must use an action to end this effect Focused (1 points). You may use another technique from this form

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This cube deals 1 point of lightning damage to any creature that touches it, or starts its turn touching it. once it has dealt 20 lightning damage this way it loses this property for 1 hour.

Wondrous Item, legendary Description This 3-inch cube crackles with electric potential energy, and resonates slightly when touched. Any creature that ends its turn touching the cube takes lightning damage equal to half their remaining hitpoints. Additionally, the creature cannot take reactions until the end of their next turn. Once the cube has discharged, it cannot do so again until 1 hour has passed.

Wondrous Item, varies Attunement Requires Attunement by a Warmage Description This arcane sigil acts as a spellcasting focus for your Warmage spells. While attuned to it, you gain a bonus to spell attack rolls with your Warmage spells and the DC for your Warmage spells and abilities increases by the same amount. The bonus is determined by the sigil's rarity. Uncommon (+1): +1 to spell attack rolls and spell save DC. Rare (+2): +2 to spell attack rolls and spell save DC. Very Rare (+3): +3 to spell attack rolls and spell save DC. In addition, while attuned to this sigil, you may spend one Bonus Action to regain one use of your Overcharge feature. This property cannot be used again until the next dawn.

Weapon (Any Bow), Very Rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description Made of a mysterious yet flexible space-metal alloy, this bow gleams a radiant silver-white, like moonlight. The Silver Bow grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it, and deals radiant damage instead of piercing damage. While attuned to the Silver Bow, you gain the following properties: Sense Hidden: While holding the Silver Bow, you have advantage on skill checks made to sense the presence of hidden creatures, shapechangers or creatures not in their true form. Unveiling: As a bonus action, you can create a 60-foot-radius sphere around you that lasts for 1 minute, or until you lose your concentration (as if you were concentrating on a spell). Whenever a hidden creature, shapechanger or creature not in their true form enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, that creature must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or glow with a faint light on a failure, gaining no benefit from being invisible until the end of its next turn. If the target is a creature in a form other than it's true form, you can also force it to make a DC 17 Charisma saving throw or revert to it's true form on a failure. You can use this feature a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, resetting on a long rest.

Weapon (scimitar), very rare (requires attunement) Attunement: Requires Attunement Description This finely crafted scimitar features a crescent-shaped blade adorned with intricate engravings. The blade is perforated with small holes and wind chambers, allowing it to emit a haunting, flute-like melody when swung or spun. Harmonic Transformation: As a bonus action, you can transform the Siren’s Crescent into a musical instrument of your choice, provided you are proficient with that instrument. While using the transformed instrument, you have advantage on ability checks made to play it. You can revert the instrument back into the scimitar as a bonus action. Arcane Harmony: If you can use a weapon as a spellcasting focus, the Siren’s Crescent grants a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DC of spells you cast through it. Weapon Bonuses: You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls for melee weapon attacks made with this magic weapon. Siren's Crescent

Weapon (scimitar), very rare (requires attunement) Attunement: Requires Attunement Description This finely crafted scimitar features a crescent-shaped blade adorned with intricate engravings. The blade is perforated with small holes and wind chambers, allowing it to emit a haunting, flute-like melody when swung or spun. Harmonic Transformation: As a bonus action, you can transform the Siren’s Crescent into a musical instrument of your choice, provided you are proficient with that instrument. While using the transformed instrument, you have advantage on ability checks made to play it. You can revert the instrument back into the scimitar as a bonus action. Arcane Harmony: If you can use a weapon as a spellcasting focus, the Siren’s Crescent grants a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DC of spells you cast through it. Weapon Bonuses: You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls for melee weapon attacks made with this magic weapon. Siren's Crescent

9th Level Necromancy (Cleric, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 Action Range: 30 feet Components: V, S Duration: 1 minute Description One creature you can see within range becomes the target of an onslaught of ethereal skeletons. At the end of each of the target's turns, four skeletons immediately appear in the closest unoccupied spaces to the target and are hostile towards it. The skeletons' attacks are considered magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunities, and last until either they or the target die, where they disappear leaving no trace. They cannot be commanded and will exclusively take actions harmful to the target, or to aid in harming the target. If any skeletons remain when more are to be summoned, that many additional skeletons are summoned.

8th Level Necromancy (Cleric, Wizard, Warlock) Casting Time: 1 Action Range: 60 feet Components: N/A Duration: Instantaneous Description When you cast this spell, target one creature you can see within range. 8d4 skeletons immediately appear in the closest unoccupied spaces to the target, and are hostile towards it. Alternatively, you can delay the appearance of the skeletons by up to an hour. The skeletons' attacks are considered magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunities, and last until either they or the target die, where they disappear leaving no trace. They cannot be commanded and will exclusively take actions harmful to the target, or to aid in harming the target. If a creature already under the effects of skeleton surprise is targeted, you instead change the time at which the skeletons appear, rather than causing more to appear. You may also change the time that the skeletons appear as an action, so long as the time you choose falls within one hour of the initial casting. The casting of this spell does not require verbal or somatic components, hence the surprise.

Weapon( Blunderbuss, Scrapshot), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description Using top-of-the-line polymorphic magic, a slug shotgun converts standard shells and ammunition into live slugs! The weapon loses both the [Point-Blank] and [Greater Point-Blank] properties if it has them, and deals 1d4 extra acid damage, or 2d4 extra acid damage if the weapon had the [Greater Point-Blank] property.

Wondrous item, common Description These cozy, knitted mittens have been enchanted to always bring a touch of winter with them. As an action while wearing the mittens, you can clamp your hands together, as if you were forming a snowball. When you open your hands again, a perfectly formed snowball appears in them. Any snow created in this way vanishes after 1 minute.

Weapon (Pistol), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Additionally, this weapon deals radiant damage instead of piercing damage. This weapon has 6 charges. Once per turn, you can expend one charge when you attack with this weapon. If this attack hits, it deals 6d10 extra radiant damage, and the target must succeed on a DC18 constitution saving throw or be blinded until the end of it's next turn. The weapon regains a single charge when it spends a full 8 hours in direct sunlight.

Bulwarks who spend their training bettering themselves against the ever-present threat of magic. Spellbreakers are the last thing a wizard wants to see on the field of battle, usually resulting in a fairly one sided encounter. Features: 3rd Level - Out of the Inferno 7th Level - Spell-Shatter 13th Level - Anticipation 18th Level - Willbreaker

When you choose this specialization at 3rd level, you learn to incorporate methods to help you avoid magical effects into your stance. While your defensive stance is active, you also gain resistance to fire, cold, lightning, and acid damage.

Starting at 7th level, magical warding effects become inefficient at halting your progress. When you hit a creature or object with a weapon attack, all spells from the abjuration school immediately end if they are affecting the target.

When you reach 13th level, you gain an understanding and fortitude against the ways that mages tend to fight. When you enter your defensive stance, you automatically succeed on the next intelligence, wisdom, or charisma saving throw you make before it ends.

At 18th level, your magical defenses allow you to nearly completely ignore the effects of lesser magic, making your foes need to drain their resources to even hope to defeat you. You are immune to the effects of cantrips and 1st and 2nd level spells, unless you wish to be affected by them.

Weapon: Simple, Melee 1gp, 1.5 lbs. --- 1d4 piercing - light, two-handed Description Proficiency with a cestus allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special: As a bonus action, you can make one attack with this weapon.

Weapon (rod), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description A sleek scepter of darkened mithril and carved obsidian gemstone, fitted with an elongated hilt and stylized silver in the shape of winding serpents and veiled masks. The shaft tapers into a ritual blade sheathed flush into the bottom of the rod. To all appearances, it is a ceremonial staff unless drawn and wielded with purpose. While attuned to this item, you can use an action to cast the Message or Detect Thoughts spells (save DC 20). You may also use it as a spellcasting focus gaining the following benefits: Spellcasting Charges: The rod has 10 charges. It regains 1d6+4 expended charges daily at dusk. You may expend charges to cast the following spells (save DC 20), not requiring material components: Spell : Charges Dissonant Whispers (5th level): 2 Fast Friends: 2 Mislead: 3 Modify Memory: 4 Hidden Blade. When unsheathed, the scepter functions as a +2 magical shortsword. While concealed, a creature can make a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) check to identify its true nature. While attuned to this item, when you damage a creature with an attack using this magic weapon, the target can't regain hit points and has disadvantage on spells cast from this scepter until the start of your next turn. If the attack is a critical hit, the target's Hit Point maximum also decreases by an amount equal to that damage. If this reduces their Hit Point maximum to 0, the target dies and its soul is trapped in the scepters gem, as if placed under the Soul Cage spell. Only one soul can be trapped at a time.

Weapon (rod), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description A sleek scepter of darkened mithril and carved obsidian gemstone, fitted with an elongated hilt and stylized silver in the shape of winding serpents and veiled masks. The shaft tapers into a ritual blade sheathed flush into the bottom of the rod. To all appearances, it is a ceremonial staff unless drawn and wielded with purpose. While attuned to this item, you can use an action to cast the Message or Detect Thoughts spells (save DC 20). You may also use it as a spellcasting focus gaining the following benefits: Spellcasting Charges: The rod has 10 charges. It regains 1d6+4 expended charges daily at dusk. You may expend charges to cast the following spells (save DC 20), not requiring material components: Spell : Charges Dissonant Whispers (5th level): 2 Fast Friends: 2 Mislead: 3 Modify Memory: 4 Hidden Blade.
