While attuned to this item, when you damage a creature with an attack using this magic weapon, the target can't regain hit points and has disadvantage on spells cast from this scepter until the start of your next turn. If the attack is a critical hit, the target's Hit Point maximum also decreases by an amount equal to that damage. If this reduces their Hit Point maximum to 0, the target dies and its soul is trapped in the scepters gem, as if placed under the Soul Cage spell. Only one soul can be trapped at a time.

Weapon (quarterstaff), rare Attunement Requires Attunement by a monk Description This finely crafted quarterstaff is made of a smooth, polished wood and bears intricate carvings depicting swirling elemental patterns along its length. This quarterstaff has 10 elemental charges that recharges at dawn, and it grants its wielder the following abilities while they are attuned to the staff: Elemental Strikes: When you hit a creature with this staff, you can choose to imbue the attack with elemental energy. The staff becomes charged with one of the following elements: fire, lightning, or cold. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 13) or take an additional 1d8 damage of the chosen element. This feature consumes an elemental charge. Elemental Focus: You gain a +1 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with it. Elemental Absorption: As a reaction when you take damage from a spell that deals fire, lightning, or cold damage, you can use your staff to absorb some of the energy. You gain resistance to the triggering damage type until the start of your next turn. This feature consumes an elemental charge.

You have spent many a night training under the stars and became touched by cosmic energy to shape light as you see fit. Creating armaments of pure light and radiance you become a beacon for those lost in the dark. Features: 3rd Level - Hardlight One With the Stars Astral Multitool Shooting Stars Galactic Aegis Stellar Expanse

3rd-Level Feature At 3rd level, you gain an amount of Hardlight charges equal to your double proficiency bonus, resetting on a long rest. You can use one charge to conjure a mundane melee weapon you are proficient with out of radiant light. This weapon does radiant damage, and counts as a magical weapon. Alternatively, you can spend one charge to conjure up an instrument or tool you have proficiency with. Equipment conjured up using this feature lasts an hour. At 15th level this changes from 1 hours to 8 hours.
7th-Level Feature At 7th level, you gain a bonus to damage and attack rolls and ability checks with Hardlight equipment equal to half your Wisdom modifier.
7th-Level Feature At 7th level, you can spend a bonus action to change your Hardlight equipment into another piece of equipment. You can use this feature once per short rest.

10th-Level Feature Starting at 10th level, your mastery over hardlight weapons has granted you the ability to create ranged weapons. Creating a ranged weapons costs 2 hardlight and a bonus action to create. The ammunition it uses looks like a shooting star as you fire the weapons, and does not consume a hardlight charge.

15th-Level Feature At 15th level, you can spend one Hardlight charge to create Hardlight armor. Hardlight armor counts as magical heavy armor, and has a base AC of 10 + your Dexterity modifier+ your Wisdom modifier. If a creature other than yourself wears this armor, it loses its properties. Additionally, you can spend one Hardlight charge to create a Hardlight shield. This shield counts as a magical shield that provides 3/4 cover for yourself, this shield does not provide the base AC of a shield. If a creature other than yourself equips this shield, it loses its properties.

18th-Level Feature At 18th level, you can spend 2 Hardlight charges to empower yourself for one minute. Whenever you hit a creature with a Hardlight weapon, the weapon does an additional 3d6 radiant damage. While you have a Hardlight shield equipped, if an enemy misses you with a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to gain advantage on all attack rolls against them until the end of your next turn. Additionally, you can maintain one piece of Hardlight equipment indefinitely. While this equipment exists, your total amount of Hardlight charges is reduced by one until it is dismissed.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description With the adhesive property of your typical ooze and the florescent spores of certain mushrooms, these special gels can be attached to the walls or ceilings of rooms. Under dim light or darkness, they glow a light-tinted green providing dim light at a 15 ft radius. The gels, mimicking the stars, can also inspire a viewer and calm their nerves via the release of sweet-scented spores. If a creature spends a short rest in a room full of gels (gazing upon them), they gain 1d8 temp hp that wears off by their next LR. Once this property is used, it cannot be used again by any creature till the next evening, when the real stars first emerge.

Storm chasers are a select few drifters along the astral plane, seeking out natural and magical phenomena to bolster their own power. While primarily existing on the astral plane, a storm chaser can be just as effective on the material plane, or anywhere a storm can be found, as they can make good use of bows and crossbows, in addition to the firearms traditionally used while on the astral plane.

Starting at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Storm Chaser Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn’t count against the number of ranger spells you know. Ranger Level Spells 3rd Thunderwave 5th Vortex Warp 9th Call Lightning 13th Ice Storm 17th Control Winds
At 3rd Level, you have learned to harness the potency of firearms to complement the powers of the storms you chase. You gain proficiency with firearms.

Starting at 3rd level, when you take this archetype at 3rd level, you are able to unleash a deafening boom when you use your ranged weapons. Once on each of your turns, when you attack with a ranged weapon, you can force each creature within 10 feet of you to make a constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d8 thunder damage. The damage increases to 2d8 at 11th level.

At 7th level, when you take the attack action, you can forgo your extra attack feature to make a single ranged weapon attack. This attack deals triple the damage dice of the weapon you used, and deals lightning damage instead of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing. This attack is also critical on a d20 roll of 19 or 20 if used during a storm.

At 11th level, you have learned to bring storms to you. As an action, you call forth a vortex at a point you can see within 60 feet. The vortex is a cylinder with a radius of 30 feet, and a height of 90 feet. The vortex counts as a storm for the purposes of Charged Shell. As a bonus action on each of your turns while the vortex lasts, you can target a creature inside, striking them with a bolt of lightning. The target must make a dexterity saving throw, taking 3d10 lightning on a failure, or half as much on a successful save. The vortex lasts for 10 minutes, and once used, cannot be summoned again until you finish a long rest, or spend a spell slot of at least 3rd level or higher to summon it again. No more than 1 vortex can exist at once.

At 15th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage. Additionally, you can target yourself with the bolt of lightning from your storm caller ability. If you do so, instead of taking damage, your next charged shell attack deals extra damage equal to twice the amount of damage the lightning would have dealt. This also causes the attack to be critical on a d20 roll of 18, 19, or 20.

weapon (Precision Rifle), legendary, increased range (1200ft) Attunement Requires attunement by a creature with a Strength and Dexterity score 19 or higher Description This large sniper rifle is made with thicker material to propel projectiles at very long distances without losing accuracy, delivering destructive capabilities that can even pierce metal gates. Each shot made with this rifle sends a loud ripple on the battlefield that would bring dread whether or not they will be the next target. The obvious drawback to this rifle is its size and weight, making it difficult to move while in combat, as well as its noise, making it not really ideal for assassinations unless you are far enough, thus only a few choice marksmen challenge themselves in wielding this weapon. The creator explained that the reason for its name is because he " . . . wanted to make a weapon that can match the power of 9th-level spells" but it has yet to be seen in the results. On a hit, this weapon deals 14d12 instead of 2d12. While equipped or simply on your body, your movement speed is reduced to a maximum of 10 feet. Each attack made with this weapon produces an explosive boom that is audible within 600 feet (the creator didn't factor in a silencer when making this weapon, thus trying to apply one would be ill-advised as it would just blow up at the first shot). This rifle deals maximum damage when you hit structures or objects that are not worn. Special - An enhanced spyglass is mounted to the weapon. While using it, creatures and objects are magnified to four times their size. This precision rifle can't be reloaded usign a bonus action

Wondrous Item, very rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description The Sundisk is a magical throwning weapon used to destroy hordes of enemies. The Sundisk has 5 charges. As an action, you can expend a charge to throw it in a line 30 feet long and 5 feet wide. All creatures in that area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw with a DC of 15 + your dexterity modifier, taking 3d6 radiant damage on a failed save. Once the disk reaches its maximum range of 30 feet, it remains in that space. You can use a bonus action to make the Sundisk return to you along the shortest path possible. All creatures in the area of the return path must repeat the same saving throw, taking 6d6 radiant damage on a failed save. The Sundisk returns to you on your next turn even if you had moved since throwing the disk. All expended charges are regained at dawn when the sun's rays touch the disk. Once the Sundisk have expended all charges, it can act as a magic boomerang.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This small sphere of thick glass weighs 1 pound. If you are within 60 feet of it, you can speak one of two command words and cause it to emanate 60ft radius of daylight. When activated, it will start dim and grow to match the time of day over the first hour. Once used, the daylight effect can't be used again until the next dawn.The light follows a set pattern, granting 12 hours of daylight before dimming to dim light or no light (determined by the command word spoken) for 12 hours, then repeating. You can speak another command word as an action to make the illuminated globe rise into the air and float no more than 5 feet off the ground. The globe hovers in this way until you or another creature grasps it.

Wondrous item, uncommon Description This handheld device has four crystaline buttons that are each associated with a different element. The device has 4 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the device, you can use an action to expend 1 of its charges and press a button. Each button causes the device to swivel and point like a compass to the nearest relevant location, as determined by the button, for 1 hour or until another button is pressed. If there's nothing for the device to point to, it spins in place for the duration or until it's within range of something to point to. Air. If you're inside or underground, the device points to the nearest outdoor exit within 1 mile of you. If you're outside, it points in the direction of the nearest storm within 50 miles of you. Earth. The device points to the nearest cave entrance that's Medium or larger and within 1 mile of you. If you're underground, it points in the direction of the nearest unpolished gemstone within 100 feet of you. Fire. The device points to the nearest active campfire, firepit, forge, or hearth that's within 1 mile of you. Water. The device points to the nearest source of fresh, drinkable water that's within 1 mile of you.

Wondrous item, uncommon Description This handheld device has four crystaline buttons that are each associated with a different element. The device has 4 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the device, you can use an action to expend 1 of its charges and press a button. Each button causes the device to swivel and point like a compass to the nearest relevant location, as determined by the button, for 1 hour or until another button is pressed. If there's nothing for the device to point to, it spins in place for the duration or until it's within range of something to point to. Air. If you're inside or underground, the device points to the nearest outdoor exit within 1 mile of you. If you're outside, it points in the direction of the nearest storm within 50 miles of you. Earth. The device points to the nearest cave entrance that's Medium or larger and within 1 mile of you. If you're underground, it points in the direction of the nearest unpolished gemstone within 100 feet of you. Fire. The device points to the nearest active campfire, firepit, forge, or hearth that's within 1 mile of you. Water. The device points to the nearest source of fresh, drinkable water that's within 1 mile of you.

Though colloquially referred to as “Sword Saints”, swords are only the most popular weapon they are seen mastering, not the only weapon. These practitioners devote themselves to training with a specific weapon of their choosing, rarely ever making use of other armaments.

At 2nd level, choose a weapon you are proficient in to pledge your devotion to (ex. longsword, shortbow, glaive, etc). When wielding the a weapon, the following features are made available to you. Flying Weapon​ You learn how to wield the weapon without needing to even touch it. You can use a bonus action to move the weapon up to 30 feet in any direction or teleport it back to your hand instantly. You can attack and use techniques with the weapon as if you were standing in the weapon’s space. While the weapon is being controlled in this way, it is treated as if you were still holding it (you require a free hand to attack with it, or two hands if it’s two-handed, etc). You cannot move it more than 120 feet away from yourself, and if brought outside of this range, you cannot control it further until it’s within the range. Draining Strike​ If you kill a hostile creature with an attack made with your flying weapon, you can use a reaction to drain the creature, regaining mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up). After you use this feature, you must take a short or long rest before you can use it again.

At 6th level, you become increasingly adept at using your weapon for techniques. In the same bonus action that you use to move the weapon, you can spend 1 mastery point to use the primary effect of a technique you know. Beginning at 14th level, you can focus the technique you use.

At 14th level, your control over the weapon you devoted yourself to extends even to being able to ride it. Your weapon can be ridden in the air, during which it cannot be used for techniques. It has a flying speed equal to your movement speed plus an additional 30 feet and can carry up to 500 pounds before it can no longer fly.

At 18th level, you can control two flying weapons at once, with the second not being treated as if you were holding it. If you use a bonus action to use a technique with one, the other can make a single weapon attack.

Wondrous Item, uncommon(+1), rare(+2), very rare(+3) Attunement Requires Attunement by a druid Description This carved bone or tooth charm hangs from a cord and is strung with a fragment of a hunter's totem. While you wear and are attuned to it, your natural weapon attacks gain a bonus to attack and damage rolls, determined by the talisman's rarity: Uncommon: +1 Rare: +2 Very rare: +3 A natural weapon is a bite, claw, horn, tail, slam, or similar attack granted by a creature form you've assumed. Unarmed strikes made with your fists or feet don't count. This bonus does not benefit attacks that already benefit from a bonus to unarmed strikes or other bonus to natural weapon attacks. Such an attack gets only the bonus it already has, never both. Beast's Instinct. While you're in a beast form from Wild Shape, you have advantage on initiative rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell. While you're in a beast shape from Wild Shape, the talisman remains active. It is worn as an amulet rather than as armor or clothing, so it doesn't meld into your new form.

Wondrous Item, Very Rare Attunement Requires attunement Description In this tome is inscribed 2 teleportation circles that come with it(DM discretion on which ones). Throughout your travels as you study and find new Teleportation Circles you can take 1 minute to write them in this tome in order to be able to reference them later. This book has 3 charges regaining all expended charges each day at dawn. You can use these charges to either use Teleport(1charge) or Teleportation Circle(2 charges) using any circles you have inscribed inside the codex. Flip the book to the page with the Teleportation Circle you wish to go and speak the command word.

Wondrous Item, rare Description This jar of mysterious purplish viscous goo was discovered to have exceptional insulative properties and can resist temperature changes for an extremely long time, it is often imbued with a little bit of magic to allow the user to alter the temperature of it like a cooling/heating unit Over the course of 10 minutes, a creature can apply this goo to any armor or clothing, the goo doesn't impact movement or agility at all, and after application, any creature wearing the armor or clothing ignores the effect of extreme heat and extreme cold

7th-level transmutation. (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock, College of Swords, College of Valor) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a few hairs from a bull) Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Description You endow yourself with endurance and martial prowess fueled by magic. Until the spell ends, you can't cast spells of 6th level or higher, and you gain two of the following benefits: You gain 50 temporary hit points. If any of these remain when the spell ends, they are lost. You have advantage on attack rolls that you make with simple and martial weapons. When you hit a target with a weapon attack, that target takes an extra 2d12 force damage. You have proficiency with shields, simple weapons, and martial weapons. You have proficiency in Strength and Constitution saving throws. You can attack twice, instead of once, when you take the Attack action on your - turn. You ignore this benefit if you already have a feature, like Extra Attack, that gives you extra attacks. Immediately after the spell ends, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or suffer one level of exhaustion. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, you can choose an additional effect for every level above 7th.

Powerful entities of the outer, or even inner planes often seek out mortals to do their bidding on the material plane. Sometimes, however, instead of power similar to their own, they might grant their warlocks an ability to pull creatures from other planes to an extraordinary degree.

The Extraplanar lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you. Spell Level - Spells: Sorcerer Level Spells 1st Bane, Sanctuary 2nd Arcanist's Magic Aura, Vortex Warp 3rd Bestow Curse, Glyph of Warding 4th Giant Insect, Summon Elemental 5th Creation, Summon Celestial

When you form this pact at 1st level, you are granted the ability to tether your summoned creatures to your plane, granting them additional strengths. When you cast a warlock spell that summons a single creature, you may undergo a special ritual during the casting of the spell. Doing so changes the spell's casting time to 10 minutes, and the summon lasts until it is dispelled. If the spell normally requires concentration, you may ignore the requirement. When you summon a creature in this way, it is referred to as your tether, and it gains the following benefits: You can replace its hit points with 5 x your warlock level. It adds your proficiency bonus to its damage rolls. If the creatures to-hit bonus is less than that of your spell attack bonus, it may instead use your spell attack bonus when attacking. You learn the Find Familiar spell, it counts as a warlock spell for you, and it does not count towards your total spells known. If you summon another creature using this ritual, any previous creatures summoned by it are immediately dispelled. After you complete this ritual, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

Starting at 6th level, you can briefly store items away for later use. You can cast the [Wristpocket] spell a number of times equal to your charisma modifier without expending a spell slot. When you do, the stored object is sent to the ethereal plane, and the spell does not require concentration. You regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a long rest. Additionally, you can see into the ethereal plane up to 10 ft.
At 10th level, when tether drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to expend a pact slot. Doing so will restore 50 hit points to the summon.

Starting on 14th level, while your Planar Tether summon is active, you can use an action to sacrifice part of yourself to empower it and your spells, doing so allows you to channel this ability until your next long rest, or until you end it as an action. While channeling this ability, you have the following effects: Your hit point maximum is reduced by 30. You have disadvantage on Constitution checks and saving throws, except for those made to maintain concentration. Your tether has advantage on all saving throws You can use a bonus action to give your tether temporary hit points equal to your warlock level Creatures within 10 ft of your tether have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells. If you end this ability early, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

You have forged a bond with one of the many planar lords, deities or arch-powers that reign over thieves, shadow and deception. These powerful entities blend cunning, guile and magical potential, and their agendas are often mysterious and cloaked in deceit. Whether through pact, vision, or calling, you are now their agent and weapon through which they influence the world—part thief, part warrior, part mage; the right tool used for the right job. Features: Design Notes The Masked Lord Expanded Spells 1st or 3rd Level - The Masks We Wear 6th Level - Gift of Shadow 10th Level - Cloak of Shared Burdens 14th Level - The Unseen Hand

This is intended to be a thematic and lore-accurate depiction of abilities, influences and blessings described in canon materials as being granted to various faiths, groups or members of organizations affiliated with The Masked Lord (in this case Vhaeraun-inspired)

The Masked Lord excels at adaptability, infiltration, opportunistic combat, and deceptive utility. Its three Masks allow the warlock to shift between thief, warrior, and mage, while later features turn shadow, enemy attacks, and hostile magic into tools of their own. Wear the Right Mask: Adapt your skills and tactics to the task at hand through the Masks of the Thief, Warrior, and Mage. Become the Perfect Instrument: Approach problems as an operative rather than a specialist—using stealth, weapons, magic, or cunning as circumstances demand. Turn Strength Against Its Owner: Redirect hostile attacks, steal enemy spells, and exploit aggression rather than meeting force with force. Shape the Shadows: Create useful equipment from shadowstuff and treat darkness as a tangible resource rather than simple concealment. Act Through Subtlety: Favor infiltration, positioning, preparation, deception, and precise intervention over overt displays of power. Become the Unseen Hand: Progress toward influencing the Material Plane from beyond its boundaries, acting where enemies struggle to reach you.

The subclass is ideal for players who want to: Shift Roles Easily: Move between infiltrator, combatant, investigator, and spellcaster depending on the mission. Reward Creative Problem-Solving: Use mundane tools, shadowcraft, positioning, and unusual applications of magic to overcome obstacles. Play an Arcane Operative: Blend rogue-like utility, martial capability, and warlock magic into the feel of a supernatural agent. Exploit Opportunities: React to enemy actions and changing battlefield conditions rather than relying on a single repeated tactic. Counter Enemy Magic: Capture and reuse hostile spells through Darkspell Mantle. Remain Difficult to Predict: Change your capabilities and approach so enemies cannot easily define your role or anticipate your methods.
documents.s: Who Would Thrive as a Masked Lord Warlock?

documents.t: 🎭 The Master of Masks — Enjoys changing tactics, identities, and roles to meet different challenges. 🗡️ The Shadow Operative — Favors infiltration, espionage, sabotage, and practical problem-solving. ♟️ The Tactical Opportunist — Watches the battlefield carefully and turns enemy actions into openings. 🕶️ The Arcane Counterspy — Enjoys stealing, redirecting, and exploiting hostile magic. 🌑 The Shadow Adept — Wants shadow to evolve from concealment into substance, tool, and eventually a means of transcending the Material Plane. 🦊 The Cunning Generalist — Values versatility over specialization and wants a useful answer to many different kinds of challenges. Core Philosophy: Never be limited to what others believe you are. Change the mask, change the method, and make every strength your enemy reveals another tool in your hand.

Your connection to the Masked Lord grants you access to additional spells. Spell Level Spells 1st dissonant whispers, sleep 2nd wristpocket, pass without trace 3rd fast friends, haste 4th greater invisibility, freedom of movement 5th bigbey's hand, passwall You always know these spells, and they don't count against your warlock spells known. They are warlock spells for you.

1st (2014) or 3rd (2024) Level Masked Lord Feature At the end of each Long Rest, choose one of the following Masks. Each represents a particular aspect of your Patron’s power and influence. Additionally, you can change the Mask over a 10 minute ritual where you must entreat your patron, expending a Pact Magic slot at the end. The chosen Mask grants you benefits until the end of your next Long Rest, or until you change it.
documents.s: 1st or 3rd Level - The Masks We Wear

documents.t: You embody the cunning thief—fierce, fast, and unrelenting. Skills of the Trade: You gain skill proficiency in Perception and your choice of either Thieves Tools, Stealth or Sleight of Hand (chosen each time you activate this Mask), using Charisma as your ability score for these skill checks. Practiced Hand: You can use your Bonus action on your turn to make a skill check with one of the skills or tools chosen above.

You are granted knowledge of warriors, fighters and duelists, your natural fighting instincts brought to the forefront. Warriors Insight: You gain skill proficiency in Insight and your choice of either Poisoners Kit, Athletics or Survival (chosen each time you activate this Mask), using Charisma as your ability score for these skill checks. Instinctual Movement: When you take the attack action on your turn, you may make a weapon attack as a Bonus Action

You are attuned to power and insight, the still mind of the quiet void, and the magic of shadow. Arcane Accuity: You gain skill proficiency in Investigation and your choice of either Calligrapher Tools, Arcana or History (chosen each time you activate this Mask), using Charisma as your ability score for these skill checks. Magical Momentum: When you cast a warlock spell with a pact slot that targets a creature and forces a saving throw, you can use a Bonus action to impose a 1d4 penalty to their next saving throw if you have affected them with a spell within the last round.

6th-Level Masked Lord Feature Your Masked Lord grants you deeper power over shadow, allowing you to manipulate shadowstuff to create projections that hinder your enemies: Shadowcraft: You can use your bonus action to pull wisps of shadow material from the Shadowfell to create a single Adventuring Gear based on your currently active Mask, as shown in the table below. The Gear appears within 10 feet of you and uses your Warlock spell save DC for any saving throws imposed when using the it. Each gear created disappears after 10 minute or when it has been used and effected a creature. Additionally, if you would use the Practiced Hand, Instinctual Movement, or Magical Momentum Bonus action from your active Mask, you may use one of your created Shadowcrafts instead. Mask of the Thief Mask of the Warrior Mask of the Mage Gear: Ball Bearings Gear: Net Gear: Alchemist Fire Gear: Grappling Hook Gear: Oil Gear: Acid You can use Shadowcraft twice per Short Rest, unless you expend a Pact Magic slot for each use restored (no action required).

10th-Level Masked Lord Feature Your patron blesses you with an enchanted Cloak that turns weapons and steals spells. This Cloak is a magical object that must be worn to gain its benefits, and can be used as your spellcasting focus for your warlock spells. When a creature you can see within 30 feet damages you with a weapon attack, targets you with a spell or includes you in its area of effect, you can use your reaction to produce one of the following effects: Blade Bend (Attack): You may force the attacker to make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attacker takes force damage equal to your Warlock level plus the damage it just dealt. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. You may then move up to half your speed immediately without provoking opportunity attacks. Darkspell Mantle (Spell): You can make an Arcana check against their spell save DC. If you succeed and the creature is casting a spell of 3rd level or lower, it is copied and stored in your Cloak until you finish a Long Rest. If you succeed on the check by 5 or more you can store a spell of 5th level or lower instead. While wearing the Cloak, you can cast the spell stored in it without expending a spell slot, after which the spell is gone. The spell uses your Warlock Pact Magic slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability. You can only have one spell stored in the cloak at a time, and storing another one replaces the old one without effect. If the Cloak is destroyed or you lose it, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive a replacement from your patron. This ceremony can be performed during a short or long rest, and the previous Cloak is destroyed if it still exists. The Cloak vanishes in a swirl of shadowy mist when you die. You can use each of these reactions once per Short Rest, unless you expend a Pact Magic slot for each use restored (no action required)

14th-Level Masked Lord Feature You are taught the Masked Lord's most disturbing skill, how to project your essence onto the material world even when you are not present within it. You can expend a Pact Magic slot (no action required) to gain the Masked Lord’s ethereal qualities, granting you the following benefits until the end of your next turn: You can spend up to 5ft of movement on a turn to enter the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane. While within the Border Ethereal, you are visible and partially corporeal on the Material Plane while your body remains on the Ethereal Plane, seen as a translucent and ghostly image of yourself. While in this state of corporeality, you can see and affect creatures or objects on the Material Plane as if you were in that space. You remain on the Ethereal Plane for the duration or until you use a Bonus Action on your turn to end the effect.

Wondrous Item, Legendary Description This 3-inch cube of condensed brimstone resonates slightly when touched, and generates enough dry heat to keep the temperature within 30 feet of it at 120 degrees Fahrenheit (~49 degrees Celsius). This area is subject to extreme heat.

Armor (spiked armor), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description You have a +2 bonus to AC while wearing this armor. When an attacker hits you with a melee attack, they take 1d8 magical piercing damage and can't regain hit points until the end of its next turn. Additionally, when you are grappled or restrained by a creature by making direct contact with you, they can't regain hit points until they end the condition and any damage dealt from feats or class features that does damage via grappling or being grappled counts as magical when wearing this armor.

Wondrous Item, Very Rare Description A Thought Gem is a smooth, hemispherical precious stone that swirls with the memories of past bearers While holding the gem, you can use the gem to store created thought strands (as with the Encode Thoughts spell) indefinitely, as well as recall them at a later time. It also functions as a spellbook for you, where you can retrieve and store information and spells within the gem at the same rate as reading and writing, its spells and other writing psychically encoded within it. While holding it, you become aware of the spells and thought strands stored within it, and can use it as a spellcasting focus for your spells. You can cast encode thoughts as an action, with the duration lasting until dispelled, and the thought strand disappearing into the gem. Casting this spell while focusing on a particular thought strand allows you to instantly receive whatever memory, idea, or message the thought strand contains. (Casting detect thoughts on the Thought Gem has the same effect, but the thought strand is determined at random unless using the deeper probe option of the spell.)

Weapon (maul), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit with a melee attack using this weapon, it deals an extra 1d6 damage. In addition, the weapon ignores resistance to bludgeoning damage. Attack rolls made with this weapon can't be hindered with spells and magical effects that increase the target's Armor Class except for the Haste spell(i.e. A target won't benefit from the bonus to AC from a Shield spell or Mage Armor spell against this magic weapon's attack rolls) as well as ignoring the magic bonuses of magical items. When your attack roll is a critical hit, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn.

weapon (maul), very rare Attunement: Creature with minimum 15 Strength Description This weapon was once wielded by the Thunderlord's an ancient paladin order that delivered swift and thunderous justice to those who opposed order. Only the strongest of the Thunderlord's could wield this large hammer. It glows a deep electric blue, has runes that say "Thunderous Wrath". The head of the maul is shaped like a large thundercloud and appears to have a deep blue flashes across the head as if it trapped a thunderbolt waiting to be released. Thunderlord's Might This weapon has a +1 to attack and damage rolls. And once per turn when you hit a creature this weapon deals an additional 2d8 Thunder damage the creature suffers the weapons normal effect, and it then becomes sheathed in booming energy until the start of your next turn. The first time it willingly moves 5 feet or more before then the target takes 3d8 thunder damage is not sheathed in energy anymore. Thunderlord's Decree This weapon has 8 charges. You can use 4 charges to cast lightning bolt as an action. You can use 2 charges to cast Thunderwave as an action. You regain 1d6+2 charges at dawn.

Weapon (maul, lucerne hammer, or warhammer), legendary armament Attunement Requires Attunement Favor Table: Yes Questable: Yes Craftable: Yes Description You gain a bonus of +3 to attack and damage rolls made using this weapon. 10 charges that recharge by 2d4+2 charges at dawn. This items Spell Save DC is 18 for the various spells it casts. You can use an action to cast the following spells expending a number of charges as the spells dictate using this items Spell Save DC, Lightning Bolt (2 charges 3rd level), Thunder Step (3 charges 3rd level), Destructive Wave (5 charges 5th level).

weapon (maul), very rare Attunement: Creature with minimum 15 Strength Description This weapon was once wielded by the Thunderlord's an ancient paladin order that delivered swift and thunderous justice to those who opposed order. Only the strongest of the Thunderlord's could wield this large hammer. It glows a deep electric blue, has runes that say "Thunderous Wrath". The head of the maul is shaped like a large thundercloud and appears to have a deep blue flashes across the head as if it trapped a thunderbolt waiting to be released. Thunderlord's Might This weapon has a +1 to attack and damage rolls. And once per turn when you hit a creature this weapon deals an additional 2d8 Thunder damage the creature suffers the weapons normal effect, and it then becomes sheathed in booming energy until the start of your next turn. The first time it willingly moves 5 feet or more before then the target takes 3d8 thunder damage is not sheathed in energy anymore. Thunderlord's Decree This weapon has 8 charges. You can use 4 charges to cast lightning bolt as an action. You can use 2 charges to cast Thunderwave as an action. You regain 1d6+2 charges at dawn.

Weapon (musket), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Thunderstrike Musket Description This magical musket is imbued with the essence of thunder and has the following properties when attuned: Thunderous Blast: On a critical hit, the weapon releases a powerful blast, dealing additional 2d6 thunder damage to the target and all creatures within a 10-foot radius of the target. The affected creatures must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be pushed back 10 feet. Deafening Shot: Once per day, the weapon can be loaded with a Deafening Shot. The next time you make an attack with this weapon, on a hit, it unleashes a concussive blast that creates a 20-foot radius sphere of silence centered on the target, that functions similar to a silence spell for 1 minute and requires the shooter to hold concentration. The sphere moves with the target.

Weapon (rapier), questable; uncraftable, legendary (requires attunement by an Eloquence Bard) Description You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this magic weapon. Tidepiercer is a spellcasting focus for you. Sapphire Ferocity You can add your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage rolls of attacks you make with this weapon. This bonus is in addition to the normal ability modifier you add to the damage roll. It applies to each attack you make with Tidepiercer (including opportunity attacks), but not to damage dealt by spells. Ribbon of the Pearl While attuned, you always know the direction and distance to the nearest coastline. Once per dawn, spend 10 minutes using Tidepiercer to cast augury without material components; the omen appears as foam-light along the blade. Sapphire Refrain You can weave brief, tide-kissed refrains into your inspiration. A number of times per short or long rest equal to your proficiency bonus, when a creature you can see rolls your Bardic Inspiration die or when you expend a die with Unsettling Words, you can invoke one of the following effects (no action): Seafoam Step. The inspired creature may move up to 10 feet. This movement can provoke opportunity attacks as normal. Brineguard. The inspired creature regains hit points equal to double your proficiency bonus. Clear the Wake. The inspired creature may end the charmed or frightened condition on itself. Undercurrent (Unsettling Words only). If the trigger was your Unsettling Words, you may instead choose the target of Unsettling Words. That creature can’t make opportunity attacks until the start of your next turn.

Wondrous Item, common Description What appears to be a typical paperweight has an innate magical quality to it, which is invoked when the paperweight is first touched by someone. When spun by the linked owner of the paperweight, it always loses momentum after exactly 6 seconds. If anyone other than the linked owner spins it the totem continues spinning until an outside force inhibits it.

Armor(Shield) 50 gp, 20lbs - AC +0 Also known as a Scutum, the tower shield is a large piece of curved metal or wood, or a composite of both. It is the size of it's user, too big and it is unwieldy if not impossible to use, and too small it becomes ineffective. The shield confers no AC bonus to it's user by default. Instead it grants a damage threshold to you and creatures that you are providing cover for, so long as they are the same size or smaller than the shield. The damage threshold equals your strength modifier, plus your proficiency bonus when wielded with one hand, or twice your strength modifier plus your proficiency bonus when wielded with two. The damage threshold increases for each allied tower shield wielder within 5 feet, adding up to two of their proficiency bonuses to the damage threshold. A creature with a strength score less than 13 has their speed lowered by 10 feet while wielding a tower shield. This shield cannot be used as a base for an animated shield.

2nd-level evocation. (Artificer, Druid, Ranger, Sorcerer, Wizard, Arcane Domain) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 120 feet Components: V, S, M (a tiny metal spike) Duration: 1 minute Description You shoot a thin toxic spike at a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. If it hits, the target takes 2d8 poison damage, and the spike is lodged in the creature’s body. At the start of each of the creature’s turns while the spike is embedded in the creature, the target takes 1d6 poison damage. The target may use their action to pull the spike out, after which the spell ends. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the initial damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd and the subsequent damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 2nd.

Wondrous Item, Common Description This small and lovingly hand-made bookmark comes in all shapes and sizes, but is perfect for any bookworms that need to keep track of their spot while perusing through thick tomes. Upon speaking a command word and flipping open the book, the tome the bookmark carries will magically adjust and flip directly to the marked page. Each tome can only contain one bookmark at a time.

8th-level conjuration. (College of Creation, Sorcerer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 hour Range: 100 feet Components: V, S, M (1,000 gp worth of Residuum or any Arcane Dust/Powder) Duration: 24 hours Description You magically expand the dimensions of an existing container, room, or otherwise fully enclosed space beyond its physical limits. Select an existing physical space (no larger than 125 sq ft.) with at most one single point of entry such as a lid, door, window or flap, (no larger than 10 sq ft), and with a solid border (no transparent walls, windows, etc.). As a part of this spell, the caster must inscribe runes around the opening and the borders of the space to maintain its external structure. The interior dimensions of that space expand by up to 5 feet in any direction that you choose as the spell takes effect, warping to accommodate any items or creatures inside. When the spell ends, the space returns to its normal size and any items or occupants unable to fit in the original space are softly ejected through the opening. If there is no opening or the objects cannot fit through it, the items or creatures are scattered randomly in the Astral Plane as determined by the GM. Casting this spell in the same space every day for 30 days makes the effect permanent; further castings can be used to expand an existing Transdimensional Space beyond its size provided that it still has a single exterior border with no more than one point of entry.

Wondrous Item, rare Description This delicate pin, shaped like a golden treble clef, serves as a pocket instrument storage device perfect for any musician. Storing an Instrument As an action, you can touch any handheld musical instrument to the pin. The instrument vanishes, stored within a pocket dimension contained by the pin. The pin's weight doesn't change, regardless of what's stored inside. Retrieving an Instrument As an action, you can tap the pin twice to summon the stored instrument. It appears in your hands immediately. If you don't have free hands, the instrument falls at your feet. Storage Limit The pin can only hold one item at a time. If you attempt to store a second instrument while one is already stored, nothing happens. Pocket Dimension Access Only you can retrieve items from the pin—others cannot summon stored instruments from it, though they could damage or destroy the pin itself to potentially recover its contents.

Wondrous item, uncommon Description While wearing this ear cuff, you can add half your proficiency bonus to any ability check you make to play an instrument if you aren't proficient with it. In addition, you can magically discern (and consequently recreate) the note of any sound you hear.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Attunement Requires Attunement Description Ostensibly an ordinary playing card, though imbued with a subtle illusion magic. One attuned with it can, with intent, tap the back of the card to change its number or suit. A single-fingered tap iterates the number by one, a tap with two fingers alternates between the four suits, and a tap with three fingers changes the design of the card to match any other card it touches.

Weapon (Any Simple or Martial Melee Weapon), common Description As an action while touching this weapon, you can transform it into a mundane item or back into its weapon form. It can't be used to make attacks while transformed into a mundane item. Different weapons look like different items, and the item a particular Trick Weapon transforms into cannot be changed.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This item generates an aura of magical freshness by keeping the air in a 10ft by 10ft cube centered on the trinket clean, you can use an action to change what the aura smells like. Food and other perishables do not decay while in the aura generated by the trinket.

The True Path requires the constant repetition of martial forms until absolute perfection is achieved. With perfection comes “truth”, an aspect of life that such practitioners would consider their peak.

At 2nd level, you learn the True Strike cantrip and can cast it as a bonus action. When you cast it, you gain its benefits on the current turn rather than the next turn, and it doesn’t require concentration for you. The spell ends at the end of your turn. Once per short or long rest, if you kill a hostile creature affected by True Strike, you can use your reaction to regain mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up).

At 6th level, when you strike true, you can bypass the defenses of your enemies. A technique’s attack that has advantage due to True Strike’s effect ignores an enemy’s resistances. At 18th level, such an enemy’s damage immunities are treated as resistances (which cannot be ignored).
At 14th level, when you cast true strike on a target, you can learn their resistances, immunities, and current hit points. Additionally, you gain advantage on insight checks against the target.

At 18th level, you can analyze the intrinsic truth about a creature. When you cast True Strike, you can spend 1 mastery point to give your next technique’s attack a +10 bonus to the attack roll and have the creature make their next save against the technique with disadvantage.

Wondrous item, uncommon Description This drab pair of empty ceramic cylinders are magically linked. Each vessel is 3 inches in diameter and one foot tall. Opening one of the vessel's lids and placing an item inside will magically teleport it to the second tube, making a quiet whoosh sound when it does. A very quiet thud can be heard when receiving an item. A tube cannot hold more than 2 pounds of materials at any time, and both lids must be closed for the items to be teleported. Items can only be sent if the two tubes are on the same plane of existence. A creature cannot be sent through the tubes. Only one tube must be empty, or else nothing occurs. The tubes must be within a 30 mile radius of one another. You can only use this property once per day, which refreshes at dawn.

Wondrous Item, rare Requires proficiency with at least one instrument to use Description Taking inspiration from an Earring of Message and a pair of Sending Stones, these metallic earcuffs are enchanted with evocation magic to recreate sounds or melodies from memory. This item has charges equal to your proficiency bonus that reset on a long rest: with an action, you can expend one charge to cause song familiar to you to play at a volume that is only audible to you. The song plays until completion in which the cuffs deactivate, requiring another charge to repeat the song or play a new one. You have disadvantage on perception checks related to hearing while this item is activated.

Wearing heavy armors tends to take immense physical strain, and as such usually restricts the movements of the wearer. Bulwarks who call themselves Unfettered work tirelessly to be just as, if not more efficient with their movements while donning these heavy suits. Features: 3rd Level - Heightened Agility 3rd Level - Armored Movement 7th Level - Iron Fist 13th Level - Quaking Vault 18th Level - Weightless Steel

At 3rd level when you select this specialization, you learn to move with better flow while wearing heavy armor. It weighs half as much to you, and it does not apply disadvantage on your dexterity (stealth) checks.
Additionally at 3rd level, you learn to move yourself with considerable speed for being weighed down. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet, and increases by another 10 feet at 18th level.

At 7th level, your movements are swift and fluid enough to carry the full force of your armor with them. When you make an unarmed attack while wearing heavy armor, you can choose to treat it as being a weapon with the heavy property, and you can roll a d8 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed attacks.

Starting at 13th level, your poise and agility work in conjunction to make landing less deadly to you, and more so to those around you. You become resistant to falling damage while wearing heavy armor, and landing no longer knocks you prone. When you land while wearing heavy armor, creatures within 15 feet of you take 2d10 bludgeoning damage, and must succeed on a strength saving throw (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be knocked prone. A creature can only be affected by this ability once per turn.

At 18th level, heavy armor ceases to be a burden for you in any meaningful way. Heavy armor weighs nothing to you while you are wearing it, and you may treat it as if it were medium armor for the purposes of adding your dexterity modifier to your armor class.

Weapon (any melee weapon), rare Attunement Requires Attunement Description You can use a bonus action to speak this magic weapon's command word, causing flames to erupt from it. These flames shed bright light in a 40-foot radius and dim light for an additional 40 feet. While the weapon is ablaze, it deals an extra 2d6 fire damage to any target it hits with a melee weapon attack. The flames last until you use a bonus action to speak the command word again or until you drop or sheathe the weapon.

Verdant Breastplate Armor (breastplate), Rare Attunement Requires attunement. Description When found, this breastplate resembles a leather cuirass covered in large, dried leaves. Once you wear and attune to it, however, it springs to life and flourishes; its leaves remain pliable and flexible, but harden against incoming harm to protect you. Sleeping in this armor has no adverse effect on you. While wearing this armor, moving through nonmagical plants that impede movement (such as by creating difficult terrain) costs you no extra movement, and you don’t take damage from nonmagical plant hazards such as thorns or spines. In addition, the “entangle” spell has no effect on you, and you have advantage on any Dexterity (Stealth) check you make to hide in areas of dense foliage. 𝘾𝙝𝙖𝙧𝙜𝙚𝙨. This armor has 7 charges and regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you’re a druid or ranger and have cast the “plant growth” spell from the armor within the last 24 hours, the armor regains all expended charges instead. 𝙎𝙥𝙚𝙡𝙡𝙨. While wearing this armor, you can use an action to expend some of its charges to cast either the “entangle” (1 charges) or “plant growth” (3 charges) spell from it, using a spell save DC of 15. If you’re a druid or ranger, you can choose to cast the spell from the armor using your spell save DC instead. When you cast “plant growth” using this armor, the plants affected by the spell are enriched for 30 days. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested.

Wonderous Item, common Attunement Optional Description While attuned to a this ornate chain, you may alter it's shape as an action. The chain may be coaxed into a bracelet, necklace, earring, or similar jewelry so long as its total length is no more than 18". As part of the same action used to change the chains shape, jewels ,charms or other trinkets may be fixed to the chain, which reshapes to form custom settings as desired. The chain may be reshaped indefinitely, so long as it does not reach a total length of more than 18" - 1" /per attached trinket.

evocation cantrip. (Artificer, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard, Arcane Domain) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 10 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous Description With an upward flourish of your hand, a splash of poisonous venom is released from your hand into the face of a creature in range. The targeted creature must make a Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 poison damage and be blinded until the start of your next turn on a failed save. The spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

Ring, common Vial Ring Description This ring is made of magic glass (That cannot be broken in ring-form) and has a cork stopper at its top like a set gemstone. You can unstopper the ring (no action required) to magically transform it into a small glass vial. The vial holds up to 1 ounce of liquid. The mouth of the vial and ring are both a half inch wide, allowing the cork to remain the same size even when the ring is transformed. When the vial is stoppered, it magically returns to its ring form. Anything contained by the vial magically fits within the ring while it's transformed. While the ring itself is magical, the cork is not. Any cork of the right size can be used to stopper the ring or vial, allowing you to mark the corks as needed or replace them, should they become lost or destroyed by acid or other similar hazardous (albeit bottleable) materials.

3rd-level evocation. (Artificer, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard, Arcane Domain) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, S, M (a splash of weak poison) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description You attempt infect a creature nearby with a nasty strain of poison. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw or take 3d8 poison damage and be infected. An infected creature is poisoned and takes an additional 2d8 poison damage at the start of each of their turns. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much poison damage and is not infected. The spell has no effect on creatures immune to the poisoned condition. When an infected creature dies, they explode in a poisonous burst. Each creature within 5 feet of the infected creature when it dies must roll a constitution saving throw or be infected as well, suffering the full effects of the spell. At the end of each of each infected creature’s turns until the spell ends, they can make another Constitution saving throw. On a success, the spell ends for that creature. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the initial damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Wondrous Item, uncommon Description This hand-held leather pouch of multi-colored gumdrops can be made in batches of 1d10+5 candies at a time. When ingesting one of these gumdrops, your vocal qualities are enhanced. You gain advantage on performance checks involving vocals for 10 minutes. However, if you ingest more than one gumdrop at a time, you lose your voice for 10 minutes instead.

Voidknight’s Maul Weapon (Maul), very rare Attunement Requires attunement by a Paladin Description The crystalline head of this magic hammer has been bathed in the latent magic of the Astral Plane. While you remain attuned to it, you age at one-tenth your normal rate. 𝘼𝙨𝙩𝙧𝙖𝙡 𝙎𝙢𝙞𝙩𝙚. Whenever you use your Divine Smite feature against a creature, you can choose for it to deal psychic damage instead of radiant damage. Furthermore, when you expend a spell slot of 2nd level or higher to use your Divine Smite, you can force the target of the attack to make a Constitution saving throw against your paladin spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature is affected by the “levitate” spell. This version of the spell can affect multiple creatures at once, though you must still concentrate on the spell as normal. If your concentration on the spell ends, any affected creature gently floats back to the ground. Otherwise, you can use your action to move one or multiple targets affected by the spell vertically, up to 20 feet, dividing the movement between them. Each affected creature must remain within the spell’s range

Weapon (any melee weapon that deals slashing damage), legendary Attunement Requires Attunement Description You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, the weapon ignores resistance to slashing damage. When you attack a creature that has at least one head with this weapon and roll a 20 on the attack roll, you cut off one of the creature's heads. The creature dies if it can't survive without the lost head. A creature is immune to this effect if it is immune to slashing damage, doesn't have or need a head, has legendary actions, or the GM decides that the creature is too big for its head to be cut off with this weapon. Such a creature instead takes an extra 6d8 slashing damage from the hit.

Armor (plate), legendary Attunement Warmog's Armor Requires Attunement Description You have a +2 bonus to AC while wearing this armor. While you don this armor, your hit point maximum increases by 30. You regain 10 hit points at the start of your turn. If you take damage, this feature doesn't function at the start of your next turn.

Armor (plate), legendary Attunement Warmog's Armor Requires Attunement Description You have a +2 bonus to AC while wearing this armor. While you don this armor, your hit point maximum increases by 30. You regain 10 hit points at the start of your turn. If you take damage, this feature doesn't function at the start of your next turn.
Weapon (Any), Legendary You have a +4 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
Weapon (Any), Legendary You have a +4 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
Weapon (any weapon with the range or thrown property), uncommon Description When you make an attack with this weapon, the short and long range is doubled.

Weapon (whip), uncommon Description If you roll a 20 on an attack roll against a creature you can choose to automatically grapple the creature. A creature grappled in this way is restrained. While grappling a creature with this whip the wielder can’t move further than the reach of the whip from the creature, and can't attack with the whip, without releasing the grapple(takes no action). A creature grappled in this way can use an action to make a strength (Athletics) or dexterity (acrobatics) check with a DC 13 to break the grapple.

Wondrous Item, common Description This carefully constructed automaton was constructed in the image of a Phoenix. When you speak the command word, small illusory flames spring to life within its empty eye sockets and the gears begin to turn, causing the small mechanical bird to fly around the speaker in circles and occasionally perch on their shoulder. This effect end if the distance between the toy and its owner is 25 feet or greater. Inscribed on one wing of this bird is the ornate depiction of a tiny smoldering Phoenix egg, a signature left there by the toy's designer.

Wondrous item, uncommon Description This silk kite (colors, shape, etc. are customizable) is 5 feet across and is attached to a 60-foot string. It weighs 1 pound, can carry up to one pound in weight, and can be folded into a 6-inch square. While holding the kite, you can use a bonus action to toss it aloft and speak its command word. When you do, you also choose how much string to let out, between 10 to 60 feet. The kite then expands to its full size (if it was folded) and creates a cylinder of moderate wind of 10 miles per hour, which allows it to continue flying. The cylinder's height and diameter is the same as the amount of let-out string, up to 60 feet. The kite and top of the cylinder remain centered above your location. You can use another bonus action to speak the flying kite's command word to end the effect and cause it to fall softly back into your hand. You can change the wind's direction at the start of each of your turns for the duration. You can use the kite to create this wind for up to 1 hour, all at once or in several shorter intervals, each one using a minimum of 1 minute from the duration. The effect ends early if you are no longer holding the string, at which point it flies up to 1d10 times 10 feet in a random direction before landing on the ground. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the string (AC 15) severs the string, causing the kite to fly away as if you let go of the string. The severed string can later be reattached by holding its ends together for 1 minute.

1st-level necromancy. (Paladin) Meta Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description Your weapon radiates terrible energy that empowers the next strike you make with it. The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack during this spell’s duration, your attack deals an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. If the target of that attack was a creature, it must make a successful Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute, its flesh rotting around the wound. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The rotting effect also ends if the affected creature receives magical healing. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage dealt by the weapon’s hit increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st. Subsequent necrotic damage doesn’t increase.
Fight Side by Side with a Brawler’s Best Friend

You summon and form a bond with a wild or stray dog, which draws strength from your bottomless well of resilience using the Hound stat block. The Hound in Combat: In combat, the hound acts during your turn. It can move and use its Reaction on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action unless you take a Bonus Action to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to command the hound to take the Bite action. If you have the Incapacitated condition, the hound acts on its own and isn’t limited to the Dodge action. Restoring or Replacing the Hound: If the hound died within the last hour, you can take a Magic action to touch it and expend 2 Moxie Points. The hound returns to life after 1 minute with all its Hit Points restored. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can summon and bond with a new dog, which appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

Medium Beast, Neutral Armor Class: 12 + your Constitution modifier + your Proficiency Bonus Hit Points: 20 + 10 times your Pugilist Level. (Additionally, the Hound gains 1 Hit Die d8for every point of your Prestige Level. Speed: 40 ft. Resistances: The Hound shares your Iron Chin feature, gaining the same damage resistances you possess. STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 18 (+4) 14 (+2) 18 (+4) 3 (-4) 12 (+1) 13 (+1) Saving Throws: STR + (4 + PB), DEX +(2 + PB), CON +(4 + PB). Senses: Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 11. Traits: Pack Bond: Add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check the beast makes. Actions: Bite: Melee Attack Roll: Bonus equals your Constitution modifier plus your PB, reach 5 ft. Hit: $2 \times (\text{your Fisticuffs Die}) + \text{your Constitution modifier}$ Piercing or Force damage. If the target is a creature Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC equals your Pugilist Save DC) or suffer one of the following: the target is Grappled, Prone, or pushed 10 feet away.

You share everything with your faithful hound. When you use abilities granted by your Moxie feature, your hound gains a benefit as well: Brace Up: When you gain Temporary Hit Points from your Brace Up ability, your hound gains the same number of Temporary Hit Points. One-Two Punch: When you use your One-Two Punch ability, your hound can make one or both attacks instead of you. Stick and Move: When you use your Stick and Move ability, your hound can take your choice of the Dash, Disengage, or Help action.

When you make an attack against a creature and your hound is within 5 feet of it, your hound can take a Reaction to give your attack Advantage. On a hit, you deal an extra 4d8 damage. Additionally, the hound's Bite and this extra damage can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

When a creature deals damage to your hound with an attack, you can take a Reaction to move up to your full Speed toward that creature and make one melee attack with a Pugilist weapon or an Unarmed Strike against it. If this attack hits, the target has Disadvantage on all attack rolls against the hound until the end of your next turn.

When your hound takes damage that causes it to become Bloodied or takes damage while it is Bloodied, you can use your Reaction to let your hound off the chain. For the next minute, the hound gains the following benefits: It gains Temporary Hit Points equal to five times your Prestige Level. Its Speed increases by 20 feet. You can command it to use its Bite action as a Free Action on your turn (no Bonus Action or Attack sacrifice required). Its Bite deals an additional 2d10 Force damage. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. Because Moxie does not recover on a Short Rest, you may restore your use of this feature by expending 8 Moxie Points (no action required).

Martial Ranged Weapon 1000gp, 18lbs - 1 fire - Ranged (60/180), Two-handed, Battery 2, Special Description An unstable device that outputs a staggering amount of energy the longer it remains active. Special: The weapon's damage cannot be modified by your ability modifier, or any other bonus provided by items, spells, or class features. However, for each consecutive hit against the same target, the weapon's damage doubles. This effect resets if an attack from this weapon misses, you attack a different target, or you do not attack with this weapon on your turn. Additionally, attacks made with this weapon automatically hit objects that are not being worn or carried. Battery X: A weapon with the Battery property can be safely fired a number of times equal to its battery score per round, so long as it contains a functional focusing crystal. Attacking more times in a round than the weapon's battery score allows will destroy its focusing crystal at the start of your next turn.

Heavy weapon and Burst specialist. Battlefield suppression role. Features: Level 3 – Heavy Weapons Training Level 7 – Suppressive Burst Level 13 – Battle Conditioning Level 17 – Battlefield Devastator
You gain proficiency in Heavy Armor. You add half your ability modifier to Volatile weapon damage. You cannot add this bonus to weapons with the Automatic Property.
When you use a weapon’s Burst property, any creature hit must succeed on a Con save using your Called Shot DC or have the frightened condition until the end of your next turn.
As a bonus action you may spend up to your entire pool of Grit, you gain temporary HP equal to 5 times the amount of Grit you spent. This temporary HP lasts until you short rest.

You can enter this state as a bonus action. You can spend 3 Grit to restore your use of this ability. Once per long rest, for 1 minute: You gain resistance to piercing, bludgeoning, and slashing damage. Your firearm weapons gain a bonus to hit equal to half your Strength modifier. Called Shots now cost one less to use down to a minimum of 0.

Wondrous Common Description The Audioshard is the audio version of the Spellshard. As an action, the user can activate the shard which allows it to store sound up to a max of 10 ft away, determined whenever the user activates the shard. The shard can store up to 40 hours of audio. The user can also take an action to play any recorded audio which can be played at a volume ranging from a whisper to a scream. *Artisans Guild invention

Weapon: Simple, Melee 1gp, 2 lbs. --- 1d4 slashing - light, two-handed Description Proficiency with a cestus allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special: As a bonus action, you can make one attack with this weapon.

Casting Time: 1 Action Range: Self; 10 ft cubes Components: S, M (a citrus fruit) Duration: concentration up to 1 minute A viscous and caustic substance spills out across eight 10 foot cubes, which you can arrange as you wish. Each cube must have at least one face adjacent to the face of another cube. Each creature in the area when the spill appears must make a dexterity saving throw or take 6d4 acid damage. After which the spill settles, making the spell's area difficult terrain. For the remainder of the spell's duration, the first time a creature enters the spill on their turn, or starts their turn in the spill, they take 6d4 acid damage. A creature also takes 2d4 acid damage for every 5 feet they move through the spill.

Weapon: Simple, Melee 1gp, 1.5 lbs. --- 1d4 bludgeoning - light, two-handed Description Proficiency with a cestus allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special: As a bonus action, you can make one attack with this weapon.

Weapon: ( Martial, Melee) 30gp, 3lbs. --- d4 slashing - finesse, light, thrown (10/30), Description Proficiency with a chakram allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. On a missed throw, a chakram returns to the thrower's hand. Finesse: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. Light: A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons. Thrown: If a weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack. If the weapon is a melee weapon, you use the same ability modifier for that attack roll and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon. For example, if you throw a handaxe, you use your Strength, but if you throw a dagger, you can use either your Strength or your Dexterity, since the dagger has the finesse property.

Druids of the Circle of Beauty vow to protect all that brings beauty in nature. From the patterns of symmetry designed to attract mates, to visual marks designed to confuse camouflage observers, these are all sights that should be admired and emulated. They marvel at how nature seamlessly blends together both form and function in a way man-made objects never could. Features: 2nd Level - Circle Spells 2nd Level - Natural Form 6th Level - Blessing of Symmetry 10th Level - Beautiful Plummage 14th Level - Radiant Appearance

Your eye for all things visually harmonious grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Beauty Spells table. Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you. Druid Level Spell 2nd disguise self, feather fall 3rd healing spirit, lesser restoration 5th daylight, hypnotic pattern 7th charm monster, compulsion 9th creation, dawn

As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Wild Shape feature to draw upon nature's splendour, rather than assuming a Beast form. While in your natural form and wearing no armour, your Armour Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit. The form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), if you die, or you use this feature again. Whenever you assume your natural form, choose the manner of natural appearance your body transforms into; your choice gives you certain benefits while in the form. Attractive. When you enter this form, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns while in this form, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you until the start of your next turn. The target automatically succeeds on its saving throw if it can't see you. It stops being charmed by you if it is attacked or damaged, or if another creature shakes it awake as a bonus action. Camouflage. You can take the Hide action as a bonus action. You can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, and other natural phenomena. Verdant. When you enter this form, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns, you can choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you (including yourself). That creature gains your Wisdom modifier temporary hit points, which lasts until the start of your next turn.

6th-level Circle of Beauty feature You strive to emulate the symmetry that occurs in the natural world. When you or a willing creature you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell with a casting time of 1 action and which deals damage to at least one target, the caster can forgo rolling damage dice and take the average damage. If the spell has an ongoing effect that can deal damage after it is cast, this feature only applies to the initial instance of damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

The transformation into your natural form is now even more stunning. Your forms gain extra benefits as detailed below: Attractive. When you charm a creature, you can command it as part of the same bonus action to use its reaction to move up to its speed and make one weapon attack against a target you can see. After the creature completes this command, it is no longer charmed by you. Camouflage. When you use the Hide action and are also obscured by natural foliage or phenomena, you become invisible until you move away from the natural foliage, or until you make an attack or cast a spell. Verdant. The you roll is now a when you give temporary hit points. While a creature has these temporary hit points, it has a bonus to AC and advantage on Constitution saving throws. Moreover, at the start of each of your turns while in your Natural Form, you can change the appearance of your form. If you do, any effects from your previous form immediately end.

Your body's aesthetically pleasing patterns and colours make others hesitate to harm you. When a creature makes an attack roll against you while in your Natural Form, you can use your reaction and force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature can't attack you with an attack or harmful spell until the end of its current turn, and must choose a new target or lose the attack or spell (this doesn't protect you from area effects, such as the explosion of15 a fireball). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Druids of the Circle of the Verdant Stalker embody the lethal stillness and precision of Chult’s jungles. They move like serpents through the undergrowth, striking with poison and vanishing into foliage. Features: 3rd Level - Circle Spells 3rd Level - Venomous Marksman 6th Level - Aspect of the Striking Viper 10th Level - Primal Toxin Mastery 14th Level - Deathbloom Aspect

Your eye for all things visually harmonious grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Beauty Spells table. Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you. Druid Level Spell 3rd Ensnaring Strike, Poison Spray 5th Plant Growth, Spike Growth 7th Grasping Vine, Stoneskin 9th Tree Stride, Cloudkill (reflavored as a deadly plant toxin cloud)

Your training centers on the precision and toxins of Chult’s hidden hunters. Blowgun Proficiency. You gain proficiency with the blowgun. You can use your Wisdom modifier instead of Dexterity for blowgun attack and damage rolls. Toxin-Enhanced Blowgun. Your blowgun darts deal greater piercing damage as you grow in mastery. Druid Level Blowgun Damage Die 3rd 1d6 10th 1d8 14th 1d10 Poisoner’s Tools. You gain proficiency with the Poisoner’s Kit. Tough to Toxin. You have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against being poisoned. Jungle Stride. You ignore nonmagical plant-based difficult terrain.

You channel primal ferocity into a deadly, focused trance. Activation. As a bonus action, expend one use of your Wild Shape to enter this Aspect for 1 minute. You can’t activate it again until you finish a short or long rest. While in this Aspect: Your blowgun attacks deal an extra 1d8 poison damage. When you take the attack action to attack with your blowgun, hit or miss, you can make another attack with the blowgun. If your first blowgun attack each turn hits, the target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC = your spell save DC) or be Poisoned until the end of its next turn.
