A creature that fails this saving throw also takes an additional 1d8 poison damage.
documents.s: 6th Level - Aspect of the Striking Viper

documents.t: Your venoms pierce the resilience of even the hardiest foes. Toxic Bypass. Your blowgun attacks and druid spells that deal poison damage treat immunity to poison damage as resistance instead. Debilitating Barrage. When you hit a creature that is Poisoned, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = your spell save DC). On a failed save, it is Blinded until the end of its next turn. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Your mastery of venom and motion refines your Aspect of the Striking Viper into the Deathbloom Aspect. When you activate your Aspect of the Striking Viper, it gains the following additional benefits: Deadly Venoms. Your extra poison damage increases to 1d10, and creatures make their Constitution saving throws against your poison with disadvantage. Viper’s Retreat. Immediately after you hit a creature with a blowgun attack, you can move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks from that creature. Predator’s Cunning. While the Aspect is active, you can take the Hide or Disengage action as a bonus action. You can also attempt to Hide even when you are only partially obscured by natural terrain, foliage, or dim light. Toxic Perfection. You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

Weapon: Martial, Melee 5gp, 1 lbs. --- 1d4 Slashing - Finesse, Light, Nick Finesse: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. Light: A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons. Special: Claw Caps can be fitted over a creature's natural weapons as an action changing it's base statistics and properties to match that of the natural weapon it is fitted over, it then gains a new weapon mastery depending on the natural weapon's damage type: Bludgeoning: Topple Piercing: Sap Slashing: Vex Natural Weapons with Claw Caps cannot be used to make unarmed strikes.

Uncommon, Wondrous Description A swirling cloud sealed within a small glass bottle. While a Cloud in a Bottle is on your person, you gain the ability to jump while mid-air. Additionally, you can treat your long and high jumps as if you had moved 10 feet before doing so, even if you didn't. Once you jump in this way, you cannot do so again until you land on the ground.

Martial Ranged Weapon 1,000gp, 12lbs - 1d12 lightning - Ranged (15), Two-handed, Battery (2), Special, Sap Description Fitted with two large metal beams coiled in conductive material, this machine fires concentrated bursts of electrical magic in a wide area. Special: When you attack with this weapon, target each creature in a cone of a length equal to its range. Each target takes the weapon's normal damage. Additionally, if you attack with this weapon past the normal safe amount its Battery would allow, double the weapon's damage and range. The focusing crystal is then immediately destroyed, rather than at the start of your next turn. Battery X: A weapon with the Battery property can be safely fired a number of times equal to its battery score per round, so long as it contains a functional focusing crystal. Attacking more times in a round than the weapon's battery score allows will destroy its focusing crystal at the start of your next turn.

Inspire Allies with Primal Tales The College of the Moon traces its origins to the ancient druidic circles of the Moonshae Isles, who entrusted the first Bards of this tradition with chronicling the stories of the islands and their people. Bards of this college draw from the isles’ Fey magic and the primal power of the moonwells to bolster their allies, protect the natural world, and inspire their bardic works. Such works tend to be based on well-known Moonshae myths such as the whimsy of fairy pranksters, the viciousness of the Beast, and the mysteries of the moonwells. Features: 3rd Level - Moonshae Folktales 3rd Level - Primal Lorist 6th Level - Blessing of the Moonwells 14th Level - Bolstered Folktales

As a Magic action, you can invoke the power of a folktale, imbuing yourself with primal magic until you use this feature again. When you use this feature, choose which of the following folktales you invoke; your choice gives you benefits while this magic is active. Tale of Life. You invoke a tale of vitality and thriving earth. When you restore Hit Points to a creature with a spell, you can expend a Bardic Inspiration die and increase the amount of Hit Points restored by a number equal to a roll of the Bardic Inspiration die. You can do this only once per turn. Tale of Gloam. You invoke a tale of mystery and secrets. When you use a Bonus Action to give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can take the Disengage or Hide action as part of that Bonus Action. Tale of Mirth. You invoke a tale of merriment and fey guile. When an enemy you can see within 60 feet of yourself succeeds on a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to expend a Bardic Inspiration die. The creature then must roll the Bardic Inspiration die and subtract the number rolled from the save’s total, possibly causing the save to fail.

You learn Druidic and one cantrip from the Druid spell list. It counts as a Bard spell for you but doesn’t count against the number of cantrips you know. Additionally, choose one of the following skills: Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, or Survival. You have proficiency in that skill.

You always have the Moonbeam spell prepared. As a Bonus Action, you can cast Moonbeam without expending a spell slot. When you cast it using this feature, you glow faintly while you maintain Concentration on the spell. While glowing, you shed Dim Light out to 5 feet, and whenever a creature fails its saving throw against the effects of this Moonbeam, another creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you regains 2d4 Hit Points. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

The power of your Moonshae Folktales improves. When you use your Tale of Life or Tale of Mirth, you can roll 1d6 and use the number rolled in place of expending a Bardic Inspiration die, and when you use your Tale of Gloam, you can also teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see as part of that Bonus Action

Weapon: Martial, Melee 120gp, 8 lbs. --- 2d4 slashing - Reach, Two-handed, Special Description Proficiency with a double-bladed scythe allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special. If you attack with a double-bladed scythe as part of the Attack action on your turn, you can use a bonus action immediately after to make a melee attack with it. This attack deals 1d4 slashing damage on a hit.

Dragonborn and Draconic Bloodline Sorcerers, Drakewarden Rangers and Ascendant Dragon Monks are updated to include the new types of dragons. New racial types follows gem dragonborn guidelines, This updated only changes the given Damage and Resistance types. -NEW- Time Force Moonstone Radiant Solar Radiant Lunar Cold Deep Psychic -Traditional- Black Acid Blue Lightning Brass Fire Bronze Lightning Copper Acid Gold Fire Green Poison Red Fire Silver Cold White Cold -Gem- Amethyst Force Crystal Radiant Emerald Psychic Sapphire Thunder Topaz Necrotic

Large Object (Siege Weapon), 35, 000 gold Armor Class: 19 Hit Points: 50 Damage Immunities: Poison, Psychic A massive steam powered high-caliber machine gun. Designed for stationary or jammer mounted use, the emplaced version of the chain gun dwarfs it in size and power. An emplaced heavy chain gun requires an external source of steam, and usually its own dedicated boiler, making it a rather permanent fixture rather than a mobile one. The gun does not regularly need reloaded, as its ammunition chains usually come in the lengths of thousands. Should it need to be reloaded, it takes two actions to do so. It takes one action to use the gun's automatic fire. Automatic Fire. The emplaced heavy chain gun makes twenty attacks. High-Caliber Bullet. Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d8) piercing. This attack expends two pieces of ammunition.

Exposure to distant forces - those that observe from beyond time or space - has left a mark on your soul. You now wield magic that shields and strikes in equal measure. Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20., You learn the sanctuary spell and one 1st-level spell of your choice. The 1st-level spell must be from the abjuration or evocation school of magic. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

Prerequisite Aasimar Description You manifested some of the powers from the Upper Planes, granting you the following benefits: Your Healing Hands and transformation traits can now use either an action or bonus action to activate and can be used again after finishing a short or long rest. Each of your transformations also gain additional effects: Necrotic Shroud. The range of the effect increases to 30 feet, and you gain advantage on attack rolls against creatures frightened by this trait. Radiant Consumption. The radius of both bright and dim light increases to 30 feet. Hostile creatures can't benefit from being hidden while within the light. If you are within magical darkness, the light would only remain on your body and won't be shed but you are able to see through that darkness instead. Creatures within or outside the magical darkness would be able to see you. Radiant Soul. You can hover. When the transformation ends while you are not on the ground, your rate of decent slows to 60 feet per round until you land. Upon landing, you take no falling damage and can land on your feet.

Master Brutality and Blood Sport Gladiators are just as much performers as they are warriors. Whether brawling in underground fighting rings or fighting for survival in bloodstained arenas, a Gladiator combines martial skill with theatrics to awe and intimidate their audiences. Features: 3rd Level - Brutality 3rd Level - Combat Theatrics 7th Level - Flourish Parry 10th Level - Bolder Brutalities 15th Level - Brutal Resurgence 18th Level - Mutilate

Shaped by the intensity of the arena, you’ve learned to execute brutal martial moves. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a Melee weapon, you can add one of the following Brutality effects of your choice. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest. Bleed. You can activate the Sap mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and the target takes extra damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 damage). The extra damage’s type is the same type as the weapon’s type. Bluff. You can activate the Vex mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and you have Advantage on the next saving throw you make before the end of your next turn. Stumble. You can activate the Topple mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and on its next turn, the target can take only an action or a Bonus Action, not both.

You’ve honed your combat skills to entertain, devastating opponents and dazzling onlookers. You gain the following benefits. Athletic Flair. Whenever you make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1). Bonus Proficiency. You gain proficiency in one of these skills of your choice: Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Intimidation, or Performance.

You’ve learned to stylishly counter blows from your opponents. When an enemy hits you with a melee attack roll, you can take a Reaction to add your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) to your AC against the attack, potentially causing the attack to miss. Flourish Counter. If this Reaction causes the attack to miss, you can retaliate with a powerful counterattack as part of the same Reaction. Make an attack roll with a Melee weapon against the triggering creature. If this attack hits, you can use one of your Brutality effects on the target without expending a use of that feature. Once this counterattack hits, you can’t use this feature to make another counterattack until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of this counterattack by expending a use of Second Wind (no action required).

Your brutal martial prowess has improved. The following effects are added to your Brutality options. Rive. You can activate the Cleave mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the additional attack made as part of that property’s activation. Rush. You can activate the Push mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and you can immediately move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Stagger. You can activate the Slow mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon, and the target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn.
Whenever you use your Second Wind to regain Hit Points, you regain an expended use of Brutality. You also regain an expended use of Brutality whenever you use your Action Surge.

When you hit a Bloodied creature with an attack roll, you can attempt to critically injure it. The target makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the target suffers the following effects: Maimed. If the target takes the Attack action, it can make only one attack. Sluggish. The target’s Speed is halved, and it has a −2 penalty to its Armor Class. These effects last until the target regains Hit Points. Once a target fails its saving throw against this feature, you can’t use it again on that creature until you finish a Long Rest.

Adventuring Gear 2 lbs. 50gp Description As an action, a character can throw a grenade at a point up to 60 feet away. With a grenade launcher, the character can propel the grenade up to 120 feet away. One round after a smoke grenade lands, it emits a cloud of smoke that creates a heavily obscured area in a 20-foot radius. A moderate wind (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses the smoke in 4 rounds; a strong wind (20 or more miles per hour) disperses it in 1 round.

Prerequisite: Proficiency with at least one type of hammer You have become adept at using hammers and can make use of their crushing weight against your opponents. When you wield a hammer and attack a creature with it, the target's AC is reduced by 2 for that attack, and you ignore the detrimental effects of the heavy property of hammers. Additionally, once per turn, when you hit a creature with a hammer, you can immediately take the shove action targeting the same creature. Hammers: Light Hammer, Warhammer, Lucerne Hammer, Maul

Description You are a master hurler of thrown weapons and can make shots that others find impossible, impaling your foes with the greatest of ease. You gain the following benefits: Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your thrown weapon attack rolls. Pinning Impalement: When you hit a creature with a thrown weapon attack from a spear, javelin or trident, you may attempt to impale them onto an adjacent surface. The creature must make a DC 8+PB+STR strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is pinned to the surface for 1 minute, or until it or another creature within reach of it uses an action to remove the weapon. A creature impaled by the weapon has its speed reduced to 0. If a flying creature with no adjacent surface is impaled this way, instead reduce their movement speed by 10ft until the weapon is removed as an action. Pinning Impalement can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all uses on a long rest.

Prerequisite Proficiency in a Martial weapon Description Iaijutsu is the martial art of drawing a weapon and attacking with it in the same fluid motion. It is the foundation of some forms of dueling in Kara-Tur, and its masters are feared and respected throughout Rokugan and other lands where iaijutsu is practiced. When you draw a weapon in combat, you have advantage on the first attack you make with that weapon until the end of the turn. If that attack hits, you may reroll the weapon's damage dice, taking the higher rolls.

Weapon (martial), 1d6 slashing or 1d4 bludgeoning, 50gp, 4 lbs. Finesse, Reach, Two-Handed, Special Description Special: You can choose to attack with either the kama (sickle) or the weighted chain on your turn. You may then make an attack with the other weapon as a bonus action. In addition, this weapon may be a monk weapon despite its properties. Kama (Sickle): The sickle deals 1d6 slashing damage. The range of this is 5ft. Weighted Chain (Kusari): The chain deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage. The range of the chain is 10ft.

Weapon: Martial, Melee 10gp, 4 lbs. --- 1d8 Bludgeoning - Reach, Two-handed, Special Description Proficiency with a Long Bo-Staff allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special: Counts as a Monk weapon (For martial arts), as well as monks would be proficiency This weapon has the following weapon mastery: Push: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or Smaller

Martial Melee Weapon - 20 gp, 6 lbs - 1d10 bludgeoning - Two-handed, Heavy, Reach, **Topple** A pole hammer designed for armored combat, or cracking the thick hides of monsters. Counts as both a hammer and a polearm.

Armor (Heavy), Non-Lootable Description Armor infused with the essence of stars. A suit of luminite armor holds with it the power to boost it's wearers abilities across a spectrum of focuses. When luminite armor is made, it can come in one of the following forms, which determines it's properties: Solar - While wearing this magical armor, you have a +3 bonus to your armor class, and resistance to fire damage. Your melee weapon attacks deal an additional 1d8 fire damage, and have a +1 bonus to hit. The armor has three charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you can expend one charge as a reaction to halve the damage, and cause the attacking creature to take fire damage equal to the reduction. Vortex - While wearing this magical armor, you have a +2 bonus to your armor class, and resistance to lightning damage. Your ranged weapon attacks deal an additional 1d6 lightning damage, and have a +2 bonus to hit. The armor has three charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. As a bonus action, you can expend one charge to become invisible until you move. Attacking does not break your invisibility. Nebula - While wearing this magical armor, you are considered to be proficienct with it even if you lack proficiency with heavy armor, and you are resistant to psychic damage. Your spell attacks have a +3 bonus to hit. The armor has three charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. As an action, you can expend one charge to gain one of the following effects for one minute: Regeneration - you regain 5 hit points at the start of each of your turns. Power - each of your spells gains a 2d8 bonus to one damage roll. Mana - When you cast a spell of 3rd level or lower, roll a d6. If the result is greater than the level of the spell, you do not expend a spell slot. Stardust - While wearing this magical armor, you are considered to be proficient with it even if you lack proficiency with heavy armor, and you are resistant to cold damage. Creatures you summon through class features or spells gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls. The armor has three charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. When you summon a creature throigh a class feature or spell, you can expend one charge to summon one additional creature. This creature lasts only half as long, or for one hour in the case of indefinite durations.

Description You master the physician's arts, gaining the following benefits: Increase your Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency in the Medicine skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it. During a short rest, you can clean and bind the wounds of up to six willing beasts, fey, and humanoids. Make a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check for each creature. On a success, if a creature spends a Hit Die during this rest, that creature can forgo the roll and instead regain the maximum number of hit points the die can restore. A creature can do so on a number of Hit Dice equal to half your Wisdom modifier, regardless of how many Hit Dice it spends.

Weapon: Martial, Ranged 3000gp, 20 lbs. --- 3d10 piercing - ammunition, special, range (120/480), two-handed Requires a Strength score of 21 or higher and have a carrying capacity of a Huge or larger creature to be able to wield this weapon Description When making an attack with this weapon, you use your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. The arrows used by this weapon costs 1000 gp (Items that create ammunition still require 1000 gp, gold is magically disappeared from your characters pouch, magic knows all).

Weapon: Martial, Ranged 300gp, 6 lbs. --- 2d6 piercing - ammunition, special, range (150/600), two-handed Requires a Strength score of 18 or higher and be Medium or larger to be able to wield this weapon Description When making an attack with this weapon, you use your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

Wondrous Item Description A small autonomous machine made to produce equally autonomous assistance. When activated, it begins production of a singular kiddywidget over the course of 30 days. The fabricator uses its own parts to produce the kiddywidget, and is fully dismantled when the process finishes. The kiddywidget is Friendly toward you and obeys your commands. Absent commands from you it does nothing. The kiddywidget cannot grow into a skitterwidget.

The philosophical path of the elite, focusing on stealth, single-target elimination, and critical precision. Shinobi of this Nindo are taught to be untraceable ghosts, utilizing concealed weapons and specialized toxins to ensure their targets never see the final blow coming. They prioritize efficiency and guarantee their kill before dissolving back into the shadows.

Nindo Jutsu. At certain levels you learn jutsu from your Shinobi Nindo, you always know these Jutsu and they do not count against your total known jutsu. Rank Jutsu Learn Level D Lightning Tackle 3rd C Chidori 5th B Lightning Cloak 8th Fighting Style: Choose one: Dueling Two-Weapon Fighting Thrown Weapon Fighting Blind Fighting Silent Elimination, You are taught to find and exploit fatal flaws with precision. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll or if a creature friendly to you is within 5 feet of the target and isn't incapacitated. The extra damage increases as you unlock higher Jutsu Ranks: 2d6 at C-Rank (5th level), 3d6 at B-Rank (8th level), 4d6 at A-Rank (13th level), and 5d6 at S-Rank (17th level). This extra damage counts as Jutsu damage for features that modify your Jutsu damage (such as the Prodigy’s Precision), but dealing it is not casting a Jutsu.

You are the ultimate skirmisher, utilizing speed and misdirection to control the engagement and facilitate escape. Skirmisher's Flow: You can take the Dash or Disengage action as a Bonus Action on your turn. Ghost Step: You strike and are gone before the blood falls. Vanishing Strike: When you deal Silent Elimination damage to a creature, you can immediately attempt to Hide as part of that attack (no action required), provided you have any cover or obscurement (such as your Hidden Mist). Silent Blow: When you hit a creature you are hidden from, that creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

You master the application of chakra-infused poisons to ensure your blows are debilitating and fatal. Preparation: As a Bonus Action, you can spend 3 Chakra to coat one weapon with a neurotoxin for 1 minute. While the coating lasts, once per turn when you hit a creature with that weapon, the creature takes an extra 3d6 Poison damage and must make a Constitution saving throw (vs. Jutsu DC) or be Poisoned for 1 minute. Toxic Expertise: Your Silent Elimination damage and your toxin damage from this Nindo ignore Resistance to Poison damage.

You achieve ultimate mastery over toxins, delivering a single, decisive blow that paralyzes the nervous system, securing the kill. Activation: When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can spend 5 Chakra to apply the Apex Neurotoxin (no action required). The creature takes an extra 8d8 Poison damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (vs. Jutsu DC) or be Paralysed for up to 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. This damage ignores Resistance to Poison damage and treats Immunity to Poison damage as Resistance.

This philosophical path is chosen by those who seek the perfect balance between mental discipline and physical execution. The Battlemind views their internal Essence as a wellspring of latent power, channeling their Intelligence to simultaneously augment their body for close combat and unleash formidable techniques. Their combat style is highly adaptable, allowing them to remain effective at any range.

Nindo Jutsu. At certain levels you learn jutsu from your Shinobi Nindo, you always know these Jutsu and they do not count against your total known jutsu. Rank Jutsu Learn Level D Manipulated Shuriken 3rd C Blade of Wind 5th B Shadow Clone 8th Fighting Style - Choose one of the following Fighting Styles: Defense Thrown Weapon Fighting Dueling Always Ready Using the Manipulated Shuriken Jutsu does not cost any chakra. The die size increases to a d6 at level 7 and d8 at level 15

You learn to stabilize and condense your internal essence, forming a flickering defensive field around your body to increase your resilience against immediate threats. As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Chakra to gather a defensive layer of surging essence. You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Intelligence modifier (maximum of +3) until the start of your next turn. You can extend the duration by 1 additional round for each additional 2 Chakra spent.

You maximize the tactical value of your duplicate techniques, turning misdirection into focused, lethal offense through superior coordination. Synchronization: When you or a Shadow Clone (created by a Jutsu) hit a creature with an attack, the next attack roll made against that creature before the end of your next turn has Advantage. Shared Essence: When a Shadow Clone is destroyed, you instantly regain 2 Chakra (if you have fewer than your maximum Chakra points).

You unlock your ultimate inner potential, reaching a temporary state of perfect coordination between your mental essence and physical vessel. Transformation: As an Action, you enter a state of Perfected Form for 1 minute. Resistance: You gain Resistance to all damage (except Psychic damage). Power Surge: You gain a +2 bonus to your Jutsu Save DC and your Jutsu Attack Rolls. Healing Flow: You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Shinobi Level at the start of each of your turns. Drawback: Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

This philosophical path is dedicated to harnessing raw elemental power. The Elementalist acts as artillery, focusing their internal Chakra into external blasts and wide-area effects. They achieve precision over manipulated elements rather than physical prowess, making them effective medium-to-long range operatives whose goal is battlefield control through destruction.

Nindo Jutsu. At certain levels you learn jutsu from your Shinobi Nindo, you always know these Jutsu and they do not count against your total known jutsu. Rank Jutsu Learn Level D Air Bullet 3rd C Phoenix Sage Fire 5th B Water Dragon Bullet 8th Fighting Style: Choose one: Archery Thrown Weapon Fighting Potent Jutsu You learn to infuse your Ninjutsu with extra raw power. When you deal damage with an elemental nature (Fire, Water, Earth, Lighting or Wind) ninjutsu, you add your Intelligence modifier to the damage roll.

You learn to shape and control the spread of your elemental techniques, protecting allies from devastating effects. When you cast a Ninjutsu Jutsu that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can choose a number of those creatures equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one). These creatures automatically succeed on their saving throw against the Jutsu and take no damage.

Your mastery over external chakra projection allows your techniques to reach unparalleled distances. The range of all your non-self or touch range elemental ninjutsu is doubled. Additionally, you can cast a B or lower rank Jutsu once per Long Rest without spending Chakra.

You reach a state of absolute elemental saturation, gaining temporary access to rapid-fire casting. Transformation: As an Action, you enter a state of Elemental Overdrive for 1 minute. You gain a Flying Speed of 60 feet. Rapid Fire: When you use your Action to cast a Jutsu, you can use your Bonus Action to cast a second Jutsu of C-Rank or lower regardless of it’s casting time(provided you have the Chakra to do so). Drawback: Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you spend 7 Chakra to do so.

This philosophical path is chosen by those dedicated to the preservation of life. Healers are masters of Yang Nature (Body/Life) techniques, utilizing their chakra not for destruction, but to repair flesh, mend bones, and sustain their comrades through the harshest battles. They are the essential core of any squad, prioritizing team endurance above all else.

Nindo Jutsu. At certain levels you learn jutsu from your Shinobi Nindo, you always know these Jutsu and they do not count against your total known jutsu. Rank Jutsu Learn Level D Healing Seal 3rd C Revitalizing Needle 5th B Sealing Seal 8th Fighting Style: Choose one: Interception Defense. Core Identity: Combat Medic When you restore hit points to a creature with a Jutsu, they regain extra hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

You master the ability to safely transfer your own internal reserves to allies, boosting their capacity to fight. Chakra Transfer: As an Action, you can touch a willing creature and transfer your Chakra to them. You lose up to 5 Chakra, and the ally gains an equal amount of Chakra points. Nindo efficiency does not apply. Slot Restoration: If the creature is a spellcaster, you can choose to convert your transferred Chakra into one of their expended spell slots. The ally immediately regains a single spell slot of a level determined by the Chakra cost, as shown in the table below. You cannot restore a spell slot higher than 5th level, and you can only restore one spell slot per action. Spell Slot Level Restored Chakra Cost Required 1st 2 Chakra 2nd 3 Chakra 3rd 5 Chakra 4th 6 Chakra 5th 7 Chakra

Your dedication to life allows you to defy death itself, preventing fatal blows from landing against you or a comrade. When you or an ally within 30 feet of you would be reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can use your Reaction and spend 5 Chakra to cause the target to drop to 1 hit point instead.

You achieve the ultimate mastery of healing, capable of regenerating flesh and curing massive damage with an overwhelming surge of life energy. Ultimate Technique: As an Action, you can emit a pulse of life chakra. All allies within a 30-foot radius of you regain 10d8 + your Intelligence modifier hit points. This Jutsu automatically ends any Poisoned or Diseased conditions on the affected allies. This technique costs 10 Chakra to cast.

This philosophical path is chosen by those who seek dominance not through physical force, but through mastery of the mind. The Illusionist specializes in Genjutsu (Yin Nature), manipulating the senses of foes to impose debilitating conditions, control the battlefield, and erode the enemy's mental resolve. They are the ultimate tacticians who win the fight before it ever begins.

Nindo Jutsu. At certain levels you learn jutsu from your Shinobi Nindo, you always know these Jutsu and they do not count against your total known jutsu. Rank Jutsu Learn Level D Ephemeral 3rd C False Surroundings 5th B Bringer of Darkness 8th Fighting Style: Choose one: Defense Blindsight. Illusory Discipline Your command over Genjutsu (Yin Nature) makes your techniques highly persuasive. The Save DC for any Genjutsu you cast increases by 1.

You learn to channel chakra into a feedback loop, punishing those who try to resist your mental techniques. When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Genjutsu, you can use your Reaction to inflict 1d8 Psychic damage on that creature. Additionally, the creature has Disadvantage on its next Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Insight) check made before the start of your next turn.

Your mental techniques are so pervasive that even temporary resistance is difficult to maintain. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your Genjutsu, you can use your Reaction to force that creature to immediately reroll the save, using the new result. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), regaining all expended uses on a Long Rest.

You unleash the ultimate mental prison, capable of isolating and debilitating a single target completely. Ultimate Technique: As an Action, you target one creature within 30 feet. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (vs. Jutsu DC) or be trapped in your Mind Cage. While trapped, the creature is Paralyzed. At the start of each of its turns, the target takes 6d8 Psychic damage. Duration: The effect lasts for up to 1 minute, but you must use your Concentration to maintain it. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Drawback: Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend another 10 Chakra.

A Subclass of Barbarian that focus on unarmed fighting Features: 3rd Level - Unarmed Combatant 3rd Level - Brawler's Prowess 6th Level - Reactive Fighting 6th Level - Packin' Heat 10th Level - Fearsome Critical 14th Level - Brawler's Focus

At level 3, your strength and general martial prowess increase the damage that you do with your bare fists. When you make an unarmed strike, your damage becomes 1d4 + your STR modifier. The damage dice increase with each level in this subclass, to become 1d6 at level 6, 1d8 at level 10 and finally 1d10 at level 14.

At level 3, While Raging, you gain new options to use as bonus actions, as long as you are not wielding any weapons or a shield. Block: While raging, you can use your bonus action to raise your arms in a defensive stance. This gives you an AC boost of +2 until the start of your next turn. At level 10, this AC boost becomes +3 Jab: While raging, you can use your bonus action to make an unarmed strike against a target.
At level 6, while you are raging, when a creature attacks you and they are within 5 feet of you, you can make an unarmed strike against that creature as a reaction.
At level 6, your unarmed strikes can even inflict damage on the toughest of foes, your unarmed strikes become magical for the purpose of overcoming non-magical resistance and immunity.

At level 10, when you score a Critical hit on a Target with your unarmed strike, you can apply brutal critical to your unarmed strike. Additionally when you score a critical hit on a target, they must save a Constitution saving throw against your save DC (8 + proficiency + strength bonus) or be frightened by you until the end of their next turn.

At level 14, while you are raging and you have only one creature within 20 feet of you, that creature has your undivided attention. You are in the "zone". You can make attacks against them with adv, and any wisdom saves they force you to make, are made with adv. While in the zone, if they try to leave your melee range, your Attack of Opportunity has the ability to stop them in their tracks, reducing their move speed to zero if they fail a strength save against your save DC (8+prof+strength bonus)

Unleash your inner light as blazing fury Barbarians infused with the power of Unlight embrace uncontrollable magic in exchange for incredible physical prowess. The Unlight burning inside them illuminates the darkness while burning and blinding the barbarian's enemies. Most barbarians on this path were first exposed to Unlight in the Underdark, sometimes referred to as the Underlight. The magic of Unlight is contagious and spreads in unpredictable ways. It infects people only briefly exposed to it and occasionally manifests in individuals who have never been to the Underdark. Features: Unlight Manifestation 3rd Level - Radiant Rage 6th Level - Unlight Revelation 10th Level - Infectious Unlight 10th Level - Harbinger of Unlight 14th Level - Brilliant Rage

Barbarians on the Path of Unlight manifest the radiant energy of Unlight when they rage, but this energy can take many forms. You can roll on or choose a result from the Unlight Manifestation table to inspire the form your Radiant Rage takes. 1d6 Your Unlight Manifests As… 1 White light blazing from your eyes and mouth. 2 Complex arcane symbols of light etched onto your body. 3 A cyclone of bright light that whirls around you. 4 Cracks in your flesh that reveal burning light within. 5 A ghostly form made of light that hovers above you. 6 Pale fire that dances on the tip of your weapon.

The Unlight coursing through you fuels your Rage. While your Rage is active, you shed Bright Light in a 15-foot radius. Additionally, if a creature damages or hits you with an attack roll while within your area of Bright Light, the creature takes Radiant damage equal to twice your Rage Damage bonus.

You have proficiency in the Perception skill, if you lack it. You also gain Expertise in that skill. While your rage is active, you have Blindsight with a range equal to that of the Bright Light provided by your Radiant Rage.

Damage you deal with Brutal Strike can be Radiant or the usual type (your choice). The following effect is now among your Brutal Strike options. Radiant Infection. The target becomes infected with Unlight for 1 minute. While infected, it sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and gains no benefit from being hidden or invisible. Additionally, at the start of each of its turns roll a 1d12; it takes that much in Radiant damage and also takes a penalty on the first attack roll and Constitution saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn equal to the amount rolled. The target can use an Action to purge the Infection from their system, ending the effect on a success.
You have Resistance to Radiant damage.

The aura of your Unlight is bolstered. While your Rage is active, you shed Bright Light in a 30-foot radius. As a Bonus Action, you unleash your blinding radiance. When you do, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, roll a number of d12's equal to your Rage Damage bonus. The target takes that much in Radiant damage and half as much radiant damage again at the start of their turn. Additionally they can see no further than 5ft in any direction until the end of their next turn. On a successful save they take half as much initial damage and no damage at the start of their turn, and suffer no effect to their vision. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Strength modifier, resetting on a Long Rest or if you expend a use of your Rage (no action required) to restore one use of it.
Throw Barbs and Hands

You gain proficiency in the Intimidation skill. If you already have it, you gain Expertise. Terrifying Presence: You can use your Strength modifier instead of Charisma for Intimidation checks. Additionally, you are immune to the Frightened condition; you’ve seen and done worse than anything the multiverse can throw at you.

As a Bonus Action, you can provoke a creature within 60 feet that can see or hear you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Pugilist Save DC. On a Failure: The target takes Psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Fisticuffs die + your Constitution modifier. Aggro Lock: Until the start of your next turn, the target has Disadvantage on any attack roll that doesn't include you as a target. If the target attempts to cast a spell that doesn't include you as a target, it must first succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or the spell fails and the action is wasted.

You have mastered the art of fighting unfair. You gain a Trick Pool equal to your Strength modifier (minimum of 1). You regain all uses of this pool on a Long Rest. You can spend a use of this pool (no action required) to apply one of the following Dirty Tricks when you hit with a Pugilist weapon or Unarmed Strike. Once your pool is empty, you can continue to use these tricks by expending 2 Moxie Points per use. Heelstomper: The creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be Restrained (not just 0 speed) until the end of your next turn as you pin them down or crush a foot. Low Blow: The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be Stunned until the start of your next turn. Pocket Sand: As a Bonus Action, you toss detritus. A creature within 15 feet must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be Blinded for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the save at the end of its turns.

Your insults are so vile they physically manifest as psychic pressure. As a Bonus Action, you can target a number of creatures up to your Prestige Level within 30 feet. Effect: Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take Psychic damage equal to three rolls of your Fisticuffs die + your CON modifier and be Frightened of you until the start of your next turn. While Frightened this way, a creature's speed is 0. Usage: You can use this once per Long Rest for free, or expend 4 Moxie Points to use it again.

Your "Dirty Tricks" now bypass certain resistances. When you use a Dirty Trick, the target has Disadvantage on the saving throw. Furthermore, you gain these elite maneuvers: Rabbit Punch: When you hit, you strike a nerve cluster. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its Damage Resistances and Immunities suppressed for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns. Sucker Punch: When you hit a creature that has Disadvantage on the attack roll or is affected by one of your Dirty Tricks, you can spend 3 Moxie to turn the hit into a Devastating Critical. Roll the damage dice four times. The target must then succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked back 30 feet and fall Prone.
Revolver master. Fast, aggressive, stylish. Built around Round Reload. Features: Level 3 – Quick Reflexes Level 7 – Quick Reload Level 13 – Trick Shooter Level 17 – Bullet Storm
When you are hit by a melee weapon attack you may spend a reaction to move up to half of your total speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Once per attack action you can spend 1 grit to reload a round reload weapon.
Called Shots cost 0 Grit when using a Revolver or Pistol. You can do this a number of times per long rest equal to your Dexterity Modifier.

Once per short rest as an action while wielding a revolver: You select 1 creature in range and unload all remaining rounds chambered into that creature. You make 1 attack roll and on a hit they take damage as if hit by the number of shots remaining in the weapon. You must reload your weapon before taking the Attack action again. I.E. 2 Shots remaining would be 4d10 damage on a hit. 4 Shots in the weapon is 8d10.

Description You can keep your enemies at bay with reach weapons. You gain the following benefits: When you take the Attack action and attack with only a glaive, lance, pike, quarterstaff, spear, or trident, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon. This attack uses the same ability modifier as the primary attack. The weapon's damage die for this attack is a d4, and it deals bludgeoning damage. While you are wielding a glaive, halberd, lance, pike, quarterstaff, spear, or trident, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter the reach you have with that weapon.

Flask - Adventuring Gear - 250 gp, 2 lbs. Also referred to as thermite in other settings, red powder is a volatile mixture of iron and aluminum powders. It burns rapidly and at extremely high temperatures, though it is not an explosive. A single flask can be emptied and contains enough powder to cover one square foot. It can then be ignited, where it burns for 1 round, shedding bright light in a 30 foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. The powder can burn or melt away a single tiny non-magical item that it remains in contact with while burning. As an action, you can recollect or brush away red powder that is yet to be ignited. Once ignited, the powder sticks to the surface and can no longer be removed until it burns away. A creature that touches red powder, or starts its turn touching red powder, while it is burning takes 4d8 fire damage, that ignores a target's resistance to fire damage.

Martial Melee Weapon - 1d10 piercing - two-handed, thrown (range 20/20), heavy, special, topple - 500 gp, 12 lbs Rocket spear. It's a spear with a rocket. Pressurized combustion reimagined to strap a simple oil-powered rocket to the head of a spear to deliver a rather excessive amount of melee force. Special - As an action, you can fuel the rocket spear with one flask of oil. While fueled, the rocket becomes active, and the weapon's thrown range increases to 60/60. While the rocket is active and you throw the spear, you can choose to hold onto it during its flight, landing in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target. Once fueled, the rocket burns out of fuel at the end of your next turn or when you make an attack with it.

Rotor Saw - Martial Melee Weapon - 1d12 slashing - 1,000 gp, 300 lbs - Two-handed, Ultra-Heavy, Fuel (Oil), Volatile, **Automatic** A steam powered rotary sawblade originally made for cutting through metal and rock. Flesh and bone prove easier, thus it's use as a weapon. Counts as an Axe.

Weapon: Simple, Melee 5gp, 2 lbs. --- 1d6 slashing - finesse, versatile (1d8) Description Proficiency with a scythe allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Finesse: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. Versatile: This weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property--the damage when the weapon is used with two hands to make a melee attack. Mastery Property - Cleave: If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
Long-range elimination specialist. Built around Sight property of firearms. Features: Level 3 – Mark Target Level 7 – Perfect Sight Level 13 – Critical Focus Level 17 – One Perfect Round
As a Bonus action you may mark a creature for 1 minute by spending 1 Grit. Once per turn, deal extra damage to a creature hit with a firearm attack: 1d8 (3rd) 2d8 (7th) 3d8 (11th) 4d8 (18th)
Your Sight weapons become magical in order to overcome resistance and immunity. You also gain proficiency in the Perception skill or another skill of your choice if you have proficiency already.
You can gain advantage for the current turn by spending 2 Grit as a bonus action, and are able to do so a number of times equal to your Dexterity Modifier per long rest.
Once per long rest, declare before you attack a creature with a firearm: If it hits, it is an automatic critical hit and ignores resistance.

Sorrow knights suffuse their opponents with grief and misery from the gloomy plane called the Shadowfell. These fighters harness their past despair to forge a connection with others and protect themselves. A sorrow knight’s intense loss - whether the loss of love, faith, or something equally profound - is the weapon they wield against their foes and their motivator to ensure that no one experiences that same pain. Features: Embracing the Gloom 3rd Level - Despairing Strikes 3rd Level - Solemn Gaze 7th Level - Dreaded Appearance 10th Level - Unsettled Strikes 15th Level - Grim Constitution 18th Level - Grieving Mantle

Sorrow knights deploy the gloom and sadness inherent to the Shadowfell, whether or not they have ever been to that grim place. Roll on or choose a result from the Shadowfell Connection table to inspire the event that forged your connection to the Shadowfell.

1d6 The Despair of the Shadowfell Claimed You After… 1 You arrived too late to save your home from monsters that destroyed it. 2 You realized a good-aligned god never intends to answer your prayers. 3 You were not strong enough to save the love of your life from their untimely death. 4 A shadow crossing opened beneath your bed as a child. 5 You understood your parents were never returning to save you. 6 You fell into an open grave.

Each sorrow knight bears an emotional wound like a deep scar, through which they channel despair against their enemies. This misery is fueled by special dice called Despairing Strike Dice. The Despairing Strike Dice table shows the die size and number of these dice you have when you reach certain Fighter levels. A Despairing Strike Die is expended when you use it. You regain all expended Despairing Strike Dice when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Fighter Level Dice Size Number 3 D8 3 10 D10 4 15 D12 5 When you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can expend a Despairing Strike Die and roll that die. You deal additional Psychic damage equal to the roll and can also add one of the following effects. You can’t expend more than one die per attack. If a Despairing Strike effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and Proficiency Bonus. Abandoned. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or have the Deafened condition until the end of your next turn. While Deafened, the target regards all creatures it can see as enemies until the end of your next turn. Dread. The target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

You can see through the darkness around you and recognize the darkness in others. You gain the following benefits. Darkvision. You gain Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet. Empathetic Inquiry. As a Magic action, you can attempt to search the mind of a creature you can see within 30 feet. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or you learn an emotion that looms large in its mind, such as a worry, love, or hate. If the target can see you, it knows you have read its emotions. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

When you use Tactical Shift, you can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself instead of moving. Immediately after you reappear, you can briefly take on the appearance of creatures’ fears, visible only to those creatures. Each creature of your choice within a 10-foot Emanation originating from you makes a Wisdom saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a target takes Psychic damage equal to a roll of your Despairing Strike die and has the Frightened condition until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half damage only. Once you take on this appearance, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

You further channel the pathos of the Shadowfell through your fighting abilities. The following effects are now among your Despairing Strike options. Apathetic. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Incapacitated condition until the start of your next turn. While Incapacitated in this way, the target can give only one-word responses when spoken to. Lost. The target makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Blinded condition, and its Speed is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the target’s Speed is halved until the end of its next turn. Weary. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or gain 1 Exhaustion level. This effect can’t increase the target’s Exhaustion level above 2. Exhaustion levels gained from this effect are removed at the end of your next turn.

You have Resistance to Necrotic and Psychic damage. In addition, when you are subjected to an effect that reduces your Hit Point maximum, you can make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, your Hit Point maximum isn’t decreased. Each time you make this Constitution saving throw after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, the DC resets to 15.

When you use your Action Surge, you attune yourself to the Shadowfell for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. For the duration, you gain the following benefits. Shade Form. When you are hit by an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to become insubstantial for a moment and reduce the attack’s total damage against you by three rolls of your despairing strike die plus half your fighter level Unwavering Resolve. You have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions. If you’re Charmed or Frightened when you activate your Grieving Mantle, the condition ends on you.

Weapon: Simple, Melee 1gp, 1.5 lbs. --- 1d4 piercing - light, two-handed Description Proficiency with a cestus allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it. Special: As a bonus action, you can make one attack with this weapon.
Drop and Lock Your Foes

You have mastered the fundamentals of wrestling and submission. You gain the following benefits: Compression Lock: Your grip is bone-crushing. When you start your turn with one or more creatures Grappled by you, you can deal Bludgeoning damage to each of those creatures (no action required). The damage equals one roll of your Fisticuffs Die + your Strength modifier. Inescapable: When a creature makes a saving throw or ability check to escape your Grapple or resist your Shove, you can expend 1 Moxie Point to give that roll Disadvantage. Stop and Drop: Your strikes lead naturally into takedowns. When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, even if you use a mastery property, you can use the shove option against that target as part of the same attack, if instead you do the grapple option from heavy hitter you make the check with advantage.

You have conditioned your body for maximum leverage. You gain proficiency in the Athletics skill. If you already have proficiency, you gain Expertise in it. Additionally, you can use your Strength modifier instead of Dexterity when determining your Armor class..

You know how to put an enemy between yourself and danger. While you have a creature Grappled, you gain Half Cover (+2 to AC and Dexterity saving throws) against attacks and effects made by creatures you aren't Grappling. Redirect Strike: When a creature you aren't Grappling misses you with a melee or ranged attack roll, you can take a Reaction to force that creature to make a new attack roll against a creature you are currently Grappling. You can do this a number of times equal to your Strength modifier per Long Rest. You may expend 2 Moxie Points to use this feature again if you have no uses remaining.

Your technique allows you to manhandle even the largest foes. Size Mastery: You count as two sizes larger for the purpose of Grappling or Shoving. Relentless Drag: You no longer spend extra movement to move a creature Grappled by you, regardless of its size. Iron Grip: Creatures have Disadvantage on any attack rolls they make against you while they are Grappled by you.

You have mastered the art of the "Lights Out" submission. When a creature ends its turn Grappled by you, you can take a Reaction to force it to make a Constitution saving throw against your Pugilist Save DC. Effect: On a failure, the creature gains the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn. The Finisher: If the creature is already Bloodied and fails this saving throw while already Incapacitated (such as from a previous turn's Clean Finish), its Hit Points are immediately reduced to 0 as you snap a vital joint or choke them into unconsciousness. Once you successfully reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points using this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a Long Rest. However, you may still use the Reaction to attempt to apply the Incapacitated condition.
Devote Yourself to Prayer and Pummeling

You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Fists of Faith and Grace of the Gods. When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which effect to create. Moxie Integration: Because Moxie is your primary long-term resource, you can use your Channel Divinity once per Long Rest for free. You can use it again by expending 3 Moxie Points (no action required). Fists of Faith: As a Bonus Action, you imbue your fists with righteous fury. For the next minute, your Unarmed Strikes deal an extra 1d8 Radiant damage. This damage increases to 2d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead. Grace of the Gods: As a Bonus Action, you beseech the gods for grace. For the next minute, you have Resistance to Necrotic and Radiant damage, and whenever you make a saving throw, you can roll 1d6 and add the number rolled to the total.

Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a Long Rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of Hit Points equal to five times your Prestige Level. Action: As a Bonus Action, you can touch a creature (including yourself) and restore a number of Hit Points up to the maximum amount remaining in your pool. Purify: You can expend 5 Hit Points from the pool to remove the Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, or Poisoned condition from the creature.

When you use your Bloodied But Unbowed core class feature, you can choose to fully replenish your Lay On Hands healing pool. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

When you use your Dig Deep core class feature, you radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 20-foot Emanation originating from you for the next 10 minutes. The aura is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition. Effect: You and your allies within the aura gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage (including magical sources). Prestige Bonus: Allies in the aura also add your Constitution modifier to their AC. Once you use this feature, you must finish a Long Rest before you can use it again, unless you expend 6 Moxie Points to use it again.

Your strikes carry the weight of divine judgment. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike or Pugilist weapon, you can expend points from your Lay On Hands pool to deal extra Radiant damage. Damage: The damage equals the number of points expended. Holy Smite: If the target is a Fiend or Undead, the damage is doubled. Maximum: You can expend a maximum number of points per hit equal to your Prestige Level.

Prerequisite Proficiency with at least one type of sword Description You have become adept at using swords and can maneuver them effectively as a result. When you wield a sword, it gains the finesse property if it does not already have it and lacks the heavy property. Additionally, when a creature misses you with a melee attack while you are wielding a sword, you can use your reaction to make one attack with the sword against that creature. Swords: Short Sword, Scimitar, Rapier, Longsword, Greatsword
Psi Warrior. The mind as a wall others stand behind. At PL 25 you choose a Doctrine; PL 29 and 33 branch within it; PL 37 gives your Doctrine's capstone.
Your Order grants these two disciplines at PL 21. They don't count against the number of disciplines you know, and no other Order can learn them.

○ Focus. Difficult terrain doesn't slow you, and your Speed can't be reduced. ● Tether (3 psi) — Bonus Action. Anchor one creature within 30 ft. Until the end of your next turn it can't willingly move more than 15 ft from where it stands. ●● Ground the Line (8 psi) — Bonus Action. For 1 minute, allies within 15 ft of you can't be knocked Prone or moved against their will. No concentration.

○ Focus. Allies within 10 ft add your Psionic Ability modifier to Constitution saves made to maintain Concentration. ●●● Immutable Line (13 psi) — Magic action. Draw a 30-ft line you can see. For 1 minute, a creature can't cross it without succeeding on a Strength save, and one that fails takes 8d10 Force damage and its movement ends. No concentration.

+4 Psionic Energy Dice, and you regain your Proficiency Bonus in them on a Short Rest. Your Protective Field improves: its range becomes 60 ft, it reduces damage by the roll plus your Prestige Level rather than your Intelligence modifier, and using it on yourself doesn't expend the die.
Protection. Allies within 10 ft of you have half cover, and your Guardian Field can be used at a range of 60 ft.
Force offense. Your Psionic Strike no longer expends a Psionic Energy Die, and you can use it twice on each of your turns rather than once.
Endurance. You can't be knocked Prone or moved against your will, and you have Advantage on saves against being Grappled, Restrained, or Paralyzed.

Interpose. When an ally within 30 ft is hit by an attack, you can use your Reaction to swap places with them; the attack hits you instead. Wide Guard. When you use Guardian Field, it reduces damage to a second creature within 30 ft by the same amount.

Repulsion. When you're hit by an attack, use your Reaction: the attacker makes a Strength save, taking 6d10 Force damage and being pushed 30 ft on a failure, half on a success. Telekinetic Volley. As a Bonus Action, hurl debris at two creatures within 60 ft. Each makes a Dexterity save, taking 4d10 Force damage on a failure, half on a success.

Gravity Well. Enemy movement within 15 ft of you costs double, and enemies that start their turn there take Force damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Rooted Mind. You can't be teleported against your will, banished, or moved to another plane, and you have Resistance to Force damage.

Kinetic Barrier. At the start of each combat, you and each ally within 30 ft gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Prestige Level. Bound Fate. Choose an ally on a Long Rest. While within 60 ft of you, they add your Psionic Ability modifier to all saving throws, and you can use Guardian Field on them without expending a die.

Shattering Force. Your Force damage ignores Resistance and treats Immunity as Resistance. On a Critical Hit, the target is also knocked Prone. Siege Mind. Once per turn when you deal Force damage, add one roll of your Manifestation Die, and the damage destroys any nonmagical object or structure it strikes.

Fortress Self. If you haven't moved since the start of your turn, you have Resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn. Unbreakable. When you're reduced to 0 Hit Points, you drop to 1 instead. Usable a number of times per Long Rest equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Shield — Absolute Aegis. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute: when an ally within 30 ft is targeted by an attack, you can use your Reaction to become the target instead, and you have Resistance to all damage taken this way. Hammer — Fist of the Unseen. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you can make a telekinetic slam as a Bonus Action on each of your turns: one creature within 60 ft makes a Strength save, taking 8d10 Force damage and being knocked Prone on a failure, half on a success. Anchor — Immovable Object. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you are immune to Critical Hits, have Resistance to all damage, and cannot be moved, Incapacitated, Stunned, or Paralyzed by any effect.

Great Old One. Rule is not persuasion. Rule is simply what is true. At PL 25 you choose a Sovereignty; PL 29 and 33 branch within it; PL 37 gives your Sovereignty's capstone. Pact Magic slots grow at PL 21, 29, and 37 only.
Your Order grants these two disciplines at PL 21. They don't count against the number of disciplines you know, and no other Order can learn them.

○ Focus. You can speak to and be understood by any creature, and you know when one knowingly lies to you. ● Suggestion Unspoken (4 psi) — Bonus Action. One creature within 60 ft makes a Wisdom save or accepts one reasonable statement you make as true until given clear evidence otherwise. ●● Chorus (9 psi) — Bonus Action. Up to three creatures within 60 ft make Wisdom saves. Each that fails is Charmed by you for 1 minute.

○ Focus. Creatures that start their turn within 10 ft of you have Disadvantage on Intelligence checks. ● Cognitive Static (3 psi) — Rider. Once per turn when you damage a creature, it can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn. ●●● Nothing Follows (14 psi) — Magic action. Each enemy in a 30-ft cone makes an Intelligence save. On a failure a creature takes 10d10 Psychic damage and, on its next turn, attacks the creature nearest to it, ally or not.

+1 Pact Magic slot. You know the surface thoughts of any creature within 60 ft you can see with Intelligence 3 or higher. As a Bonus Action, one such creature makes a Wisdom save, taking 3d8 Psychic damage and having Disadvantage on its next attack roll on a failure.
Control. You can control two creatures at once with Dominate Impulse, and dominated creatures act on your initiative.

Terror in melee. You can manifest a weapon of solidified thought as a Bonus Action, whether or not you have the Pact of the Blade invocation. It counts as your pact weapon for any feature referencing one, is magical, deals Psychic damage, and uses your Psionic Ability modifier for attack and damage rolls. When you hit a creature with it, that creature makes a Wisdom save or is Frightened of you until the end of its next turn.
Unreality. Once per turn when you damage a creature, you can teleport it 15 ft to an unoccupied space you can see.

Puppet Strings. A creature you dominate can use its Reaction at your command, and you can see and hear through its senses. Hollow Regent. Creatures you dominate gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Prestige Level and add your Psionic Ability modifier to their attack rolls.

Feast of Fear. Creatures Frightened of you take Psychic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus at the start of each of their turns. The first time this damage is dealt each round, you gain that many Temporary Hit Points. Eldritch Strike. Once per turn when you hit with your pact weapon, you can expend a Pact Magic slot to deal an extra 2d8 Psychic damage per slot level. The target has Disadvantage on its next saving throw against you.

Unspeakable Truth. As a Bonus Action, one creature within 60 ft makes an Intelligence save, taking 6d8 Psychic damage and being Stunned until the end of your next turn on a failure. Usable a number of times per Long Rest equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Nonsense Geometry. Attacks against you from more than 30 ft have Disadvantage, and you can teleport 15 ft as part of any move.

Whispers Made Law. Once per turn when a creature fails a saving throw against one of your disciplines, it takes Psychic damage equal to your Prestige Level. No Word Refused. A creature that has failed a save against Dominate Impulse in this encounter has Disadvantage on all further saves against you.

Terror Incarnate. Creatures Frightened of you can't take Reactions and have Disadvantage on all attack rolls. Warped Blade. Your pact weapon ignores Resistance and scores Critical Hits on a 19 or 20. When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with it, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Prestige Level.

Thin the Veil. Once per turn, force a creature you damage to make an Intelligence save or be banished to a pocket of the Far Realm until the end of your next turn. Wrong Angles. Enemies within 30 ft treat the area as difficult terrain and have Disadvantage on Intelligence and Wisdom saves.

Whisper — Throne of the Far Realm. Once per Long Rest as a Magic action, each enemy within 60 ft that can see you makes a Wisdom save or is Incapacitated for 1 minute, repeating at the end of each of its turns. While a creature is Incapacitated this way, you can spend 4 psi as a Bonus Action to have it take one action of your choosing. Dread — The Unbearable. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute: each enemy within 30 ft that can see you makes a Wisdom save at the start of its turn or is Frightened of you, you make one additional attack whenever you take the Attack action, and your pact weapon deals an extra 2d10 Psychic damage against Frightened creatures. Alien — Apotheosis of the Outside. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute your creature type becomes Aberration, you gain a flying speed of 60 ft and Resistance to all damage, and each enemy starting its turn within 30 ft makes an Intelligence save or takes 6d10 Psychic damage.
documents.s: PL 37: Sovereignty Capstone (+1 Pact Magic slot)

documents.t: Warlock Subclass (2024 Ruleset) Your patron is a Metallic Dragon—a creature of ancient nobility, elemental might, and boundless memory. Unlike the terrifying tyrants that demand souls, your patron seeks a Steward: a mortal agent capable of walking where dragons cannot, mediating conflicts, and standing as a bulwark against the encroachment of Tiamat. Possible Patrons of Faerûn: * The King of Justice (Gold): You serve Protanther, the ancient King of Justice who dwells in the Galena Mountains. Your pact is one of strict law and punishing the wicked. * The Silver Cloud (Silver): You serve Otaaryliakkarnos, the Silver Dragon who often walks Mulmaster in human guise. Your pact focuses on compassion and protecting the "small folk." * The Coastal Warden (Bronze): You serve Nymmurh, the Bronze ancient of the Alambur Sea. Your pact is martial; you are a soldier against the aberrations of the deep. * The Whispering Sand (Brass): You serve Ileuthra, the great information broker of the Anauroch Desert. Your pact compels you to gather intelligence and talk before you strike. Features: 3rd Level - Sovereign Spells 3rd Level - Metallic Lineage 3rd Level - Scales of the Steward 3rd Level - Draconic Rebuke 6th Level - Guardian’s Wing 10th Level - Bastion of the Elements 14th Level - Awe of the Wyrm

The following spells are added to your Warlock spell list. | Level | Spells | | 3 | Aid, Chromatic Orb, Command, Dragon's Breath | | 5 | Ashardalon’s Stride, Rime’s Binding Ice | | 7 | Leomund’s Secret Chest, Raulothim’s Psychic Lance | | 9 | Legend Lore, Summon Draconic Spirit |

When you select this subclass, you must choose the type of dragon you serve. This choice determines the damage type for your subclass features. | Dragon Type | Damage Type | | Gold / Brass | Fire | | Silver | Cold | | Bronze | Lightning | | Copper | Acid | You learn to speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, you gain Proficiency in the History or Persuasion skill. Whenever you make a Charisma check to interact with dragons, you add double your Proficiency Bonus to the check.

Your skin hardens with a shimmering, metallic sheen, acting as natural armor to prepare you for the front lines. Natural Armor: While you are not wearing armor, your Armor Class equals 14 + your Dexterity modifier. Shield Training: You gain proficiency with Shields. You can use a shield and still gain the benefit of your Natural Armor.

Your armor hums with the elemental fury of your patron, punishing those who dare to strike you. When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can force that creature to make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes damage equal to 1d8 + your Charisma modifier. The damage type is determined by your Metallic Lineage. You can use this feature 3 times per long rest, regaining a single use when finished a short rest The damage increases by 1d8 and the amount of uses increases by 1 when you reach Warlock levels 6 (2d8, 4 uses), 10 (3d8, 5 uses), and 14 (4d8, 6 uses).

You can manifest the protective instinct of your patron. When a creature other than you, you can see within 10 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can use your Reaction to manifest a spectral, hardened dragon wing to shield them. The damage of that attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Warlock Level.

Your physical form has been tempered by the elemental fury of your patron, turning you into an immovable object. Elemental Resilience: You gain Resistance to the damage type associated with your Metallic Lineage. Unshakable: You are Immune to the Frightened condition. You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks to avoid being knocked Prone or moved against your will. Mental Sustenance: Whenever you succeed on a saving throw, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Warlock Level.

As a Magic Action, you force any number of creatures within 30 feet that can see or hear you to make a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your choice of Charisma (Intimidation) or Charisma (Performance). If you win the contest, the target suffers a condition for 1 minute: Intimidation: The target is Frightened of you. Performance: The target is Charmed by you. While affected, the target cannot take Reactions. The target can make a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that wins the contest or succeeds on the saving throw is immune to this ability for 24 hours. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma Modifier (minimum of once), regaining all uses on a Long Rest.
Mass over speed. Heavy shoulders, a hide that has stopped pretending to be skin, a frame that treats being hit as an administrative matter. Ursine in proportion, broadly speaking.

Great Frame: You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your carrying capacity doubles. While in Hybrid Shape, your Size increases to Large if you were Medium. Thick Hide: You have resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from nonmagical attacks, and you cannot be moved against your will or knocked Prone by any effect that doesn't first reduce you below half your Hit Point maximum.

Absorb: As a Reaction when you or a creature within 10 feet of you takes damage, reduce that damage by your Martial Arts die + your Wisdom modifier + half your Prestige Level. Feed On It: You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the amount reduced.
documents.s: Signature — Break the Blow (1 Primal Point)

documents.t: Choose one: The Wall, The Mountain, or The Maul.

Opener — Sheltering Bulk: Allies within 10 feet of you gain half cover and have advantage on saving throws against being moved, knocked Prone, or Frightened. You are immune to the Frightened condition. PL 30 — choose one: Step In: When you use Break the Blow to protect an ally, you first move up to half your Speed to a space adjacent to them as part of the same Reaction, and the damage you reduce is dealt to you instead of them — after the reduction applies. Bulwark Aura: The radius of Sheltering Bulk increases to 20 feet, and allies within it add your Wisdom modifier to their AC against Opportunity Attacks. PL 35 — choose one: Nothing Passes: Enemies treat every space within 10 feet of you as Difficult Terrain, and cannot end their movement in a space adjacent to an ally you can see. Warding Growth: When you cast a spell of level 1 or higher, choose a number of allies within 30 feet up to your Wisdom modifier; each gains half cover and your Thick Hide resistance until the start of your next turn. PL 40 — Capstone: The Line Holds: Break the Blow costs no Primal Point, has no limit on uses per round, and can protect any ally within 30 feet. While you are conscious, no ally within 10 feet can be reduced below 1 Hit Point by a single attack.

Opener — Deep Reserves: Whenever you would drop to 0 Hit Points, you can spend 3 Primal Points to instead drop to Hit Points equal to five times your Prestige Level, and end one condition affecting you. Once per Short or Long Rest. PL 30 — choose one: Unmoving: You are immune to being moved, knocked Prone, Grappled, or Restrained by any effect whatsoever. Slow to Wound: Any single instance of damage is reduced by your Prestige Level before anything else applies. PL 35 — choose one: Rooted Casting: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration, your Concentration cannot be broken by being moved or knocked Prone, and you automatically succeed on saves against Exhaustion. Bottomless: Deep Reserves recharges on a Short Rest, and its cost is reduced to 1 Primal Point. PL 40 — Capstone: Standing Stone: While above half your Hit Point maximum you have resistance to all damage except Force. While below it, you have advantage on every attack roll, and cannot be reduced to 0 Hit Points by anything short of a critical hit.

Opener — Retaliation: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee attack, if that creature has damaged you since the end of your last turn, you can make one additional melee attack against it as part of the same action. If you are using Flurry of Blows, this attack does not count against its number of strikes. PL 30 — choose one: Crushing Grip: When you hit a creature with a melee attack you can Grapple it as part of the attack, and Grappled creatures take your Martial Arts die at the start of each of their turns.
