Sweep: When you hit a creature, you can force a Strength saving throw against your save DC; on a failure it is pushed 15 feet and knocked Prone. PL 35 — choose one: Punish: Your Retaliation attack deals additional damage equal to the damage you last reduced with Break the Blow. Spellbreaker: When you hit a creature that is Concentrating on a spell, it has disadvantage on the saving throw to maintain it, and you can spend 2 Primal Points to impose automatic failure instead. PL 40 — Capstone: Everything Breaks: Retaliation triggers once per turn against every creature that has damaged you, rather than only one. Your melee attacks score critical hits against Grappled or Prone creatures on a roll of 19–20.

Armor(Shield) 50 gp, 20lbs - AC +0 Also known as a Scutum, the tower shield is a large piece of curved metal or wood, or a composite of both. It is the size of it's user, too big and it is unwieldy if not impossible to use, and too small it becomes ineffective. The shield confers no AC bonus to it's user by default. Instead it grants a damage threshold to you and creatures that you are providing cover for, so long as they are the same size or smaller than the shield. The damage threshold equals your strength modifier, plus your proficiency bonus when wielded with one hand, or twice your strength modifier plus your proficiency bonus when wielded with two. The damage threshold increases for each allied tower shield wielder within 5 feet, adding up to two of their proficiency bonuses to the damage threshold. A creature with a strength score less than 13 has their speed lowered by 10 feet while wielding a tower shield. This shield cannot be used as a base for an animated shield.

You have made your pact with a being of the Shadowfell—not a tyrant, not a monster, but a sovereign of sorrow. The Umbral Lord is a force of stillness and forgetting, a presence woven into the death of joy and the fading of names. It offers you no glory, only power—drawn from what others try not to remember. Features: 3rd Level - Umbral Lord Spells 3rd Level - Echoes of the Forgotten 6th Level - Gravity of Sorrow 10th Level - Despair-Wrought Form 14th Level - Embrace of Oblivion

The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Umbral Lord Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. Umbral Lord Spells​ 3rd: Dissonant Whispers, Phantasmal Force, Calm Emotions, Cause Fear 5th: Summon Shadowspawn, Fear 7th: Shadow of Moil, Phantasmal Killer 9th: Dream, Modify Memory These spells reflect the patron’s nature—magic that distorts perception, suppresses emotion, and turns sorrow into power.

3rd-Level Umbral Lord Feature Your presence carries the emotional residue of the Shadowfell—haunting, weighty, and impossible to shake. Even the fiercest mind stumbles under the echo of forgotten regrets. You gain proficiency in Insight or Intimidation (your choice). Additionally, when you damage a creature with a Warlock spell or cantrip, you can mark it with Lingering Regret until the end of your next turn. The next time the creature makes an attack roll or ability check, it subtracts your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) from the roll, as if gripped by an emotion it cannot name. You can affect a number of creatures this way equal to your Warlock level divided by 3 (rounded up), regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

6th-Level Umbral Lord Feature Despair halts even the strongest charge. You call forth a field of emotional gravity—a stillness that seeps into flesh and will alike. As a bonus action, you designate a point within 60 feet. That point becomes the center of a 15-foot radius zone of heavy emotional drag until the start of your next turn. Each creature of your choice that starts its turn in the area or enters it for the first time on a turn must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have its speed reduced to 0 until the end of that turn. On a failed save, the creature also cannot Dash until the end of its next turn, as if the very act of movement had become too much to bear. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

10th-Level Umbral Lord Feature Your patron reshapes you into an embodiment of psychic weight. You don’t lash out with fire or blade—you unravel resolve, layer by layer. You gain resistance to necrotic and psychic damage. As an action, you can manifest a mantle of oppressive sorrow for 1 minute. While active: You emit a 20-foot radius aura of emotional gravity. Each enemy that starts its turn in the aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened until the start of its next turn. If a creature fails this saving throw a second time in a row, it becomes incapacitated until the start of its next turn, lost in overwhelming emotion. If a creature fails the save on three consecutive turns, it becomes Paralyzed until it succeeds on the Wisdom saving throw or is outside the aura of oppressive sorrow. The oppresive sorrow overrides any fear you are feeling, while the aura is active you are immune to frightened condition. You can use this feature once per long rest, or by expending a pact magic spell slot.

14th-Level Umbral Lord Feature You carry the end in your wake. When a soul slips away nearby, you seize its unraveling and cast it like a shadow across the battlefield. When a creature you can see within 60 feet drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to claim its fading essence. Choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) within 30 feet of the dying creature. Each must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 psychic damage and is frightened until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is not frightened. While frightened in this way, a creature loses all temporary hit points, cannot gain temporary hit points, and cannot benefit from healing. If a creature is already frightened by any means, it must use its action on its next turn to Dash away from you. If it cannot move, it instead takes an additional 5d10 psychic damage, writhing in place under the pressure of oblivion. You can use this reaction up to a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier per long rest. You are not a torch in the darkness. You are the hush after the flame goes out.

"Horn of the Regiment." Uphondo is the horn — the same word used for the horn of an ox, and for the two wings of warriors that run wide and close behind an enemy while the chest holds them in place. Ibutho is the regiment: an age-set, everyone who came of age in the same season, trained together and sent into the field together. Together the name means something closer to one of the horns than a warrior who has a horn — you are not a soldier who belongs to a regiment, you are a piece of it, and the piece that moves. Plural, the tradition is called the izimpondo zebutho, the regiment's horns. They do not wear armor. They wear a shield taller than a man and a spear shorter than an arm, and they arrive a day before anyone expects them. A regiment fights as one body: the chest holds the enemy in place, the horns run wide and close behind them, and the loins sit with their backs turned, waiting to be spent. A single warrior of this tradition carries the whole doctrine in their bones — hook the shield, open the ribs, stab once, call out.

Faerûn's closest parallel is the Shaar — the enormous savanna sweeping east from the Lake of Steam to the Eastern Shaar, where grassland nations rise and fall on the strength of their regiments rather than their walls. Shaaran warriors live and die by mobility across open ground, and a discipline built on encirclement, forced marches, and the shield line belongs there more naturally than anywhere in the North. South and west, the tradition shades into other things. On the Chultan Peninsula, the same drill contracts to jungle warfare — shorter sightlines, ambush instead of encirclement, the horns closing through undergrowth. Further south still, across the Great Sea, lies Katashaka, the continent almost nothing in the North has mapped; regiments trained in this style occasionally arrive from there with no interest in explaining themselves. A warrior of this tradition on the Sword Coast is almost always far from home; a veteran of a Shaaran ibutho who marched north with a caravan, or a Chultan raised to the shield in Port Nyanzaru and hired out of it. Features: 3rd Level - Ukuzivocavoca Kwebutho (Regimental Drill) 3rd Level - Izimpondo ZeNyathi (Horns of the Buffalo) 7th Level - Bamba Isihlangu (Hook the Shield) 7th Level - Uhambo Olude (Barefoot March) 10th Level - Bamba bese uhlasela (Chest and Loins) 15th Level - USUTHU! (Frightful Warcry) 18th Level - NGADLA! (Cry of Victory)

Unarmored Defense. While you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals the higher of 12 + your Strength modifier, or 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Strength modifier. You can use a Shield. You lose this benefit while a magic item is setting or increasing your Strength or Dexterity; a permanent increase you have already consumed, such as a Manual of Gainful Exercise, is your own. Spear and Shield. While wielding a Shield and a Spear or Javelin, that weapon deals 1d8 in one hand and its thrown ranges are doubled.

Once per turn when you hit with a melee weapon, you can mark the target Encircled until the end of your next turn. Only one creature at a time; marking a new one ends the old. An Encircled creature has its Speed reduced by 10 feet and can't Disengage. Once on each of your turns, when you or an ally hits it while you are both within 5 feet of it, that attack deals extra damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
documents.s: 3rd Level - Izimpondo ZeNyathi (Horns of the Buffalo)

documents.t: Once on each of your turns when you hit an Encircled creature, you can hook its guard aside (no action required). It makes a Strength save (DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failure, until the start of your next turn it gains no benefit from a Shield or Cover, and the next attack against it has Advantage.

You and up to five companions can travel at a Fast pace without the penalty to passive Perception, and can force march extra hours equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1) without saving against Exhaustion. You have Advantage on saves against Exhaustion from heat, thirst, or marching.

Hold the Chest. Enemies leaving your reach treat that space as Difficult Terrain. Send the Loins. As a Bonus Action, choose up to two allies within 30 feet who can see or hear you. Each can use their Reaction to move up to half their Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, ending closer to your Encircled creature if able. Uses equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regained on a Short or Long Rest.
documents.s: 10th Level - Bamba bese uhlasela (Chest and Loins)

documents.t: As a Bonus Action, each enemy within 30 feet that can see or hear you makes a Wisdom save (DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier) or is Frightened of you for 1 minute, the creature can make the save again at the end of each of their turns. Your Encircled creature saves with Disadvantage. Until the start of your next turn, the first attack each ally makes against your Encircled creature has Advantage. Once per Short or Long Rest.

Your Encircled damage rider no longer needs an ally — it applies whenever you are within 5 feet of the target — and it triggers on every hit rather than once per turn. When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with a melee attack, you can make one additional attack against a different creature: a melee attack within reach, or a thrown Spear or Javelin within normal range, drawing the weapon as part of the attack. You can move half your Speed first without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and the attack applies Encircled on a hit. Uses equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regained on a Long Rest.

The bow is an extension of the body. The draw is a breath, the release a strike, and the arrow is simply the fist arriving late. Throughout this subclass, bow means a Shortbow or Longbow. Features: 3rd Level - Way of the Bow 6th Level - Unerring Archer 11th Level - Perfected Arts 17th Level - Heart-Seeker

You gain proficiency with Longbows, and bows count as Monk weapons for you. You can also use the Mastery property of any bow you wield. Arrow Arts. After you attack with a bow on your turn, you can spend Focus Points as a Bonus Action to loose one special arrow: Focused Shot (1 point). Make one bow attack with Advantage. On a hit, add one roll of your Martial Arts die to the damage. Split Shot (1 point). Make two bow attacks with Disadvantage against two creatures within 30 feet of each other. Volley (2 points). Choose a Line 120 feet long and 5 feet wide originating from you, or a 15-foot-radius Sphere centered within 60 feet. Each creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking Piercing damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

You don't have Disadvantage on ranged attack rolls because a hostile creature is within 5 feet of you. Focused Quiver. You can conjure an arrow as part of any bow attack or Arrow Art, so you never need ammunition. Conjured arrows deal Force damage instead of Piercing.

Focused Shot adds two rolls of your Martial Arts die, and the target has Disadvantage on its next saving throw before the start of your next turn. Split Shot makes three attacks instead of two. Volley deals four rolls of your Martial Arts die, and you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) to be unaffected.

Inescapable Arrow. As an Action, spend 4 Focus Points to hit one creature you can see within your bow's long range — no attack roll is made. It makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 10d12 Piercing damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage dies.

Monk Subclass — D&D 5e (2014) (HB) Homebrew Revision Sun Soul monks channel their ki into searing light and solar flame, empowering their strikes, projecting radiant energy, and eventually embodying the brilliance of the sun. Features: 3rd Level - Radiant Sun Soul 6th Level - Blinding Radiance 11th Level - Solar Ascension 17th Level - Radiance Incarnate

Whenever you make an unarmed strike as part of your Attack action, Martial Arts, or Flurry of Blows, you can replace that attack with a Radiant Sun Bolt. Make a ranged spell attack using Dexterity as your spellcasting ability against a creature within 60 feet. You are proficient with this attack. On a hit, the target takes radiant damage equal to your Martial Arts die + your Dexterity modifier.
Your unarmed strikes can deal radiant damage instead of their normal damage type.
You can cause your body to shed bright light in a 10-foot emanation and dim light for an additional 10 feet. You can activate or suppress this light at will (no action required).

After you hit a creature with a radiant unarmed strike or Radiant Sun Bolt, you can use your bonus action and spend 1 ki point to force it to make a Constitution saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failure, the creature is blinded until the end of your next turn. On a success, it is unaffected.
When you use Step of the Wind, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover until the end of your current turn.

As an action, you create an explosion of radiant energy centered on a point you can see within 120 feet. Creatures of your choice within a 20-foot-radius sphere must make a Constitution saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes radiant damage equal to four Martial Arts dice, is pushed up to 15 feet away from the center, and suffers Solar Burn. On a successful save, it takes half as much radiant damage and suffers no additional effects. Solar Burn. The target takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of its turns for up to 3 rounds. It can use a bonus action to extinguish the flames. Multiple applications refresh the duration instead of stacking. You can use Searing Sunburst once without spending ki, regaining that use when you finish a long rest. Additional uses cost 3 ki points each.

As a bonus action, you can spend 5 ki points to embody the full brilliance of the sun for 1 minute. The transformation ends early if you’re incapacitated or choose to end it (no action required). While transformed, you gain the following benefits: Solar Flight. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover. Blazing Soul. Once on each of your turns when you hit with an unarmed strike or Radiant Sun Bolt, you deal additional radiant damage equal to two Martial Arts dice. Sun Shield. When a creature within 10 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to deal radiant damage equal to two Martial Arts dice. Eyes of the Sun. You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would impose the blinded condition. Wrath of the Sun. Once during the transformation, you can use your action to unleash a wave of solar energy. Creatures of your choice within 30 feet must make a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes radiant damage equal to five Martial Arts dice and falls prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn’t knocked prone.
Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Intelligence score increases by 1.
Like humans, naga reach adulthood in their late teens. They show no signs of aging beyond that point except for growing larger, so in theory, a naga could live well over a century.
Most naga are either neutral or neutral evil in alignment.
Naga stand about 5 feet tall when upright, but the total length of their bodies, head to tail, ranges from 10 to as much as 20 feet. Your size is Medium.
Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Using your tail as a propellant you can give yourself a speed boost. Immediately after you move at least 10 feet in a straight line, you can propel yourself 15 feet in the same direction without provoking opportunity attacks. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Your fanged maw and constricting serpentine body are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with your bite, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d4 + your Strength modifier, and your target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier). On a failed save, the target takes 1d4 poison damage. If you hit with your constrict attack, you deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, and if the target is one size larger or smaller than the naga, the target is grappled (escape DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and you can’t constrict another target.
You are immune to poison damage and can’t be poisoned.
You gain proficiency with the poisoner’s kit.
You can speak, read, and write Common and Naga.
Your Dexterity score increases by 2. Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

Although elves reach physical maturity at about the same age as humans, the elven understanding of adulthood goes beyond physical growth to encompass worldly experience. An elf typically claims adulthood and an adult name around the age of 100 and can live to be 750 years old.
Avariel typically range from under four and a half to over five and a half feet tall and have slender builds with hollow bones. Your size is Medium.
Your base walking speed is 30 feet.
Thanks to your wings, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed. You can’t use this flying speed if you’re wearing medium or heavy armor.

Accustomed to twilit mountains and the night sky, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
You have proficiency in the Perception skill.
You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can’t put you to sleep.

Elves don’t need to sleep. Instead, they meditate deeply, remaining semiconscious, for 4 hours a day. (The Common word for such meditation is “trance.”) While meditating, you can dream after a fashion; such dreams are actually mental exercises that have become reflexive through years of practice. After resting in this way, you gain the same benefit that a human does from 8 hours of sleep.

You can speak, read, and write Elvish and one other language of your choice, typically Common, also known as Thorasta. Avariel typically speak the Skaevrym variant of Thorasta which is derived from North Eeastern Faerun near Sossel, the region nearest their settlement atop Mount Sundabar. Elvish is fluid, with subtle intonations and intricate grammar, which some Avariel speak with a more relaxed and breathy intonation akin to Auran, and the language is sometimes mixed with their own unique form of sign language based around aerial movement. Involving things such as flaps, stalls, and wind dips. It was a less subtle sign language than those of non-flying races, having been developed primarily for communication during flight.

Prerequisite: Changeling Your ability to shapechange is more than skin deep, and you are able to assume more forms than the average Changeling. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Consititution score by 1, to a maximum of 20 When you use your Shapechanging trait, you can choose one of these benefits which lasts until you change your shape again: - Darkvision You adapt your eyes and gain Darkvision out to 60ft. - Aquatic Adaption You sprout gills and are able to breath underwater, and you gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. - Natural Weapons You grow claws, fangs, spines, horns or a different natural weapon of your choice. Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage as appropriate, and you are considered proficient with unarmed strikes. - Wings You grow wings, which can take on whatever appearance/shape you desire. You gain 30 ft. of flying speed. - Extra Appendage You grow a prehensile tail, tentacles, crab claws, or another limb of your choice, which can only be used to grapple someone as an action (even if your main hands are currently full), and cannot be used to hold equipment, weapons, or any other objects. You can use these features an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus (shared among all), resetting on a Long Rest.

A rare type of kobold, with a stronger connection to true dragons. Often bearing the scale colors of their related dragons, and even some of their elemental abilities. Dragonwrought kobolds also tend to posses wings, and increased durability compared to the more common kobolds.
Your character can speak, read and write common and draconic.
Your draconic lineage makes you closer to the dragons than other kobolds. Your creature type is Dragon.
Dragonwrought kobolds stand between 2 and 4 feet tall, and weigh between 30 and 45 pounds. Your size is small or tiny.
Your base walking speed in 30 feet.
You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
You either hatched with, or later grew a pair of leathery dragon wings. At 5th level, they become usable, granting you a flying speed of 30 feet.
You have a knack for appraising gemstones and other such treasures. By spending 1 minute studying an object, you can determine its approximate value to the nearest 100 gp.

Your connection to dragons can manifest in a number of ways, choose one of the following traits when you select this race: Draconic Endurance - Your hit point maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 every time you gain a level. Unhindered - Magic cannot cause you to have the paralyzed condition. Elemental Potency - Once on each of your turns when you deal damage, you can deal 1d6 extra damage of a type correlating to your draconic lineage

Physical Description Faerie elves are roughly the same height as gnomes but weigh roughly 25 to 60 lbs. Faeries tend to have more vibrant eye colors of shimmering greens, blues, and reds. They have a pair of transparent wings that allow them to fly. Other than that they look like most wood elves. History Although not many people have seen these crossbreeds, the faerie elf is a mixture of a elf and a fey. They tend to keep their societies and culture hidden from public view. Faerie elves are known to have many conflicts within their society, from what little has been observed. They tend to have very different views of other races and cultures. Society Faerie elves tend to keep to themselves and tend to hide from other outside sources, mainly due to the harsh discrimination and prejudice their ancestors have experienced. They are buried deep within forests and caves and have a strong sense of family. They tend to have a hard time developing new relations with others, especially if they're neither fey, elf, or faerie. The ones who do leave the villages tend to be brave adventurers determined to prove the old ways are over. Elf Subrace Ability Score Increase​ Your Charisma score increases by 1. Size​ Unlike most elves Faerie elves range from 3 to over 4 foot tall but have slender builds and weigh very little. Your size is Small. Speed​ Your base walking speed is 20 feet and your flying speed is 30 feet. Fairy Wings​ You have a pair of light, transparent wings that grant you a fly speed of 30-feet, allowing you a certain degree of flight. However, these wings can only fly up to a height of 10 feet, any higher and they fail until you are 10 feet above the ground again. This flight speed cannot negate damage inflicted from falling a height of 20 feet or more, only halve it. You lose your flying speed until you complete a short or long rest if they are directly exposed to water. Tranquil Magic​ The typical faerie focuses more on their mind rather than their strength. You know one cantrip of your choice from the cleric spell list. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

Be it from the merging of peaceful clans, or a more unwelcome coupling of savage gnolls and their victims, some cases of Half-Gnolls can appear. Half-Gnoll's heritages are human and gnoll, as different as night and day. The result of this often portrays itself as instinctual and common sense confusion: with two separate parts fighting on what the proper choice is. The only thing all can agree on is the strong sense of being part of a group, be it a village or a hunting pack. Whether they attempt to do so with humans or gnolls, they often face an uphill battle. Half-Gnolls still have a craving for chaos and killing that their Gnoll blood possesses, but it is mostly easier to control, and can often be quelled with hunting and the occasional consuming of any blood and guts. If they end up killing or consuming an intelligent creature, however, there is still a high risk of them going on similar rampages.

When determining your character’s ability scores, increase one score by 2 and increase a different score by 1, or increase three different scores by 1. Follow this rule regardless of the method you use to determine the scores, such as rolling or point buy. The “Quick Build” section for your character’s class offers suggestions on which scores to increase. You can follow those suggestions or ignore them, but you can’t raise any of your scores above 20.

Half-Gnolls usually mature by the age of ten, and they often die of various reasons by the age of 35, but there are cases where they live up to the age of 75 without a real sign of old age, before seeming to lose all their strength immediately and falling into an eternal slumber.
Half Gnolls are lean, lanky and tower over humans, often found in the range between 6 and 7 feet tall. Your size is Medium.
Your base walking speed is 35 feet
Thanks to your gnoll blood, you can see in 60ft of darkness as if in bright light, and the rest in dim light. You can't discern colour in the dark, only black and white.
Your jaws are a natural weapon, and your mouth is a breeding ground for disease. If you hit with this bite attack, you deal 1d4 + STR piercing damage plus an additional 1d4 poison damage.
You gain advantage on any Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) checks that involve smell.
When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with a melee attack on your turn, you may use a bonus action to move up to half your speed and make a bite attack

You can speak, read and write Common, Gnoll. Gnoll is an abrasive language, communicating in growls, barks and broken Abyssal. Beings that can speak Gnoll can understand general concepts and few keywords in Abyssal. It has no script of its own, often using Infernal script.

Half-goblins were humanoids born from a pairing of goblins with another race, such as humans. They could be found wherever such a pairing took place. Half-goblins with human blood were taller than regular goblins. Their eyes had colors on the human spectrum, such as blue, rather than the standard goblin red. Ability Score Increase: Your Constitution or Dexterity score increases by 2 and your Charisma score increases by 1. Age: Half goblins lives a tiny bit longer than normal goblins, maturing at around 8 and living about 70 to 75 years. Alignment: Many have a cynical and chaotic outlook in life. Size: While some are short, your size is Medium. Speed: Your base walking speed is 35 feet. Darkvision: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray. Experienced Liar: You are proficient in the Deception skill. Scheming Wrath: Living under everyone's heel has made you incredibly insidious with your methods. When you target a creature which has dealt you damage previously with an attack or spell, you can channel your rage to roll the attack or spell with advantage. Once you use this trait, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest. Necessary Tools: You are proficient with 1 simple weapon and 1 tool of your choice. Languages: You can speak, read and write in Common, Goblin, and one other language of your choice. Random Height and Weight Base height: 4'0" Height modifier: +2d12 Base weight: 50 lb. Weight modifier: x(1d20) lb. Height = Base height + height modifier. Weight = Base weight + (height modifier x weight modifier)

Cowardly tricksters which are often used as battle fodder, and yet even so they are deft thieves and shapeshifters. Ability Score Improvements: When determining your character’s ability scores, increase one score by 2 and increase a different score by 1, or increase three different scores by 1. You can't raise any of your scores above 20. Age: Imps reach maturity at around 5 and live until they are killed. Creature Type: Imps are considered fiends. Size: Your size is tiny. Speed: Your walking speed is 20ft. Languages: You speak common and infernal Darkvision: Thanks to your infernal heritage, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray. Hellish Resistance: You gain resistance to fire damage. Fiendish Trickery: You gain proficiency in Stealth or Deception checks, and starting at 5th level you can cast Invisibility once per long rest. Flight: You have a flying speed of 40ft while not wearing medium or heavy armor. Barbed Stinger: You have a have stinger as a natural weapon attack which deals 1d4+your dexterity or strength modifier piercing damage and any target hit by this attack must make a dc 11 constitution saving throw or take 2d4 poison damage.
Your Dexterity score increases by 2. You may put +1 to any ability that does not already benefit from a racial ASI.
A typical kitsune lives to 600 to 1000. It gains an additional century for every tail it grows, to a maximum of 9 tails.
As kitsune are natural tricksters, they tend towards gentler forms of chaos.
You are a fey.
A kitsune is usually between 4'5inch and 5'10inch. Your size is Medium.
Your base walking speed is 35 feet.
You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Much like the foxes they resemble, kitsunes have heightened senses. You are proficient in the Perception skill.
Your fey lineage gives you advantage on saving throws against being charmed. Magic cannot put you to sleep.

You can appear as a human indefinitely using a very simple illusion magic. However, on a (DC 10 + proficiency bonus + Charisma Modifier) Investigation check, a person looking directly at you can tell that you are not what you appear. You always appear to be the same human when you cast this spell. While in human form you have -1 to all dice rolls.

You have one tail when you are born and every 3 levels you gain another tail; lvl3 = 2, lvl6 = 3, etc. A kitsune's tails are a symbol of growth and realization for themselves and reflects how powerful they are. To your DM's discretion, A kitsune can also grow tail's for pivotal moments in its life or personal growth.

So long as your tails are not severed, you can cast certain spells. You know the dancing lights cantrip. At 3rd level you gain the ability to cast faerie fire once per long rest. Charisma is your casting ability for these spells.
You can read and write both Common and Sylvan.
Once mad servants of ancient gods, kuo-toa are strange, amphibious humanoids capable of surviving both land and sea.
Humanoid
+2 Wisdom, +1 Constitution
Mature by 10, live up to 70 years.
Medium
Walk 30 ft., Swim 30 ft.
You can breathe air and water.
Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape a grapple or restraint.
Disadvantage on attack rolls and Perception checks relying on sight in sunlight.
Undercommon, Aquan

Prerequisite Leonin Description Your ancestry manifests in your fierceness; the pride of Oreskos echoes through you. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the frightened condition on yourself. Your natural weapons count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. The range of your Daunting Roar trait increases to 30 feet and you can add your Charisma modifier to its Save DC. Additionally, you regain a use of this trait when you bring a Huge or larger creature to 0 hit points.
Level 20 Cycle: You must have completed 20 levels of Monk with no multiclassing.

When you take this prestige class, choose two additional skills from the Monk skill list. You gain proficiency in both.
Your training has transcended mortal limits. Your Martial Arts die is now 1d12.

You can now use your Uncanny Metabolism feature twice per Long Rest, the second time you use it you only recover half of your total focus points. Additionally, when you use it, you regain a number of Hit Points equal to four times your Prestige Level.

You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against melee, ranged, and energy-based attack rolls. When you do so, you can roll an additional Martial arts die and add the result to the damage reduction. The Deflection damage is increased to 4 martial arts die rolls

Your talents expand, You may choose the same Monk tradition, or you may choose a new one to reflect the different studies and focus learned from another tradition. At PL 23, PL 26, PL 31 and PL37, you gain more features from your Monk tradition.

At PL 24, 28, 32, 36, and 39, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or two ability scores by 1. As normal, you cannot increase a score above 20 (unless another feature allows it). You may select a Feat instead of an ASI.

When a creature successfully saves against your stunning strike feature, their speed is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn and they are considered to be dazed for the same duration, your next attack against that creature will have advantage. Additionally, once per turn when you attack a creature that is already dazed from one of your stunning strike attempts, you can attempt another stunning strike. The target makes the save with disadvantage.
Your strikes are consistently devastating. When you roll a Martial Arts die, you treat any roll lower than a 2 as a 2. This minimum increases to 3 at PL 32, and 4 at PL 38.

At 27th level, your monk’s training and mental fortitude allows you to resist assaults on the mind. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Intelligence or Wisdom saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
When you use your Step of the Wind feature, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed until the end of your current turn. Additionally your movement speed increases by 20 feet.

documents.t: Any time you roll a Martial Arts die (for damage or features), you can expend 1 Focus Point to roll an additional Martial Arts die and add the result to the first roll.
Whenever you fail a saving throw that deals damage, you can use your perfect deflection ability to reduce the damage. You cannot however deflect the damage back if you reduce the damage to 0.

Your mental and physical discipline grants you expertise in your defenses. Choose two saving throws in which you are proficient: One Major Save (Dexterity, Constitution, or Wisdom). One Minor Save (Strength, Intelligence, or Charisma). You add your Proficiency Bonus twice to those saving throws instead of once.
You gain an additional Reaction on every round of combat. This reaction can only be used for Monk class features (such as Deflect Attacks or Slow Fall).
The cost of your superior defense or empty body is now 3 Focus Points, and you are invisible for the duration. Additionally, your heightened senses give you blindsight to 30 feet.

Your body and soul reach their ultimate form. You gain 6 ability points to distribute between your Dexterity and Wisdom scores as you choose. You can increase the ability scores to a maximum of 30 with this feature.
Graceful denizens of the sea, merfolk are at home beneath the waves, rarely surfacing except to defend their homes or trade with land-dwellers.
Humanoid
+2 Dexterity, +1 Charisma
Mature at the same rate as humans and live about 120 years.
Medium (7–9 feet from head to tail)
Walk 10 ft., Swim 40 ft.
You can breathe air and water.
Common, Aquan
You know the light cantrip. Once per long rest, you can cast color spray (Charisma).
You have darkvision (60 ft.) and resistance to cold damage.
You know the friends cantrip. Once per long rest, you can cast charm person (Charisma).
Your Wisdom score increases by 2 and your Constitution score increases by 1.
Myconids reach maturity at 6 years old and can live to be over 1000 with the oldest ones becoming sovereigns.
Most myconids are True Neutral with good myconids are fairly common and evil myconids are very rare.
Myconids range from 4 to 8 feet and weigh 70 to 180 lbs. Your size is Medium.
Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Accustomed to the darkness of the underdark, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 120 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern colours in darkness, only shades of grey.
You have disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight whenever you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

Your fists are home to toxic spores that can harm your enemies upon contact, and count as natural weapons that you can use to make unarmed attacks. If you hit with them, you deal 1d4 + your Strength modifier poison damage.

As an action, you can eject spores at one creature you can see within 15 foot of you. At the start of the target’s turn, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw equal to 8 + your proficiency modifier + your Constitution modifier or be stunned for 1 minute or until it takes damage. The target can repeat the saving throw at the start of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The effect also ends if the target takes damage. You regain use of this trait once you have completed a short or long rest.

You may, as an action, extend rapport spores in a 20-foot radius. These spores can go around corners and affect only creatures with an Intelligence of 2 or higher that aren't undead, constructs, or elementals. Affected creatures can communicate telepathically with one another while within 60 feet. The effect lasts for 1 hour.

At 1st level, you gain the ability to start fires with a touch. As an action, you can magically ignite a flammable object you touch with your hand—an object such as a torch, a piece of tinder, or the hem of drapes.

Starting at 1st level, you can unleash the phoenix fire that blazes within you. As a bonus action, you magically wreathe yourself in swirling fire, as your eyes glow like hot coals. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits: You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Any creature takes fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier if it hits you with a melee attack from within 5 feet of you or if it touches you. Whenever you roll fire damage on your turn, the roll gains a bonus to equal to your Charisma modifier. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Starting at 6th level, the fiery energy within you grows restless and vengeful. In the face of defeat, it surges outward to preserve you in a fiery roar. If you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to draw on the spark of the phoenix. You are instead reduced to 1 hit point, and each creature within 10 feet of you takes fire damage equal to half your sorcerer level + your Charisma modifier. If you use this feature while under the effects of your Mantle of Flame, this feature instead deals fire damage equal to your sorcerer level + double your Charisma modifier, and your Mantle of Flame immediately ends. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Starting at 14th level, your fire spells soothe and restore you. When you expend a spell slot to cast a spell that includes a fire damage roll, you regain hit points equal to the slot's level + your Charisma modifier.

At 18th level, you finally master the spark of fire that dances within you. While under the effect of your Mantle of Flame feature, you gain additional benefits: You have a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover. You have resistance to Poison & Fire If you use your Phoenix Spark, that feature deals an extra 20 fire damage to each creature.

Prerequisite Elf Description You are descended from a master of the double-bladed scimitar, and some of that mastery has passed on to you. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Dexterity or Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20. While you are holding a double-bladed scimitar with two hands, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. A double-bladed scimitar has the finesse property when you wield it.
Seal-folk who slip between human and animal forms, selkies are gentle and mysterious beings tied to coastal waters.
Monstrosity
+2 Dexterity, +1 Wisdom
Up to 150 years.
Medium
Walk 30 ft., Swim 40 ft.
You can assume the form of a seal by donning or removing your sealskin (use a seal stat block).
You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can’t put you to sleep.
Common, Aquan
When determining your character’s ability scores, increase one score by 2 and increase a different score by 1, or increase three different scores by 1. You can't raise any of your scores above 20.
You are a construct.
Your size is small or medium (your choice).
Your base walking speed is 30 feet.
You speak Common, and Deep Speech.

When you take a long rest, you must spend at least six hours in an inactive, motionless state, rather than sleeping. In this state, you appear inert, but it doesn’t render you unconscious, and you can see and hear as normal.

If the Mending spell is cast on you, you can spend a Hit Die, roll it, and regain a number of hit points equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point). In addition, your nature has allowed you to benefit from several spells that preserve life but that normally don't affect Constructs: Cure Wounds, Healing Word, Mass Cure Wounds, Mass Healing Word, and Spare the Dying.

You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see, provided the creature is within 30ft of you. You don't need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your telepathic utterances, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language. Either creature can break this connection at any time.

Crystalline nature is represented by the following benefits: You have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned, and you have resistance to poison damage. You don’t need to eat, drink, or breathe. You are immune to disease. You don't need to sleep.

Your crystalline shell provides you a base AC of 17 (your Dexterity modifier doesn’t affect this number). You can’t wear light, medium, or heavy armor, but if you are using a shield, you can apply the shield’s bonus as normal.
You gain proficiency in Arcana or Religion checks.

The reanimated corpse of a once living creature given new purpose in undeath. Often created by necromancers, sapient skeletons or other undead can arise when rituals go awry. Such skeletons walk in undeath for as long as they remain intact, often seeing the world undergo grand changes should they go undisturbed.
You know common and one other language of your choice.
One of the most famous examples of it, your creature type is undead.
Skeletons come in many shapes and sizes. Your size is medium or small.
You have a walking speed of 30 feet.
Bludgeoning damage dealt to you is doubled.

Being undead sets you drastically apart from living creatures, granting you the following effects: You are immune to poison damage, and the poisoned and exhaustion conditions. You do not bleed. You succeed on death saving throws on a d20 roll of 5 or higher, rather than 10 or higher. Nothing can cause you to add more than one failed death saving throw at once. You do not need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe. If you die, you are destroyed, and cannot be returned to undeath via resurrection spells such as revivify or raise dead.
You are proficient in light armor, medium armor, shields, and two weapons of your choice.
You gain one skill and one tool proficiency of your choice.

When you would take necrotic damage, you can choose to instead gain temporary hit points equal to the damage you would have taken. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Star Spawn are created emissaries for various outer beings, they present themselves as somewhat humanoid with some “oddities” associated with the eldritch being that sent them.
When determining your character’s ability scores, increase one score by 2 and increase a different score by 1, or increase three different scores by 1. You can't raise any of your scores above 20.
You are an aberration.
Your size is small or medium (your choice)
Your walking speed is 30ft.
You speak Common, and Deep Speech.

Your body possesses an unnatural resilience and autonomy. You do not need to breathe, eat, drink, or sleep. Magic cannot force you to sleep. To gain the benefits of a long rest, you must spend 8 hours in a motionless state.

When you are forced to make an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you can call upon the unnatural resilience granted by your eldritch connection, granting yourself advantage on that saving throw (no action required). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
You commune with the entity that guides you. You can cast the spell Augury once per day, requiring no material components. The spell otherwise functions as normal.
Due to your nature you are more resistant to things that would terrify others, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
You gain proficiency in a skill or tool of your choice.

Psionic Prestige Class Every psi-adept eventually finds the same wall. The soulknife learns to sharpen thought into a blade but never learns what else thought can be. The psi warrior learns to shove the world with their mind but never learns to unmake it. The wall is not a limit of power — it is a limit of vocabulary. The Mystic is what happens when a mortal stops using the gift as a tool and begins speaking the language it was cut from.

Level 20 Cycle. You must have completed a full 20-level paragon cycle satisfying the Purity Rule. The Purity Rule. That cycle must have consisted entirely of levels from one of the following, with no multiclassing: Rogue (Soulknife) Fighter (Psi Warrior) Sorcerer (Aberrant Mind) Warlock (Great Old One Patron) Hit Die: 1d8 per Mystic level Your entry path determines your Order. You do not choose it. Entry Order Soulknife The Whetstone Psi Warrior The Aegis Aberrant Mind The Aberrant Bloom Great Old One The Hollow Crown

This class is additive. You already have a combat loop that works — Sneak Attack, Flurry of Blows, Extra Attack, Metamagic, Eldritch Blast. The Mystic does not replace it and should never compete with it for your Action. Almost every discipline is a Bonus Action, a Reaction, or a rider on something you were already doing. The handful that cost a full Magic action are Ascendant-band effects meant for the turn you decide to end an encounter. Your Manifestation Dice are a separate pool from any psionic resource you already had. The two never convert. Your Order deepens the old pool across five growth points; the class runs the new one.

At the start of each of your turns, you can expend any number of your Manifestation Dice, rolling them all at once. The total is your Manifested Psi for the round. That psi is available until the start of your next turn, including during other creatures' turns. Any left over is lost. Generating psi costs no action. Expending dice is one decision, made once per round, before you know what the round holds. You regain half your expended Manifestation Dice (rounded up) on a Short Rest, and all of them on a Long Rest.

When you aren't in initiative, there are no turns to key off. You can expend Manifestation Dice at any time with no action; the resulting psi lasts 1 minute or until spent, whichever comes first. Any effect you pay for runs its full written duration regardless.

Two phrases appear throughout this class and they mean different things: "A roll of your Manifestation Die" refers only to the size of the die on the table — d8, d10, or d12. You roll one and use the number. Nothing is expended. Your pool is untouched. "Expend a die" means the die leaves your pool and must be recovered on a rest. So a feature that adds a roll of your Manifestation Die to damage costs you nothing and works every round forever. A feature that says expend is spending a resource. The same distinction applies to Psionic Energy Dice.

documents.t: Band Cost Typical action Dice to cover it Unlocks Reflex 2–4 psi Rider, Reaction, Bonus Action one die covers two PL 21 Committed 6–9 psi Bonus Action or Reaction one die PL 23 Ascendant 11–14 psi Magic action two dice PL 33 There is no per-activation cap to track. If you can afford it and the band is unlocked, you can use it. Psi is the only thing you spend. A psychic focus costs nothing and runs continuously, so a turn where you expend no dice still has psionics in it — just passive ones.

Any feature that rewards you for reducing a creature to 0 Hit Points triggers only on creatures of Challenge Rating 1 or higher that you did not summon, create, or command. This covers Relentless, Feed, Siphon, Warped Blade, and anything like them. Minions are not a resource farm.

No feature of this class ever lets you concentrate on, or maintain, more than one spell at a time. Disciplines can stack with each other and with a spell where a feature allows it, but a second spell always ends the first. This holds regardless of Fractured Concentration, Psionic Mastery, or any combination of them.

A PL 26 Whetstone Soulknife. 8d10 Manifestation Dice. Start of turn. She expends one die, rolls a 6. 6 psi for the round. Action. Attack action with Psychic Blades, as normal. Sneak Attack, as normal. On the hit she folds in Mindspike's Lance — 3 psi, no action — for an extra 3d8 and an Intelligence save. 3 left. Bonus Action. Cunning Action to Disengage, exactly as she always did. Someone else's turn. The wizard gets targeted. She spends her Reaction on Intellect Fortress's Ward, 3 psi. 0 left. Start of her next turn. The 3 evaporates. She decides again.

documents.t: Any feature referring to your level uses your Prestige Level (PL) = 20 + your Mystic level. Discipline save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Psionic Ability modifier. Discipline attack modifier = Proficiency Bonus + Psionic Ability modifier.
Choose two additional skills from Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, and Religion.

Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. That ability powers every feature of this class. The choice is permanent, alterable only by retraining, and does not change the ability used by your entry subclass. Soulknives may instead choose Dexterity — see The Whetstone.

You know the number of disciplines shown on the table, chosen from the Shared Disciplines list. Your Order grants two Order Disciplines that don't count against this number and that no other Order can learn. On each level in this class you can swap one discipline for another.

As a Bonus Action, choose one discipline you know. You gain that discipline's ○ Focus benefit, which lasts until you are Incapacitated or until you use a Bonus Action to focus on a different discipline. Focus costs nothing. It is not Concentration — it can't be broken by damage, and it doesn't interfere with a spell or discipline you are concentrating on. Focus and manifestation are independent. Focusing on a discipline does not let you activate its options for free, and activating a discipline's options does not require you to be focused on it. You can be focused on Iron Skin for the AC while spending all your psi on Mindspike, and you can activate any option of any discipline you know regardless of what you are focused on. In practice you set a focus once at the start of a fight and leave it. Switching costs a Bonus Action, so mid-combat changes should be a deliberate call — dropping the Stealth focus to pick up +1 AC when the fighting starts, for instance.

Manifestation Dice are their own resource. They are not Psionic Energy Dice, Focus Points, Sorcery Points, or spell slots, and never convert into each other in either direction. Your entry subclass's resource continues to work exactly as written, on its own recovery schedule — and your Order deepens it at each of its five growth points.

Once per Short or Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you can expend any number of Manifestation Dice and regain Hit Points equal to the total rolled, rather than gaining psi from them. This is the mirror of Consumptive Power: that feature turns blood into thought, this one turns thought into blood. Neither can pay for the other — Mystical Recovery spends dice, not psi, so psi gained from Consumptive Power can never be converted back into Hit Points.

You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 1 mile, and to any creature you've previously touched or linked with on the same plane. Language is unnecessary, though the creature must understand at least one language or be telepathic. You can maintain links with up to your Psionic Ability modifier in willing creatures, letting them speak to each other through you.

After each Long Rest, choose two ability scores. You gain saving throw proficiency in them until your next Long Rest. If you are already proficient in a chosen ability, add half your Proficiency Bonus again to those saves instead.
At PL 24, 28, 32, 36, and 39. Increase one score by 2 or two by 1, max 20 unless stated otherwise, or take a Feat.
Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon or Unarmed Strike, or when you deal damage with a spell or discipline, deal an extra 2d8 Psychic damage, rising to 3d8 at PL 35.
When you roll a Manifestation Die, treat any result below 2 as a 2. This rises to 3 at PL 33 and 4 at PL 38.

At any point during your turn, you can spend up to twice your Proficiency Bonus in Hit Points to gain an equal amount of Manifested Psi. No action required. Your current and maximum Hit Points are both reduced by that amount; the reduction to your maximum can't be lessened and lasts until a Long Rest. Usable a number of times per Long Rest equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This is your correction when you underestimated the round.

You can maintain the psychic focus of two disciplines at once, gaining both benefits. Setting a focus while two are active replaces one of your choice. It still costs one Bonus Action to change either.

Once per turn when you activate a discipline, choose one: Amplify. The damage dice of that manifestation are maximized. Widen. Double the area or range of that manifestation, or add one target within its range. Entrench. Double the duration of that manifestation. Overchannel only ever affects the discipline you are activating. It does not touch weapon damage, Sneak Attack, Martial Arts dice, spell dice, Psionic Energy Dice, or any other damage in the same attack or turn — only the dice printed in the manifestation itself. You take Psychic damage equal to the psi spent, which can't be reduced or prevented, and have Disadvantage on Constitution saves for concentration until the end of your next turn. Overchannel can't be applied to Ascendant-band options.

Concentrate on two disciplines at once, provided both were paid with Manifested Psi. You can't concentrate on a spell while doing so — see the one-spell rule. On a Constitution save to maintain, roll once with Disadvantage; failure loses both.

Once per Long Rest, at the start of your turn, you can gain Manifested Psi equal to your Mystic level — not your Prestige Level — without expending any dice. At PL 34 that is 14 psi, rising to 20 at PL 40. Until the start of your next turn, you can concentrate on any number of disciplines paid for with that psi simultaneously; concentrating on anything else ends them all.

Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing; immunity to Psychic damage. You no longer age; immune to disease, Poison damage, and the Poisoned condition. No need to eat, drink, or breathe. If you would die, roll a d20. On a 10+ you discorporate instead, vanishing with your gear at 0 Hit Points and reappearing at a place of your choice 1d3 days later on that plane, with the benefits of a Long Rest.

Inexhaustible. Once per Short or Long Rest, at the start of your turn, if you have no unspent Manifestation Dice, regain a number equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded up. Perfect Manifestation. Once per Long Rest, when you expend Manifestation Dice at the start of your turn, treat every one of them as its maximum. This applies only to Manifestation Dice rolled for psi — not to damage dice, Psionic Energy Dice, or any other roll. Untouchable Will. Immune to the Charmed and Frightened conditions, to thought-reading and lie detection, and to possession or memory alteration. Mastery Redoubled. You gain a second use of Psionic Mastery.

Each discipline has one ○ Focus benefit and several paid options. The Focus applies only while you are focused on that discipline (see PL 21: Psychic Focus); the paid options can be used any time, focused or not. Saves are against your Discipline save DC. Action cost is listed on every option. Rider means no action at all — you fold it into an attack or spell you were already making. Mark Band Cost ○ Focus Free. Always on while focused. ● Reflex 2–4 psi ●● Committed 6–9 psi ●●● Ascendant 11–14 psi Most manifestations do not require Concentration. Where one does, it is marked.

○ Focus. Your psionic damage ignores Resistance to Psychic damage. ● Lance (3 psi) — Rider. Once per turn when you hit a creature or damage it with a spell, it makes an Intelligence save, taking 3d8 Psychic damage on a failure, half on a success. ●● Shatter (8 psi) — Bonus Action. One creature within 60 ft makes an Intelligence save, taking 8d8 Psychic damage and being Incapacitated until the end of your next turn on a failure, half damage on a success. ●●● Erase (13 psi) — Magic action. One creature within 60 ft makes an Intelligence save. Failure: 16d8 Psychic damage and Stunned for 1 minute, save repeats at end of each of its turns. Success: half damage.

○ Focus. Once per turn when you hit with a weapon or spell attack, push or pull the target 10 ft. ● Thrust (2 psi) — Rider. Once per turn when you hit, the target makes a Strength save or is pushed 20 ft and knocked Prone. ●● Wave (7 psi) — Bonus Action. Each creature in a 30-ft cone makes a Strength save, taking 6d8 Force damage and being pushed 30 ft and knocked Prone on a failure, half damage on a success.

○ Focus. +1 AC. ● Brace (3 psi) — Reaction, when you take damage: halve it. ●● Adamant (8 psi) — Bonus Action. For 1 minute you have Resistance to all damage and can't be moved against your will or knocked Prone. No concentration.

○ Focus. You don't provoke Opportunity Attacks. ● Step (2 psi) — Bonus Action. Teleport up to 30 ft to a space you can see. ●● Slip (6 psi) — Reaction, when you're targeted by an attack or forced to make a save: teleport up to 120 ft to a space you can see, bringing one willing creature within 5 ft. If this moves you out of the effect, you're unaffected.

○ Focus. Advantage on Stealth checks. ● Fade (4 psi) — Bonus Action. You're Invisible for 1 minute. Concentration. ●● Unseen (8 psi) — Bonus Action. As Fade, no concentration, and you can't be detected by divination magic, blindsight, tremorsense, or truesight.

○ Focus. You can't be surprised, and you add your Psionic Ability modifier to initiative. ● Foresee (3 psi) — Reaction, when a creature within 60 ft makes an attack roll or save: it has Disadvantage. ●● Rewrite (7 psi) — Reaction, after any d20 test within 60 ft: the roller rerolls and must use the new result. A Critical Hit rerolled this way is not a Critical Hit.

○ Focus. Advantage on Persuasion, Intimidation, and Deception. ● Compel (4 psi) — Bonus Action. One creature within 60 ft makes a Wisdom save or follows a one-word command on its next turn, as Command. ●● Seize (9 psi) — Bonus Action. One creature within 60 ft makes a Wisdom save or is Charmed and controlled for 1 minute, as Dominate Monster. Concentration. ●●● Enthrone (14 psi) — Magic action. As Seize, up to three creatures. Concentration.

○ Focus. At the end of a Short Rest, you and each ally who rested with you regain Hit Points equal to your Psionic Ability modifier. ● Knit (4 psi) — Bonus Action. One creature within 30 ft regains 6d8 Hit Points. ●● Restore (8 psi) — Bonus Action. One creature within 30 ft regains 12d8 Hit Points, and you end one condition on it from Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned.

○ Focus. Creatures Frightened of you have Disadvantage on saves against your disciplines. ● Dread (3 psi) — Rider. Once per turn when you damage a creature, it makes a Wisdom save or is Frightened of you for 1 minute, repeating at the end of each of its turns. ●● Panic (7 psi) — Bonus Action. Each creature in a 30-ft cone makes a Wisdom save, taking 5d8 Psychic damage and being Frightened for 1 minute on a failure. No concentration.

○ Focus. You can move Small or smaller unattended objects within 30 ft at will, speed 20 ft. ● Grip (3 psi) — Bonus Action. One creature within 60 ft makes a Strength save or is Restrained until the end of your next turn. No concentration. ●● Hurl (7 psi) — Magic action. Lift a creature or object of Huge size or smaller within 60 ft and throw it 60 ft. A thrown creature takes 6d10 Bludgeoning damage, as does anything it lands on.

○ Focus. Darkvision 60 ft; you can breathe in any environment. ● Adapt (3 psi) — Bonus Action. For 1 hour, climbing and swimming speeds equal to your walking speed, and Advantage on saves against environmental hazards. No concentration. ●● Take Wing (6 psi) — Bonus Action. Flying speed 60 ft for 10 minutes. No concentration.

○ Focus. Advantage on Constitution saves to maintain concentration. ● Ward (3 psi) — Reaction, when you or an ally within 30 ft takes damage: reduce it by 3d8 plus your Psionic Ability modifier. ●● Bastion (8 psi) — Bonus Action. For 1 minute, you and allies within 10 ft have Resistance to Psychic and Force damage and Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saves. No concentration.

○ Focus. Once per turn, when you make a d20 test, roll twice and use either result. ●●● Splinter (12 psi) — Bonus Action. Three duplicates of you appear within 5 ft for 1 minute, moving with you as a Reaction. You can make attacks and target spells from any duplicate's position. When a creature attacks you, roll a d4; on a 2+ a duplicate is struck instead and destroyed. No concentration. ●●● Divergent Turn (14 psi) — Magic action. Take an additional turn immediately after this one. You gain no Manifested Psi at the start of that turn, and once-per-turn features you already used are not refreshed. You can't use this option again until you finish a Long Rest.

○ Focus. Your weapon attacks and psionic damage ignore Resistance. ●●● Erasure (12 psi) — Magic action. One creature or object within 60 ft. A creature makes a Constitution save, taking 14d10 Force damage on a failure, half on a success. A creature killed by this leaves nothing and returns only via True Resurrection or Wish. A nonmagical object of Large size or smaller is destroyed outright. ●●● Unwrite (13 psi) — Magic action. End one magical effect of 8th level or lower within 60 ft, permanently. A magic item property ends until repaired, 1 week has passed.

Every Order has five growth points — PL 21, 25, 29, 33, and 37. Each carries a feature and a deepening of the pool you arrived with. PL 21 also grants your two Order Disciplines, detailed on each Order's page. Growth rates. Your entry bump is proportional to your original pool: a third for Psionic Energy Dice, which are a subclass resource of twelve, and a quarter for Focus and Sorcery Points, which are full class resources of twenty. Every growth point after that adds a flat amount. Pool PL 21 25 29 33 37 Total Psionic Energy Dice +4 +2 +2 +2 +2 12 → 24 Sorcery Points +5 +2 +2 +2 +2 20 → 33 Pact Magic slots +1 — +1 — +1 4 → 7 Psionic Energy Dice and Sorcery Points also gain Short Rest recovery at PL 21, equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Focus Points and Pact slots already refresh on a Short Rest. Your Order is fixed by your entry path, not chosen: The Whetstone The Aegis The Aberrant Bloom The Hollow Crown

Prerequisite Tortle Description You have a higher grasp in making full use of your shell to better protect yourself and others. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20. Your Natural Armor trait now provides a base AC of 18 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). As a reaction when you are forced to make a Dexterity saving throw, you can choose which of the two will take effect: You gain a +4 bonus to Dexterity saving throws until the end of your next turn. All creatures within 5 feet of you are considered to have half cover against any harmful attacks or effects while within range until the end of your next turn. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you've finished a short or long rest.

5th-level necromancy. (Wizard, Cleric) Meta Casting Time: 1 minute Range: 10 feet Components: V, S, M (V, S, M (a black onyx gem worth at least 150 gp, which the spell consumes, and four humanoid corpses or piles of bones)) Duration: Instantaneous Description Choose four Medium or Small humanoid corpses or piles of bones within range. You fuse them into a single Bone Hulk under your control. It uses the Bone Hulk stat block. On each of your turns, you can use a bonus action to mentally command any creature you created with this spell if it is within 60 feet of you. You can command it to move and take its action. If you issue no command, it takes the Dodge action. The Bone Hulk remains under your control for 24 hours. To maintain control, you must cast this spell again on the Bone Hulk before the current duration ends. This use of the spell reasserts control rather than creating a new creature. At Higher Levels At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you can reassert control over one additional undead created by this spell per slot level above 5th.

Large Undead, Neutral Evil AC 15 (Natural Armor) Initiative +0 (10) HP 95 (10d10 + 40) Speed 35ft. Immunities Poison; Exhaustion, Poisoned Senses Darkvision 60ft., passive Perception 10; Passive Perception 10 Languages Understands the languages you speak CR 6 (XP 2,300; PB +3) STR: 22 DEX: 10 CON: 18 INT: 4 WIS: 10 CHA: 5 Traits Bone Mass. The Bone Hulk counts as Large for grappling, shoving, and creature interaction. Momentum Charge. If the Bone Hulk moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature before hitting it with Bone Cleaver, the attack deals an extra 2d8 bludgeoning damage. Patchwork Frenzy. When reduced to half its hit points or fewer, the Bone Hulk enters frenzy. Once per turn, when it hits with Bone Cleaver, it deals an extra 1d8 necrotic damage. Actions Bone Cleaver. Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 2d12 + 6 slashing damage. Bone Crush (Recharge 5–6). Each creature of your choice within 10 ft. must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage and is pushed 10 ft. away. On a success, half damage and not pushed. Bone Crush (Recharge 5–6). Each creature of your choice within 10 ft. must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage and is pushed 10 ft. away. On a success, half damage and not pushed.

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (5-foot radius) Components: V, M (a melee weapon) Duration: Instantaneous As part of the action used to cast this spell, you must make a melee attack with a weapon against one creature within the spell’s range, otherwise the spell fails. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack’s normal effects, except that any damage dealt by the attack is lightning damage instead of its normal type. Additionally, an arc of lightning jumps to a second creature of your choice within 5 feet of the target, dealing 1d6 lightning damage. At 5th level, the weapon attack deals an additional 1d8 lightning damage on a hit. At 11th level, that additional damage becomes 2d8 and the arc becomes 2d6. At 17th level, the additional damage becomes 3d8 and the arc becomes 3d6.

A sorcerer of selfless nature and protective pursuit, your magic manifests itself through your desire to support others, bringing you safety and security in the process. Imbuing allies with the same magic that suffuses themselves, these sorcerers augment their strengths, covering their weaknesses, and upon reaching mastery, become catalyst for the inevitable success of everyone under their influence. Often called Arcane Guardians these sorcerers take a backseat to the events of life, letting others shine while they lift them higher, watching and protecting them. Many a hero was made by the hands of an Arcane Guardian. Features: 1st Level - Guardian Magic 1st Level - Loving Protection 6th Level - Gifting Inner Strength 14th Level - Altruistic Splinter 18th Level - Arcane Enlightenment

You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Guardian table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know. Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be an abjuration or a transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list.
1st: bless, protection from evil and good 3rd: aid, pass without trace 5th: aura of vitality, protection from energy 7th: aura of life, aura of purity 9th: mass cure wounds, skill empowerment

Starting at 1st level, your selfless nature begins to show in your spellcasting. Whenever an ally within 30 feet of you fits the casting requirements for a spell with a casting time of 1 Reaction, you can spend an amount of sorcery points equal to the spell level to cast the spell and give the effects to them. You can do this an amount of times equal to your Charisma modifier, resetting when you finish a long rest.

Starting at 6th level, you harness the ability to spread your talents to your allies. Once per turn, as a bonus action, you can strengthen an ally's next spell or attack with a Metamagic option you have access to, spending sorcery points as you would to use the options normally. These options last for a minute. The viable Metamagic options are as listed:

When your target casts a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, they can choose to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting. Alternatively, they can make one melee or ranged weapon attack as a bonus action.
When the target casts a spell, they can choose to cast it without any somatic or verbal components. Alternatively, they can give themself advantage on one melee or ranged weapon attack roll.
When the target rolls damage for a spell or weapon attack, they can reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). They must use the new rolls.

When the target casts a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, they can give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell. Alternatively, if they make a melee or ranged weapon attack and hit, they can add your Charisma modifier to one of the damage rolls (minimum of one).

Starting at 14th level, you learn to manipulate the bounds of your sorcery. Whenever you cast a spell that has a range of Self, you can spend an amount of sorcery points equal to twice the spell's level to change the range to Touch as long as the target is a willing creature. The spell level limit of this feature is half your Charisma modifier. You can do this an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, resetting when you finish a long rest.

Starting at 18th level, you gain the ability to funnel your strength into your allies. As an action on your turn, you can boost your allies' power until the end of your next turn. Every creature of your choice that is currently under the effects of a concentration spell cast by you receives the following additional effects: Their speed is increased by 30 feet. Every melee and ranged weapon attack roll they make is made with advantage. This advantage ignores any disadvantage also being applied to the target. Any attacks the target makes that hit receive a damage bonus equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). The target gains a bonus to AC equal to half your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). This feature can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, resetting on a long rest. Simulacrums are unable to use this feature.

2nd-level abjuration. Artificer, Cleric, Paladin Meta Casting Time: 1 Bonus Action Range: Self (10ft) Components: V, S, M (a small magnet) Duration: 10 minutes Description: You grant yourself and allies within range the ability to transfer the kinetic energy of attacks. Until the spell ends you can use an action to gravitate all attacks against allies within range until the end of your next turn. All allies within range can use their reaction to redirect any attack made against them, or an ally within 5ft of them, to you. Melee attacks will still be able to be made regardless of the effective range of the attack. Attacks made at long range because of this effect aren’t at disadvantage. At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the range increases by 5ft for every 2 slot levels above 2nd.

8th-level necromancy. (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 ft Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous Description You shoot a black ray of entropic energy from your outstretched hand, on a hit, your foe violently expell blood or similar vital fluids from their skin. Make a ranged spell attack to strike a target within range. On a hit, the target must make a successful Constitution Saving Throw vs your Spell Save DC, or take Necrotic damage equal to half its total hit points (rounded down), and be stunned until the end of its next turn.

9th-level necromancy. (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (60 ft. sphere) Components: V, S, M ((A ritual knife with an obsidian blade worth at least 25,000 gp infused with the essence of a powerful undead to be quested for and a humanoid brain embedded with onyx worth at least 10,000 gp, which the spell consumes)) Duration: Instantaneous Description You strike the onyx embedded in the blade, sending a wave of intelligence into nearby undead. Up to 6d6 undead under your control within 60ft of you gain 2d4 intelligence, to a max of 18. Such undead gain the armor and weapon proficiencies of the caster. In addition, they gain proficiency in a single skill, and learn one language, to represent the skills they had in life. This effect last until it is dispelled or you lose control of the undead. You may dispel this effect on a single undead under your control as an action. Casting this spell sacrifices your own life force, a fragment of mind spreading through the undead. The strain on a construct such as a simulacrum kills it instantly, and the spell fails to take effect. You gain 1d4 levels of exhaustion which must be removed naturally (no magic). If you die from this exhaustion, you lose the ability to cast this spell.

2nd-level Necromancy (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock) Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30ft Components: V, S, M (A dagger) Duration: 1 hour The weapon you indicate during the spell's casting briefly shimmers with a black aura that disappears in an eyeblink. When you cast this spell, choose one melee weapon within range. The next time a creature uses this weapon to make a melee attack, they have advantage on their attack roll and then the weapon turns on its wielder, provided the spell hasn't ended. The next attack afterward that hits a creature deals damage to the weapon's wielder instead of their target, in addition to the weapon's typical effects. This damage cannot be made non-lethal.
