As an action, a creature can attempt an investigation check against your spell save DC when closely analyzing the weapon to find that it was tampered with. As an action, a creature can make an arcana check against your spell save DC to disarm the weapon and end this spell. Once the weapon attacks its wielder, regardless of whether the attack hits or misses, the spell ends. At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd or 4th level, this spell lasts up to 8 hours. When you use a spell slot of 5th or 6th level, this spell lasts up to 24 hours. When you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, this spell lasts until dispelled.

4th-level divination. (Artificer, Bard, Paladin, Ranger, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, S, M (a piece of glas) Duration: 24 hours Description When you cast this spell, target either a creature, object, or location within range. When you do so, choose up to 10 creatures that you are familiar with. If a creature you choose is on the same plane as you, they become aware of the target, and know the most direct path. While within 1 mile of the target object, the creatures you chose can see a pinpoint of light above the target. This light can be seen through solid objects, except a thin sheet of lead. When you cast the spell, you may also send a message of 25 words to each of the creatures you choose to be aware of the target. They all receive the same message.

3rd-level necromancy. (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self Components: V, S Duration: 1 hour Description You dig into your chest and pull out a bone which turns into a magical bladed weapon for the duration. You take 2d6 bludgeoning damage when you first cast this spell, and each time you make an attack with this weapon, you take 1d6 necrotic damage. This damage cannot be reduced in any way, and bypasses resistance and immunity. If this damage would reduce you to 0 hit points, it reduces you to 1 hit point instead, and the spell ends. When you cast the spell, choose a mundane melee weapon that deals slashing damage. The bone becomes the chosen weapon, with which you are considered proficient. You can use your spellcasting modifier for the attack and damage rolls with this weapon. This blade deals an extra 1d6 necrotic damage on a hit and has advantage on attack rolls made against Good-aligned creatures. This blade lasts for the duration. If you ever let go of the weapon, it disappears, and you can resummon it to your hand as a bonus action. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the additional damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 3rd.

2nd-level necromancy. (Bard, Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Warlock) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60 feet Components: V, S, M ((a small whistle made of petrified wood)) Duration: Instantaneous Description You transfer your vital essence upon a spectral wind to a creature within range. Choose another creature within range, then spend and roll one of your unspent Hit Dice. The target gains a number of temporary hit points equal to 5 + the number rolled. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the number of temporary hitpoints increases by 5, and you can roll an additional Hit Dice for every two slot levels above 2nd. At 9th level, the number of temporary hitpoints increases to 25, and you can roll five Hit Dice.

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (5-foot radius) Components: V, M (a melee weapon) Duration: 1 round As part of the action used to cast this spell, you must make a melee attack with a weapon against one creature within the spell’s range, otherwise the spell fails. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack’s normal effects, except that any damage dealt by the attack is fire damage instead of its normal type. Additionally, embers whirl in the target’s space. Until the start of your next turn, when a creature enters that space for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there, you can use your reaction to deal 1d6 fire damage to it, ending the spell. At 5th level, the weapon attack deals an additional 1d8 fire damage on a hit. At 11th level, that additional damage becomes 2d8 and the ember damage becomes 2d6. At 17th level, the additional damage becomes 3d8 and the ember damage becomes 3d6.

necromancy cantrip. (Wizard, Cleric, Sorcerer) Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous Description You violently animate the tendons of a fresh corpse within range, causing it to explode outward in a spray of bone and sinew. Creatures within a 10-foot radius of the corpse must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 1d10 piercing damage on a failed save, or no damage on a successful one. The corpse is destroyed by this spell and cannot be used again for necromancy. The corpse must be relatively intact and cannot be a construct, elemental, ooze, or plant. A corpse destroyed by fire, acid, or radiant damage cannot be used. At Higher Levels The spell’s damage increases as you gain levels: 2d10 at 5th level, 3d10 at 11th level, and 4d10 at 17th level.

Transmutation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60 feet Components: V, S, M (a deck of playing cards) Duration: Instantaneous With a flash of your hands, you fling a playing or tarot card charged with energy at your opponent. Choose whether you make a ranged spell attack roll against the target or the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a hit or a failed saving throw, the target takes 1d6 force damage. This spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6) and 17th level (4d6).

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (5-foot radius) Components: V, M (a melee weapon) Duration: Instantaneous As part of the action used to cast this spell, you must make a melee attack with a weapon against one creature within the spell’s range, otherwise the spell fails. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack’s normal effects, except that any damage dealt by the attack is acid damage instead of its normal type. If you miss by 3 or less, acid splashes onto the target anyway and you deal 1d8 acid damage to it. At 5th level, the weapon attack deals an additional 1d8 acid damage on a hit. At 11th level, that additional damage becomes 2d8 and the splash damage becomes 2d8. At 17th level, the additional damage becomes 3d8 and the splash damage becomes 3d8.

Divination cantrip Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: S, M (a weighted die) Duration: 1 round You subtly twist your fingers, and fate seems to follow suit. For the duration, you can reroll any ability check you make to play a nonmagical game of chance. This spell could influence a game of poker, but not the result of a deck of many things.

5th-level abjuration. (Bard, Druid, Cleric, Paladin) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (30 ft. sphere) Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Description You conjure a field of magical inspiration that bolsters the resolve of your allies. Any creature you choose while they are in this field will have resistance against psychic damage and gain advantage on saving throws against the frightened and charmed conditions. If their save fails, any additional saves against the same effect succeed automatically.

Conjuration cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: Unlimited Components: V, S, M (a small written message) Duration: Instantaneous You send a small scroll bearing a short message to a creature of your choice. The recipient must be a creature known to you and must be on the same plane of existence as you. The scroll hovers in front of the recipient, drops into their pocket, or appears sitting on something nearby. The scroll’s message can be up to 8 characters long, and spaces count as characters. You can send only one scroll to a single target each day.

6th-level evocation. (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 120ft Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Description You conjure a ball of concentrated magic energy the size of a soccer ball loudly thrumming with energy, which slowly moves toward a target of your choice, moving through any nonmagical barrier. If it hits a magical barrier made from a spell of 9th level or lower, the orb and the barrier disappear. Otherwise, the orb disappears. It appears 60ft away from the target at a random location, moving 15ft closer at the beginning of your turn. If the creature touches the orb, they must make a Dexterity Saving Throw or take 20d6+40 force damage on a failure, or take half that much on a successful save. The orb then fades into nothingness. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell at 7th level or higher, you deal an additional 5d6 force damage for every level above 6th.

1st-level evocation. (Cleric, Druid, Paladin) Meta Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V, M (a shield worth at least 1 sp) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description As a bonus action, you can infuse a shield you're currently wielding with divine energy. If the shield is not magical, your AC increases by 1 until you stop wielding the shield or the spell ends. The first time a creature targets you with a melee attack and misses during this spell's duration, your shield bursts with divine radiance as you deflect the blow. The stored energy within releases and deals 1d6 radiant damage to any hostile creatures within 5 feet. When this blast hits an undead or a fiend, it deals an additional 1d6 radiant damage to it. After the blast, the spell ends. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the radiant damage dealt by the blast increases by 1d6 for each slot level after the 1st.

PC Creation: Dorren Level: 6 Casting Time: 10 Minutes Range: 10 feet, 10x10 square Components: V,S,M (a collar) Duration: Special School: Conjuration This spell is cast immediately after the 4th level Faithful Hound. The Faithful Hound duration extends to 24 hours. An invisible leash tethers the hound to the ground, it may move within the area of effect, and the caster may move more than 100 feet away from the hound. Casting both Faithful Hound and Dorren’s Leashed Hound every day for a year makes both spells permanent. Spell Lists: Wizard and any hb class that has faithful hound

4th level Divination Casting Time: 1 Action (Ritual) Range/Area: Self Components: V, S Duration: 1 Hour Class Lists: Wizard, Warlock, Sage, Bard (2014 & 2024 Class lists) Description Knowledge seems to leap directly from the page and into your brain. For the duration you gain the ability to read non-magical texts at a rate of 100 pages per minute. You also have perfect recall of any knowledge gained through this spell during its duration. After the spell has ended you can remember the details of what you read as if you had read it normally. You must be able to comprehend the language in which a text is written in order to utilize this spell.

5th-level abjuration. (Bard, Druid, Cleric, Wizard, Arcana Domain) Meta Casting Time: 1 hour Range: 60 feet Components: V, S, M (a jewel worth at least 1,000 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: 24 hours Description With this spell, you attempt to bind a celestial, an elemental, a fey, or a fiend to the Prime Material Plane for the Duration. The creature must be within range for the entire casting of the spell. At the completion of the casting, the target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is persuaded to stay on this plane for the duration. If the creature was summoned or created by another spell, that spell's duration is extended to match the duration of this spell. A bound creature is friendly to you and follows your instructions to the best of its ability. You might command the creature to accompany you on an adventure, to guard a location, or to deliver a message. The creature obeys the letter of your instructions. If the creature carries out your instructions completely before the spell ends, it travels to you to report this fact if you are on the same plane of existence. If you are on a different plane of existence, it returns to the place where you bound it and remains there until the spell ends. Ethical Caveat: The binding is a mutual agreement. Should the celestial, elemental. fey, or fiend feel that its binder is acting contrary to its original alignment, or forcing the creature to act in ways that it would not normally wish to do, the summoned creature may make a new CHA save with advantage to immediately teleport back to its own plane of existence. It may do this every round and will not take other actions beyond this save and protecting itself. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of a higher level, the duration increases to 10 days with a 6th-level slot, to 30 days with a 7th- level slot, to 180 days with an 8th-level slot, and to a year and a day with a 9th-level spell slot.

1st-level transmutation. (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Artificer) Meta Casting Time: 1 hour (ritual) Range: Touch Components: M (50 gp of calcium) Duration: Instantaneous Description What is a necromancer to do when society deems their school of magic evil? Why, of course, go against the natural way of things and make a body or two. This ritual allows one to make a set of bones to animate. The main difference between a real skeleton and the one this ritual creates is that the skeleton is always 5'4" tall, with no pinky toe, jaw, or marrow.

6th-level Abjuration (Artificer, Ranger, Wizard, Clockwork Sorcery) Meta Casting Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (a tiny silver bell worth 50 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Until dispelled Description You set a ward against intrusions. The ward covers an area no larger than a 20-foot Cube. You designate a specific condition that triggers the ward, such as a creature crossing a boundary, touching an object, opening a door, or speaking a specific phrase. The condition must be observable and occur within the ward's area. When the pre-defined condition is met, you receive a mental alert. The alert reaches you regardless of distance or planar boundaries, unless you are in an antimagic field or otherwise unable to receive telepathic messages, and you know which ward was triggered and how. The ward can be dispelled or suppressed by any effect that would do so normally, and also breaks if it moves more than 10 ft from its original location. If it is broken because it moved more than 10 ft, you do not receive any notification that it has been broken. In addition to the classes listed above, this spell is available to any class, subclass, or prestige class that allows you to take alarm as a spell.

Evocation cantrip (renaissance) Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous You extend your forefingers and thumbs, a dangerous gesture mimicking a pair of pistols, and fire. Make two ranged spell attacks against one or two creatures you can see within range. On a hit, a target takes 1d6 force damage. At 11th level, you make three attacks instead of two. Your finger guns require no ammunition, but they are considered to be firearms for spells and effects that apply to firearms.

5th-level conjuration. (Artificer, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard, Circle of Wildfire, Arcane Domain, Forge Domain) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description You gain the ability to enter any source of flame and move from inside it to inside another flame within 500 feet. Both flames must be at least the same size as you. You must use 5 feet of movement to enter the source of fire. You instantly know the location of all other flames within 500 feet and, as part of the move used to enter the flame, can either pass into one of those sources of fire or step out of the fire you're in. You appear in a spot of your choice within 5 feet of the destination fire, using another 5 feet of movement. If you have no movement left, you appear within 5 feet of the flame you entered. You can use this transportation ability once per round for the duration. You must end each turn outside a flame. You are temporarily immune to fire damage caused by the flame you're stepping into, but not other sources.

Abjuration cantrip Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a specially prepared gauntlet worth at least 5 gp) Duration: 1 round You summon a translucent yet visible field of force, which springs forth from the prepared gauntlet. Until the start of your next turn, this shield grants you a +2 bonus to your Armor Class, as if you were wielding a shield. The spell ends early if you are hit by an attack.

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: 120 feet Components: V, S, M (a specially prepared gauntlet worth at least 5 gp) Duration: Instantaneous You fling a dart of magical force at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 force damage. This spell’s damage increases by 1d10 when you reach 5th level (2d10), 11th level (3d10) and 17th level (4d10).

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: 5 feet Components: V, S, M (a specially prepared gauntlet worth at least 5 gp) Duration: 1 round You conjure a blade of magical force in the air, which lashes out at your foes. Make a melee spell attack against a creature within range. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 force damage. The blade remains in existence for a short time: until the start of your next turn, you can make a single strike with it as an opportunity attack. You make one additional attack when you cast this spell at 5th level (two attacks), 11th level (three attacks) and 17th level (four attacks). You can direct the attacks at the same target or at different ones, and you make a separate attack roll for each.

9th-level necromancy. (Wizard, Cleric) Meta Casting Time: 8 hours Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (an intricate black onyx idol inlaid with precious gems worth 10,000gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Instantaneous Description This spell must be cast within ten minutes after dusk. You must press the idol used for the material component of this spell to the corpse of a creature with a challenge rating of 10 or lower and hold it there for the duration of the casting of this spell. The corpse must be intact for the duration of this spell’s casting— a destroyed corpse causes this spell to fail. The corpse reanimates, returning to life and using the statblock of the creature it belonged to, with the following changes: its creature type becomes undead its hit point maximum is halved if it has class levels, it loses all of them it loses any legendary actions and legendary resistances It is unable to cast spells it gains immunity to necrotic damage As a bonus action on each of your turns, you can mentally command any creature you animated with this spell if the creature is within 120 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one). You decide what action the creature will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor. If you issue no commands, the creature only defends itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete. An undead raised by this spell is under your control for 24 hours, after which it makes a charisma saving throw. On a failure, you regain control of it for another 24 hours, whereupon it makes the save again. Each time it fails this saving throw, it gains a cumulative +2 bonus to the Charisma save. On a success, it is hostile to all creatures (including yourself) and is under no compulsion to follow any orders you give it. It has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws it makes against you (except for the saving throws it makes to break free from your control).

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (5-foot radius) Components: V, M (a melee weapon) Duration: 1 round As part of the action used to cast this spell, you must make a melee attack with a weapon against one creature within the spell’s range, otherwise the spell fails. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack’s normal effects, except that any damage dealt by the attack is cold damage instead of its normal type. Additionally, the target is covered in a brittle frost until the start of your next turn. If the target willingly moves before then, you can use your reaction to deal 1d6 cold damage to it, ending the spell. At 5th level, the weapon attack deals an additional 1d8 cold damage on a hit. At 11th level, that additional damage becomes 2d8 and the frost damage becomes 2d6. At 17th level, the additional damage becomes 3d8 and the frost damage becomes 3d6.

1st-level transmutation. (Cryomancy Magic) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60 feet Components: V, S, M (a piece of pure ice) Duration: Instantaneous Description You form a large ice shard from the moisture of your surroundings to launch at a target that you can see within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. If the attack hits, the target takes 2d6 cold damage and the shard shatters into pieces that embed into the target until the start of your next turn. If the target takes an action or bonus action before then, the target takes 1d4 cold damage. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 to the target, and the damage the target takes for doing an action or bonus action increase by 1d4 for each slot level above 1st.

5th-level divination. (rtificer, Bard, Cleric, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 minute Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a focus worth at least 1,000 gp, such as a crystal ball, a silver mirror, or a font filled with holy water) Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Description You can choose a small or smaller object that is familiar to you that isn’t being worn or carried and is on the same plane of existence as you. The spell creates an invisible sensor within 10 feet of the object’s location for the duration. You mentally receive visual information from the sensor, which has normal vision and darkvision out to 30 feet. The sensor allows you to look in every direction. The sensor moves with the object, remaining within 10 feet of it for the duration. A creature that can see invisible objects sees the sensor as a luminous orb about the size of your fist. At any time while concentrating on the spell, you can use an action to ping the object’s location. If the object is on the same plane as you, you learn the object’s general direction (but not its distance or any other information).
You were told nature has no true masters. You intend to prove that wrong. Prerequisites: 5.5e (2024) Druid 20
When you take this prestige class, choose two more skills from the Druid skill proficiencies. You are proficient in both of those skills.

Additionally when you take this prestige class, you gain a new set of spell slots to fuel your spells. You gain spell slots as per the Druid table based on your prestige level minus 20. When you prepare spells for the day, you may now prepare a number of spells equal to your prestige level + your Wisdom modifier. You learn one Druid cantrip of your choice, and one additional Druid cantrip at 24th and 30th level.

21st level. Your connection to the primal has outgrown mortal limits. You gain one additional use of Wild Shape. Your known forms increase by 2, and the maximum Challenge Rating for your forms increases by 1 (added to whatever maximum you already have from your class and subclass features). In addition, you may now learn Elemental stat blocks (in place of Beasts) up to CR 1 as known forms, representing your growing kinship with the raw substance of the world.

22nd level. Your practice of the old ways deepens and broadens. You may choose the same Druid Circle you already belong to, or you may choose a new one to reflect the different truths nature has revealed to you. Your choice grants you additional features at 22nd level, and again at 26th and 34th level.

23rd level. Nature itself shields you from harm. You gain resistance to poison damage and immunity to the Poisoned condition. While you are Wild Shaped, you also have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

24th, 28th, 32nd, 36th, and 39th level. You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. You may select a feat instead of an Ability Score Improvement.

25th level. Your magic no longer cares what shape you wear. While using Wild Shape, you can cast any Druid spell you have prepared, including spells with a Material component that has a cost or is consumed, provided you have access to the required component or a Druidic Focus that can be worn or held in your current form (at your DM's discretion for unusual anatomies).

27th level. Your command of the elements grows so complete that you no longer have to choose a single expression of it. You now have both options granted by Elemental Fury and Improved Elemental Fury, improved as follows. Potent Spellcasting. Once on each of your turns when you deal damage with a Druid spell of 1st level or higher, you can add your Wisdom modifier to that damage. Primal Strike. The extra damage of your Primal Strike increases to 3d8.

29th level. Your mastery of shapechanging reaches new heights. Your known forms increase by 2, and the maximum Challenge Rating for your forms increases by 2 (added to whatever maximum you already have from your class, subclass, and other features). Forms you adopt may now be Huge.

30th level. You can, as a Bonus Action, expend two uses of Wild Shape to instead take the form of a Primal Avatar: a towering, elemental-infused shape of your own design (DM's discretion on appearance) using the stat block of any Beast, Elemental, or Monstrosity with a Challenge Rating up to your Proficiency Bonus + 4 (CR 10 for most characters). While in this form, you retain the benefits of Greater Beast Spells and Elemental Ascendancy, and you gain temporary hit points equal to five times your prestige level. This form lasts for up to 10 minutes, until you drop to 0 hit points, or until you revert to your normal form as a Bonus Action. You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest. If you've already used it, you can expend a spell slot of 8th level to use it again.
33rd level. You regain all expended uses of Wild Shape whenever you finish a Short Rest, in addition to your normal recovery.

38th level. You have walked with nature long enough that its patience has become your own. You age at one-tenth the normal rate, have advantage on death saving throws, and gain resistance to necrotic damage.

40th level. You have become a living conduit for nature's oldest and mightiest power. As a Bonus Action, you can cause a verdant grove to bloom across the ground in a 30-foot radius centered on you. The grove lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you use this feature again. While it persists: The area is difficult terrain for enemies of your choice, but not for you or any creatures you choose. At the start of each of your turns, you and up to five creatures you choose within the grove regain hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier + your Prestige level. Alternatively, you can instead deal that same amount of poison damage to a number of enemies of your choice within the grove (no save). Ranged attacks made against a creature within the grove by an attacker outside it have disadvantage. As a Bonus Action on later turns, while you are standing on natural terrain, you can teleport through the natural world to another point of natural terrain within 60 feet of your current position. If you aren't standing on natural terrain, you can instead teleport to any point within the grove. Either way, the grove's area then shifts to remain centered on you. You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

7th-level transmutation. (Druid) Meta Casting Time: 1 hour Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (rare oils and unguents worth at least 5,000 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Instantaneous Description You touch a willing living humanoid. The spell transforms their body into an adult form of another race. If the target isn’t willing, the spell fails.. The GM rolls a d100 and consults the reincarnate table to determine what form the creature takes when the spell is complete or the GM chooses. The reincarnated creature recalls its former life and experiences. It retains the capabilities it had in its original form, except it exchanges its original race for the new one and changes its racial traits accordingly.

Evocation Cantrip (Cleric, Celestial Warlock) Casting Time: 1 Action Range: 90 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous You conjure and fire a bolt of radiant energy at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 radiant damage. If the target is an undead or fiend, it takes 1d10 radiant damage instead. This spell's damage increases by one die when you reach 5th level (2d8 or 2d10), 11th level (3d8 or 3d10), and 17th level (4d8 or 4d10).

Evocation cantrip. (Artificer, Ranger, Sorcerer, Warlock) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 20 feet Components: S, M (a ranged weapon worth at least 1 sp) Duration: Instantaneous Description You brandish the weapon used in the spell’s casting and make a ranged attack with it against one creature within 20 feet of you. On a hit, your walking speed increases by 5 ft until the end of your turn. This spell’s damage and speed bonus increases when you reach certain levels. At 5th level, the ranged attack deals an extra 1d6 fire damage and your speed increases by 10 feet instead of 5 feet. The damage roll and speed bonus increases by 1d6 and 5 feet at 11th level (2d6 and 15 feet) and 17th level (3d6 and 20 feet).

9th-level Conjuration (Cleric, Celestial Patron, Druid, Sage, Sorcerer) Casting Time: 1 action Range: Sight Components: V, S, M (a diamond worth 5,000gp) Duration: Concentration, 1 minute A pillar of radiance rises from a point you can see, enclosing an area of up to a 360ft radius, and 1 mile high in bright light. When you cast this spell, creatures of your choice must make a Constitution saving throw or be blinded for 1 minute. They may repeat the saving throw at the end of their turn, ending the blindness on a success. Each round that you maintain concentration produces an additional effect, in addition to the last: Healing Waves (Round 2): Creatures and objects within the area regain hit points equal to your spellcasting modifier. Creatures of an alignment you choose receive no healing and instead take the same amount as radiant damage so long as they have no fewer than half their hit points total. Community (Round 3): Up to 5 willing creatures within the area can each sacrifice a number of hit points up to half your level. These hit points are represented as a pool of temporary hit points that can be divided as you choose among any number of creatures that you can see within range. Creatures can only sacrifice hit points once over the duration of the spell. Vitality (Round 4): Creatures and objects within the area gain your choice of either bludgeoning, piercing or slashing damage resistance until the start of your next turn. Creatures of an alignment you choose receive no resistances and instead lose resistances, if any, of the chosen damage types until the start of your next turn. Guiding Light (Rounds 5): Creatures within the area gain a 1d4 bonus to ability checks and saving throws until the start of your next turn. Creatures of an alignment you choose instead receive a 1d4 penalty to ability checks and saving throws until the start of your next turn.

6th-level Enchantment (Bard, Sorcerer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet (10-foot-radius Sphere) Components: V Duration: 1 minute Description You proclaim an insightful or inflammatory statement, such as a claim about the politics of a nearby town. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you choose within range must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or have the Charmed condition until the spell ends. Any creature that doesn't share a language with you or that has an Intelligence score lower than 3 automatically succeeds on the saving throw. While Charmed, a target must spend its turn discussing or arguing for or against your statement. For the duration, the target has a Speed of 0 and has the Blinded and Deafened conditions with respect to everyone except you and other targets affected by this spell. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success.

3rd-level abjuration. (Bard, Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60ft/30ft sphere Components: V, S, M (a bit of fleece) Duration: 1 minute Description This spell creates a mental phantasm of lights and sounds that dull the senses. Choose a point within range. Each creature you choose in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, their vision and hearing are restricted to 30ft for the duration. An effected creature can make a Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the effected targets lose an additional 5ft of vision and hearing for each slot level above 3rd.

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (5-foot radius) Components: V, S, M (two bits of copper wire) Duration: Instantaneous You emit a dazzling array of short lightning bolts in all directions. Each other creature within 5 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d6 lightning damage. This spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6) and 17th level (4d6).

Conjuration cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous With a flourish, you conjure a throwing dagger of magical force out of thin air and flick it from your wrist at a target you can see. Make a ranged spell attack against a creature within range. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 force damage. The dagger vanishes after the attack. At higher levels you conjure more daggers and make additional attacks: two daggers at 5th level, three at 11th level and four at 17th level. You can direct the daggers at the same target or at different ones, and you make a separate attack roll for each.

Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual) Range: 30 feet Components: V, S, M (a pinch of iron and cobalt powder worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Until Dispelled You implant a small repeatable magical mechanical force within a tiny object within range. When you do so, choose two rotational states relative to it's current rotation for the item to switch between. When the spell causes the item to switch between the two rotational states, it does so with the least required movement and can be designated to take anywhere from 1 second to 10 minutes. Finally, determine the circumstance that will trigger the spell to rotate the object. When the circumstance occurs, the object rotates to the next or previous state (the second state when triggered for the first time). If an outside force or object would prevent the object from rotating, it stops harmlessly and that particular trigger is ignored. When you cast this spell, you can have the spell end after it returns to its original position, or it can remain and repeat its rotation whenever the trigger occurs. The triggering circumstance can be as general or as detailed as you like, though it must be based on visual or audible conditions that occur within 30 feet of the object. For example, you could instruct a lock to automatically reset its rotation when the door is closed.

4th-level evocation. (Bard, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard, Battle Smith) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self Components: S Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description You charge a free hand with crackling magical energy. When you cast this spell, and as a bonus action on subsequent turns, you can point at a creature you can see within 60 feet of you and release a bolt, provided the spell hasn't ended. The target must make a constitution saving throw or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn. When you successfully incapacitate a target with this spell, you can instantly teleport to an empty space of your choice within 5 feet of it, and your melee weapon attacks against the incapacitated creature deal an additional 1d6 lightning damage. The spell ends early if a target succeeds on its saving throw, or if you use your bonus action to do anything else. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the additional lightning damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 4th.

The Memory Thief is a sorcerer touched by the silent weight of unspoken thoughts, lost truths, and stolen moments. Whether chosen by a god of shadows and secrets or born with the uncanny ability to pierce the veil of another’s mind, these sorcerers draw power not from raw elements—but from memory, emotion, and identity itself. Every spell is an intrusion, every glance a chance to unravel another’s story. They are masters of mental trespass and psychic influence, collecting knowledge the way others collect coins. Some act as spies for hidden powers like Vhaeraun, gods of forbidden knowledge, or remnants of psionic empires. Others awaken to their abilities after surviving moments of profound trauma or divine contact—left able to steal what others cannot even remember. "Thoughts and Emotions are the truest form of currency. I never pay full price." - Memory Thief

The Memory Thief excels at subtle control, emotional manipulation, and deep utility in both narrative and combat play. With features that allow you to read and manipulate the thoughts and motivations of others, this subclass rewards strategic roleplay, creative problem-solving, and players who love to know more than they should. Reclaim the Past: Seeking to recover a stolen or fragmented identity by stitching together memories from others. Weaponize Secrets: Collecting powerful memories from kings, archmages, or ancient evils to manipulate the tides of history or blackmail enemies into silence. Protect the Mindscape: Standing as a psychic guardian or counter-spy, exposing hidden corruption or breaking mind control through counter-manipulation.

The Memory Thief is perfect for players who want to: Influence Story Through Subtlety: Gain leverage by collecting key memories, discovering hidden motives, or creating complex emotional bonds with NPCs. Play with Identity and Perception: Use your magic to assume false roles, mimic memories, or veil your soul against detection. Master Battlefield Presence Without Direct Violence: Weaken enemies emotionally, disrupt their thoughts, and track them across time and space. Ideal Players and Characters 🧠 The Intrigue Manipulator Players who thrive in espionage-heavy or social-intrigue campaigns, especially those who enjoy steering conversations with secrets and subtle leverage. 🕯 The Shadowed Seer Players who love mysteries and clues, piecing together narrative threads from the minds of others, treating every memory like a breadcrumb on a hidden trail. 🎭 The Identity Shifter Players who want to play with masks, personas, and the line between truth and falsehood—taking on aspects of others through their memories, voices, and fears. Features: 3rd Level - Umbral Spike 6th Level - Thought Scribe 14th Level - Hollow Mask 18th Level - Dark One's Trespass
documents.s: Who Would Thrive as a Memory Thief?

documents.t: Once per turn when damaging a creature with a spell or attack, you can deal an additional 2d6 psychic damage and mark them. While the creature is marked, you know their direction and distance while they are within 90 ft of you, lasting up to 1 hour. You can spend sorcery points to extend the duration by an additional hour per sorcery point spent. The extra damage increases at 6th (3d6) level, 14th (4d6) level, and 18th (5d6) level. You can use this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all uses on a Long Rest, or by expending a spell slot for each use restored (no action required).

When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can extract a thought strand (as with the Encode Thoughts cantrip) on a failure. Once you use this feature on a creature, you cannot use this feature on that target again until you complete a short or long rest. The thought strand contains one memory of a significant event within the past 24 hours. Significant events typically involve powerful emotions, such as battles and betrayals, marriages and murders, births and funerals, or meetings with important friends or leaders. However, they might also include more mundane events that are nevertheless important to that creature. In addition, while holding the thought strand, you can communicate telepathically with the target while they are on the same plane of existence as you. You can choose if they are able to respond or not.

As a bonus action, you can spend 1 or more sorcery points to magically transform your essence for 10 minutes. For each sorcery point you spend, you can gain one of the following benefits of your choice, the effects of which last until the transformation ends: You can see through solid objects to a range of 30 feet, and can see any invisible creatures to a range of 60 feet. Within that range you have advantage on checks made to find hidden creatures, traps, or secret doors for the duration of the transformation. You cannot be detected or targeted by any divination magic, or perceived through magical scrying sensors unless you wish to be. If you choose to be affected, you can present false information to the divination magic or scrying sensor for the duration of the transformation. You can choose a creature type other than your actual creature type. Spells and other magical effects treat you as if you were a creature of the chosen type. After the transformation expires, ongoing and future spells and magical effects treat you as your original creature type. You have advantage on saving throws against effects which would cause you to be charmed, frightened, or possessed. If you succeed against such an effect, you have advantage on Charisma checks made against that source for the duration of the transformation.

As an Action, you can force a target you can see within 60ft of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed or frightened (your choice) and you are able to detect the creatures surface thoughts and emotional state for up to 8 hours (those foremost in its mind, reflecting its current emotions and what it is actively thinking about). You can spend sorcery points to extend the duration by an additional hour per sorcery point spent. Alternatively, if you are holding a thought strand created by your Thought Scribe feature, you can target that creature as long as they are on the same plane of existence. While charmed or frightened in this way, it undertakes to perform any services or activities you ask of it to the best of its ability. You can set the creature new tasks when a previous task is completed, or if you decide to end its current task. If the service or activity might cause harm to the creature, or if it conflicts with the creature's desires, the creature can make another Wisdom saving throw to try to end the effect. This save is made with advantage if you or your companions are fighting the creature. If the activity would result in certain death for the creature, the effect ends. During that time you can use a Bonus Action to see and hear through that creatures senses until the end of your next turn. You are blinded and deafened while this persists. Once you use this Action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 7 sorcery points to use it again.

1st-level illusion. (Bard, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 10 minutes (ritual) Range: Touch Components: S, M (enchanted ink worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Special Description You imbue a piece of parchment, paper, or some other suitable writing material with illusory writing that lasts for the duration. This writing is not suitable for scribing a spell scroll or filling a spellbook. When you cast this spell, the page is instantly filled with text of your choosing. Choose a duration between 1 minute and 1 year. After this amount of time has elapsed, the magic fades and the writing vanishes. Any time before the spell ends, you, and any creatures you designate when you cast the spell, can cast it again to extend the duration, up to a maximum of 1 year. Extending the duration in this way does not require the material component.

Transmutation cantrip (chronomancy) Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V Duration: Instantaneous You briefly stop time for everyone but yourself. You can take one additional action and move around within your space while no time passes for other creatures. That action can be used only to take the Search or Use an Object action, or to make an Intelligence check to remember information about something. You can’t affect or damage any creature or object other than objects you are wearing or carrying. If an object leaves your hand, it too becomes frozen in time.

5th-level evocation. (Cleric, Paladin, Sorcerer, Ranger, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a melee weapon worth at least 1 sp) Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Description You imbue a melee weapon you touch with moonlight and enchant your own shadow to hinder your foes. Until the spell ends, the weapon emits bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15. If the weapon isn't already a magic weapon, it becomes one for the duration. When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn, that attack can originate from any space within the lights radius as if you were in that space. You make this choice for each attack, as the moonlight solidifies to attack them. Once during this spell's duration, you may use an action to fill a 30-foot radius circle, centered on the ground underneath you, with a magical shadow that remains there for the spell's duration. If a creature ends it's turn within this area, you may force them to make a strength saving throw. On a failure they are knocked prone and must use all of their speed to stand back up, rather than half.
4th-level illusion. (Wizard (Legacy), Wizard, The Undead (VRGtR))
Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual) Range: 30 feet Components: V, S Duration: 1 hour

A Huge, quasi-real, horse-drawn coach appears on the ground in an unoccupied space of your choice within range. You decide the creature's and coach's appearance, and it is equipped with the necessary gear to pull the carriage. Any of the equipment created by the spell vanishes in a puff of smoke if it is carried more than 10 feet away from the steed or coach. For the duration, you and up to 4 other creatures you choose can ride in the coach. The steeds uses the Riding Horse stat block, except it has a Speed of 100 feet and can travel 11 miles in an hour. When the spell ends, the steeds and coach gradually fades, giving the riders 1 minute to dismount. The spell ends early if the steed takes any damage.

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous You conjure a chain and hook made of magical force, which you propel at a creature or an unoccupied space you can see within range. When you target a space, or a creature of Huge size or larger, your grapnel pulls you to that target in a straight line. You provoke opportunity attacks for this movement as normal. When you target a creature of Large size or smaller, you pull the target up to 10 feet toward you. The creature can make a Strength saving throw to resist this movement.

Wondrous item, very rare Description This small rusted anchor charm is bound to a cursed, lost ship: The Specter’s Breath. This ship and its crew were lost to the Ethereal Plane centuries ago, cursed to remain there and wander aimlessly until called back by an ancient relic charm. This small charm acts as the ship's tether to the Material Plane. As an action, you can call out to the ship while holding the charm aloft. If you're within 30 feet of a body of water on the Material Plane, a full-sized anchor appears on the ground in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the water. A wispy, gray chain appears on the anchor that extends into nothingness. After 1 minute, the Specter’s Breath emerges from the Ethereal Plane, pulled by the anchor's chain, and coming to rest in the water nearby. The ship is a longship 70 feet long and 20 feet wide. It's piloted by thirty-four crewmembers and five officers, all of whom are long-dead, ghostly remains of their former selves. They are formless and harmless, but are nevertheless visible and friendly to you and your companions. They can interact with the rigging, sails, and other equipment on the ship, but nothing else while they remain on the Material Plane. While the ship remains, it moves at a speed of 10 miles per hour, or half as much when there isn't any wind. Only you can command it and its crew while the charm is on your person. The ship may be commanded for up to 10 days, after which you cannot summon it again until a further 10 days have passed. Every day at dawn the ship and its crew begin to gradually fade over 10 minutes before they are returned to the Ethereal Plane. They may be resummoned the following dusk. The ship returns early if you speak the command phrase "Until the night calls once more," or if the ship takes enough damage that it would be destroyed. Anything not summoned with the ship is dropped into the water below the ship when it disappears.

8th-level necromancy. (Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 Action Range: 60 ft. Components: V Duration: Instantaneous Description You utter a word of defilement on a creature you see within range. If the creature you choose has 150 hit points of fewer, the target gains vulnerability to all damage that they are not resistant or immune to. Otherwise, the spell has no effect on it. A defiled creature must make a Constitution Save at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, the creature is no longer defiled.

2nd-level illusion. (Artificer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual) Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (crushed glass worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Until Dispelled Description You implant a magical light into an object that you touch which activates when a trigger condition is met. Next, determine the circumstances that will trigger the spell to turn on the light. When that circumstance occurs, the object begins to glow, emitting dim light in a radius of 5 feet around the object. If the trigger condition you specified is a spoken phrase, the object itself becomes colored if the final word of the phrase is a color. Otherwise, the object turns white. When you cast this spell, you can have the spell end after it activates for the first time, or it can remain and continue to change colors if the trigger condition occurs again. If the trigger condition occurs while the light is already on, the object changes color to the new color at the end of a spoken message, or returns to normal and stops glowing if no color is spoken. The triggering circumstance can be as general or as detailed as you like, though it must be based on visual or audible conditions that occur within 30 feet of the object. For example, you could instruct the object to light up when any creature moves within 30 feet of the object or when a silver bell rings within 30 feet of it.

2nd-level transmutation (Artificer, Druid, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual) Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (an amber crystal worth at least 10 gp, which the spell consumes) Duration: Until dispelled Description You touch a nonmagical object, warding it against the ravages of time and nature. For the duration, the object is immune to natural wear and tear, including weathering, rust, rot, mildew, and other forms of gradual decay. The object resists tarnishing and maintains its structural integrity despite exposure to the elements. Additionally, the object gains a damage threshold equal to 5 × the level of the spell slot used to cast this spell. An object with a damage threshold has immunity to all damage unless it takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, in which case it takes damage as normal, and the spell ends.

Transmutation cantrip Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V Duration: 1 round You call upon your inner reserves to give yourself a brief flash of speed. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

3rd-level evocation. (Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous Description Channeling the vile and scheming nature of the Rakshasa, you evoke by splaying three fingers apart and making a downward vertical slash in the air. It can also be done with a horizontal swipe to deal less damage to more targets at once. A target you choose within range must make a Dexterity save or suffer 6d8 magical slashing damage. You can alternatively choose to target any creature in a 20-foot cube originating from yourself, dealing 3d8 magical slashing damage to each target. In either case, on a successful save, each target takes half as much magical slashing damage. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for both single-target attacks and multi-target attacks for each slot level above 3rd.

3rd-level evocation. (Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous Description Channeling the vile and scheming nature of the Rakshasa, you evoke by splaying three fingers apart and making a downward vertical slash in the air. It can also be done with a horizontal swipe to deal less damage to more targets at once. A target you choose within range must make a Dexterity save or suffer 6d8 magical slashing damage. You can alternatively choose to target any creature in a 20-foot cube originating from yourself, dealing 3d8 magical slashing damage to each target. In either case, on a successful save, each target takes half as much magical slashing damage. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for both single-target attacks and multi-target attacks for each slot level above 3rd.

6th-level abjuration. (Bard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a small sprinkling of powdered silver) Duration: 10 minutes Description You create a reflective magical barrier that turns harmful attacks back upon their attackers. For the duration, when a creature hits you with an attack, it takes 2d8 radiant damage. Additionally, if you fail a saving throw against a spell cast by a creature you can see, they take 1d8 radiant damage + an extra 1d8 for each spell slot level of the spell cast.

transmutation cantrip. (Bard (Legacy), Sorcerer (Legacy), Wizard (Legacy), Bard, Sorcerer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: 15 feet Components: V Duration: Instantaneous Description You cause an object within range that isn't being worn or carried to fly to your open hand. The object must weigh no more than 10 pounds or the spell fails.

4th-level evocation. (Bard, Druid, Sage, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, M (a small paper cone) Duration: Instantaneous Description You let out a deafening roar as a shockwave of energy collides with all around you. Each creature within range must succeed on a constitution saving throw or take 5d8 thunder damage and be pushed up to 20 feet away from you. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage and is not moved. Regardless of success or failure, a creature within range is deafened for 1 minute. Objects within range also take this damage. At Higher Levels When cast with a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the damage dealt increases by 1d8 for each spell level above 4th.

4th-level Divination Meta Casting Time: 1 minute Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a polished obsidian mirror) Duration: Special Description As an action you may target a specific creature you have seen or heard about on the same plane of existence, forcing them to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save you can extract a thought strand (as with the Encode Thoughts cantrip) as shadowy scenes are presented on the mirrors surface. If you have a body part, lock of hair, clipping from a nail, or similar portion of the target's body, the target makes its saving throw with disadvantage. The thought strand contains one memory of a significant event within a number of days equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. Significant events typically involve powerful emotions, such as battles and betrayals, marriages and murders, births and funerals, or meetings with important friends or leaders. However, they might also include more mundane events that are nevertheless important to that creature (DM's discretion). In addition, while holding the thought strand, you can communicate telepathically with the target while they are on the same plane of existence as you. The target is unable to respond. If you cast the spell two or more times before completing your next long rest, there is a cumulative 25 percent chance for each casting after the first that you get a random memory of no significance. The DM makes this roll in secret. Classes: Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard, Warlock

3rd-level conjuration (Artificer, Wizard, Ranger) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self Components: S, M (a melee weapon worth at least 1 sp) Duration: Instantaneous Description You flourish the weapon used in the casting and vanish, instantly teleporting to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of a creature you can see within 30 feet of the caster. Upon appearing, you immediately make one melee weapon attack against that creature using the weapon used in the spell's casting. You have advantage on this attack roll. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack's normal effects, plus an additional 2d10 force damage. At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the extra force damage increases by 1d10, and the distance to the creature range increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 3rd.

9th Level Necromancy (Cleric, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 Action Range: 30 feet Components: V, S Duration: 1 minute Description One creature you can see within range becomes the target of an onslaught of ethereal skeletons. At the end of each of the target's turns, four skeletons immediately appear in the closest unoccupied spaces to the target and are hostile towards it. The skeletons' attacks are considered magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunities, and last until either they or the target die, where they disappear leaving no trace. They cannot be commanded and will exclusively take actions harmful to the target, or to aid in harming the target. If any skeletons remain when more are to be summoned, that many additional skeletons are summoned.

8th Level Necromancy (Cleric, Wizard, Warlock) Casting Time: 1 Action Range: 60 feet Components: N/A Duration: Instantaneous Description When you cast this spell, target one creature you can see within range. 8d4 skeletons immediately appear in the closest unoccupied spaces to the target, and are hostile towards it. Alternatively, you can delay the appearance of the skeletons by up to an hour. The skeletons' attacks are considered magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunities, and last until either they or the target die, where they disappear leaving no trace. They cannot be commanded and will exclusively take actions harmful to the target, or to aid in harming the target. If a creature already under the effects of skeleton surprise is targeted, you instead change the time at which the skeletons appear, rather than causing more to appear. You may also change the time that the skeletons appear as an action, so long as the time you choose falls within one hour of the initial casting. The casting of this spell does not require verbal or somatic components, hence the surprise.

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous You compress a thunderous boom into an invisible ball and project it at a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or it takes 1d8 thunder damage and is deafened until the start of your next turn. If the target is within 10 feet of you, this spell’s damage dice become d10s instead of d8s. This spell’s damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8) and 17th level (4d8).

5th-level necromancy. (Warlock, Wizard, Sorcerer, Death Domain, Grave Domain, Oathbreaker, College of Spirits) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, S, M (a pinch of bone dust, and a tarnished silver chain) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description You attempt to forcefully tear the spirit of a creature from its body, leaving it momentarily defenseless. Choose one humanoid creature within range (creatures under the effects of a spell, feature or magic item that wards them against Undead or possession cannot have their spirit ejected by this spell). The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, their spirit is ejected from their body and manifests as a spectral form within 10 feet of them. The target’s body becomes incapacitated, and has disadvantage on saving throws against effects that would possess them. The spirit resembles their mortal form in almost every way, replicating game statistics but not their possessions. Any damage or other effects that apply to your spirit or physical body affects the other. In addition, the spirit is incorporeal, resistant to all damage except psychic or radiant, and it must choose whether it gets a move, an action, or a bonus action on a turn; it gets only one of the three. The spirit is tethered to the body and cannot move more than 60 feet away from it. At the start of each of the target’s turns, they can attempt a Wisdom saving throw to end the effect early. If they succeed, their spirit returns to their body, and they regain control at the start of their next turn. If the body is reduced to 0 hit points while the spirit is still ejected, the creature dies instantly. If killed in this way, its spirit detaches from its corpse as a Specter under your control, the statistics of which are in the Monster Manual. You can mentally command the Specter or any creature you made with this spell if the creature is within 60 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one), and in combat the Specter shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. The Specter remains in your service for up to 10 days, at which point it vanishes to the afterlife. While the Specter is in your service, its soul is trapped and cannot be revived. A Remove Curse, Dispel Evil and Good, or Wish spell ends this spells effect. At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th or 7th level or higher, the target has disadvantage on its initial saving throw. At 8th or 9th level, the target instead rises as a Poltergeist if killed.

5th-level necromancy. (Warlock, Wizard, Sorcerer, Death Domain, Grave Domain, Oathbreaker, College of Spirits) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (a silver chain mesh worth at least 1,500+ GP) Duration: 10 days Description Weaving a web of necromantic energies around you or another, you are protected against influences upon your soul or animating spirit. You touch a living humanoid or a corpse. For the duration, the target has advantage on death saving throws, and is protected from spells and effects that would allow their soul, spirit or body to be queried, trapped, possessed or manipulated, such as Soul Cage, Speak with Dead, Magic Jar, Spirit Ejection or other related effects. If the humanoid or corpse is targeted by such an effect, it automatically fails and the enemy takes 4d10 psychic damage, as the Ward lashes out to protect them. At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the duration is increased by 5 days and the psychic damage is increased by 1d10 for each level beyond 5th.

Transmutation cantrip Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V Duration: 1 round You flood magic into your legs, allowing you to bound high into the air from a standstill. Your jump distance increases by 10 feet until the start of your next turn, and you can make a running high jump or a running long jump without a running start.

6th-level Illusion Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30ft Sphere Centered on self Components: V, S, Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Spell Lists: Wizard (Legacy), Wizard, Warlock(Legacy), Warlock, Sage, Sorcerer(Legacy), Sorcerer Description You create a magical illusion around yourself, revealing a vast, star-lit night with a multitude of shooting stars, each with a different, brighter hue. Each creature you choose within the area of the spell must make a wisdom saving throw or take 5d6 psychic damage half on a successful save and become charmed or frightened for one round(caster's choice). Until the spell ends the caster must use their action to maintain concentration reforcing the wisdom save. At Higher levels For each spell slot above 6th level, this spell does 2d6 extra psychic damage Spell created by Daemos

transmutation cantrip. (Bard (Legacy), Sorcerer (Legacy), Warlock (Legacy), Wizard (Legacy), Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 15 feet Components: S Duration: 1 hour Description With a flick of your wrist, you magically start the process of completing a small and simple task, such as flipping a book page, buttering bread, or heating a cup of tea, without any physical interaction. The task can't include anything that is intended to inflict a harmful effect on a creature and must be something you'd normally be able to accomplish without the use of magic. If the task would take longer than the duration (such as folding laundry, etc.), the task only progresses as far as it would within the hour. The spell fails if the target of the task has total cover from you. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three tasks active at a time, and you can dismiss one of them as a bonus action.

7th-level transmutation. (Wizard, Sorcerer, Warlock, College of Swords, College of Valor) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self Components: V, S, M (a few hairs from a bull) Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Description You endow yourself with endurance and martial prowess fueled by magic. Until the spell ends, you can't cast spells of 6th level or higher, and you gain two of the following benefits: You gain 50 temporary hit points. If any of these remain when the spell ends, they are lost. You have advantage on attack rolls that you make with simple and martial weapons. When you hit a target with a weapon attack, that target takes an extra 2d12 force damage. You have proficiency with shields, simple weapons, and martial weapons. You have proficiency in Strength and Constitution saving throws. You can attack twice, instead of once, when you take the Attack action on your - turn. You ignore this benefit if you already have a feature, like Extra Attack, that gives you extra attacks. Immediately after the spell ends, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or suffer one level of exhaustion. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 8th level or higher, you can choose an additional effect for every level above 7th.
Aberrant Mind. The thought and the spell were never separate things. At PL 25 you choose a Weave; PL 29 and 33 branch within it; PL 37 gives your Weave's capstone.
Your Order grants these two disciplines at PL 21. They don't count against the number of disciplines you know, and no other Order can learn them.

○ Focus. Your cantrips deal one additional damage die on a hit. ● Lance (3 psi) — Rider. Once per turn when you hit a creature or damage it with a spell, it makes an Intelligence save, taking 3d8 Psychic damage on a failure, half on a success. ●●● Grafted Casting (11 psi) — Magic action. Cast a spell of level 4 or lower that you know without expending a spell slot. If you choose, it deals Psychic damage instead of its normal type.

○ Focus. You have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed and 5 ft of additional reach. ● Unspool (3 psi) — Bonus Action. Until the end of your next turn your reach increases by 15 ft, and you can Grapple at that range. ●● Wrong Anatomy (8 psi) — Bonus Action. For 1 minute you're immune to Critical Hits and have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. No concentration.

+5 Sorcery Points, and you regain your Proficiency Bonus in them on a Short Rest. Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell of level 1 or higher, you can activate one Reflex-band option as part of that same action.
Fusion. When you cast a spell that targets a single creature, a Reflex-band option you activate this turn can target that creature without spending psi.

Shaping. Every sorcerer spell you know of level 5 or lower counts as a Psionic Spell for the purpose of Psionic Sorcery. You can cast such a spell by spending Sorcery Points equal to its level, with no verbal, somatic, or material components — including materials that would be consumed, which the psionic casting supplies from nothing.
Sustain. Once per turn when you damage a creature with a spell, regain Hit Points equal to twice the spell's level.

Resonant Weave. When you cast a spell of level 1 or higher, the first discipline you activate before the end of that turn costs 2 less psi, to a minimum of 0. Dual Weave. Once per turn you can cast a cantrip as part of activating a discipline.

Reshape. When you cast a spell, you can change its damage type to Psychic or Force. Displaced Casting. Your spells can originate from any point you can see within 60 ft. You must have a clear path to that point, and the spell's own range is measured from there.

Feed. When a creature dies within 60 ft of you, regain 2 Sorcery Points. Once per turn. Siphon. When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with a spell or discipline, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Prestige Level.

Aberrant Reach. The range of your spells and disciplines increases by 30 ft and they ignore half and three-quarters cover. Twin Manifestation. Once per turn, a Committed-band option you activate can target a second creature within range at no additional cost.

Unanswerable. Your spells and disciplines can't be counterspelled, dispelled, or detected as magic, and creatures have Disadvantage on the first saving throw they make against a spell of yours each combat. Free Shaping. Once per turn you can apply one Metamagic option without spending Sorcery Points. You can't apply Quickened Spell or Twinned Spell this way.

Bloom. Enemies starting their turn within 10 ft take Psychic damage equal to your Psionic Ability modifier, and you regain that many Hit Points. Consume Magic. When you end or counter a magical effect you did not create, regain Sorcery Points equal to its level.

Woven Mind — Apotheosis of Mind. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute: you can cast one spell of level 5 or lower as a Bonus Action on each of your turns, and your spells and disciplines ignore Resistance to Psychic and Force damage. Warped Word — The Unwritten Word. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute the shape of a spell stops constraining you. For the duration: Every spell you cast can reshape its area into any form covering no more spaces than the original, and change its damage type to Psychic or Force. The range of your spells increases by 60 ft. The first time each turn a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells, it takes additional Psychic damage equal to your Prestige Level. This changes a spell's shape, not its rules. It never alters which ability a saving throw uses, a spell's level, or its casting time. Hungering Mind — Devourer. Once per Long Rest as a Bonus Action, for 1 minute all damage you deal heals you for half the amount, and each enemy that fails a saving throw against you gives you 2 Sorcery Points.
Hollowed bone and spread pinion. A frame stripped of everything that isn't lift, ending in feet built to close on something and not open again. Bird of prey in shape, if not in species.

Open Sky: You gain a Fly Speed equal to half your Speed. While in Hybrid Shape, it becomes equal to your full Speed and you can hover. Far Sight: You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight and on Initiative rolls, and you can see clearly up to 1 mile with no penalty for distance.

Dive: As part of your Attack action, drop up to 60 feet in a straight line and make a melee attack. On a hit, add three Martial Arts dice of damage. Carry Off: The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your save DC or be carried with you up to 20 feet in any direction and knocked Prone when released.
Choose one: The Stooping Death, The Stormwing, or The Sky Sovereign.

Opener — Sky's Advantage: You don't provoke Opportunity Attacks while flying, and any creature that is Prone, falling, or has no Fly Speed grants you advantage on attack rolls while you are airborne. PL 30 — choose one: Terminal Velocity: Stoop adds one additional Martial Arts die for every 20 feet you dove, to a maximum of six total. Wingover: After a Stoop, you can immediately fly up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. PL 35 — choose one: Broken on Impact: A creature hit by Stoop has its Speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn and cannot take Reactions during that time. Falling Star: When you end a Stoop, you can cast a spell with a casting time of an action as a Bonus Action. Once per Short or Long Rest. PL 40 — Capstone: The Falling Sky: Stoop costs 1 Primal Point, can be used as a Bonus Action, and your Fly Speed doubles. Any creature you drop from any height takes falling damage as if it had fallen twice the actual distance.

Opener — Cyclone: As an Action, spend 2 Primal Points to raise a 30-foot-radius storm around you for 1 minute. It is Difficult Terrain for creatures without a Fly Speed, ranged attacks through it have disadvantage, and creatures entering or starting their turn in it make a Strength saving throw against your save DC or are pushed 15 feet and knocked Prone. PL 30 — choose one: Eye of the Storm: You and allies you choose are unaffected by your Cyclone and can fly at half Speed within it. Howling Winds: Creatures in your Cyclone are Deafened and cannot cast spells with Verbal components. PL 35 — choose one: Gathering Front: Cyclone's radius becomes 60 feet, and it moves with you. Storm's Conduit: While your Cyclone is active, spells you cast that deal Lightning or Thunder damage add your Wisdom modifier to their damage, and their range doubles within the storm. PL 40 — Capstone: Weather Front: Cyclone costs nothing, lasts until you dismiss it, and requires no Action to raise. Once per round you can direct a stroke of lightning at any creature within it, dealing four Martial Arts dice of Lightning damage.

Opener — Talon Grip: When you hit a Large or smaller creature with a melee attack, spend 1 Primal Point to Grapple it as part of the attack. It moves with you when you fly, has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you, and takes your Martial Arts die at the start of each of its turns. PL 30 — choose one: Iron Grip: You can Grapple Huge creatures. A creature you Grapple has disadvantage on checks to escape, and takes two Martial Arts dice instead of one at the start of each of its turns. Two Talons: You can maintain Talon Grip on two creatures at once. PL 35 — choose one: Drop: Releasing a Grappled creature while airborne deals falling damage and forces a Constitution save against your save DC or the creature is Stunned until the end of its next turn. Weightless Casting: You can cast spells with Somatic components while Grappling a creature, and creatures you Grapple have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells. PL 40 — Capstone: Nothing Below Is Safe: Talon Grip costs nothing and can seize a creature of any size. While you hold a creature aloft, it cannot be targeted by its allies' spells or abilities, and you can carry it at full Fly Speed without penalty.
Long-limbed and deep-chested. Digitigrade legs, a jaw built for closing distance and refusing to let go. Canine in silhouette, whatever the details.

Relentless Stride: Your Speed increases by 15 feet and you ignore Difficult Terrain. The first time you move at least 20 feet toward a creature on your turn, your next melee attack against it before the end of that turn deals additional damage equal to your Martial Arts die. Hunter's Nose: You gain Blindsight out to 30 feet via scent, you have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to avoid Exhaustion, and you can track a creature you've smelled within the last 24 hours with advantage.

Give Chase: As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet of you moves, takes the Disengage action, or is reduced to half its Hit Points or fewer, you move up to your Speed toward it without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Snap: If you end that movement within reach of the triggering creature, you can make one melee attack against it.
Choose one: The Pack Leader, The Relentless, or The Tracker.

Opener — Shared Instinct: Allies within 30 feet of you add your Wisdom modifier to Initiative rolls. When you use Run Down, one willing ally within 30 feet may also move up to half their Speed as part of your Reaction. PL 30 — choose one: Drive the Quarry: Allies scoring attacks against a creature you moved toward this turn score critical hits on a roll of 19–20. Herd: When an ally hits a creature within your reach, you can move that creature up to 10 feet to a space you choose. PL 35 — choose one: Wolf at Every Door: Run Down now pulls two willing allies along instead of one. Bloom of the Pack: When you cast a spell of level 1 or higher, each ally within 30 feet gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier plus the spell's level.
