PL 40 — Capstone: Alpha: Allies within 30 feet gain your Tireless Gait Speed bonus and ignore Difficult Terrain. Run Down no longer costs a Primal Point and can be used twice per round. When you or an ally within 30 feet hits a creature you moved toward this turn, that attack deals additional damage equal to your Martial Arts die.

Opener — Hamstring: When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can reduce its Speed by 15 feet until the start of your next turn. If its Speed reaches 0 this way, it falls Prone. PL 30 — choose one: Worry the Wound: A creature whose Speed you reduced this turn has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn. Long Wind: You can take the Dash action twice per turn, and you ignore the first 30 feet of any forced movement imposed on you. PL 35 — choose one: Closing Jaws: Your first melee attack each turn against a creature whose Speed is 0, that is Prone, or that you moved at least 20 feet toward deals additional damage equal to two Martial Arts dice. Hounding Magic: When a creature fails a saving throw against a spell you cast, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn and it cannot teleport during that time. PL 40 — Capstone: Nowhere to Go: No creature can take the Dash or Disengage action within 30 feet of you without first succeeding on a Wisdom saving throw against your save DC; on a failure, the action is wasted. Any creature whose Speed you have reduced to 0 takes damage equal to two Martial Arts dice at the start of each of its turns while it remains within 30 feet of you.

Opener — Deep Scent: Your scent Blindsight extends to 60 feet, and you know the exact direction and distance to any creature you have scented within the last 24 hours. PL 30 — choose one: Never Lost: You always know the way back to any place you have been, and you cannot be magically deceived about direction, distance, or location. Run It Down: As a Bonus Action, name a creature you have scented within 60 feet. Until the end of your next turn you know its location, ignore any cover it has, and your attacks against it cannot miss due to concealment, invisibility, or illusion. PL 35 — choose one: Quarry's Curse: Once per turn, when you cast a spell targeting a creature you have scented, you can force it to reroll one successful saving throw against that spell, using the new result. Cut Off: When a creature you have scented attempts to teleport or planeshift, you can spend 2 Primal Points to force a Charisma saving throw against your save DC; on a failure, the effect fails and is wasted. PL 40 — Capstone: The Hunt Ends Where I Say: Your scent Blindsight extends to 120 feet and pierces invisibility, illusion, and shapechange. A creature you have scented cannot hide from you by any means, has disadvantage on saving throws against your spells and features, and takes additional damage equal to two Martial Arts dice the first time you hit it each turn.
Coiled and silent. Retractable claws, a spine that stores tension like a drawn bow, eyes that resolve detail in near-total dark. Feline in build, though not necessarily in kind.

Night Eyes: You gain Darkvision out to 120 feet, or extend your existing Darkvision by 60 feet. Soundless: You have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed and can move across ceilings and vertical surfaces without a check. You can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action even when only lightly obscured, and your first melee attack against a creature that cannot see you deals additional damage equal to your Martial Arts die.

Spring: As part of your Attack action, leap up to 30 feet to a space you can see and make a melee attack on landing. First Blood: If you were Hidden or the target hasn't acted yet this combat, that strike is an automatic critical hit, and the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your save DC or fall Prone.
Choose one: The Ambusher, The Shadow, or The Ripper.

Opener — Patient Blood: You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn yet this combat, and against any creature that can't see you. PL 30 — choose one: Held Breath: Your Stealth checks cannot be reduced below your passive Wisdom (Perception) score, and moving at full Speed imposes no penalty on them. Coiled: You automatically win Initiative against any creature that has not detected you, acting before the first round begins. PL 35 — choose one: Opening Salvo: The first spell you cast in each combat is treated as though cast with a spell slot one level higher, and creatures that have not yet taken a turn have disadvantage on saving throws against it. Second Spring: If your Pounce reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points, you can immediately Pounce again at no cost. PL 40 — Capstone: The First and Last Moment: Once per Short or Long Rest, at the start of a combat in which no enemy has detected you, you take a free turn before Initiative is rolled. Pounce used on that turn costs nothing.

Opener — Vanish: As a Bonus Action, spend 1 Primal Point to become Invisible until the end of your next turn or until you deal damage. When you end this invisibility by attacking, that attack scores a critical hit on a roll of 19–20. PL 30 — choose one: Nowhere and Everywhere: While Invisible, your Speed doubles and you leave no tracks, scent, or trace of passage. Blur the Line: When a creature misses you with an attack, you can spend 1 Primal Point to immediately become Invisible until the end of your next turn. PL 35 — choose one: Gone Again: Once per turn, when you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, you immediately become Invisible until the end of your next turn without spending a Primal Point. Veiled Casting: You can cast spells while Invisible without ending the invisibility, provided the spell deals no damage. Spells cast this way need no Verbal component. PL 40 — Capstone: Never There At All: Vanish costs no Primal Point and you can use it as a Free Action. Dealing damage no longer ends it; instead it ends at the start of your second turn after you deal damage, and you can renew it freely once it has ended.

Opener — Severing Claws: When you score a critical hit with a melee attack, the target's Hit Point maximum is reduced by the damage dealt until it finishes a Long Rest, and it cannot regain Hit Points until the end of your next turn. PL 30 — choose one: Wide Wound: Your melee attacks score critical hits on a roll of 19–20. Bleed: A creature whose Hit Point maximum you reduced takes damage equal to your Martial Arts die at the start of each of its turns until it finishes a Short or Long Rest. PL 35 — choose one: Tear: On a critical hit, roll your Martial Arts dice three times instead of twice. Withering Magic: A creature whose Hit Point maximum you reduced has disadvantage on saving throws against your spells, and takes an extra Martial Arts die of damage from them. PL 40 — Capstone: Nothing Heals: A creature can succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your save DC at the end of each of its turns to end the Hit Point maximum reduction from Severing Claws; until it does, the reduction persists through rests. A creature reduced below half its original maximum this way has the Frightened condition with respect to you.
Soulknife. Thought sharpened until it cuts. The Whetstone branches. At PL 25 you choose an Edge; at PL 29 and 33 you choose within it; at PL 37 your Edge gives its capstone. Each choice is permanent.
You alone may choose Dexterity as your Psionic Ability. A Soulknife's power was never seated in the intellect; it lives in the hand and the reflex.
Your Order grants these two disciplines at PL 21. They don't count against the number of disciplines you know, and no other Order can learn them.

○ Focus. Your Psychic Blades don't vanish at the end of your turn, and you can manifest them again with no action. ● Whetted (3 psi) — Rider. Once per turn when you hit with a blade, the target's Armor Class drops by 1 until the end of your next turn, stacking to 3. ●● Blade Chorus (7 psi) — Bonus Action. Make one blade attack against each of up to three creatures within 5 ft of you.

○ Focus. You have Advantage on Initiative, and a creature you damage can't speak, shout, or cast spells with verbal components until the end of your next turn. ● Unseen Edge (4 psi) — Bonus Action. Until the end of your turn, your blade attacks against creatures that can't see you deal an extra 2d12 damage. ●●● The Quiet Between (12 psi) — Magic action. One creature within 30 ft makes a Constitution save. On a failure it takes 12d12 Psychic damage and is Stunned until the end of your next turn. If this reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it falls without a sound and no other creature notices for 1 minute.
+4 Psionic Energy Dice, and you regain your Proficiency Bonus in them on a Short Rest. Your Psychic Blades deal 1d12 Psychic damage, rising to 2d6 at PL 33, and gain the Light property.
Range. Your Psychic Blades' thrown range becomes 120/240 ft, and you can originate a thrown blade from any point within 30 ft of you.

Melee. Your blades gain the Nick property. When you hit with a blade in melee, you gain +1 AC until the start of your next turn, stacking up to +3. Nick and Psychic Blades. Your Soulknife's Bonus Action blade attack and the Light property's extra attack are the same attack, not two separate ones. Nick lets you make that attack as part of your Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action, once per turn. It does not grant an extra attack — what it buys you is your Bonus Action back, which on this class is the scarcest thing you have. It still uses the smaller blade die.

Strategy. When you deal Sneak Attack damage with your Psychic Blade, you can also deal Sneak Attack damage with the blade you use as a Bonus Action on the same turn. The Bonus Action blade uses half as many Sneak Attack dice, rounded down. Note. The Close Edge and the Quiet Edge don't combine — they're different branches, and you choose one at PL 25. A Quiet Edge Soulknife keeps the standard Bonus Action blade attack and gets a second helping of Sneak Attack from it; a Close Edge Soulknife gets Nick and can fold that attack into the Attack action, but has no second Sneak Attack to apply to it.

Splitting Throw. When a thrown blade hits, it ricochets to a second creature within 30 ft of the first; make a separate attack roll against it. Down the Blade. You have no Disadvantage on thrown blade attacks at long range, and you deal an extra 1d12 damage to creatures at least 60 ft away.
documents.s: If you took the Thrown Edge

documents.t: Whirl. When you take the Attack action, you can make one additional blade attack against a different creature within 5 ft of you. Riposte. When a creature within 5 ft misses you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to make one blade attack against it.
documents.s: If you took the Close Edge

documents.t: Mark the Opening. As a Bonus Action, mark a creature within 60 ft. Until the end of your next turn, attacks against it by you or your allies have Advantage. Vanishing Act. Immediately after you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can teleport up to 30 ft and become Invisible until the end of your turn.
documents.s: If you took the Quiet Edge

documents.t: Storm of Edges. As a Magic action, throw a blade at each of up to your Proficiency Bonus in creatures you can see within 120 ft. Piercing Line. As a Magic action, hurl a blade in a 60-ft line. Each creature makes a Dexterity save, taking 8d12 Psychic damage on a failure, half on a success.

Rending Thought. Once per turn, when you hit a creature that has already taken damage from you this turn, add one roll of your Manifestation Die to the damage. Bladelock. When you hit a creature with a melee blade, it makes a Strength save or is Restrained by psychic edges until the end of your next turn.

Sever. Once per turn when you hit with a blade, expend a Psionic Energy Die: the target makes a Constitution save or takes maximum damage from the attack and can regain no Hit Points for 1 minute. Read the Room. At the start of combat, you know the Armor Class and current Hit Points of every creature you can see, and you have Advantage on attacks against any creature that has not yet acted.

Thrown Edge — Blade Beyond Distance. Twice per turn you can attack with your Psychic Blades against any creature you can see within 120 ft, ignoring cover and any AC bonus from cover or shields. Close Edge — Unmaking Cut. Once per turn when you hit a creature in melee, it makes a Constitution save. On a failure it takes an extra 6d12 Psychic damage and its Armor Class is reduced by 2 until the end of the encounter, stacking. Quiet Edge — The Perfect Kill. Once per Long Rest, when you hit a creature that is unaware of you or that you have Advantage against, the attack is a Critical Hit and you roll maximum Sneak Attack damage.

7th-level transmutation. (Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (30 ft. sphere) Components: V, S, M ((a gemstone worth at least 5,000gp, which the spell consumes)) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description Through carefully crafted thought projections and the transmutation of mental energies, you create a field of potentiality around you, exceeding your normal limitations. When you cast this spell you create 6 Thought Forms. You can consume these Thought Forms in a number of ways, granting additional benefits depending on your choice: When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you misses with an attack, you can consume any number of Thought Form. They gain a +2 bonus to the attack roll equal to the number of Thought Forms consumed, potentially turning the miss into a hit. Once per turn, when you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you take the Attack action, you can consume 2 Thought Forms to allow them to make an additional attack as part of that same action. When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you take damage from an attack, you can consume any number of Thought Forms as a reaction, granting them 10 temporary hit points for each Thought Form consumed. These temporary hit points last until the start of your next turn. When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can use your reaction to consume any number of your Thought Forms. They gain a +2 bonus to your saving throw for each Thought Form consumed, potentially turning the failure into a success. As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend an unused spell slot to create a number of Thought Forms equal to the level of the spell slot expended, up to a maximum of 6.

Evocation cantrip Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (10-foot cone) Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous You produce a distorted wave of noise in a 10-foot cone, which can be heard up to 100 feet away. Each creature in that area must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 thunder damage. An echo of this noise persists until the end of your next turn. If you cast this spell again before the end of your next turn, its damage dice become d8s instead of d6s. This spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6) and 17th level (4d6).

7th-level Enchantment (Bard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 60 ft Components: V, S, M (a polished obsidian mirror worth at least 5,000 gp) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description You place a curse on a creature that you can see within range, forcing them to make a Wisdom saving throw or be cursed for the duration. While cursed, you are aware of the target's surface thoughts and emotional state, and can communicate telepathically with them. Once on each of your turns when you hit the target with an attack or they fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect originating from you, it deals an additional 5d6 psychic damage in addition to its other effects, and you become Vindicated, gaining advantage on the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check (your choice) you make before the end of your next turn. Once on each of the target's turns when they miss you with an attack or you succeed on a saving throw against a spell or magical effect originating from them, it takes 5d6 psychic damage and they become Discouraged, gaining disadvantage on the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check (your choice) they make before the end of their next turn. At Higher Levels When casting this spell with a spell slot of 8th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 7th.

2nd-level evocation. (Artificer, Druid, Ranger, Sorcerer, Wizard, Arcane Domain) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 120 feet Components: V, S, M (a tiny metal spike) Duration: 1 minute Description You shoot a thin toxic spike at a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. If it hits, the target takes 2d8 poison damage, and the spike is lodged in the creature’s body. At the start of each of the creature’s turns while the spike is embedded in the creature, the target takes 1d6 poison damage. The target may use their action to pull the spike out, after which the spell ends. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the initial damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd and the subsequent damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 2nd.

8th-level conjuration. (College of Creation, Sorcerer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 hour Range: 100 feet Components: V, S, M (1,000 gp worth of Residuum or any Arcane Dust/Powder) Duration: 24 hours Description You magically expand the dimensions of an existing container, room, or otherwise fully enclosed space beyond its physical limits. Select an existing physical space (no larger than 125 sq ft.) with at most one single point of entry such as a lid, door, window or flap, (no larger than 10 sq ft), and with a solid border (no transparent walls, windows, etc.). As a part of this spell, the caster must inscribe runes around the opening and the borders of the space to maintain its external structure. The interior dimensions of that space expand by up to 5 feet in any direction that you choose as the spell takes effect, warping to accommodate any items or creatures inside. When the spell ends, the space returns to its normal size and any items or occupants unable to fit in the original space are softly ejected through the opening. If there is no opening or the objects cannot fit through it, the items or creatures are scattered randomly in the Astral Plane as determined by the GM. Casting this spell in the same space every day for 30 days makes the effect permanent; further castings can be used to expand an existing Transdimensional Space beyond its size provided that it still has a single exterior border with no more than one point of entry.

8th-level illusion. (Artificer Elite, Sage, Sorcerer, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 minute (ritual) Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (a medium or smaller object) Duration: Until Dispelled Description You touch the item used as the spell's material component for the duration of the spellcasting, imbuing it with the illusion of another object. The target object then looks, feels, and otherwise takes on the cosmetic properties of any other item of your choosing of the same category or similar nature. For example, you can cause a suit of armor to look like robes, a sword to look like a mace, etc. The item retains all of its original statistics. If the item requires a part of itself for its normal function that would not be present in the illusion, that part is hidden while not in use.

3rd-level Conjuration spell (Artificer, Bard, Cleric, Paladin, Ranger, Sage, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 90 feet Components: V, S, M (an object weighing less than 10 pounds and worth at least 1 sp) Duration: Instantaneous Description When you cast this spell, you present the object used as the material component. You magically twist space around that object, teleporting it to an unoccupied space within range. Alternatively, you can choose another target non-magical object you can see within range. Both the material component and the target object is teleported, swapping places. If the object is being worn or carried, the creature must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity (its choice) saving throw, negating the effects on a success. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the range of the spell increases by 30 feet and the maximum weight of objects that you can use with this spell increases by 5 pounds for each slot level above 3rd.

Casting Time: 8 hours Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (clay and runes worth 2,000 gp, consumed) Duration: Instantaneous You awaken the mind of a creature, granting it sentience and self-awareness. Choose one non-hostile creature you touch. You can have a number of creatures awakened by this spell equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of one). If casting this spell would exceed your limit, the creature awakened longest ago immediately loses all benefits of True Awaken. Restrictions: This spell automatically fails if the target is summoned or maintained by a concentration spell, is planar bound, has Legendary Resistance, or has an Intelligence score of 10 or higher. Effects: If the spell succeeds, the target’s Intelligence becomes 10. The target gains the ability to understand one language you know and becomes capable of basic reasoning, learning, and self-awareness. Limitations: This spell grants no combat benefits, proficiencies, spellcasting, or CR increases. It does not remove or alter magical control already affecting the creature, and it does not restore lost memories or identity. Creation: Spell is created by Momo's Character Daemos

9th-level transmutation. (Druid) Meta Casting Time: 1 hour Range: Touch Components: V, S, M (rare oils and unguents worth at least 10,000 gp, which the spell consumes, and vial of willingly given blood from the race to be reincarnated into) Duration: Instantaneous Description You touch a willing living humanoid. The spell transforms their body into an adult form of another race. If the target isn’t willing, the spell fails. The caster can choose a medium or small humanoid race for the humanoid to transform into, but must have a vial of willing given blood from a member of that race. The reincarnated creature recalls its former life and experiences. It retains the capabilities it had in its original form, except it exchanges its original race for the new one and changes its racial traits accordingly.

You've made a pact with a deathless being, a creature that defies the cycle and life and death, forsaking its mortal shell so it might eternally pursue its unfathomable ambitions. For such beings, time and morality are fleeting things, the concerns of those for whom grains of sand still rush through life's hourglass. Having once been mortal themselves, these ancient undead know firsthand the paths of ambition and the routes past the doors of death. They eagerly share this profane knowledge, along with other secrets, with those who work their will among the living. Beings of this type include the demilich Acererak, the vampire tyrant Kas the Bloody-Handed, the githyanki lich-queen Vlaakith, the dracolich Dragotha, the undead pharaoh Ankhtepot, and the elusive Darklord, Azalin Rex. Features: Expanded Spell List 3rd Level - Form of Dread 6th Level - Grave Touched 10th Level - Necrotic Husk Spirit Projection

3rd-level Undead feature When you reach a Warlock level specified in the Undead Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells available and it doesn't count towards your amount of warlock spells known.

3rd-level Undead feature You manifest an aspect of your patron's dreadful power. As a bonus action, you transform for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits while transformed: You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level., Once during each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw, and if the saving throw fails, the target is frightened of you until the end of your next turn., You are immune to the frightened condition.,You can transform a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. The appearance of your Form of Dread reflects some aspect of your patron. For example, your form could be a shroud of shadows forming the crown and robes of your lich patron, or your body might glow with glyphs from ancient funerary rites and be surrounded by desert winds, suggesting your mummy patron.

6th-level Undead feature Your patron's powers have a profound effect on your body and magic. You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. In addition, once during each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll and roll damage against the creature, you can replace the damage type with necrotic damage. While you are using your Form of Dread, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the necrotic damage the target takes.

10th-level Undead feature Your connection to undeath and necrotic energy now saturates your body. You have resistance to necrotic damage. If you are transformed using your Form of Dread, you instead become immune to necrotic damage. In addition, when you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to retore your hit points to twice your warlock level instead and cause your body to erupt with deathly energy. Each creature of your choice that is within 30 feet of you takes necrotic damage equal to 2d10 + your warlock level. You then gain 1 level of exhaustion. Once you use this reaction, you can't do so again until you finish 1d4 long rests.

Your spirit can become untethered from your physical form. As an action, you can project your spirit from your body. The body you leave behind is unconscious and in a state of suspended animation. Your spirit resembles your mortal form in almost every way, replicating your game statistics but not your possessions. Any damage or other effects that apply to your spirit or physical body affects the other. Your spirit can remain outside your body for up to 1 hour. When your projection ends, your spirit returns to your body or your body magically teleports to your spirit's space (your choice). While projecting your spirit, you gain the following benefits: Your spirit and body gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage., When you cast a spell of the conjuration or necromancy school, the spell doesn't require verbal or somatic components or material components that lack a gold cost., You have a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover. You can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, but you take 1d10 force damage if you end your turn inside a creature or an object., While you are using your Form of Dread, once during each of your turns when you deal necrotic damage to a creature, you regain hit points equal to half the amount of necrotic damage dealt., Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest or by expending a Pact slot.

evocation cantrip. (Artificer, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard, Arcane Domain) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 10 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous Description With an upward flourish of your hand, a splash of poisonous venom is released from your hand into the face of a creature in range. The targeted creature must make a Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 poison damage and be blinded until the start of your next turn on a failed save. The spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

3rd-level evocation. (Artificer, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard, Arcane Domain) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, S, M (a splash of weak poison) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description You attempt infect a creature nearby with a nasty strain of poison. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw or take 3d8 poison damage and be infected. An infected creature is poisoned and takes an additional 2d8 poison damage at the start of each of their turns. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much poison damage and is not infected. The spell has no effect on creatures immune to the poisoned condition. When an infected creature dies, they explode in a poisonous burst. Each creature within 5 feet of the infected creature when it dies must roll a constitution saving throw or be infected as well, suffering the full effects of the spell. At the end of each of each infected creature’s turns until the spell ends, they can make another Constitution saving throw. On a success, the spell ends for that creature. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the initial damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

2nd-level conjuration. (Artificer, Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard) Meta Casting Time: 1 reaction (when a creature within 5 ft of you hits you with an attack) Range: Self (5 ft. radius) Components: V, S Duration: Instantaneous Description The attacker must make a constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is teleported to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 ft of you. If the result of this teleport places the target in a location where the attack would no longer be in range, it misses.

5th-level transmutation. (Artificer, Cleric, Paladin) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Touch Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour Description A weapon you touch becomes heavier on impact towards enemies. For the duration, the weapon becomes magical, if it isn't already, and deals one extra die of the weapon's damage die. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the extra damage increases to two dice.

1st-level necromancy. (Paladin) Meta Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: Self Components: V Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Description Your weapon radiates terrible energy that empowers the next strike you make with it. The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack during this spell’s duration, your attack deals an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. If the target of that attack was a creature, it must make a successful Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute, its flesh rotting around the wound. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The rotting effect also ends if the affected creature receives magical healing. At Higher Levels When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage dealt by the weapon’s hit increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st. Subsequent necrotic damage doesn’t increase.
Augmenter Greaser Physicist Scrapper

The Augmenter is a unique blend of artificer and psychic, merging technology with mental prowess. These specialists understand the psyche and wield their own bodies as tools for both combat and manipulation. Whether augmenting their limbs or delving into the minds of others, Augmenters are masters of self-enhancement Features: 3rd Level - Augmenter Spells 3rd Level - Self Augmentation 5th Level - Extra Attack 9th Level - Mind Over Matter 15th Level - Master Augmenter Augmenter Infusions

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Augmenter Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare. Augmenter Spells reflect your understanding of the psyche and allows you to influence the mind of others. Augmenter Spells 3rd Level - Command, Dissonant Whispers 5th Level - Tasha’s Mind Whip, Crown of Madness 9th Level - Antagonize, Fast Friends 13th Level - Raulothim’s Psychic Lance, Compulsion 17th Level - Synaptic Static, Modify Memory

Starting at 3rd level, you master the technique of augmenting your own body. Each of the following parts of your body can be infused using your artificer Infusions; Torso, Head, Legs. You also gain access to Augmenter Infusions, these infusions are known and does not count toward your total of known infusions. For the purposes of normal Infusions, the Torso is seen as Armor, head as a Helmet or any peripheral that is worn on the head, and legs are seen as boots. You also learn how to augment your arms with special arm weapons. These can also be infused, and you can only have one arm enhancement active at a time. Whenever you finish a long rest you can swap arm enhancements.

These Enhancements count as weapons and infusions can be applied to them. Each enhancement grants the artificer an applicable fighting Style based on the installed enhancement. Mantis Blade​ You gain retractable blade attachments on either of your arms Properties: Finesse Fighting Style: Dueling Damage: 1d6 piercing Special: The blade can be retracted or unsheathed as a bonus action, leaving the hand free to wield other items. When you score a critical hit with the mantis blade the target needs to make a constitution save against your Spell DC or start to bleed. When bleeding the target loses hp equal to your proficiency bonus at the start of each of its turn. It can make the save again at the end of each turn. Monowire Attachment​ These fine wires get pulled from your wrists and are wielded like a whip. Properties: Finesse, Reach Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting Damage: 1d4 slashing Special: The wires count as two separate weapons for the purpose of two weapon fighting, but only require a single infusion. The wires use Intelligence for its attack and damage modifiers. Gorilla Arms​ Your Hands and forearms are augmented with heavier metals and mechanical support. Properties: Heavy Fighting Style: Unarmed Fighting Damage: Unarmed Strike, Bludgeoning Special: You make your attacks with the Gorilla Arms as unarmed strikes. You also have advantage on Strength( Athletics) checks to escape, attempt, maintain grapples. Arm Launcher​ You can load bolts or sling bullets into your arm and fire them as projectiles. Properties: Ranged (40/80), Reload (6) Fighting Style: Archery Damage: 1d8 piercing (bolts), bludgeoning (sling bullets) Special: The Launcher leaves your hands open while firing. On a hit, the launcher does 1d4 force damage to the target, all creatures within 5ft of the target must make Dexterity save against your spell save DC or take 1d4 force damage.
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

At 9th level, your deep understanding of the mind allows you to manipulate the physical world with your thoughts. You gain the following abilities: Mental Shield: You gain resistance to psychic damage. Additionally, when you take psychic damage, you can use your reaction to reflect half of that damage back to the attacker. Psychic Insight: You can use your action to read the surface thoughts of a creature you can see within 30 feet. This effect lasts for 1 minute, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you can also implant a simple suggestion (as per the Suggestion spell) into their mind. This ability can be used once per short rest.

At 15th Level your ability to enhance your augmentations has reached unparalleled heights: You can now add 2 infusions to any of your augmentations. You are able to use master properties for your arm augmentations. Each arm augmentation has two possible properties. When you switch out your arm augmentation you can choose which master property to use. Mantis Blades: Graze, Sap Monowire: Nick, Slow Gorilla Arms: Sap, Push Arm Launcher: Push, Vex

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter, Unarmored Item: Torso Augmentation (requires Attunement) Effect: Your skin is reinforced with a layer of protective material, making you more resilient to physical attacks. Subdermal Armor makes the wearer’s AC equal 10 + Constitution Modifier + Intelligence Modifier

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Torso Augmentation (requires Attunement) Effect: You can use an action to blend into your surroundings, gaining advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks for 1 hour. This ability can be used once per short or long rest.

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Torso Augmentation (requires Attunement) Effect: A sophisticated system of micro-projectors and sensors enables you to alter your appearance at will. As a bonus action you can cast the Disguise self spell on yourself, without spending a spell slot. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.
Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Head Augmentation Effect: You gain proficiency in the perception skill, and can use Intelligence instead of Wisdom for Passive perception and perception checks
Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Head Augmentation Effect: You gain dark vision out to 60 feet, if you already have dark vision from another source, its range is extended by 60 feet.

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Head Augmentation Effect: The infusion highlights your positive features and filters your words, making you sound and look more alluring than you are. You can add your Intelligence modifier to any charisma(persuasion) check you make against a single target.
Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Leg Augmentation Effect: You gain a +10 feet to your walking speed, and your high and long jump distances are doubled.

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Leg Augmentation Effect: Your footfalls are dampened allowing for silent movement. You gain advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. Damage taken from falling is halved.

Prerequisite: 3rd Level Augmenter Item: Leg Augmentation. Effect: You can take the dodge action as a bonus action. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 6th Level Augmenter Item: Special Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: After finishing a short rest you can load any magical potion into the pump. You can then as a reaction to taking damage, prior to taking damage or making an attack inject the potion to activate its effect. Once activated the potion is consumed.

Prerequisite: 6th Level Augmenter Item: Special Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to cast Shield without expending a spell slot. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 6th Level Augmenter Item: Special Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: As a bonus action, you can release nanobots that heal a creature you touch for 2d8 + your Intelligence modifier hit points. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter Item: Mantis Blade Effect: When you hit a creature with the Mantis Blades, you can choose to deal an additional 2d6 psychic damage. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter Item: Monowire Attachment Effect: When you hit a creature with the Monowire Attachment, you can choose to restrain the target. The target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be restrained until the end of your next turn. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter Item: Gorilla Arms Effect: When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can choose to knock the target prone. The target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked prone. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 10th Level Augmenter Item: Arm Launcher Effect: You gain a +4 bonus to attack rolls with the Arm Launcher. Additionally, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on a ranged attack made against you.

Prerequisite: 14th Level Augmenter Item: Torso Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: Advanced optical technology allows you to blend into your surroundings, becoming nearly invisible. As a bonus action you become invisible until the end of your next turn, or until you take damage from any source. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

Prerequisite: 14th Level Augmenter Item: Head Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal 1d6 lightning damage to the attacker. This damage increases to 2d6 if the attacker is wearing metal armor.

Prerequisite: 14th Level Augmenter Item: Leg Augmentation (requires attunement) Effect: You can use a bonus action to jump up to 30 feet in any direction. If you land within 5 feet of an enemy, you can make a melee attack as part of the same bonus action.
Avengers seek to right a wrong, stopping at nothing to correct a past sleight. They dole out their revenge with their own hands, using steel just as much as spirit to forward their goals.

At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons, and you can use weapons as your spiritual focus. When you activate your spirit tether, you gain an amount of temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + half your spiritualist level (rounded down).
Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your soul’s hunger for vengeance.

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to initiate a spirit duel with your target. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or be blinded. While the target is blinded this way, you are also blinded, except you and your target can still see each other normally. As long as this blindness persists, your weapon attacks deal an additional 1d6 damage.

When you are attacked by your tethered target while you are holding a shield, you can use your reaction to spend 1 spirit point and force the target to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the attack misses, and the next attack you make against the tethered target has advantage.
As an action, you can spend 2 spirit points to share your suffering with the tethered target. For the next minute, whenever you take damage, the target takes half as much necrotic damage.

Beginning at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can use a spirit art that uses an action in place of one of these attacks.

At 13th level, your soul lashes out at any creature that would harm you or your allies. Whenever a creature you can see within range of your spirit tether damages you or an ally within 30 feet, you can use your reaction to immediately create a spirit tether. The creature must be one of the targets.
At 18th level, you master the art of vengeance. You learn the following spirit art:

You can use 5 spirit points as an action to empower your weapon. For the next minute, whenever you hit a tethered target with a weapon attack, the attack deals an additional 3d6 force damage. The first time you hit a tethered target after using this art, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the target is rended by your spirit, and cannot restore hit points or gain temporary hit points as long as your spirit tether lasts.

Command a Retinue of the Restless Dead Barrow Lords call upon the dead as readily as the living, commanding the risen as soldiers and sending them into battle without hesitation. The dead may be mindless, but the habits of service endure long after the flesh has failed. Features: 3rd Level - Dread Retinue 3rd Level - Grave Tithe 7th Level - Formations 10th Level - Disposable Forces 15th Level - Deathly Drills 18th Level - Grasp of the Starved Barrow Thrall

You can call the dead from the earth to serve you. Your retinue holds thralls equal to one-third your Fighter level (round down), each using the Brute or Archer stat block (your choice) and sharing your saving throw proficiencies. Your thralls are Friendly to you and your allies and obey your commands. A thrall sinks into the ground when it drops to 0 Hit Points or you die. Summoning Your Retinue. As a Bonus Action, you can summon a thrall in an unoccupied space of earth, sand, loose stone, or grave soil within 30 feet of yourself. You can do so a number of times equal to one-third your Fighter level (round down), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. Summoning a thrall from the corpse of a Small or Medium creature within range expends no use. You can dismiss any number of your thralls at any time (no action required). If a summon would exceed your retinue's maximum, choose one existing thrall to sink into the ground. The Retinue in Combat. Your thralls act during your turn. Each can move and use its Reaction freely, but can take no action other than Dodge unless you take a Bonus Action to command your retinue, in which case each thrall can take any action. While you have the Incapacitated condition, your thralls act freely.

When you or a thrall in your retinue reduces a Hostile creature to 0 Hit Points, you can regain an expended use of Second Wind. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Whenever you use Second Wind, you can also choose a Formation and command your retinue. The Formation lasts until the start of your next turn. A thrall benefits from the Formation only while within 60 feet of you. Phalanx: A thrall has a +2 bonus to AC while within 5 feet of at least one other thrall. Starting at 15th level, each creature also gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Fighter Level. Vanguard: Each thrall's Speed increases by 15 feet. Starting at 15th level, when you choose this Formation, you can also designate one creature within 60 feet of yourself; your thralls have Advantage on attack rolls against it. Wedge: Your thralls deal an extra 1d4 Necrotic damage on a hit. This extra damage increases to 2d4 at 15th level.

Once on each of your turns, when you take the Attack action, you can cause one thrall within 30 feet of yourself to sink into the earth. If you do, you can make one additional attack as part of that action, and that attack deals an extra 2d6 Necrotic damage.

When you choose a Formation using Second Wind, your retinue also gain its passive benefit until you use another Formation. Phalanx: Your thralls gain a +2 bonus to AC. Vanguard: Your thralls' Speed increases by 10 feet. Wedge: Your thralls deal an extra 1d4 Necrotic damage on a hit.

As an Action, choose a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Your thralls sink into the earth, and you summon up to your retinue's maximum number of thralls into unoccupied spaces within 30 feet of that point, regardless of the surface. As they rise, grasping hands erupt: each creature of your choice within 30 feet of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus plus your Constitution modifier). On a failed save, a target takes 5d8 Necrotic damage and is Restrained until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage and isn't Restrained. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

Medium Undead, Neutral AC 15 (Brute only) or 12 (Archer only) HP equal to your Fighter level + 10 Speed 25 ft. STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 14 14 13 5 7 7 +2 +2 +1 −3 −2 −2 Immunities Poison; Exhaustion, Poisoned Senses Darkvision 60 ft., Passive Perception 8 Languages Understands languages you know but can't speak. CR None (XP 0; PB equals your Proficiency Bonus) Actions Grave-Iron (Brute Only). Melee Attack Roll: your Constitution modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2d4 Necrotic damage Barrow Shot (Archer Only). Ranged Attack Roll: your Constitution modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus, range 60/240 ft. Hit: 1d6 Necrotic damage. Reactions Body Block (Brute Only). Trigger: A creature the thrall can see attacks a target other than itself within 5 feet of it. Response: The thrall takes the damage instead of the target. Source: Barrow Lord by Mendax1

Those who enter the order of the symbiote are either a crazed or brave few. Taking in a new being into their own during an induction to hemocraft, they are able to tap into a special power granted by being now two halves of a greater whole. Whether the symbiote be embedded within their flesh, or coiling around their skin, as this new creature's host the Blood Hunters of this order boast an unmatched ability to tear down the biologies of those they may face.

When you join this order at 3rd level, you learn the rite of the blighted as part of your crimson rite features. When you activate the rite of the blighted, the extra damage dealt is poison damage. Additionally, hitting a creature with a weapon infused with this rite that is neither undead or a construct deals extra poison damage equal to your hemocraft modifier.

A limited consciousness within your symbiote grants you an increased perception of your surroundings. You gain proficiency in the perception skill. Additionally, you may add your hemocraft modifier to your initiative rolls.

At 7th level you know the Blood Curse of Exposure, which does not count towards your total number of blood curses known, and its potential rises to great power in combination with your toxins. If you apply your Blood Curse of Exposure to a creature after dealing poison damage from your Rite of the Blighted, the curse will instead last for 1 minute. If you have amplified the curse, you take damage equal to a roll of your hemocraft die at the start of each of your turns in exchange for your symbiote sustaining the infection. If you already know the Blood Curse of Exposure, you may learn a different blood curse of your choice that you qualify for.

At 7th level, when you apply your Brand of Castigation to a creature while you have your Rite of the Blighted active, you may choose to inflict the target with a virulent infection. The target must succeed a constitution saving throw or experience one of the following effects, as determined by rolling your hemocraft die. Hemocraft Die Roll Effect 1 The target becomes Poisoned for 1 minute, and can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, expelling the poison on a successful save. 2 A wave of weakness falls over the target. All attack rolls have advantage against the target until the start of its next turn. 3 Your opponent's blood mixes with your symbiote, allowing a temporary breach in their immune system. The next blood curse you apply to that target within 1 minute that requires a saving throw will take effect regardless of whether or not their saving throw is successful or not. 4 A mild paralytic compound infuses itself within the target, reducing all of its speeds by 10 ft for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. 5 The toxins of your weapon attack invade the target's mind, causing them to make concentration saves at disadvantage until the start of your next turn. 6 Your target has its physical attributes ravaged to some degree. The target suffers a penalty to all Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution Checks and Saving throws equal to your hemocraft die until the end of its next turn. 7 Your target's vision fogs temporarily, causing them to become Blinded until the end of its next turn. 8 Toxins invade your target's body entirely, causing their muscles to lock. The target is Paralyzed until the end of its next turn. 9 An increased spike in potency causes your rite to deliver vastly increased lethality. For one minute, your Rite of the Blighted deals extra damage equal to three rolls of your hemocraft die instead of one. 10 Toxins manage to tear into your target regardless of their biologies. The target loses all resistance and immunity to poison damage for 1 minute, gaining vulnerability instead. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a successful save. Effects listed under a higher number than you can roll with your hemocraft die remain inaccessible until a level in which you can.

Starting at 11th level, your symbiote is able to grant you a further boon to your health. Whenever an effect would restore your hit points, you regain an additional amount of hit points equal to a roll of your hemocraft die. Additionally, you learn the druidcraft cantrip. Your hemocraft ability is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

At 15th Level, If you are reduced to 0 hit points, your symbiote may assume control over your basic motor functions for a limited time in order to protect you. During this time you experience the following: Your speed is halved You cannot use your extra attack feature You cannot take reactions You Still make Death Saving Throws at the start of each of your turns You suffer the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points The symbiote can maintain its control for a number of rounds equal to your hemocraft modifier (minimum of one), until you die, or until you regain at least one hit point. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

At 18th level, your symbiotic connection grants you the ability to entirely ravage a creature's health. You gain the Blood Curse of Lethality for your Blood Maledict feature. This doesn’t count against your number of blood curses known. Blood Curse of Lethality - When you hit a creature with a weapon infused with your Rite of the Blighted, you may choose to apply this Blood Curse. The target must make a constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 8d8 poison damage and suffers a random effect of your Brand of Contagion. The target takes half as much damage on a successful save and suffers no other effects. Amplify - Amplifying this curse will instead reduce the target's hit points to 1 should they fail the saving throw, and take the full 8d8 poison damage on a success.

The blood knight is the title given to an eldritch knight who chooses to delve into the taboo discipline of hemomancy, or the magic of controlling blood and life force. These warriors thrive in the heart of battle where the blood flows thickest, using it to enhance their offensive and defensive capabilities. Features: 3rd Level - Combat Hemomancy 7th Level - Sense Life 10th Level - Blood-Fueled Overdrive 15th Level - Hemomantic Precision 18th Level - Bloody Tyrant

Starting at 3rd level when you choose this archetype, you gain access to a series of hemomantic abilities that allow you to use the blood of your enemies to your advantage. When you damage a creature that has blood within 30 feet of you with a weapon attack, you gain a special die called a blood die, which is a D6. You can have a number of these dice up to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. Creatures that do not have blood do not generate blood dice, and you do not gain blood dice from attacks that are modified by blood dice. You can expend blood dice to perform a number of hemomantic abilities described at the end of this features description. Each time a hemomantic ability asks you to expend your blood dice, you can choose how many you want to roll and gain a benefit based on what you rolled.

Combat Regeneration. At the start of your turn, you can spend blood dice to gain temporary hit points. Roll the dice you spend, add them together, and gain temporary hit points equal to the total, replacing any temporary hit points you already have. Crimson Strike. You can use the Attack action to make a special melee attack, a crimson strike. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them. You brandish the weapon used in the technique and make a melee attack with it against one creature within 15 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes magical piercing, bludgeoning, or slashing damage equal to the total of the blood dice you spent. Blood Shell. When you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to spend blood dice. Roll the dice you spend, add them together, and increase your AC by the amount equal to the total rolled against that attack. Blood Clotting. As a bonus action, you can spend blood dice to throw blood onto a surface at a range of 15 feet and have it stick in a 25 ft. square. Any creature that starts its turn in that area or that enters that area during its turn must make a Strength saving throw with a DC of 10 + the amount you roll on your blood dice (A maximum DC of 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, the creature's speed is reduced to zero until the start of their next turn.

At 7th level, you gain advantage on wisdom (perception) checks to spot and track enemies that have blood in their veins. In addition, your ability to sense blood can be so precise that you have advantage wisdom (insight) checks to tell if someone is lying to you.
At 10th level, when you use your indomitable feature, you can expend one blood die and add it to the roll.
At 15th level, you have a very tight control over blood you spill. You can re-roll one blood die once whenever you roll them for a hemomantic ability.

At 18th level, when you hit a creature with an attack and have the maximum number of blood dice, you can expend them all to force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength or Dexterity modifier. On a failed save, the creature is paralyzed for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the paralyzed target must make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, this paralyzing effect ends.

Considered taboo by many societies and magic practitioners, the use of blood magic—also known as hemocraft—is a rare art that harnesses the latent powers of a creature’s vitality to fuel and amplify the caster’s own capabilities, while manipulating and weakening the bodies of enemies from the inside. Some of the more macabre mages seeking to empower their arcane pursuits turn to hemocraft as a means of bolstering their spells, giving their own life’s blood to reach new heights of frightening magical prowess. The secrets of hemocraft and other forms of blood magic were once the sole purview of the mysterious Claret Orders. In recent years, however, these secrets have begun to spread beyond the order’s members and into the hands of less scrupulous mages. Blood magic has a bad reputation in Tal’Dorei, even though its powers can be used for much more than evil. Features: 2nd Level - Blood Channeling 2nd Level - Sanguine Burst 6th Level - Bond of Mutual Suffering 10th Level - Glyph of Hemorrhaging 14th Level - Thicker than Water

When you choose this arcane tradition at 2nd level, you are able to use your own depleted life essence to channel your magical abilities. Whenever your current hit points are below your hit point maximum, you can use your own body as an arcane focus. In addition, when casting a wizard spell that requires a costly material component, you can forego the component by taking 1d10 necrotic damage per 50 gp of the cost of the component (minimum 1d10). This damage can’t be reduced in any way. If this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, the spell fails but the spell slot is not expended.

Also at 2nd level, you learn how to weave your life force into a spell you cast, boosting its intensity at the cost of your vitality. Whenever you roll damage for a spell you’ve cast of 1st level or higher, you can choose to take necrotic damage equal to the spell’s level to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one). This damage can’t be reduced in any way, and you must use the new rolls.

At 6th level, when a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to bind your vitality to the attacker and force them to share your pain. The attacker takes damage equal to the damage you took. This feature cannot be used against constructs or undead. You can use this feature once. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. At 14th level, you can use this feature twice between rests.

Starting at 10th level, when you damage a creature with a spell, you can choose to curse that creature for 1 minute. While cursed in this way, whenever the creature is hit by an attack, it takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. At the end of each of the creature’s turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the curse on a success. This feature cannot be used against creatures that are undead or constructs. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Upon reaching 14th level, the blood that flows through your veins is empowered with arcane vigor that mends wounds and helps preserve your life. Whenever a spell or magical effect causes you to regain hit points, you regain an additional number of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. In addition, while you are concentrating on a spell, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

Where the Alchemist brings life, the Bombardier brings ruin. Bombardiers are masters of volatile reagents, crafting incendiary flasks, caustic vials, and toxic brews designed to engulf their foes in lingering devastation. On the battlefield, they are walking arsenals, hurling explosive concoctions that set the world ablaze. Features: 3rd Level - Tool Proficiency 3rd Level - Bombardier Spells 3rd Level - Experimental Bomb 5th Level - Volatile Savant 9th Level - Corrosive Concoctions 9th Level - Rapid Alchemy 15th Level - Master of Ruin

When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with alchemist’s supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with another type of artisan’s tools of your choice.

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Bombardier Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you and don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare. Artificer Level | Spells 3rd | grease, inflict wounds 5th | web, Melf's acid arrow 9th | gaseous form, stinking cloud 13th | greater invisibility, vitriolic sphere 17th | wall of force, immolation

Starting at 3rd level, whenever you finish a long rest, you can magically produce an experimental bomb in an empty flask or vial you touch. Roll on the Experimental Bomb table to determine its effect, which is triggered when you throw it. As an action, you or another creature can throw the bomb up to 30 feet, where it shatters and releases its effect. A creature in the bomb’s area must make a saving throw against your artificer spell save DC to avoid or reduce its effects. You can create additional experimental bombs by expending a spell slot of 1st level or higher for each one. When you do so, you use your action to create the bomb and roll for its effect on the Experimental Bomb table. Creating a bomb requires alchemist’s supplies on your person, and any bomb you create with this feature lasts until it is thrown or until the end of your next long rest.

Corrosive Acid. Deals 2d6 acid damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, the acid clings to creatures, dealing 1d6 acid damage at the start of each of their turns until a creature uses its action to scrape or wash it off. Incendiary Fire. Deals 2d6 fire damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, creatures are set ablaze, taking 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns until they or an ally uses an action to douse the flames. Toxic Gas. Creates a 10-foot radius cloud of poisonous gas that lasts for 1 minute. (Con save or be poisoned until the start of your next turn; repeat the save at the end of each turn). A creature must make the save whenever it enters the gas or starts its turn in the gas. Cryo Flask. Deals 2d6 cold damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, a creature is hindered by ice formations for 1 minute, or until it or another creature within reach uses an action to break the ice. Shrapnel Bomb. Deals 2d6 piercing damage in a 10-foot radius (Dex save for half). On a failed save, the creature takes 1d6 slashing damage the first time on each turn it moves 1 foot or more without teleporting. An affected creature or ally can use its action to remove the shrapnel. Sonic Blast. Deals 2d8 thunder damage in a 10-foot radius (Str save for half). Creatures that fail the save are pushed 10 feet from the center of the blast and are deafened until the start of your next turn. Scaling: The initial and persistent damage increase at higher levels: 6th level: +1d6 (or +1d4/+1d8 for relevant bombs) 11th level: +2d6 16th level: +3d6

At 5th level, you have mastered the art of combining spellwork and alchemical destruction into seamless attacks. Whenever you cast an artificer spell or cantrip on your turn, you can throw one of your Experimental Bombs as a bonus action. You can treat any alchemical item (such as alchemist’s fire, acid vial, or an experimental bomb) as a simple ranged weapon with a range of 30/90 feet, using your Dexterity or Strength modifier for attack rolls. Damage dealt by the throw is 1d4 slashing damage plus your Dexterity or Strength modifier, in addition to the damage or effect normally dealt by the item.

At 9th level, your concoctions weaken enemy defenses and allow you to control the battlefield: Creatures that fail their saving throw against one of your bombs have disadvantage on saving throws against the next alchemical effect you deal to them (from your bombs or alchemical items such as acid vial or alchemist’s fire) before the end of your next turn.
Also at 9th level, you are able to craft bombs with remarkable speed: You can use a bonus action instead of an action to craft your Experimental Bombs.

At 15th level, your expertise in destruction allows you to maximize the potency of your creations and have better control over what you use: You gain resistance to fire, and acid damage. When a creature takes persistent damage from one of your Experimental Bombs (acid or fire) or an alchemical item (alchemist’s fire, acid vial), you can use your reaction to make the creature take maximum damage instead of rolling. You can use this ability a number of times equal to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). All expended uses are restored when you finish a long rest.
Artistry Channeler

The Channel of Artistry represents channelers who want to master controlling the flow of their arcane energy, manipulating their power with finesse and elegance. They weave through combat like dancers and cast spells with the delicacy of an accomplished maestro. Features 1st Level - Armaments of Artistry 1st Level - Elemental Savant 6th Level - Weaving Strike 11th Level - Beautiful Virtuosity 11th Level - Harmonized Strikes 17th Level - Culmination of Artistry
When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in shortswords, scimitars, and whips. You also gain proficiency in one type of artisan’s tools of your choice.

Your use and control of elemental energy is beautiful to many, and distracting to your opponents. Starting at 1st level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you have resistance to the first attack they make against you until the beginning of your next turn. Additionally, you may imbue two weapons instead of one. The imbued damage types must be the same for both weapons.

At 6th level, you can sculpt your elemental energy with your weapon, enhancing both your own movements and your energy’s potency. When you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement, the next attack roll you make during this turn has advantage, and your movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks until the beginning of your next turn.

At 11th level, the beauty of your movement and the flow of your energy is entrancing and inspiring to allies. When you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement, you may choose a creature within 30 feet that can see you. That creature may add your Elemental Imbuement die to the next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check they make until the beginning of your next turn.

At 11th level, if you hit with a weapon attack from your attack action and hit with a spell attack roll made with your Overchanneled Imbuement in one turn, you may take a second bonus action that turn.

At 17th level, you’ve perfected your casting as a form of art. You may use your Flash Charge feature an unlimited amount of times per day. When you hit with an attack, you may use your Flash Charge feature as a reaction. When you do, the attack deals additional damage equal to two rolls of your new Elemental Imbuement die.
Features: 1st Level - Armaments of Containment 6th Level - Brawl Binding 11th Level - Elemental Fortitude 11th Level - Extra Attack 17th Level - Culmination of Containment

When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in improvised weapons. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor. Elemental Core You learn to confine your arcane energy within your body, empowering your unarmed attacks. You may choose to Imbue your body with elemental energy as opposed to a weapon. While imbued, you gain the following benefits: Your unarmed strikes use your Elemental Imbuement dice for its damage type. When you attack with an unarmed strike, you may use your Intelligence modifier, rather than your strength modifier, for attack and damage rolls. You gain resistance to the damage type you chose for your Imbuement You can use your body as a focus for your Channeler spells

Beginning at 6th level, when you use the attack action to grapple a creature, the target takes damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die if the grapple succeeds. Whenever you take the attack action against the creature on subsequent turns, if you are still grappling the creature, you may choose to deal this damage again. Additionally, if you succeed on grappling a creature, you can use your Overchanneled Imbuement as a bonus action. Creatures you grapple have disadvantage on saving throws against spells you cast.

At 11th level, your contained energy provides a defensive ward that sits just under your skin, protecting you from harm. When you are subjected to an effect that has you roll a saving throw to take half damage, if the damage type is acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

Beginning at 17th level, your arcane energy binds perfectly to your flesh. You gain the following benefits while Imbued: You gain immunity to the damage type you chose for your Imbuement Your walking speed increases by 20 feet You no longer need to hit with an Imbued weapon attack to cast Channeler spells as a bonus action. When you cast a Channeler spell, add your Intelligence modifier to your unarmed strike damage and any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution checks you make until the end of your next turn.
Devastation Channeler

The Channel of Devastation represents channelers who prefer focusing their energy in short, powerful bursts, often leading to disastrous results. Those who choose this channel work tirelessly to keep their energy concealed and suppressed, until they can let it all out in a violent burst. Features 1st Level - Armaments of Devastation 1st level - Accelerant 6th Level - Devastating Presence 11th Level - Devastating Strikes 11th Level - Extra Attack 17th Level - Culmination of Devastation
When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in glaives, greataxes, greatswords, halberds, and pikes. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor and shields.

At 1st level, you’ve learned how to create an accelerant with your devastating energy, overcharging your attacks. When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can force the target to roll a strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the target is knocked prone and suffers an additional effect depending on your imbuement. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier. When you take a short or long rest, you regain all expended uses. Accelerant Effect​ Damage Type Effect Acid The target’s AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn. Fire The target takes additional fire damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die. Cold The target’s speed is reduced by half of their maximum until the end of your next turn. Lightning You may force one other creature of your choice within 10 feet of the target to take lightning damage equal to two rolls of your Elemental Imbuement die. Thunder The target is pushed back 15 feet.

At 6th level, your mere presence is recognized as a threat, inciting opponents to focus their aggression on you. Each creature of your choice that starts its turn within 30 feet of you and can see you must roll a Wisdom saving throw against to your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature has disadvantage on attacks that don’t target you until the end of that creature’s turn. If a creature succeeds on this saving throw, they are immune to this effect for the next 24 hours.

Starting at 11th level, whenever you deal damage with your Elemental Imbuement or a channeler spell that shares a damage type with your chosen Elemental Imbuement, you ignore resistance to that damage type, and you may treat immunity to that damage type as resistance.
Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

At 17th level, you’ve wrought elemental devastation everywhere you’d gone, and have found the perfect way to channel it. When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can reroll that attack against any number of other targets within 30ft, hitting each target simultaneously. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.
Madness Channeler

The channel of Madness represents a rare and often fanatical sect of channelers that believe in submitting control over their mind and actions to the powers within themselves, even to their own detriment Features 1st Level - Armaments of Madness 1st Level - Medium For Madness 6th Level - Braincharge 11th Level - Mental Overchannel 11th Level - Psychic Armaments 17th Level - Culmination of Madness
When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in hand crossbows, heavy crossbows, and longbows.

At 1st level, you may select two 1st level enchantment spells. You learn these spells and may cast each of them once per day without expending a spell slot. At 6th level, you may choose two 2nd level enchantment spells, two 3rd level enchantment spells at 11th level, and two 4th level enchantment spells at 17th level. Additionally, you may pick psychic damage as the damage type for your Elemental Imbuement.

At 6th level, you’re able to overload the minds of others, driving them further towards insanity. When a creature fails the first save from an enchantment spell you cast, they take extra psychic damage equal to your Elemental Imbuement die. Then, you may have one creature you can see within 30 feet of you gain advantage on the next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw they make until the beginning of your next turn.

At 11th level, when you deal psychic damage to a creature, you may choose to deal maximum psychic damage rather than rolling. If you do, the target is stunned until the beginning of your next turn. You cannot use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

At 11th level, when you imbue a weapon with psychic damage, you can change that weapon’s base damage type to psychic for as long as it’s imbued. Add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage of your weapon attacks imbued with psychic damage.

At 17th level, it’s hard to tell if you’re still sane or not; your internal energy has corroded your mind past the point of no return. You gain advantage on saving throws against enchantment spells. In addition, you gain immunity to psychic damage and immunity to effects that would charm or frighten you. Once per day, when you cast an enchantment spell, if it would target only one creature and no other creatures, you can instead make it target as many creatures as you can see within 60 feet of you.

The Channel of Volatility is a controversial path to undertake, as though it is the easiest channel to ‘master’, it may prove most perilous to the channeler using it. Those who practice the channel of Volatility must exercise extreme caution, else they risk losing control of their magic to horrific consequence. Features: 1st Level - Armaments of Volatility 1st Level - Volatile Charge 6th Level - Volatile Surge 11th Level - Risk and Reward 11th Level - Extra Attack 17th Level - Culmination of Volatility
When you pick this channel at 1st level, you gain proficiency in flails, mauls, and warhammers. You also gain proficiency in heavy armor and shields.

Your internal energy is difficult to predict and control, yet it assists you when you need it most. Starting at 1st level, whenever you hit with a weapon attack using your imbued weapon, note the result of the attack roll and your Imbuement die roll. Odd. If the result of the attack roll is odd, you gain temporary hit points equal to the result of your Imbuement die, which disappears whenever you take a short or long rest. Even. If the result of the attack roll is even, the attack deals extra damage equal to the result of your Imbuement die.

The unpredictable effects of your magic have branched into even more peculiar effects. Starting at 6th level, when you cast a channeler spell, roll your Elemental Imbuement die and note the result. Consult the Volatile Surge table for additional effects. Surge Effect​ Result Effect 1 You take damage equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die. 2 You add another roll of your Elemental Imbuement die to the spell’s damage. 3 Your AC increases by 1 until the start of your next turn. 4 You gain advantage on your next attack roll until the end of your next turn. 5 You gain additional temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Elemental Imbuement die. 6 You can make an additional weapon attack as part of the same bonus action. 7 You gain resistance to the next attack that hits you until the start of your next turn. 8 Reroll on this table twice, and the effects of both rolls occur. If you roll the same effect twice, the effect only applies once.
At 11th level; your frequent interactions with fickle energies have allowed you to lean further into their volatility. You learn one additional Ante option, and gain an additional Ante charge.
Beginning at 11th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the attack action on your turn.

At 17th level, your destructive magic is longing for escape from your mortal shell. Once per day, when you’re reduced to zero hit points, you may choose to release all of your internal energy in one burst.
