Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must roll a dexterity saving throw equal to your spell save DC. On a failed save, a target takes 15d10 damage and is stunned until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and isn’t stunned. The damage type is the same as your elemental Imbuement. In either case, the explosion kills you immediately, disintegrating all non-magical gear and equipment you’re carrying and wearing.

In the domain of chaos, where whims rule and order trembles, the chosen clerics of the Chaos Domain walk a path paved with unpredictability and capriciousness. Whether by the whispered machinations of trickster deities or the primal forces of wild gods, these clerics wield the very essence of chaos itself. Features: 1st Level - Chaos Domain Spells 1st Level - Chaos Bonus Proficiencies 2nd Level - Channel Divinity: Chaos Warp 6th Level - Twisted Fate 8th Level - Divine Strike: Chaos Domain 17th Level - Empowered Warp

You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Chaos Domain Spells table. See the Divine Domain class feature for how domain spells work. Cleric Level Spells 1st Chaos Bolt, Dissonant Whispers 3rd Mirror Image, Enlarge/Reduce 5th Haste, Slow 7th Confusion, Polymorph 9th Dominate Person, Modify Memory
When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons.

Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to warp probability around you, causing unpredictable effects. As an action, you present your holy symbol and a number of creatures equal to your wisdom modifier you can see within 30 feet of you. Those creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your cleric spell save DC or be affected by one of the following effects rolled randomly for each target: 1d4 Effect 1 The target takes 2d10 psychic damage. 2 The target is blinded until the end of its next turn. 3 The target is charmed by you until the end of its next turn. 4 The target is frightened until the end of its next turn.

At 6th level, your connection to the chaos that drives your every action allows you to twist the threads of fate in the world around you. As a reaction when a creature within 30 feet of you excluding yourself fails a saving throw, or check or misses an attack roll, the triggering creature must reroll the d20 and use the higher roll. You can then choose a different creature you can see within 30 feet range. The chosen creature has disadvantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes within 1 minute. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Wisdom Modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

At 17th level, when you use your Chaos Warp, rather than rolling 1d4, roll 2d4. Each target that fails the save is affected by both effects you rolled. If both d4s land on the same number, the target makes the saving throw with disadvantage and the effect is enhanced as follows: d4 Effect 1 The target takes 4d10 psychic damage and can't use reactions until the end of its next turn 2 The Target is blinded and subtracts 1d6 from any attack roll or saving throw it makes until the end of its next turn. 3 The target is under the effects of the confusion spell until the end of its next turn. 4 The target is under the effects of the slow spell until the end of its next turn.

Druids of the Circle of Beauty vow to protect all that brings beauty in nature. From the patterns of symmetry designed to attract mates, to visual marks designed to confuse camouflage observers, these are all sights that should be admired and emulated. They marvel at how nature seamlessly blends together both form and function in a way man-made objects never could. Features: 2nd Level - Circle Spells 2nd Level - Natural Form 6th Level - Blessing of Symmetry 10th Level - Beautiful Plummage 14th Level - Radiant Appearance

Your eye for all things visually harmonious grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Beauty Spells table. Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you. Druid Level Spell 2nd disguise self, feather fall 3rd healing spirit, lesser restoration 5th daylight, hypnotic pattern 7th charm monster, compulsion 9th creation, dawn

As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Wild Shape feature to draw upon nature's splendour, rather than assuming a Beast form. While in your natural form and wearing no armour, your Armour Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit. The form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), if you die, or you use this feature again. Whenever you assume your natural form, choose the manner of natural appearance your body transforms into; your choice gives you certain benefits while in the form. Attractive. When you enter this form, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns while in this form, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you until the start of your next turn. The target automatically succeeds on its saving throw if it can't see you. It stops being charmed by you if it is attacked or damaged, or if another creature shakes it awake as a bonus action. Camouflage. You can take the Hide action as a bonus action. You can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, and other natural phenomena. Verdant. When you enter this form, and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns, you can choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you (including yourself). That creature gains your Wisdom modifier temporary hit points, which lasts until the start of your next turn.

6th-level Circle of Beauty feature You strive to emulate the symmetry that occurs in the natural world. When you or a willing creature you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell with a casting time of 1 action and which deals damage to at least one target, the caster can forgo rolling damage dice and take the average damage. If the spell has an ongoing effect that can deal damage after it is cast, this feature only applies to the initial instance of damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

The transformation into your natural form is now even more stunning. Your forms gain extra benefits as detailed below: Attractive. When you charm a creature, you can command it as part of the same bonus action to use its reaction to move up to its speed and make one weapon attack against a target you can see. After the creature completes this command, it is no longer charmed by you. Camouflage. When you use the Hide action and are also obscured by natural foliage or phenomena, you become invisible until you move away from the natural foliage, or until you make an attack or cast a spell. Verdant. The you roll is now a when you give temporary hit points. While a creature has these temporary hit points, it has a bonus to AC and advantage on Constitution saving throws. Moreover, at the start of each of your turns while in your Natural Form, you can change the appearance of your form. If you do, any effects from your previous form immediately end.

Your body's aesthetically pleasing patterns and colours make others hesitate to harm you. When a creature makes an attack roll against you while in your Natural Form, you can use your reaction and force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature can't attack you with an attack or harmful spell until the end of its current turn, and must choose a new target or lose the attack or spell (this doesn't protect you from area effects, such as the explosion of15 a fireball). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

5th-level abjuration. (Bard, Druid, Cleric, Paladin) Meta Casting Time: 1 action Range: Self (30 ft. sphere) Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes Description You conjure a field of magical inspiration that bolsters the resolve of your allies. Any creature you choose while they are in this field will have resistance against psychic damage and gain advantage on saving throws against the frightened and charmed conditions. If their save fails, any additional saves against the same effect succeed automatically.
Features: 2nd Level - Circle Spells Where the Wind Guides Early Bird 6th Level - Gale Force 10th Level - Jetstream 14th Level - The Sky's the Limit

Your connection to the sky allows you to learn certain spells. At 2nd level, you learn the gust cantrip, and it does not count towards the number of druid cantrips you know. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to the spells listed for that level in the Circle of the Sky Spells table. Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn’t count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn’t appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you. Druid Level Spells 3rd Air Bubble, Skywrite 5th Fly, Lightning Bolt 7th Conjure Minor Elementals, Freedom of Movement 9th Control Winds, Steel Wind Strike

Your connection to the winds allows you to reliably control vehicles and other structures that rely on them. You gain proficiency in either water or air vehicles (your choice), and while you are aboard such a vehicle, you always have optimal wind for traveling to your intended destination.
When you use your wildshape feature, the beasts you transform into can have a flying speed.

At 6th level, you gain the ability to harness windflow to greater effect. Any wind powered structure, such as a wind mill, works at twice it's normal rate while within 5 miles of you. Additionally, water or air vehicles that utilize sails move twice as fast while you are on board. Additionally, whenever you roll lightning, thunder, or bludgeoning damage from a druid spell you cast, you add your wisdom modifier to the total damage.

When you reach 10th level, you gain the ability to move with a supernatural flow. Your walking speed increases by 15 feet, as does any flying speed of creatures you transform into with your wildshape feature. Additionally, you are considered to always be under the effects of the Freedom of Movement spell.

At 14th level, your connection to the skies has given you a shared connection with all life that calls it home. When you use your wildshape feature, you can transform into any Beast, Dragon, or Monstrosity of Challenge Rating 4 or lower, so long as it has a flying speed.

Druids of the Circle of the Verdant Stalker embody the lethal stillness and precision of Chult’s jungles. They move like serpents through the undergrowth, striking with poison and vanishing into foliage. Features: 3rd Level - Circle Spells 3rd Level - Venomous Marksman 6th Level - Aspect of the Striking Viper 10th Level - Primal Toxin Mastery 14th Level - Deathbloom Aspect

Your eye for all things visually harmonious grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Beauty Spells table. Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you. Druid Level Spell 3rd Ensnaring Strike, Poison Spray 5th Plant Growth, Spike Growth 7th Grasping Vine, Stoneskin 9th Tree Stride, Cloudkill (reflavored as a deadly plant toxin cloud)

Your training centers on the precision and toxins of Chult’s hidden hunters. Blowgun Proficiency. You gain proficiency with the blowgun. You can use your Wisdom modifier instead of Dexterity for blowgun attack and damage rolls. Toxin-Enhanced Blowgun. Your blowgun darts deal greater piercing damage as you grow in mastery. Druid Level Blowgun Damage Die 3rd 1d6 10th 1d8 14th 1d10 Poisoner’s Tools. You gain proficiency with the Poisoner’s Kit. Tough to Toxin. You have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against being poisoned. Jungle Stride. You ignore nonmagical plant-based difficult terrain.

You channel primal ferocity into a deadly, focused trance. Activation. As a bonus action, expend one use of your Wild Shape to enter this Aspect for 1 minute. You can’t activate it again until you finish a short or long rest. While in this Aspect: Your blowgun attacks deal an extra 1d8 poison damage. When you take the attack action to attack with your blowgun, hit or miss, you can make another attack with the blowgun. If your first blowgun attack each turn hits, the target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC = your spell save DC) or be Poisoned until the end of its next turn. A creature that fails this saving throw also takes an additional 1d8 poison damage.
documents.s: 6th Level - Aspect of the Striking Viper

documents.t: Your venoms pierce the resilience of even the hardiest foes. Toxic Bypass. Your blowgun attacks and druid spells that deal poison damage treat immunity to poison damage as resistance instead. Debilitating Barrage. When you hit a creature that is Poisoned, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = your spell save DC). On a failed save, it is Blinded until the end of its next turn. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Your mastery of venom and motion refines your Aspect of the Striking Viper into the Deathbloom Aspect. When you activate your Aspect of the Striking Viper, it gains the following additional benefits: Deadly Venoms. Your extra poison damage increases to 1d10, and creatures make their Constitution saving throws against your poison with disadvantage. Viper’s Retreat. Immediately after you hit a creature with a blowgun attack, you can move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks from that creature. Predator’s Cunning. While the Aspect is active, you can take the Hide or Disengage action as a bonus action. You can also attempt to Hide even when you are only partially obscured by natural terrain, foliage, or dim light. Toxic Perfection. You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

There are many things that need to be protected, some worth protecting with your life. Druids of this circle protect the natural order of the wilderness with their lives, often picking a place and staking their claim there for a large portion of their lives. Though they protect the land, the spirits of nature see fit to protect them in turn, the mark of a true Warden. Features: 2nd Level - Improved Shillelagh 2nd Level - Warden Form 6th Level - Forestwalker 6th Level - Extra Attack 10th Level - Arboreal Fortitude 14th Level - Protector’s Resolve

At 2nd level, you unlock the versatile potential within the Shillelagh cantrip. You learn the shillelagh cantrip. If you already know this cantrip, you may learn a different cantrip of your choice from the druid spell list. Whenever you roll initiative and are not surprised, you can choose to immediately cast shillelagh as a reaction. Additionally, when you cast shillelagh, you can choose to change the damage type of the weapon to bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage for the duration of the spell. The form of the weapon changes to suit the damage type chosen.

At 2nd level, you can allow the spirits of nature to wreath your form in protective foliage to enhance your endurance and martial capability. As a bonus action, you can expend a use of Wild Shape to take on your warden form. Warden form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you are incapacitated or until you dismiss it (as a free action). While in warden form, you gain the following benefits: When you enter warden form, you gain temporary hit points equal to your wisdom modifier + double your druid level Your AC is equal to 13 + your constitution modifier. You are immune to all plant-based difficult terrain, as well as all difficult terrain created by Druid spells you cast.

At 6th level, you become a natural at navigating the rugged and tough terrain of forests. You gain the following benefits while in warden form: You are resistant to damage from Druid spells you cast. You gain a bonus to all strength checks and saves equal to your wisdom modifier while in warden form. Additionally, you are now unaffected by plant-based difficult terrain when not in warden form.
At 6th level, when you take the attack action, you can make an additional weapon attack as part of the same action. You can replace up to one of these attacks with one of your druid cantrips.

At 10th level, the fortitude of your warden form grows to reflect a growth in your resolve. While in warden form, you gain a bonus to any constitution saving throw you make to maintain concentration on a spell. This bonus is equal to your wisdom modifier. If you begin your turn in warden form and do not have any temporary hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your wisdom modifier. Additionally, you have adapted your warden form to be fluid and fierce. You gain the following additional benefits while in warden form: Your walking speed increased by 10 feet. Your melee weapon attacks deal an extra 1d8 force damage on a hit.

At 14th level, your will is inseparable from that of the forest, and you learn to command nature as your blade. You always have the wrath of nature spell prepared, and it doesn't count against the total number of druid spells you have prepared. Additionally, as part of the same bonus action that you take to activate your warden form, you may cast this spell. If you cast wrath of nature in this way, it will not require concentration, and the area of effect remains centered on and moves with you throughout the duration of the spell. You may only cast this spell in this way once per long rest.
Now THIS is some real fuckin’ divinity Prerequisites: Cleric 20
When you take this prestige class, choose two more skills from the Cleric skill proficiencies. You are proficient in both of those skills.

Additionally when you take this prestige class, you gain a new set of spell slots to fuel your spells. You gain spell slots as per the Cleric table based on your prestige level minus 20. When you prepare spells for the day, you may now prepare a number of spells equal to your prestige level + your wisdom modifier. You learn one cleric cantrip of your choice, and one additional cleric cantrip at 24th and 30th level.

When you select this prestige class, choose one domain related to your deity. You may choose the same divine domain, or you may choose a new one to reflect the different aspects of your deity. Your choice grants you domain spells and other features when you choose it at 21st level. It also grants you additional ways to use Channel Divinity at 22nd level, and additional benefits at 6th, 8th, and 17th levels.

Connection to your deity has reached new heights at 22nd level. You gain one extra use of your channel divinity, and regain all expended uses of your channel divinity after you complete a short rest. You gain an additional use of your channel divinity at 33rd level.

When you reach 24th level, and again at 28th, 32nd, 36th, and 39th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

When you reach 25th level, your deity supplies you with overflowing power, ensuring you are always able to carry out your duties. Whenever you roll initiative and have no uses of your channel divinity, you regain one use.

At 29th level your divine might is bolstered. If you have the Divine Strike feature, the extra damage increases by an amount equal to your wisdom modifier. If you have the Potent Spellcasting feature, the extra damage increases by 2d8.

When you reach 30th level, your deity is more swayed to intervene in more personal matters. When you use Divine Intervention for the purposes of replicating a spell, you only need to complete one long rest before you can use the feature again. 2024 Clerics are no longer limited to spells of 5th level or lower, but are still limited to spells on the cleric spell list or their domain spells.

At 34th level, nearly all of your divine abilities carry with them the ability to deter the undead. When you cast a cleric spell of 1st level or higher, or use any channel divinity option, you may choose to activate your turn undead feature without expending a use of your channel divinity.

When you reach 38th level, you always have the demiplane and word of recall spells prepared. Both of these count as cleric spells for you and do not count towards your number of spells prepared. When you cast Word of Recall, you can designate warp to one of any number of previously designated locations, though they must still meet the spell’s requirements.

At 40th level, your deity will never leave you in your times of need. You will always regain your use of divine intervention when you finish a long rest, regardless of what you use it for. 2024 Clerics will no longer be stricken with the sickness from the wish spell if they use it to do anything other than replicating spells of 8th level or lower.

In the domain of chaos, where whims rule and order trembles, the chosen clerics of the Chaos Domain walk a path paved with unpredictability and capriciousness. Whether by the whispered machinations of trickster deities or the primal forces of wild gods, these clerics wield the very essence of chaos itself.

You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Chaos Domain Spells table. See the Divine Domain class feature for how domain spells work. Cleric Level Spells 1st Chaos Bolt, Dissonant Whispers 3rd Mirror Image, Enlarge/Reduce 5th Haste, Slow 7th Confusion, Polymorph 9th Dominate Person, Modify Memory
When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons.

Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to warp probability around you, causing unpredictable effects. As an action, you present your holy symbol and a number of creatures equal to your wisdom modifier you can see within 30 feet of you. Those creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your cleric spell save DC or be affected by one of the following effects rolled randomly for each target: 1d4 Effect 1 The target takes 2d10 psychic damage. 2 The target is blinded until the end of its next turn. 3 The target is charmed by you until the end of its next turn. 4 The target is frightened until the end of its next turn.

At 6th level, your connection to the chaos that drives your every action allows you to twist the threads of fate in the world around you. As a reaction when a creature within 30 feet of you excluding yourself fails a saving throw, or check or misses an attack roll, the triggering creature must reroll the d20 and use the higher roll. You can then choose a different creature you can see within 30 feet range. The chosen creature has disadvantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes within 1 minute. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Wisdom Modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

At 17th level, when you use your Chaos Warp, rather than rolling 1d4, roll 2d4. Each target that fails the save is affected by both effects you rolled. If both d4s land on the same number, the target makes the saving throw with disadvantage and the effect is enhanced as follows: d4 Effect 1 The target takes 4d10 psychic damage and can't use reactions until the end of its next turn 2 The Target is blinded and subtracts 1d6 from any attack roll or saving throw it makes until the end of its next turn. 3 The target is under the effects of the confusion spell until the end of its next turn. 4 The target is under the effects of the slow spell until the end of its next turn.

Any bard can write a story or compose an epic, yet none with as much flair and verbal panache as one who studies under the college of fables. Such bards are masters at crafting narratives, telling tales, and captivating readers far and wide. They tell stories of that which was, that which is, and with enough creative magic, that which will be. Features: 3rd Level - Natural Writer 3rd Level - Wordcraft 6th Level - Life Imitates Art 14th Level - Art Imitates Life

Beginning at 3rd level, you can spend at least one workweek of downtime (max. 5) and 10 gp of materials per week to write a story. When the story is complete, roll a d20 and add your charisma modifier, as well as a number of dice equal to the amount of workweeks you spent on the story to the roll. The value of the dice is the same as your bardic inspiration dice. The quality of the story you create depends on the result of the roll as shown below. Story Quality: Check Totals > Quality 1-10 > Poor 11-20 > Good 21-30 > Great 31-40 > Sensational 41+ > Genre-Definining Depending on the quality of the book, your reputation as a writer may broaden. Your skills might be recognized by nobles and peasants alike, and you may receive invitations to events that are difficult to enter, and might be able to curry favors with your fame.

At 3rd level, when you cast a spell with only verbal components and no somatic or material components, you can expend one use of your bardic inspiration die to cast the spell as a story. When you do so, you may add your bardic inspiration die to one of the spell’s attack rolls, or subtract your bardic inspiration die from the saving throw of one creature affected by the spell. Alternatively, you can have a creature within 60 feet of you that can hear you gain temporary hit points equal to one roll of your bardic inspiration die.

At 6th level, you can spin together tales that can bend reality around them to an extent. As a reaction to when a creature fails an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw within 60 feet of you, you can describe that course of action succeeding. That creature can then reroll the d20 and use the new roll, potentially allowing it to succeed. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your charisma modifier. You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

At 14th level, some of your tales are powerful enough to gain corporeal form. As an action, you can create a living story, the manifestation of your wordcraft, in an unoccupied space you can see within range. If you already have a living story, it disappears when the new one is created The creature is an ally to you and your companions. In combat, the creature shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don’t issue any, it takes the Dodge action and uses its move to avoid danger. You can only use this feature once per long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 5th level or higher to use it again.

The College of Poetry celebrates the beauty of concise expression, weaving magic through the ancient art of word play. Bards who follow this path find inspiration in nature, emotions, and fleeting moments. Their words resonate with power, evoking both sorrow and hope. Features: 3rd Level - A Poet's tools 3rd Level - Whispered Verses 6th Level - Serene Resonance 14th Level - Tranquil Ode

At level 3 the stillness required to master poetry has given you an above natural insight into the world and the people around you. You gain proficiency in Calligraphy Supplies and can use it as your spellcasting focus. You also have extraordinary insight which allows you to use your charisma instead of wisdom when making an insight skill check.

At 3rd Level you gain the ability to infuse your spells with the essence of poems. Whenever you cast a spell that requires a spell slot and has a verbal component, you can choose to infuse one of the following poems into your spell before casting the spell Poem of Lamentation: When you cast a spell that deals damage you can infuse it with the Poem of Lamentation to deal extra damage of the spells damage type equal to two rolls of your bardic inspiration die. Poem of Dissociation: When you cast a spell that forces a saving throw from a single target you can infuse it with the Poem of Dissociation to Increase the saving throw DC of the Spell by 2 Poem of a Soothing Breeze: When you cast a spell that targets a single ally you can Infuse it with the Poem of a Soothing Breeze to grant the ally temporary hit points equal to your Bard Level. You can use each Haiku once per short rest and can only one Haiku per spell, when you reach certain levels you gain an extra use per Haiku. 2 uses at level 6, 3 uses at level 14.

At 6th Level your poems resonate with the natural world, granting you deeper insight. When you use your Bardic Inspiration die to inspire an ally, they gain the following benefits: Resistance: The inspired creature gains resistance to a damage type of your choice until the start of your next turn. Guidance: The inspired creature has advantage on the next saving throw they make while they are inspired.

At level 14 Your mastery of poems reaches its zenith. As an action, you can recite a Tranquil Ode—a profound Poem that resonates with the cosmos. Choose one of the following effects: Harmony's Blessing: All allies within 30 feet regain hit points equal to your Bardic Inspiration die roll + your Charisma modifier. Elegy of Stillness: All enemies within 30 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, they are stunned until the end of their next turn. You can use each Tranquil Ode only once per long rest.

Clerics of the Commerce Domain are devoted to the principles of trade, wealth, and prosperity. They believe that economic strength and fair exchange can bring about harmony and stability in the world. Gods of commerce, such as Abadar or Waukeen, often bless their followers with the ability to navigate markets, negotiate deals, and protect their wealth. Features: 1st Level - Commerce Domain Spells 1st Level - Sales Strategy 1st Level - Divine Bargain 2nd Level - Merchant’s Blessing 6th Level - Spiritual Investments 8th Level - Potent Spellcasting 17th Level - Treasury of the Divine

1st Cleric Level: Distort Value, Identify 3rd Cleric Level: Arcane Lock, Zone of Truth 5th Cleric Level: Incite Greed, Tongues 7th Cleric Level: Faithful Hound, Secret Chest 9th Cleric Level: Animate Objects, Scrying
At 1st level, you gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice, as well as proficiency in the Persuasion or Deception skills.

Also at 1st level, your spiritual savvy manifests itself as material wealth. You gain a number of divine coins up to a maximum equal to your wisdom modifier, and you regain any spent coins during a long rest. As a Bonus Action on your turn, you can magically conduct a spiritual trade with one conscious creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. Choose either Buy or Sell: Buy. Give one of your divine coins to the target. It can spend the divine coin as if it had your Divine Bargain feature. The target takes 1d8 Necrotic damage, and you regain Hit Points equal to the damage taken. Sell. Gain a divine coin. You take 1d8 Necrotic damage, lose maximum hit points equal to the damage taken, and the target regains Hit Points equal to the damage taken. The damage cannot be reduced by any means.

You can use your Channel Divinity as an action to enhance your dealings. For the next hour: Whenever you make a Charisma ability check, you may substitute your Wisdom modifier for your Charisma modifier. If the check uses the skill you gained from Sales Strategy, you may add your proficiency bonus twice instead of once.

You can spend divine coins to empower your miracles. When you cast a spell or use a feature, you may spend coins for one of the following effects: Extend Contract. As a bonus action when you are currently concentrating on a spell, you can spend 1 coin to extend its duration by a round. Sweeten the Deal. As a reaction when you roll damage or healing for a spell you can spend 1 coin to reroll any number of dice for the spell’s healing or damage, taking the new results. Collateral Loan. As a bonus action, you can spend 1 coin to grant temporary hit points equal to 2d8 + your Wisdom modifier to a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. You may only use one of these benefits per turn.
You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

You gain an incorruptible storehouse of divine wealth. At the start of each of your turns, you automatically gain 1 divine coin. In addition, the maximum amount of divine coins you can hold increases up to 2 times your wisdom modifier.

Prerequisite: Defensive Duelist, 12th level+ You turn a parry into the opening for a deadly counter. Counterstance. While you benefit from the AC bonus of your Defensive Duelist Parry, you gain the following special reaction: Counterattack. When a creature misses you with a melee attack, due to the AC Bonus from the Defensive Duelist feat, you can make one melee weapon attack against it. You can use this reaction once on each creature’s turn, except your own. You can only use this counterattack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest* Ranged Parry. When you aren’t wielding a shield, you can also use your Defensive Duelist Parry against a ranged weapon attack that targets only you.

Specializing on ice magic, wizards that have learned from the Cryomancy arcane tradition manipulate the crystalline structure of ice and bend it to their will. Many foolishly only see this magic as beautiful, and it is, but within the beauty of all that shimmering ice, is a slow and shivering death.

Your manipulation of ice allow you to acclimate to it and change the properties of spells. When you cast a spell that deals damage, you are able to change the damage type to cold damage unless its bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. You gain resistance to cold damage. When you reach 13th level on this class, you also gain resistance to fire damage, and at 17th level, you gain immunity to cold damage and the area 5 feet of you has the effects of extreme cold.

As an action, you can freeze a 5-foot cube of nonmagical water. The cube will remain frozen for one minute or until your concentration ends (as if you were concentrating on a spell). You can manipulate the ice as a bonus action to mold its shape to form objects or structures. The objects or structures you make have hit points equal to your wizard level. At 8th and 15th level, you freeze an area of 15-foot and 25-foot cube respectively. You can also create the ice out of moisture in the air, though the cubic footage you are able to manipulate is halved (i.e. you can produce a 7-foot cube from a 15-foot cube of air). Additionally, when you reach 15th level you can also freeze magical water, manipulate magical ice, and the cube can now be frozen for up to 1 hour.

Your body fills with ice magic and acts at times in preservation from external factors. When you become unconscious or asleep or are rendered unconscious or asleep, you are immediately encased in a layer of dense ice. This ice has hit points equal to twice your wizard level and an AC equal to your spell save DC. When the ice encases you as a result of being reduced to 0 hit points, the ice will stabilize you and freezes the area around you. All creatures within 10 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be restrained until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, they are not restrained but their speed is halved. When the restrained condition from this feature ends, the creature's speed is also halved. They can make another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of their turns. On a success, their speed returns to normal. The ice lasts for 1 minute, until it is destroyed, or when you choose to break the ice upon regaining consciousness. Once this feature is used it cannot be used again until a long rest.

Your control over ice have reached to an abnormal extreme, even by magical standards. Choose one wizard spell that deals damage in your spellbook. That spell's damage type permanently becomes cold damage when you cast it without using your Frigid Magic feature or other similar effect. You can change the spell for a different spell by spending 8 hours in study. The first time you deal damage to a creature that does not have resistance or immunity to cold damage on your turn, they take extra cold damage equal to your wizard level.

After extensive use of bending ice to your every whim, you understand all of its inner workings. You're able to apply this knowledge by performing grand feats on a monumental scale. As an action, you are able to freeze everything within a 60 foot radius sphere centered around you. This creates sleets of ice and snow on the ground and super chilling the air, rendering the area as difficult terrain. All creatures of your choice takes 3d6 cold damage upon activation and must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be frozen. While frozen, a creature is considered incapacitated and their speed is reduced to 0 until the end of their next turn. Furthermore, you create a 30 foot radius sphere of a perpetual blizzard that is centered around and moves with you. When a creature of your choice enters the area for the first time or starts their turn in it, the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take cold damage equal to half your wizard level and have its speed halved until the start of its next turn. The area inside the blizzard acts as a heavily obscured area for all creatures except you. Both the difficult terrain and blizzard lasts for 1 minute or when you end both effects using an action, afterwards you no longer gain the effects of the Frigid Magic feature until you take a short rest. Once this feature is used it cannot be used again until a long rest.

The Daredevil fighter thrives on style, versatility and unpredictably. Their use of different weapon types makes them dangerous to any foe and they gain more confidence the more stylish their fighting is. Features: 3rd Level - Daredevil Impulse 3rd Level - Hotswap 7th Level - Fight or Flight Double Trouble 15th Level - Wild Rush 18th Level - Inferno Trigger

Starting at 3rd level, every time you make an attack of a type different from the previous attack in the current combat, you gain one Style point. You have a maximum amount of style points equal to your proficiency bonus. When you roll Initiative your Style points reset to 0. Attack types are classified as: Melee weapon attack, Ranged weapon attack and thrown attacks. Style Points can be used to power your Flairs.

Wide attack: If you hit with a melee attack, you may spend 2 Style points to deal melee damage equal to half your Fighter level to all foes within 5 feet of your target. Laser Focus: Spend 2 Style Points to gain advantage on your next attack roll. Range Extender: You can add 10 feet to any ranged or thrown weapon's normal range for every point spent Rush: Gain 10 feet of movement speed for each Style Point spent until the end of your turn. Burst (4th level and up): As a bonus action, Spend 3 Style points to make a weapon attack.
At 3rd level, whenever you make an attack roll with a weapon, you can sheathe it and draw another in the same action. You can only do this once per action.

From 7th level you have a choice between staying in action and fighting defensively or moving around or to continue as is. As a bonus action you can choose to either fight or flee from combat. Fight: As a Bonus action you can give yourself a Bonus to your AC equal to the amount of Style Points you spend. This bonus lasts until the end of your next turn or until you are incapacitated. While Fight is active you cannot gain more Style points. Flight: You can spend 2 Style points to disengage, you can't be targeted by opportunity attacks. You gain an additional 10 feet of movement until the end of your turn for every additional Style Point spent.

You can choose an additional Fighting Style. Additionally, using the Disengage, Dodge or Dash actions also builds your Style chain. For example: If you use a dodge action and make an attack on your next turn or vice versa you also gain a Style Point

Starting at 15th level, when an enemy within 30 feet of you gets incapacitated or restrained you can use 2 Style Points as an reaction to dash straight toward the enemy. You move 10 feet for every point spent (minimum 2 points) and can spend additional Style for added Rush movement. You can sheath your current weapon and draw another as part of the dash and make a single attack against that target.

From 18th level, once per short rest you can expend 6 Style points as an action to trigger your Inferno action. Inferno action: Can attack 6 times, ignore the loading and ammunition properties if the weapon has it. Any Critical hit deals an additional 10 damage of the weapons damage type. These attacks don't provide any Style points

The embodiment of grit, luck, and a well-placed shot, fighters who choose this martial archetype strive to emulate paradigms of accuracy. Deadeyes generally prefer fighting from comfortable ranges, employing the use of crossbows, firearms, and even throwing knives if a situation calls for them. 3rd Level - Perfect Sixth 7th Level - Line ‘em Up 10th Level - Gambit 15th Level - Duelist’s Aim 18th Level - High Noon

Once per attack action beginning at 3rd level, when you make a ranged weapon attack roll against a creature, you can add a d6 to the result. You can add the d6 before or after seeing the results of the attack roll, but before the effects are applied. If the result of the d6 is a 6, you severely injure your target. Roll on the severe injury table to see the effect of the injury. Severe Injury Table​ 2d6 | Severe Injury 2 | Shock. The target is stunned until the end of its next turn. 3 | Fracture. The target can only take either an action, bonus action, or move on its next turn. 4 | Punctured Lung. The target gains one level of exhaustion for the next minute. 5 | Crushed Throat. The target cannot speak, use verbal components, or use any features that involve its voice until the end of its next turn. 6 | Crushed Grip. The target drops anything it is currently holding, including grappled creatures. 7 | Whiplash. The attack deals one additional die of weapon damage. 8 | Broken Leg. The target’s movement speed is halved until the end of its next turn. 9 | Embedded Ammunition. Until the end of its next turn, for every 5 feet the target moves, it takes 1d6 slashing damage. 10| Tear. The target has disadvantage on melee attacks until the end of its next turn. 11| Blind. The target is blinded until the end of its next turn. 12| Dead Shot. The triggering hit becomes a critical hit. Before you make a ranged weapon attack, you can take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If you hit, you apply a severe injury immediately. You can only apply one severe injury with each attack action. A creature cannot be affected by the same severe injury more than once at a time, and a creature can expend one use of legendary resistance to ignore a severe injury’s effect.

At 7th level, you become a master at hitting successive targets. When you take the attack action on your turn, each time you target a different creature than any other you’ve targeted this turn, you gain a cumulative +1 bonus to the attack roll.

At 10th level, when you roll initiative, you can gambit a d4, d6, d8, or d10. Roll the chosen die and subtract it from your initiative. Until the end of your next turn, every creature below you in initiative takes extra damage when hit with your ranged attack rolls equal to the chosen die.
At 15th level, when you use the attack action to make a ranged weapon attack and you hit at least three consecutive attacks, your third attack inflicts a severe injury.

At 18th level, you are adept at ending multiple targets at once. As an action, choose any number of targets that you can see within a cone the size of your weapon’s short range, up to 60 feet. You may make one ranged weapon attack against each target you chose inflicting the Dead Shot severe injury with each of them. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.

The archetypal death knight focuses on honing negative energies into their attacks and integrating necromancy into their fighting style. While death knights don’t have to be tragic and dark, the energies used often corrupts the user Features: Death Tokens 3rd Level - Undead Soldier 3rd Level - Rebuke of the Damned 7th Level - Sink or Swim 10th Level - Cull the Horde 15th Level - Black Speech 18th Level - Grave Warden

During combat, when you kill a hostile creature, you gain a number of death tokens equal to half the creature's proficiency bonus (rounded down), which can be used to fuel your death knight abilities. Once a creature grants a death token, it may not do so until you finish a long rest. You may have a maximum number of death tokens equal to 1 + half your fighter level, rounded down, which last until your next long rest.

Starting at 3rd level, you learn to reanimate undead in the midst of combat. As an action, you may expend 2 death tokens to infuse negative energy into a corpse or pile of bones that you can see to turn it into an undead soldier. The corpse becomes a zombie or skeleton which lasts until your next long rest, where it then turns into dust. Undead soldiers share initiative with each other, but roll initiative on their own. As a bonus action, you may give them commands. If no commands are given, they do their best to defend themselves and you. Your undead soldiers additionally count as you for the purpose of gaining death tokens. You may have a total number of undead soldiers equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down).

Starting at 3rd level, you can expend one death token as a reaction when you or an undead soldier within 30ft of you is hit by an attack. Roll a number of d4 dice equal to your proficiency bonus, and reduce the damage taken by the total rolled, dealing the total back to the attacker as necrotic damage.

Starting at 7th level, you learn various uses for your death tokens. As a bonus action, you can use a death token and select an undead soldier within 30 feet of you. Then, spend and roll up to a number of hit dice equal to your proficiency bonus. The undead soldier regains hit points equal to the total of the dice rolled. As an action, you can spend a number of death tokens and target a undead soldier or corpse within 30 feet of you. Every creature within 10 feet of the undead soldier or corpse must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier) or take 1d4 necrotic damage and 1d4 fire damage per death token expended. Once per turn, you may expend a death token slay an undead soldier early, instantly turning it into dust. When doing so, you may make an additional attack before the end of your next turn when you take the attack action.

Starting at 10th level, you can use death tokens to empower you and your undead. Your undead soldiers gain a bonus to attack rolls and saving throws equal to half the death tokens you currently carry, rounded down. Attacks done by your undead soldiers count as magical for the purpose of overcoming defenses. You may spend two death tokens when creating an undead soldier to grant the soldier proficiency in light, medium, and heavy armor, shields, and martial weapons.

Starting at 15th level, You learn to speak, read, and write Black Speech, which can be used to communicate with undead and can not be learned through traditional means. Most undead lack the intelligence to convey or understand sophisticated concepts, but a non-hostile undead could relay what it has seen or heard in the recent past. This ability doesn't grant you friendship with undead, though you can combine this ability with gifts to curry favor with them as you would with any nonplayer character. Additionally, having access to this speech grants you resistance to necrotic damage.

Starting at 18th levels, when using your undead soldier feature, you can expend 6 death tokens to create a sword wraith warrior instead. In addition, you can use death tokens to do the following: Armor of Bones: You may spend a death token when creating an undead to create large spikes of bones which protrude out the created undead. When a creature attacks that undead with a melee attack, they take magical piercing damage equal to your constitution modifier. Lament of the Lost: As a bonus action, you can spend a death token to reposition any of your undead soldiers within 30 feet of you. You determine the new arrangement of these soldiers, and may swap your location with one of them.

Those that follow this path believe that rather than hard training, true mastery comes with application. Like a branch drifting across a river, such practitioners make do with what’s thrown at them, adapting to the issues they are faced with and prospering in the worst of conditions.

At 2nd level, you find it easy to manipulate your techniques to fit their situations. As a bonus action, you can enter the flowing river stance for 1 minute, gaining the following benefits: If you focus a technique, you can choose whether it’s a mental or physical type for you. When you make a weapon attack with a technique, you can use your mental ability for attack and damage rolls rather than Strength or Dexterity. If a creature fails its save against your technique, you can use a reaction to regain mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up). After you use this feature, you must take a short or long rest before you can use it again. You can exit the flowing river stance as a bonus action. It ends early if you are incapacitated or if your turn ends and you haven’t used a technique since your last turn. You can enter the flowing river stance a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.

At 6th level, you improve upon your ability to adapt to change. When you enter the flowing river stance, choose a damage type aside from bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. You become resistant to that damage type until the flowing river stance ends.

At 14th level, you become adept at stringing techniques from different forms together. After spending mastery points to focus a technique while in the flowing river stance, you can use a bonus action to use another technique from a different martial form.

At 18th level, if you use three physical techniques or three mental techniques in a row, you gain a benefit: Physical. The next time a creature hits you with an attack until the end of your next turn, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against them. Mental. The next time you use a technique that forces a creature to make a save until the end of your next turn, they have disadvantage on that save.

Type: Varies Prerequisites: Novice, Drifter Make a weapon attack against a creature or object. The attack deals an amount of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus in additional psychic damage if this technique is mental or bludgeoning damage if this technique is physical. Focused (1 point, or 0 points if in flowing river stance). If the target is a creature, they must make a Constitution saving throw or have their speed halved until the end of their next turn. Your movement speed increases by the same amount until the end of your turn.

Type: Varies Prerequisites: Intermediate, Drifter, Flowing river stance If you take damage that matches the damage type you chose for your flowing river stance, you can use your reaction to become immune to that damage instead. Focused (1 point). In the same reaction, you can use another technique that includes a weapon attack.

Type: Varies Prerequisites: Advanced, Drifter The next technique you use from a different form until the end of your next turn can be focused with 1 less mastery point (min. 1) Focused (1 point). The next technique you focus does not require mastery points, and once performed, you can immediately make a weapon attack against a creature or object.

Type: Varies Prerequisites: Master, Drifter, Flowing river stance Duration: Concentration, 1 min. If you use a physical or mental technique, you gain a benefit. Physical. If you hit a creature with a weapon attack during this technique, they must succeed on a wisdom saving throw or be forced to use their action to make one melee weapon attack against you on their next turn. Mental. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack during this technique, they must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. Focused (1 point). Whenever you use a physical or mental technique, it counts as if you had used three physical or three mental techniques respectively.

Your connection to the sky allows you to learn certain spells. At 2nd level, you learn the gust cantrip, and it does not count towards the number of druid cantrips you know. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to the spells listed for that level in the Circle of the Sky Spells table. Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn’t count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn’t appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you. Druid Level Spells 3rd Air Bubble, Skywrite 5th Fly, Lightning Bolt 7th Conjure Minor Elementals, Freedom of Movement 9th Control Winds, Steel Wind Strike

Your connection to the winds allows you to reliably control vehicles and other structures that rely on them. You gain proficiency in either water or air vehicles (your choice), and while you are aboard such a vehicle, you always have optimal wind for traveling to your intended destination.
When you use your wildshape feature, the beasts you transform into can have a flying speed.

At 6th level, you gain the ability to harness windflow to greater effect. Any wind powered structure, such as a wind mill, works at twice it's normal rate while within 5 miles of you. Additionally, water or air vehicles that utilize sails move twice as fast while you are on board. Additionally, whenever you roll lightning, thunder, or bludgeoning damage from a druid spell you cast, you add your wisdom modifier to the total damage.

When you reach 10th level, you gain the ability to move with a supernatural flow. Your walking speed increases by 15 feet, as does any flying speed of creatures you transform into with your wildshape feature. Additionally, you are considered to always be under the effects of the Freedom of Movement spell.

At 14th level, your connection to the skies has given you a shared connection with all life that calls it home. When you use your wildshape feature, you can transform into any Beast, Dragon, or Monstrosity of Challenge Rating 4 or lower, so long as it has a flying speed.

There are many things that need to be protected, some worth protecting with your life. Druids of this circle protect the natural order of the wilderness with their lives, often picking a place and staking their claim there for a large portion of their lives. Though they protect the land, the spirits of nature see fit to protect them in turn, the mark of a true Warden.

At 2nd level, you unlock the versatile potential within the Shillelagh cantrip. You learn the shillelagh cantrip. If you already know this cantrip, you may learn a different cantrip of your choice from the druid spell list. Whenever you roll initiative and are not surprised, you can choose to immediately cast shillelagh as a reaction. Additionally, when you cast shillelagh, you can choose to change the damage type of the weapon to bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage for the duration of the spell. The form of the weapon changes to suit the damage type chosen.

At 2nd level, you can allow the spirits of nature to wreath your form in protective foliage to enhance your endurance and martial capability. As a bonus action, you can expend a use of Wild Shape to take on your warden form. Warden form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you are incapacitated or until you dismiss it (as a free action). While in warden form, you gain the following benefits: When you enter warden form, you gain temporary hit points equal to your wisdom modifier + double your druid level Your AC is equal to 13 + your constitution modifier. You are immune to all plant-based difficult terrain, as well as all difficult terrain created by Druid spells you cast.

At 6th level, you become a natural at navigating the rugged and tough terrain of forests. You gain the following benefits while in warden form: You are resistant to damage from Druid spells you cast. You gain a bonus to all strength checks and saves equal to your wisdom modifier while in warden form. Additionally, you are now unaffected by plant-based difficult terrain when not in warden form.
At 6th level, when you take the attack action, you can make an additional weapon attack as part of the same action. You can replace up to one of these attacks with one of your druid cantrips.

At 10th level, the fortitude of your warden form grows to reflect a growth in your resolve. While in warden form, you gain a bonus to any constitution saving throw you make to maintain concentration on a spell. This bonus is equal to your wisdom modifier. If you begin your turn in warden form and do not have any temporary hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your wisdom modifier. Additionally, you have adapted your warden form to be fluid and fierce. You gain the following additional benefits while in warden form: Your walking speed increased by 10 feet. Your melee weapon attacks deal an extra 1d8 force damage on a hit.

At 14th level, your will is inseparable from that of the forest, and you learn to command nature as your blade. You always have the wrath of nature spell prepared, and it doesn't count against the total number of druid spells you have prepared. Additionally, as part of the same bonus action that you take to activate your warden form, you may cast this spell. If you cast wrath of nature in this way, it will not require concentration, and the area of effect remains centered on and moves with you throughout the duration of the spell. You may only cast this spell in this way once per long rest.
Exorcists use their spiritual abilities to purge the lands of evil spirits and those that would do harm to society. With pure souls and unmatched bravery, they face the most vile of creation head-on.

At 3rd level, you become adept in tracking down and hunting all manners of evil. You gain proficiency in Investigation and Survival, and undead and fiends have disadvantage on saving throws against your exorcist arts. If the target of your spirit tether is a creature and is reduced to 0 hit points, you can regain a number of spirit points equal to half your spiritualist level (rounded down). If the target was an undead or a fiend, you regain additional spirit points equal to your wisdom modifier. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your power over evil forces.

If your tethered target is a creature, you can use your action to spend 1 spirit point to root your target in place. The target must make a strength saving throw or be restrained for one minute and take 2d6 radiant damage at the start of each of its turns. A target can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending this effect on a success.

You can use an action and spend 1 spirit point to lash out at your target with your righteous spirit. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the target takes 4d6 radiant damage, taking half of the damage on a success.

You can use an action and spend 1 spirit point to cover your target in radiant light. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or be covered in an aura of light that emits bright sunlight for 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet. When the target fails its saving throw against your radiant lash while this sunlight persists, you can blind them until the end of its next turn.

At 6th level, you can use an action to exorcise creatures of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. For each creature, you can spend 1 spirit point to end one effect that’s causing the creature to be charmed, frightened, or possessed.

At 13th level, you can cleanse an area and temporarily ward it from evil. As an action, you can spend 3 spirit points to create a field in a 20-foot-radius sphere at a point you can see within 120 feet of yourself. The area becomes pure, and creatures of your choice within the area cannot be frightened, charmed, or possessed, and have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws. The field lasts for one minute, whereupon its cleansing abilities fade and its effects end.
At 18th level, you master your abilities to drive evil from this world. You learn the following spirit art:

You can use 10 minutes of chanting and 20 spirit points to attempt to banish a creature from existence. At the end of the ten minutes, the target must make a Charisma saving throw or be banished. Regardless of the target’s native plane, they are banished to an empty and infinite demiplane that is accessible by nothing less than a god. It is impossible for the creature to leave the demiplane from the inside by any means. While banished, the target does not need to breathe, eat, or sleep, and it doesn’t age. Divination spells can’t locate or perceive the target. You can spend 10 minutes to bring a banished creature back from its banishment. If you’re within 30 feet of the location the target was originally banished from, you can bring them back to a point you can see within 30 feet of you.

The Fey Duelist archetype merges the cunning and agility of a rogue with the enchanting power of the Feywild. These rogues are gifted (or cursed) with the boons of Archfey patrons, weaving magic and mischief into their every movement. They are agile combatants and masters of manipulation, channeling Fey magic to outmaneuver foes, charm allies, and spread chaos on the battlefield. Whether as emissaries of a Fey court, champions of their Archfey patron, or independent agents who stumbled into the gifts of the Feywild, Fey Duelists tread a fine line between mortal pragmatism and the capricious beauty of the Fey. Their motivations are as varied as the Feywild itself, often driven by a blend of personal ambition, devotion to their patron, or a desire to unweave the chains of mundane reality and reshape the world with Fey-inspired artistry. Playstyle and Motivations​ The Fey Duelist excels in roles that combine agility, cunning, and creativity. They bring versatility to combat and social interactions, offering a mix of mobility, control, and spellcasting that allows them to adapt to nearly any situation. Players who enjoy weaving spells and martial combat together will find the Fey Duelist a rewarding choice. Motivations for a Fey Duelist might include: Devotion to an Archfey: Serving a powerful Fey entity as a trusted agent or champion, spreading their influence or carrying out their will. Personal Freedom: Using Fey gifts to escape or defy systems of control, embracing the chaotic and whimsical nature of the Feywild. Vengeance or Redemption: Seeking to right a past wrong or balance a perceived injustice using the unique powers of the Fey. Curiosity and Mischief: Exploring the boundaries of mortal and Fey realms, motivated by wonder and the joy of discovery. Who Would Thrive as a Fey Duelist?​ The Fey Duelist appeals to characters who want to: Command the Social Arena: Features like Binding Words provide robust tools for persuasion, manipulation, and intrigue. Outmaneuver and Disrupt Enemies: Abilities like Elusive Action and Distant Dodge emphasize mobility and tactical positioning. Ideal Players and Characters​ The Charismatic Manipulator: Players who enjoy talking their way out of trouble, influencing NPCs, and using charm to solve problems. The Tactical Trickster: Players who like to use cunning, positioning, and the environment to control the flow of combat. The Fey Enthusiast: Players who love the whimsical, mysterious, and chaotic themes of the Feywild and want to embody its spirit. Features 3rd Level - Spellcasting 3rd Level - Vexing 9th Level - Delicate Deception 13th Level - Binding Words 17th Level - Archfeys Guile
