In addition to their suite of cantrips, Rooks are light on their feet and know a few tricks for opening doors in utter silence.

Starting when you choose this house at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to gain advantage on the next attack roll you make on your turn. Alternatively, you can impose disadvantage on a saving throw a creature makes against a warmage spell you cast before the end of your turn. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest, or until you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with a warmage cantrip.

Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Stealth skill. Additionally, you can cast the knock spell at will without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell in this way, it has a casting time of 1 minute and its casting is completely silent.

At 7th level, you gain proficiency in the Acrobatics and Sleight of Hand skills, and you can add your Intelligence modifier to Dexterity (Stealth) checks you make. Additionally, when you fall and aren’t incapacitated, you can subtract up to 60 feet from the fall when calculating falling damage.

Beginning at 10th level, as a reaction when you take damage from a creature you can see, you raise a defensive illusion to protect yourself from further harm. The next attack roll made against you before the start of your next turn has disadvantage.
By 15th level, you are extremely difficult to pin down. Your movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks, and you can move through the space of any creature as though it were difficult terrain.

Starting at 18th level, you can cast the invisibility spell once, targeting only yourself, without expending a spell slot or spell components. While you are invisible in this way, your speed is doubled, and you can make one attack or cast one warmage cantrip without ending the spell. Once you use this feature to cast invisibility, you can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

Your soul is bound to the primal weave of the four great elements—Fire, Earth, Water, and Air. Each spell you cast leaves a lingering Strain, a trace of elemental magic you can mold into disruptive bursts or overwhelming force.

When you gain a level in this class, you can choose from this list in addition to the sorcerer list. These spells count as sorcerer spells for you and don’t count against the number of sorcerer spells you know. Sorcerer Level | Spells 3rd | Chromatic Orb, Earth Tremor, Thunderwave, Melf’s Acid Arrow 5th | Fireball, Lightning Bolt 7th | Ice Storm, Stone Shape 9th | Cone of Cold, Wall of Stone

You gain access to Strains, elemental charges tied to the four primal elements. Elements & Damage Types: Fire — Fire damage Earth — Bludgeoning or Force damage Water — Cold or Acid damage Air — Thunder or Lightning damage

Whenever you deal damage with a spell and spend a sorcery as part of the spell, you gain 1 Strain of the matching element. You can only gain 1 Strain per spell, even if it affects multiple creatures. Strains reset to 0 on a short or long rest or if you don’t use any Strains for 1 minute. Maximum Strains per Type: 3rd Level: 1 6th Level: 2 14th Level: 3 18th Level: 4

You may only expend Strains when you also spend at least 1 Sorcery Point on the spell, you use a bonus action to surge a spell. The Strain adds an extra effect to the spell: Fire: Target ignites, taking 1d6 fire damage at the start of its next turn. Earth: Target’s speed is reduced by 10 ft. until your next turn. Water: Target has disadvantage on the next Strength or Dexterity saving throw it makes before your next turn. Air: Target cannot take reactions until the start of your next turn. You can apply only one Strain Surge per spell at this level. You do not gain Strain when you Surge

You can now expend up to 2 Strains on a single spell, applying both single-element Surge effects to the same target. If you choose two different elements, the combined magic creates an additional combo effect from the table below. This effect applies in addition to the normal Surge effects of both elements. Two-Element Combo Table Elements (2 Strains) Combo Effect Fire + Earth A violent explosion scatters debris; creatures within 5 ft. of the target (other than the target) take 1d6 bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Strength save or be knocked prone. Fire + Water Steam burst blinds the target; it must succeed on a Constitution save or be blinded until the start of your next turn. Fire + Air Superheated wind scorches and shoves; target takes an extra 1d8 fire damage and is pushed 10 ft. away from you. Earth + Water Slick mud grips the target’s feet; target’s speed is halved and it must succeed on a Dexterity save or fall prone. Earth + Air Shrapnel-laden gust; target takes an extra 1d8 piercing damage and must make a Constitution saving throw, on a fail loses concentration if concentrating. Water + Air Icy wind chills the target’s bones; target takes an extra 1d8 cold damage and has disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn. Save DC: All saves use your Sorcerer Spell Save DC. Extra Damage Scaling: Extra damage dice from combo effects increase to 2d8 at 14th level.

You can now expend up to 3 Strains on a single spell to induce a Major Strain effect, when you do so replace its normal Surge with a Major effect, these effects can only target a single creature Major Strain Effects: Fire: Dexterity save or the Target is engulfed in flames, taking 3d6 fire damage at the start of its turns for 1 minute, the target can make a dexterity saving throw at the end of it's turn to stop the burning. Earth: Strength save or Target is restrained as stone or force binds them, the target can make a strength saving throw at the end of it's turn to free itself from its binding. Water: Wisdom save or a single target is slowed (as the Slow spell) for 1 minute, the target can make a wisdom saving throw at the end of it's turn to end the effect. Air: Constitution saving throw or the target is pushed 20 ft. and stunned for 1 minute the target can make a wisdom saving throw at the end of it's turn to end the effect. If the initial saving throw is successful the target still suffers the effect from single surge table Strain Conversion: As a bonus action, when you have at least 1 Strain of three different elements, you can expend all three to regain 1 Sorcery Point.

When you have 4 Strains stored, you can absorb them as an action, entering an Ascendant Form for 1 minute. You automatically enter your Innate Sorcery state without spending Sorcery Points. While in an Ascendant Form, you gain resistance to the relevant damage types and special powers as listed below.

Inferno Sovereign (4 Fire Strains)​ Fire damage you deal ignores resistance. Flame Wreath: A creature that touches you or hits you with a melee attack while within 5 feet of you takes 1d10 fire damage. Blazing Ingress: You can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. The first time you enter a creature’s space on a turn, that creature takes 1d10 fire damage. Earth Titan (4 Earth Strains)​ You gain temporary hit points equal to twice your sorcerer level. You cannot be pushed, knocked prone, or restrained unless you wish it. Seismic Crash (1/turn): When you deal damage, you can cause the ground to quake in a 10-ft radius around the target. Each creature of your choice in the area must make a Strength save or be knocked prone and take bludgeoning damage equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus. Tide Monarch (4 Water Strains)​ You gain a swim speed equal to twice your walking speed and can breathe underwater. Water Form. You can enter an enemy's space and stop there. You can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so. Crushing Pressure (1/turn): As an action you can attempt to crush a creature in your space, it must make a Strength saving throw (DC = your spell save DC). On a failed save, the creature takes 4d8 + your Charisma modifier bludgeoning damage and, if it is Large or smaller, it becomes grappled (escape DC = your spell save DC). While grappled in this way, the creature is restrained, begins suffocating unless it can breathe water. A creature within 5 feet of you can use its action to pull a grappled creature free, succeeding on a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC. You can only grapple one creature in this way Tempest Emperor (4 Air Strains)​ You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed. When you deal lightning or thunder damage, you deal an extra 1d8 of that damage type, you can roll an extra d8 of damage if you roll an 8. This damage can do a max of 5d8 damage. Storm Burst (1/turn): When you deal damage, you can unleash a 10-ft radius shockwave centered on the target. Creatures of your choice in the area take lightning damage equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus and can’t take reactions until the start of your next turn.
documents.s: Single-Element Forms (4 Strains of one element)

documents.t: Choose 4 damage types from the following list: fire, bludgeoning, cold, acid, lightning, and thunder damage You gain resistance to the chosen types Your spells ignore resistance to any of these damage types. When you deal damage of one of the chosen damage types, you deal an extra 1d6 for each of the other damages (your choice each time). Prismatic Pulse (1/turn): The first time you damage a single creature each turn, you unleash a burst in a 15-ft radius around it. Each creature of your choice in the area, excluding the target, takes damage equal to your Charisma modifiers of each of the four elemental types

Throughout the continent of kara-tur, one mineral stands above all else in terms of status. Where in the west you would display decadence with gold, in the east, the truest symbol of power is jade. Legends tell of warriors embellished with regality, often proud in status and seeped in regality. The Jade Lords of Shou Lung were legendary figures that displayed power and wealth in equal measure, fighting with both honor and flair. Features: 3rd Level - Regal Countenance 3rd Level - Jade Shards 7th Level - Mystic Stone 10th Level - Jade Armor 15th Level - Verdant Generosity 18th Level - Jade Emperor

Even at 3rd level, you carry yourself with grace and nobility. You gain proficiency in either Persuasion or Intimidation. If you already have both of those proficiencies, you can choose a different proficiency instead.

At 3rd level, the gutteral flow of combat splinters jade around you. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or a creature hits you with an attack, a jade shard splinters off of you and orbits you for the duration. You can only have a number of jade shards equal to half your fighter level (rounded up) at a time. When initiative ends, any remaining jade shards drop to the floor and disappear. You can expend any number of these shards to take special actions called jade tricks. If the trick requires the target to make a saving throw, the DC is calculated as follows: Jade Trick DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice) If you’re able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, a trick replaces one of them. You can only use a trick once per attack action.

Make a melee attack with a melee weapon you are holding against a target within range. On a hit, the target suffers the weapon attack’s normal effects and takes a number of d6s in additional damage equal to the amount of shards spent.
Make a ranged or thrown weapon attack (your choice) against a target within 120 feet of you. The attack deals a number of d8s of piercing damage equal to the amount of shards spent.
Choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Creatures within 10 feet of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw or take a number of d10s in slashing damage equal to the jade shards spent.
At 7th level, the jade you create is fortified. Damage from jade tricks count as magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage.

At 10th level, you learn to pull in the jade shards orbiting you to use as armor. As a bonus action, you can expend any number of jade shards to create jade armor. While this armor is active, you have half cover, or 3/4ths cover if you spent five or more shards. This armor lasts for a number of rounds equal to the jade shards spent or until the end of initiative.

At 15th level, you are able to protect allies with your jade armor as well. If any ally is attacked or is forced to roll a saving throw, you can use your reaction to expend any amount of jade shards and encase them in jade armor. This armor confers the same amount of cover as your jade armor feature, but only lasts until the end of that ally’s next turn.
At 18th level, you learn a new jade trick.

By expending any amount of jade shards, you can create a jadestorm around you in a 20 foot radius, designating any creatures you wish to be unaffected by it. The storm travels with you, with its area being lightly obscured. An affected creature that begins its turn within the jadestorm takes bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage equal to the shards expended. Additionally, their AC is reduced by half the expended amount (rounded down) until the start of their next turn or until they leave the jadestorm. The jadestorm lasts for the expended amount of rounds or until the end of initiative.

While in many cases using heavier two-handed weapons would put the user at a disadvantage defensively, Juggernauts utilize this augment to their offensive capabilities to compliment their defenses with little tradeoff. Features: 3rd Level - Martial Training 3rd Level - Defensive Battering 5th Level - Crushing Force 13th Level - Demolishing Stance 18th Level - Raw Terror
When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in martial weapons.

Additionally at 3rd level, you have the ability to use larger weapons to block and deflect incoming attacks. While you are wielding a weapon with two hands, you gain a +1 bonus to your armor class. If the weapon has a magical bonus to attack and damage rolls, you can apply that same bonus to your armor class while wielding it in two hands.

Starting at 7th level, the sheer force you deliver with your attacks is enough to shatter your foe’s defenses. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can reduce the effectiveness of their armor, if they are wearing any, reducing their armor class by 3. Shields, and armor created by spells or other magic are unaffected, and you cannot reduce a creature’s armor class below what it would be without armor. This reduction lasts until the end of the creature’s next turn.

When you reach 13th level, your martial capability reaches new heights in conjunction with your defenses. While your defensive Stance is active, you gain a bonus to damage rolls with weapons equal to the armor class bonus given to you by your stance.

At 18th level, your very presence strikes terror into your foes. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your dueling stance, that creature becomes frightened of you until the start of their next turn.

Water is the element of change. The creatures of the deep survive because they can adapt to anything — shifting, flowing, enduring. They are never truly alone; the ocean itself is community, a vast and endless embrace where life persists against crushing darkness. The Leviathan is this truth given form: the abyssal power of the ocean, both merciless and sheltering, both devourer and protector. Those who carry its mark become vessels of unfathomable power, embodying the adaptability, love, and crushing might of the deep. A Leviathan Vessel suffocates breath, bends water into chains, and calls forth the jaws of the abyss to devour all who defy them. Features: 1st Level — Body of Water Leviathan Vessel Expanded Spells 6th Level — Crushing Currents 14th Level — Abyssal Chains 18th Level — Leviathan Ascendant

The Leviathan Vessel lets you choose from an expanded list of spells whenever you learn a sorcerer spell. The following spells are added to the sorcerer spell list for you. Sorcerer Level Spells 1st create or destroy water, fog cloud 2nd blur, misty step 3rd tidal wave, wall of water 4th watery sphere, greater invisibility 5th maelstrom, cone of cold 7th* control water, dimension door 9th* tsunami, gate *Spells above 5th level count as Signature Spells. DMs may gate access to these as high-tier content

You are bound to the ocean’s depths. You gain a swim speed equal to your walking speed and can breathe underwater. Once per long rest, or by spending 2 sorcery points, you can slip your form into liquid for an instant. As a bonus action, you may move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

You can choke the life from others with conjured water. As an action, choose one creature within 30 feet that needs to breathe. Spend 2 sorcery points and force the target to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, water floods their throat, making them gag. They cannot speak or cast spells with verbal components until the start of your next turn. If the creature is already underwater, it instead takes 2d6 cold damage as the abyss crushes its lungs. On a success, the creature resists the effect. Creatures that do not need to breathe are immune.

The abyss answers your will with shackles of water. As an action, choose up to 3 creatures within 30 feet. Each must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become restrained by spectral chains of water until the start of your next turn. While restrained in this way, a creature is treated as if caught within crushing currents. Ocean’s Reach. You can spend 1 sorcery point as a bonus action to conjure and shape water manifestations. You may: Create a platform of hardened water (Large, lasts 1 minute, supports creatures). The platform can hover and move up to 20 feet per round in any direction while you remain within 60 feet of it. You may mentally command its movement as a bonus action. Form a wall of water (10 ft high, 10 ft wide, 1 ft thick, lasts 1 minute). Summon a tendril of water to push or pull one creature within 20 feet up to 10 feet (Strength save negates).

You call forth the jaws of the deep. Maw of the Abyss. As an action, you may spend 3 sorcery points to manifest the Leviathan’s spectral jaws. Choose a 30-foot line, 20 feet wide, within 60 feet. • Each enemy in the line must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. • On a failed save, the creature takes 2d10 force + 1d10 cold damage and is restrained inside the jaws until the start of your next turn. • On a success, the creature takes half damage and isn’t restrained. • Lingering Rift. After the jaws vanish, the ground (or space) in the area becomes a zone of churning abyssal water until the start of your next turn. Enemies treat this area as difficult terrain.

Water is the element of change. The creatures of the deep survive because they can adapt to anything — shifting, flowing, enduring. They are never truly alone; the ocean itself is community, a vast and endless embrace where life persists against crushing darkness. The Leviathan is this truth given form: the abyssal power of the ocean, both merciless and sheltering, both devourer and protector. Those who carry its mark become vessels of unfathomable power, embodying the adaptability, love, and crushing might of the deep. A Leviathan Vessel suffocates breath, bends water into chains, and calls forth the jaws of the abyss to devour all who defy them. Features: Leviathan Vessel Expanded Spells 3rd Level - Hydrokinesis Incarnate 3rd Level - Dominion of Water 6th Level - Binding Currents 6th Level - Sculpted Water 10th Level - Reactive Tide 10th Level - Claim the Battlefield 14th Level - Siphoning Cyclone 18th Level - Leviathan’s Maw

The Leviathan Vessel lets you choose from an expanded list of spells whenever you learn a sorcerer spell. The following spells are added to the sorcerer spell list for you. Sorcerer Level Spells 3rd create or destroy water, fog cloud, tidal wave, wall of water 5th maelstrom, cone of cold 7th control water, dimension door 9th tsunami, gate
You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. You can breathe air and water. You gain resistance to cold damage.

As an action, you activate a 10-foot aura of water for 1 minute. Enemies treat it as difficult terrain. The first time each turn an enemy enters or starts its turn there, it takes magical bludgeoning damage equal to your Charisma modifier. Uses equal to proficiency bonus per long rest.

When a creature within 30 feet moves or fails a save against your Sorcerer spell, you may use your reaction. On a failed Strength save, it is restrained and takes 1d6 magical cold damage. On a success, it takes half damage and speed becomes 0. The restraint ends at the end of its next turn or earlier if it uses an action to break free. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

As a bonus action, create one water construct (Platform, Arm, or Mirror) within 30 feet for 1 minute. One at a time. Uses equal to your charisma modifier per long rest or 1 sorcery point. Constructs have AC 13 + PB and HP 10 + five times Sorcerer level.
Once per turn when you cast a Sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, one creature affected or within Dominion takes magical piercing damage equal to your Sorcerer level.

When you or an ally within 30 feet is hit by an attack, use your reaction and spend 1 sorcery point to reduce damage by 2d8 + CHA. If the attacker is within 30 feet, push it 10 feet or move an ally 5 feet without opportunity attacks.

You wrench moisture from flesh and air alike, drawing it inward in a crushing spiral. As an action, each creature of your choice within 20 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 4d10 magical necrotic damage and is knocked prone. On a success, a creature takes half damage and is not knocked prone. You then distribute hit points equal to half the total damage dealt, dividing them as you choose among yourself and any allies you can see within 30 feet. You can use this feature by spending 4 sorcery points. Creatures that do not rely on moisture to survive have advantage on the saving throw, at the DM’s discretion..

As a bonus action, choose a point within 60 feet. Creatures in a 30-foot radius make Strength saves. Failures take 6d10 magical bludgeoning damage, are restrained until the end of your next turn, and pulled 15 feet inward. Successes take half damage. The area is difficult terrain and blocks teleportation until the start of your next turn. Once per long rest, regainable by spending 5 sorcery points.

Your powers are drawn from the spark of light kindled within you. In places of great darkness, there are those born with an affinity for light, and every shadow has a source. The magic within you represents cosmic balance, flickering from radiance to darkness moment to moment. Features: 1st Level - Trick of the Light 1st Level - Flickering Aura 6th Level - Refraction Shield 14th Level - Aura Magnification 18th Level - Light Weaver

Starting at 1st level, you have darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, it increases its range by 60 feet. You learn the Light and Sacred Flame cantrips. At 3rd-level you learn the Darkness and Faerie Fire spells, which are sorcerer spells and do not count against your spells known. They can cast normally, or by expending 2 sorcery points.

Starting at 1st level, you can magnify the properties of light around you. At the end of a short or long rest, you can choose whether your magic is light-shifted or dark-shifted. While light-shifted you can use an action to emit an aura in a 15-foot radius around you. This area is bright light. While the aura persist, you can use a bonus action to expand or reduce its radius by 5 feet, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet. While dark-shifted you gain the same ability, but you project an aura of nonmagical darkness. This effect lasts for 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated. Once used, you cannot use this ability again until you finish a short or long rest

At 6th level, you can manipulate the light around you for protection. As a bonus action, you can spend 2 sorcery points to magically create a shield of light or dark. The shield lasts for 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated. While this shield is in place, whenever a creature within 10 feet of you hits you with an attack, this shield flashes with searing energy, and the attacker takes 2d6 radiant damage if you are light-shifted or 2d6 necrotic damage if you are dark-shifted.

While your Flickering Aura is active, you can now expand it up to 10 feet as a bonus action, up to a maximum of 60 feet. While within the aura, a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier also gain the benefit of your Refraction Shield, but no more than once per turn. Additionally, you and those creatures have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) skill checks made while light-shifted, or Dexterity (Stealth) checks made while dark-shifted. You can add your proficiency bonus when making these skill checks by expending a sorcery point.

Embodying both aspects of Light and Dark, you gain resistance to both radiant and necrotic damage. Additionally, as part of the action to activate your Flickering Aura, you can transform yourself and gain the following benefits for up to 1 minute: Upon activation or as part of the bonus action to expand or reduce it's radius, you can switch to either light-shifted or dark-shifted. Each creature of your choice within your aura must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 radiant and 2d8 necrotic damage and becoming blinded till the end of their next turn on a failure, or half as much damage and not being blinded in a success. While your Radiant Shield is active, the radius of its effect increases to 30 feet, and you deal both the radiant and the necrotic damage when hit with an attack. Once you use this action, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 5 sorcery points to use it again.

Clerics of the Love Domain serve gods of love, passion, and beauty, such as Sune, drawing on the purifying and enchanting power of the sacred waters, the Evergold. They are focused on protective healing, social grace, and captivating presence. Features: Love Domain Spells 1st Level - Bonus Proficiencies & Evergold Touch 2nd Level - Channel Divinity: Purifying Cascade 6th Level - Flow of Beauty 8th Level - Potent Spellcasting 17th Level - Aura of Ideal Radiance
Cleric Level | Spells 1st | Charm Person, Ceremony 3rd | Aid, Calm Emotions 5th | Beacon of Hope, Hypnotic Pattern 7th | Compulsion, Aura of Life 9th | Commune, Mass Cure Wounds
When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Persuasion skill and the Performance skill.

Starting at 1st level, whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, that creature gains **temporary hit points equal to your Cleric level + your Charisma modifier** (minimum of 1). These temporary hit points last for 1 hour.

You can use your Channel Divinity to instantly cleanse and refresh those around you. As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke a wave of purifying golden energy. Choose any number of creatures within 30 feet of you. Any target you choose that is **Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned** immediately ends that condition. Additionally, any creature whose condition is removed **regains a number of hit points equal to 1d6 + your Wisdom modifier.**

Starting at 6th level, you are perpetually surrounded by a faint glamour. You are under the constant effect of the *Disguise Self* spell, but you can only choose to appear as yourself at your most ideal and radiant. This effect cannot be dispelled by normal means. Moreover, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw against the **Charmed** or **Frightened** condition, you can use your reaction to grant that creature **advantage** on its next attack roll made before the start of your next turn.
Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

At 17th level, the Evergold flows through you in a constant, palpable wave of grace, affecting all who draw near. You gain the following benefits: Sanctuary of Beauty. When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll or targets you with a harmful spell, it must first succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Cleric Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a new target or the attack or spell is wasted. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect until the start of its next turn.This effect functions only if you haven't made an attack roll or cast a spell that affects an enemy creature since the end of your last turn. If you break this condition, the effect automatically resumes at the start of your next turn. Protective Aegis. When a friendly creature within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage taken by an amount equal to your Cleric level + your Wisdom modifier. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Sneaky Sneak, Stabby Stab Prerequisites: Rogue 20
When you take this prestige class, choose any four more skills. You are proficient in all of those skills.

Additionally when you take this prestige class your Sneak Attack improves to reflect greater precision and accuracy. Your Sneak Attack damage increases to a number of d6s equal to half your prestige level rounded up.

At 21st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and one of your tool proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check that uses either of the chosen proficiencies. If the skill already benefits from your expertise ability, your proficiency bonus is tripled instead. At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or tools) to gain this benefit.

At 22nd level, you can grant yourself moments of heightened agility when you need it the most. You gain a special bonus action that can be used only to use your cunning action. You can use this bonus action twice between short or long rests, and only once on each of your turns.

At 23rd level, you choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your rogue abilities. You may choose the same archetype, or you may choose a new one to further your techniques. Your archetype choice grants you features at 23rd level, and then again at 29th, 33rd, and 37th level.

When you reach 24th level, and again at 28th, 30th, 32nd, 36th, and 39th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Starting at 25th level your ability to move out of the way of life ending blows extends to new heights. When you use your uncanny dodge feature, the total damage is further reduced by half your prestige level. Additionally, if you use your uncanny dodge feature on an attack, damage from that attack cannot reduce you to 0 hit points.
Practice has honed your strikes by 25th level. When you apply multiple cunning strike options on your sneak attack, you only pay the die cost for the most expensive effect.

Beginning at 27th level, your ability to dodge effects is no longer limited to just your quick reflexes. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half if you fail. You cannot use this ability if you are incapacitated.

At 31st level, your defining skills have truly been perfected to the point of never failing you. Whenever you make an ability check using any of the skills enhanced by your Expertise or Superior Expertise features, you can treat a d20 roll of 14 or lower as a 15.

At 34th level, you’ve practiced further ways to use your sneak attack to its fullest extent. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options. Bleed (Cost: 5d6) - The target suffers large hemorrhages. At the start of each of the creature’s turns, it takes slashing damage equal to half your sneak attack damage. The bleeding creature, or a creature within 5 feet of them, can use an action to make a medicine check (DC = your cunning strikes DC) ending the effect on a success. Execute (Cost: 10d6) - If the damage from this attack leaves the target with 60 hit points or less, they die.

When you reach 35th level, you are exceptionally difficult to pin down by any. Your proficiency bonus for dexterity saving throws, and your choice of intelligence, wisdom, or charisma saving throws, is doubled.
At 38th level, your ability and flexibility when it comes to movement are unmatched. The bonus action granted by Cunning Flexibility no longer requires you to rest between uses.
When you reach 40th level, your consistency is no longer mere luck. Once per turn when you miss with an attack roll which you have advantage on, you may choose to hit instead.
Mediums are the bridge between life and death, often treading over the gap between the two. They call forth spirits of the past, using them for power and knowledge.

At 3rd level, you are able to tap into knowledge from spirits that you know of. You learn speak with dead and can cast it only as if it were a ritual spell. Rather than targeting a corpse, you can speak the name of a deceased individual who died within 1 mile. If their soul is able, they can choose to manifest in an empty space within 5 feet of you and answer your questions. Once a soul is manifested in this way, you can’t manifest the same soul again for 24 hours.
Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your capacity to channel souls.

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to channel the spirit of a warrior. The spirit manifests as a spectral fighter that is always 5 feet away from your target. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, you can have the warrior strike at the target in the same action. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 force damage. If you use this spirit art again on the same target, you can channel another warrior, up to a maximum of 3 total. Each new warrior increases the force damage dealt to the target by an extra 2d6.

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to channel the spirit of a trickster. The spirit manifests in the form of an imp, fairy, or any other tricky creature that is always 5 feet away from your target. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, you can have the trickster distract at the target in the same action. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have disadvantage on attack rolls and Perception checks until the end of its next turn.

As an action, you can spend 1 spirit point to channel the spirit of a guardian. The spirit manifests as an ancestor, patron, or angel that is always within 5 feet of you. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, the guardian bestows 1d6 temporary hit points to you. If you use this spirit art again, you can channel another guardian, up to a maximum of 3 total. Each new guardian increases the temporary hit points gained by an extra 1d6.

At 6th level, your frequent interactions with other spirits has strengthened your own considerably. The range of your spirit tether increases to 300 feet. In addition, if your tether breaks while you have at least one active spirit art, you regain one spirit point.

At 13th level, by drawing upon the experiences of the dead, you become temporarily able to utilize their skills. If you make a skill check in any skill you’re not proficient in, you can spend a spirit point to add your proficiency bonus to the roll. You can use this feature after the roll is made, but only before you know the results.
At 18th level, you master your influence over the souls of others. You learn the following spirit art:

If your target is a creature, you can use an action and spend 5 spirit points to attempt to possess them temporarily. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be possessed by you for a minute. During this time, your soul is transferred into the target’s form, and your original body is left paralyzed. You now control the body but you don’t deprive the target of awareness. You use the possessed target’s statistics, but you retain your alignment, Wisdom, Intelligence, and Charisma. You don’t gain access to the target’s knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. You may end the possession at any time, upon which you return to your body without harm. At the end of each of their turns, the target can repeat the Charisma save, ending the possession on a success. If the target dies while you possess it, your soul is returned to your body without harm. However, if your body dies while possessing the target, the possession ends and you die.
Monks who follow the Way of the Feral Fang tap into their primal instincts, channeling the savage power of beasts. They unleash their inner ferocity, embodying the untamed fury of nature itself.

Starting at 3rd level, when you use your Flurry of Blows feature, you can replace one of the unarmed strikes with the primal savagery cantrip. The primal savagery cantrip uses wisdom as your spellcasting ability modifier for its attack rolls.
Starting at 3rd level, you can choose to learn the druidcraft or shillelagh cantrip, you use wisdom as your spellcasting ability modifier for this cantrip

At 6th level, your connection to primal instincts enhances your speed and agility. You gain the following benefits: You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would cause you to be restrained or paralyzed If you use your Primal savagery cantrip granted by Feral Strikes in a turn you can use your reaction when an enemy makes an attack of opportunity against you to roll a Martial Art Die and add the result to your AC until the end of your turn.

At 11th level, your strikes become even more savage and relentless. When you hit a creature with your primal savagery cantrip granted by your Feral Strikes feature, you can add your wisdom modifier to the damage dealt, in addition, if you spend 1 ki point, the target must also make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

Starting at 17th level, your primal connection enhances your body’s resilience and ferocity. As a bonus action, you can spend 4 ki points to enter a primal state of feral resilience that last for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits when in this state: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened. You add an additional Martial Art die to your unarmed strikes You have advantage on all Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and you gain temporary hit points equal to your Monk level at the start of each of your turns. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

3rd-level Mirror Soul feature Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can create reflections that disorient your foes and bolster your defense. When you use your flurry of blows, you can spend 2 ki points to cast the mirror image spell, replacing one of the unarmed strikes. When casted this way, you only make one illusory duplicate, unless you spend one ki point for an additional duplicate (3 duplicates max). For each duplicate you create, you gain 5 temporary hit points.

6th-level Mirror Soul feature As an action you may magically project your consciousness into a reflective surface that you can see. Projecting allows you to see and hear, as well as project your voice as though you were in that reflections space. During this time, you are blinded and deafened. You can sustain this effect for up to 10 minutes, and you can end it at any time (requires no action). While being used in this way, you can use an action to project to another reflective surface that you can see. While you are projecting into a reflection, your reflection is visible, and can be interacted with by others, such as speaking with them. If any reflective surface along this path is destroyed or disrupted (in the case of liquids), this effect ends.

11th-level Mirror Soul feature You gain the ability to magically enter a mirror or reflective surface within 5 feet of you and move from inside it to inside another mirror or reflective surface being effected by your Fractal Vision feature. You must spend 1 ki point and use 5 feet of movement to enter a reflection. As part of the movement used to enter the reflection, you can either pass into one of those reflections or step out of the reflection you're in. You appear in a spot of your choice within 5 feet of the destination, using another 5 feet of movement. If you have no movement left, you appear within 5 feet of the reflection you entered. You can use this ability once per round, and take 1d10 force damage if you end your turn inside a reflection.

17th-level Mirror Soul feature Starting at 17th level, you empower your Mirror Images for both defense and offense. While your Mirror Images persist, you gain the following benefits: You and your illusory duplicates gain a +1 to Armor Class and Saving Throws for each duplicate still active (up to a maximum of +3) Your unarmed strikes and monk weapon attacks deal additional psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier. (edited)

Masters of a martial discipline intertwined with the ethereal energies of ki, the practitioners of the Way of the Ki Blade are formidable warriors who wield weapons forged from the very essence of their inner strength. These adept martial artists combine their physical prowess with the disciplined art of ki manipulation, creating a dance of blades that transcends the limits of the mundane.

At 3rd level, you can spend 1 ki point as a bonus action to manifest a ki-forged weapon, turning a melee monk weapon into a weapon of pure energy for 1 minute. This weapon deals force damage instead of its regular damage type and uses your Wisdom modifier for attack and damage rolls. In addition, at level 5 the weapon gains a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls, unless it is a magic weapon that already has a bonus to those rolls, this bonus increases to +2 at level 11

At 6th level, once per turn you can spend a ki-point to temporarily transform your ki-forged weapon into an ethereal weapon. The next melee attack you make with it before the end of your turn ignores the target’s armor, requiring no attack roll. Instead, the target makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Ki save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes damage as if hit by an attack from your ki-forged blade and it's inner balance and movement is disrupted by your ki, the target's speed is halved, and it can't use reactions. On its next turn, it can use either an action or a bonus action, not both. On a successful save, the target takes half damage from the attack and isn't disrupted. The blade returns to normal immediately after the attack
At 6th level, If your Ki-Forged blade has the thrown property you can make it return to your hand immediately after it is thrown by spending 1 ki point.

At 11th level, your focused ki protects you from mental intrusions and damage. Your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it, and you also have resistance to psychic damage.
At 11th level, when you use your flurry of blows, you can attack with your ki-forged blade instead of unarmed strikes.

At 17th level, your connection to the essence of ki reaches its pinnacle. You can now infuse your ki-forged weapon with extraordinary power. As an action, you can spend 4 ki points to enter the state of Ki-Blade Ascendancy, which lasts for 1 minute. While in this state: Your ki-forged weapon deals an additional 1d8 force damage on each hit, and you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to twice the force damage dealt by this feature. Whenever you hit a stunned creature with your ki-forged weapon, you can spend an additional ki point to attempt to paralyze the target. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your Ki save DC or be paralyzed until the end of its next turn.

Curiously, the Way of the Dragon Turtle is a bit of a misnomer for the monks that follow this style. Their link to the legendary beasts is practically nonexistent, only dubbed this way by others for their fortitude and control over heat and steam. Monks that follow this martial style are rarely taught formally, though they may occasionally take on no more than a few students who wish to learn the style. Those who follow the Way of the Dragon Turtle are self-made and remarkable, often gaining an innate understanding of the ki flowing through and around them after overcoming intense hardship. Although this style may seem less refined than its contemporaries, the technical ability of these monks is fatal to underestimate. They pose as much of a threat to their own bodies by manipulating pressure and heat as they do to others, and they must always understand their limits above all else.

Perseverance manifested in the form of raw ki has scorched and hardened your soul and body. When calculating your Monk unarmored defense, you may instead use 13 + your Constitution modifier. Additionally, your body is altered by the unrefined, explosive ki you harness, often leaving a strange mark on your likeness. You determine its appearance, or generate it randomly by rolling on the Ki-Scorched Characteristic table. d6 Ki-Scorched Characteristic 1 Your hands and feet are blackened, giving them the appearance of charcoal. 2 Steam often rises from your ears, mouth and body when you experience intense emotions. 3 The skin around your elbows and shoulders is cracked and ossified, peeling slightly upward like the scutes of a turtle. 4 You have a large scar or burn mark on your body, which becomes searing hot in a fight. 5 Still sources of waters nearby you tend to become restless, showing tiny ripples and tremors. 6 Your skin fluctuates between feeling extremely hot and cold to the touch.

Your rudimentary abilities in channeling ki allow you to compress and expel moisture and heat. As an action, you can cast fog cloud without providing material components. Once you cast fog cloud using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you spend 2 ki points to cast it again. Additionally, you gain the ability to convert the heat and force from blows you take into powerful outbursts. As a bonus action, if you have taken damage between the end of your last turn and the start of your current turn, you may spend 1 ki point to enter the Combustion state until the end of your turn. While in the Combustion state, you gain the following benefits: You make Strength-based attack rolls with advantage. Your unarmed strikes deal additional fire damage on a hit equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier. You can make one additional unarmed strike as part of your Attack action.

At 6th level, you gain the ability to catalyze the heat and momentum you build by moving into a volatile enhancement. If you move at least 30 feet in a straight line on your turn, you may immediately spend 2 ki points to increase your walking speed by 30 feet until the end of your turn. If you continue the current movement for at least 60 feet in a straight line, you may choose to emit a blast of excess pressure around you. When you end this movement, each creature within a 10-foot radius of you must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take a number of d10s equal to your proficiency bonus in force damage and be knocked prone. If a creature passes this saving throw, it takes half damage and is not knocked prone.

At 11th level, your control of ki becomes more refined, allowing you to manipulate the elements of your physical form. As an action, you can spend 4 ki points to cast gaseous form on yourself, without providing material components. While in this form, your movement speed is not restricted to 10 feet. Additionally, you may exit this form at any time on your turn. When you exit this form, you may heal 5d8 hit points. Once you regain hit points using this ability, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

At 17th level, your mastery over the convergence and direction of ki reaches explosive heights. As a reaction to taking damage from a source other than yourself, you may spend up to six ki points. For each ki point you spend as a part of this reaction, you mitigate 5 damage. This damage mitigation is applied before any resistances you have. You may also redirect the force from this mitigated damage, blasting out a 40-foot cone of crushing steam. Creatures in this area must pass a Constitution saving throw against your ki save DC or take 10 fire damage for each ki point you spent as part of this reaction, taking half damage if they pass. Being underwater does not grant resistance to this attack. Additionally, you are no longer required to have taken damage to enter the Combustion state as a bonus action.

You learn the art of siphoning life from dying enemies and combining it with negetive energy to imbue necromancy into your fighting style. Reavers often kill those who are closest to death, whose spiritual binds are thin enough to cut free and use. Features: 3rd Level - Criticality 9th Level - Rend 13th Level - Ward of Mortality 17th Level - Echo of Reaping

Starting at 3rd level, creatures with less than half of their total hit points gain a Death Mark, granting you the following benefits: You gain an additional way to use your sneak attack; you don’t need advantage on the attack roll to use your Sneak Attack against a marked creature, so long as you don’t have disadvantage on the attack roll. Attack rolls against marked creatures crit on 19-20. You have a bonus on attack rolls against marked creatures. This bonus equals half your proficiency bonus.

Starting at 9th level, you gain the ability to rend those close to death. When you hit a marked creature with your Sneak Attack, you can deal additional damage equal to your rogue level. Once you use this ability, you may not do so against until you complete a short or long rest. If you reduce a creature to zero hit points with this ability, you regain a use.

Starting at 13th level, you learn to collect and conserve the life force you steal from dying opponents, which materializes as a ward. When you hit a marked creature with rend, roll your total sneak attack die. You gain temporary hit points equal to the total, unless you already have more.

Starting at 17th level, you learn to travel to and harness remnants of death. When you hit a creature with rend, you may teleport to a corpse within 90 ft of you as a bonus action, and the next attack you make before the end of your next treats the target as being blood marked. In addition, through a one-minute ritual, you may travel to an area of mass death or a sight where you slew a creature within 2 miles, bringing a number of willing creatures equal to the number of creatures you have killed today (maximum of 10). Once you use this ability, you may not do so again until you complete a long rest.

While many paladins may follow a just code, one holding their morals and beliefs above all else, there exist those who instead swear an oath only to themselves. Paladins who undertake an oath of deceit take it upon themselves to do whatever it may take to come out on top of whatever situation they may find themselves in. They may employ underhanded tactics, subterfuge, and other such tactics to ensure their success. Despite this, these paladins still follow a code, and are not always out for evil. Tenets of Deceit: Concealment - Never tell too much about your intentions, and never let your foes know what you are going to do next. Willingness - Never settle for second best when victory is attainable, even if you need to employ less than savory means to do so. Self-Worth - You are the most important person to completing your goals, and never let anyone let you doubt your worth to them. Features: 3rd Level - Oath Spells 3rd Level - Channel Divinity 7th Level - Aura of Betrayal 15th Level - Underhanded Tactics 20th Level - Cloak of Lies

You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed in the Oath of Deceit Spells table. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how oath spells work. Paladin Level Spells 3rd Disguise Self, Silvery Barbs 5th Phantasmal Force, Invisibility 9th Enemies Abound, Hypnotic Pattern 13th Confusion, Phantasmal Killer 17th Dominate Person, Mislead
At 3rd level, you gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works.

You can use your channel divinity to feint an attack against an enemy. As a bonus action, you can distract a target that you can see within 30 ft of you. Doing so will grant you advantage on attack rolls against the target until the end of your next turn, and impose disadvantage on attack rolls for the target to hit you. Additionally, your next weapon attack against the target deals an additional 2d6 psychic damage. The extra damage increases to 3d6 at 7th level, 4d6 at 15th level, and 5d6 at 20th level.

As an action, you can use your channel divinity to invoke a supernatural sense of confidence within yourself. For the next minute, you make all charisma checks at advantage. If you already have advantage from another source, you may reroll one of the dice. Additionally, no matter what you say, magic that would determine if you are telling the truth indicates that you are being truthful if you so choose.

At 7th level, You emit an aura of magical charm while you aren't incapacitated. Creatures hostile towards you within 10 ft must succeed a Wisdom Saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed until you or an ally deal damage to it. When a charmed creature is hit by an attack from you or an ally, the attack is automatically critical. Any creature that succeeds this saving throw is immune to your Aura of Betrayal for 24 hours. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 ft.

Starting at 15th level, you gain the ability to undermine a foe's initiative. When you roll initiative, you may choose to gain advantage on the roll. In doing so, you must impose disadvantage on another creature you can see within 60 ft of you. Additionally, that creature's speed is halved until the end of its first turn.

At 20th level, none can hold an advantage over you no matter how they try. As an action, you gain the following benefits for one minute: The area within 5 ft of you becomes heavily obscured to creatures other than you. You add your charisma modifier to damage rolls of weapon attacks. creatures have disadvantage against saving throws against your enchantment and illusion spells, as well as your aura of betrayal. creatures have disadvantage on ability checks made to discern the true nature of illusions created by you. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th level spell slot to use it again.

Paladins aligned to the Oath of Providence are protected by the mysterious forces that guide our fates. Proud and stoic, they seek to prove their devotion to a chosen cause or deity, with the utmost faith that they are a part of a grand design, protected by destiny and fulfilling a higher purpose. Features: 3rd Level - Channel Divinity 7th Level - Aura of Penitence 15th Level - Twist of Fate 20th Level - Divine Champion
3rd-level Oath of Providence feature You gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works.

You can use your Channel Divinity to invest your presence with the guiding powers of fate. As an action, you can choose a number of creatures you can see within 30 feet of you, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). For 1 minute, you and the chosen creatures have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma ability checks.

As a bonus action, you can suspend judgement between yourself and another creature you can see within 10 feet of you, using your Channel Divinity. The damage dealt by you and the chosen creature against each other is delayed until the end of your next turn. At the end of that turn both you and that creature take the damage that was delayed and must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, the damaged received from the delayed attacks is doubled, receiving the normal amount instead on a success.

7th-level Oath of Providence feature Starting at 7th level, you emanate an aura of regretful penitence as long as you’re not incapacitated. Whenever a creature misses an attack against the paladin, or any friendly creatures within 10 feet of the paladin, the attacking creatures takes radiant damage equal to half your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

15th-level Oath of Providence feature You’ve learned to help your allies avoid a dire fate. Whenever a friendly creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails a Strength, a Dexterity, or a Constitution saving throw, you can use your reaction to have that creature regain hit points equal to 2d8 + your Charisma modifier if it has no more than half its hit points.

20th-level Oath of Providence feature Starting at 20th level, once per turn when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with your Divine Smite, you can regain a number of hit points equal to your paladin level, and regain one charge of your Channel Divinity. This is usable a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, resetting on a Long Rest

Paladins who swear the Oath of the Dusk embody twilight’s mysteries. They walk the line between light and darkness, embracing dusk as both an ending and a beginning. Where the sun fades, they stand vigilant, comforting those who fear the night and striking at terrors that thrive in it. To them, dusk is balance — a veil between hope and despair, life and death.

The tenets of the Oath of the Dusk vary slightly between orders, but all share a devotion to twilight’s balance: Balance. Neither light nor darkness holds dominion — each has its place. Comfort in Darkness. Offer peace when hope wanes, and be a lantern when others are lost. Vigilance. Stand watch when others sleep; protect them from the dangers that stalk the night. Endings & Beginnings. Accept what must fade, but kindle what must endure. Features 3rd Level - Dusk Oath Spells 3rd Level - Channel Divinity 7th Level - Aura of Dusk – Protective Twilight 15th Level - Midnight Envelopment 20th Level - Avatar of the Dusk

You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed. Paladin Level Spells 3rd Faerie Fire, Sleep 5th Moonbeam, Misty Step 9th Aura of Vitality, Counterspell 13th Greater Invisibility, Aura of Purity 17th Wall of Light, Dream

When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following Channel Divinity options: Twilight Sanctuary. As an action, you emanate a 20-foot-radius aura of soothing dusk. Allies inside the aura immediately gain temporary hit points equal to your paladin level + your Charisma modifier. Cloak of Shadows. As a bonus action, you can veil yourself in dusk for 1 minute. Until the effect ends, you have advantage on Stealth checks. This effect ends early if you make an attack, cast a spell, or force a creature to make a saving throw.

Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you are shrouded in twilight’s protective veil. While within this aura, allies gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
documents.s: 7th Level - Aura of Dusk – Protective Twilight

documents.t: At 15th level, your twilight presence smothers and binds those who oppose you. When a hostile creature starts its turn within 10 feet of you, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your paladin spell save DC or be restrained until the start of its next turn. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your Midnight Envelopment until the next dusk. At 18th level, the range of this effect increases to 30 feet.

At 20th level, you can invoke the mantle of twilight, becoming dusk incarnate for 1 minute. You emit a 30-foot aura of twilight (bright light in 15 feet, dim light in the next 15). Hostile creatures that start their turn in the aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the start of their next turn. Allies in the aura regain 10 hit points at the start of their turns. You gain a flying speed of 60 feet, surrounded by swirling dusk and shadow. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

The tenets of the Oath of the Grave have been passed down for generations. This oath honors the passage from the warmth of life to the everlasting cold of death, and it punishes those who defile that passage by raising the undead. Tenets of the Grave Annihilate the Unholy. The undead and those who foster them are unholy and wicked. Destroy them before they defile more than they already have. Preserve the Righteous. Death should not come early to those who have led a blessed life. Preserve the righteous, so they may live on without fear. Let Souls Pass On. Every soul deserves its place in the afterlife. When you see a creature forced into undeath, set its soul free. Accept Death. Death comes to us all eventually. Accept it, and you will find a place in the afterlife. Features Paladin Level Feature 3rd Channel Divinity, Oath Spells 7th Aura of Preservation 15th Sanctity of the Grave 20th Walker of the Last Road

You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed. Paladin Level Spells 3rd ice knife, sanctuary 5th gentle repose, Rime's binding ice 9th sleet storm, speak with dead 13th guardian of faith, Mordenkainen's faithful hound 17th cone of cold, destructive wave
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer against undeath, using your Channel Divinity. Each undead within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is frozen for 1 minute or until it takes damage. A frozen creature has the petrified condition until the effect ends.

As a bonus action, you utter a vow of death against one undead you can see within 30 feet of you, using your Channel Divinity. For 1 minute, the undead has vulnerability to the radiant damage dealt by your Divine Smite and Improved Divine Smite. The vow ends early if the undead is destroyed or if you use this feature again.

Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed and have resistance to necrotic damage while you are conscious. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
Beginning at 15th level, you carry the peace of the grave with you, and dark magic falters in your presence. You gain the following benefits.
Undead within your Aura of Preservation can't regain hit points. Corpses within the aura can't be animated or raised as undead.

When you see a creature within 60 feet of you cast a necromancy spell, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the spell fails, the spell slot is wasted, and the caster takes radiant damage equal to 2d8 + your paladin level. On a success, the spell resolves normally. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

At 20th level, you have made peace with your own death, and the powers beyond know your soul. Your soul can't be trapped or stolen, and you can't be raised as undead by any means. As an action, you can walk the road of death for 10 minutes. You gain the following benefits for the duration:
documents.s: 20th Level - Walker of the Last Road

documents.t: Chilling winds surround you in a 30-foot radius. When an enemy creature starts its turn within the area, it takes 10 cold damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
When a creature dies within the area, its soul passes freely to the afterlife. It can't be raised as undead. If it was undead, it can't rejuvenate or re-form by any means short of a wish spell.

Tame, Control, Become. The "curse" of lycanthropy can be and must be controlled to not be defined by it, but rather to define it as a means of protecting others. Great Power, Even Greater Responsibility. Lycanthropy is not something that should be spread without caution, those who don't have the will or the drive to be able to master the curse, should not have it, and those who use it without understanding it must be taken care of. (Healed or Killed depending on you/your deities morality) Shield the Innocent Use your new strengths to shield the innocent from those who would harm them. Never Take Vengeance Against The Ignorant. Never take vengeance against those that do not understand the curse you bear. Instead show mercy and teach them that all is not always as it seems. Features: 3rd Level - Channel Divinity 3rd Level - Oath Spells 7th Level - Aura of Feral Speed 15th Level - Primal Roar 20th Level - True Alpha
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

As an action, you can reveal the beast inside and imbue your body with divine power, for 1 minute you can apply your Divine Smite feature to your unarmed strikes. You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes, which deal 1d6 bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing damage (your choice). This damage increases to 1d8 at 11th level. Additionally, when you use the Attack action to make an unarmed strike, you can make one additional unarmed strike as a bonus action.

As an action, you channel the powerful roars/howls/screeches of your lycanthrope namesake. You force creatures of your choice equal to your proficiency bonus within 15 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature becomes frightened of you for 5 rounds(half a minute). The frightened creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed. Oath of the Howling Moon Spells​ PALADIN LEVEL SPELLS 3rd hunter's mark, shield of faith 5th darkvision, pass without trace 9th haste, remove curse 13th dominate beast, freedom of movement 17th hold monster, mass cure wounds

Starting at 7th level, you fill nearby creatures with the feral speed of the beast inside. While you’re not incapacitated, you and creatures of your choice within 10 feet have their walking, swimming, and climbing speeds increased by 10 feet. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

At 15th level you learn to channel your divine power and primal fury to others. As a bonus action, you unleash a primal roar infused with divine energy. Creatures of your choice up to half your paladin level (including yourself) within 40 feet of you that can hear you gain advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next turn. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your charisma modifier per long rest.
At 20th level you have learned how to fully master the beast inside. You can use your action to perform one of the following options for 1 hour:

You have resistance to nonmagical slashing, piercing, and bludgeoning damage from non-silvered weapons. You gain a +1 bonus to ac while not wearing heavy armor. You gain 5d8 + your Paladin Level temporary hit points.

You grant one willing creature resistance to nonmagical slashing, piercing, and bludgeoning damage from non-silvered weapons, a +1 bonus to ac while not wearing heavy armor, and 5d8 + your Paladin Level temporary hit points. This effect ends early if you are incapacitated or die. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

You have given yourself to a cause of protection, to watch over a person, place, or thing until your dying breath. Their loyalty to their cause knows no bounds, and their patience is unending as they wait for a threat to arise. The few who take the Oath of the Sentinel are the most devout people that one would ever meet, almost machine-like in their duties. Paladins of this nature are most often found serving a monarch or other important political figure, guarding a vault or sacred object, or watching over a plot of holy land. In addition to their loyalty, the amount of power they have to muster to perform their duties is legendary even among other paladins. A paladin who has sworn this oath cannot ever falter in their watch. A single rest could spell doom for a countless number of innocents, regardless of the length. TENETS OF THE SENTINEL Though the exact words and strictures of the Oath of the Sentinel vary, paladins of this oath share these tenets. Lead from the Front. Go gallantly and willingly to the front lines, placing yourself in danger to stir the hearts and minds of your companions. You need no standard-bearer; be the standard that draws the eyes of enemies and allies alike to the thickest part of the battle. Be Ever Prepared. Your enemy never rests, but you must never be unable to answer the call. Abstain from drink, and gluttony. Keep your body strong, and your will unbreakable. Comrades Before Oneself. A soldier alone is merely a soldier; many soldiers together are a force to be reckoned with. You are nothing without your comrades in arms; you must put the well-being and safety of your battle companions before your own, and when an ally falls, it is your duty to pick them up and carry them to safety if need be. Defense for All. Those who are living be able to live and be free from the fear of the uncertain as they deserve to until the end. Features: 3rd Level - Channel Divinity 3rd Level - Oath Spells 7th Level - Aura of Obstruction 15th Level - Custodian's Directive 20th Level - Unfelled Bastion
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

When you or a friendly creature within 60 feet of you takes damage, you can absorb the energy using a reaction and a use of your Channel Divinity. You reduce the damage taken by an amount equal to five times your paladin level. The first time you hit with a melee attack, you deal extra force damage equal to half of the damage mitigated.
You can use your action or bonus action and a use of your Channel Divinity to don on armor you are proficient in that you can see within 30 feet of you. You must have worn the armor before.

You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed. Oath of the Sentinel Spells​ Paladin Level Spells 3rd alarm, sanctuary 5th ray of enfeeblement, spiritual weapon 9th protection from energy, slow 13th guardian of faith, otiluke's resilient sphere 17th antilife shell, wall of light

Starting at 7th level, you constantly emanate a compelling force around you. Hostile creatures treat the area within 10 feet of you as difficult terrain. If those creatures attempt to leave the aura, they are forced to make a Charisma saving throw. On a fail, they take radiant damage equal to your paladin level and the force prevents them from leaving and can only move within the aura. Those creatures that are subjected to teleportation or planar travel out of the aura must also make the save, being unable to teleport or planar travel on a fail. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

At 15th level, the first time you deal radiant damage on a turn, you can deal additional radiant damage equal to your proficiency bonus. If the target is an undead or fiend, they take double the amount of damage from this feature. The damage dealt by this feature bypasses resistances.

At 20th level, you take a stand as a sentry that fights against all you deem an enemy. As an action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute: Your speed becomes 0. In exchange, you can hover and can use your bonus action to teleport to a location that you can see within 30 feet of you. The reach of all your melee attacks extends up to 30 feet of you as a beam of energy reaches your targets instead. You can use this extended reach for purposes like opportunity attacks or other abilities. When you hit with attacks that are beyond your weapon's original reach, the damage dealt is radiant damage instead of the weapon's damage. You can't be grappled, petrified knocked prone, restrained, or stunned. Once you use this action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.
Features: 3rd Level - Channel Divinity 3rd Level - Oath Spells 7th Level - Aura of the Steelsoul 15th Level - Immovable Stance 20th Level - Steelsoul Empyrean
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.
As a bonus action, your proficiency bonus increases by 1 for one minute.

When you suffer an effect that requires you to make a saving throw at the end of your turn to end the effect, you can use your reaction to enter a focused state for 1 minute. While in this focused state you make end of turn saving throws at the beginning of your turn, instead of at the end. This saving throw is made with advantage.

You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed. Paladin Level Spells 3rd Protection from Evil and Good, Shield 5th Spiritual Weapon, Warding Bond 9th Dispel Magic, Water Walk 13th Freedom of Movement, Otiluke's Resilient Sphere 17th Greater Restoration, Skill Empowerment

At 7th level, when you or any creature of your choice within 10 feet of you take damage, that damage is reduced by an amount equal to your Charisma modifier(minimum of 1, maximum of 5). At 18th level, this aura increases in range up to 30 feet.

Starting at 15th level, you are immune to effects that would knock you prone. If an effect moves you against your will along the ground(like being pushed or pulled), the distance you are moved is reduced by up to 10 feet. Alternatively, you can use a reaction to reduce the distance you are moved by up to 30 feet.

Starting at 20th level, as an action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute: You gain 100 temporary hit points. Any attack roll that isn't against you has disadvantage on any creature of your choice within 30 feet of you. When a creature hits you with a melee attack, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become stunned until the end of its next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Paladins who swear the Oath of the Stormborn wield the fury of the heavens, channeling thunder and lightning as both shield and hammer. They are relentless warriors of the storm, striking down foes with divine force and protecting those caught in the tempest of war. Tenets of the Stormborn Thunder’s Wrath: Let your enemies tremble before the storm’s fury. Strike down oppressors with righteous force. Storm’s Shelter: Like the eye of the hurricane, you are a protector. Stand firm as a shield for the innocent. Unbreakable Tempest: The storm does not yield; neither shall you. Remain steadfast in your convictions. Sky’s Judgment: Let the wicked know there is no escape from the storm’s retribution. Features: 3rd Level - Stormborn Oath Spells 3rd Level - Channel Divinity 7th Level - Thunder's Fury 7th Level - Aura of the Tempest 15th Level - Stormforged Arsenal 20th Level - Ascension of the Stormlord

Paladin Level | Spells 3rd | Thunderwave, Fog Cloud 5th | Shatter, Gust of Wind 9th | Call Lightning, Fly 13th | Storm Sphere, Freedom of Movement 17th | Destructive Wave (thunder/lightning), Control Winds

You summon a weapon bound to your soul, a conduit of the storm’s might. You can summon or dismiss your Thunderbound Weapon as a bonus action. Your Thunderbound Weapon must be a warhammer, battleaxe, greataxe, or maul. You can spend 1 hour binding a magical weapon to make it your Thunderbound Weapon. When using Divine Smite, you can choose to deal radiant, thunder, or lightning damage, the damage type is chosen whenever you use the Thunderbound weapon Channel divinity. This also applies to Improved Divine Smite. The weapon deals 1d8 Additional thunder or lighting damage.

You can cast Witch Bolt without expending a spell slot. This version: Deals thunder damage instead of lightning. Automatically casts at the highest level available for a Paladin spell slot you have (up to 5th).
Your Thunderbound Weapon becomes magical for the purpose overcoming resistance.

The storm’s energy crackles around you, offering both protection and retribution. You and allies within 10 feet gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage. Additionally once per turn when an enemy within 10 feet of you attacks an ally, you can, deal 1d8 thunder damage to the attacker and push the attacker 10 feet away from you. At 18th level, the aura increases to 30 feet.

Your Thunderbound Weapon becomes an extension of the storm’s fury gaining the following benefits: It gains the Thrown property and magically returns to your hand after an attack. You can Divine Smite on ranged (thrown) attacks made with your thunderbound weapon Versatile weapons (warhammer, battleaxe) have a thrown range of 30/60 feet. Heavy weapons (greataxe, maul) have a thrown range of 15/30 feet.

For 1 minute, you become a living storm, gaining the following benefits: You gain a flying speed of 60 feet and hover. Storm Strikes: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with your thunderbound weapon, you can cause a concussive thunder to explode on the target. You force them to make constitution saving thrown. On a failed save they attacked is incapacitated until the start of your next turn. If they fail the save by more than 5 they are instead stunned. Additional a bolt of lightning arcs to another creature of your choice within 30 feet, forcing the creature to make dexterity saving thrown, dealing 4d10 lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a save. You also become immune to lighting and thunder damage for the duration Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest or expend a 5th-level spell slot.

In the darkest of times, when evil looms on the horizon and hope seems but a fleeting whisper, the Valiant Guardians rise. These Paladins are the beacons of courage, the bulwarks against despair, and the heralds of victory. They swear an oath not just to protect, but to inspire, lead, and become the legends that songs are sung about. Their deeds are the stories that will be told for generations, for they are the embodiment of heroism itself. Features: 3rd level - Channel Divinity: Valiant Guardian 3rd Level - Oath Spells: Valiant Guardian 7th Level - Aura of Mighty Deeds 15th Level - Never surrender! 20th Level - A True Hero
