As a bonus action you can use your Channel Divinity to instantly teleport willing creatures within 60 feet of you to within 10 feet of yourself. The number of creatures you can teleport is equal to your Charisma Modifier (minimum of 1).
You can use your Channel Divinity to augment your influence on those around you with divine favor. As a bonus action, you gain advantage on all Charisma checks for the next 10 minutes.

You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed. Oath of the Valiant Guardian Spells Paladin Level - Spells 3rd - Expeditious Retreat, Heroism 5th - Enhance Ability, Enthrall 9th - Haste, Protection from Energy 13th - Freedom of Movement, Compulsion 17th - Commune, Steel Wind Strike

At 7th level, you build divine favor through your heroic deeds, for every hostile creature within 10 feet of you, you gain a +1 bonus to your AC, the bonus cannot exceed your Charisma Modifier. In addition non-hostile creatures already inside your Aura of Mighty Deeds when you use the To Me! Channel Divinity can make a weapon attack as a reaction against a foe within their range before or after teleporting to you. At 18th level, this aura increases in range up to 30 feet.

At 15th level, your actions on the battlefield can supernaturally bolster your allies and demoralize your enemies. Whenever you score a critical hit or reduce a creature to 0 hit points, you can choose one or more creatures that you can see within 30 feet of you, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). All the chosen creatures are affected by one of the following effects of your choice. The creature gains temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + your Charisma modifier. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be frightened of you until the start of your next turn. Once you use this feature you can't use it again until the start of your next turn.

Starting at 20th level, you take on the visage of an ageless hero, breathing life into your companions, and possibly turning the tides of battle. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 10 minutes. Once on each of your turns when you use your Divine Smite feature, instead of dealing smite damage to the enemy you hit, you can heal a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see for the amount of damage you would have dealt with the smite. Your presence in battle is overwhelming causing your opponents to focus their attention on you. When an attack is made against a friendly creature that you can see, if they or the attacker is within 10 feet of you, the attacker has disadvantage on attack rolls made against them. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest

Oracles are seers, soothsayers, and augurs, glimpsing into the future and oftentimes attempting to shape it. Whether your goal lies in preventing horrid events or keeping the future pure and unadulterated, an oracle bears the responsibility of influencing fate itself.
At 3rd level, you are able to predict the future to an extent. You can cast augury at will, using your spiritual focus in place of material components.

At 3rd level, you can subtly tug on the strings of fate to lessen the burden on your allies. Whenever you activate your spirit tether, you can choose whether to deal damage to a target or give them an equal amount of temporary hit points. These temporary hit points disappear if the tether breaks.

Also at 3rd level, you gain access to new spirit arts that reflect your ability to shape the future. Predestined Strike​ When your linked target hits with an attack, you can use your reaction to spend 1 spirit point and choose between these options: Fortune. Roll a d20. On a roll of 10 or above, the attack becomes a critical hit. Disaster. Roll a d20. On a roll of 10 or below, the attack becomes a critical miss. Eyes of Prescience​ You can use an action and spend 1 spirit point to forsee any harm that might befall your target. Choose between these options: Fortune. Until the beginning of your next turn, attack rolls against your target have disadvantage and the target makes Dexterity saving throws with advantage. Disaster. Until the beginning of your next turn, the first attack roll against your target each turn has advantage. Rewound Wounds​ When you activate your spirit tether, you can spend 1 spirit point to use the following effects: Fortune. If your target has taken damage within the last round, you can restore their hit points equal to 2d6 + your wisdom modifier, up to the total damage taken. Disaster. If your target has had hit points restored or has gained temporary hit points within the last round, you can deal necrotic damage equal to 2d6 + your wisdom modifier up to the amount healed or the temporary hit points gained.

At 6th level, your experience with fortune telling allows you to gain a deeper insight into the emotional states of others. While tethered to a creature, you gain an understand of their emotions, giving you insight into fine details. You know how they feel about their current situation, how they react to events that transpire around them, and are able to recognize how they feel about other people, yourself included.

At 13th level, fate bows to your will. If you or an ally within 30 feet misses with an attack roll or fails an ability check or saving throw, you can use your reaction to allow that ally to reroll, potentially succeeding. The ally must use the new roll. You can only use this feature once per short rest, unless you spend 3 spirit points to use it again.

At 18th level, you master your influnece over controlling fate. You learn the following spirit art: Divergence​ If your tethered target becomes critical (10% or fewer hit points) or dies, you can use your reaction to spend 5 spirit points and use one of the following effects: Fortune. You can shift fate so that such an event never occured. If dead, the target is brought back to life, all conditions on the tethered target are ended, and it regains 50 hit points. Disaster. You can use the event to spell disaster for enemies. Tethered targets of your choice take 50 force damage and must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be stunned. If this damage reduces the target to 0 hit points, the target is disintegrated along with every nonmagical object it is wearing or carrying. Each successful use of this spirit art each day increases its chance to fail by 33%. After three sucessful uses of this spirit art, further uses will fail automatically.

Those who enter the order of the symbiote are either a crazed or brave few. Taking in a new being into their own during an induction to hemocraft, they are able to tap into a special power granted by being now two halves of a greater whole. Whether the symbiote be embedded within their flesh, or coiling around their skin, as this new creature's host the Blood Hunters of this order boast an unmatched ability to tear down the biologies of those they may face. Features 3rd Level - Rite of the Blighted 3rd Level - Symbiotic Awareness 7th Level - Infected Exposure 7th Level - Brand of Contagion 11th Level - Mutualistic Host 15th Level - Walking Dead 18th Level - Blood Curse of Lethality

When you join this order at 3rd level, you learn the rite of the blighted as part of your crimson rite features. When you activate the rite of the blighted, the extra damage dealt is poison damage. Additionally, hitting a creature with a weapon infused with this rite that is neither undead or a construct deals extra poison damage equal to your hemocraft modifier.

A limited consciousness within your symbiote grants you an increased perception of your surroundings. You gain proficiency in the perception skill. Additionally, you may add your hemocraft modifier to your initiative rolls.

At 7th level you know the Blood Curse of Exposure, which does not count towards your total number of blood curses known, and its potential rises to great power in combination with your toxins. If you apply your Blood Curse of Exposure to a creature after dealing poison damage from your Rite of the Blighted, the curse will instead last for 1 minute. If you have amplified the curse, you take damage equal to a roll of your hemocraft die at the start of each of your turns in exchange for your symbiote sustaining the infection. If you already know the Blood Curse of Exposure, you may learn a different blood curse of your choice that you qualify for.

At 7th level, when you apply your Brand of Castigation to a creature while you have your Rite of the Blighted active, you may choose to inflict the target with a virulent infection. The target must succeed a constitution saving throw or experience one of the following effects, as determined by rolling your hemocraft die. Hemocraft Die Roll Effect 1 The target becomes Poisoned for 1 minute, and can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, expelling the poison on a successful save. 2 A wave of weakness falls over the target. All attack rolls have advantage against the target until the start of its next turn. 3 Your opponent's blood mixes with your symbiote, allowing a temporary breach in their immune system. The next blood curse you apply to that target within 1 minute that requires a saving throw will take effect regardless of whether or not their saving throw is successful or not. 4 A mild paralytic compound infuses itself within the target, reducing all of its speeds by 10 ft for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. 5 The toxins of your weapon attack invade the target's mind, causing them to make concentration saves at disadvantage until the start of your next turn. 6 Your target has its physical attributes ravaged to some degree. The target suffers a penalty to all Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution Checks and Saving throws equal to your hemocraft die until the end of its next turn. 7 Your target's vision fogs temporarily, causing them to become Blinded until the end of its next turn. 8 Toxins invade your target's body entirely, causing their muscles to lock. The target is Paralyzed until the end of its next turn. 9 An increased spike in potency causes your rite to deliver vastly increased lethality. For one minute, your Rite of the Blighted deals extra damage equal to three rolls of your hemocraft die instead of one. 10 Toxins manage to tear into your target regardless of their biologies. The target loses all resistance and immunity to poison damage for 1 minute, gaining vulnerability instead. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a successful save. Effects listed under a higher number than you can roll with your hemocraft die remain inaccessible until a level in which you can.

Starting at 11th level, your symbiote is able to grant you a further boon to your health. Whenever an effect would restore your hit points, you regain an additional amount of hit points equal to a roll of your hemocraft die. Additionally, you learn the druidcraft cantrip. Your hemocraft ability is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

At 15th Level, If you are reduced to 0 hit points, your symbiote may assume control over your basic motor functions for a limited time in order to protect you. During this time you experience the following: Your speed is halved You cannot use your extra attack feature You cannot take reactions You Still make Death Saving Throws at the start of each of your turns You suffer the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points The symbiote can maintain its control for a number of rounds equal to your hemocraft modifier (minimum of one), until you die, or until you regain at least one hit point. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

At 18th level, your symbiotic connection grants you the ability to entirely ravage a creature's health. You gain the Blood Curse of Lethality for your Blood Maledict feature. This doesn’t count against your number of blood curses known. Blood Curse of Lethality - When you hit a creature with a weapon infused with your Rite of the Blighted, you may choose to apply this Blood Curse. The target must make a constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 8d8 poison damage and suffers a random effect of your Brand of Contagion. The target takes half as much damage on a successful save and suffers no other effects. Amplify - Amplifying this curse will instead reduce the target's hit points to 1 should they fail the saving throw, and take the full 8d8 poison damage on a success.

Barbarian Primal Path “Ye don’t fight the enemy so much as let the enemy fight ye — and lose.” Dwarven warriors in the tradition of Thibbledorf Pwent’s Gutbuster Brigade, who wear brutal spiked armor and crush their foes in a bristling, bloody embrace. Features: 3rd Level - Spiked Armor 6th Level - The Gutbuster Draught 10th Level - Bloodied Iron 14th Level - Battlerager Ascendant

All of this path’s features require you to be wearing spiked armor. Its gauntlets and plates let you make unarmed strikes as simple melee weapons, the gauntlets can be chosen as weapon mastery chosen and have the vex weapon mastery, dealing piercing damage equal to the Unarmed Strike Die on the table below plus your Strength modifier, instead of the normal bludgeoning damage. Your Spike Damage is a separate flat value of piercing damage used by Impaling Grip, shown in the table’s third column. Battlerager Defense. While wearing spiked armor, you use your Constitution modifier instead of Dexterity to determine its AC. This bonus can exceed the armor’s normal +2 limit, up to a maximum equal to your Rage Damage bonus. While wearing the armor and raging: Impaling Grip. While you have a creature grappled, it takes the spike damage below at the start of each of its turns. Likewise, when a creature within 5 feet grapples you or hits you with a melee attack, it takes that same spike damage. A creature can take this spike damage only once per turn. Barbarian Level Unarmed Strike Die Spike Damage 3 1d4 Str modifier 6 1d6 Str modifier 10 1d8 (magical) Str modifier + Rage Damage bonus 14 1d10 (magical) Str modifier + Rage bonus + Con modifier

A foul, potent dwarven spirit that burns away fear. When you enter a Rage, you can drink a draught as part of that same bonus action. You can do this twice per long rest (twice per short rest at 14th level). Until that Rage ends: You can make an unarmed strike as a bonus action on each of your turns. Gain temporary hit points equal to your Barbarian level. Advantage on saves against being frightened and charmed. Additional you are immune to poison for the duration as the deaught burns away any other foreign substances. Your spike damage increases by 1d6 while a creature is grappled by you. The Crash. When that Rage ends, the spirit hits back. Make a Constitution saving throw (DC 15). On a failure, you are incapacitated until the end of your next turn as the frenzy leaves your body. The saving throw DC is 15 for the first use and 20 for the second, resetting when your uses reset. Not for the faint of gut. If anyone who isn’t a Battlerager drinks a draught, they must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or fall incapacitated for 1 minute. On a success, nothing happens beyond a vile taste in their mouth. You gain proficiency in the use of Brewers Supplies.

Your spiked armor is now wreathed in primal fury. Your gauntlet strikes and spike damage count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity, and the spike damage rises to Str modifier + Rage Damage bonus (as shown on the table). While raging, you also can’t be frightened. Terrifying Frenzy. Whenever you score a critical hit with an unarmed strike while raging, each enemy within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn any creature grappled by you as disadvantage on the saving throw..

While raging: When a creature within 5 feet hits you with a melee attack or grapples you, you can use your reaction to make one unarmed strike against it. You can grapple creatures 2 sizes bigger than you. A creature you have grappled takes your spike damage at the start of and end of its turn, making your embrace a genuine death grip. Your Spike Damage adds your Constitution modifier, as shown on the table. (Your unarmed strikes still add only your Strength modifier.)

A Subclass of Barbarian that focus on unarmed fighting Features: 3rd Level - Unarmed Combatant 3rd Level - Brawler's Prowess 6th Level - Reactive Fighting 6th Level - Packin' Heat 10th Level - Fearsome Critical 14th Level - Brawler's Focus

At level 3, your strength and general martial prowess increase the damage that you do with your bare fists. When you make an unarmed strike, your damage becomes 1d4 + your STR modifier. The damage dice increase with each level in this subclass, to become 1d6 at level 6, 1d8 at level 10 and finally 1d10 at level 14.

At level 3, While Raging, you gain new options to use as bonus actions, as long as you are not wielding any weapons or a shield. Block: While raging, you can use your bonus action to raise your arms in a defensive stance. This gives you an AC boost of +2 until the start of your next turn. At level 10, this AC boost becomes +3 Jab: While raging, you can use your bonus action to make an unarmed strike against a target.
At level 6, while you are raging, when a creature attacks you and they are within 5 feet of you, you can make an unarmed strike against that creature as a reaction.
At level 6, your unarmed strikes can even inflict damage on the toughest of foes, your unarmed strikes become magical for the purpose of overcoming non-magical resistance and immunity.

At level 10, when you score a Critical hit on a Target with your unarmed strike, you can apply brutal critical to your unarmed strike. Additionally when you score a critical hit on a target, they must save a Constitution saving throw against your save DC (8 + proficiency + strength bonus) or be frightened by you until the end of their next turn.

At level 14, while you are raging and you have only one creature within 20 feet of you, that creature has your undivided attention. You are in the "zone". You can make attacks against them with adv, and any wisdom saves they force you to make, are made with adv. While in the zone, if they try to leave your melee range, your Attack of Opportunity has the ability to stop them in their tracks, reducing their move speed to zero if they fail a strength save against your save DC (8+prof+strength bonus)

Many barbarians never concern themselves with the intricacies of magic, leaving others around them to cast their fancy spells and incantations. A Pact Sealer is no different, however enlisting the aid of a patron to grant them magical capabilities similar to a warlock. These barbarians know as much or as little about these spells as they wish, with their main concern being the power this magic grants them to crush their opponents on the battlefield. Features: 3rd Level - Pact Magic 3rd Level - Raging Focus 3rd Level - Pact Resilience 6th Level - Rage of Hadar 10th Level - Eldritch Invocations 14th Level - Eldritch Frenzy

At 3rd level, you augment your combat techniques with the ability to cast spells. See chapter 10 of the Player’s Handbook for the general rules of spellcasting and chapter 11 of the Player’s Handbook for the warlock spell list.
You learn two cantrips of your choice from the warlock spell list. You learn an additional warlock cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

The Pact Sealer Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have. The table also shows what the level of those slots is; all of your spell slots are the same level. To cast one of your warlock spells of 1st level or higher, you must expend a spell slot. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a short or long rest. For example, when you are 8th level, you have two 2nd-level spell slots. To cast the 1st-level spell witch bolt, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a 2nd-level spell. Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher: At 3rd level, you know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the warlock spell list. The Spells Known column of the Pact Sealer Spellcasting table shows when you learn more warlock spells of your choice of 1st level and higher. A spell you choose must be of a level no higher than what’s shown in the table’s Slot Level column for your level. When you reach 13th level, for example, you learn a new warlock spell, which can be 1st, 2nd, or 3rd level. Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the warlock spells you know and replace it with another spell from the warlock spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Your spellcasting ability is charisma for your warlock spells, so you use your charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a warlock spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

Barbarian Level - Cantrips Known - Spells Known - Spell Slots - Slot Level 3rd - 2 - 2 - 1 - 1st 4th - 2 - 2 - 1 - 1st 5th - 2 - 3 - 1 - 1st 6th - 2 - 3 - 2 - 1st 7th - 2 - 4 - 2 - 2nd 8th - 2 - 4 - 2 - 2nd 9th - 2 - 5 - 2 - 2nd 10th - 3 - 5 - 2 - 2nd 11th - 3 - 6 - 2 - 2nd 12th - 3 - 6 - 2 - 2nd 13th - 3 - 7 - 2 - 3rd 14th - 3 - 7 - 2 - 3rd 15th - 3 - 8 - 2 - 3rd 16th - 3 - 8 - 2 - 3rd 17th - 3 - 9 - 2 - 3rd 18th - 3 - 9 - 2 - 3rd 19th - 3 - 10 - 2 - 4th 20th - 3 - 11 - 2 - 4th

At 3rd level, while raging, you are able to use any simple or martial weapon you are holding as a focus for your Pact Sealer spells In addition, you are able to cast any spell granted by Pact Magic while raging. Doing so requires a successful constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. Starting at 11th level, you can also concentrate on spells granted by Pact Magic.

Determined by the patron you struck a deal with, you are able to gain an additional damage resistance while raging starting at 3rd level. Patron - Damage Type The Archfey - Psychic The Celestial - Radiant The Fathomless - Cold The Fiend - Fire The Genie (Efreeti) - Fire The Genie (Marid) - Cold The Genie (Djinni) - Thunder The Genie (Dao) - Force The Great Old One - Psychic The Hexblade - Force The Undead - Necrotic The Undying - Poison

Starting at 6th level when you rage, once before your rage ends you can use a bonus action to cast the Arms of Hadar spell at the highest level available to you on the Pactsealer table without expending a spell slot.

Starting at 10th level, you may choose 2 of the following invocations. You can choose a third invocation at 14th level. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you may change one of the invocations you selected for another.
When you roll damage for a Pact Magic spell you cast while raging, you can add your rage damage modifier to the damage roll.
While you are raging, you can replace the bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage type of your weapon attacks with that related to your patron.
You cannot be disarmed against your will, and you have advantage on checks made to grapple another creature. Creatures have disadvantage on checks made to escape your grapples.
While raging, you gain a flying speed of 30 feet.

When you take damage of the type corresponding to your patron, you can use your reaction to instead become immune to the damage until the start of your next turn. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus before taking a long rest.
You gain Darkvision out to a range of 120ft. Additionally, magical darkness does not impede your darkvision.

As an action, you can bolster your natural regeneration. Doing so will cause you to regain hit points equal to 5 + your constitution modifier at the start of each of your turns for 1 minute. You cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.
You gain proficiency in the athletics and acrobatics skills.
You can cast haste once using a pact slot. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.
You can cast Blinding Smite once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.
You can cast Blink once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.
When you score a critical hit against an enemy, you can recover one of your pact slots. You cannot restore another slot in this way until you finish a short rest

A warrior who presents time in the way it was meant to be, a torrent of destruction. Barbarians who follow the Path of The Ravager use the breakage of time as their weapon, devastating enemies with powerful attacks with lasting impact. Features: 3rd Level - Filling The Hourglass 3rd Level - Ravaging Strike 6th Level - Chronometry 10th Level - Cadence 14th Level - Time Templar 14th Level - Clockbreaker

Starting at 3rd Level, you learn to extract a portion of a creature's lifespan from within the moments spent interacting with them. You extract a Grain of Time from a creature you land a critical hit against. Additionally you can touch the body of a creature you damaged in the last minute as a bonus action draining a portion of the time you stole gaining a Grain of Time. You can store a number of Grains of Time equal to twice your proficiency bonus. When rolling initiative you lose all Grains of Time you currently hold. Furthermore you can consume a Grain of Time as bonus action to heal your injuries, when doing so you regain a number of hit points equal to half your Barbarian level.

Starting at 3rd Level, you learn a powerful attack that allows you to drain time itself. As an action while raging you may make a melee weapon with your weapon. On a hit, you can expend Grains of Time to deal an additional number of d8s equal to the number of Grains of Time spent necrotic damage. The creature is then afflicted with the Time Ravaged condition for 1 minute upon a failed Charisma Saving Throw, save dc equal to 8+your proficiency bonus+your Constitution modifier. A creature afflicted with the Time Ravaged condition takes 1d4 (6th Level (2d4), 10th Level (3d4), and 14th Level (4d4) necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns as you siphon grains of its future. As an action, the creature or an ally within its reach can disrupt the siphon, ending the Time Ravaged condition.
Starting at 6th Level when taking the attack action you may use a Ravaging Strike in place of one of those attacks. Additionally, your Ravaging Strikes crit on a 19-20.

Starting at 10th Level The first time an enemy fails the saving throw for becoming time ravaged, they are also stunned until the end of your next turn. Additionally you are resistant to necrotic damage, and immune to being magically aged, and you may use a Grain of Time as an action to gain another month on your natural lifespan.
Beginning at 14th Level due to your mastery over time after rolling initiative you only lose half the Grains of Time you have stored.

Starting at 14th Level when your Ravaging Strikes or the Time Ravaged condition reduces a creature to 0hp, you disintegrate them into sand, gaining an additional Grain of Time. Furthermore, you can make an additional Ravaging Strike as a Bonus Action.

A Phalanx draws their strength from their allies and coordination. Phalanx make excellent commanders as their leadership and guidance helps to assure not only their own success, but their entire unit’s as well. Features: 3rd Level - Tactical Commander 3rd Level - Unbreakable Formation 7th Level - Tactical Authority 13th Level - Perfect Block 18th Level - Battle Tide

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain access to your cohesion die, which is a d4. Other features will refer to your cohesion die, and will allow you to roll it. Your cohesion die is not expended when rolled. Your cohesion die increases to a d6 at 7th level, to a d8 at 13th, and to a d10 at 18th.

Additionally at 3rd level, you learn to weave your own defenses into those around you, resulting in a stronger whole for both you and your allies. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you gains a bonus to saving throws equal to one roll of your cohesion die. Additionally, creatures of your choice that start their turn within that range gain a +1 bonus to their armor class for each creature within 10 feet of you, with a maximum bonus equal to half your proficiency bonus.

At 7th level, you gain the ability to have greater control over how a fight will play out. When you enter your defensive stance, choose either the dodge, disengage, or dash action. Creatures of your choice within 5 feet of you while your stance is active will be unable to take the chosen action. You may select a new action from the specified list at the start of each of your turns until your stance ends (no action required). Additionally, creatures of your choice within the same range (other than you) gain a bonus to damage rolls equal to a roll of your cohesion die. They can use this bonus no more than once per turn.

Your ability to use shields extends to protecting your allies as well as you beginning at 13th level. When an ally within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to give them a bonus to their armor class equal to one roll of your cohesion die. If this bonus causes the attack to miss, you may use this reaction again, even if you have already used your reaction this round.

When you reach 18th level, your ability to shift the tide of battle with your presence alone has been realized. As an action, you can grant each creature of your choice within 20 feet of you temporary hit points equal to twice your Bulwark level, and remove all conditions of your choice from them. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

A sage who focuses on refining their own mind to fully control the magic they wield. Such arcanists hold themselves to particularly high degrees of perfection, allowing little room for failure even among the most basic of tasks. Their work in achieving this perfection however is reflected in full by their arcane mastery.
Meticulous work has gone into perfecting your spellcasting. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that deals damage, you may treat a roll of 1 on any damage die as a 2.
Through your constant work, your mental fortitude is nigh unbreakable. At 6th level, you gain proficiency in Charisma saving throws.

At 10th level, you can further shape your spells to reflect your diligence. When you cast a focused spell, it ignores a target’s resistance to damage. You also gain the following Mind Shape, which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:
When you roll damage with the spell, you can treat a dice roll of one below its maximum amount as its maximum amount.

At 14th level, control over your spells has given you a large degree of control over their success. When you cast a spell that requires you to make a check using your spellcasting ability, you can treat any d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10. Additionally, your Quality Spellcasting feature now treats a roll of 1 or 2 on any damage die as a 3.

At 18th level, your mastery over your very mind has granted you the power to exert your will on others to a greater, and invariable effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against one of your focused spells, you can choose to make them fail instead. Alternatively, if you miss on an attack roll with a focused spell, you can cause the attack to hit instead. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

Sages who follow this philosophy, often called “Blue Mages” due to the color of the robes many traditionally wear, embody the ever-flowing state of the world and others, taking that change into themselves and granting them the uncanny ability to adapt their very beings into something that can at times be completely unrecognizable. Class features: 2nd Level - Bonus Proficiencies 2nd Level - Azure Lores 6th Level - Flesh Writer 10th Level - Shaper of Evolution 14th Level - Hardened Study 18th Level - Ever-Evolving

When you select this study at 2nd level, you gain proficiency with longswords and scimitars, as well as the survival and nature skills. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any check you make that uses either of those skills.

Additionally at 2nd level, you begin to uncover the ability to fundamentally change yourself in order to accommodate your continually evolving magic, starting with the ability to take the abilities of the monsters you face, using them as your own. When you are targeted by a creature’s ability that does not originate from a weapon attack, spell, legendary action, or lair action, you can attempt to tap into a deeper understanding of it, and combine it with yourself. If you do so, any attack roll that is part of the ability automatically hits you, and any saving throw is automatically failed. Immediately after the effects are resolved, you may make a wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + the creature’s proficiency bonus + the creature’s constitution modifier). On a success, you may add the ability to your collection of Azure Lore, unless the creature’s challenge rating is higher than your sage level. You may only learn one Azure Lore ability per individual creature. Whenever you use your Meditation feature to replace a spell that you know, you may replace it with one of your Azure Lore abilities. You can cast the ability as a spell, expending a spell slot of a level determined by the challenge rating of the creature. You automatically have any cantrip-level ability you gain through this feature available when you learn it. Follow Link to view Table Challenge Rating Spell Slot Level < 1 Cantrip 1 - 3 1st 4 - 5 2nd 6 - 7 3rd 8 - 9 4th 10 - 11 5th 12 - 13 6th 14 - 15 7th 16 - 17 8th 18 - 20 9th Casting the spell requires Somatic components, but not Verbal or Material, and has a casting time equal to the action it took the original creature. If the ability has a recharge condition, you must meet that condition before you are able to cast that Azure Lore ability again. You may place mind shapes on your Azure Lore abilities as normal when you gain that feature at 3rd Level.

When you reach 6th level, you unlock the ability to tap into the abilities of the fallen and dead creatures you encounter. You may spend ten minutes while in contact with the corpse of a creature to attempt to absorb one of the abilities that it had in life. After the ritual has been completed, make a wisdom saving throw (DC 12 + the creature’s proficiency bonus + the creature’s constitution modifier). On a success, you may choose a single special trait from the creature to add to yourself. On a success or failure, you cannot use that corpse again to gain abilities through this feature. The added trait cannot be Legendary Resistance or Limited Magic Immunity. Once you add a trait to yourself, it cannot be removed by any means short of giving up the knowledge of the trait, which you can do as an action. You can maintain a number of these traits equal to your wisdom modifier. If you try to assimilate more traits than your maximum would allow, you may choose to give up one of your current traits for the new one.

At 10th level, your spells shift to better reflect the evolution that you yourself have undergone. When you cast any of your Azure Lore skills as Focused Spells, you may expend one spell slot level lower than you normally would need to (minimum of 1st level). You also gain the following Mind Shape, which can be placed on your focused spells as normal: Evolving: You can cast this spell as a reaction to a creature you can see within 60 feet of you ending their turn.

When you reach 14th level, you no longer need to completely lower your defenses in order to intertwine your understanding of the abilities of others. When you attempt to learn an Azure Lore ability, attack rolls no longer automatically hit you, and you no longer automatically fail saving throws.

Normal physical limits no longer apply to the abilities you learn from your Azure Lore feature when you reach 18th level. You are now able to copy natural weapons, and Legendary Actions that target you. If you cast a creature’s Legendary Action as a spell, it takes an action to do so.

There are ways of thinking that are often called incorrect by many, exhibiting illogical methods, or even simply being incorrect. However, certain Sages can utilize these ways of thinking in shaping their magic into something truly bizarre.

The spells you cast carry the capacity to trick the very weave itself into allowing extra magic to be cast. When you cast a focused spell by expending a spell slot of first level or higher, the next time you or a creature within 30 feet of you casts that same spell at the same level before the start of your next turn, they do so without expending a spell slot, so long as the spell is of 5th level or lower.

Your illogical reasoning extends far enough to prevent harm to you, though opening you to potentially greater damage. Starting at 6th level, as a reaction when you take damage, you can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you, creating an illusory copy to take the damage instead. If you take damage from any source before the start of your next turn, you are vulnerable to that damage.

At 10th level, you can further shape your spells to your own fallacy. When a creature casts one of your focused spells that benefits from your [Bandwagon] feature, that creature gets advantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw they make within the next minute. You also gain the following Mind Shape, which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:
When you cast the spell, you can choose to have it not take effect until you cast your next spell.

You learn to use your thoughts to distract those around you at 14th level. When a creature within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the roll. If the creature fails their ability check, saving throw, or attack roll, it takes psychic damage equal to half your sage level. If it succeeds, you take the damage instead. You can do so a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all uses after you finish a long rest.

At 18th level, you gain the ability to turn other’s perceptions to better serve your spellcasting, and at a heavy detriment to them. As an action, you can force a creature within 60 feet of you to make a charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature will willingly fail any saving throw against your sage spells, and is no longer considered willing for beneficial effects from allies. This effect lasts for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

Those who undertake the Philosophy of Finality hold the understanding that all things must come to their eventual end. Inclusive of their foes, and themselves. A Sage who follows this study may work to bring, delay, or even stop the meddling with of such events. Regardless of how these Sage’s may work, they have a full understanding that it cannot, and will not last forever.

As your pool of magic runs out, you manage to extort additional power drawing from its end. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher, and expend the last spell slot of a given level, you gain a bonus to one damage roll equal to 2d8.

At 6th level, lasting harmful effects are far less effective against you, as your understanding forces them to end. When you are targeted by a harmful effect with a duration of one minute or longer, you can choose to end the effect at the end of your next turn (no action required). Once you do so, you cannot do so again until you complete a short or long rest.

At 10th level, your spells reflect the absolute finality that shapes your spells. When a focused spell ends on a creature, you can choose to end all beneficial or detrimental effects currently affecting them. You also gain the following Mind Shape, which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:

If the spell causes a creature to be reduced to 0 hit points, it does not consume a spell slot. Once your denying spell prevents a spell slot from being expended, it cannot do so again until you create a new denying spell.

Your understanding of the end of all around you can allow you to bring it to the present instantly, empowering you in the process. At 14th level, you learn the Dispel Magic spell if you don’t already know it. You cannot replace this spell through meditation, and it does not count towards the total number of spells you know. When you successfully end a spell or effect with Dispel Magic, you can use your Last Cast feature on the next spell you cast of 1st level or higher, even if you have spell slots remaining of the level you cast.

At 18th level, the knowledge of your end fuels you to persist should you fall before your time. If you die to any source other than old age, you are returned to life 24 hours later with all of your hit points at the location you died, so long as your soul is able to. If your body was destroyed, a new one is created. Once you are restored to life by this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

There are those who take their connection to magic to a completely higher level, sometimes utilizing understanding through godly entities or beings of similar power. Sages who undertake the Philosophy of Mysticism may work closely with clerics, paladins, or even warlocks to further strengthen their connection to the divine.

When you take this philosophy at 2nd level, you gain a small spark connecting you to a divine entity, granting you enhanced magic. Choose two spells of 1st level from the Cleric or Warlock spell lists. Both spells need not be from the same list. These spells count as sage spells for you, and do not count towards your number of spells learned. If you choose to replace either of these spells through Meditation[1], you can learn a Cleric or Warlock spell of any level of which you have spell slots to cast in its place.

Your spells carry with them the capacity to heal both yourself and your allies. At 6th level, when you cast a sage spell of 1st level or higher that targets either you or an ally, you can cause that creature to restore a number of hit points equal to your sage level. You can do so a number of times equal to your wisdom modifier, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

At 10th level, you can further shape your spells to more closely fit the divinity you follow. When you cast a focused spell from the cleric or warlock spell lists, you can choose to have the spell count as one level higher than the slot used to cast it. In doing so, you can cast no spells other than focused spells for the next minute. You also gain the following Mind Shape[1], which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:
When a celestial, fiend, or undead fails a saving throw against the spell, or are hit with a spell attack roll, they take extra damage equal to half your sage level.

Your mental connections to divine magic have had a profound effect on both your mind and body at 14th level. When you make a charisma check, you can add your wisdom modifier to the total. Additionally, angel or bat wings sprout from your back (your choice) giving you a flying speed of 30 ft. You also gain resistance to radiant damage (if you chose angel wings), or necrotic damage (if you chose bat wings).

At 18th level, your spells carry with them the very essence of the divine entities you’ve spent your life connected with. You gain the following benefits. You can replace the damage type of your focused spells with radiant or necrotic. Celestials, Fiends and Undead have disadvantage on saving throws against your sage spells. When you restore hit points of another creature with a sage spell, you regain hit points equal to half the amount you healed. ↑ 1.0 1.1 Sage

So it is said that with patience comes wisdom. That wisdom can come in the form of great magical power for those who take upon patience into their very being. A sage who has undertaken the philosophy of patience is never the first to start conflict, but is rarely the first to fall as a result of it.
A sage of patience is always prepared should theirs outweigh that of others. As such, you gain proficiency in light armor, medium armor, and shields.

Starting at 2nd level, you gain the ability to enhance your longer lasting spells at the cost of a slower start. When you cast a spell that makes multiple damage rolls, or lasts for multiple rounds, the first damage roll, or damage rolls during the first round, have all damage dice treated as their lowest value. In return, the last damage roll, or damage rolls during the final round, have all damage dice treated as their highest amount.

Your spells open a window of clarity to you, allowing you to avoid harm for a short time immediately after casting them. Starting at 6th level, you can take the dodge action as a bonus action if you use your action to cast a sage spell of 1st level or higher.

At 10th level, your spells further evolve to reflect your patience. When you cast a focused spell, you gain temporary hit-points equal to your sage level. You also gain the following Mind Shape, which can be placed on your focused spells as normal:
Creatures cannot react to you casting this spell.

While concentrating on spells, both your mind and body become far more rigid. Starting at 14th level, while you maintain concentration on a spell, you gain a +2 bonus to your armor class and saving throws. Your concentration also cannot be broken as a result of taking damage.

At 18th level your patience opens opportunities to you that others could not even hope to achieve. When you roll initiative, you may choose to instead place yourself at initiative 0. If you do so, you may take a second turn immediately after your first turn in the first round of combat.
Features: 1st Level - Ignite 1st Level - Mantle of Flame 6th Level - Phoenix Spark 14th Level - Nourishing Fire 18th Level - Form of the Phoenix

At 1st level, you gain the ability to start fires with a touch. As an action, you can magically ignite a flammable object you touch with your hand—an object such as a torch, a piece of tinder, or the hem of drapes.

Starting at 1st level, you can unleash the phoenix fire that blazes within you. As a bonus action, you magically wreathe yourself in swirling fire, as your eyes glow like hot coals. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits: You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Any creature takes fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier if it hits you with a melee attack from within 5 feet of you or if it touches you. Whenever you roll fire damage on your turn, the roll gains a bonus to equal to your Charisma modifier. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Starting at 6th level, the fiery energy within you grows restless and vengeful. In the face of defeat, it surges outward to preserve you in a fiery roar. If you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to draw on the spark of the phoenix. You are instead reduced to 1 hit point, and each creature within 10 feet of you takes fire damage equal to half your sorcerer level + your Charisma modifier. If you use this feature while under the effects of your Mantle of Flame, this feature instead deals fire damage equal to your sorcerer level + double your Charisma modifier, and your Mantle of Flame immediately ends. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Starting at 14th level, your fire spells soothe and restore you. When you expend a spell slot to cast a spell that includes a fire damage roll, you regain hit points equal to the slot's level + your Charisma modifier.

At 18th level, you finally master the spark of fire that dances within you. While under the effect of your Mantle of Flame feature, you gain additional benefits: You have a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover. You have resistance to Poison & Fire If you use your Phoenix Spark, that feature deals an extra 20 fire damage to each creature.

The world we know has many rules and laws that dictate how it functions. Some explain why the sky is blue, others dictate how things fall, some even to help understand the best trajectory for a bolt or bullet. Regardless of what it may be, a Physicist is a specialized artificer that takes study of these natural laws to even greater lengths than most, learning to exploit them to achieve things previously thought impossible. While they may shy away from a technological side of artifice, make no mistake that the work of physicists is invaluable to almost all fields. Features: 3rd Level - Analytic 3rd Level - Physicist Spells 3rd Level - Experimental Formulas 5th Level - Kinetic Bombard 9th Level - Advanced Formulas 15th Level - Newtonian Defiance
When you choose this specialization at 3rd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) to any Intelligence check you are not already proficient with.

You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Physicist Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

3rd Level: Magnify Gravity, Magic Missile 5th Level: Borrowed Knowledge, Immovable Object 9th Level: Counterspell, Pulse Wave 13th Level: Gravity Sinkhole, Fire Shield 17th Level: Antilife Shell, Telekinesis

Starting at 3rd level, you learn various formulas that can be used to alter or improve your performance. You have a number of experiment points equal to half your artificer level (rounded down) and regain all expended points when you finish a long rest. Alternatively, you can expend a spell slot as an action to regain experiment points equal to the slot's level. You spend experiment points on different formulas, of which you learn three from the following list: Alternate Angle: When you make an attack with a weapon that deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, you can expend one experiment point to change the damage type to a different type from the same list. The attack also deals an extra 3 damage. Thermodynamics: When you take fire or cold damage, you can use your reaction to expend one experiment point to deal half that damage of the opposite type to the creature that dealt the damage to you. Conservation of Energy: When you deal force damage to a creature or object, you can expend one experiment point to deal extra damage equal to half your artificer level. Doing so reduces your speed to 0 until the end of your next turn. Electron Shell: As an action, you can expend one to five experiment points to create a shell around you, which has 4 charges, plus one for every additional point spent. When you take damage, the damage is reduced by the amount of charges, and one is expended. All remaining charges dissipate after one hour. Polarize: When you make an attack or cast a spell that deals damage, you can expend an experiment point to forgo rolling damage to deal the average damage. Applied Science: When you make an ability check, you can expend an experiment point to predict the result before seeing it. If you are correct, you gain a +10 bonus to the roll. If you are within 1, you gain a +5 bonus instead.

Starting at 5th level, you are able to harness the outgoing kinetic energy of attacks. Once per round, when you make a weapon or spell attack, you can increase the damage of the attack by 2d4, this damage is force damage. The damage dealt by this ability increases to 3d4 at 9th level, and to 4d4 at 15th level.

A breakthrough has led to your creation of even further refined formulas. At 9th level you learn two of the following advanced formulas: Genius Precision: When you or a creature you can see within 30 ft of you make an attack roll, you can expend one experiment point to apply your flash of genius to the attack roll. Kinetic Battery: As a bonus action, you can expend one experiment point to begin storing kinetic energy. For every 10 feet you move, you add 1d6 to the total stored kinetic energy, up to 10d6. The next time you damage a creature or object, the target takes damage equal to your kinetic energy. The battery lasts for 1 minute, and if the battery expires before you deal damage, you take force damage equal to your kinetic energy. Meltdown: As an action, you can expend 2 experiment points to deal acid damage to a creature you can see within 60 ft equal to twice the amount of hit dice it has. This formula does not effect targets resistant or immune to acid damage. Super-Magnetism: If a spell or effect you create would move a creature on a failed saving throw, you can expend one experiment point to move the creature even if they succeed. You must use this formula before the creature makes the saving throw.

At 15th level, the natural laws of the world begin to bend at your command. You can cast the following spells with the following changes: Reverse Gravity: The spell has the normal effect, except that you can orient the area in any direction and creatures and objects fall toward the end of the area. Arcane Gate: The portals created by this spell can be oriented in any direction you choose, but must be created flat against a solid surface large enough to hold it. Telekinesis: You can manipulate up to three objects at once. If one of those objects is a weapon, you can attack with that weapon as if you were holding it. You can cast each of these spells once in this way, and must finish a long rest to do so again.

Volatile and dangerous, Powderkegs typically make use of exceedingly dangerous chemicals or magic to act as the ultimate deterrent. Despite this, Bulwarks under this specialization tend to show great care for the power they wield. Features: 3rd Level - Powderkeg Training 3rd Level - Volatile Ward 7th Level - Combustion 13th level - Explosive Ward 18th Level - Fission
When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with firearms and alchemist supplies.

Additionally at 3rd level, you have the ability to work volatile compounds into your armor and defensive strategies. Whenever you use your fortitude feature, the triggering creature takes fire damage equal to your bulwark level.

Starting at 7th level, your knack for mixing potent reactions extends to aid you in combat. While you are holding alchemist supplies and take the attack action, you can replace one attack on each of your turns with a burst of chemical energy. Target a creature within 15 feet of yourself. The target must succeed a Dexterity Saving Throw (DC 8 + your Strength Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d8 damage. This damage is acid, fire or poison (your choice).

When you reach 13th level, you learn to improve your Volatile Ward with even more explosive potential. When you use your Volatile Ward feature, you can choose to have each creature within 20 feet of you take the damage, instead of just the triggering creature. If you do so, the feature deals only half damage.

Starting at 18th level, the explosive potential within you reaches its pinnacle. As an action, you can trigger a chain reaction within your armor to detonate out in a violent burst. You immediately take 20d6 fire damage and 20d6 bludgeoning damage, and each creature within 40 feet of you must succeed a dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Strength Modifier + you Proficiency Bonus) or take the same damage, taking half as much on a successful save. Objects that are not being worn or carried in the area also take this damage. After using this feature, you have immunity to all damage until the end of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

In the silent reaches of wild places and hidden thresholds of civilization, there lies a path few can follow: that of the mind-hunter. The Psi Tracker merges the instincts of the wilderness stalker with the latent power of psionics, becoming a tracker not just of footprints and scent, but of thoughts, memories, and the flicker of intent. What begins as simple survival becomes something far deeper: the Psi Tracker reads the currents of the mind, discerns the trail left by fears and desires, and strikes when prey least expects that the hunter knows their inner terrain. Over long hunts and sustained engagements, the Psi Tracker thrives in drawn-out chases where others would rush to violence. They wear down foes by probing their psyche, disrupting their will, and shifting the battlefield of consciousness. In that way, they become the perfect predator for aberrant threats, whispering shadows of alien thought or intruding into minds as subtly as the wind rustles forest leaves. Their power comes not simply from blade or bow, but from the mind’s edge.

You prefer slow, methodical engagements rather than outright brawls—tracking, disrupting, then striking. You are motivated by uncovering hidden minds, unraveling secrets, and turning that insight into advantage. You wield psionic power as a tool of the hunt: buffing yourself, marking your quarry, and manipulating the mental battlefield before delivering the kill.
documents.s: Potential playstyle & motivations for a Psi Tracker:

documents.t: Players who enjoy a mix of exploration, investigation, and combat—not just shooting arrows but reading intentions. Players drawn to subtle control-effects, debuffs, and layered tactics rather than pure damage output. Players who like characters with a mysterious aura—someone attuned to mental shadows and the unseen.
documents.s: Who would thrive playing this subclass:

documents.t: A ranger whose backstory involves studying strange psychic phenomena, or hunting aberrations that prey on minds. A player comfortable juggling resources (psionic dice) and making choices about when to engage or wear down enemies. A gamer who wants to emphasize role-play of perception, interrogation, and tracking as much as weapon attacks. Features: 3rd Level - Psionic Power 3rd Level - Psychic Spells 7th Level - Empathic Awareness 11th Level - Cognitive Bypass 15th level - Mental Dissonance

Starting at 3rd level, you harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. This energy is represented by your Psionic Energy dice, which are each a d6. You have a number of these dice equal to twice your proficiency bonus, and they fuel various psionic powers you have, which are detailed below. Some of your powers expend the Psionic Energy die they use, as specified in a power's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when your dice are all expended. You regain all your expended Psionic Energy dice when you finish a long rest. In addition, as a bonus action, you can regain one expended Psionic Energy die, but you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest. When you reach certain levels in this class, the size of your Psionic Energy dice increases: at 5th level (d8), 11th level (d10), and 17th level (d12). The powers below use your Psionic Energy dice. Psychic Mark: Whenever you cast Hunters Mark, you can expend a Psionic Energy dice and modify it. When cast in this way, it requires no components and once per turn you can deal additional damage equal to one roll of your Psionic Energy Die when you hit with an attack. Psionic Fortitude: When your nonpsionic training fails you, your psionic power can help: if you fail a saving throw with which you have proficiency, you can roll one Psionic Energy die, adding half the number rolled to the save, potentially turning failure into success. You expend the die only if the roll succeeds.
When you cast a spell from the Conjuration or Transmutation school, you can do so without Verbal or Somatic components.

Starting at 7th level, your psionics have deepened your awareness of the world around you. You can use your action to roll and expend one Psionic Energy die to open your mind to the emotional and mental resonance of your surroundings. For a number of hours equal to the number rolled, you can sense whether any of the following are present within 3 miles of you (or within 1 mile if you are underground), or have been present within a number of days equal to your Wisdom modifier: Intense thoughts or emotions (fear, anger, grief, ecstasy, anxiety) Presence of Intelligent minds (creatures with Intelligence 6 or higher) Psionic or magical phenomena of significant power (DM’s discretion) You learn the direction of each detected source within range, but not its exact distance or number. Additionally, once per use of this feature, you can make a Wisdom (Survival) or Wisdom (Nature) check, with a DC equaling your spell save DC. On a success you learn the distance to one significant location or creature from one of the options above, regardless of distance. If you succeed the check by 5 or more, you learn the distance to a specific location or creature (DM’s discretion), provided you have seen or heard of them before. Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you expend an additional Psionic Energy die to use it again.

When you move, you can temporarily blur the distinction between your body and your psychic echo. When you use the Tireless feature, you can roll and expend up to two Psionic Energy dice and add the number rolled to the Temporary Hit Points gained. Additionally, you become partially incorporeal granting the following benefits for up to 1 minute, or until you are incapacitated: You can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. The first time you enter a creature's space on a turn, that creature takes force damage equal to one roll of your Psionic Energy dice. Additionally, if you end your turn inside a creature or object, you and that target both take the same amount again in force damage. When you hit a creature you have passed through with a melee weapon attack, you do not provoke opportunity attacks for leaving their reach.

Your mastery of psionics lets you unleash waves of psychic intention that collapses thought and will. Psychic Feedback: Hostile creatures that start their turns within 30ft of you take take Psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier if you have attacked or dealt damage to them within the last turn. Intellect Spike: Additionally, as an action you can target a number of creatures within 30 feet of you equal to half your Wisdom modifier. Creatures targeted in this way must make an Intelligence saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier), taking psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier plus two rolls of your Psionic Energy dice and is incapacitated for up to 1 minute. On a successful save they take half damage and their speed is instead halved until the end of their next turn. At the start of each of their turns while incapacitated, the damage they take from Psychic Feedback is doubled. They can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending on a successful save. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you expend two Psionic Energy dice to use it again.
Features: 1st Level - Heart of Fire 6th Level - Fire in the Veins 14th Level - Pyromancer's Fury 18th Level - Fiery Soul

At 1st level, whenever you start casting a spell that deals fire damage, fiery magic erupts from you. This eruption causes creatures of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you to take fire damage equal to half your sorcerer level (minimum of 1).
At 6th level, you gain resistance to fire damage. In addition, spells you cast and effects you create ignore resistance to fire damage.

Starting at 14th level, when you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal fire damage to the attacker. The damage equals your sorcerer level, and ignores resistance to fire damage.

At 18th level, you gain immunity to fire damage. In addition, you ignore resistance to fire damage and treat immunity to fire damage as resistance to fire damage. When treating immunity as resistance, features or feats that allow you to ignore resistance do not do so.

A Raven Knight is fearsome in battle, fusing martial prowess with strange abilities gifted by the Raven Queen. Many Raven Knights work alone, though some may find a small band of companions to aid them in battle, and some may even command and lead entire armies into battle. Masters of death, Raven Knights seek to protect those who cannot protect themselves from undeath and the afterlife. Powerful Raven Knights may even become champions of the Raven Queen, and thus champions of the battlefield. Features: 3rd Level - Knowledge of Death 3rd Level - Soul Severing 7th Level - Feather Step 10th Level - Queens Blessing 15th Level - Deaths Embrace 18th Level - Duty in Death

When you choose this Archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Investigation and Medicine skills. Additionally, you can make Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Medicine) checks with advantage when attempting to determine the cause of death of a creature.

At 3rd level, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points you sever the connection of the creatures soul to its body. That creature cannot be turned into an undead. Additionally, as a reaction, when a creature is reduced to 0 hit points within 15ft of you you can empower your next attack with that creatures soul energy. Your next weapon attack deals additional necrotic damage equal to half your fighter level.

At 7th level, you move with the grace of the raven. Your walking speed increases by 10ft. Additionally, as a bonus action you gain a flight speed equal to your walking speed until the end of your turn, if you end your turn in midair you drop to the ground.
At 10th level, the Raven Queen grants you a blessing. You gain advantage on death saving throws, immunity to the frightened condition, and resistance to necrotic damage.
At 15th level, when you or an ally critically hit a creature, you can use your reaction to add 3d10 necrotic damage to the attacks damage roll.

At 18th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack against the creature that killed you. On a hit you critically hit that creature and regain hit points equal to the damage dealt. You can do this once per long rest.
Features: 3rd Level - Arcane Archer Lore 3rd Level - Arcane Shot 7th Level - Magic Ammunition 7th Level - Curving Shot 15th Level - Quick-draw Shot 18th Level - Eldritch Mastery

At 3rd level, you learn magical theory or some of the secrets of nature -- typical for practitioners of this elven martial tradition. You choose to gain proficiency in either the Arcana or the Nature skill, and you choose to learn either the prestidigitation or the druidcraft cantrip.

At 3rd level, you learn to unleash special magical effects with some of your shots. When you gain this feature, you learn two Arcane Shot options of your choice (see Arcane Shot Options below). Once per turn when you fire an arrow or bolt from any bow as part of the Attack action, you can apply one of your Arcane Shot options to that piece of ammunition. You decide to use the option when the ammunition hits a creature, unless the option doesn't involve an attack roll. You have a number of uses equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a short or long rest. You gain an additional Arcane Shot option of your choice when you reach certain levels in this class: 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level. Each option also improves when you become a 15th-level fighter.

The Arcane Shot feature lets you choose options for it at certain levels. The options are presented here in alphabetical order. They are all magical effects, and each one is associated with one of the schools of magic. If an option requires a saving throw, your Arcane Shot save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. Banishing Arrow​ You use abjuration magic to try to temporarily banish your target to a harmless location in the Feywild. The creature hit by the arrow must also succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be banished for 1 minute, or until you release the magic as a free action. While banished in this way, its speed is 0, and it is incapacitated. The affected creature can make a Charisma saving throw at the end of their turn, ending the effect on a success. At the end of the duration, the target reappears in the space it vacated or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. After you reach 15th level in this class, a target also takes 4d6 force damage when the arrow hits it. Beguiling Arrow​ Your enchantment magic causes this arrow to temporarily beguile its target. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 psychic damage, and choose one of your allies within 30 feet of the target. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it is charmed by the chosen ally for 1 minute or until you release the magic as a free action. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success. Additionally, this effect ends early if the chosen ally attacks the charmed target, deals damage to it, or forces it to make a saving throw. The psychic damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. Bursting Arrow​ You imbue your arrow with force energy drawn from the school of evocation. The arrow detonates after your attack. Immediately after the arrow hits the creature, the target and all other creatures within 10 feet of it take 2d6 force damage each and succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Arcane Shot save DC, or be knocked prone. The force damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. (edited) Enfeebling Arrow​ You weave necromantic magic into your arrow. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 necrotic damage on hit, as well as at the start of each of their turns for 1 minute or until you release the magic as a free action. The target must also succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or the damage dealt by its weapon attacks is halved until the start of your next turn. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success. The necrotic damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. Grasping Arrow​ When this arrow strikes its target, conjuration magic creates grasping, poisonous brambles, which wrap around the target. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 poison damage, its speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it takes 2d6 slashing damage the first time on each turn it moves 1 foot or more without teleporting. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the brambles with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC. The brambles last for 1 minute, until you use another option, or until you release the magic as a free action. The poison damage and slashing damage both increase to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. Piercing Arrow​ You use transmutation magic to give your arrow an ethereal quality. When you use this option, you don’t make an attack roll for the attack. Instead, the arrow fires forward in a line, which is 5 foot wide and 30 feet long, before disappearing. The arrow passes harmlessly through objects, ignoring cover. Each creature in that line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes damage as if it were hit by the arrow, plus an extra 2d6 piercing damage. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage. This option lasts for 1 minute, until you use another option, or until you release the magic as a free action. The piercing damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. Seeking Arrow​ Using divination magic, you grant your arrow the ability to seek out your target, allowing the arrow to curve and twist its path in search of its prey. When you use this option, you don’t make an attack roll for the attack. Instead, choose one creature you have seen in the past minute. The arrow flies toward that creature, moving around corners if necessary and ignoring three-quarters cover and half cover. If the target is within the weapon’s range and there is a path large enough for the arrow to travel to the target, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes damage as if it were hit by the arrow, plus an extra 2d6 force damage, and you learn the target’s current location and distance for 1 hour or until you release the magic as a free action. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage, and you only learn the targets current location and distance for one round. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success. The force damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class. (edited) Shadow Arrow​ You weave illusion magic into your arrow, causing it to occlude your foe’s vision with shadows. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra 2d6 psychic damage, and it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be unable to see anything farther than 5 feet away for 1 minute or until you release the magic as a free action. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the arrow with a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your Arcane Shot save DC, ending the effect on a success. The psychic damage increases to 4d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.

At 7th level, you gain the ability to infuse ammunition with magic. Whenever you fire a nonmagical arrow from a bow, you can make it magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. The magic fades from the ammunition immediately after it hits or misses its target.

At 7th level, you learn how to direct an errant ammunition toward a new target. When you make an attack roll with a magic ammunition and miss, you can use a bonus action to reroll the attack roll against a different target within 60 feet of the original target.

Starting at 15th level, your magical archery makes your movements swift. Whenever you hit a target with an Arcane Shot you can use your bonus action to make another ranged weapon attack against the same target using the same weapon.

At 18th level, your mastery of blending magic with archery teaches you to infuse your arrows with even greater magic, as well as combining them for greater effect. Once per attack action, you can infuse a single arrow with two different arcane shot options, excluding piercing shot, having the target be affected by and taking damage from both shots. However when doing this you expend two uses of your Arcane shot. You have two uses of this ability, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.

All barbarians harbor a fury within. Their rage grants them superior strength, durability, and speed. Barbarians who follow the Path of the Storm Herald learn to transform that rage into a mantle of primal magic, which swirls around them. When in a fury, a barbarian of this path taps into the forces of nature to create powerful magical effects. Storm heralds are typically elite champions who train alongside druids, rangers, and others sworn to protect nature. Other storm heralds hone their craft in lodges in regions wracked by storms, in the frozen reaches at the world’s end, or deep in the hottest deserts. Features: 3rd Level - Storm Aura 6th Level - Storm Soul 10th Level - Shielding Storm 14th Level - Raging Storm
documents.s: Revised Path of the Storm Herald

documents.t: Starting at 3rd level, you emanate a stormy, magical aura while you rage. The area within the aura is lightly obscured. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover. Your aura has an effect that activates when you enter your rage, and you can activate the effect again on each of your turns as a bonus action. Choose desert, sea, or tundra. Your aura’s effect depends on that chosen environment, as detailed below. You can change your environment choice whenever you rage. If your aura’s effects require a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier. Desert. When this effect is activated, creatures of your choice in your aura take 1d6 fire damage. The damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 2d6 at 5th level, 3d6 at 11th level, 4d6 at 17th level. Sea. When this effect is activated, you can choose one other creature you can see in your aura to strike with lightning. The target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the target takes 1d6 lightning damage on a failed save and is knocked prone. On a success, it takes half as much damage and isn’t knocked prone. The damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 2d6 at 5th level, 3d6 at 11th level, and 4d6 at 17th level. Tundra. When this effect is activated, creatures of your choice in your aura must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature’s speed is reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn, and the creature can’t take reaction for the duration.

At 6th level, the storm grants you benefits while your aura is active. The benefits are based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura. Desert. You gain resistance to fire damage. You can use an action to scatter sand in the area within your aura. Creatures within the area must make a Dexterity saving throw or be blinded until the end of your next turn. Sea. You gain resistance to lightning damage, and you can breathe underwater. You can use an action to create a whirlpool around a creature you can see within your aura. It must make a Strength saving throw or be restrained until the end of your next turn. Tundra. You gain resistance to cold damage. You can use an action to to grant temporary hit points to creatures of your choice in your aura equal to your barbarian level, as icy armor encases them.

At 10th level, you learn to use your mastery of the storm to protect others. Each creature of your choice has the damage resistance you gained from the Storm Soul feature while the creature is in your Storm Aura.

At 14th level, the power of the storm you channel grows mightier, lashing out at your foes. The effect is based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura. Desert. Immediately after a creature in your aura hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature catches fire; until someone takes an action to douse the fire, the creature takes fire damage equal to half your barbarian level at the end of each of its turns. Sea. When you create a lighting strike with your Storm Aura or a whirlpool with your Storm Soul feature, you can target two creatures instead of one. Tundra.
