The area in your aura is heavily obscured, except for yourself and creatures of your choice when you activate the aura.
Features: 3rd Level - Rallying Cry Royal Envoy 10th Level - Inspiring Surge 15th Level - Bulwark 18th Level - Loyalty to the Crown

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn how to inspire your allies to fight on past their injuries. When you use your Second Wind feature, each creature of your choice within 15 feet of you regains hit points equal to your fighter level, provided that the creature can see or hear you.

A Purple Dragon knight serves as an envoy of the Cormyrean crown. Knights of high standing are expected to conduct themselves with grace. At 7th level, you gain proficiency in the Persuasion skill. If you are already proficient in it, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Insight, Intimidation, or Performance. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses Persuasion. You receive this benefit regardless of the skill proficiency you gain from this feature.

Starting at 10th level, when you use your Action Surge feature, you can choose an amount of creatures equal to half your fighter level (rounded down) within 15 feet of you. Those creatures can make one melee or ranged weapon attack with their reaction, provided that they can see or hear you. Starting at 18th level, the range of your inspiration increases to 30 feet.

Beginning at 15th level, you can extend the benefit of your Indomitable feature to your allies. When you decide to use Indomitable to reroll an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma saving throw and you aren't incapacitated, you can choose an amount of creatures equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) within 30 feet of you that also failed its saving throw against the same effect. If those creatures can see or hear you, they can reroll their saving throw and must use the new roll.

Starting at 18th level, when you target an ally with any of your bannerette features, that ally gains advantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes until the end of its next turn.

Decisive tactics and thoughtful planning are both highly important factors in the game of chess, and as certain Bulwarks are aware, the same goes for the art of war. Rooks are master tacticians, able to turn the tide of battle in their favor from nearly any position. Features: 3rd Level - One Step Ahead 7th Level - Recapture 13th Level - Gambits 18th Level - Checkmate

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you learn to apply yourself on the battlefield in a similar way to the pieces of a chess board. You gain a pool of material equal to thrice your bulwark level to spend on plays. If a play allows you to move as part of it, you do so without expending your own movement, but you cannot have a speed of 0. You recover all expended material when you finish a long rest. Below is the list of plays: Advance: When you take the attack action, you may expend three material to move up to your speed. You may take this movement before or after you make your attacks. Back Rank: When you enter your defensive stance you can expend 3 material to impose disadvantage on all ranged attacks against you for the duration. En Passant: When you attack a creature within 5 feet of you, you may expend 2 material to move up to 10 feet to another point within 5 feet of that creature. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks, and your next attack roll against it has advantage. Pawn’s Fury: During the first round of combat, you may expend 3 material to take an additional action. That action can be used to take only the Attack (one attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Interact with an Object action. Knight’s Leap: When you jump, you may expend 1 material to triple your jump distance. It does not cost you any additional movement to do so. Bishop’s Grace: As an action, you may expend 2 material to cast both guidance and resistance on yourself. Neither spell requires your concentration.
Starting at 7th level, you learn to reclaim the potential of the foes you fell. When you kill a creature with at least 30 hit points, you recover 5 material.

When you reach 13th level, you gain the ability to perform greater plays with great risk, though the potential payout is just as grand. You gain access to the following plays: Castling: When you enter your defensive stance, you may spend 7 material to choose one willing creature within 30 feet of you to trade places with. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. If when initiative ends, that creature has not taken damage since the switch, you regain 7 material. Discovered Attack: When a creature within 5 feet of you targets you with an attack, you may use your reaction to expend 10 material. In doing so, you may make a melee attack against that target. If the attack reduces the creature to 0 hit points, you regain 10 material. Promote: When you roll initiative, you may spend 20 material. For the duration of that combat you make plays, but not gambits, without expending material. Queen’s Majesty: As a bonus action, you may expend 25 material in order to move up to twice your speed. For one minute after taking this bonus action, the amount of material you gain from your recapture feature is doubled. King’s Command: As an action, you may spend 20 material to cast the Command spell (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) on any number of creatures within range. You must use the same command on each target. If no target succeeds their saving throw, you regain 10 material. Rook’s Defiance: When you use your Fortitude feature, you may spend up to 20 material and further reduce the damage by that amount. If you reduce the damage to 0, you regain half the material spent.

At 18th level, you have mastered the art of bringing fights to a decisive finish. When you take the attack action while your stance is active, you may choose to end your stance early. If you do, the first creature you hit takes extra damage equal to your bulwark level and is knocked prone.
Features: 2nd Level - Arcane Might 6th Level - Special Delivery 10th Level - Extra Attack 14th Level - The ol' One-Two

When you take this tradition at 2nd level, you learn to better partake in unarmed combat. You can replace the damage of your unarmed strikes with a d4 instead of their normal damage, and is considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical attacks. This damage increases to 1d6 at 6th level, to 1d8 at 10th level, and again to 1d10 at 14th level. Additionally, your hit point maximum increases by 2, and again by one each time you gain a level in this class.

When you reach 6th level, your technique has been honed to cast your spells through your martial combat. Once per turn, when you make an unarmed strike, you can deliver a spell's effects to the target as if you had cast it on them, in addition to the effects of the unarmed strike. The spell must have a casting time of one action, and must either be able to target another creature or area. If the spell would target an area, the effect's point of origin must be the target. Otherwise, you may shape the spell as you choose within the restrictions of the area of effect.. If the spell requires a saving throw, the target must make the saving throw as usual. If the spell requires an attack roll, the spell hits if the unarmed strike hits. You expend a spell slot to cast the spell as normal, and the spell must be of a level no greater than your proficiency bonus.
Beginning at 10th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Your culmination of martial and arcane knowledge has combined to great effect, allowing you to use one to make targets more vulnerable to another. If you hit a target twice on the same turn with unarmed strikes, the target has disadvantage on saving throws from the next spell you cast before the end of your next turn. Additionally, when you damage a creature with a spell, the next unarmed strike you make against them has advantage, and deals extra damage equal to your wizard level.

Sometimes seen as the oddball of the various Artificer specialists, the Scrapper is a master of what other Artificers discard as junk. Make no mistake though, these hoarder misfits exemplify everything an artificer is at their core - Innovative, curious, with a spark of insanity mixed in with genius. They take what others see as trash, and turn it into works of art. Features: 3rd Level - Tool of the Trade 3rd Level - Scrapper Spells 3rd Level - Another's Treasure 5th Level - Extra Attack 9th Level - Junkrat's Armor 15th Level - Sage of Junk

You have proficiency with improvised weapons. You also gain proficiency with smith's tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

Starting at 3rd level, you always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Scrapper Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare. 3rd level - magic missile, shield 5th level - cloud of daggers, locate object 9th level - leomund's tiny hut, melf's minute meteors 13th level - dimension door, fire shield 17th level - passwall, steel wind strike

Beginning at 3rd level, you can take anything lying around - A table leg, a shard of glass, a cooking pot - and turn it into a deadly weapon of war. When you hold/make an improvised weapon, the DM will determine if it deals slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning damage, and if it is one-handed (base 1d4 damage) or two-handed (base 1d6 damage) based on its resemblance to real weapons. You can use a bonus action to use your smithing tools to roll on the Upgrade Table to apply a random upgrade to an improvised weapon you are holding. An upgraded improvised weapon count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. d6 - Effect 1 Heavy Smashers. You affix heavy weights to the weapon, adding a bonus 1d6 bludgeoning damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, you can knock the target away from you up to 10 feet. 2 Spiky Stabbers. You attach spiky things such as rusted nails, sharpened sticks, etc. to your weapon, adding a bonus 1d6 piercing damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, you reduce that target's AC by 2 until the end of its next turn. 3 Sharp Slicers. You add sharp metal scraps, broken glass, or other slicing edges to your weapon, adding a bonus 1d6 slashing damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, the target's speed is halved until the end of its next turn. 4 Burning Flames. You coat the weapon in flammable materials, and set it alight, adding a bonus 1d6 fire damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, you can ignite the target. A target on fire takes 1d10 fire damage at the start of its turn. The target can use an action to put the fire out. 5 Shocking Coils. You wrap your weapon with suspect electrical components and wires, adding a bonus 1d6 lightning damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn. 6 Venomous Goo. You slather the weapon in dangerous chemicals and diseased meat, adding a bonus 1d6 poison damage. When you damage a target with this weapon, roll 1d4. On a 4, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. An upgraded improvised weapon can be used in a number of attacks equal to your Intelligence modifier plus your proficiency bonus(a minimum of twice) before they break and become unusable. You can apply only one upgrade on an improvised weapon and it is removed when you drop or stow the weapon. If you try to upgrade another improvised weapon, the old upgrade is immediately removed, and then the new upgrade applies. You can also consume a spell slot to apply an upgrade to an improvised weapon as a bonus action. If you do, you may choose the upgrade applied from the Upgrade Table. You are able to apply your infusions to your upgraded improvised weapons.
Starting 5th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

At 9th level, you have found new uses for all the scrap you carry around for makeshift weapons. Now, you know how to enhance your armor with ad hoc ablative shielding. After finishing a long rest and if you are wearing medium or heavy armor, your armor gains a bonus to Armor Class equal to your Intelligence modifier (a minimum bonus of +1). Whenever you take damage, roll 1d4. On a 4, pieces of this scrap-built extra armor break off, and your bonus decreases by 1 point until it returns to its normal base value.

By 15th level, you have become a lethal force with any random object that fits your fancy: Whenever you hold an improvised weapon, you can automatically apply a random upgrade from the Upgrade Table. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher, the next attack you make with an upgraded improvised weapon deals extra force damage equal to 1d10 times the level of the spell cast, to a maximum of 5d10. You now gain the Junkrat's Armor bonus after a short or long rest, instead of only a long rest.

The Sentinel Blade embodies the essence of unwavering defense, blending masterful swordplay with unbreakable resolve. Trained to stand as the ultimate shield for their allies, these warriors adopt a specialized stance that turns every strike against them into an opportunity. Their blades move with precision, deflecting blows with ease and delivering calculated ripostes.

Starting at 2nd level, you learn to develop flow during the midst of combat, building on each success as you begin to flow like a dance. While using a melee weapon without a shield, whenever you land a successful hit your first time in a turn, an attack misses you, or you succeed on a saving throw from a hostile creature, you gain flow equal to 1d6 + half your total mastery. Whenever you take damage from an attack, you lose flow instead. If this damage reduces your flow to 0, you take any remaining damage. If you reduce an attack's damage to zero, you suffer no additional effects from the weapon. You can have a max amount of flow equal to twice your practitioner level, which depletes at the end of combat. You can only build flow whilst in combat.

Starting at 6th level, when an attack misses you, or you block one with flow completely, you may make a melee attack as a reaction against the target. Additionally, you may instead spend 1 mastery point to use a technique.
Starting at 14th level, when an ally within melee range is hit by an attack, you can use your flow to block the attack as if it were targeting you.

Starting at 18th level, you learn to harness your flow into focus. When you have at least 75% of your maximum flow and focus on a technique or use a technique through riposte, you may sacrifice 7 flow to spend 1 less mastery point. The following goes with the subclass as part of the practitioner class

Type: Physical Prerequisites: Novice, Sentinel Blade Make a weapon attack against a creature or object. The attack deals a number of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus in additional damage. Focused (1 point) Hit or miss, roll a number or d4s equal to half your total mastery. You gain flow equal to the total.

Type: Physical Prerequisites: Intermediate, Sentinel Blade You move in a mirage, teleporting to an area within 60ft of you. Focused (1 point, 0 if you have your maximum flow). You can use another technique that includes a weapon attack. This may be before or after you teleport.

Type: Mental Prerequisites: Advanced, Sentinel Blade You may temporarily steel yourself against other manners of attacks. Until the end of your next turn, you may block damage from any source using Aegis Flow. Focused (2 points, 1 if you your maximum flow). The duration of this technique becomes 1 minute. Until the end of your next turn, if you would succeed on a saving throw and normally take half damage, you would instead take no damage.

Type: Physical Prerequisites: Master, Sentinel Blade Duration: 1 minute For the next minute, your maximum flow and the flow you gain is doubled. During this time, you have vulnerability to attacks while your flow is 0. You must use an action to end this effect Focused (1 points). You may use another technique from this form

Bulwarks who spend their training bettering themselves against the ever-present threat of magic. Spellbreakers are the last thing a wizard wants to see on the field of battle, usually resulting in a fairly one sided encounter. Features: 3rd Level - Out of the Inferno 7th Level - Spell-Shatter 13th Level - Anticipation 18th Level - Willbreaker

When you choose this specialization at 3rd level, you learn to incorporate methods to help you avoid magical effects into your stance. While your defensive stance is active, you also gain resistance to fire, cold, lightning, and acid damage.

Starting at 7th level, magical warding effects become inefficient at halting your progress. When you hit a creature or object with a weapon attack, all spells from the abjuration school immediately end if they are affecting the target.

When you reach 13th level, you gain an understanding and fortitude against the ways that mages tend to fight. When you enter your defensive stance, you automatically succeed on the next intelligence, wisdom, or charisma saving throw you make before it ends.

At 18th level, your magical defenses allow you to nearly completely ignore the effects of lesser magic, making your foes need to drain their resources to even hope to defeat you. You are immune to the effects of cantrips and 1st and 2nd level spells, unless you wish to be affected by them.

You have spent many a night training under the stars and became touched by cosmic energy to shape light as you see fit. Creating armaments of pure light and radiance you become a beacon for those lost in the dark. Features: 3rd Level - Hardlight One With the Stars Astral Multitool Shooting Stars Galactic Aegis Stellar Expanse

3rd-Level Feature At 3rd level, you gain an amount of Hardlight charges equal to your double proficiency bonus, resetting on a long rest. You can use one charge to conjure a mundane melee weapon you are proficient with out of radiant light. This weapon does radiant damage, and counts as a magical weapon. Alternatively, you can spend one charge to conjure up an instrument or tool you have proficiency with. Equipment conjured up using this feature lasts an hour. At 15th level this changes from 1 hours to 8 hours.
7th-Level Feature At 7th level, you gain a bonus to damage and attack rolls and ability checks with Hardlight equipment equal to half your Wisdom modifier.
7th-Level Feature At 7th level, you can spend a bonus action to change your Hardlight equipment into another piece of equipment. You can use this feature once per short rest.

10th-Level Feature Starting at 10th level, your mastery over hardlight weapons has granted you the ability to create ranged weapons. Creating a ranged weapons costs 2 hardlight and a bonus action to create. The ammunition it uses looks like a shooting star as you fire the weapons, and does not consume a hardlight charge.

15th-Level Feature At 15th level, you can spend one Hardlight charge to create Hardlight armor. Hardlight armor counts as magical heavy armor, and has a base AC of 10 + your Dexterity modifier+ your Wisdom modifier. If a creature other than yourself wears this armor, it loses its properties. Additionally, you can spend one Hardlight charge to create a Hardlight shield. This shield counts as a magical shield that provides 3/4 cover for yourself, this shield does not provide the base AC of a shield. If a creature other than yourself equips this shield, it loses its properties.

18th-Level Feature At 18th level, you can spend 2 Hardlight charges as a bonus action to empower yourself for one minute. Whenever you hit a creature with a Hardlight weapon, the weapon does an additional 3d4 radiant damage. While you have a Hardlight shield equipped, if an enemy misses you with a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to gain advantage on all attack rolls against them until the end of your next turn. Additionally, you can maintain one piece of Hardlight equipment indefinitely. While this equipment exists, your total amount of Hardlight charges is reduced by one until it is dismissed.

Storm chasers are a select few drifters along the astral plane, seeking out natural and magical phenomena to bolster their own power. While primarily existing on the astral plane, a storm chaser can be just as effective on the material plane, or anywhere a storm can be found, as they can make good use of bows and crossbows, in addition to the firearms traditionally used while on the astral plane.

Starting at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Storm Chaser Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn’t count against the number of ranger spells you know. Ranger Level Spells 3rd Thunderwave 5th Vortex Warp 9th Call Lightning 13th Ice Storm 17th Control Winds
At 3rd Level, you have learned to harness the potency of firearms to complement the powers of the storms you chase. You gain proficiency with firearms.

Starting at 3rd level, when you take this archetype at 3rd level, you are able to unleash a deafening boom when you use your ranged weapons. Once on each of your turns, when you attack with a ranged weapon, you can force each creature within 10 feet of you to make a constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d8 thunder damage. The damage increases to 2d8 at 11th level.

At 7th level, when you take the attack action, you can forgo your extra attack feature to make a single ranged weapon attack. This attack deals triple the damage dice of the weapon you used, and deals lightning damage instead of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing. This attack is also critical on a d20 roll of 19 or 20 if used during a storm.

At 11th level, you have learned to bring storms to you. As an action, you call forth a vortex at a point you can see within 60 feet. The vortex is a cylinder with a radius of 30 feet, and a height of 90 feet. The vortex counts as a storm for the purposes of Charged Shell. As a bonus action on each of your turns while the vortex lasts, you can target a creature inside, striking them with a bolt of lightning. The target must make a dexterity saving throw, taking 3d10 lightning on a failure, or half as much on a successful save. The vortex lasts for 10 minutes, and once used, cannot be summoned again until you finish a long rest, or spend a spell slot of at least 3rd level or higher to summon it again. No more than 1 vortex can exist at once.

At 15th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage. Additionally, you can target yourself with the bolt of lightning from your storm caller ability. If you do so, instead of taking damage, your next charged shell attack deals extra damage equal to twice the amount of damage the lightning would have dealt. This also causes the attack to be critical on a d20 roll of 18, 19, or 20.
We know you’re still a spellblade Prerequisites: Wizard 20
When you take this prestige class, choose two more skills from the Wizard skill proficiencies. You are proficient in both of those skills.

Additionally when you take this prestige class, you gain a new set of spell slots to fuel your spells. You gain spell slots as per the Wizard table based on your prestige level minus 20. When you prepare spells for the day, you may now prepare a number of spells equal to your prestige level + your intelligence modifier. You learn two wizard cantrips of your choice, and one additional wizard cantrip at 24th and 30th level.

At 21st level when you use your Arcane Recovery Feature, you instead use your prestige level when determining the amount of spell levels you can recover. Additionally, any unspent spell levels may be recovered on later short rests before the end of your next long rest.

When you reach 22nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic throughout a multitude of schools. You may choose the same tradition, or you may choose to expand to a new tradition to expand your capabilities. Your choice grants you features at 22nd level, and again at 26th, 30th, and 34th level.

At 23rd level, your repertoire of signature spells improves to encompass higher level spells. Choose one 4th and one 5th level spell in your spellbook to add to your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don’t count towards the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast them once each at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

When you reach 24th level, and again at 28th, 32nd, 36th, and 39th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

At 25th level, your magic flows through you effortlessly, and is able to produce your most practiced spells at no drain to you. Choose one of your 3rd level signature spells. You are now able to cast that spell at its lowest level without expending a spell slot. You no longer need to finish a short or long rest to do so again. At 29th level, the other 3rd level signature spell is granted the same benefit. Revised Wizards instead gain +1 to the maximum spellforge modifications to all of their created spells at 29th level.

When you reach 33rd level, it is practically nothing for you to produce even the most potent of your signature spells. You are now able to cast your 4th level signature spell at its lowest level without expending a spell slot, and do not need to finish a short or long rest to do so again. When you reach 37th level, your 5th level signature spell is granted the same benefit.

At 38th level, your vast collection of arcane knowledge is always an arm’s reach away, and can never again be taken from you. Should a spellbook of yours ever be lost or destroyed, you can use an action to return the book to your hands in perfect condition. If the book was destroyed, it is returned in its entirety.

When you reach 40th level, your constant dealing with arcane knowledge has opened your mind to concepts that, prior to now, you could not even begin to conceive. Your Intelligence and Wisdom scores both increase by 4, to a maximum of 30.

Cheaters go by many names; swindlers, con-artists, charlatans. Whatever they may call you, whoever you might be perceived as, you’ll always be the first to let the world know that the cards in your hand are there entirely legitimately— you couldn’t have stacked the deck, the dealer shuffled beforehand! You weren’t responsible for the incomprehensibly lucky die rolls, either— you were borrowing the dealer’s dice, after all. Oh, and the drinking game you outlasted the dwarf barbarian in? You couldn’t have watered your drink down, the dealer poured it out for you! …What? You’re being accused of paying off the dealer? Poppycock. Features: 3rd Level - Swindler’s Luck 9th Level - Loaded Dice 13th Level - Sure Shot 17th Level - Don of Con

At 3rd level, luck seems to appear whenever it benefits you, almost as if you’re cheating. Whenever you make a roll with advantage, you may meddle with the roll, forgoing that advantage, and roll normally. The next time you roll without advantage, you roll with advantage.

At 9th level, you cheat act with more finesse, giving you more control over your actions. Whenever you make a roll with advantage, you may forgo that advantage to create a loaded die. You may store a number of loaded dice equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. These loaded dice disappear on a short or long rest. Whenever you roll an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you may spend one of your loaded dice to give yourself advantage on that roll. You may only spend one loaded die per turn.

By 13th level, your “luck” is far too consistent to be inconspicuous. When you roll with advantage, you may forgo that advantage to add +3 to the roll’s total. If the roll succeeds, you gain one loaded die.

At 17th level, it’s quite clear you’ve been cheating all this time, some way, somehow. On the bright side, you don’t have to hide it anymore— whenever you miss with an attack roll, you can spend 3 loaded dice to turn that miss into a hit. When you fail a saving throw, you can spend 2 loaded dice to succeed automatically. When you fail an ability check, you can spend 1 loaded die to make the result 20.

Though colloquially referred to as “Sword Saints”, swords are only the most popular weapon they are seen mastering, not the only weapon. These practitioners devote themselves to training with a specific weapon of their choosing, rarely ever making use of other armaments.

At 2nd level, choose a weapon you are proficient in to pledge your devotion to (ex. longsword, shortbow, glaive, etc). When wielding the a weapon, the following features are made available to you. Flying Weapon​ You learn how to wield the weapon without needing to even touch it. You can use a bonus action to move the weapon up to 30 feet in any direction or teleport it back to your hand instantly. You can attack and use techniques with the weapon as if you were standing in the weapon’s space. While the weapon is being controlled in this way, it is treated as if you were still holding it (you require a free hand to attack with it, or two hands if it’s two-handed, etc). You cannot move it more than 120 feet away from yourself, and if brought outside of this range, you cannot control it further until it’s within the range. Draining Strike​ If you kill a hostile creature with an attack made with your flying weapon, you can use a reaction to drain the creature, regaining mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up). After you use this feature, you must take a short or long rest before you can use it again.

At 6th level, you become increasingly adept at using your weapon for techniques. In the same bonus action that you use to move the weapon, you can spend 1 mastery point to use the primary effect of a technique you know. Beginning at 14th level, you can focus the technique you use.

At 14th level, your control over the weapon you devoted yourself to extends even to being able to ride it. Your weapon can be ridden in the air, during which it cannot be used for techniques. It has a flying speed equal to your movement speed plus an additional 30 feet and can carry up to 500 pounds before it can no longer fly.

At 18th level, you can control two flying weapons at once, with the second not being treated as if you were holding it. If you use a bonus action to use a technique with one, the other can make a single weapon attack.

The scourge of the unholy. Bulwarks who call themselves Templar are the bane of all undead, fiends, and those that follow evil practices. Being a Bulwark, this means that such forces are met with only the strongest protections whilst engaging a Templar. Features: 3rd Level - Protection from Evil 3rd Level - Spellcasting 7th Level - Sanctify 13th Level - Divine Stance 18th Level - Evil’s Bane

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, you gain a supernatural protection from the forces of evil. When an undead, fiend, or other evil aligned creature deals damage to you, the total damage is reduced by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus.

Additionally when you select this specialization, you learn to merge divine magic with your defensive tactics. Cantrips You learn two cantrips of your choice from the cleric spell list. You learn an additional cleric cantrip of your choice at 10th level. Spell Slots The Templar Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your cleric spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell’s level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest. For example, if you know the 1st-level spell cure wounds and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast cure wounds using either slot. Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher You know three 1st-level cleric spells of your choice. The Spells Known column of the Templar Spellcasting table shows when you learn more cleric spells of 1st-level or higher. Each of these new spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 7th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the cleric spells you know with another spell of your choice from the cleric spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots. Spellcasting Ability Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your cleric spells. The power of your spells may come from a deity, or personal sense of conviction against the unholy. Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier Templar Spellcasting Level Cantrips Known Spells Known - Spell Slots per Spell Level - - Spell Slots per Spell Level - - Spell Slots per Spell Level - - Spell Slots per Spell Level - 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 3 2 3 2 - - - 4 2 4 3 - - - 5 2 4 3 - - - 6 2 4 3 - - - 7 2 5 4 2 - - 8 2 6 4 2 - - 9 2 6 4 2 - - 10 3 7 4 3 - - 11 3 8 4 3 - - 12 3 8 4 3 - - 13 3 9 4 3 2 - 14 3 10 4 3 2 - 15 3 10 4 3 2 - 16 3 11 4 3 3 - 17 3 11 4 3 3 - 18 3 11 4 3 3 - 19 3 12 4 3 3 1 20 3 13 4 3 3 1

When you reach 7th level, you gain the ability to absolve creatures of the evil they embody. When an undead, fiend, or other evil aligned creature damages you, you may use your reaction to expend a spell slot. Doing so places the creature under the effects of Turn Undead (even if the target is not undead) on a failed wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. While they are turned in this way, the creature does not run away, and instead falls prone where they are standing on their turn.

At 13th level your defensive stance now carries with it the capacity to share your magic with your allies. When you cast a cleric spell with a range of self, or a cleric spell that only affects you while your defensive stance is active, you can choose to have it also affect each ally within 20 feet of you. If a spell’s duration would last longer than your defensive stance, it ends on your allies when your defensive stance ends.

When you reach 18th level your presence alone is enough to force evil from their hiding places. Undead, fiends, and other evil aligned creatures automatically fail saving throws against your dueling stance.

Powerful entities of the outer, or even inner planes often seek out mortals to do their bidding on the material plane. Sometimes, however, instead of power similar to their own, they might grant their warlocks an ability to pull creatures from other planes to an extraordinary degree. Features: Extended Spell List 1st Level - Planar Tether 6th Level - Ethereal Stores 10th Level - Undying Binds 14th Level - Sacrificial Summoning

The Extraplanar lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you. Spell Level - Spells: Sorcerer Level Spells 1st Bane, Sanctuary 2nd Arcanist's Magic Aura, Vortex Warp 3rd Bestow Curse, Glyph of Warding 4th Giant Insect, Summon Elemental 5th Creation, Summon Celestial

When you form this pact at 1st level, you are granted the ability to tether your summoned creatures to your plane, granting them additional strengths. When you cast a warlock spell that summons a single creature, you may undergo a special ritual during the casting of the spell. Doing so changes the spell's casting time to 10 minutes, and the summon lasts until it is dispelled. If the spell normally requires concentration, you may ignore the requirement. When you summon a creature in this way, it is referred to as your tether, and it gains the following benefits: You can replace its hit points with 5 x your warlock level. It adds your proficiency bonus to its damage rolls. If the creatures to-hit bonus is less than that of your spell attack bonus, it may instead use your spell attack bonus when attacking. You learn the Find Familiar spell, it counts as a warlock spell for you, and it does not count towards your total spells known. If you summon another creature using this ritual, any previous creatures summoned by it are immediately dispelled. After you complete this ritual, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

Starting at 6th level, you can briefly store items away for later use. You can cast the [Wristpocket] spell a number of times equal to your charisma modifier without expending a spell slot. When you do, the stored object is sent to the ethereal plane, and the spell does not require concentration. You regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a long rest. Additionally, you can see into the ethereal plane up to 10 ft.
At 10th level, when tether drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to expend a pact slot. Doing so will restore 50 hit points to the summon.

Starting on 14th level, while your Planar Tether summon is active, you can use an action to sacrifice part of yourself to empower it and your spells, doing so allows you to channel this ability until your next long rest, or until you end it as an action. While channeling this ability, you have the following effects: Your hit point maximum is reduced by 30. You have disadvantage on Constitution checks and saving throws, except for those made to maintain concentration. Your tether has advantage on all saving throws You can use a bonus action to give your tether temporary hit points equal to your warlock level Creatures within 10 ft of your tether have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells. If you end this ability early, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

There is undeath in your blood. Where other sorcerers inherit fire or storm, you inherited the grave — and the authority that comes with it. The dead do not merely answer you; they kneel. Features: 1st Level - There's Undeath in Your Blood 1st Level - Born to Rule 6th Level - A King, and His Legion 14th Level - Undead Lord 18th Level - All for One
Starting at 1st level, you gain access to all spells from the Necromancy school that create or manipulate undead. These count as sorcerer spells for you.
documents.s: 1st Level - There's Undeath in Your Blood

documents.t: Starting at 1st level, as an action you can animate one humanoid corpse within 30 feet of you into a zombie, or one pile of bones into a skeleton. All undead created with this feature exist under your control for 1 hour, at which point they revert to an inanimate corpse or pile of bones. They act at the end of your turn in initiative, following your telepathic or verbal commands to the best of their ability. You may use this feature once per long rest, unless you spend a sorcery point to do so again.

At 6th level, you gain a new Metamagic option. This does not count against the number of Metamagic options you know. When you cast a spell that creates undead, you may spend a number of sorcery points equal to the level of the spell to double the number of undead created by that spell, or the number of undead you may re-assert control of with the spell.
documents.s: 6th Level - A King, and His Legion

documents.t: At 14th level, spells and effects that specify a creature's type as undead treat you as an undead. You no longer require food, water, air, or sleep. To take a long rest, you must spend 4 hours in an inactive state in order to complete the rest. As an action, you may veil yourself to undead. If they would otherwise be hostile, they treat you with indifference for 10 minutes, or until you take any harmful action towards them. Additionally, for this duration, undead have disadvantage on all attacks against you, and you have advantage on any saving throws they force you to make. You may take this action once per short or long rest.

At 18th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points, you may spend 2 sorcery points and reduce one undead under your control within 15 feet of you to ash. You teleport to where that undead was, and regain hit points equal to half your sorcerer level plus your Charisma modifier.

The True Path requires the constant repetition of martial forms until absolute perfection is achieved. With perfection comes “truth”, an aspect of life that such practitioners would consider their peak.

At 2nd level, you learn the True Strike cantrip and can cast it as a bonus action. When you cast it, you gain its benefits on the current turn rather than the next turn, and it doesn’t require concentration for you. The spell ends at the end of your turn. Once per short or long rest, if you kill a hostile creature affected by True Strike, you can use your reaction to regain mastery points equal to half your maximum (rounded up).

At 6th level, when you strike true, you can bypass the defenses of your enemies. A technique’s attack that has advantage due to True Strike’s effect ignores an enemy’s resistances. At 18th level, such an enemy’s damage immunities are treated as resistances (which cannot be ignored).
At 14th level, when you cast true strike on a target, you can learn their resistances, immunities, and current hit points. Additionally, you gain advantage on insight checks against the target.

At 18th level, you can analyze the intrinsic truth about a creature. When you cast True Strike, you can spend 1 mastery point to give your next technique’s attack a +10 bonus to the attack roll and have the creature make their next save against the technique with disadvantage.

You have made your pact with a being of the Shadowfell—not a tyrant, not a monster, but a sovereign of sorrow. The Umbral Lord is a force of stillness and forgetting, a presence woven into the death of joy and the fading of names. It offers you no glory, only power—drawn from what others try not to remember. Features: 3rd Level - Umbral Lord Spells 3rd Level - Echoes of the Forgotten 6th Level - Gravity of Sorrow 10th Level - Despair-Wrought Form 14th Level - Embrace of Oblivion

The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Umbral Lord Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. Umbral Lord Spells​ 3rd: Dissonant Whispers, Phantasmal Force, Calm Emotions, Cause Fear 5th: Summon Shadowspawn, Fear 7th: Shadow of Moil, Phantasmal Killer 9th: Dream, Modify Memory These spells reflect the patron’s nature—magic that distorts perception, suppresses emotion, and turns sorrow into power.

3rd-Level Umbral Lord Feature Your presence carries the emotional residue of the Shadowfell—haunting, weighty, and impossible to shake. Even the fiercest mind stumbles under the echo of forgotten regrets. You gain proficiency in Insight or Intimidation (your choice). Additionally, when you damage a creature with a Warlock spell or cantrip, you can mark it with Lingering Regret until the end of your next turn. The next time the creature makes an attack roll or ability check, it subtracts your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) from the roll, as if gripped by an emotion it cannot name. You can affect a number of creatures this way equal to your Warlock level divided by 3 (rounded up), regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

6th-Level Umbral Lord Feature Despair halts even the strongest charge. You call forth a field of emotional gravity—a stillness that seeps into flesh and will alike. As a bonus action, you designate a point within 60 feet. That point becomes the center of a 15-foot radius zone of heavy emotional drag until the start of your next turn. Each creature of your choice that starts its turn in the area or enters it for the first time on a turn must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have its speed reduced to 0 until the end of that turn. On a failed save, the creature also cannot Dash until the end of its next turn, as if the very act of movement had become too much to bear. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

10th-Level Umbral Lord Feature Your patron reshapes you into an embodiment of psychic weight. You don’t lash out with fire or blade—you unravel resolve, layer by layer. You gain resistance to necrotic and psychic damage. As an action, you can manifest a mantle of oppressive sorrow for 1 minute. While active: You emit a 20-foot radius aura of emotional gravity. Each enemy that starts its turn in the aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened until the start of its next turn. If a creature fails this saving throw a second time in a row, it becomes incapacitated until the start of its next turn, lost in overwhelming emotion. If a creature fails the save on three consecutive turns, it becomes Paralyzed until it succeeds on the Wisdom saving throw or is outside the aura of oppressive sorrow. -The oppresive sorrow overrides any fear you are feeling, while the arua is active you are immune to frightened condition. You can use this feature once per long rest, or by expending a pact magic spell slot.

14th-Level Umbral Lord Feature You carry the end in your wake. When a soul slips away nearby, you seize its unraveling and cast it like a shadow across the battlefield. When a creature you can see within 60 feet drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to claim its fading essence. Choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) within 30 feet of the dying creature. Each must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 psychic damage and is frightened until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is not frightened. While frightened in this way, a creature loses all temporary hit points, cannot gain temporary hit points, and cannot benefit from healing. If a creature is already frightened by any means, it must use its action on its next turn to Dash away from you. If it cannot move, it instead takes an additional 5d10 psychic damage, writhing in place under the pressure of oblivion. You can use this reaction up to a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier per long rest. You are not a torch in the darkness. You are the hush after the flame goes out.

You've made a pact with a deathless being, a creature that defies the cycle and life and death, forsaking its mortal shell so it might eternally pursue its unfathomable ambitions. For such beings, time and morality are fleeting things, the concerns of those for whom grains of sand still rush through life's hourglass. Having once been mortal themselves, these ancient undead know firsthand the paths of ambition and the routes past the doors of death. They eagerly share this profane knowledge, along with other secrets, with those who work their will among the living. Beings of this type include the demilich Acererak, the vampire tyrant Kas the Bloody-Handed, the githyanki lich-queen Vlaakith, the dracolich Dragotha, the undead pharaoh Ankhtepot, and the elusive Darklord, Azalin Rex.

3rd-level Undead feature When you reach a Warlock level specified in the Undead Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells available and it doesn't count towards your amount of warlock spells known.

3rd-level Undead feature You manifest an aspect of your patron's dreadful power. As a bonus action, you transform for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits while transformed: You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level., Once during each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw, and if the saving throw fails, the target is frightened of you until the end of your next turn., You are immune to the frightened condition.,You can transform a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. The appearance of your Form of Dread reflects some aspect of your patron. For example, your form could be a shroud of shadows forming the crown and robes of your lich patron, or your body might glow with glyphs from ancient funerary rites and be surrounded by desert winds, suggesting your mummy patron.

6th-level Undead feature Your patron's powers have a profound effect on your body and magic. You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. In addition, once during each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll and roll damage against the creature, you can replace the damage type with necrotic damage. While you are using your Form of Dread, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the necrotic damage the target takes.

10th-level Undead feature Your connection to undeath and necrotic energy now saturates your body. You have resistance to necrotic damage. If you are transformed using your Form of Dread, you instead become immune to necrotic damage. In addition, when you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to retore your hit points to twice your warlock level instead and cause your body to erupt with deathly energy. Each creature of your choice that is within 30 feet of you takes necrotic damage equal to 2d10 + your warlock level. You then gain 1 level of exhaustion. Once you use this reaction, you can't do so again until you finish 1d4 long rests.

Your spirit can become untethered from your physical form. As an action, you can project your spirit from your body. The body you leave behind is unconscious and in a state of suspended animation. Your spirit resembles your mortal form in almost every way, replicating your game statistics but not your possessions. Any damage or other effects that apply to your spirit or physical body affects the other. Your spirit can remain outside your body for up to 1 hour. When your projection ends, your spirit returns to your body or your body magically teleports to your spirit's space (your choice). While projecting your spirit, you gain the following benefits: Your spirit and body gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage., When you cast a spell of the conjuration or necromancy school, the spell doesn't require verbal or somatic components or material components that lack a gold cost., You have a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover. You can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, but you take 1d10 force damage if you end your turn inside a creature or an object., While you are using your Form of Dread, once during each of your turns when you deal necrotic damage to a creature, you regain hit points equal to half the amount of necrotic damage dealt., Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest or by expending a Pact slot.

Wearing heavy armors tends to take immense physical strain, and as such usually restricts the movements of the wearer. Bulwarks who call themselves Unfettered work tirelessly to be just as, if not more efficient with their movements while donning these heavy suits. Features: 3rd Level - Heightened Agility 3rd Level - Iron Fist 7th Level - Armored Movement 13th Level - Quaking Vault 18th Level - Weightless Steel

When you select this specialization at 3rd level, your movements are swift and fluid enough to carry the full force of your armor with them. When you make an unarmed attack while wearing heavy armor, you can choose to treat it as being a weapon with the heavy property, and you can roll a d8 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed attacks.

Additionally at 3rd level, the strength built by wearing heavy armor extends to enhance your reflexes. Whenever you make an ability check or saving throw, you can replace your dexterity modifier with your strength modifier.
When you reach 7th level, you learn to move yourself with considerable speed for being weighed down. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet, and increases by another 10 feet at 18th level.

Starting at 13th level, your poise and agility work in conjunction to make landing less deadly to you, and more so to those around you. You become resistant to falling damage while wearing heavy armor, and landing no longer knocks you prone. When you land while wearing heavy armor, creatures within 15 feet of you take 2d10 bludgeoning damage, and must succeed on a strength saving throw (DC 8 + your strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be knocked prone. A creature can only be affected by this ability once per turn.

At 18th level, heavy armor ceases to be a burden for you in any meaningful way. Heavy armor weighs nothing to you while you are wearing it, and you can add half your strength modifier to your armor class while wearing it.

Monks who follow the Warrior of the Unbound Mind manifest fragments of their consciousness as psionic projections. These spectral clones serve as both weapons and tools, allowing the monk to fight across multiple positions at once, confuse enemies, and strike with thought alone. Features: 3rd Level - Psionic Projection 6th Level - Mental Anchor 11th Level - Unbound Multiplicity 17th Level - Ascendant Mind

At 3rd Level you learn to manifest one psychic shadow that shares your mobility. Summon Projection: As a Bonus Action summon one Projection (lasts 1 hour) in an unoccupied space within 30 ft, the projection is a Construct of Psionic energy. Stats: AC equals your Focus Save DC. HP equals two Martial Arts dice + Wisdom Mod. It is vulnerable to force damage, but immune to all conditions. Mobile Strike: Any unarmed strike you make can originate from your space or the Projection's space. Attacks originating from the Projection deal Psychic damage. Projection Movement: The Projection shares your movement speed. You can move the Projection up to your speed, using your movement allowance. It must remain within 60 ft. of you. Psionic Burst: When the Projection is destroyed, use a Reaction and 1 Focus Point. Creatures of your choice within 10 ft. make an Intelligence Save, taking 2 Martial Arts dice psychic damage on a failure, or half damage on a success.

Your Projection can now bind foes with psychic energy. Psionic Grapple: Once per turn, when a Projection hits a creature with an unarmed strike, you can forgo the damage to attempt a psionic grapple. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or be grappled by psionic force. The DC for the saving throw and any escape attempts equals your Focus Point DC. The Projection immediately dissipates when the grapple succeeds, and cannot trigger Psionic Burst.

Your mind’s grasp over its projections expands, granting superior tactical options. Dual Existence: You can maintain up to two Psionic Projections at the same time. You may use all features from either Projection. Projection Tactics: When a creature is hit by your stunning strike and within 5 feet of both your projections, they have disadvantage on the saving throw to resist the stun

You gain the power to lock down multiple foes and achieve psychic dominance. Unbound Grip: Your Psionic Grapple no longer requires you to forgo damage on the attack, and it can target a creature of any size. Domination Burst: When a creature fails its save against your Psionic Burst, the psychic damage increases to 3 rolls of your martial arts die, and they have disadvantage on all wisdom, intelligence and charisma saving throws and checks until the end of their next turn. Relentless Command: While a creature is grappled by your Psionic Grapple, you can spend 1 Focus Point as a bonus action to move that creature up to 30 ft. This movement uses up to 30 feet of your own movement allowance.

Monks who follow the Way of the Feral Fang tap into their primal instincts, channeling the savage power of beasts. They unleash their inner ferocity, embodying the untamed fury of nature itself. Features: 3rd Level - Feral Strikes 3rd Level - Closer to Nature 6th Level - Bestial Agility 11th Level - Fury of the Beast 17th Level - Primal Resilience

Starting at 3rd level, when you use your Flurry of Blows feature, you can replace one of the unarmed strikes with the primal savagery cantrip. The primal savagery cantrip uses wisdom as your spellcasting ability modifier for its attack rolls.
Starting at 3rd level, you can choose to learn the druidcraft or shillelagh cantrip, you use wisdom as your spellcasting ability modifier for this cantrip

At 6th level, your connection to primal instincts enhances your speed and agility. You gain the following benefits: You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would cause you to be restrained or paralyzed If you use your Primal savagery cantrip granted by Feral Strikes in a turn you can use your reaction when an enemy makes an attack of opportunity against you to roll a Martial Art Die and add the result to your AC until the end of your turn.

At 11th level, your strikes become even more savage and relentless. When you hit a creature with your primal savagery cantrip granted by your Feral Strikes feature, you can add your wisdom modifier to the damage dealt, in addition, if you spend 1 ki point, the target must also make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

Starting at 17th level, your primal connection enhances your body’s resilience and ferocity. As a bonus action, you can spend 4 ki points to enter a primal state of feral resilience that last for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits when in this state: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened. You add an additional Martial Art die to your unarmed strikes You have advantage on all Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and you gain temporary hit points equal to your Monk level at the start of each of your turns. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

The Way of the Crimson Veil is an ancient discipline, its roots tangled in the dark history of Toril. Legends trace the origin of these blood monks to the city of Yûlash, a fallen city located near the ruined kingdom of Cormanthor. In the twilight of the city’s prosperity, a small sect of monks sought knowledge in places best left undisturbed. They unearthed forbidden tomes from the deep catacombs beneath Yûlash, written in blood and sealed by ancient rites. Features: 3rd Level - Crimson Transfusion 3rd Level - Sanguine Arts 6th Level - Bloodbound Pact 11th Level - Improved Sanguine Arts 17th Level - Sanguine Edict

Starting at 3rd level, you learn to harness the power of your blood to fuel your abilities. You may use Crimson Transfusion to substitute your life force in place of ki. When you would normally expend a ki point, you can instead expend a use of Crimson Transfusion. When you do so, you take necrotic damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die for each ki point replaced. Necrotic damage dealt by this ability treats immunity as resistance. You may use this ability a number of times equal to your wisdom modifier, regaining all uses upon completing a short or long rest.

Starting at 3rd level, you unlock blood magic techniques that tap into your life force. You take necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your martial arts die. Necrotic damage dealt by this ability treats immunity as resistance. You gain access to the following Sanguine Arts abilities, which allow you to manipulate the power of blood for various effects: Fleshweaver’s Mantle: As a bonus action, you may spend up to 3 ki points to weave a ward through blood magic. For each ki point spent, you may roll three of your martial arts die and gain temporary hit points equal to the total. Leeching Blows: When you use your flurry of blows, you may choose to expend 2 ki points. During this flurry, your attacks deal additional necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your martial arts die. You regain hit points equal to the total necrotic damage dealt by these attacks.

Starting at 6th level, you bind yourself and another willing creature through spilled blood. You may spend 2 ki to initiate a one-minute ritual, after which both you and the creature take necrotic damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die. Once the ritual is complete, until your next long rest, both of you are aware of each other’s total hit points, general emotional state, and any conditions the other is afflicted by, provided they are also aware of the condition. In addition, both you and the creature gain resistance to necrotic damage for the duration. Only one such pact may be active at a time.

Starting at 11th level, you learn how to harness more sanguine arts. Hemal Torrent: When you spend a ki point or use crimson transfusion, you may imbue your unarmed strikes with blood magic. Until the end of your next turn, your unarmed strikes deal slashing or piercing damage instead of bludgeoning, and you can target enemies within 30 feet. Crimson Mist: As a bonus action, when expending a ki point, or when using crimson transfusion, you can expend 1 ki point to prepare yourself for an incoming attack. Before the end of your next turn, when you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to transform into a crimson mist, avoiding the attack and reappearing in an unoccupied space within 15 feet of your original location. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

Starting at 17th level, when you take necrotic damage, as a reaction, you can make a ranged attack against a creature within 30 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes necrotic damage equal to the necrotic damage you received, before any damage reductions. This attack uses your Wisdom modifier for both the attack and damage rolls, and counts as an unarmed strike for the purpose of bonuses.

Curiously, the Way of the Dragon Turtle is a bit of a misnomer for the monks that follow this style. Their link to the legendary beasts is practically nonexistent, only dubbed this way by others for their fortitude and control over heat and steam. Monks that follow this martial style are rarely taught formally, though they may occasionally take on no more than a few students who wish to learn the style. Those who follow the Way of the Dragon Turtle are self-made and remarkable, often gaining an innate understanding of the ki flowing through and around them after overcoming intense hardship. Although this style may seem less refined than its contemporaries, the technical ability of these monks is fatal to underestimate. They pose as much of a threat to their own bodies by manipulating pressure and heat as they do to others, and they must always understand their limits above all else. Features: Ki-Scorched Body Impact Combustion 6th Level - Pneumatic Blitz 11th Level - Body of Vapor 17th Level - Pressurized Retribution

Perseverance manifested in the form of raw ki has scorched and hardened your soul and body. When calculating your Monk unarmored defense, you may instead use 13 + your Constitution modifier. Additionally, your body is altered by the unrefined, explosive ki you harness, often leaving a strange mark on your likeness. You determine its appearance, or generate it randomly by rolling on the Ki-Scorched Characteristic table. d6 Ki-Scorched Characteristic 1 Your hands and feet are blackened, giving them the appearance of charcoal. 2 Steam often rises from your ears, mouth and body when you experience intense emotions. 3 The skin around your elbows and shoulders is cracked and ossified, peeling slightly upward like the scutes of a turtle. 4 You have a large scar or burn mark on your body, which becomes searing hot in a fight. 5 Still sources of waters nearby you tend to become restless, showing tiny ripples and tremors. 6 Your skin fluctuates between feeling extremely hot and cold to the touch.

Your rudimentary abilities in channeling ki allow you to compress and expel moisture and heat. As an action, you can cast fog cloud without providing material components. Once you cast fog cloud using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you spend 2 ki points to cast it again. Additionally, you gain the ability to convert the heat and force from blows you take into powerful outbursts. As a bonus action, if you have taken damage between the end of your last turn and the start of your current turn, you may spend 1 ki point to enter the Combustion state until the end of your turn. While in the Combustion state, you gain the following benefits: You make Strength-based attack rolls with advantage. Your unarmed strikes deal additional fire damage on a hit equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier. You can make one additional unarmed strike as part of your Attack action.

At 6th level, you gain the ability to catalyze the heat and momentum you build by moving into a volatile enhancement. If you move at least 30 feet in a straight line on your turn, you may immediately spend 2 ki points to increase your walking speed by 30 feet until the end of your turn. If you continue the current movement for at least 60 feet in a straight line, you may choose to emit a blast of excess pressure around you. When you end this movement, each creature within a 10-foot radius of you must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take a number of d10s equal to your proficiency bonus in force damage and be knocked prone. If a creature passes this saving throw, it takes half damage and is not knocked prone.

At 11th level, your control of ki becomes more refined, allowing you to manipulate the elements of your physical form. As an action, you can spend 4 ki points to cast gaseous form on yourself, without providing material components. While in this form, your movement speed is not restricted to 10 feet. Additionally, you may exit this form at any time on your turn. When you exit this form, you may heal 5d8 hit points. Once you regain hit points using this ability, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

At 17th level, your mastery over the convergence and direction of ki reaches explosive heights. As a reaction to taking damage from a source other than yourself, you may spend up to six ki points. For each ki point you spend as a part of this reaction, you mitigate 5 damage. This damage mitigation is applied before any resistances you have. You may also redirect the force from this mitigated damage, blasting out a 40-foot cone of crushing steam. Creatures in this area must pass a Constitution saving throw against your ki save DC or take 10 fire damage for each ki point you spent as part of this reaction, taking half damage if they pass. Being underwater does not grant resistance to this attack. Additionally, you are no longer required to have taken damage to enter the Combustion state as a bonus action.

Masters of a martial discipline intertwined with the ethereal energies of ki, the practitioners of the Way of the Ki Blade are formidable warriors who wield weapons forged from the very essence of their inner strength. These adept martial artists combine their physical prowess with the disciplined art of ki manipulation, creating a dance of blades that transcends the limits of the mundane. Features: 3rd Level - Ki-Forged Weapon 6th Level - Disruptive Weapon 6th Level - Ki-Bound Weapon 11th Level - Ki-Enhanced Focus 11th Level - Ki-Forged Flurry 17th Level - Ki-Blade Ascendancy

At 3rd level, you can spend 1 ki point as a bonus action to manifest a ki-forged weapon, turning a melee monk weapon into a weapon of pure energy for 1 minute. This weapon deals force damage instead of its regular damage type and uses your Wisdom modifier for attack and damage rolls. In addition, at level 5 the weapon gains a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls, unless it is a magic weapon that already has a bonus to those rolls, this bonus increases to +2 at level 11

At 6th level, once per turn you can spend a ki-point to temporarily transform your ki-forged weapon into an ethereal weapon. The next melee attack you make with it before the end of your turn ignores the target’s armor, requiring no attack roll. Instead, the target makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Ki save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes damage as if hit by an attack from your ki-forged blade and it's inner balance and movement is disrupted by your ki, the target's speed is halved, and it can't use reactions. On its next turn, it can use either an action or a bonus action, not both. On a successful save, the target takes half damage from the attack and isn't disrupted. The blade returns to normal immediately after the attack
At 6th level, If your Ki-Forged blade has the thrown property you can make it return to your hand immediately after it is thrown by spending 1 ki point.

At 11th level, your focused ki protects you from mental intrusions and damage. Your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it, and you also have resistance to psychic damage.
At 11th level, when you use your flurry of blows, you can attack with your ki-forged blade instead of unarmed strikes.

At 17th level, your connection to the essence of ki reaches its pinnacle. You can now infuse your ki-forged weapon with extraordinary power. As an action, you can spend 4 ki points to enter the state of Ki-Blade Ascendancy, which lasts for 1 minute. While in this state: Your ki-forged weapon deals an additional 1d8 force damage on each hit, and you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to twice the force damage dealt by this feature. Whenever you hit a stunned creature with your ki-forged weapon, you can spend an additional ki point to attempt to paralyze the target. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your Ki save DC or be paralyzed until the end of its next turn.
Features: 3rd Level - Light Echo's 6th Level - Fractal Vision 11th Level - Mirror Stride 17th Level - Soul of Reflection

3rd-level Mirror Soul feature Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can create reflections that disorient your foes and bolster your defense. When you use your flurry of blows, you can spend 2 ki points to cast the mirror image spell, replacing one of the unarmed strikes. When casted this way, you only make one illusory duplicate, unless you spend one ki point for an additional duplicate (3 duplicates max). For each duplicate you create, you gain 5 temporary hit points.

6th-level Mirror Soul feature As an action you may magically project your consciousness into a reflective surface that you can see. Projecting allows you to see and hear, as well as project your voice as though you were in that reflections space. During this time, you are blinded and deafened. You can sustain this effect for up to 10 minutes, and you can end it at any time (requires no action). While being used in this way, you can use an action to project to another reflective surface that you can see. While you are projecting into a reflection, your reflection is visible, and can be interacted with by others, such as speaking with them. If any reflective surface along this path is destroyed or disrupted (in the case of liquids), this effect ends.

11th-level Mirror Soul feature You gain the ability to magically enter a mirror or reflective surface within 5 feet of you and move from inside it to inside another mirror or reflective surface being effected by your Fractal Vision feature. You must spend 1 ki point and use 5 feet of movement to enter a reflection. As part of the movement used to enter the reflection, you can either pass into one of those reflections or step out of the reflection you're in. You appear in a spot of your choice within 5 feet of the destination, using another 5 feet of movement. If you have no movement left, you appear within 5 feet of the reflection you entered. You can use this ability once per round, and take 1d10 force damage if you end your turn inside a reflection.

17th-level Mirror Soul feature Starting at 17th level, you empower your Mirror Images for both defense and offense. While your Mirror Images persist, you gain the following benefits: You and your illusory duplicates gain a +1 to Armor Class and Saving Throws for each duplicate still active (up to a maximum of +3) Your unarmed strikes and monk weapon attacks deal additional psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier. (edited)
Features: 3rd Level - Deft Grip 3rd Level - Flowing Stance 7th Level - Rapid Strike 10th Level - Shatter the Horde 15th Level - Focused Strike 18th Level - Omnipath

Starting at 3rd level, after you make a weapon attack using the attack action you can use a free action to swap to another weapon. When you attack with a weapon, you receive a bonus to the attack based on the list below, however you may only benefit from a single bonus once per turn, even if your attack misses; You can however receive an additional bonus if you attack with a different weapon that causes a different type of damage. Ranged weapons do not benefit from Deft Grip, nor do generic “Elemental Weapons” (which collectively count as a single weapon), consumable items that grant additional damage, or spells. Deft Grip DC: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier Damage Type Effect Bonus Damage Bludgeoning The heavy blow causes both stone and steel to crumple. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≥ 15 1d6 or 2d6 bludgeoning damage Piercing A swift thrust gives you extra reach. +5ft attack range 1d6 piercing damage Slashing A swift slice carves through lightly armored opponents with ease. Additional 1d6 damage if AC ≤ 15 1d6 or 2d6 slashing damage Acid The acid begins to eat away at flesh and damage armor. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, the creature’s AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn. At level 10 the AC reduction is increased to 2, and at level 20 it is increased to 3. 1d6 acid damage Cold Frost begins to coalesce around the creature’s body, restricting movement. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature’s speed is reduced by half until the end of your next turn. 1d6 cold damage Fire Flames engulf the target. Dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is set ablaze and takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of their turn. The fame can be put out by a suitable liquid or by using an action to extinguish it. 1d6 fire damage Force The weapon impacts with incredible force. Strength saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is knocked prone. 1d6 force damage Lightning Lightning arcs to the flesh of another creature on impact. A random hostile creature within 10ft is chosen. That creature makes a dexterity saving throw. Upon a failure, they take the full damage of the attack. 1d6 lightning damage Necrotic The necrotic energy tears apart facsimiles of life. Doubled damage against temporary hp and creatures not in their original form (wildshape, poly, true-poly, shapechange, etc). Any damage that goes over the temp HP or the HP of the transformed creature is not doubled when applied to their HP/base form. 1d6 necrotic damage Poison Poison seeps into the wound. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature suffers from the poisoned condition. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of their turns. 1d6 poison damage Psychic Psychic damage racks the mind of the target. The creature has disadvantage on any concentration saving throws for the damage caused by this attack. 1d6 psychic damage Radiant Radiant light bursts from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is blinded. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 radiant damage Thunder A thundercrack roars forth from the weapon. Constitution saving throw. Upon a failure the creature is deafened. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. 1d6 thunder damage

At 3rd level, when you successfully hit another creature with a weapon that benefits from the Deft Grip bonus you receive a +1 to hit and to damage for your next attack if your next attack will also benefit from the Deft Grip bonus. These bonuses stack then reset to zero at the end of your turn.

Starting at 7th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you take the Attack action on your turn and have advantage on an attack roll against against one of the targets, you can forgo the advantage for that roll to make an additional weapon attack against that target, as part of the same action. You can do so no more than once per turn.

Starting at 10th level you can expend a use of your Action Surge to cause your melee attacks to strike any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target. This benefit lasts for a single turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn.

Starting at level 15 you can expend a use of your Action Surge to focus all of your ability into a singular strike. Instead of making multiple attacks, you make a single attack against a target, and if it hits that attack is essentially multiplied by however many attacks you have remaining, including bonuses for each attack from Deft Grip and Flowing Stance; Additionally, after you use this ability, you can make no more attacks on the same turn. This does not prevent a second Action Surge from being used on the same turn. This ability must be declared prior to knowing if the Focused Strike hits.

At level 18, attunement slots for weapons that require attunement can shared in a single slot however, you can not dual wield weapons that require attunement without using a second slot, you receive no benefit from the weapon when it is not in use (such as auras or other passive buffs), and you can use one of the weapons at a time.
Managed by @Loremasters The Wandering Realm's world is based on the world of Faerûn, but as a living world, it has evolved over time.

And so it came to pass that the evils of long-past would not rest idly by. Arising from the crater of Dockers Bay, the entity which had wrought its destruction upon the town arose once again, and headed toward the survivors' encampment. Hastily were plans made, and the evacuation of all that remained was underway. With groups of adventurers splitting to achieve differing objectives, ultimately the entity was stalled in a climactic battle, and in its haste, rent its destructive energy prematurely. Having successfully evacuated North of the Cloud Peaks into the Wood of Sharp Teeth, the survivors once again set camp. In the wake of the comet entity's second destructive event, several changes had been observed: First, the light of the comet in the sky dimmed to a level in which it is only just barely visible in the night sky.
