Second, unlike in the wake of the destruction of Dockers Bay, there seemed to have been very little residual energy in the second crater - Almost no Nightwalkers or shadow entities of any kind. Lastly, as the comet's light dimmed, something appeared to break off of it, hurtling across the sky like a meteor before impacting the ground some distance to the East of the new encampment. The expelled mass from the comet turned out to be a device created in the ancient Nethereil Empire by the Magos of Xiandlier Enclave. The floating enclaves of Netheril, powered by Mythallars, ultimately fell when the Mythallars, not wholly unexpectedly, were destroyed in what became known as Karsus's Folly. Within the unique device was the creator himself, Magos Esra. Finding himself a man out of time, he was met by several adventurers from the encampment who had come to investigate the meteor which had fallen from the sky. The Magos explained that his enclave had been destroyed by the elder-evil, the Star of Ice and Hate, Delban. His description of the entity which came to do its master's bidding was identical to that of the Comet Entity which had destroyed Dockers Bay, and had sought to destroy the encampment at the Cloud Peaks. Seeking the power of the Mythallars of Xiandlier, it also took interest in the Magos' experiment, and ripped it straight from the enclave's core as well, taking the Magos along with it. Now, having learned of the fate of the Netheril Empire, and much of the history that had passed in the thousand years or so since his own time, Esra seeks to rebuild his device, improve upon it, and re-create an enclave like those of ancient Netheril. At the invitation of the adventurers who had come across him after crashing into the forest, he appeared above the encampment with the beginnings of a new enclave: a mass of land and earth approximately 800 x 800 ft. He suggested that if he were able to get more power to the crystal core which sustained its floating and traveling capability, that it might be expanded upon in the future. To that end, he invited the people of the encampment knowing they, too, had suffered at the destructive hand of Delban, to come aboard the nascent enclave, and stay there. In exchange, he asked that they render their aid should the floating island come under attack, or for the occasional task that might be required to maintain its integrity. He added that all were welcome to stay on the island, so long as they also did not interfere with his work, nor the operations of the crystal entombed at the core of the island mass.

The island, which Esra named Elysium (for the hubris of the Netherese would naturally lead one to name their island for a Celestial Plane), was designed specifically to travel. It would not do to have it remain stationery over the Cloud Peaks once the refugees of Docker's Bay had come to settle the floating landmass.

Having developed on the island a bit, and established a permanent residence and facilities, the new residents of Elysium decided that the island should set sail for Waterdeep. After several days of travel, Elysium arrived just over the horizon, staying fifty miles outside the border of Waterdeep. The city's denizens, quite suspicious and wary of the sudden appearance of a giant floating landmass, resorted to keeping scouts on patrol regularly. Never was Elysium left without the watching eyes of Waterdeep scouts. While the adventurers of Elysium were regarded with mistrust and suspicion in Waterdeep, they had not as yet been barred from entering or conducting business there. Tensions however were high, and the slightest provocation, perceived or not, may tilt relations into open hostility. The Annexation of Elysium​ For a time, Elysium and Waterdeep coexisted relatively peacefully, though never without tension. Helping Waterdeep with some of its contracts helped the Elysians gain rapport, but it wasn't long before those in power found another avenue of taxation in the rich adventurers of the floating island, and Ramiel's Crusade in the east becoming an increasing threat provided yet more (albeit convenient) reason for Waterdeep to annex Elysium. The annexation began cordially, if not gladly. While the adventurers weren't happy to have to pay taxes -- some even going so far as to find every way possible to avoid doing so -- many did see the value in such a close alignment with the Lords' Alliance. But it wasn't long before even that thin connection began to break down. Word soon spread among Waterdeep's nobility of the new ward and the rich adventurers inhabiting it. Not to be outdone by these overpaid mercenaries who merely played at being nobles, but who clearly didn't see value of the land under their very feet, rich Waterdhavians began purchasing it and moving in. With the influx of people came an influx of problems, culminating in the attempted murder of a noble in the middle of the Cloud Top Inn. Elysium Regains Independence​ As the island further developed and began to move again, relations with Waterdeep were strained and Gray Wardens were placed as a proxy for the city staff to alleviate tensions and allow the island to roam without inciting diplomatic incidents. However, this was but a band aid, and relations with Waterdeep were stretched to the breaking point, resulting in Waterdeep releasing Elysium and allow it to become its own independent island. Negotiations were conducted among the land owners within the Cloud Top Inn about what should be done for the new government, and it was decided that an unusual form of government known as a democracy would be set up on the island. So Thorlas, Lord Commander of the Gray Wardens and Noble Lord of Waterdeep, acting as the city-state's representative, officialized the documents set up during the discussion and independence was declared, resulting in the withdrawal of the Warden peacekeepers and the passing of the torch to the new government. A woman by the name of Phoenix was elected to Mayor, with a supporting council comprised of Kaynes, Jerry, Alina, Alkafyn, Jack, and Cabbage. However they were not the only ones involved in the city's independence. Bryan, Clark Aiwon, Ajani, Loops Silva, Pon, Anastasia, and Vapor, among a number of other land owners, were present as well and contributed to the discussion. Together, they began the long and arduous process of nurturing the fledgling government.

And so it came to pass that the evils of long-past would not rest idly by. Arising from the crater of Dockers Bay, the entity which had wrought its destruction upon the town arose once again, and headed toward the survivors' encampment. Hastily were plans made, and the evacuation of all that remained was underway. With groups of adventurers splitting to achieve differing objectives, ultimately the entity was stalled in a climactic battle, and in its haste, rent its destructive energy prematurely. Having successfully evacuated North of the Cloud Peaks into the Wood of Sharp Teeth, the survivors once again set camp. In the wake of the comet entity's second destructive event, several changes had been observed: First, the light of the comet in the sky dimmed to a level in which it is only just barely visible in the night sky. Second, unlike in the wake of the destruction of Dockers Bay, there seemed to have been very little residual energy in the second crater - Almost no Nightwalkers or shadow entities of any kind. Lastly, as the comet's light dimmed, something appeared to break off of it, hurtling across the sky like a meteor before impacting the ground some distance to the East of the new encampment. The expelled mass from the comet turned out to be a device created in the ancient Nethereil Empire by the Magos of Xiandlier Enclave. The floating enclaves of Netheril, powered by Mythallars, ultimately fell when the Mythallars, not wholly unexpectedly, were destroyed in what became known as Karsus's Folly. Within the unique device was the creator himself, Magos Esra. Finding himself a man out of time, he was met by several adventurers from the encampment who had come to investigate the meteor which had fallen from the sky. The Magos explained that his enclave had been destroyed by the elder-evil, the Star of Ice and Hate, Delban. His description of the entity which came to do its master's bidding was identical to that of the Comet Entity which had destroyed Dockers Bay, and had sought to destroy the encampment at the Cloud Peaks. Seeking the power of the Mythallars of Xiandlier, it also took interest in the Magos' experiment, and ripped it straight from the enclave's core as well, taking the Magos along with it. Now, having learned of the fate of the Netheril Empire, and much of the history that had passed in the thousand years or so since his own time, Esra seeks to rebuild his device, improve upon it, and re-create an enclave like those of ancient Netheril. At the invitation of the adventurers who had come across him after crashing into the forest, he appeared above the encampment with the beginnings of a new enclave: a mass of land and earth approximately 800 x 800 ft. He suggested that if he were able to get more power to the crystal core which sustained its floating and traveling capability, that it might be expanded upon in the future. To that end, he invited the people of the encampment knowing they, too, had suffered at the destructive hand of Delban, to come aboard the nascent enclave, and stay there. In exchange, he asked that they render their aid should the floating island come under attack, or for the occasional task that might be required to maintain its integrity. He added that all were welcome to stay on the island, so long as they also did not interfere with his work, nor the operations of the crystal entombed at the core of the island mass.

The island, which Esra named Elysium (for the hubris of the Netherese would naturally lead one to name their island for a Celestial Plane), was designed specifically to travel. It would not do to have it remain stationery over the Cloud Peaks once the refugees of Docker's Bay had come to settle the floating landmass.

Having developed on the island a bit, and established a permanent residence and facilities, the new residents of Elysium decided that the island should set sail for Waterdeep. After several days of travel, Elysium arrived just over the horizon, staying fifty miles outside the border of Waterdeep. The city's denizens, quite suspicious and wary of the sudden appearance of a giant floating landmass, resorted to keeping scouts on patrol regularly. Never was Elysium left without the watching eyes of Waterdeep scouts. While the adventurers of Elysium were regarded with mistrust and suspicion in Waterdeep, they had not as yet been barred from entering or conducting business there. Tensions however were high, and the slightest provocation, perceived or not, may tilt relations into open hostility. The Annexation of Elysium​ For a time, Elysium and Waterdeep coexisted relatively peacefully, though never without tension. Helping Waterdeep with some of its contracts helped the Elysians gain rapport, but it wasn't long before those in power found another avenue of taxation in the rich adventurers of the floating island, and Ramiel's Crusade in the east becoming an increasing threat provided yet more (albeit convenient) reason for Waterdeep to annex Elysium. The annexation began cordially, if not gladly. While the adventurers weren't happy to have to pay taxes -- some even going so far as to find every way possible to avoid doing so -- many did see the value in such a close alignment with the Lords' Alliance. But it wasn't long before even that thin connection began to break down. Word soon spread among Waterdeep's nobility of the new ward and the rich adventurers inhabiting it. Not to be outdone by these overpaid mercenaries who merely played at being nobles, but who clearly didn't see value of the land under their very feet, rich Waterdhavians began purchasing it and moving in. With the influx of people came an influx of problems, culminating in the attempted murder of a noble in the middle of the Cloud Top Inn. Sigil Clarifications Sigil, the City of Doors, is a fairly special place in the multiverse. It is the ultimate neutral ground where people of all planes and background can meet and coexist. It also comes with some special rules, courtesy of the Lady of Pain, the godlike ruler of the mind bending city. Access to the city is granted via portals, which can be any threshold from a doorway to window or a simple clearing in a forest, and is accessed via a portal key which can be anything from a literal key to a simple thought or whistled tune as you pass the threshold. These portals are not static and can be open for centuries, seconds, or for a five uses. In other words, access is based DM/Lady of Pain discretion. Teleportation within the city does not function. Need to get around using good old fashioned leg power and it would be prudent to hire a guide if you're not a native or very familiar with the occasional loops of Mc Escher esque architecture. Creatures or people spotted in Sigil are not considered to be within their natural environment for the purposes of Shapechange, Poly, etc unless the creature is native/unique to the city or Outlands such as a Cranium Rat Squeaker or Sunfly. Binding and summoning magics also do not function within the city. Can't exactly allow the celestials to go around binding the fiends walking about, and vice versa. This is a city of neutrality, where all are permitted so long as they behave. Items or knowledge brought back from alternate universes, timelines, settings, don't transfer to our main setting. Space is... weird... in the city. Buildings move seemingly on their own, space is simultaneously compact and infinite, travel between any two places seeming to take a indeterminate amount of time. One can walk for years to get down a city block or seconds to cross to the other side of the city. It is as difficult to traverse as the DM desires and the space for new construction is seemingly infinite. Laws of the Lady Worship of the Lady is prohibited. No harm may come to any dabus. There are to be no challenges to the Lady's ultimate rule or authority within Sigil. Any action which harms the city of Sigil either directly or indirectly will be considered as a direct attack against the Lady herself, and punished appropriately. No divine entity may enter Sigil. There may be at no time more than 15 factions operating within Sigil. (Though this rule was put into place during the Great Upheaval, it is unknown if it is still amongst her laws, and the dabus have refused comment. Most haven't risked testing it.) However, there are more laws, but are determined and enforced by internal factions of the city and are not ultimate rules laid down by the Lady of Pain, who has instantly flayed and killed even the most powerful of adventurers for so much as looking at her. Thankfully she isn't seen around much.

It is often the case that fairy tales have a definitive beginning and end. The real world, however, seldom confines itself to such limitations. Our story, set as it is within the Forgotten Realms, thus begins at the end of another: The port-town of Dockers Bay, located along the Sword Coast just West of The Cloud Peaks, saw a curious collection of characters: from the typical humans making their way in the world, to the demigods that lived among them as adventurers. Long had the city been protected by powerful magic, beyond even that of the adventurers who resided there. So, when cataclysm befell the land, it confounded beliefs and shattered the sense of safety that all had resided comfortably under. It had started quite simply: A comet in the skies above. Over time, the comet revealed an unnatural nature - mages felt pain in their heads, people and animals were prone to emotional outbursts, and magical energies became unpredictable. As time passed, these effects grew in gravity, and new, worse effects appeared. Shadow creatures crept around the area, stalking the night - and certain people and creatures started being targeted. None of these events, however, hinted at what was to come. A group of some of the most powerful adventurers - not just in Dockers Bay, but indeed the world - set out to investigate the comet, determine its origin, and put a stop to its increasingly dangerous effects. What they found was nothing short of an incomprehensibly overwhelming presence, nearly killing them all simply by way of hearing its thoughts through one of them as a medium. As the intrepid heroes retreated back to safety, events only grew worse. The sun turned red, and a massive, imposing figure appeared, levitating in the skies above the bay's massive harbor. And then it awoke. None who were present to witness it directly survived, but what happened in its wake was apparent for all to see: The massive magical crystal towers which had long protected the town exploded, their devastating eldritch energy wiping out most ordinary people in the area. The town was engulfed in magical flames of purple and green, and the dark silhouette of the massive imposing figure stood silent and still in the sky above as devastation spread across the land. A few of the adventurers, at least, were quick to act: escaping by various methods of teleportation and fast-moving travel on foot. Most others were not so fortunate, and were consumed in the cataclysm. Fleeing East, the surviving adventurers of Dockers Bay set up a makeshift camp settlement at the foot of The Cloud Peaks. With only their clothes and equipment on their backs, and very little in the way of food and supplies, they regrouped, with more survivors finding their way to the makeshift settlement. It was there that these fine adventurers rested - discussing plans regarding the founding of a new settlement; perhaps somewhere far away, or perhaps somewhere else along the coast.

This section provides a navigational entry point for official D&D 5e Systems Reference Document (SRD 5.1) content, published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC-BY-4.0). Data Quarantine Notice SRD content is physically airgapped from The Wandering Realm's curated Homebrew data at the backend level. JSON files, registry outputs, and Avrae export payloads are never merged — SRD data lives exclusively under data/srd/ and avrae/srd/. The Catalog page surfaces SRD content only when the "Include Official SRD Content" toggle is explicitly enabled by the user. It defaults to off to preserve the curated, server-approved Homebrew-only view.

The Systems Reference Document 5.1 is a curated subset of the D&D 5e rules published by Wizards of the Coast under CC-BY-4.0. It includes: 319 official spells — canonical spell descriptions, components, and damage data 362 magic items — official item descriptions and rarity ratings Automation ASTs — Avrae-compatible automation payloads generated by the Polarity Engine

SRD spells and items are browsable in the Content Catalog via the "Include Official SRD Content" toggle. Entries from the SRD are clearly marked with an [SRD] badge to distinguish them from approved Homebrew content.
All SRD content is attributed to Systems Reference Document 5.1 © 2016 Wizards of the Coast LLC.
